examples.text: Why do you want to learn Dutch?

translations.de: Warum willst du Niederländisch lernen?
translations.fr: Pourquoi veux-tu apprendre le néerlandais ?
translations.pt: Porque queres aprender holandês?

more.definition: The cardinal number occurring after el and before do one in a duodecimal system. Written 10, decimal value 12.
more.etymology: Shortening of dozen.

examples.text: Where did I put my magic wand?

translations.de: Wo habe ich meinen Zauberstab hingelegt?
translations.fr: Où ai-je mis ma baguette magique ?
translations.pt: Onde é que eu pus minha varinha mágica?

examples.text: What are you doing here, young man?

translations.de: Was machst du hier, junger Mann?
translations.fr: Que fais-tu ici, jeune homme ?
translations.pt: O que você está fazendo aqui, jovem?

examples.text: We do not have medicines at home.

translations.de: Wir haben keine Medikamente zu Hause.
translations.fr: Nous n'avons pas de médicaments à la maison.
translations.pt: Não temos remédios em casa.

examples.text: I've already done this several times.

translations.de: Ich habe das schon ein paarmal gemacht.
translations.fr: Je l'ai déjà fait plusieurs fois.
translations.pt: Eu já fiz isso várias vezes.

more.definition: A syntactic marker in a question whose main verb is not another auxiliary verb or be.; A syntactic marker in negations with the indicative and imperative moods.; A syntactic marker for emphasis with the indicative, imperative, and subjunctive moods.
more.etymology: From Middle English don, from Old English dōn, from Proto-West Germanic *dōn, from Proto-Germanic *dōną, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to put, place, do, make”). For senses 4 and 5, compare Old Norse duga, also Northern English dow.

examples.text: We saw many animals in the forest.

translations.de: Wir haben viele Tiere im Wald gesehen.
translations.fr: Nous avons vu beaucoup d'animaux dans la forêt.
translations.pt: Vimos muitos animais na floresta.

examples.text: We have salty meat in the kitchen.

translations.de: Wir haben eingesalzenes Fleisch in der Küche.
translations.fr: Nous avons de la viande salée dans la cuisine.
translations.pt: Temos carne salgada na cozinha.

examples.text: We have two refrigerators in the kitchen.

translations.de: Wir haben zwei Kühlschränke in der Küche.
translations.fr: Nous avons deux réfrigérateurs dans la cuisine.
translations.pt: Temos dois frigoríficos na cozinha.

examples.text: What is the minimum wage in Greece?

translations.de: Was ist der Mindestlohn in Griechenland?
translations.fr: Quel est le salaire minimum en Grèce ?
translations.pt: Qual é o salário mínimo na Grécia?

more.definition: Located indoors, especially at home or at one's office or place of work.; Located inside something.; Falling or remaining within the bounds of the playing area.
more.etymology: PIE word *h₁en Preposition and verb from Middle English in, from Old English in, from Proto-Germanic *in. Adverb, noun and adjective from Middle English in, from Old English inn and inne, from Proto-Germanic *innai. Sense 1/2 "in"/"into" are from the original PIE prefix, with locative/accusative case respectively. Sense 3/4 "qualification"/"means" are from the PIE metaphor of all infinitives coming from locatives.

examples.text: What is the biggest city in Greece?

translations.de: Was ist die größte Stadt in Griechenland?
translations.fr: Quelle est la plus grande ville de Grèce ?
translations.pt: Qual é a maior cidade da Grécia?

examples.text: The weather in Greece is generally good.

translations.de: Das Wetter in Griechenland ist im Allgemeinen gut.
translations.fr: Le temps en Grèce est généralement bon.
translations.pt: O tempo na Grécia é geralmente bom.

examples.text: I like the feasts in the village.

translations.de: Ich mag die Feste im Dorf.
translations.fr: J'aime les fêtes au village.
translations.pt: Gosto das festas da aldeia.

examples.text: She looks at herself in the mirror.

translations.de: Sie betrachtet sich im Spiegel.
translations.fr: Elle se regarde dans le miroir.
translations.pt: Ela se olha no espelho.

more.definition: At or towards the interior of a defined space, such as a building or room.; Towards the speaker or other reference point.; So as to be enclosed or surrounded by something.
more.etymology: PIE word *h₁en Preposition and verb from Middle English in, from Old English in, from Proto-Germanic *in. Adverb, noun and adjective from Middle English in, from Old English inn and inne, from Proto-Germanic *innai. Sense 1/2 "in"/"into" are from the original PIE prefix, with locative/accusative case respectively. Sense 3/4 "qualification"/"means" are from the PIE metaphor of all infinitives coming from locatives.

examples.text: The food is heated in the oven.

translations.de: Das Essen wird im Ofen erhitzt.
translations.fr: La nourriture est chauffée au four.
translations.pt: A comida é aquecida no forno.

examples.text: I live in the northeast of Brazil.

translations.de: Ich lebe im Nordosten von Brasilien.
translations.fr: Je vis dans le nord-est du Brésil.
translations.pt: Eu moro no nordeste do Brasil.

examples.text: How beautiful the valleys are in spring!

translations.de: Wie schön sind die Täler im Frühling!
translations.fr: Qu'elles sont belles les vallées au printemps !
translations.pt: Como são belos os vales na primavera!

examples.text: Numbers are not important in Toki Pona.

translations.de: Zahlen sind in Toki Pona nicht wichtig.
translations.fr: Les chiffres ne sont pas importants à Toki Pona.
translations.pt: Os números não são importantes em Toki Pona.

more.definition: A position of power or influence, or a way to get it.; One who, or that which, is in; especially, one who is in office.; The state of a batter/batsman who is currently batting; see innings.
more.etymology: PIE word *h₁en Preposition and verb from Middle English in, from Old English in, from Proto-Germanic *in. Adverb, noun and adjective from Middle English in, from Old English inn and inne, from Proto-Germanic *innai. Sense 1/2 "in"/"into" are from the original PIE prefix, with locative/accusative case respectively. Sense 3/4 "qualification"/"means" are from the PIE metaphor of all infinitives coming from locatives.

examples.text: I never got good marks in maths.

translations.de: Ich hatte nie gute Noten in Mathematik.
translations.fr: Je n'ai jamais eu de bonnes notes en maths.
translations.pt: Nunca tirei boas notas em matemática.

examples.text: The ice cubes melted in my glass.

translations.de: Die Eiswürfel schmolzen in meinem Glas.
translations.fr: Les glaçons ont fondu dans mon verre.
translations.pt: Os cubos de gelo derreteram no meu copo.

examples.text: Your husband was not in this country.

translations.de: Ihr Mann war nicht in diesem Land.
translations.fr: Votre mari n'était pas dans ce pays.
translations.pt: Seu marido não esteve neste país.

examples.text: The rainbow will disappear in little time.

translations.de: Der Regenbogen wird in kurzer Zeit verschwinden.
translations.fr: L'arc-en-ciel disparaîtra en peu de temps.
translations.pt: O arco-íris desaparecerá em pouco tempo.

more.definition: Contained by; inside.; Within the bounds or limits of.; Surrounded by; among; amidst.
more.etymology: PIE word *h₁en Preposition and verb from Middle English in, from Old English in, from Proto-Germanic *in. Adverb, noun and adjective from Middle English in, from Old English inn and inne, from Proto-Germanic *innai. Sense 1/2 "in"/"into" are from the original PIE prefix, with locative/accusative case respectively. Sense 3/4 "qualification"/"means" are from the PIE metaphor of all infinitives coming from locatives.

examples.text: How long will you stay in town?

translations.de: Wie lange bleibst du in der Stadt?
translations.fr: Combien de temps resterez-vous en ville ?
translations.pt: Quanto tempo você vai ficar na cidade?

examples.text: The victim is in very critical condition.

translations.de: Das Opfer befindet sich in einem sehr kritischen Zustand.
translations.fr: La victime est dans un état très critique.
translations.pt: A vítima está em estado muito crítico.

examples.text: Musical theater is not popular in Greece.

translations.de: Musiktheater ist in Griechenland nicht beliebt.
translations.fr: Le théâtre musical n'est pas populaire en Grèce.
translations.pt: O teatro musical não é popular na Grécia.

examples.text: Do you like singing in the rain?

translations.de: Singst du gerne im Regen?
translations.fr: Vous aimez chanter sous la pluie ?
translations.pt: Você gosta de cantar na chuva?

more.etymology: PIE word *h₁en Preposition and verb from Middle English in, from Old English in, from Proto-Germanic *in. Adverb, noun and adjective from Middle English in, from Old English inn and inne, from Proto-Germanic *innai. Sense 1/2 "in"/"into" are from the original PIE prefix, with locative/accusative case respectively. Sense 3/4 "qualification"/"means" are from the PIE metaphor of all infinitives coming from locatives.

examples.text: Will we have bread on the table?

translations.de: Werden wir Brot auf dem Tisch haben?
translations.fr: Aurons-nous du pain sur la table ?
translations.pt: Teremos pão na mesa?

examples.text: We have two new subjects this semester.

translations.de: Wir haben zwei neue Fächer in diesem Semester.
translations.fr: Nous avons deux nouveaux sujets ce semestre.
translations.pt: Este semestre temos duas novas matérias.

examples.text: I would give everything to have her.

translations.de: Ich würde alles geben, um sie zu haben.
translations.fr: Je donnerais tout pour l'avoir.
translations.pt: Eu daria tudo para tê-la.

examples.text: I have never seen a talking dog.

translations.de: Ich habe noch nie einen sprechenden Hund gesehen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai jamais vu un chien qui parle.
translations.pt: Eu nunca vi um cachorro falante.

more.definition: A wealthy or privileged person.; A fraud or deception; something misleading.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *kap-der. From Middle English haven, from Old English habban (“to have”), from Proto-West Germanic *habbjan, from Proto-Germanic *habjaną (“to have”), durative of *habjaną (“to lift, take up”), from Proto-Indo-European *kapyéti, an imperfective formation to the root *kap- (“to take, seize, catch”). Related to heave.

examples.text: A free world doesn't have leaders.

translations.de: Eine freie Welt hat keine Führer.
translations.fr: Un monde libre n'a pas de dirigeants.
translations.pt: Um mundo livre não tem líderes.

examples.text: The cat had hidden behind the fridge.

translations.de: Die Katze hatte sich hinter dem Kühlschrank versteckt.
translations.fr: Le chat s'était caché derrière le frigo.
translations.pt: O gato tinha-se escondido atrás da geladeira.

examples.text: She left five minutes after having arrived.

translations.de: Sie ging fünf Minuten nach ihrer Ankunft.
translations.fr: Elle est partie cinq minutes après être arrivée.
translations.pt: Ela saiu cinco minutos depois de ter chegado.

examples.text: Dogs have senses we don't have.

translations.de: Hunde haben Sinne, die wir nicht haben.
translations.fr: Les chiens ont des sens que nous n’avons pas.
translations.pt: Os cães têm sentidos que nós não temos.

more.definition: To possess, own.; To hold, as something at someone's disposal.; To include as a part, ingredient, or feature.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *kap-der. From Middle English haven, from Old English habban (“to have”), from Proto-West Germanic *habbjan, from Proto-Germanic *habjaną (“to have”), durative of *habjaną (“to lift, take up”), from Proto-Indo-European *kapyéti, an imperfective formation to the root *kap- (“to take, seize, catch”). Related to heave.

examples.text: I was impressed with what I saw.

translations.de: Was ich sah, beeindruckte mich.
translations.fr: J'ai été impressionné par ce que j'ai vu.
translations.pt: Fiquei impressionado com o que vi.

examples.text: We know what we have to do.

translations.de: Wir wissen, was wir zu tun haben.
translations.fr: Nous savons ce que nous avons à faire.
translations.pt: Sabemos o que temos que fazer.

examples.text: This is what I want to do.

translations.de: Das ist es, was ich tun möchte.
translations.fr: C'est ce que je veux faire.
translations.pt: Isto é o que eu quero fazer.

examples.text: That's what Tom wants to know.

translations.de: Ebendas will Tom wissen.
translations.fr: C'est ce que Tom veut savoir.
translations.pt: Isso é o que Tom quer saber.

more.definition: In what way; to what extent.; Used before a prepositional phrase to emphasise that something is taken into consideration as a cause or reason; usually used in combination with 'with' (see what with), and much less commonly with other prepositions.
more.etymology: From Middle English what, from Old English hwæt (“what”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwat, from Proto-Germanic *hwat (“what”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷód (“what”), neuter form of *kʷós (“who”).

examples.text: You won’t believe what happened next.

translations.de: Du wirst nicht glauben, was als nächstes passierte.
translations.fr: Tu ne croiras pas ce qui est arrivé ensuite.
translations.pt: Não vais acreditar no que aconteceu depois!

examples.text: You know very well what I want.

translations.de: Du weißt ganz genau, was ich will.
translations.fr: Tu sais très bien ce que je veux.
translations.pt: Você sabe muito bem o que eu quero.

examples.text: Tell me what you know about it.

translations.de: Sag mir, was du darüber weißt!
translations.fr: Dites-moi ce que vous en savez.
translations.pt: Me conte o que você sabe sobre isso.

examples.text: Pay attention to what you're eating!

translations.de: Achte darauf, was du isst!
translations.fr: Prête attention à ce que tu manges !
translations.pt: Presta atenção no que estás comendo!

more.definition: Which, especially which of an open-ended set of possibilities.; Which.; Any ... that; all ... that; whatever.
more.etymology: From Middle English what, from Old English hwæt (“what”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwat, from Proto-Germanic *hwat (“what”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷód (“what”), neuter form of *kʷós (“who”).

examples.text: I didn't know what I wanted.

translations.de: Ich wusste nicht, was ich wollte.
translations.fr: Je ne savais pas ce que je voulais.
translations.pt: Eu não sabia o que estava querendo.

examples.text: I said what had to be said.

translations.de: Ich habe gesagt, was gesagt werden musste.
translations.fr: J'ai dit ce qui devait être dit.
translations.pt: Eu disse o que tinha que ser dito.

examples.text: I don't know what you do.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, was du tust.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas ce que tu fais.
translations.pt: Eu não sei o que você faz.

examples.text: That's just what you need now.

translations.de: Das ist genau, was du jetzt brauchst.
translations.fr: C'est juste ce dont tu as besoin maintenant.
translations.pt: Isso é o que você precisa agora.

more.definition: An expression of surprise or disbelief.; What do you want? An abrupt, usually unfriendly enquiry as to what a person desires.; What did you say? I beg your pardon? This usage is often considered impolite, with the more polite "Pardon?" or "Excuse me?" preferred.
more.etymology: From Middle English what, from Old English hwæt (“what”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwat, from Proto-Germanic *hwat (“what”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷód (“what”), neuter form of *kʷós (“who”).

examples.text: You're responsible for what you do.

translations.de: Du bist verantwortlich für das, was du tust.
translations.fr: Tu es responsable de ce que tu fais.
translations.pt: Tu és responsável pelo que fazes.

examples.text: At what time does the bus come?

translations.de: Um welche Uhrzeit kommt der Bus?
translations.fr: À quelle heure arrive le bus ?
translations.pt: A que horas chega o ônibus?

examples.text: Mary said what she intended to say.

translations.de: Maria sagte, was sie sagen wollte.
translations.fr: Marie a dit ce qu'elle avait l'intention de dire.
translations.pt: Maria disse o que ela pretendia dizer.

examples.text: We don't know what Tom wants.

translations.de: Wir wissen nicht, was Tom will.
translations.fr: Nous ne savons pas ce que veut Tom.
translations.pt: Não sabemos o que Tom quer.

more.definition: The identity of a thing, as an answer to a question of what.; Something that is addressed by what, as opposed to a person, addressed by who.
more.etymology: From Middle English what, from Old English hwæt (“what”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwat, from Proto-Germanic *hwat (“what”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷód (“what”), neuter form of *kʷós (“who”).

examples.text: We imagine immediately what is the worst.

translations.de: Wir stellen uns sofort das Schlimmste vor.
translations.fr: On imagine tout de suite ce qui est le pire.
translations.pt: Imaginamos imediatamente o pior.

examples.text: A man is but what he knows.

translations.de: Der Mensch ist nur das, was er weiß.
translations.fr: Un homme n'est que ce qu'il sait.
translations.pt: O homem é apenas o que ele sabe.

examples.text: By the way, what time is it?

translations.de: Übrigens, wie spät ist es?
translations.fr: Au fait, quelle heure est-il ?
translations.pt: A propósito, que horas são?

examples.text: I know not what tomorrow will bring.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, was der Morgen sein wird.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas ce que demain m'apportera.
translations.pt: Eu não sei o que o amanhã vai trazer.

more.definition: Emphasizes the truth of an assertion made to contradict an evidently false assumption held by the listener.; Used to invite agreement or acknowledgment when something is assumed to be straightforward or already obvious to begin with; similar in function to “right?” and “as you know”.; Used after a direct assertion to reinforce a disagreeing opinion.
more.etymology: From Middle English what, from Old English hwæt (“what”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwat, from Proto-Germanic *hwat (“what”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷód (“what”), neuter form of *kʷós (“who”).

examples.text: I didn't buy what I needed.

translations.de: Ich habe nicht gekauft, was ich brauchte.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas acheté ce dont j'avais besoin.
translations.pt: Eu não comprei o que precisava.

examples.text: At what time will you come back?

translations.de: Um wieviel Uhr kommst du wieder?
translations.fr: À quelle heure revenez-vous ?
translations.pt: A que horas você voltará?

examples.text: I know what you did last summer.

translations.de: Ich weiß, was du letzten Sommer getan hast.
translations.fr: Je sais ce que tu as fait l'été dernier.
translations.pt: Eu sei o que você fez no verão passado.

examples.text: Look what I found in the garden.

translations.de: Guck mal, was ich im Garten gefunden habe!
translations.fr: Regarde ce que j'ai trouvé dans le jardin.
translations.pt: Veja o que encontrei no jardim.

more.definition: Which thing, event, circumstance, etc.: used in asking for the specification of an identity, quantity, quality, etc.; That which; those that; the thing(s) that.; Anything that; all that; whatever.
more.etymology: From Middle English what, from Old English hwæt (“what”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwat, from Proto-Germanic *hwat (“what”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷód (“what”), neuter form of *kʷós (“who”).

examples.text: Did you follow him as we said?

translations.de: Bist du ihm gefolgt, wie wir sagten?
translations.fr: L'avez-vous suivi comme nous l'avons dit ?
translations.pt: Você o seguiu como dissemos?

examples.text: Where should we have dinner this evening?

translations.de: Wo sollen wir heute Abend zu Abend essen?
translations.fr: Nous dînons où ce soir ?
translations.pt: Onde devemos jantar esta noite?

examples.text: It's time we went to bed.

translations.de: Es ist Zeit, dass wir ins Bett kommen.
translations.fr: C'est l'heure de nous coucher.
translations.pt: É hora de irmos para a cama.

examples.text: Tomorrow we will buy turkey and veal.

translations.de: Morgen kaufen wir Puter und Kalb.
translations.fr: Demain, nous achèterons de la dinde et du veau.
translations.pt: Amanhã compraremos peru e vitela.

more.definition: Designates the speaker(s)/writer(s) as belonging to or constituting the stated category of people.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *wéyder. From Middle English we, from Old English wē (“we”), from Proto-West Germanic *wiʀ, from Proto-Germanic *wīz, *wiz (“we”), from Proto-Indo-European *wéy (“we (plural)”).

examples.text: We are not children, we are men.

translations.de: Wir sind keine Kinder, wir sind Männer.
translations.fr: Nous ne sommes pas des enfants, nous sommes des hommes.
translations.pt: Não somos crianças, somos homens.

examples.text: Why can't we divide by zero?

translations.de: Warum können wir nicht durch Null teilen?
translations.fr: Pourquoi ne pouvons-nous pas diviser par zéro ?
translations.pt: Por que não podemos dividir por zero?

examples.text: Why can we not divide by zero?

translations.de: Warum können wir nicht durch Null teilen?
translations.fr: Pourquoi ne pouvons-nous pas diviser par zéro ?
translations.pt: Por que não podemos dividir por zero?

examples.text: Tonight, we will go to the opera.

translations.de: Heute Abend gehen wir in die Oper.
translations.fr: Ce soir, nous irons à l'opéra.
translations.pt: Esta noite, iremos à ópera.

more.definition: Excluding the person(s) being addressed. (This is the exclusive we.); Including the person(s) being addressed. (This is the inclusive we.); The institution which the speaker/writer is acting for. (This is the editorial we, used by writers and others when speaking with the authority of their publication or organisation.)
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *wéyder. From Middle English we, from Old English wē (“we”), from Proto-West Germanic *wiʀ, from Proto-Germanic *wīz, *wiz (“we”), from Proto-Indo-European *wéy (“we (plural)”).

examples.text: They didn't give me an answer.

translations.de: Sie gaben mir keine Antwort.
translations.fr: Ils ne m'ont pas donné de réponse.
translations.pt: Não me deram resposta.

examples.text: A true friend would never forget me.

translations.de: Ein wahrer Freund würde mich nie vergessen.
translations.fr: Un véritable ami ne m'oublierait jamais.
translations.pt: Uma amiga de verdade jamais me esqueceria.

examples.text: My daughter gives me so much joy.

translations.de: Meine Tochter macht mir so viel Freude.
translations.fr: Ma fille me donne tellement de joie.
translations.pt: Minha filha me dá muita alegria.

examples.text: The cat is between me and you.

translations.de: Die Katze ist zwischen mir und dir.
translations.fr: Le chat est entre moi et toi.
translations.pt: O gato está entre mim e você.

more.definition: The self or personality of the speaker, especially their authentic self.; The solfeggio syllable used to indicate the flat of the third note of a major scale.
more.etymology: From Middle English me, from Old English mē (“me”, originally dative, but later also accusative, supplanting accusative mec), from Proto-West Germanic *miʀ, from Proto-Germanic *miz (“me”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁me- (“me”).

examples.text: I see you, and you see me.

translations.de: Ich sehe dich und du siehst mich.
translations.fr: Je te vois, et tu me vois.
translations.pt: Eu vejo você, e você me vê.

examples.text: Is there anyone coming to help me?

translations.de: Kommt jemand, um mir zu helfen?
translations.fr: Quelqu'un va-t-il venir m'aider ?
translations.pt: Há alguém vindo me ajudar?

examples.text: The blue jacket fits me just right.

translations.de: Die blaue Jacke passt mir sehr gut.
translations.fr: La veste bleue me va parfaitement.
translations.pt: A jaqueta azul me serve direitinho.

examples.text: Something ineffable about you fascinates me, woman.

translations.de: Etwas Unaussprechliches an dir fasziniert mich, Frau.
translations.fr: Quelque chose d'ineffable en toi me fascine, femme.
translations.pt: Algo inefável me fascina em ti, mulher.

more.definition: As the object (direct or indirect) of a verb.; As the object of a preposition.; Used in isolation or apposition, or (sometimes proscribed) as the complement of the copula (be).
more.etymology: From Middle English me, from Old English mē (“me”, originally dative, but later also accusative, supplanting accusative mec), from Proto-West Germanic *miʀ, from Proto-Germanic *miz (“me”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁me- (“me”).

examples.text: Is this supposed to be a gift?

translations.de: Soll das ein Geschenk sein?
translations.fr: C'est censé être un cadeau ?
translations.pt: Isto deveria ser um presente?

examples.text: He thought this was a bad idea.

translations.de: Er hielt dies für eine schlechte Idee.
translations.fr: Il pensait que c'était une mauvaise idée.
translations.pt: Ele achou que isto era uma má idéia.

examples.text: What would happen if I did this?

translations.de: Was würde passieren, wenn ich das täte?
translations.fr: Que se passera-t-il si je fais ça ?
translations.pt: O que aconteceria se eu fizesse isso?

examples.text: Who was the director of this film?

translations.de: Wer war der Regisseur dieses Films?
translations.fr: Qui était le réalisateur de ce film ?
translations.pt: Quem foi o diretor desse filme?

more.definition: To the degree or extent indicated.
more.etymology: From Middle English þis, this, from Old English þis (neuter demonstrative), from the North Sea Germanic base *þa- (“that”), from Proto-Germanic *þat, from Proto-Indo-European *tód, extended form of demonstrative base *to-; + North-West Germanic definitive suffix *-s, from Proto-Indo-European *só (“this, that”).

examples.text: What is the difference between these concepts?

translations.de: Was ist der Unterschied zwischen diesen Konzepten?
translations.fr: Quelle est la différence entre ces concepts ?
translations.pt: Qual é a diferença entre esses conceitos?

examples.text: I read this book two years ago.

translations.de: Ich habe dieses Buch vor zwei Jahren gelesen.
translations.fr: J'ai lu ce livre il y a deux ans.
translations.pt: Eu li este livro há dois anos.

examples.text: Which district does this number belong to?

translations.de: Zu welchem Bezirk gehört diese Nummer?
translations.fr: À quel arrondissement appartient ce numéro ?
translations.pt: A que distrito pertence este número?

examples.text: Do you know whose tie this is?

translations.de: Weißt du, wem diese Krawatte gehören könnte?
translations.fr: Savez-vous à qui est cette cravate ?
translations.pt: Você sabe de quem é essa gravata?

more.definition: The (thing) here (used in indicating something or someone nearby).; Referring to oneself.; The known (thing) (used in indicating something or someone just mentioned).
more.etymology: From Middle English þis, this, from Old English þis (neuter demonstrative), from the North Sea Germanic base *þa- (“that”), from Proto-Germanic *þat, from Proto-Indo-European *tód, extended form of demonstrative base *to-; + North-West Germanic definitive suffix *-s, from Proto-Indo-European *só (“this, that”).

examples.text: There are two churches on this street.

translations.de: In dieser Straße befinden sich zwei Kirchen.
translations.fr: Il y a deux églises dans cette rue.
translations.pt: Há duas igrejas nesta rua.

examples.text: I read this book in two days.

translations.de: Ich habe dieses Buch in zwei Tagen gelesen.
translations.fr: J'ai lu ce livre en deux jours.
translations.pt: Li esse livro em dois dias.

examples.text: I like the picture on this jar.

translations.de: Ich mag das Bild auf diesem Glas.
translations.fr: J'aime la photo sur ce pot.
translations.pt: Eu gosto da imagem neste jarro.

examples.text: We will discuss this book next lesson.

translations.de: Wir werden dieses Buch in der nächsten Stunde besprechen.
translations.fr: Nous discuterons de ce livre au prochain cours.
translations.pt: Discutiremos este livro na próxima aula.

more.definition: Indicates the speaker's strong approval or agreement with the previous material.
more.etymology: From Middle English þis, this, from Old English þis (neuter demonstrative), from the North Sea Germanic base *þa- (“that”), from Proto-Germanic *þat, from Proto-Indo-European *tód, extended form of demonstrative base *to-; + North-West Germanic definitive suffix *-s, from Proto-Indo-European *só (“this, that”).

examples.text: My darling, this spoon is not clean!

translations.de: Mein Schatz, dieser Löffel ist nicht sauber!
translations.fr: Mon chéri, cette cuillère n'est pas propre !
translations.pt: Querida, essa colher não está limpa!

examples.text: Are people still talking about this creep?

translations.de: Reden die Leute immer noch über diesen Typen?
translations.fr: Est-ce que les gens parlent encore de ce type ?
translations.pt: As pessoas ainda estão falando desse cara?

examples.text: Is this material useful for our project?

translations.de: Ist dieses Material für unser Projekt nützlich?
translations.fr: Ce matériel est-il utile pour notre projet ?
translations.pt: Este material é útil para o nosso projeto?

examples.text: Society does not agree with this law.

translations.de: Die Gesellschaft ist mit diesem Gesetz nicht einverstanden.
translations.fr: La société n'est pas d'accord avec cette loi.
translations.pt: A sociedade não concorda com esta lei.

more.definition: Something being indicated that is here; one of these.
more.etymology: From Middle English þis, this, from Old English þis (neuter demonstrative), from the North Sea Germanic base *þa- (“that”), from Proto-Germanic *þat, from Proto-Indo-European *tód, extended form of demonstrative base *to-; + North-West Germanic definitive suffix *-s, from Proto-Indo-European *só (“this, that”).

examples.text: Where is the mother of these children?

translations.de: Wo ist die Mutter dieser Kinder?
translations.fr: Où est la mère de ces enfants ?
translations.pt: Onde está a mãe dessas crianças?

examples.text: The streets are empty at this hour.

translations.de: Um diese Zeit sind die Straßen leer.
translations.fr: Les rues sont vides à cette heure.
translations.pt: As ruas estão vazias a esta hora.

examples.text: You'll learn to use these devices.

translations.de: Du wirst lernen, diese Geräte zu benutzen.
translations.fr: Tu apprendras à utiliser ces appareils.
translations.pt: Você aprenderá a usar esses dispositivos.

examples.text: I think this book is very interesting.

translations.de: Ich finde dieses Buch sehr interessant.
translations.fr: Je pense que ce livre est très intéressant.
translations.pt: Acho que este livro é muito interessante.

more.definition: The thing, item, etc. being indicated.
more.etymology: From Middle English þis, this, from Old English þis (neuter demonstrative), from the North Sea Germanic base *þa- (“that”), from Proto-Germanic *þat, from Proto-Indo-European *tód, extended form of demonstrative base *to-; + North-West Germanic definitive suffix *-s, from Proto-Indo-European *só (“this, that”).

examples.text: And he knew my deceased father well.

translations.de: Und er kannte meinen verstorbenen Vater gut.
translations.fr: Et il connaissait bien mon père décédé.
translations.pt: Ele se dava bem com meu finado pai.

examples.text: He is Indian and he speaks English.

translations.de: Er ist Inder und spricht Englisch.
translations.fr: Il est indien et il parle anglais.
translations.pt: Ele é indiano e fala Inglês.

examples.text: Is he leaving or is he staying?

translations.de: Geht er oder bleibt er?
translations.fr: Est-ce qu'il part ou reste-t-il ?
translations.pt: Ele está de partida ou vai ficar?

examples.text: Tom said he had nowhere to sleep.

translations.de: Tom sagte, er könne nirgendwo schlafen.
translations.fr: Tom a dit qu'il n'avait nulle part où dormir.
translations.pt: Tom disse que não tinha onde dormir.

more.definition: Synonym of his.
more.etymology: From Middle English he, from Old English hē, from Proto-West Germanic *hiʀ, from Proto-Germanic *hiz (“this, this one”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱís (“this”). Cognate with Scots he (“he”), North Frisian he, hi (“he”), Saterland Frisian hie (“he”), West Frisian hy (“he”), Dutch hij, ie (“he”), German Low German he (“he”), Middle High German her (“he”) Central Franconian hä (“he”), Gothic *𐌷𐌹𐍃 (*his, “this”).

examples.text: Tom said he wasn't a thief.

translations.de: Tom sagte, er sei kein Dieb.
translations.fr: Tom a dit qu'il n'était pas voleur.
translations.pt: O Tom disse que não era ladrão.

examples.text: We remember he doesn't like dogs.

translations.de: Wir erinnern uns, dass er keine Hunde mag.
translations.fr: Nous nous souvenons que les chiens ne lui plaisent pas.
translations.pt: Nós lembramos que ele não gosta de cachorros.

examples.text: I don't know where he is.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, wo er ist.
translations.fr: J'ignore où il se trouve.
translations.pt: Eu não sei onde ele está.

examples.text: Tom can feed himself, can't he?

translations.de: Tom kann sich selbst ernähren, nicht wahr?
translations.fr: Tom peut se nourrir tout seul, n'est-ce pas ?
translations.pt: O Tom pode se alimentar sozinho, não pode?

examples.text: Did Tom jump, or was he pushed?

translations.de: Ist Tom gesprungen oder wurde er gestoßen?
translations.fr: Tom a-t-il sauté ou a-t-il été poussé ?
translations.pt: Tom pulou ou foi empurrado?

examples.text: I asked him if he knew her.

translations.de: Ich fragte ihn, ob er sie kenne.
translations.fr: Je lui ai demandé s'il la connaissait.
translations.pt: Perguntei-lhe se a conhecia.

examples.text: He came as soon as he could.

translations.de: Er kam, sobald er konnte.
translations.fr: Il est venu dès qu'il a pu.
translations.pt: Ele veio assim que pôde.

examples.text: A year has passed since he died.

translations.de: Ein Jahr ist seit seinem Tod vergangen.
translations.fr: Un an s'est écoulé depuis sa mort.
translations.pt: Um ano se passou desde que ele morreu.

more.definition: The game of tag, or it, in which the player attempting to catch the others is called "he".; The player who chases and attempts to catch the others in this game.; A male.
more.etymology: From Middle English he, from Old English hē, from Proto-West Germanic *hiʀ, from Proto-Germanic *hiz (“this, this one”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱís (“this”). Cognate with Scots he (“he”), North Frisian he, hi (“he”), Saterland Frisian hie (“he”), West Frisian hy (“he”), Dutch hij, ie (“he”), German Low German he (“he”), Middle High German her (“he”) Central Franconian hä (“he”), Gothic *𐌷𐌹𐍃 (*his, “this”).

examples.text: He invited his colleagues to his wedding.

translations.de: Er lud seine Kollegen zu seiner Hochzeit ein.
translations.fr: Il a invité ses collègues à son mariage.
translations.pt: Ele convidou seus colegas para seu casamento.

examples.text: I commended him according to his merits.

translations.de: Ich lobte ihn nach seinen Verdiensten.
translations.fr: Je l'ai loué selon ses mérites.
translations.pt: Eu o elogiei de acordo com seus méritos.

examples.text: I don't think he would mind.

translations.de: Ich glaube nicht, dass es ihm etwas ausmacht.
translations.fr: Je ne pense pas que ça le dérangerait.
translations.pt: Eu acho que ele não se importaria.

examples.text: Tom regards himself as a world citizen.

translations.de: Tom hält sich für einen Weltbürger.
translations.fr: Tom se considère comme un citoyen du monde.
translations.pt: Tom se considera um cidadão do mundo.

more.definition: A person who identifies as male, or animal already known or implied.; A genderless object regarded as masculine, such as certain stars or planets (e.g. Sun, Mercury, Mars, Jupiter) or certain ships.
more.etymology: From Middle English he, from Old English hē, from Proto-West Germanic *hiʀ, from Proto-Germanic *hiz (“this, this one”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱís (“this”). Cognate with Scots he (“he”), North Frisian he, hi (“he”), Saterland Frisian hie (“he”), West Frisian hy (“he”), Dutch hij, ie (“he”), German Low German he (“he”), Middle High German her (“he”) Central Franconian hä (“he”), Gothic *𐌷𐌹𐍃 (*his, “this”).

examples.text: He's nervous and gets scared easily.

translations.de: Er ist nervös und ängstigt sich schnell.
translations.fr: Il est nerveux et facilement effrayé.
translations.pt: Ele é nervoso e se assusta fácil.

examples.text: He gets a haircut once a month.

translations.de: Er lässt sich einmal im Monat die Haare schneiden.
translations.fr: Il se fait couper les cheveux une fois par mois.
translations.pt: Ele corta o cabelo uma vez por mês.

examples.text: Eat your soup before it gets cold.

translations.de: Iss deine Suppe, bevor sie kalt wird.
translations.fr: Mange ta soupe avant qu'elle ne refroidisse.
translations.pt: Tomai a sopa antes que ela esfrie.

examples.text: I hope Tom never gets out of prison.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, dass Tom das Gefängnis niemals verlassen wird.
translations.fr: J'espère que Tom ne sortira jamais de prison.
translations.pt: Espero que Tom nunca saia da prisão

more.definition: Lineage.; A difficult return or block of a shot.; Something gotten, something gained or won; an acquisition.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *gʰe(n)d-der. Old Norse getabor. From Middle English geten, from Old Norse geta, from Proto-Germanic *getaną (“to find; to acquire, attain, get, hold, receive”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰed- (“to find; to hold; to seize; to take”).

examples.text: My dog got scared of your cat.

translations.de: Mein Hund hatte Angst vor deiner Katze.
translations.fr: Mon chien a eu peur de ton chat.
translations.pt: Meu cão se assustou com teu gato.

examples.text: The veil of ignorance is getting thinner.

translations.de: Der Schleier der Unwissenheit wird dünner.
translations.fr: Le voile de l'ignorance s'amincit.
translations.pt: Está ficando mais diáfano o véu da ignorância.

examples.text: My grandmother gets up early every morning.

translations.de: Meine Großmutter steht jeden Morgen früh auf.
translations.fr: Ma grand-mère se lève tôt tous les matins.
translations.pt: Minha avó acorda cedo todas as manhãs.

examples.text: Were you here when Tom got shot?

translations.de: Warst du hier, als Tom erschossen wurde?
translations.fr: Tu étais là quand on a tiré sur Tom ?
translations.pt: Estava aqui quando o Tom foi alvejado?

more.definition: To obtain; to acquire.; To receive.; To have. See usage notes.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *gʰe(n)d-der. Old Norse getabor. From Middle English geten, from Old Norse geta, from Proto-Germanic *getaną (“to find; to acquire, attain, get, hold, receive”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰed- (“to find; to hold; to seize; to take”).

examples.text: I like to eat pizza for breakfast.

translations.de: Ich esse gerne Pizza zum Frühstück.
translations.fr: J'aime manger de la pizza au petit-déjeuner.
translations.pt: Eu gosto de comer pizza no café da manhã.

examples.text: The thieves are greedy for your ring.

translations.de: Die Diebe sind gierig nach deinem Ring.
translations.fr: Les voleurs sont avides de votre bague.
translations.pt: Os ladrões estão ávidos por teu anel.

examples.text: Chess books were something irreplaceable for him.

translations.de: Schachbücher waren für ihn etwas Unersetzliches.
translations.fr: Les livres d'échecs étaient quelque chose d'inéchangeable pour lui.
translations.pt: Os livros de xadrez eram algo insubstituível para ele.

examples.text: This activity is too dangerous for you.

translations.de: Diese Tätigkeit ist zu gefährlich für Sie.
translations.fr: Cette activité est trop dangereuse pour toi.
translations.pt: Esta atividade é muito perigosa para você.

more.definition: Because.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *preh₂-der. Inherited from Middle English for, from Old English for (“for, because of”), from Proto-Germanic *furi (“for”), from Proto-Indo-European *preh₂-.

examples.text: I eat bread with jam for breakfast.

translations.de: Ich esse Brot mit Marmelade zum Frühstück.
translations.fr: Je mange du pain avec de la confiture au petit déjeuner.
translations.pt: Eu como pão com geleia no café da manhã.

examples.text: I know which party to vote for.

translations.de: Ich weiß, welche Partei ich wählen soll.
translations.fr: Je sais pour quel parti voter.
translations.pt: Eu sei em qual partido votar.

examples.text: The ticket for the subway is cheap.

translations.de: Das Ticket für die U-Bahn ist billig.
translations.fr: Le ticket de métro est bon marché.
translations.pt: A passagem de metrô é barata.

examples.text: We're making plans for our vacation.

translations.de: Wir schmieden Pläne für unseren Urlaub.
translations.fr: Nous faisons des plans pour nos vacances.
translations.pt: Estamos fazendo planos para nossas férias.

more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *preh₂-der. Inherited from Middle English for, from Old English for (“for, because of”), from Proto-Germanic *furi (“for”), from Proto-Indo-European *preh₂-.

examples.text: With hands outstretched, they sued for peace.

translations.de: Mit ausgestreckten Händen flehten sie um Frieden.
translations.fr: Les mains tendues, ils imploraient la paix.
translations.pt: Com as mãos estendidas, imploravam a paz.

examples.text: Where are the medicines for the cold?

translations.de: Wo gibt es Erkältungsmedikamente?
translations.fr: Où sont les médicaments contre le rhume ?
translations.pt: Onde estão os remédios para o resfriado?

examples.text: I didn't ask you for anything.

translations.de: Ich habe Sie um nichts gebeten.
translations.fr: Je ne t'ai rien demandé.
translations.pt: Não te pedi nada.

examples.text: The sofa is for the living room.

translations.de: Das Sofa ist für das Wohnzimmer.
translations.fr: Le canapé est pour le salon.
translations.pt: O sofá é para a sala.

more.definition: Towards; in the direction of.; Leading towards in time or circumstance.; Directed at; intended to belong to.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *preh₂-der. Inherited from Middle English for, from Old English for (“for, because of”), from Proto-Germanic *furi (“for”), from Proto-Indo-European *preh₂-.

examples.text: Everyone that I know can speak French.

translations.de: Jeder, den ich kenne, kann Französisch sprechen.
translations.fr: Toutes les personnes que je connais savent parler français.
translations.pt: Todos que conheço sabem falar Francês.

examples.text: Maybe we can help each other out.

translations.de: Vielleicht können wir uns gegenseitig helfen.
translations.fr: Peut-être que nous pouvons nous entraider.
translations.pt: Talvez possamos ajudar um ao outro.

examples.text: You can't run away from yourself.

translations.de: Du kannst nicht vor dir selbst weglaufen.
translations.fr: Tu ne peux pas te fuir toi-même.
translations.pt: Você não pode fugir de si mesmo.

examples.text: We can't drink the tap water.

translations.de: Wir können das Leitungswasser nicht trinken.
translations.fr: Nous ne pouvons pas boire l'eau du robinet.
translations.pt: Não podemos beber água encanada.

more.definition: OK, sure; indicates approval or acknowledgment.; Used to convey reassurance.
more.etymology: From Middle English can, first and third person singular of connen, cunnen (“to be able, know how”), from Old English can(n), first and third person singular of cunnan (“to know how”), from Proto-West Germanic *kunnan, from Proto-Germanic *kunnaną, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵneh₃- (whence also know). Doublet of con. See also: canny, cunning.

examples.text: I'm tired and can't concentrate.

translations.de: Ich bin müde und kann mich nicht konzentrieren.
translations.fr: Je suis fatigué et je n'arrive pas à me concentrer.
translations.pt: Estou cansado e não consigo me concentrar.

examples.text: What can I find on this website?

translations.de: Was kann ich auf dieser Website finden?
translations.fr: Que puis-je trouver sur ce site ?
translations.pt: O que posso encontrar neste website?

examples.text: The priest can sacrifice on the altar.

translations.de: Der Priester kann auf dem Altar opfern.
translations.fr: Le prêtre peut sacrifier sur l'autel.
translations.pt: O sacerdote pode sacrificar no altar.

examples.text: She can't live far from here.

translations.de: Sie kann nicht weit weg von hier wohnen.
translations.fr: Elle ne peut pas vivre loin d'ici.
translations.pt: Ela não pode morar longe daqui.

more.definition: A container or vessel, especially for liquids, usually made of metal.; A sealed metal container, cylindrical or cuboid in form, typically used to store preserved foods.; A container used to carry and dispense water for plants (a watering can).
more.etymology: From Middle English canne, from Old English canne (“glass, container, cup, jar”), from Proto-Germanic *kannǭ (“can, tankard, mug, cup”).

examples.text: At night, she can see the stars.

translations.de: Nachts kann sie die Sterne sehen.
translations.fr: La nuit, elle peut voir les étoiles.
translations.pt: À noite ela pode ver as estrelas.

examples.text: Is it true Tom can't swim?

translations.de: Stimmt es, dass Tom nicht schwimmen kann?
translations.fr: Est-ce vrai que Tom ne sait pas nager ?
translations.pt: É verdade que o Tom não sabe nadar?

examples.text: Metals can become brittle at low temperatures.

translations.de: Metalle können bei tiefen Temperaturen spröde werden.
translations.fr: Les métaux peuvent devenir fragiles à basse température.
translations.pt: Metais podem ficar frágeis em baixas temperaturas.

examples.text: They say that they can help us.

translations.de: Sie sagen, dass sie uns helfen können.
translations.fr: Ils disent qu'ils peuvent nous aider.
translations.pt: Eles dizem que podem nos ajudar.

more.definition: OK(?); used at the end of a question when seeking approval or acknowledgment.
more.etymology: From Middle English can, first and third person singular of connen, cunnen (“to be able, know how”), from Old English can(n), first and third person singular of cunnan (“to know how”), from Proto-West Germanic *kunnan, from Proto-Germanic *kunnaną, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵneh₃- (whence also know). Doublet of con. See also: canny, cunning.

examples.text: Emotional, she could hardly hide her tears.

translations.de: Emotional konnte sie ihre Tränen kaum verbergen.
translations.fr: Émue, elle a du mal à cacher ses larmes.
translations.pt: Emocionada, ela mal conseguia esconder as lágrimas.

examples.text: I can't paint without my brush.

translations.de: Ohne meinen Pinsel kann ich nicht malen.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas peindre sans mon pinceau.
translations.pt: Não consigo pintar sem meu pincel.

examples.text: I wasn't able to do anything.

translations.de: Ich konnte nichts machen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas pu faire quoi que ce soit.
translations.pt: Eu não fui capaz de fazer nada.

examples.text: You can't separate time from space.

translations.de: Zeit und Raum kann man nicht trennen.
translations.fr: On ne peut pas séparer le temps de l'espace.
translations.pt: Não se pode separar o espaço do tempo.

more.definition: To know how to.; To be able to.; May; to be permitted or enabled to.
more.etymology: From Middle English can, first and third person singular of connen, cunnen (“to be able, know how”), from Old English can(n), first and third person singular of cunnan (“to know how”), from Proto-West Germanic *kunnan, from Proto-Germanic *kunnaną, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵneh₃- (whence also know). Doublet of con. See also: canny, cunning.

examples.text: Don't go out! There's lightning!

translations.de: Geh nicht aus! Es blitzt!
translations.fr: Ne sors pas ! Il y a des éclairs !
translations.pt: Não saia! Está trovejando!

examples.text: Does the subway go to the airport?

translations.de: Fährt die U-Bahn zum Flughafen?
translations.fr: Le métro va-t-il à l'aéroport ?
translations.pt: O metrô vai até o aeroporto?

examples.text: You need to go to hospital immediately.

translations.de: Sie müssen sofort ins Krankenhaus fahren.
translations.fr: Il faut aller à l'hôpital immédiatement.
translations.pt: Você precisa ir imediatamente para o hospital.

examples.text: It was too cold to go out.

translations.de: Es war zu kalt, um auszugehen.
translations.fr: Il faisait trop froid pour sortir.
translations.pt: Estava muito frio para sair.

more.definition: Working correctly and ready to commence operation; approved and able to be put into action.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₁-der. From Middle English gon, goon, from Old English gān (“to go”), from Proto-West Germanic *gān, from Proto-Germanic *gāną (“to go”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₁- (“to leave”). The inherited past tense form yode (compare Old English ēode) was replaced through suppletion in the 15th century by went, from Old English wendan (“to go, depart, wend”).

examples.text: Children have to go to bed early.

translations.de: Kinder müssen früh ins Bett gehen.
translations.fr: Les enfants doivent se coucher tôt.
translations.pt: As crianças devem ir para a cama cedo.

examples.text: They wish to go there for vacation.

translations.de: Sie möchten dort Urlaub machen.
translations.fr: Ils souhaitent y aller en vacances.
translations.pt: Eles desejam ir para lá de férias.

examples.text: You'd better not go there again.

translations.de: Du solltest besser nicht wieder dorthin gehen.
translations.fr: Tu ferais mieux de ne pas y retourner.
translations.pt: É melhor você não ir lá de novo.

examples.text: I want to go to the cinema.

translations.de: Ich möchte ins Kino gehen.
translations.fr: Je veux aller au cinéma.
translations.pt: Quero ir ao cinema.

more.definition: A turn at something, or in something (e.g. a game).; An attempt, a try.; A period of activity.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₁-der. From Middle English gon, goon, from Old English gān (“to go”), from Proto-West Germanic *gān, from Proto-Germanic *gāną (“to go”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₁- (“to leave”). The inherited past tense form yode (compare Old English ēode) was replaced through suppletion in the 15th century by went, from Old English wendan (“to go, depart, wend”).

examples.text: We went to the match last night.

translations.de: Wir sind gestern Abend zum Spiel gegangen.
translations.fr: On est allé au match hier soir.
translations.pt: Fomos ao jogo ontem à noite.

examples.text: I am going to solve the problem.

translations.de: Ich werde das Problem lösen.
translations.fr: Je vais résoudre le problème.
translations.pt: Vou resolver o problema.

examples.text: Many people go to church on Christmas.

translations.de: Viele Menschen gehen zu Weihnachten in die Kirche.
translations.fr: Beaucoup de gens vont à l'église à Noël.
translations.pt: Muitas pessoas vão à igreja no Natal.

examples.text: The sick woman goes to the doctor.

translations.de: Die kranke Frau geht zum Arzt.
translations.fr: La femme malade va chez le médecin.
translations.pt: A mulher doente vai ao médico.

examples.text: I go to work on foot every day.

translations.de: Ich gehe jeden Tag zu Fuß zur Arbeit.
translations.fr: Je vais au travail à pied tous les jours.
translations.pt: Eu vou a pé para o trabalho todos os dias.

examples.text: She went to the movies yesterday.

translations.de: Sie ist gestern ins Kino gegangen.
translations.fr: Elle est allée au cinéma hier.
translations.pt: Ela foi ao cinema ontem.

more.definition: To move through space (especially to or through a place). (May be used of tangible things such as people or cars, or intangible things such as moods or information.); To move or travel through time (either literally—in a fictional or hypothetical situation in which time travel is possible—or in one's mind or knowledge of the historical record). (See also go back.); To navigate (to a file or folder on a computer, a site on the internet, a memory, etc.).
collocations: go for a walk — to take a walk
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₁-der. From Middle English gon, goon, from Old English gān (“to go”), from Proto-West Germanic *gān, from Proto-Germanic *gāną (“to go”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₁- (“to leave”). The inherited past tense form yode (compare Old English ēode) was replaced through suppletion in the 15th century by went, from Old English wendan (“to go, depart, wend”).

examples.text: I saw an owl at my window.

translations.de: Ich sah eine Eule an meinem Fenster.
translations.fr: J'ai vu une chouette à ma fenêtre.
translations.pt: Eu vi uma coruja na minha janela.

examples.text: Send me your new address by email.

translations.de: Senden Sie mir Ihre neue Adresse per E-Mail.
translations.fr: Envoyez-moi votre nouvelle adresse par courriel.
translations.pt: Envie-me seu novo endereço por e-mail.

examples.text: I spend my time doing various things.

translations.de: Ich verbringe meine Zeit damit, verschiedene Dinge zu tun.
translations.fr: Je passe mon temps à faire diverses choses.
translations.pt: Passo meu tempo fazendo várias coisas.

examples.text: My father and my uncle are brothers.

translations.de: Mein Vater und mein Onkel sind Brüder.
translations.fr: Mon père et mon oncle sont frères.
translations.pt: Meu pai e meu tio são irmãos.

more.definition: Belonging to me.; Associated with me.; Related to me.
more.etymology: From Middle English mi, my, apocopated form of min, myn, from Old English mīn (“my, mine”), from Proto-West Germanic *mīn, from Proto-Germanic *mīnaz (“my, mine”, pron.) (possessive of *ek (“I”)), from Proto-Indo-European *méynos (“my; mine”). Cognate with West Frisian myn (“my”), Afrikaans my (“my”), Dutch mijn (“my”), German mein (“my”), Swedish min (“my”). More at me.

examples.text: I change my toothbrush every three months.

translations.de: Ich wechsle meine Zahnbürste alle drei Monate.
translations.fr: Je change de brosse à dents tous les trois mois.
translations.pt: Troco minha escova de dentes cada três meses.

examples.text: He always tells me the same story.

translations.de: Er erzählt mir immer die gleiche Geschichte.
translations.fr: Il me raconte toujours la même histoire.
translations.pt: Ele sempre me conta a mesma história.

examples.text: The garden around my house is beautiful.

translations.de: Der Garten um mein Haus herum ist wunderschön.
translations.fr: Le jardin autour de ma maison est magnifique.
translations.pt: O jardim ao redor da minha casa é lindo.

examples.text: He was one of my best friends.

translations.de: Er war einer meiner besten Freunde.
translations.fr: C'était l'un de mes meilleurs amis.
translations.pt: Era um dos meus maiores amigos.

more.definition: Used to express surprise, shock or amazement.
more.etymology: From my, kept upon ellipsis of an oath such as my word or my God.

examples.text: There is an alligator on your top.

translations.de: Auf deiner Bluse ist ein Alligator.
translations.fr: Il y a un alligator sur ta blouse.
translations.pt: Há um jacaré em tua blusa.

examples.text: The bees are sitting on the flowers.

translations.de: Die Bienen sitzen auf den Blumen.
translations.fr: Les abeilles sont assises sur les fleurs.
translations.pt: As abelhas estão pousadas nas flores.

examples.text: She is watching the news on television.

translations.de: Sie sieht sich die Nachrichten im Fernsehen an.
translations.fr: Elle regarde les nouvelles à la télévision.
translations.pt: Ela está assistindo ao noticiário na televisão.

examples.text: I read the text on page nine.

translations.de: Ich habe den Text auf Seite neun gelesen.
translations.fr: J'ai lu le texte de la page neuf.
translations.pt: Eu li o texto da página nove.

more.definition: In the state of being active, functioning or operating.; Happening; taking place; being or due to be put into action.; Of a person, used to express agreement to or acceptance of a proposal or challenge made by that person; most commonly with subject "you" (see you're on).
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₂en-der. From Middle English on, from Old English on, an (“on, upon, onto, in, into”), from Proto-West Germanic *ana, from Proto-Germanic *ana (“on, at”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂en- (“on, onto”).

examples.text: There's a sparrow on the windowsill.

translations.de: Da ist ein Spatz auf der Fensterbank!
translations.fr: Il y a un moineau sur le rebord de la fenêtre.
translations.pt: Há um pardal no parapeito da janela.

examples.text: You have some ink on your face.

translations.de: Du hast Tinte im Gesicht.
translations.fr: Tu as de l'encre sur le visage.
translations.pt: Você tem um pouco de tinta no rosto.

examples.text: There are stripes only on the sleeves.

translations.de: Nur an den Ärmeln sind Streifen.
translations.fr: Il n'y a des rayures que sur les manches.
translations.pt: Há listras apenas nas mangas.

examples.text: There are spots even on the sun.

translations.de: Sogar auf der Sonne gibt es Flecken.
translations.fr: Il y a des taches même sur le soleil.
translations.pt: Existem manchas até no sol.

more.definition: To an operating state.; So as to cover or be fitted.; Along, forwards (continuing an action), onwards.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₂en-der. From Middle English on, from Old English on, an (“on, upon, onto, in, into”), from Proto-West Germanic *ana, from Proto-Germanic *ana (“on, at”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂en- (“on, onto”).

examples.text: The siblings are walking on the beach.

translations.de: Die Geschwister gehen am Strand spazieren.
translations.fr: Les frères et sœurs se promènent sur la plage.
translations.pt: Os irmãos estão andando na praia.

examples.text: The children drew butterflies on the wall.

translations.de: Die Kinder haben an die Wand Schmetterlinge gezeichnet.
translations.fr: Les enfants ont dessiné des papillons sur le mur.
translations.pt: As crianças desenharam borboletas na parede.

examples.text: Tom had a bruise on his face.

translations.de: Tom hatte einen blauen Fleck in seinem Gesicht.
translations.fr: Tom avait un bleu au visage.
translations.pt: Tom tinha um hematoma no rosto.

examples.text: Why is the soap on the table?

translations.de: Warum liegt die Seife auf dem Tisch?
translations.fr: Pourquoi le savon est-il sur la table ?
translations.pt: Por que o sabonete está na mesa?

more.definition: In the Japanese language, a pronunciation, or reading, of a kanji character that was originally based on the character's pronunciation in Chinese, contrasted with kun.
more.etymology: From Japanese 音読み (on'yomi, literally “sound reading”).

examples.text: The exit door is on the right.

translations.de: Die Ausgangstür befindet sich auf der rechten Seite.
translations.fr: La porte de sortie est à droite.
translations.pt: A porta de saída fica à direita.

examples.text: They put the lamp on the nightstand.

translations.de: Die Lampe wurde auf den Nachttisch gestellt.
translations.fr: Ils posèrent la lampe sur la table de nuit.
translations.pt: Colocaram a luminária na mesa de cabeceira.

examples.text: All our books are on the floor.

translations.de: Alle unsere Bücher liegen auf dem Boden.
translations.fr: Tous nos livres sont par terre.
translations.pt: Todos os nossos livros estão no chão.

examples.text: We lost our passports on the trip.

translations.de: Wir haben unsere Pässe auf der Reise verloren.
translations.fr: Nous avons perdu nos passeports pendant le voyage.
translations.pt: Perdemos nossos passaportes na viagem.

more.definition: Positioned at the upper surface of, touching from above.; Positioned at or resting against the outer surface of; attached to.; Covering.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₂en-der. From Middle English on, from Old English on, an (“on, upon, onto, in, into”), from Proto-West Germanic *ana, from Proto-Germanic *ana (“on, at”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂en- (“on, onto”).

examples.text: This dress looks really good on her.

translations.de: Dieses Kleid steht ihr wirklich gut.
translations.fr: Cette robe lui va très bien.
translations.pt: Este vestido fica muito bem nela.

examples.text: You've got something on your lip.

translations.de: Du hast etwas auf deiner Lippe.
translations.fr: Tu as quelque chose sur la lèvre.
translations.pt: Você tem algo no seu lábio.

examples.text: Did you do well on the test?

translations.de: Haben Sie bei dem Test gut abgeschnitten?
translations.fr: Tu as bien réussi le test ?
translations.pt: Saíram-se bem na prova?

examples.text: Is there a school on your street?

translations.de: Gibt es eine Schule in Ihrer Straße?
translations.fr: Y a-t-il une école dans ta rue ?
translations.pt: Há uma escola na sua rua?

more.definition: To switch on.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₂en-der. From Middle English on, from Old English on, an (“on, upon, onto, in, into”), from Proto-West Germanic *ana, from Proto-Germanic *ana (“on, at”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂en- (“on, onto”).

examples.text: What is the currency of your country?

translations.de: Was ist die Währung Ihres Landes?
translations.fr: Quelle est la devise de votre pays ?
translations.pt: Qual é a moeda do vosso país?

examples.text: My donkey is faster than your car.

translations.de: Mein Esel ist schneller als dein Auto.
translations.fr: Mon âne est plus rapide que ta voiture.
translations.pt: Meu burro é mais rápido que seu carro.

examples.text: Can you be faster than your shadow?

translations.de: Kannst du schneller sein als dein Schatten?
translations.fr: Pouvez-vous être plus rapide que votre ombre ?
translations.pt: Você pode ser mais rápido que sua sombra?

examples.text: Don't you care about your education?

translations.de: Ist dir deine Ausbildung egal?
translations.fr: Votre éducation ne vous intéresse pas ?
translations.pt: Você não se importa com sua educação?

more.definition: Belonging to you; of you; related to you (singular; one owner).; Belonging to you; of you; related to you (plural; more owners).; A determiner that conveys familiarity and mutual knowledge of the modified noun.
more.etymology: From Middle English your, youre, ȝour, ȝoure, from Old English ēower, īower (“your”, plural), from Proto-West Germanic *iuwar, from Proto-Germanic *izweraz. Cognate with Saterland Frisian jou (“your”), Dutch jouw (“your”), German Low German jo, jos (“your”), German euer (“your”, plural), Danish jeres (“your”).

examples.text: I'd like to know more languages.

translations.de: Ich möchte mehr Sprachen wissen.
translations.fr: J'aimerais connaître plus de langues.
translations.pt: Gostaria de saber mais idiomas.

examples.text: Who else knows how to do this?

translations.de: Wer weiß noch, wie das geht?
translations.fr: Qui d'autre sait comment faire ça ?
translations.pt: Quem mais sabe fazer isso?

examples.text: Do you know anyone who speaks Japanese?

translations.de: Kennst du jemanden, der Japanisch spricht?
translations.fr: Connaissez-vous quelqu'un qui parle japonais ?
translations.pt: Vocês conhecem alguém que fale Japonês?

examples.text: Now I know much more than before.

translations.de: Jetzt weiß ich viel mehr als vorher.
translations.fr: Maintenant, j'en sais beaucoup plus qu'avant.
translations.pt: Agora eu sei muito mais do que antes.

more.definition: Knowledge; the state of knowing. (Now confined to the fixed phrase in the know.)
more.etymology: From Middle English knowen, from Old English cnāwan (“to know, perceive, recognise”), from Proto-West Germanic *knāan, from Proto-Germanic *knēaną (“to know”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵneh₃- (“to know”). Cognates * from Proto-Germanic: Scots knaw (“to know, recognise”), Icelandic knega (“to know, know how to, be able”), Old High German knājan (“to know, recognise”), Old Norse kná (“to know how”).

examples.text: I'd love to know to fly.

translations.de: Ich würde gerne fliegen können.
translations.fr: J'aimerais savoir voler.
translations.pt: Eu adoraria saber voar.

examples.text: She doesn't know where Mary lives.

translations.de: Sie weiß nicht, wo Maria wohnt.
translations.fr: Elle ne sait pas où habite Marie.
translations.pt: Ela não sabe onde Maria mora.

examples.text: Do you know how much you weigh?

translations.de: Wissen Sie, wie viel Sie wiegen?
translations.fr: Savez-vous combien vous pesez ?
translations.pt: Você sabe qual é o seu peso?

examples.text: Next time, let me know in advance.

translations.de: Nächstes Mal gibst du mir im Voraus Bescheid!
translations.fr: La prochaine fois, préviens-moi à l'avance.
translations.pt: Da próxima vez, avise-me com antecedência.

more.definition: Used at the end of a sentence to draw attention to information one thinks the listener should keep in mind.; Synonym of you know (used as a conversational discourse marker, to emphasize something)
more.etymology: Shortening of you know (sense 4)—Singapore English favours pro-drop constructions (Wee, 2003).

examples.text: The prime minister does not know English.

translations.de: Der Premierminister spricht kein Englisch.
translations.fr: Le premier ministre ne parle pas l'anglais.
translations.pt: O primeiro ministro não sabe inglês.

examples.text: Who knows the answer to this question?

translations.de: Wer kennt die Antwort auf diese Frage?
translations.fr: Qui connait la réponse à cette question ?
translations.pt: Quem sabe a resposta para esta questão?

examples.text: He knew he was no longer needed.

translations.de: Er wusste, dass er nicht mehr gebraucht wurde.
translations.fr: Il savait qu'il n'était plus nécessaire.
translations.pt: Ele sabia que não era mais necessário.

examples.text: I didn't know you had come.

translations.de: Ich wusste nicht, dass du gekommen bist.
translations.fr: Je ne savais pas que tu étais venu.
translations.pt: Não sabia que tinhas vindo.

more.definition: To perceive the truth or factuality of; to be certain of; to be certain that.; To be or become aware or cognizant.; To be aware of; to be cognizant of.
more.etymology: From Middle English knowen, from Old English cnāwan (“to know, perceive, recognise”), from Proto-West Germanic *knāan, from Proto-Germanic *knēaną (“to know”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵneh₃- (“to know”). Cognates * from Proto-Germanic: Scots knaw (“to know, recognise”), Icelandic knega (“to know, know how to, be able”), Old High German knājan (“to know, recognise”), Old Norse kná (“to know how”).

examples.text: There was no one in the library.

translations.de: In der Bibliothek war niemand.
translations.fr: Il n'y avait personne à la bibliothèque.
translations.pt: Não tinha ninguém na biblioteca.

examples.text: There's no one better than you.

translations.de: Es gibt niemanden, der besser ist als du.
translations.fr: Il n’y a personne de mieux que toi.
translations.pt: Não há ninguém melhor do que você.

examples.text: There is no such word in Russian.

translations.de: So ein Wort gibt es im Russischen nicht.
translations.fr: Un tel mot n'existe pas en russe.
translations.pt: Tal palavra não existe em russo.

examples.text: Why is no one visiting my website?

translations.de: Warum besucht niemand meine Website?
translations.fr: Pourquoi personne ne visite mon site web ?
translations.pt: Por que ninguém está visitando meu site?

more.definition: Used before different, before comparatives with more and less, and idiomatically before other comparatives.; Used idiomatically before certain other adjectives.; Not.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English no, na, from Old English nā, nō (“no, not, not ever, never”), from Proto-West Germanic *naiwō, from Proto-Germanic *naiwô (“never”), from *ne (“not”) + *aiwō (“ever”), equivalent to ne + aye.

examples.text: We have no way to verify this.

translations.de: Wir haben keine Möglichkeit, das zu überprüfen.
translations.fr: Nous n'avons aucun moyen de vérifier ceci.
translations.pt: Não temos nenhuma maneira de verificar isso.

examples.text: I have no intention of getting married.

translations.de: Ich habe nicht die Absicht zu heiraten.
translations.fr: Je n'ai aucune intention de me marier.
translations.pt: Não tenho a intenção de me casar.

examples.text: Oh no, you have revealed our secret!

translations.de: O nein! Du hast unser Geheimnis verraten!
translations.fr: Oh non, tu as révélé notre secret !
translations.pt: Oh não, você revelou nosso segredo!

examples.text: There's no need to be embarrassed.

translations.de: Du brauchst dich nicht zu schämen.
translations.fr: Tu ne dois pas avoir honte.
translations.pt: Você não precisa ter vergonha.

more.definition: Not any.; Hardly any.; Not any possibility or allowance of (something).
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English no, noo, na, a reduced form of none, noon, nan (“none, not any”) used before consonants (compare a to an), from Old English nān (“none, not any”), from Proto-West Germanic *nain, from Proto-Germanic *nainaz (“not any”, literally “not one”), equivalent to ne (“not”) + a. Piecewise doublet of none.

examples.text: From tomorrow, I will no longer smoke.

translations.de: Von morgen ab werde ich nicht mehr rauchen.
translations.fr: À partir de demain, je ne fumerai plus.
translations.pt: A partir de amanhã, eu não vou fumar mais.

examples.text: I hope no one saw me dancing.

translations.de: Hoffentlich hat mich keiner tanzen sehen.
translations.fr: J'espère que personne ne m'a vu danser.
translations.pt: Espero que ninguém me tenha visto dançando.

examples.text: I'm no longer afraid of spiders.

translations.de: Ich habe keine Angst mehr vor Spinnen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai plus peur des araignées.
translations.pt: Eu já não tenho medo de aranhas.

examples.text: I had no friends except for Tom.

translations.de: Außer Tom hatte ich keine Freunde.
translations.fr: Je n'avais aucun ami excepté Tom.
translations.pt: Eu não tinha nenhum amigo exceto Tom.

examples.text: There was no reason to be concerned.

translations.de: Es gab keinen Grund zur Sorge.
translations.fr: Il n'y avait aucune raison de s'inquiéter.
translations.pt: Não havia motivo para se preocupar.

examples.text: I'm no better than a beggar.

translations.de: Ich bin nicht besser als ein Bettler.
translations.fr: Je ne vaux pas mieux qu'un mendiant.
translations.pt: Não sou melhor que um mendigo.

examples.text: There's no grass on the moon.

translations.de: Es gibt kein Gras auf dem Mond.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas d'herbe sur la lune.
translations.pt: Não há grama na Lua.

examples.text: I had no one to talk with.

translations.de: Ich hatte niemanden, mit dem ich reden konnte.
translations.fr: Je n'avais aucun interlocuteur.
translations.pt: Eu não tinha ninguém com quem falar.

more.definition: A negating expression; an answer that shows disagreement, denial, refusal, or disapproval.; A vote not in favor, or opposing a proposition.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English no, na, from Old English nā, nō (“no, not, not ever, never”), from Proto-West Germanic *naiwō, from Proto-Germanic *naiwô (“never”), from *ne (“not”) + *aiwō (“ever”), equivalent to ne + aye.

examples.text: There is no grammatical gender in Hungarian.

translations.de: Im Ungarischen gibt es kein grammatikalisches Geschlecht.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas de genre grammatical en hongrois.
translations.pt: Não há gênero gramatical em húngaro.

examples.text: She knows that she has no choice.

translations.de: Sie weiß, dass sie keine andere Wahl hat.
translations.fr: Elle sait qu'elle n'a pas le choix.
translations.pt: Ela sabe que não tem escolha.

examples.text: Tom had no choice but to surrender.

translations.de: Tom hatte keine andere Wahl, als sich zu ergeben.
translations.fr: Tom n'avait pas d'autre choix que de se rendre.
translations.pt: O Tom não teve escolha a não ser se render.

examples.text: There are no badgers in this forest.

translations.de: In diesem Wald gibt es keine Dachse.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas de blaireaux dans cette forêt.
translations.pt: Não existem texugos na floresta.

more.definition: Used to show disagreement, negation, denial, refusal, or prohibition.; Used to ask for confirmation.; Used to express sadness or disappointment.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English no, na, from Old English nā, nō (“no, not, not ever, never”), from Proto-West Germanic *naiwō, from Proto-Germanic *naiwô (“never”), from *ne (“not”) + *aiwō (“ever”), equivalent to ne + aye.

examples.text: I'm no longer afraid of dogs.

translations.de: Ich habe keine Angst mehr vor Hunden.
translations.fr: Je n'ai plus peur des chiens.
translations.pt: Eu já não tenho medo de cães.

examples.text: Invertebrates have no backbone or spinal column.

translations.de: Wirbellose haben kein Rückgrat oder eine Wirbelsäule.
translations.fr: Les invertébrés n'ont pas d'épine dorsale ou de colonne vertébrale.
translations.pt: Os invertebrados não possuem espinha dorsal ou coluna vertebral.

examples.text: I'm afraid I have no experience.

translations.de: Ich habe leider keine Erfahrung.
translations.fr: Je crains de ne pas avoir d'expérience.
translations.pt: Infelizmente, não tenho nenhuma experiência.

examples.text: I have no one to play with.

translations.de: Ich habe niemanden zum Spielen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai personne avec qui jouer.
translations.pt: Eu não tenho ninguém com quem brincar.

more.definition: Without.; Like.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English no, na, from Old English nā, nō (“no, not, not ever, never”), from Proto-West Germanic *naiwō, from Proto-Germanic *naiwô (“never”), from *ne (“not”) + *aiwō (“ever”), equivalent to ne + aye.

examples.text: You're no longer a spring chicken.

translations.de: Du bist nicht mehr die Jüngste.
translations.fr: Tu n'es plus tout jeune.
translations.pt: Você não é mais tão jovem.

examples.text: There's no one in the classroom.

translations.de: Es ist niemand im Klassenzimmer.
translations.fr: Il n'y a personne dans la salle de classe.
translations.pt: Não há ninguém na sala de aula.

examples.text: I'm no longer angry at you.

translations.de: Ich bin dir nicht mehr böse.
translations.fr: Je ne suis plus en colère après toi.
translations.pt: Não estou mais bravo com você.

examples.text: There was no one on the beach.

translations.de: Es war niemand am Strand.
translations.fr: Il n'y avait personne sur la plage.
translations.pt: Não tinha ninguém na praia.

more.definition: To say “no”.; To answer with “no”; to decline, reject.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English no, na, from Old English nā, nō (“no, not, not ever, never”), from Proto-West Germanic *naiwō, from Proto-Germanic *naiwô (“never”), from *ne (“not”) + *aiwō (“ever”), equivalent to ne + aye.

examples.text: Do not forsake me, oh my darling.

translations.de: Verlass mich nicht, mein Schatz!
translations.fr: Ne m'abandonne pas, oh ma chérie.
translations.pt: Não me abandones, oh meu querido.

examples.text: This is not a very good example.

translations.de: Das ist kein sehr gutes Beispiel.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas un très bon exemple.
translations.pt: Isto não é um exemplo muito bom.

examples.text: Translation is an art, not a science.

translations.de: Das Übersetzen ist eine Kunst, keine Wissenschaft.
translations.fr: La traduction est un art, et non pas une science.
translations.pt: A tradução é uma arte, não uma ciência.

examples.text: I do not want to stay here.

translations.de: Ich will nicht hierbleiben.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas rester ici.
translations.pt: Eu não quero ficar aqui.

more.definition: Negates the meaning of the modified verb.; To no degree.; Used to indicate the opposite or near opposite, often in a form of understatement.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-osinflu. From Middle English not, nat, a variant of noght, naht (“not, nothing”), from Old English *nōht, nāht (“nought, nothing”), shortening of nōwiht, nāwiht (“nothing”, literally “not anything”), from Proto-West Germanic *naiwwiht, corresponding to ne (“not”) + ōwiht, āwiht (“anything”), corresponding to ā (“ever, always”) + wiht (“thing, creature”).

examples.text: The knight does not move like that.

translations.de: Der Springer bewegt sich nicht so.
translations.fr: Le cavalier ne se déplace pas comme ça.
translations.pt: O cavalo não se move assim.

examples.text: That word's not in my dictionary.

translations.de: Dieses Wort ist nicht in meinem Wörterbuch.
translations.fr: Ce mot n'est pas dans mon dictionnaire.
translations.pt: Essa palavra não está no meu dicionário.

examples.text: Brazil is not far away from Argentina.

translations.de: Brasilien ist nicht weit von Argentinien.
translations.fr: Le Brésil n'est pas loin de l'Argentine.
translations.pt: O Brasil fica perto da Argentina.

examples.text: My life does not belong to me.

translations.de: Mein Leben gehört mir nicht.
translations.fr: Ma vie ne m'appartient pas.
translations.pt: Minha vida não me pertence.

more.definition: And not.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-osinflu. From Middle English not, nat, a variant of noght, naht (“not, nothing”), from Old English *nōht, nāht (“nought, nothing”), shortening of nōwiht, nāwiht (“nothing”, literally “not anything”), from Proto-West Germanic *naiwwiht, corresponding to ne (“not”) + ōwiht, āwiht (“anything”), corresponding to ā (“ever, always”) + wiht (“thing, creature”).

examples.text: It seems I'm not wanted here.

translations.de: Es scheint, dass sie mich hier nicht haben wollen.
translations.fr: On dirait qu'ils ne veulent pas de moi ici.
translations.pt: Parece que não me querem aqui.

examples.text: I spoke but I was not heard.

translations.de: Ich sprach, aber ich wurde nicht gehört.
translations.fr: J'ai parlé, mais je n'ai pas été entendu.
translations.pt: Eu falei, mas não fui ouvido.

examples.text: I'm not going to wait forever.

translations.de: Ich werde nicht ewig warten.
translations.fr: Je ne vais pas attendre éternellement.
translations.pt: Não vou esperar para sempre.

examples.text: I am not ninety years old yet.

translations.de: Ich bin noch nicht neunzig Jahre alt.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas encore quatre-vingt-dix ans.
translations.pt: Ainda não tenho noventa anos.

more.definition: Used to indicate that the previous phrase was meant sarcastically or ironically.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-osinflu. From Middle English not, nat, a variant of noght, naht (“not, nothing”), from Old English *nōht, nāht (“nought, nothing”), shortening of nōwiht, nāwiht (“nothing”, literally “not anything”), from Proto-West Germanic *naiwwiht, corresponding to ne (“not”) + ōwiht, āwiht (“anything”), corresponding to ā (“ever, always”) + wiht (“thing, creature”).

examples.text: These girls are not speaking but singing.

translations.de: Diese Mädchen sprechen nicht, sondern singen.
translations.fr: Ces filles ne parlent pas mais chantent.
translations.pt: Estas meninas não estão falando, mas cantando.

examples.text: The baths are not in the forum.

translations.de: Die Bäder sind nicht im Forum.
translations.fr: Les bains ne sont pas dans le forum.
translations.pt: Os banhos não ficam no fórum.

examples.text: Are you going to answer or not?

translations.de: Willst du antworten oder nicht?
translations.fr: Est-ce que tu veux répondre ou non ?
translations.pt: Você vai responder ou não?

examples.text: That's not something that you forget.

translations.de: Das ist etwas Unvergessliches.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas quelque chose qu'on oublie.
translations.pt: Isso não é algo que se possa esquecer.

more.definition: An instance of using the word "not"; a negation or denial.; Alternative letter-case form of NOT (“unary operation on logical values that changes true to false, and false to true”).
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-osinflu.
