From Middle English not, nat, a variant of noght, naht (“not, nothing”), from Old English *nōht, nāht (“nought, nothing”), shortening of nōwiht, nāwiht (“nothing”, literally “not anything”), from Proto-West Germanic *naiwwiht, corresponding to ne (“not”) + ōwiht, āwiht (“anything”), corresponding to ā (“ever, always”) + wiht (“thing, creature”).

examples.text: Every morning I drink coffee with milk.

translations.de: Jeden Morgen trinke ich Kaffee mit Milch.
translations.fr: Chaque matin, je bois du café avec du lait.
translations.pt: Todas as manhãs tomo café com leite.

examples.text: The boy plays with the wooden horse.

translations.de: Der Junge spielt mit dem Holzpferd.
translations.fr: Le garçon joue avec le cheval de bois.
translations.pt: O menino brinca com o cavalo de pau.

examples.text: Don't be so harsh with her.

translations.de: Seien Sie nicht so streng mit ihr.
translations.fr: Ne soyez pas si dur avec elle.
translations.pt: Não seja tão duro com ela.

examples.text: Teachers need to be patient with children.

translations.de: Lehrer müssen geduldig mit Kindern sein.
translations.fr: Les enseignants doivent être patients avec les enfants.
translations.pt: Os professores precisam ser pacientes com as crianças.

more.definition: Along, together with others, in a group, etc.
more.etymology: From Middle English with, from Old English wiþ (“against, opposite, toward, with”), from Proto-West Germanic *wiþi, a shortened form of Proto-Germanic *wiþrą (“against”).

examples.text: I came wanting to be with you.

translations.de: Ich bin gekommen, weil ich bei dir sein wollte.
translations.fr: Je suis venu ici pour rester avec toi.
translations.pt: Eu vim querendo estar com você.

examples.text: You think differently talking with little children.

translations.de: Wir denken anders, wenn wir mit kleinen Kindern sprechen.
translations.fr: On pense différemment en parlant avec des petits enfants.
translations.pt: Você pensa de maneira diferente falando com crianças pequenas.

examples.text: She drinks tea with a little milk.

translations.de: Sie trinkt Tee mit etwas Milch.
translations.fr: Elle boit du thé avec un peu de lait.
translations.pt: Ela bebe chá com um pouco de leite.

examples.text: The baby is playing with the cat.

translations.de: Das Baby spielt mit der Katze.
translations.fr: Le bébé joue avec le chat.
translations.pt: O bebê está brincando com o gato.

more.definition: Against.; In the company of; alongside, close to; near to.; In addition to; as an accessory to.
more.etymology: From Middle English with, from Old English wiþ (“against, opposite, toward, with”), from Proto-West Germanic *wiþi, a shortened form of Proto-Germanic *wiþrą (“against”).

examples.text: The telephone rang, but no one answered.

translations.de: Das Telefon klingelte, doch es nahm niemand ab.
translations.fr: Le téléphone a sonné, mais personne n'a répondu.
translations.pt: O telefone tocou, mas ninguém atendeu.

examples.text: I like broccoli, but I hate cauliflower.

translations.de: Broccoli mag ich, aber ich hasse Blumenkohl.
translations.fr: J'aime le brocoli, mais je déteste le chou-fleur.
translations.pt: Eu gosto de brócolis, mas detesto couve-flor.

examples.text: I'm sorry, but you're wrong.

translations.de: Ich bedauere, aber Sie irren sich.
translations.fr: Je suis désolé, mais tu as tort.
translations.pt: Lamento, mas não tens razão.

examples.text: The bus stopped, but nobody got off.

translations.de: Der Bus hielt, doch niemand stieg aus.
translations.fr: Le bus s'est arrêté, mais personne n'est descendu.
translations.pt: O ônibus parou, mas ninguém desembarcou.

more.definition: Merely, only, just, no more than.; Though, however.; Used to repeat an adverb for emphasis; simply; just; absolutely.
more.etymology: From Middle English but, buten, boute, bouten, from Old English būtan (“without, outside of, except, only”), from Proto-West Germanic *biūtan, *biūtini, equivalent to be- + out.

examples.text: Winning is temporary, but learning is forever.

translations.de: Der Sieg ist vorübergehend, aber das Lernen ist für immer.
translations.fr: La victoire est temporaire, mais l'apprentissage est éternel.
translations.pt: Vencer é temporário, mas aprender é para sempre.

examples.text: The meal was excellent but very expensive.

translations.de: Das Essen war ausgezeichnet, aber sehr teuer.
translations.fr: Le repas était excellent mais très cher.
translations.pt: A refeição foi excelente, mas muito cara.

examples.text: I tripped, but I didn't fall.

translations.de: Ich bin gestolpert, aber nicht gefallen.
translations.fr: J'ai trébuché, mais je ne suis pas tombé.
translations.pt: Eu tropecei mas não caí.

examples.text: I'm nothing but a poor peasant.

translations.de: Ich bin nur ein armer Bauer.
translations.fr: Je ne suis qu'un pauvre paysan.
translations.pt: Eu não sou nada mais que um pobre camponês.

more.definition: However, although, nevertheless, on the other hand (introducing a clause contrary to prior belief or in contrast with the preceding clause or sentence).; On the contrary, rather (as a regular adversative conjunction, introducing a word or clause in contrast or contradiction with the preceding negative clause or sentence).; Used at the beginning of a sentence to express opposition to a remark.
more.etymology: From Middle English but, buten, boute, bouten, from Old English būtan (“without, outside of, except, only”), from Proto-West Germanic *biūtan, *biūtini, equivalent to be- + out.

examples.text: Eat what you are served, no buts about it.

translations.de: Iss, was man dir serviert hat, keine Widerrede.
translations.fr: Ne te plains pas et mange ce qu'on te donne.
translations.pt: Coma o que lhe for servido, sem discussões a esse respeito.

examples.text: Tom does that, but Mary doesn't.

translations.de: Tom macht das, aber Maria nicht.
translations.fr: Tom fait ça, mais pas Marie.
translations.pt: Tom faz isso, mas Mary não faz.

examples.text: Tom did that not once, but twice.

translations.de: Tom hat das nicht ein-, sondern zweimal getan.
translations.fr: Tom ne l'a pas fait une fois mais deux fois.
translations.pt: Tom fez isso não uma vez, mas duas.

examples.text: John makes music, but doesn't sing.

translations.de: Johannes macht Musik, singt aber nicht.
translations.fr: Jean fait de la musique, mais ne chante pas.
translations.pt: O Jean faz música, mas não canta.

more.definition: An instance of using the word "but"; an objection or caveat.; The outer room of a small two-room cottage.; A limit; a boundary.
more.etymology: From Middle English but, buten, boute, bouten, from Old English būtan (“without, outside of, except, only”), from Proto-West Germanic *biūtan, *biūtini, equivalent to be- + out.

examples.text: She doesn't need sympathy, but support.

translations.de: Sie braucht kein Mitleid, sondern Unterstützung.
translations.fr: Elle n'a pas besoin de compassion, mais de soutien.
translations.pt: Ela não precisa de compaixão, mas sim de apoio.

examples.text: Envious people die, but envy never does.

translations.de: Die Neider sterben, der Neid nie.
translations.fr: Les envieux meurent, mais l’envie, jamais.
translations.pt: Os invejosos morrem, mas nunca a inveja.

examples.text: Memory fades but the written word remains.

translations.de: Die Erinnerung verblasst, doch das geschriebene Wort bleibt bestehen.
translations.fr: La mémoire s'estompe mais les écrits restent.
translations.pt: Memórias se vão, mas palavras escritas permanecem.

examples.text: I see yours, but where are mine?

translations.de: Ich sehe deine, aber wo sind meine?
translations.fr: Je vois les tiennes, mais où sont les miennes ?
translations.pt: Vejo o seu, mas onde está o meu?

more.definition: Apart from, except (for), excluding.; Outside of.
more.etymology: From Middle English but, buten, boute, bouten, from Old English būtan (“without, outside of, except, only”), from Proto-West Germanic *biūtan, *biūtini, equivalent to be- + out.

examples.text: Thank you, but I'm not interested.

translations.de: Danke, aber ich bin nicht interessiert.
translations.fr: Merci, mais je ne suis pas intéressé.
translations.pt: Obrigado, mas não tenho interesse.

examples.text: Eat what you are served, no buts about it.

translations.de: Iss, was man dir serviert hat, keine Widerrede.
translations.fr: Ne te plains pas et mange ce qu'on te donne.
translations.pt: Coma o que lhe for servido, sem discussões a esse respeito.

examples.text: I want one, but not this one.

translations.de: Ich will eins, aber nicht dieses.
translations.fr: J'en veux un, mais pas celui-ci.
translations.pt: Eu quero um, mas não esse.

examples.text: I want to, but I can't.

translations.de: Ich würde, aber ich kann nicht.
translations.fr: Je veux mais je ne peux pas.
translations.pt: Eu quero, mas não posso.

more.etymology: From Middle English but, buten, boute, bouten, from Old English būtan (“without, outside of, except, only”), from Proto-West Germanic *biūtan, *biūtini, equivalent to be- + out.

examples.text: We need to start all over again.

translations.de: Wir müssen ganz von vorne anfangen.
translations.fr: Il faut tout recommencer.
translations.pt: Temos que começar tudo de novo.

examples.text: She is pressing all the phone buttons.

translations.de: Sie drückt alle Tasten am Telefon.
translations.fr: Elle appuie sur tous les boutons du téléphone.
translations.pt: Ela está pressionando todas as teclas do telefone.

examples.text: The ship sank with all the crew.

translations.de: Das Schiff sank mit der gesamten Besatzung.
translations.fr: Le bateau a coulé avec tout l'équipage.
translations.pt: O navio afundou com toda a tripulação.

examples.text: We didn't expect that at all.

translations.de: Damit haben wir überhaupt nicht gerechnet.
translations.fr: On ne s'attendait pas du tout à ça.
translations.pt: Não esperávamos isso de forma alguma.

more.etymology: From Middle English all, from Old English eall, from Proto-West Germanic *all, from Proto-Germanic *allaz, of uncertain origin but perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *h₂el- (“all”).

examples.text: We're all vegetarian in my family.

translations.de: Wir sind alle Vegetarier in meiner Familie.
translations.fr: Nous sommes tous végétariens dans ma famille.
translations.pt: Somos todos vegetarianos em minha família.

examples.text: The soldiers were all wearing gas masks.

translations.de: Die Soldaten trugen alle Gasmasken.
translations.fr: Les soldats portaient tous des masques à gaz.
translations.pt: Os soldados estavam todos usando máscaras de gás.

examples.text: What does he think about all this?

translations.de: Was hält er von all dem?
translations.fr: Que pense-t-il de tout ça ?
translations.pt: O que ele pensa sobre tudo isso?

examples.text: Clothes were strewn all over the floor.

translations.de: Überall auf dem Boden lagen Kleidungsstücke herum.
translations.fr: Des vêtements étaient éparpillés sur le sol.
translations.pt: As roupas estavam espalhadas por todo o chão.

more.definition: Wholly; entirely; completely; totally.; Apiece; each.; So much; used with "the" and a comparative.
more.etymology: From Middle English all, from Old English eall, from Proto-West Germanic *all, from Proto-Germanic *allaz, of uncertain origin but perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *h₂el- (“all”).

examples.text: I think that they were all fired.

translations.de: Die sind, glaube ich, alle entlassen worden.
translations.fr: Je crois qu'ils ont tous été virés.
translations.pt: Eu acho que foram todos demitidos.

examples.text: I think about this all the time.

translations.de: Ich denke ständig daran.
translations.fr: J'y pense tout le temps.
translations.pt: Eu penso sobre isto o tempo todo.

examples.text: Men talk about women all the time.

translations.de: Männer sprechen andauernd über Frauen.
translations.fr: Les hommes parlent des femmes tout le temps.
translations.pt: Homens falam sobre mulheres o tempo todo.

examples.text: I know all your songs by heart.

translations.de: Ich kenne alle Ihre Lieder auswendig.
translations.fr: Je connais toutes vos chansons par cœur.
translations.pt: Eu sei de cor todas as suas músicas.

more.etymology: From Middle English all, from Old English eall, from Proto-West Germanic *all, from Proto-Germanic *allaz, of uncertain origin but perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *h₂el- (“all”).

examples.text: We all think that we're unique.

translations.de: Wir alle halten uns für einzigartig.
translations.fr: Nous pensons tous être uniques.
translations.pt: Todos pensamos que somos únicos.

examples.text: We should stay in Boston all summer.

translations.de: Wir sollten den ganzen Sommer über in Boston bleiben.
translations.fr: On devrait rester à Boston tout l'été.
translations.pt: Devemos ficar em Boston durante todo o verão.

examples.text: I'm glad you're all here.

translations.de: Ich bin froh, dass ihr alle hier seid.
translations.fr: Je suis content que vous soyez toutes là.
translations.pt: Fico contente de que vocês estejam todos aqui.

examples.text: May God have mercy on us all.

translations.de: Möge Gott uns allen gnädig sein!
translations.fr: Que Dieu ait pitié de nous.
translations.pt: Que Deus tenha piedade de todos nós.

more.definition: Every individual or anything of the given class, with no exceptions (the noun or noun phrase denoting the class must be plural or uncountable).; Throughout the whole of (a stated period of time; generally used with units of a day or longer).; Only; alone; nothing but.
more.etymology: From Middle English all, from Old English eall, from Proto-West Germanic *all, from Proto-Germanic *allaz, of uncertain origin but perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *h₂el- (“all”).

examples.text: That was the mother of all battles.

translations.de: Das war die Mutter aller Schlachten.
translations.fr: C'était la mère de toutes les batailles.
translations.pt: Aquela foi a mãe de todas as batalhas.

examples.text: We use the Internet all the time.

translations.de: Wir nutzen ständig das Internet.
translations.fr: Nous utilisons l'Internet tout le temps.
translations.pt: Usamos a Internet o tempo todo.

examples.text: Did you already forget all of it?

translations.de: Hast du das alles schon vergessen?
translations.fr: Tu as déjà oublié tout ça ?
translations.pt: Já se esqueceu de tudo?

examples.text: Information processing permeates all aspects of life.

translations.de: Die Informationsverarbeitung durchdringt alle Aspekte des Lebens.
translations.fr: Le traitement de l'information imprègne tous les aspects de la vie.
translations.pt: O processamento de informações permeia todos os aspectos da vida.

more.definition: Everything that one is capable of.; The totality of one's possessions.; Everything in general; all that matters.
more.etymology: From Middle English all, from Old English eall, from Proto-West Germanic *all, from Proto-Germanic *allaz, of uncertain origin but perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *h₂el- (“all”).

examples.text: Tom has been watching TV all day.

translations.de: Tom sieht schon den ganzen Tag fern.
translations.fr: Tom a regardé la télé toute la journée.
translations.pt: Tom tem assistido televisão o dia todo.

examples.text: I never wanted all this to happen.

translations.de: Ich habe nie gewollt, dass all dies geschieht.
translations.fr: Je n'ai jamais voulu que tout ça arrive.
translations.pt: Eu nunca quis que tudo isto acontecesse.

examples.text: I don't like him at all.

translations.de: Ich mag ihn überhaupt nicht.
translations.fr: Je ne l'aime pas du tout.
translations.pt: Eu não gosto nada dele.

examples.text: It's all you can really do.

translations.de: Mehr kannst du nicht wirklich tun.
translations.fr: C'est tout ce que tu peux vraiment faire.
translations.pt: É tudo o que você pode realmente fazer.

more.definition: Everything.; Everyone.; The only thing(s).
more.etymology: From Middle English all, from Old English eall, from Proto-West Germanic *all, from Proto-Germanic *allaz, of uncertain origin but perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *h₂el- (“all”).

examples.text: Why are you so obsessed with cars?

translations.de: Warum bist du so besessen von Autos?
translations.fr: Pourquoi es-tu autant obsédé par les voitures?
translations.pt: Por que você é obcecado com carros?

examples.text: Why does he hate you so much?

translations.de: Warum hasst er dich so sehr?
translations.fr: Pourquoi te déteste-t-il autant ?
translations.pt: Por que ele odeia tanto você?

examples.text: Are there always so many people here?

translations.de: Sind hier immer so viele Menschen?
translations.fr: Y a-t-il toujours autant de monde ici ?
translations.pt: Sempre há muitas pessoas aqui?

examples.text: I'm sorry I'm so stupid.

translations.de: Es tut mit leid, dass ich so dumm bin.
translations.fr: Désolé d'être si stupide.
translations.pt: Peço desculpas por ser tão idiota.

more.definition: Agreeing with actual facts or reality; true.; In that state or manner; with that attribute. A proadjective that replaces the aforementioned adjective phrase.
more.etymology: From Middle English so, swo, zuo, swa, swe, from Old English swā, swǣ, swē (“so, as, the same, such, that”), from Proto-West Germanic *swā, from Proto-Germanic *swa, *swē (“so”), from Proto-Indo-European *swē, *swō (reflexive pronomial stem).

examples.text: Why's it so hot in here?

translations.de: Warum ist es hier drin so heiß?
translations.fr: Pourquoi fait-il si chaud ici ?
translations.pt: Por que é tão quente aqui?

examples.text: I don't like Tom so much.

translations.de: Ich mag Tom nicht sonderlich.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas beaucoup Tom.
translations.pt: Eu não gosto muito de Tom.

examples.text: Why does love make us so happy?

translations.de: Warum macht uns Liebe so glücklich?
translations.fr: Pourquoi l'amour nous rend-il si heureux ?
translations.pt: Por que o amor nos faz assim felizes?

examples.text: Why do you speak French so well?

translations.de: Warum sprichst du so gut Französisch?
translations.fr: Pourquoi parlez-vous si bien français ?
translations.pt: Por que você fala francês tão bem?

more.definition: To the (explicitly stated) extent.; To the (implied) extent.; Very (positive or negative clause).
more.etymology: From Middle English so, swo, zuo, swa, swe, from Old English swā, swǣ, swē (“so, as, the same, such, that”), from Proto-West Germanic *swā, from Proto-Germanic *swa, *swē (“so”), from Proto-Indo-European *swē, *swō (reflexive pronomial stem).

examples.text: Why do you like squirrels so much?

translations.de: Warum hast du Eichhörnchen so gern?
translations.fr: Pourquoi aimes-tu autant les écureuils ?
translations.pt: Por que gostas tanto de esquilos?

examples.text: I've never seen anything so beautiful.

translations.de: Ich habe noch nie so etwas Schönes gesehen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai jamais rien vu d'aussi beau.
translations.pt: Eu nunca vi nada tão bonito.

examples.text: There's so much more to learn.

translations.de: Es gibt noch so viel zu lernen.
translations.fr: Il y a tant à apprendre, encore.
translations.pt: Ainda há tanto que aprender.

examples.text: I'm learning so much from you.

translations.de: Ich lerne so viel von Ihnen.
translations.fr: J'apprends tant de vous.
translations.pt: Eu estou aprendendo tanto com você.

more.definition: As a result; for that reason; therefore; because of this; due to this.; Used to connect previous conversation or events to the following question.; Used to introduce a rhetorical question.
more.etymology: From Middle English so, swo, zuo, swa, swe, from Old English swā, swǣ, swē (“so, as, the same, such, that”), from Proto-West Germanic *swā, from Proto-Germanic *swa, *swē (“so”), from Proto-Indo-European *swē, *swō (reflexive pronomial stem).

examples.text: I have so many things to do.

translations.de: Ich habe so viel zu tun!
translations.fr: J'ai tant de choses à faire.
translations.pt: Tenho muitas coisas para fazer.

more.definition: A syllable used in solfège to represent the fifth note of a major scale.; Sometimes syllable for both the second and the fifth.; A type of dairy product, made especially in Japan between the seventh and tenth centuries, by reducing milk by boiling it.

translations.fr: Tom a demandé à Marie d'où elle vient.
translations.pt: Tom perguntou a Mary de onde ela era.

examples.text: Just between us, she's my girlfriend.

translations.de: Nur unter uns: sie ist meine Freundin.
translations.fr: Juste entre nous, c'est ma petite copine.
translations.pt: Cá entre nós, ela é minha namorada.

examples.text: My friend says that she's suicidal.

translations.de: Mein Freund sagt, sie sei suizidgefährdet.
translations.fr: Mon ami dit qu'elle est suicidaire.
translations.pt: Meu amigo diz que ela é suicida.

examples.text: If only she could see you now.

translations.de: Wenn sie dich doch jetzt nur sehen könnte!
translations.fr: Si seulement elle pouvait te voir, désormais.
translations.pt: Se ela pudesse te ver agora.

more.definition: To refer to (someone) using she/her pronouns.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English sche, scho, hyo, ȝho (“she”), whence also Yorkshire dialectal shoo (“she”), Scots she, sho (“she”). Probably from Old English hēo (whence dialectal English hoo), with an irregular change in stress from hēo to heō /hjoː/, then a development from /hj-/ to /ç/ to /ʃ-/, similar to the derivation of Shetland from Old Norse Hjaltland.

examples.text: I think that you look really great.

translations.de: Ich finde, du siehst großartig aus.
translations.fr: Je trouve que tu as l'air superbe.
translations.pt: Acho que você está realmente ótima.

examples.text: I think you're doing that wrong.

translations.de: Ich glaube, du machst das falsch.
translations.fr: Je pense que tu ne le fais pas comme il faut.
translations.pt: Acho que você está fazendo isso errado.

examples.text: I think Tom would've liked that.

translations.de: Ich glaube, Tom hätte das gefallen.
translations.fr: Je pense que Tom aurait apprécié.
translations.pt: Acho que o Tom teria gostado disso.

examples.text: I think you'll like the dessert.

translations.de: Der Nachtisch wird dir bestimmt schmecken.
translations.fr: Je pense que tu vas aimer le dessert.
translations.pt: Acho que você vai gostar da sobremesa.

more.definition: An act of thinking; consideration (of something).
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *teng-der. From Middle English thinken, thynken, thenken, thenchen, from Old English þenċan, from Proto-West Germanic *þankijan, from Proto-Germanic *þankijaną (“to think”), from Proto-Indo-European *teng- (“to think, feel, know”).

examples.text: I think it'll be sunny tomorrow.

translations.de: Ich glaube, morgen wird es sonnig.
translations.fr: Je pense qu'il fera beau demain.
translations.pt: Acho que amanhã estará ensolarado.

examples.text: Are you thinking about something in particular?

translations.de: Denkst du an etwas Bestimmtes?
translations.fr: Tu penses à quelque chose en particulier?
translations.pt: Você está pensando em algo em particular?

examples.text: Tom thinks he's stronger than me.

translations.de: Tom glaubt, er sei stärker als ich.
translations.fr: Tom pense qu'il est plus fort que moi.
translations.pt: Tom acha que é mais forte do que eu.

examples.text: I think now is the right time.

translations.de: Ich denke, jetzt ist der richtige Zeitpunkt.
translations.fr: Je pense que c'est le bon moment.
translations.pt: Acho que este é o momento oportuno.

examples.text: I often think of my family.

translations.de: Ich denke oft an meine Familie.
translations.fr: Je pense souvent à ma famille.
translations.pt: Eu penso muito na minha família.

examples.text: What do you think about this book?

translations.de: Was denkst du über dieses Buch?
translations.fr: Que penses-tu de ce livre ?
translations.pt: O que você pensa sobre este livro?

more.definition: To ponder, to go over in one's mind.; To have (some statement) in one's mind; to say to oneself mentally.; To communicate to oneself in one's mind, to try to find a solution to a problem.
collocations: think twice — to consider carefully first
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *teng-der. From Middle English thinken, thynken, thenken, thenchen, from Old English þenċan, from Proto-West Germanic *þankijan, from Proto-Germanic *þankijaną (“to think”), from Proto-Indo-European *teng- (“to think, feel, know”).

examples.text: Tom would help us if he could.

translations.de: Tom würde uns helfen, wenn er könnte.
translations.fr: Tom nous aiderait s'il le pouvait.
translations.pt: O Tom nos ajudaria se pudesse.

examples.text: I wonder if Tom still remembers me.

translations.de: Ich frage mich, ob Tom sich noch an mich erinnert.
translations.fr: Je me demande si Tom se souvient encore de moi.
translations.pt: Será que Tom ainda se lembra de mim?

examples.text: You can sleep here if you want.

translations.de: Wenn du willst, kannst du hier schlafen.
translations.fr: Tu peux dormir ici si tu veux.
translations.pt: Você pode dormir aqui, se quiser.

examples.text: Tom asked me if I was hungry.

translations.de: Tom fragte mich, ob ich hungrig sei.
translations.fr: Tom me demanda si j'avais faim.
translations.pt: Tom me perguntou se eu estava com fome.

more.definition: Supposing that, assuming that, in the circumstances that; suppositive used to introduce a condition that may be (or prove to be) either true or false.; A keyword that invokes conditional processing: in the event that a given condition is true, execute the given statement(s) (otherwise execute other statements).; Supposing that; used with past or past perfect subjunctive to indicate a counterfactual or hypothetical condition.
more.etymology: From Middle English if, yif, yef, from Old English ġif (“if”), from Proto-West Germanic *jabu, *jabē, from Proto-Germanic *jabai (“when, if”). Cognate with Scots gif (“if, whether”), Saterland Frisian af, of (“if, whether”), West Frisian oft (“whether”), Dutch of (“or, whether, but”), Middle Low German ef, if, af, of ("if; whether"; > German Low German of), German ob (“if, whether”), Icelandic ef (“if”).

examples.text: I wonder if you're truly happy.

translations.de: Ich frage mich, ob du wirklich glücklich bist.
translations.fr: Je me demande si tu es vraiment heureux.
translations.pt: Será que vocês são mesmo felizes?

examples.text: She asked if I need a taxi.

translations.de: Sie fragte, ob ich ein Taxi brauche.
translations.fr: Elle demanda si j'avais besoin d'un taxi.
translations.pt: Ela perguntou se eu preciso de um táxi.

examples.text: Tom asked me if I were hungry.

translations.de: Tom fragte mich, ob ich hungrig sei.
translations.fr: Tom me demanda si j'avais faim.
translations.pt: Tom me perguntou se eu estava com fome.

examples.text: Mary wondered if Tom really loved her.

translations.de: Maria fragte sich, ob Tom sie wohl wirklich liebhabe.
translations.fr: Marie se demandait si Tom l'aimait vraiment.
translations.pt: Mary se perguntava se o Tom realmente a amava.

more.definition: An uncertainty, possibility, condition, doubt etc.
more.etymology: From Middle English if, yif, yef, from Old English ġif (“if”), from Proto-West Germanic *jabu, *jabē, from Proto-Germanic *jabai (“when, if”). Cognate with Scots gif (“if, whether”), Saterland Frisian af, of (“if, whether”), West Frisian oft (“whether”), Dutch of (“or, whether, but”), Middle Low German ef, if, af, of ("if; whether"; > German Low German of), German ob (“if, whether”), Icelandic ef (“if”).

examples.text: If anything happens, call me right away.

translations.de: Ruf mich sofort an, wenn etwas passiert.
translations.fr: S'il arrive quoi que ce soit, appelle-moi tout de suite.
translations.pt: Se acontecer alguma coisa, me ligue imediatamente.

examples.text: I can't do it right now.

translations.de: Ich kann es im Moment nicht tun.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas le faire maintenant.
translations.pt: Não posso fazer isso agora.

examples.text: You have the right to remain silent.

translations.de: Sie haben das Recht zu schweigen.
translations.fr: Vous avez le droit de garder le silence.
translations.pt: Você tem o direito de permanecer calado.

examples.text: We have to do this right away.

translations.de: Wir müssen das sofort erledigen.
translations.fr: Nous devons le faire sur-le-champ.
translations.pt: Temos de fazer isto imediatamente.

more.definition: Designating the side of the body which is positioned to the east if one is facing north, the side on which the heart is not located in most humans. This arrow points to the reader's right: →; Clockwise, particularly when describing a change in direction or orientation.; Complying with justice, correctness, or reason; correct, just, true. See also the interjection senses below.
more.etymology: From Middle English reȝt, right, righte, riht, riȝt, riȝte, ryght, ryȝt, from Old English reht, reoht, rieht, riht, ryht (“right,” also the word for “straight” and “direct”), from Proto-West Germanic *reht, from Proto-Germanic *rehtaz (“right, straight; just, morally upright”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃reǵtós (“right, straightened”), from *h₃reǵ- (“to straighten; to righten”).

examples.text: My house is right across the street.

translations.de: Mein Haus befindet sich direkt gegenüber.
translations.fr: Ma maison est juste de l'autre côté de la rue.
translations.pt: Minha casa é bem do outro lado da rua.

examples.text: That's the right thing to do.

translations.de: Es ist das Richtige.
translations.fr: C'est la bonne chose à faire.
translations.pt: Esta é a coisa certa a fazer.

examples.text: I personally believe that you're right.

translations.de: Ich persönlich glaube, dass du recht hast.
translations.fr: Je crois personnellement que tu as raison.
translations.pt: Eu pessoalmente creio que você está certo.

examples.text: Arabic is read from right to left.

translations.de: Arabisch wird von rechts nach links gelesen.
translations.fr: L'arabe se lit de droite à gauche.
translations.pt: O árabe se lê da direita para a esquerda.

more.definition: On the right side.; Towards the right side.; Exactly, precisely.
more.etymology: From Middle English right, righte, from Old English rihte, rehte (“right; rightly; due; directly; straight”), from Proto-Germanic *rehta, from *rehtaz (“right; straight”).

examples.text: I'm not very hungry right now.

translations.de: Ich bin im Moment nicht besonders hungrig.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas très faim à l'instant.
translations.pt: Eu não estou com muita fome neste exato momento.

examples.text: I think you did the right thing.

translations.de: Ich denke, du hast das Richtige getan.
translations.fr: Je pense que tu as fait la chose qu'il fallait.
translations.pt: Eu acho que você fez a coisa certa.

examples.text: I think Tom and Mary are right.

translations.de: Ich finde, Tom und Maria haben recht.
translations.fr: Je pense que Tom et Mary ont raison.
translations.pt: Eu acho que Tom e Maria estão certos.

examples.text: I think I did the right thing.

translations.de: Ich glaube, das Richtige getan zu haben.
translations.fr: Je crois que j'ai fait ce qu'il fallait faire.
translations.pt: Eu acho que fiz a coisa certa.

more.definition: Yes, that is correct; I agree.; I have listened to what you just said and I acknowledge your assertion or opinion, regardless of whether I agree with it (opinion) or can verify it (assertion).; Signpost word to change the subject in a discussion or discourse.
more.etymology: From Middle English right, righte, from Old English rihte, rehte (“right; rightly; due; directly; straight”), from Proto-Germanic *rehta, from *rehtaz (“right; straight”).

examples.text: I have to do what's right.

translations.de: Ich muss das Richtige tun.
translations.fr: Il me faut faire ce qui convient.
translations.pt: Eu preciso fazer o que é certo.

examples.text: This is the right thing to do.

translations.de: Es ist das Richtige.
translations.fr: C'est la bonne chose à faire.
translations.pt: Esta é a coisa certa a fazer.

examples.text: Tom is the boy on the right.

translations.de: Tom ist der Junge rechts.
translations.fr: Tom est le garçon sur la droite.
translations.pt: Tom é o garoto à direita.

examples.text: You had no right to do that.

translations.de: Du hattest kein Recht, das zu tun.
translations.fr: Tu n'avais aucun droit de faire ça.
translations.pt: Não tinhas o direito de fazer isso.

more.definition: That which complies with justice, law or reason.; A legal, just or moral entitlement.; The right side or direction.
more.etymology: From Middle English right, from Old English riht, reht, ġeriht (“that which is right, just, or proper”), from Proto-West Germanic *reht, from Proto-Germanic *rehtą (“a right”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃reǵtom, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃reǵt- (“to straighten; direct”). Cognate with Dutch recht (“a right; privilege”), German Recht (“a right”), Danish ret (“a right”).

examples.text: I personally believe that you are right.

translations.de: Ich persönlich glaube, dass du recht hast.
translations.fr: Je crois personnellement que tu as raison.
translations.pt: Particularmente, creio que você esteja certo.

examples.text: Eventually, his rights had to be acknowledged.

translations.de: Letzten Endes mussten seine Rechte anerkannt werden.
translations.fr: À la fin, ses droits ont dû être reconnus.
translations.pt: Finalmente, os direitos dele tiveram de ser reconhecidos.

examples.text: Is Tom left-handed or right-handed?

translations.de: Ist Tom Links- oder Rechtshänder?
translations.fr: Tom est-il gaucher ou droitier ?
translations.pt: Tom é canhoto ou destro?

examples.text: It's a privilege, not a right.

translations.de: Es ist ein Privileg, kein Recht.
translations.fr: C'est un privilège, non un droit.
translations.pt: É um privilégio, não um direito.

more.definition: To correct.; To set upright.; To return to normal upright position.
more.etymology: From Middle English righten, reghten, riȝten, from Old English rihtan, ġerihtan (“to straighten, judge, set upright, set right”), from Proto-West Germanic *rihtijan, from Proto-Germanic *rihtijaną (“to straighten; rectify; judge”).

examples.text: No, nobody wants to hear you sing.

translations.de: Nein, niemand will Sie singen hören.
translations.fr: Non, personne ne veut t'entendre chanter.
translations.pt: Não, ninguém quer te ouvir cantar.

examples.text: Do you want to be my wife?

translations.de: Willst du meine Frau werden?
translations.fr: Veux-tu devenir ma femme ?
translations.pt: Quer ser minha mulher?

examples.text: I want to pay by credit card.

translations.de: Ich will mit Kreditkarte bezahlen.
translations.fr: Je veux payer par carte de crédit.
translations.pt: Quero pagar com cartão de crédito.

examples.text: We don't want to take sides.

translations.de: Wir wollen keine Partei ergreifen.
translations.fr: Nous ne voulons pas prendre parti.
translations.pt: Não queremos tomar partido.

more.definition: A desire, wish, longing.; Lack, absence, deficiency.; Poverty.
more.etymology: Old Norse vantabor. From Middle English wanten (“to lack, to need”), from Old Norse vanta (“to lack”), from Proto-Germanic *wanatōną (“to be wanting, lack”), from *wanô (“lack, deficiency”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁weh₂- (“empty”). Cognate with Middle High German wan (“not full, empty”), Middle Dutch wan (“empty, poor”), Old English wana (“want, lack, absence, deficiency”), Latin vanus (“empty”). See wan, wan-.

examples.text: I want to sing and to dance.

translations.de: Ich möchte singen und tanzen.
translations.fr: Je veux chanter et danser.
translations.pt: Eu quero cantar e dançar.

examples.text: The cat wants to catch the mouse.

translations.de: Die Katze will die Maus fangen.
translations.fr: Le chat veut attraper la souris.
translations.pt: O gato quer pegar o rato.

examples.text: He really wanted to dance with her.

translations.de: Er wollte sehr gerne mit ihr tanzen.
translations.fr: Il voulait vraiment danser avec elle.
translations.pt: Ele queria muito dançar com ela.

examples.text: Do you want to visit this monument?

translations.de: Möchten Sie dieses Denkmal besuchen?
translations.fr: Ça te dit de visiter ce monument ?
translations.pt: Você quer visitar este monumento?

more.definition: To wish for or desire (something); to feel a need or desire for; to crave, hanker, or demand.; To make it easy or tempting to do something undesirable, or to make it hard or challenging to refrain from doing it.; To wish, desire, or demand to see, have the presence of or do business with.
more.etymology: Old Norse vantabor. From Middle English wanten (“to lack, to need”), from Old Norse vanta (“to lack”), from Proto-Germanic *wanatōną (“to be wanting, lack”), from *wanô (“lack, deficiency”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁weh₂- (“empty”). Cognate with Middle High German wan (“not full, empty”), Middle Dutch wan (“empty, poor”), Old English wana (“want, lack, absence, deficiency”), Latin vanus (“empty”). See wan, wan-.

examples.text: The genie is out of the bottle.

translations.de: Der Geist ist aus der Flasche.
translations.fr: Le génie est hors de la bouteille.
translations.pt: O gênio está fora da garrafa.

examples.text: When did you find out the truth?

translations.de: Wann bist du hinter die Wahrheit gekommen?
translations.fr: Quand as-tu découvert la vérité ?
translations.pt: Quando você descobriu a verdade?

examples.text: I didn't feel like going out.

translations.de: Ich hatte keine Lust auszugehen.
translations.fr: Je n'avais pas envie de sortir.
translations.pt: Eu não estava a fim de sair.

examples.text: Tom has been kicked out of school.

translations.de: Thomas wurde der Schule verwiesen.
translations.fr: Tom a été expulsé de son école.
translations.pt: Tom foi expulso da escola.

more.definition: Not inside or within a place, especially a place that someone or something was formerly inside or is customarily inside; Not at home, or not at one's office or place of employment.; Not in jail, prison, or captivity; freed from confinement.
more.etymology: From Middle English out, oute, from a combination of Old English ūt (“out”, preposition & adverb), from Proto-West Germanic *ūt, from Proto-Germanic *ūt (“out”); and Old English ūte (“outside; without”, adverb), from Proto-Germanic *ūtai (“out; outside”); both from Proto-Indo-European *úd (“upwards, away”).

examples.text: You missed out on a great party!

translations.de: Du hast eine tolle Party versäumt!
translations.fr: Tu as raté une super fête !
translations.pt: Você perdeu uma festa e tanto!

examples.text: Take your hand out of your pocket!

translations.de: Nimm deine Hand aus der Hosentasche!
translations.fr: Sortez la main de votre poche !
translations.pt: Tire as mãos do bolso!

examples.text: I want to find out what happened.

translations.de: Ich möchte rausbekommen, was los war.
translations.fr: Je veux découvrir ce qui s'est passé.
translations.pt: Quero descobrir o que aconteceu.

examples.text: What are you doing out of bed?

translations.de: Was machst du außerhalb des Bettes?
translations.fr: Que fais-tu hors du lit ?
translations.pt: O que você está fazendo fora da cama?

more.definition: Away from the inside or centre.; Away from, or at a distance from, some point of reference or focus.; Specifically, away from home or one's usual place.
more.etymology: From Middle English out, oute, from a combination of Old English ūt (“out”, preposition & adverb), from Proto-West Germanic *ūt, from Proto-Germanic *ūt (“out”); and Old English ūte (“outside; without”, adverb), from Proto-Germanic *ūtai (“out; outside”); both from Proto-Indo-European *úd (“upwards, away”).

examples.text: I want to go out with her.

translations.de: Ich will mit ihr ausgehen.
translations.fr: Je veux sortir avec elle.
translations.pt: Quero sair com ela.

examples.text: I had to find out for myself.

translations.de: Ich musste es selber rausbekommen.
translations.fr: J'ai dû le découvrir tout seul.
translations.pt: Eu tive de descobrir por mim mesmo.

examples.text: Poke the fire. It's going out.

translations.de: Schüre das Feuer! Es ist dabei auszugehen.
translations.fr: Tisonne le feu. Il s'éteint.
translations.pt: Atice o fogo. Está se apagando.

examples.text: Lock the door when you go out.

translations.de: Schließe die Tür ab, wenn du aus dem Haus gehst!
translations.fr: Fermez la porte à clé quand vous sortez.
translations.pt: Tranque a porta quando sair.

more.definition: A radio procedure word meaning that the station is finished with its transmission and does not expect a response.; Used as a brusque or dramatic farewell; Get out; begone; away!
more.etymology: From Middle English out, oute, from a combination of Old English ūt (“out”, preposition & adverb), from Proto-West Germanic *ūt, from Proto-Germanic *ūt (“out”); and Old English ūte (“outside; without”, adverb), from Proto-Germanic *ūtai (“out; outside”); both from Proto-Indo-European *úd (“upwards, away”).

examples.text: Do you want to go out tonight?

translations.de: Willst du heute Abend ausgehen?
translations.fr: Voulez-vous sortir ce soir ?
translations.pt: Quer sair hoje à noite?

examples.text: Why are you out at this hour?

translations.de: Warum bist du so spät noch draußen?
translations.fr: Qu'est ce que tu fais dehors à cette heure ?
translations.pt: O que você está fazendo aí fora a esta hora?

examples.text: I want to go out with you.

translations.de: Ich möchte mit dir ausgehen.
translations.fr: Je veux sortir avec toi.
translations.pt: Eu quero sair com você.

examples.text: Are we going to eat out tonight?

translations.de: Gehen wir heute Abend zum Essen aus?
translations.fr: On sort dîner ce soir ?
translations.pt: Vamos comer fora hoje à noite?

more.definition: A means of exit, escape, reprieve, etc.; A state in which a member of the batting team is removed from play due to the application of various rules of the game such as striking out, hitting a fly ball which is caught by the fielding team before bouncing, etc.; A dismissal; a state in which a member of the batting team finishes his turn at bat, due to the application of various rules of the game, such as the bowler knocking over the batsman's wicket with the ball.
more.etymology: From Middle English out, oute, from a combination of Old English ūt (“out”, preposition & adverb), from Proto-West Germanic *ūt, from Proto-Germanic *ūt (“out”); and Old English ūte (“outside; without”, adverb), from Proto-Germanic *ūtai (“out; outside”); both from Proto-Indo-European *úd (“upwards, away”).

examples.text: The orchestra is playing out of tune.

translations.de: Das Orchester ist nicht richtig gestimmt.
translations.fr: L'orchestre joue faux.
translations.pt: A orquestra está desafinando.

examples.text: When are you getting out of bed?

translations.de: Wann stehen Sie auf?
translations.fr: Quand est-ce que tu sors du lit ?
translations.pt: Quando você vai sair da cama?

examples.text: We're getting out of the elevator.

translations.de: Wir steigen aus dem Aufzug.
translations.fr: Nous sortons de l'ascenseur.
translations.pt: Estamos saindo do elevador.

examples.text: I'd love to try that out.

translations.de: Das würde ich liebend gerne einmal ausprobieren.
translations.fr: J'adorerais essayer ça !
translations.pt: Eu adoraria tentar isso.

more.etymology: From Middle English out, oute, from a combination of Old English ūt (“out”, preposition & adverb), from Proto-West Germanic *ūt, from Proto-Germanic *ūt (“out”); and Old English ūte (“outside; without”, adverb), from Proto-Germanic *ūtai (“out; outside”); both from Proto-Indo-European *úd (“upwards, away”).

examples.text: I'd rather not go out today.

translations.de: Ich möchte heute lieber nicht ausgehen.
translations.fr: Je préférerais ne pas sortir aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Eu preferia não sair hoje.

examples.text: I'm trying to figure out something.

translations.de: Ich versuche gerade, mir über etwas klar zu werden.
translations.fr: J'essaye de comprendre quelque chose.
translations.pt: Eu estou tentando descobrir uma coisa.

examples.text: Once in a while, we eat out.

translations.de: Wir gehen ab und zu essen.
translations.fr: De temps en temps, nous allons au restaurant.
translations.pt: De vez em quando, comemos fora.

examples.text: I'm a little out of practice.

translations.de: Ich bin etwas aus der Übung.
translations.fr: Je manque un peu de pratique.
translations.pt: Perdi um pouco a prática.

more.definition: To eject; to expel.; To come or go out; to get out or away; to become public, revealed, or apparent.; To reveal (a person or organization) as having a certain secret, such as a being a secret agent or undercover detective.
more.etymology: From Middle English out, oute, from a combination of Old English ūt (“out”, preposition & adverb), from Proto-West Germanic *ūt, from Proto-Germanic *ūt (“out”); and Old English ūte (“outside; without”, adverb), from Proto-Germanic *ūtai (“out; outside”); both from Proto-Indo-European *úd (“upwards, away”).

examples.text: Mary is very passionate about her work.

translations.de: Maria begegnet ihrer Arbeit mit großer Leidenschaft.
translations.fr: Marie est très passionnée par son travail.
translations.pt: Mary é muito apaixonada pelo seu trabalho.

translations.fr: Je veux que tu dises la vérité.

examples.text: What do you want to tell me?

translations.de: Was wollen Sie mir sagen?
translations.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu veux me dire ?
translations.pt: O que você quer me contar?

more.definition: A reflexive, often habitual behavior, especially one occurring in a context that often features attempts at deception by persons under psychological stress (such as a poker game or police interrogation), that reveals information that the person exhibiting the behavior is attempting to withhold.; A giveaway; something that unintentionally reveals or hints at a secret.; A private message to an individual in a chat room; a whisper.
more.etymology: From Middle English tellen (“to count, tell”), from Old English tellan (“to count, tell”), from Proto-West Germanic *talljan, from Proto-Germanic *taljaną, *talzijaną (“to count, enumerate”), from Proto-Germanic *talą, *talō (“number, counting”), from Proto-Indo-European *dol- (“calculation, fraud”).

examples.text: I promise to always tell the truth.

translations.de: Ich verspreche, immer die Wahrheit zu sagen.
translations.fr: Je promets de toujours dire la vérité.
translations.pt: Prometo dizer sempre a verdade.

examples.text: I was planning on telling you tomorrow.

translations.de: Ich wollte es Ihnen morgen sagen.
translations.fr: Je comptais te le dire demain.
translations.pt: Eu planejava te contar amanhã.

examples.text: You've already told me this story.

translations.de: Du hast mir diese Geschichte schon erzählt.
translations.fr: Tu m'as déjà raconté cette histoire.
translations.pt: Vocês já me contaram esta história.

examples.text: It's probably too soon to tell.

translations.de: Es ist wahrscheinlich noch zu früh, um darüber zu reden.
translations.fr: Il est probablement trop tôt pour le dire.
translations.pt: É realmente muito cedo para contar.

more.definition: To determine the number, amount, or value of [something].; To notice, discern. (Roughly, "can tell" means "know" but with a sense of direct perception.); To pick up on a difference. (See tell apart for more.)
more.etymology: From Middle English tellen (“to count, tell”), from Old English tellan (“to count, tell”), from Proto-West Germanic *talljan, from Proto-Germanic *taljaną, *talzijaną (“to count, enumerate”), from Proto-Germanic *talą, *talō (“number, counting”), from Proto-Indo-European *dol- (“calculation, fraud”).

examples.text: Tom did exactly as he was told.

translations.de: Tom tat genau, was man ihm sagte.
translations.fr: Tom fit exactement ce qu'on lui dit.
translations.pt: Tom fez exatamente como ele falou.

examples.text: Tom is working as a security guard.

translations.de: Tom arbeitet als Wächter.
translations.fr: Tom travaille comme agent de sécurité.
translations.pt: Tom está trabalhando como um segurança.

examples.text: My opinion is the same as yours.

translations.de: Ich bin gleicher Meinung wie du.
translations.fr: Mon opinion est la même que la tienne.
translations.pt: Minha opinião é a mesma que a sua.

examples.text: Occasionally, things don't go as planned.

translations.de: Nicht immer läuft es wie geschmiert.
translations.fr: Parfois, les choses ne se déroulent pas comme prévu.
translations.pt: Às vezes, as coisas não correm como planeado.

more.definition: To such an extent or degree; to the same extent or degree.; Considered to be, in relation to something else; in the relation (specified).; Used to intensify an adjective; very much; extremely.
more.etymology: From Middle English as, als(a), alswa, from Old English eallswā (“just so; as”), thus representing a reduced form of also. Compare German Low German a(l)s, German als, Dutch als.

examples.text: She is as slow as a turtle.

translations.de: Sie ist langsam wie eine Schildkröte.
translations.fr: Elle est aussi lente qu'une tortue.
translations.pt: Ela é lenta como uma tartaruga.

examples.text: The fog dissipated as the sun rose.

translations.de: Der Nebel löste sich auf, als die Sonne aufging.
translations.fr: Le brouillard s'est dissipé au lever du soleil.
translations.pt: A névoa se dissipou quando o sol surgiu.

examples.text: Tom played with dolls as a child.

translations.de: Tom spielte als Kind mit Puppen.
translations.fr: Tom a joué avec des poupées lorsqu'il était enfant.
translations.pt: Tom brincava com bonecas quando era criança.

examples.text: This story is old as the world.

translations.de: Diese Geschichte ist so alt wie die Welt.
translations.fr: Cette histoire est vieille comme le monde.
translations.pt: Esta história é tão velha quanto o mundo.

more.definition: In the (same) way or manner that; to the (same) degree that.; Used after so or as to introduce a comparison.; Used to introduce a result: with the result that it is; as to.
more.etymology: From Middle English as, als(a), alswa, from Old English eallswā (“just so; as”), thus representing a reduced form of also. Compare German Low German a(l)s, German als, Dutch als.

examples.text: Tom isn't as patient as Mary.

translations.de: Tom ist nicht so geduldig wie Maria.
translations.fr: Tom n'est pas aussi patient que Marie.
translations.pt: Tom não é tão paciente quanto Maria.

examples.text: He is not the same as before.

translations.de: Er ist nicht mehr derselbe wie früher.
translations.fr: Il n'est plus le même qu'avant.
translations.pt: Ele não é mais o mesmo de antes.

examples.text: Your death will serve as an example.

translations.de: Dein Tod wird als Exempel dienen.
translations.fr: Votre mort servira d'exemple.
translations.pt: Sua morte servirá de exemplo.

examples.text: You're not as young as Tom.

translations.de: Du bist nicht so jung wie Tom.
translations.fr: Tu n'es pas aussi jeune que Tom.
translations.pt: Tu não és tão jovem quanto o Tom.

more.definition: A libra, a Roman pound.; Any of several coins of Rome, coined in bronze or later copper; or the equivalent value.
more.etymology: Borrowed from Latin as. Doublet of ace.

examples.text: She is as skinny as a toothpick.

translations.de: Sie ist schlank wie ein Zahnstocher.
translations.fr: Elle est maigre comme un clou.
translations.pt: Ela é magrinha como um palito.

examples.text: I'm not as brave as Tom.

translations.de: Ich bin nicht so mutig wie Tom.
translations.fr: Je ne suis pas aussi courageux que Tom.
translations.pt: Não sou tão valente coma o Tom.

examples.text: John is as old as I am.

translations.de: John ist so alt wie ich.
translations.fr: John a le même âge que moi.
translations.pt: John é tão velho quanto eu.

examples.text: Latin is not as difficult as Greek.

translations.de: Latein ist nicht so schwierig wie Griechisch.
translations.fr: Le latin n'est pas aussi difficile que le grec.
translations.pt: O latim não é tão difícil como o grego.

more.definition: Introducing a basis of comparison, with an object in the objective case.; In the role of.; In the form of.
more.etymology: From Middle English as, als(a), alswa, from Old English eallswā (“just so; as”), thus representing a reduced form of also. Compare German Low German a(l)s, German als, Dutch als.

examples.text: Don't let this opportunity slip away.

translations.de: Lass dir diese Gelegenheit nicht entgehen!
translations.fr: Ne laisse pas filer cette occasion.
translations.pt: Não deixe essa oportunidade passar!

examples.text: Tom never lets anyone do anything.

translations.de: Tom lässt nie jemanden etwas tun.
translations.fr: Tom ne laisse jamais personne faire quoi que ce soit.
translations.pt: Tom nunca deixa ninguém fazer alguma coisa.

examples.text: Don't let it get you down.

translations.de: Lass dich davon nicht unterkriegen.
translations.fr: Ne te laisse pas abattre.
translations.pt: Não deixe isto te abater.

examples.text: You'd better let me do that.

translations.de: Das überlässt du besser mir.
translations.fr: Tu ferais mieux de me laisser faire.
translations.pt: É melhor você me deixar fazer isso.

more.definition: The allowing of possession of a property etc. in exchange for rent.; The hindrance caused by the net during serve, only if the ball falls legally.
more.etymology: Derived from Middle English leten, læten, from Old English lǣtan (“to allow, let go, bequeath, leave, rent”), from Proto-West Germanic *lātan, from Proto-Germanic *lētaną (“to leave behind, allow”), from Proto-Indo-European *leh₁d- (“to be tired, leave”).

examples.text: Don't let this ruin your friendship.

translations.de: Lasst eure Freundschaft daran nicht zerbrechen.
translations.fr: Ne laisse pas ceci ruiner votre amitié.
translations.pt: Não deixe que isso estrague sua amizade.

examples.text: You have to let me help you.

translations.de: Du musst mich dir helfen lassen.
translations.fr: Tu dois me laisser t'aider.
translations.pt: Você tem que me deixar ajudá-lo.

examples.text: Tom shouldn't have let Mary drive.

translations.de: Tom hätte Maria nicht fahren lassen sollen.
translations.fr: Tom n'aurait pas dû laisser Mary conduire.
translations.pt: Tom não devia ter deixado Maria dirigir.

examples.text: I can't let you do that.

translations.de: Ich kann dich das nicht tun lassen.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas te laisser faire ça.
translations.pt: Não posso permitir que você faça isso.

more.definition: To allow to, not to prevent (+ infinitive, but usually without to).; To allow to be or do without interference; to not disturb or meddle with; to leave alone.; To allow the release of (a fluid).
more.etymology: Derived from Middle English leten, læten, from Old English lǣtan (“to allow, let go, bequeath, leave, rent”), from Proto-West Germanic *lātan, from Proto-Germanic *lētaną (“to leave behind, allow”), from Proto-Indo-European *leh₁d- (“to be tired, leave”).

examples.text: Will artificial intelligence make these jobs disappear?

translations.de: Wird künstliche Intelligenz diese Jobs verschwinden lassen?
translations.fr: L'intelligence artificielle fera-t-elle disparaître ces emplois ?
translations.pt: A inteligência artificial fará desaparecerem esses empregos?

examples.text: He makes my life a living hell.

translations.de: Er macht mir das Leben zur Hölle.
translations.fr: Il fait de ma vie un enfer.
translations.pt: Ele faz da minha vida um inferno.

examples.text: I still make a lot of mistakes.

translations.de: Ich mache noch immer viele Fehler.
translations.fr: Je fais encore beaucoup d'erreurs.
translations.pt: Eu ainda cometo muitos erros.

examples.text: People who desire power make bad leaders.

translations.de: Wer nach Macht strebt, ist ein schlechter Führer.
translations.fr: Les personnes qui désirent le pouvoir font de mauvais dirigeants.
translations.pt: Quem deseja ter poder não é bom líder.

more.definition: Brand; marque; manufacturer; maker.; Manner or style of construction (style of how a thing is made).; Origin (of a manufactured article); manufacture; production.
more.etymology: From Middle English maken, make, from Old English macian (“to build, make, work”), from Proto-West Germanic *makōn (“to build, make, work”), from *mak (“agreeable, comfortable, fit, suitable”), from Proto-Germanic *makaz (“agreeable, comfortable, fit, suitable”), from Proto-Indo-European *meh₂ǵ-, *meh₂ḱ- (“to knead”) or *meg- (“to be comfortable, pleasant”). Related to match.

examples.text: This castle was made into a museum.

translations.de: Dieses Schloss wurde in ein Museum umgewandelt.
translations.fr: Ce château a été transformé en musée.
translations.pt: Este castelo foi transformado em museu.

examples.text: She'll make a doctor's appointment.

translations.de: Sie wird einen Arzttermin vereinbaren.
translations.fr: Elle prendra rendez-vous chez le médecin.
translations.pt: Ela vai marcar uma consulta médica.

examples.text: Tom is making a lot of money.

translations.de: Tom verdient viel Geld.
translations.fr: Tom gagne beaucoup d'argent.
translations.pt: Tom ganha muito dinheiro.

examples.text: Everyone makes mistakes from time to time.

translations.de: Jeder macht von Zeit zu Zeit Fehler.
translations.fr: Tout le monde fait des erreurs de temps en temps.
translations.pt: Todo mundo comete erros de vez em quando.

more.definition: To build, construct, produce, or originate.; To write or compose.; To bring about; to effect or produce by means of some action.
more.etymology: From Middle English maken, make, from Old English macian (“to build, make, work”), from Proto-West Germanic *makōn (“to build, make, work”), from *mak (“agreeable, comfortable, fit, suitable”), from Proto-Germanic *makaz (“agreeable, comfortable, fit, suitable”), from Proto-Indo-European *meh₂ǵ-, *meh₂ḱ- (“to knead”) or *meg- (“to be comfortable, pleasant”). Related to match.

examples.text: Do you know who won the race?

translations.de: Weißt du, wer das Rennen gewonnen hat?
translations.fr: Tu sais qui a remporté la course ?
translations.pt: Você sabe quem ganhou a corrida?

examples.text: I don't know who I am.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, wer ich bin.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas qui je suis.
translations.pt: Eu não sei quem eu sou.

examples.text: It remains to be seen who wins.

translations.de: Es bleibt abzuwarten, wer gewinnt.
translations.fr: Reste à savoir qui gagnera.
translations.pt: Resta saber quem ganha.

examples.text: I hate people who talk like that.

translations.de: Ich hasse Menschen, die so reden.
translations.fr: Je déteste les gens qui parlent comme ça.
translations.pt: Odeio pessoas que falam assim.

more.etymology: From Middle English who, hwo, huo, wha, hwoa, hwa, from Old English hwā (dative hwām, genitive hwæs), from Proto-West Germanic *hwaʀ, from Proto-Germanic *hwaz, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷos, *kʷís.

examples.text: There are people who eat cat meat.

translations.de: Es gibt Menschen, die Katzenfleisch essen.
translations.fr: Il y a des gens qui mangent de la viande de chat.
translations.pt: Há gente que come carne de gato.

examples.text: The woman who is speaking is tall.

translations.de: Die Frau, die spricht, ist groß.
translations.fr: La femme qui parle est grande.
translations.pt: A mulher que está falando é alta.

examples.text: You need to remember who you are.

translations.de: Du musst dich erinnern, wer du bist.
translations.fr: Tu dois te souvenir de qui tu es.
translations.pt: É preciso lembrar quem você é.

examples.text: Who's the idiot who did that?

translations.de: Was für ein Idiot hat das gemacht?
translations.fr: Qui est l'idiot qui a fait ça ?
translations.pt: Quem foi o idiota que fez isso?

more.definition: A person under discussion; a question of which person.
more.etymology: From Middle English who, hwo, huo, wha, hwoa, hwa, from Old English hwā (dative hwām, genitive hwæs), from Proto-West Germanic *hwaʀ, from Proto-Germanic *hwaz, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷos, *kʷís.

examples.text: Those who want to stay can stay.

translations.de: Wer will, kann bleiben.
translations.fr: Ceux qui veulent rester peuvent rester.
translations.pt: Aqueles que quiserem ficar podem ficar.

examples.text: I don't know who did it.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, wer es getan hat.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas qui l'a fait.
translations.pt: Não sei quem fez isso.

examples.text: Do you know who broke the window?

translations.de: Weißt du, wer das Fenster kaputt gemacht hat?
translations.fr: Sais-tu qui a cassé la fenêtre ?
translations.pt: Você sabe quem quebrou a janela?

examples.text: Do you not know who I am?

translations.de: Weißt du nicht, wer ich bin?
translations.fr: Ne sais-tu pas qui je suis ?
translations.pt: Tu não sabes quem sou eu?

more.definition: What person or people; which person or people; asks for the identity of someone; used in a direct or indirect question.; With antecedent as subject.; With antecedent as object: whom.
more.etymology: From Middle English who, hwo, huo, wha, hwoa, hwa, from Old English hwā (dative hwām, genitive hwæs), from Proto-West Germanic *hwaʀ, from Proto-Germanic *hwaz, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷos, *kʷís.

examples.text: I know why Tom is in trouble.

translations.de: Ich weiß, warum Tom in Schwierigkeiten steckt.
translations.fr: Je sais pourquoi Tom a des ennuis.
translations.pt: Eu sei por que Tom está em apuros.

examples.text: Tom asked Mary why she was crying.

translations.de: Tom fragte Mary, warum sie weinte.
translations.fr: Tom a demandé à Mary pourquoi elle pleurait.
translations.pt: Tom perguntou a Mary por que ela chorava.

examples.text: I wondered why people stared at me.

translations.de: Ich hätte gerne gewusst, warum die Leute mich anstarrten.
translations.fr: Je me demandais pourquoi les gens me fixaient.
translations.pt: Eu ficava imaginando por que as pessoas estavam me olhando.

examples.text: I wonder why he is so angry.

translations.de: Ich frage mich, warum er so böse ist.
translations.fr: Je me demande pourquoi il est tant en colère.
translations.pt: Eu me pergunto porque ele está tão bravo.

more.definition: Introducing a complete question.; With a negative, used rhetorically to make a suggestion.; Introducing a verb phrase (bare infinitive clause).
more.etymology: From Middle English why, from Old English hwȳ (“why”), from Proto-Germanic *hwī (“by what, how”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷey, instrumental case of *kʷís (“who”), *kʷid (“what”).

examples.text: I asked Mary why she was studying French.

translations.de: Ich fragte Maria, warum sie Französisch lerne.
translations.fr: J'ai demandé à Mary pourquoi elle étudiait le français.
translations.pt: Perguntei a Mary por que ela estava estudando francês.

examples.text: I wonder why there are so many wars.

translations.de: Ich frage mich, warum es so viele Kriege gibt.
translations.fr: Je me demande pourquoi il y a tant de guerres.
translations.pt: Eu me pergunto por que há tantas guerras.

examples.text: We still don't know why.

translations.de: Wir wissen immer noch nicht, warum.
translations.fr: On ne sait toujours pas pourquoi.
translations.pt: Ainda não sabemos a razão.

examples.text: I don't know why they do it.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, warum sie das machen.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas pourquoi ils le font.
translations.pt: Não sei por que eles fazem isso.

more.etymology: From Middle English why, from Old English hwȳ (“why”), from Proto-Germanic *hwī (“by what, how”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷey, instrumental case of *kʷís (“who”), *kʷid (“what”).

examples.text: Tom asked Mary why she was late.

translations.de: Tom fragte Mary, warum sie zu spät gekommen war.
translations.fr: Tom a demandé à Mary pourquoi elle était en retard.
translations.pt: O Tom perguntou à Mary por que ela estava atrasada.

examples.text: The scientists are investigating why the experiment failed.

translations.de: Die Wissenschaftler untersuchen, warum das Experiment fehlgeschlagen ist.
translations.fr: Les scientifiques étudient pourquoi l'expérience a échoué.
translations.pt: Os cientistas estão investigando por que a experiência falhou.

examples.text: Is that why you hired me?

translations.de: Haben Sie mich deshalb eingestellt?
translations.fr: Est-ce pour cela que vous m'avez embauché ?
translations.pt: É por isso que você me contratou?

examples.text: That's why they came here.

translations.de: Ebendeswegen sind die hierhergekommen.
translations.fr: C'est pourquoi ils sont venus ici.
translations.pt: Por isso que eles vieram aqui.

more.definition: Reason.
more.etymology: From Middle English why, from Old English hwȳ (“why”), from Proto-Germanic *hwī (“by what, how”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷey, instrumental case of *kʷís (“who”), *kʷid (“what”).

examples.text: That's why I bought this book.

translations.de: Deswegen habe ich mir dieses Buch gekauft.
translations.fr: C'est la raison pour laquelle j'ai acheté ce livre.
translations.pt: É por isso que comprei este livro.

examples.text: I wonder why the dogs are barking.

translations.de: Ich frage mich, warum die Hunde bellen.
translations.fr: Je me demande pourquoi les chiens aboient.
translations.pt: Por que será que os cachorros estão latindo?

examples.text: That's why you're still single.

translations.de: Ebendeshalb bist du noch immer Single.
translations.fr: C'est pour ça que tu es toujours célibataire.
translations.pt: É por isso que você ainda está solteiro.

examples.text: Don't you want to know why?

translations.de: Wollen Sie nicht wissen, warum?
translations.fr: Ne veux-tu pas savoir pourquoi ?
translations.pt: Não quer saber por quê?

more.definition: To ask (someone) the question "why?".
more.etymology: From Middle English why, from Old English hwȳ (“why”), from Proto-Germanic *hwī (“by what, how”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷey, instrumental case of *kʷís (“who”), *kʷid (“what”).

examples.text: The soul is different from the body.

translations.de: Die Seele unterscheidet sich vom Körper.
translations.fr: L'âme est différente du corps.
translations.pt: A alma é diferente do corpo.

examples.text: Thessaloniki is five hundred kilometers from Athens.

translations.de: Thessaloniki ist fünfhundert Kilometer von Athen entfernt.
translations.fr: Thessalonique est à cinq cents kilomètres d'Athènes.
translations.pt: Salónica fica a 500 quilómetros de Atenas.

examples.text: We must move from words to actions.

translations.de: Wir müssen von Worten zu Taten übergehen.
translations.fr: Nous devons passer des paroles aux actes.
translations.pt: Devemos passar das palavras às ações.

examples.text: The keenest pleasure is derived from learning.

translations.de: Die größte Freude bereitet das Lernen.
translations.fr: Le plaisir le plus vif est celui d'apprendre.
translations.pt: O prazer mais apurado deriva do aprendizado.

more.definition: Used to indicate source or provenance.; Originating at (a year, time, etc.); Used to indicate a starting point or initial reference.
more.etymology: From Middle English from (“from”), from Old English from, fram (“forward, from”), from Proto-West Germanic *fram, from Proto-Germanic *fram (“forward, from, away”).

examples.text: I don't like you very much.

translations.de: Ich kann dich nicht besonders leiden.
translations.fr: Je ne t'aime pas beaucoup.
translations.pt: Eu não gosto muito de você.

examples.text: Thank you very much for your generosity.

translations.de: Vielen Dank für Ihre Großzügigkeit!
translations.fr: Je vous remercie beaucoup de votre générosité.
translations.pt: Eu lhe agradeço muito a generosidade.

examples.text: How much does a bus ticket cost?

translations.de: Wie viel kostet eine Busfahrkarte?
translations.fr: Combien coûte un ticket de bus ?
translations.pt: Quanto custa uma passagem de ônibus?

examples.text: We don't have too much time.

translations.de: Wir haben nicht viel Zeit.
translations.fr: On n'a pas beaucoup de temps.
translations.pt: Nós não temos muito tempo.

more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-lósder. From Middle English muche (“much, great”), apocopated variant of muchel (“much, great”), from Old English myċel, miċel (“big, much”), from Proto-West Germanic *mikil, from Proto-Germanic *mikilaz (“great, many, much”), from Proto-Indo-European *meǵh₂- (“big, stour, great”). See also mickle, muckle.

examples.text: How much do olives and cookies cost?

translations.de: Wie viel kosten die Oliven und Kekse?
translations.fr: Combien coûtent les olives et les biscuits ?
translations.pt: Quanto custam as azeitonas e os biscoitos?

examples.text: You'd better not eat too much.

translations.de: Du solltest lieber nicht zu viel essen.
translations.fr: Vous feriez mieux de ne pas trop manger.
translations.pt: É melhor você não comer demais.

examples.text: I should've studied French much harder.

translations.de: Ich hätte fleißiger Französisch lernen sollen.
translations.fr: J'aurais dû étudier le français plus assidûment.
translations.pt: Eu deveria ter estudado francês muito mais.

examples.text: How much water is in the bucket?

translations.de: Wie viel Wasser ist im Eimer?
translations.fr: Combien d'eau y a-t-il dans le seau ?
translations.pt: Quanta água há no balde?

more.definition: To a great extent.; for emphasis or to indicate a great difference; Often; frequently.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-lósder. From Middle English muche (“much, great”), apocopated variant of muchel (“much, great”), from Old English myċel, miċel (“big, much”), from Proto-West Germanic *mikil, from Proto-Germanic *mikilaz (“great, many, much”), from Proto-Indo-European *meǵh₂- (“big, stour, great”). See also mickle, muckle.

examples.text: He's been drinking too much lately.

translations.de: Er trinkt in letzter Zeit zu viel.
translations.fr: Il boit trop ces jours-ci.
translations.pt: Ele está bebendo demais ultimamente.

examples.text: How much do a dozen eggs cost?

translations.de: Wie viel kostet ein Dutzend Eier?
translations.fr: Combien coûte une douzaine d'œufs ?
translations.pt: Quanto custa a dúzia de ovos?

examples.text: My family didn't have much money.

translations.de: Meine Familie hatte nicht viel Geld.
translations.fr: Ma famille n'avait pas beaucoup d'argent.
translations.pt: Minha família não tinha muito dinheiro.

examples.text: You're much faster than I am.

translations.de: Du bist viel schneller als ich.
translations.fr: Tu es bien plus rapide que moi.
translations.pt: Você é muito mais rápido do que eu.

more.definition: A large amount of.; Used to indicate, demonstrate or compare the quantity of something.; many ( + plural countable noun).
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-lósder. From Middle English muche (“much, great”), apocopated variant of muchel (“much, great”), from Old English myċel, miċel (“big, much”), from Proto-West Germanic *mikil, from Proto-Germanic *mikilaz (“great, many, much”), from Proto-Indo-European *meǵh₂- (“big, stour, great”). See also mickle, muckle.

examples.text: I don't like Tom very much.

translations.de: Ich mag Tom nicht sonderlich.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas beaucoup Tom.
translations.pt: Eu não gosto muito de Tom.

examples.text: Tom isn't much of a dancer.

translations.de: Tom ist kein großartiger Tänzer.
translations.fr: Tom n'est pas un grand danseur.
translations.pt: Tom não é um grande dançarino.

examples.text: I don't know much about Australia.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht viel über Australien.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas grand-chose sur l'Australie.
translations.pt: Eu não sei muito sobre a Austrália.

examples.text: How much did you pay the electrician?

translations.de: Wie viel hast du dem Elektriker bezahlt?
translations.fr: Combien avez-vous payé l'électricien ?
translations.pt: Quanto vocês pagaram ao eletricista?

more.definition: A large amount or great extent; a lot.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-lósder. From Middle English muche (“much, great”), apocopated variant of muchel (“much, great”), from Old English myċel, miċel (“big, much”), from Proto-West Germanic *mikil, from Proto-Germanic *mikilaz (“great, many, much”), from Proto-Indo-European *meǵh₂- (“big, stour, great”). See also mickle, muckle.

examples.text: We spend a lot of time together.

translations.de: Wir verbringen viel Zeit zusammen.
translations.fr: Nous passons beaucoup de temps ensemble.
translations.pt: Passamos muito tempo juntos.

examples.text: My wife was pregnant at the time.

translations.de: Meine Frau war damals schwanger.
translations.fr: Ma femme était enceinte à l'époque.
translations.pt: Minha esposa estava grávida na época.

examples.text: I said this a long time ago.

translations.de: Das habe ich vor langer Zeit gesagt.
translations.fr: J'ai dit ceci il y a longtemps.
translations.pt: Eu disse isso há muito tempo.

examples.text: In my free time, I write poetry.

translations.de: Ich schreibe in meiner Freizeit Gedichte.
translations.fr: Pendant mon temps libre, j'écris des poèmes.
translations.pt: No meu tempo livre, escrevo poesias.

more.definition: Reminder by the umpire for the players to continue playing after their pause.; The umpire's call in prizefights, etc.; A call by a bartender to warn patrons that the establishment is closing and no more drinks will be served.
more.etymology: From Middle English tyme, time, from Old English tīma (“time, period, space of time, season, lifetime, fixed time, favorable time, opportunity”), from Proto-West Germanic *tīmō, from Proto-Germanic *tīmô (“time”), from Proto-Indo-European *déh₂imō, from Proto-Indo-European *deh₂-i- (“to divide”), from the root *deh₂-. examples.text: What time are you planning to leave?

translations.de: Wann haben Sie vor, zu gehen?
translations.fr: À quelle heure comptes-tu t'en aller ?
translations.pt: A que horas estão planejando partir?

examples.text: I have already done this several times.

translations.de: Ich habe das schon ein paarmal gemacht.
translations.fr: Je l'ai déjà fait plusieurs fois.
translations.pt: Eu já fiz isso várias vezes.

examples.text: You've gone too far this time.

translations.de: Diesmal bist du zu weit gegangen.
translations.fr: Tu es allé trop loin, cette fois.
translations.pt: Você foi longe demais desta vez.

examples.text: I was extremely naive at the time.

translations.de: Ich war damals äußerst naiv.
translations.fr: J'étais extrêmement naïf à l'époque.
translations.pt: Naquela época eu era extremamente ingênuo.

more.definition: The inevitable progression into the future with the passing of present and past events.; The feeling of the passage of events and their relative duration, as experienced by an individual.; A dimension of spacetime with the opposite metric signature to space dimensions; the fourth dimension.
more.etymology: From Middle English tyme, time, from Old English tīma (“time, period, space of time, season, lifetime, fixed time, favorable time, opportunity”), from Proto-West Germanic *tīmō, from Proto-Germanic *tīmô (“time”), from Proto-Indo-European *déh₂imō, from Proto-Indo-European *deh₂-i- (“to divide”), from the root *deh₂-. examples.text: I cry every time I study Greek.

translations.de: Ich weine jedes Mal, wenn ich Griechisch lerne.
translations.fr: Je pleure à chaque fois que j'étudie le grec.
translations.pt: Eu choro toda vez que estudo grego.

examples.text: I don't have time for anything.

translations.de: Ich habe keine Zeit für etwas.
translations.fr: Je n'ai le temps pour rien.
translations.pt: Não tenho tempo para nada.

examples.text: It's time to turn the page.

translations.de: Es ist an der Zeit, umzublättern.
translations.fr: Il est temps de tourner la page.
translations.pt: É tempo de voltar a página.

examples.text: It was a difficult time for us.

translations.de: Es war eine schwierige Zeit für uns.
translations.fr: Ce fut une période difficile pour nous.
translations.pt: Foi um momento difícil para nós.

more.etymology: From Middle English tyme, time, from Old English tīma (“time, period, space of time, season, lifetime, fixed time, favorable time, opportunity”), from Proto-West Germanic *tīmō, from Proto-Germanic *tīmô (“time”), from Proto-Indo-European *déh₂imō, from Proto-Indo-European *deh₂-i- (“to divide”), from the root *deh₂-.
