examples.text: She has been to France three times.

translations.de: Sie ist dreimal in Frankreich gewesen.
translations.fr: Elle est venue en France à trois reprises.
translations.pt: Ela foi à França três vezes.

examples.text: What time did you go to sleep?

translations.de: Um wieviel Uhr bist du schlafen gegangen?
translations.fr: À quelle heure t'es-tu endormi ?
translations.pt: A que horas você foi dormir?

examples.text: We'll never get there in time.

translations.de: Wir werden es nie rechtzeitig dorthin schaffen.
translations.fr: Nous n'y arriverons jamais à temps.
translations.pt: Nunca chegaremos lá a tempo.

examples.text: We don't have time for that.

translations.de: Wir haben dafür keine Zeit.
translations.fr: Nous n'avons pas de temps pour ça.
translations.pt: Não temos tempo para isso.

more.definition: To measure or record the time, duration, or rate of something.; To choose when something commences or its duration.; To regulate as to time; to accompany, or agree with, in time of movement.
more.etymology: From Middle English tyme, time, from Old English tīma (“time, period, space of time, season, lifetime, fixed time, favorable time, opportunity”), from Proto-West Germanic *tīmō, from Proto-Germanic *tīmô (“time”), from Proto-Indo-European *déh₂imō, from Proto-Indo-European *deh₂-i- (“to divide”), from the root *deh₂-. Related to tide. Not related to Latin tempus.

examples.text: The answer is yes.

translations.de: Die Antwort ist ja.
translations.fr: La réponse est oui.
translations.pt: A resposta é sim.

examples.text: No... I mean, yes.

translations.de: Nein... Ich meine, ja.
translations.fr: Non... Je veux dire, oui.
translations.pt: Não... quer dizer, sim.

examples.text: Yes. No. Maybe. I don't know.

translations.de: Ja. Nein. Vielleicht. Ich weiß nicht.
translations.fr: Oui. Non. Peut-être. Je ne sais pas.
translations.pt: Sim. Não. Talvez. Eu não sei.

examples.text: The answer was yes.

translations.de: Die Antwort war „ja“.
translations.fr: La réponse était oui.
translations.pt: A resposta foi sim.

more.definition: There is; indicating the existence of something.; Indicating the possibility or allowance of something.
more.etymology: From Middle English yes, from Old English ġīese (“by all means, of course, yes”), derived from the same root as yea. Compare Faroese júsá (“yes, indeed, certainly”).

examples.text: I would've said yes.

translations.de: Ich hätte ja gesagt.
translations.fr: J’aurais dit oui.
translations.pt: Eu teria dito que sim.

examples.text: I would have said yes.

translations.de: Ich hätte ja gesagt.
translations.fr: J’aurais dit oui.
translations.pt: Eu teria dito que sim.

examples.text: He will not say yes.

translations.de: Er wird nicht ja sagen.
translations.fr: Il ne va pas dire oui.
translations.pt: Ele não dirá que sim.

examples.text: He has already said yes.

translations.de: Er hat schon ja gesagt.
translations.fr: Il a déjà dit oui.
translations.pt: Ele já disse sim.

more.definition: An exclamation of pleasure or approval, usually transcribed with an exclamation point.; Response that confirms that the user is paying attention.; Used to ask for more information with a request.
more.etymology: From Middle English yes, from Old English ġīese (“by all means, of course, yes”), derived from the same root as yea. Compare Faroese júsá (“yes, indeed, certainly”).

examples.text: Just say yes or no.

translations.de: Sag nur ja oder nein.
translations.fr: Dis juste oui ou non !
translations.pt: Apenas diga sim ou não.

examples.text: Maybe yes, maybe not.

translations.de: Vielleicht ja, vielleicht nein.
translations.fr: Peut-être que oui, peut-être que non.
translations.pt: Talvez sim, talvez não.

examples.text: He replies saying yes.

translations.de: Er antwortet mit "Ja".
translations.fr: Il répond en disant oui.
translations.pt: Ele responde que sim.

examples.text: Yes, I want you to do it.

translations.de: Ja, ich will, dass du es tust.
translations.fr: Oui, je veux que tu le fasses.
translations.pt: Sim, eu quero que você o faça.

more.definition: An affirmative expression; an answer that shows agreement or acceptance.; A vote of support or in favor of something.
more.etymology: From Middle English yes, from Old English ġīese (“by all means, of course, yes”), derived from the same root as yea. Compare Faroese júsá (“yes, indeed, certainly”).

examples.text: Do you want to be my girlfriend? □ Yes. □ No. □ Maybe.

translations.de: Möchtest Du meine Freundin sein? □ Ja. □ Nein. □ Vielleicht.
translations.fr: Veux-tu être ma copine ? □ Oui. □ Non. □ Peut-être.
translations.pt: Você quer ser minha namorada? □ Sim. □ Não. □ Talvez.

examples.text: Was that a yes?

translations.de: War das ein Ja?
translations.fr: Était-ce un oui ?
translations.pt: Aquilo foi um sim?

examples.text: The answer's yes.

translations.de: Die Antwort ist ja.
translations.fr: La réponse est : oui.
translations.pt: A resposta é sim.

examples.text: Yes, yes, of course.

translations.de: Ja, ja, na klar.
translations.fr: Oui, oui, bien sûr.
translations.pt: Sim, sim, claro.

more.definition: Used to show agreement or acceptance.; Used to indicate disagreement or dissent in reply to a negative statement.; Answer to a question presuming one answer when all answers are correct.
more.etymology: From Middle English yes, from Old English ġīese (“by all means, of course, yes”), derived from the same root as yea. Compare Faroese júsá (“yes, indeed, certainly”).

examples.text: He told me when to say yes.

translations.de: Er hat mir gesagt, wann ich „Ja“ sagen soll.
translations.fr: Il me dit quand dire oui.
translations.pt: Ele me disse quando dizer sim.

examples.text: We haven't said yes yet.

translations.de: Wir haben noch nicht ja gesagt.
translations.fr: Nous n'avons pas encore dit oui.
translations.pt: Nós não dissemos que sim ainda.

examples.text: Is that a yes or no?

translations.de: Heißt das ja oder nein?
translations.fr: Est-ce un oui ou un non ?
translations.pt: Isso é um sim ou um não?

examples.text: The heart says yes but the mind says no.

translations.de: Das Herz sagt ja, aber der Verstand sagt nein.
translations.fr: Le cœur dit oui mais l'esprit dit non.
translations.pt: O coração diz que sim, mas o juízo diz que não.

more.definition: To agree with, affirm, approve.; To say “yes”.; To attempt to flatter someone by habitually agreeing
more.etymology: From Middle English yes, from Old English ġīese (“by all means, of course, yes”), derived from the same root as yea. Compare Faroese júsá (“yes, indeed, certainly”).

examples.text: Love happens when you least expect it.

translations.de: Die Liebe schlägt zu, wenn man am wenigsten damit rechnet.
translations.fr: L'amour survient quand on s'y attend le moins.
translations.pt: O amor acontece quando menos se espera.

examples.text: I like it when it's cold.

translations.de: Ich mag es, wenn es kalt ist.
translations.fr: J'aime qu'il fasse froid.
translations.pt: Eu gosto do frio.

examples.text: I know when I'm not wanted.

translations.de: Ich weiß, wenn ich unerwünscht bin.
translations.fr: Je sais lorsque je suis indésirable.
translations.pt: Sei quando não sou desejado.

examples.text: I was very young when that happened.

translations.de: Ich war sehr jung, als das passierte.
translations.fr: J'étais très jeune quand ça s'est produit.
translations.pt: Eu era muito novo quando isso aconteceu.

more.definition: At what time? At which time? Upon which occasion or circumstance? Used to introduce direct or indirect questions about time.; Used after a noun or noun phrase in isolation to express impatience with an anticipated future event.; At an earlier time and under different, usually less favorable, circumstances.
more.etymology: From Middle English when(ne), whan(ne), from Old English hwonne, from Proto-West Germanic *hwannē, from Proto-West Germanic *hwan, from Proto-Germanic *hwan (“at what time, when”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷís (interrogative base).

examples.text: I drink water when I'm thirsty.

translations.de: Ich trinke Wasser, wenn ich Durst habe.
translations.fr: Je bois de l'eau quand j'ai soif.
translations.pt: Eu bebo água quando estou com sede.

examples.text: What did you feel when you won?

translations.de: Was hast du gefühlt, als du gewonnen hast?
translations.fr: Qu'avez-vous ressenti lorsque vous avez gagné ?
translations.pt: O que você sentiu quando ganhou?

examples.text: I hear voices when I am alone.

translations.de: Ich höre Stimmen, wenn niemand da ist.
translations.fr: J’entends des voix quand je suis seul.
translations.pt: Eu ouço vozes quando estou sozinho.

examples.text: We close the windows when it rains.

translations.de: Wir schließen die Fenster, wenn es regnet.
translations.fr: Nous fermons les fenêtres quand il pleut.
translations.pt: Fechamos as janelas quando chove.

more.definition: At (or as soon as) that time that; at the (or any and every) time that; if.; During the time that; at the time of the action of the following clause or participle phrase.; At what time; at which time.
more.etymology: From Middle English when(ne), whan(ne), from Old English hwonne, from Proto-West Germanic *hwannē, from Proto-West Germanic *hwan, from Proto-Germanic *hwan (“at what time, when”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷís (interrogative base).

examples.text: We saw her when leaving the house.

translations.de: Wir sahen sie, als wir das Haus verließen.
translations.fr: Nous la vîmes en quittant la maison.
translations.pt: Nós a vimos quando saíamos de casa.

examples.text: I can tell when someone is lying.

translations.de: Ich merke es, wenn jemand lügt.
translations.fr: Je peux deviner quand quelqu'un ment.
translations.pt: Eu posso dizer quando alguem está mentindo.

examples.text: She always cries when he is drunk.

translations.de: Sie weint immer, wenn er betrunken ist.
translations.fr: Elle pleure toujours lorsqu'il est ivre.
translations.pt: Sempre chora quando está bêbado.

examples.text: He was exhausted when he got home.

translations.de: Als er nach Hause kam, war er fix und fertig.
translations.fr: Il était épuisé quand il est rentré chez lui.
translations.pt: Ele estava exausto quando chegou em casa.

more.definition: That's enough: a command asking someone to stop adding something, especially an ingredient or portion of food or drink; used in, or as if in, literal response to ‘Say when’.
more.etymology: From Middle English when(ne), whan(ne), from Old English hwonne, from Proto-West Germanic *hwannē, from Proto-West Germanic *hwan, from Proto-Germanic *hwan (“at what time, when”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷís (interrogative base).

examples.text: He always cries when he is drunk.

translations.de: Er weint immer, wenn er betrunken ist.
translations.fr: Il pleure toujours lorsqu'il est saoul.
translations.pt: Sempre chora quando está bêbado.

examples.text: We'll go when it stops raining.

translations.de: Wir gehen, wenn es aufhört zu regnen.

examples.text: Time flies when you're having fun.

translations.de: Die Zeit vergeht schnell, wenn man sich gut unterhält.
translations.fr: Le temps file quand on s'amuse.
translations.pt: O tempo voa quando estamos nos divertindo.

examples.text: Please close the door when you leave.

translations.de: Wenn du rausgehst, schließe bitte die Tür.
translations.fr: Fermez la porte quand vous sortirez, s'il vous plaît.
translations.pt: Por favor, feche a porta ao sair.

more.definition: The time at which something happens.
more.etymology: From Middle English when(ne), whan(ne), from Old English hwonne, from Proto-West Germanic *hwannē, from Proto-West Germanic *hwan, from Proto-Germanic *hwan (“at what time, when”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷís (interrogative base).

translations.de: Tom trägt normalerweise eine Brille, wenn er liest.
translations.fr: Tom porte habituellement des lunettes quand il lit.
translations.pt: O Tom usa óculos quando lê.

examples.text: Let me know when you've finished.

translations.de: Lass es mich wissen, wenn du es beendet hast.
translations.fr: Préviens-moi quand tu as fini !

translations.de: Mein Vater starb, als ich dreizehn war.
translations.fr: Mon père est mort quand j'avais treize ans.
translations.pt: Meu pai faleceu quando eu tinha treze anos.

more.definition: What time; which time.

translations.pt: Tom levou Mary a um restaurante italiano.

examples.text: I didn't even get an invitation.

translations.de: Ich habe eine Orange und einen Apfel.
translations.fr: J'ai une orange et une pomme.

examples.text: This is a pear, not an apple.

translations.de: Das ist eine Birne, kein Apfel.

translations.pt: Isso é uma pêra, não uma maçã.

examples.text: Tom has an older brother named John.

translations.de: Tom hat einen älteren Bruder mit Namen Johannes.

examples.text: Tom seems to be an honest person.

translations.de: Tom scheint ein ehrlicher Mensch zu sein.

translations.pt: Tom parece ser uma pessoa honesta.

examples.text: Do you think I'm an idiot?

translations.de: Hältst du mich für einen Idioten?

translations.pt: Você é uma inspiração para todos nós.

examples.text: I'll keep an eye on Tom.

translations.de: Ich werde auf Tom aufpassen.
translations.fr: Je vais garder un œil sur Tom.
translations.pt: Ficarei de olho em Tom.

examples.text: I'm going to be an uncle.

translations.de: Ich werde Onkel.

examples.text: Your question doesn't have an answer.

translations.pt: Ele fala Francês com sotaque inglês.

examples.text: Tom is the man of the house.

translations.fr: Combien de fois cela s'est-il produit depuis ?
translations.pt: Quantas vezes isso já aconteceu desde então?

more.definition: Being so at that time.
more.etymology: From Middle English then(ne), than(ne), from Old English þonne, þanne, þænne (“then, at that time”), from Proto-West Germanic *þan, from Proto-Germanic *þan (“at that (time), then”), from earlier *þam, from Proto-Indo-European *tóm, accusative masculine of *só (“demonstrative pronoun, that”). Cognate with Dutch dan (“then”), German dann (“then”), Swedish då (“then”), Icelandic þá (“then”). Doublet of than.

examples.text: I've learned a lot since then.

translations.de: Ich habe seither viel dazugelernt.
translations.fr: J'ai beaucoup appris depuis.
translations.pt: Tenho aprendido muito desde então.

examples.text: Tom has changed a lot since then.

translations.de: Tom hat sich seitdem sehr verändert.
translations.fr: Tom a beaucoup changé depuis.
translations.pt: Tom mudou muito desde então.

examples.text: I haven't seen him since then.

translations.de: Ich habe ihn seitdem nicht mehr gesehen.
translations.fr: Je ne l'ai pas vu depuis lors.
translations.pt: Não o tenho visto desde então.

examples.text: Back then, people communicated using smoke signals.

translations.de: In der Anfangszeit kommunizierten die Menschen über Rauchzeichen.
translations.fr: Aux premiers temps, les hommes communiquaient par signaux de fumée.
translations.pt: Antigamente eles se comunicavam com sinais de fumaça.

more.definition: At that time.; Soon afterward.; Next in order of place.
more.etymology: From Middle English then(ne), than(ne), from Old English þonne, þanne, þænne (“then, at that time”), from Proto-West Germanic *þan, from Proto-Germanic *þan (“at that (time), then”), from earlier *þam, from Proto-Indo-European *tóm, accusative masculine of *só (“demonstrative pronoun, that”). Cognate with Dutch dan (“then”), German dann (“then”), Swedish då (“then”), Icelandic þá (“then”). Doublet of than.

examples.text: I only understand some words now and then.

translations.de: Ich verstehe nur von Zeit zu Zeit einige Wörter.
translations.fr: Je comprends quelques mots de temps en temps seulement.
translations.pt: Só entendo algumas palavras de vez em quando.

examples.text: Two years have passed since then.

translations.de: Zwei Jahre sind seitdem vergangen.
translations.fr: Deux années se sont écoulées depuis.
translations.pt: Dois anos se passaram desde então.

examples.text: And then, what did you do?

translations.de: Und was hast du dann gemacht?
translations.fr: Et alors, qu'as-tu fait ?
translations.pt: E então, o que tu fizeste?

examples.text: Tom kissed Mary and then went to work.

translations.de: Tom gab Maria einen Kuss und fuhr dann zur Arbeit.
translations.fr: Tom embrassa Mary puis alla travailler.
translations.pt: Tom beijou Maria e depois foi trabalhar.

more.definition: That time.
more.etymology: From Middle English then(ne), than(ne), from Old English þonne, þanne, þænne (“then, at that time”), from Proto-West Germanic *þan, from Proto-Germanic *þan (“at that (time), then”), from earlier *þam, from Proto-Indo-European *tóm, accusative masculine of *só (“demonstrative pronoun, that”). Cognate with Dutch dan (“then”), German dann (“then”), Swedish då (“then”), Icelandic þá (“then”). Doublet of than.

examples.text: What is easier, to forgive or forget?

translations.de: Was ist leichter? Vergeben oder vergessen?
translations.fr: Qu'est-ce qui est le plus facile, pardonner ou oublier ?
translations.pt: O que é mais fácil: perdoar ou esquecer?

examples.text: Do you prefer white or red wine?

translations.de: Bevorzugen Sie weißen oder roten Wein?
translations.fr: Est-ce que vous préférez le vin blanc ou le vin rouge ?
translations.pt: Você prefere vinho branco ou tinto?

examples.text: I don't speak French or German.

translations.de: Ich spreche weder Französisch noch Deutsch.
translations.fr: Je ne parle ni français, ni allemand.
translations.pt: Não falo francês nem alemão.

examples.text: Lions often target sick or injured animals.

translations.de: Löwen greifen oft kranke oder verletzte Tiere an.
translations.fr: Les lions prennent souvent pour cible les animaux malades ou blessés.
translations.pt: Leões geralmente visam animais doentes ou machucados.

more.definition: Of gold or yellow tincture on a coat of arms.
more.etymology: From late Middle English or (“gold”), borrowed from Middle French or (“yellow”), from Old French or, from Latin aurum (“gold”). Doublet of aurum.

examples.text: Are you a leader or a follower?

translations.de: Bist du eine Führungskraft oder ein Mitarbeiter?
translations.fr: Es-ce que tu es un meneur ou un suiveur ?
translations.pt: Você é um líder ou um seguidor?

examples.text: Are you for or against the war?

translations.de: Bist du für oder gegen den Krieg?
translations.fr: Es-tu pour ou contre la guerre ?
translations.pt: Vocês são contra ou a favor da guerra?

examples.text: Did you go to Cairo or Alexandria?

translations.de: Bist du nach Kairo oder nach Alexandria gefahren?
translations.fr: Est-ce que tu es allé au Caire ou à Alexandrie ?
translations.pt: Você foi ao Cairo ou a Alexandria?

examples.text: He will come back sooner or later.

translations.de: Er wird früher oder später zurückkommen.
translations.fr: Il reviendra tôt ou tard.
translations.pt: Ele vai voltar mais cedo ou mais tarde.

more.etymology: From Late Old English ār, from Old Norse ár. Compare ere.

examples.text: Onions can be eaten raw or cooked.

translations.de: Zwiebeln können roh oder gekocht verzehrt werden.
translations.fr: On peut manger les oignons crus ou cuits.
translations.pt: As cebolas podem ser comidas cruas ou cozidas.

examples.text: Do you have any brothers or sisters?

translations.de: Haben Sie Brüder und Schwestern?
translations.fr: Avez-vous des frères et sœurs ?
translations.pt: Vocês têm irmãos?

examples.text: Are you gonna help me or what?

translations.de: Wirst du mir helfen, oder was?
translations.fr: Vas-tu m'aider ou quoi ?
translations.pt: Você vai ou não vai me ajudar?

examples.text: Does he speak English, French or German?

translations.de: Spricht er Englisch, Französisch oder Deutsch?
translations.fr: Parle-t-il anglais, français ou allemand ?
translations.pt: Ele fala inglês, francês ou alemão?

more.definition: Connects at least two alternative words, phrases, clauses, sentences, etc., each of which could make a passage true.; An operator denoting the disjunction of two propositions or truth values. There are two forms: the inclusive or and the exclusive or.; Used to present two or more options from which a choice is to be made.
more.etymology: From Middle English or; partially contracted from other, auther, from Old English āþor, āwþer, āhwæþer ("some, any, either"; > either); and partially from Middle English oththe, from Old English oþþe, from Proto-Germanic *efþau (“or”).

examples.text: Do you want to go or not?

translations.de: Willst du gehen oder nicht?
translations.fr: Tu veux y aller ou pas ?
translations.pt: Vocês querem ir ou não?

examples.text: Is Buddhism a religion or a philosophy?

translations.de: Ist der Buddhismus eine Religion oder eine Philosophie?
translations.fr: Le bouddhisme est-il une religion ou une philosophie ?
translations.pt: O budismo é uma religião ou uma filosofia?

examples.text: Are you going to go or not?

translations.de: Gehst du nun oder nicht?
translations.fr: Allez-vous vous y rendre ou pas ?
translations.pt: Você vai ou não?

examples.text: Is this a stallion or a mare?

translations.de: Ist das ein Hengst oder eine Stute?
translations.fr: Est-ce un étalon ou une jument ?
translations.pt: É este um garanhão ou uma égua?

more.definition: The gold or yellow tincture on a coat of arms.
more.etymology: From Etymology 1 (sense 2 above).

examples.text: Are you buying or are you selling?

translations.de: Kaufst du oder verkaufst du?
translations.fr: Tu achètes ou tu vends ?
translations.pt: Você está comprando ou vendendo?

examples.text: Is light a wave or a particle?

translations.de: Besteht das Licht aus Wellen oder Teilchen?
translations.fr: La lumière est-elle une onde ou une particule ?
translations.pt: A luz é uma onda ou uma partícula?

examples.text: What passions cannot music raise or quell?

translations.de: Welche Leidenschaften vermag die Musik nicht zu steigern oder zu unterdrücken?
translations.fr: Quelles passions la musique ne saurait-elle susciter ou étouffer ?
translations.pt: Que paixões não pode suscitar ou mitigar a música?

examples.text: Eat, or else it will go cold.

translations.de: Iss, oder es wird kalt!
translations.fr: Mange, ça va refroidir.
translations.pt: Coma, senão vai esfriar.

more.etymology: From Late Old English ār, from Old Norse ár. Compare ere.

examples.text: I need to forget, therefore I drink.

translations.de: Ich muss vergessen; drum trinke ich.
translations.fr: J'ai besoin d'oublier, donc je bois.
translations.pt: Preciso esquecer, portanto bebo.

examples.text: I think Tom needs to do that.

translations.de: Ich denke, Tom muss das tun.
translations.fr: Je pense que Tom doit le faire.
translations.pt: Eu acho que Tom precisa fazer isso.

examples.text: I don't need anyone except you.

translations.de: Ich brauche niemanden außer dir.
translations.fr: Je n'ai besoin de personne à part toi.
translations.pt: Não preciso de ninguém exceto de você.

examples.text: The flowers in the garden need water.

translations.de: Die Blumen im Garten brauchen Wasser.
translations.fr: Les fleurs du jardin ont besoin d'eau.
translations.pt: As flores no jardim precisam de água.

more.definition: A requirement for something; something needed.; A desire or craving for the satisfaction of a requirement perceived as essential or primal.; Lack of means of subsistence; poverty; indigence; destitution.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *neh₂w-der. From Middle English nede, a merger of two terms: * Old English nīed (West Saxon), nēd (Mercian), nēad (“necessity, compulsion, want”), from Proto-West Germanic *naudi, from Proto-Germanic *naudiz, from Proto-Indo-European *neh₂w- (“death”).

examples.text: I need to open a bank account.

translations.de: Ich muss ein Bankkonto eröffnen.
translations.fr: J'ai besoin d'ouvrir un compte bancaire.
translations.pt: Preciso abrir uma conta bancária.

examples.text: Everyone needs a place to call home.

translations.de: Jeder braucht ein Zuhause.
translations.fr: Chacun a besoin d'un endroit qu'il nomme son chez soi.
translations.pt: Todo mundo precisa de um lugar para chamar de lar.

examples.text: You need onions in the marinara sauce.

translations.de: Man braucht Zwiebeln in der Marinarasoße.
translations.fr: Il faut qu'il y ait des oignons dans la sauce marinara.
translations.pt: Você precisa de cebolas no molho marinara.

examples.text: You don't need to convince me.

translations.de: Du musst mich nicht überzeugen.
translations.fr: Tu n'as pas besoin de me convaincre.
translations.pt: Você não precisa me convencer.

more.definition: To have an absolute requirement for.; To want strongly; to feel that one must have something.; To be obliged or required (to do something).
more.etymology: From Middle English neden, from Old English nēodian.

examples.text: I want to give it a shot.

translations.de: Ich will es versuchen.
translations.fr: Je veux essayer.
translations.pt: Eu quero tentar.

examples.text: When life gives you lemons, make lemonade.

translations.de: Wenn das Leben dir Zitronen zuteilt, mache Limonade.
translations.fr: Lorsque la vie te procure des citrons, fais de la limonade.
translations.pt: Quando a vida lhe dá os limões, faça uma limonada.

examples.text: I give the book to my friend.

translations.de: Ich gebe meinem Freund das Buch.
translations.fr: Je donne le livre à mon ami.
translations.pt: Eu dou o livro ao meu amigo.

examples.text: Can you give her a ride home?

translations.de: Kannst du sie nach Hause fahren?
translations.fr: Peux-tu la déposer chez elle ?
translations.pt: Tu podes levá-la para casa de carro?

more.definition: The amount of bending that something undergoes when a force is applied to it; a tendency to yield under pressure; resilience.
more.etymology: From Middle English given, yeven, yiven, ȝiven, from merger of Old English ġefan, ġeofan, ġiefan, ġifan, ġiofan, ġyfan (“to give”) and Old Norse gefa (“to give”), from Proto-Germanic *gebaną (“to give”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰebʰ- (“to give; to take”). Displaced yive, from Middle English yiven, of the same origin, from influence of Old Norse gefa.

examples.text: I've given Tom too many chances.

translations.de: Ich habe Tom zu viele Chancen gegeben.
translations.fr: J'ai donné trop de chances à Tom.
translations.pt: Eu dei muitas chances ao Tom.

examples.text: I use the pen you gave me.

translations.de: Ich benutze den Stift, den du mir gabst.
translations.fr: J'utilise le stylo que tu m'as donné.
translations.pt: Utilizo a caneta que você me deu.

examples.text: Why are you giving this to me?

translations.de: Warum gibst du mir das?
translations.fr: Pourquoi me donnez-vous ça ?
translations.pt: Por que você está me dando isto?

examples.text: What did Tom give you for Christmas?

translations.de: Was hat Tom dir zu Weihnachten geschenkt?
translations.fr: Qu'est-ce que Tom t'a offert à Noël ?
translations.pt: O que o Tom te deu de natal?

more.definition: To transfer one's possession or holding of (something) to (someone).; To make a present or gift of.; To pledge.
more.etymology: From Middle English given, yeven, yiven, ȝiven, from merger of Old English ġefan, ġeofan, ġiefan, ġifan, ġiofan, ġyfan (“to give”) and Old Norse gefa (“to give”), from Proto-Germanic *gebaną (“to give”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰebʰ- (“to give; to take”). Displaced yive, from Middle English yiven, of the same origin, from influence of Old Norse gefa.

examples.text: Are you sure this thing is safe?

translations.de: Bist du dir sicher, dass dieses Ding ungefährlich ist?
translations.fr: Es-tu sûr que ce truc est sûr ?
translations.pt: Você tem certeza de que isso é seguro?

examples.text: I do things in my own way.

translations.de: Ich mache die Dinge auf meine Weise.
translations.fr: Je fais les choses à ma façon.
translations.pt: Faço as coisas do meu jeito.

examples.text: I did a stupid thing last night.

translations.de: Ich habe letzte Nacht eine Dummheit gemacht.
translations.fr: J'ai fait une chose stupide la nuit dernière.
translations.pt: Fiz algo estúpido ontem à noite.

examples.text: Who would do such a stupid thing?

translations.de: Wer würde solch eine Dummheit machen?
translations.fr: Qui ferait une chose aussi stupide ?
translations.pt: Quem faria uma coisa tão estúpida?

more.definition: That which is considered to exist as a separate entity, object, quality or concept.; A word, symbol, sign, or other referent that can be used to refer to any entity.; An individual object or distinct entity.
more.etymology: From Middle English thing, from Old English þing, from Proto-West Germanic *þing, from Proto-Germanic *þingą.

examples.text: Sex and love are two different things.

translations.de: Sex und Liebe sind zwei verschiedene Dinge.
translations.fr: Le sexe et l'amour sont deux choses différentes.
translations.pt: Sexo e amor são duas coisas diferentes.

examples.text: The thing is, he broke the window.

translations.de: Um die Wahrheit zu sagen, hat er die Fensterscheibe kaputtgemacht.
translations.fr: Le fait est qu'il a cassé la fenêtre.
translations.pt: O fato é que ele quebrou a janela.

examples.text: My aunt remembers a lot of things.

translations.de: Meine Tante erinnert sich an viele Dinge.
translations.fr: Ma tante se souvient de beaucoup de choses.
translations.pt: Minha tia se lembra de muitas coisas.

examples.text: It's a thing women already know.

translations.de: Das ist etwas, was die Frauen schon wissen.
translations.fr: C'est une chose que les femmes savent déjà.
translations.pt: É uma coisa que as mulheres já sabem.

more.etymology: From Middle English thing, from Old English þing, from Proto-West Germanic *þing, from Proto-Germanic *þingą.

examples.text: The birds fly low over our garden.

translations.de: Die Vögel fliegen tief über unseren Garten.
translations.fr: Les oiseaux volent bas au-dessus de notre jardin.
translations.pt: Os pássaros voam baixo sobre o nosso jardim.

examples.text: Our children's happiness is our happiness.

translations.de: Das Glück unserer Kinder ist unser Glück.
translations.fr: Le bonheur de nos enfants est notre bonheur.
translations.pt: A felicidade dos nossos filhos é a nossa felicidade.

examples.text: This is a city in our country.

translations.de: Dies ist eine Stadt in unserem Land.
translations.fr: C'est une ville de notre pays.
translations.pt: Esta é uma cidade de nosso país.

examples.text: Tom carried our suitcases to our room.

translations.de: Tom trug die Koffer auf unser Zimmer.
translations.fr: Tom a porté nos valises dans notre chambre.
translations.pt: Tom levou nossas malas para o nosso quarto.

more.definition: Belonging to us, excluding the person(s) being addressed (exclusive our).; Belonging to us, including the person(s) being addressed (inclusive our).; Of, from, or belonging to any entity that the speaker is a part of or identifies with, such as place of employment or education, nation, region, language, etc.
more.etymology: From Middle English oure, from Old English ūre, ūser (“our”), from Proto-Germanic *unseraz (“of us, our”), from Proto-Indo-European *n̥-s-ero- (“our”). Cognate with Scots oor (“our”), West Frisian ús (“our”), Low German uns (“our”), Dutch onze (“our”), German unser, unsere (“our”) Danish vor (“our”), Norwegian vår (“our”), and more distantly Latin noster.

examples.text: I think I'm gonna shit myself.

translations.de: Ich denke, ich werde mir in die Hosen machen.
translations.fr: Je pense que je vais chier dans mon froc.
translations.pt: Acho que vou me cagar.

examples.text: Nothing is gonna happen overnight.

translations.de: Nichts wird über Nacht passieren.
translations.fr: Rien ne se passera du jour au lendemain.
translations.pt: Nada vai acontecer da noite para o dia.

examples.text: I'm gonna shoot him.

translations.de: Ich werde ihn erschießen.
translations.fr: Je vais le descendre.
translations.pt: Eu vou atirar nele.

examples.text: Sorry, I don't think I'm gonna be able to.

translations.de: Tut mir leid, ich denke nicht, dass ich können werde.
translations.fr: Désolée, je ne pense pas que je vais pouvoir.
translations.pt: Sinto muito, acho que não serei capaz.

more.definition: A modal used to express a future action that is being planned or prepared for in the present.
more.etymology: Contraction of going to. Attested since 1913 (OED, "gonna"). The pronunciation of present participles with the sound n rather than ng has a long history (see g-dropping on Wikipedia).

examples.text: I'm really proud of my students.

translations.de: Ich bin echt stolz auf meine Schüler.
translations.fr: Je suis vraiment fier de mes élèves.
translations.pt: Tenho muito orgulho dos meus alunos.

examples.text: I don't really understand your question.

translations.de: Ich verstehe deine Frage nicht wirklich.
translations.fr: Je ne comprends pas vraiment ta question.
translations.pt: Eu realmente não entendo sua pergunta.

examples.text: I find this whole discussion really stupid.

translations.de: Ich finde diese ganze Diskussion total blöd.
translations.fr: Je trouve toute cette discussion vraiment stupide.
translations.pt: Acho toda essa discussão realmente estúpida.

examples.text: We really shouldn't have done that.

translations.de: Das hätten wir wirklich nicht tun sollen.
translations.fr: Nous n'aurions vraiment pas dû faire ça.
translations.pt: Nós realmente não deveríamos ter feito isso.

more.definition: In a way or manner that is real, not unreal.; Actually; in fact; in reality.; Very (modifying an adjective); very much (modifying a verb).
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *(H)reh₁-der. Late Latin reālisder. Old French reelbor. Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der. Proto-Germanic *līkąder. From Middle English really, realy, rialliche, equivalent to real + -ly.

examples.text: I think that Tom really deserves it.

translations.de: Ich denke, Tom hat das wirklich verdient.
translations.fr: Je pense que Tom le mérite vraiment.
translations.pt: Eu acho que Tom realmente merece.

examples.text: We really have a lot in common.

translations.de: Wir haben eine ganze Menge Gemeinsamkeiten.
translations.fr: Nous avons vraiment beaucoup en commun.
translations.pt: Realmente, nós temos muito em comum.

examples.text: Do you really want me to go?

translations.de: Willst du wirklich, dass ich gehe?
translations.fr: Voulez-vous vraiment que j'y aille ?
translations.pt: Você quer mesmo que eu vá?

examples.text: I really don't need any help.

translations.de: Ich brauche wirklich keine Hilfe.
translations.fr: Je n'ai vraiment pas besoin d'aide.
translations.pt: Eu, realmente, não preciso de nenhuma ajuda.

more.definition: Indicating surprise at, or requesting confirmation of, some new information; to express skepticism.; A phatic confirmation by a listener, to signal active listening; mostly devoid of literal meaning, with the phatically contrived incredulity being merely formulaic.; Indicating that what was just said was obvious and unnecessary; contrived incredulity.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *(H)reh₁-der. Late Latin reālisder. Old French reelbor. Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der. Proto-Germanic *līkąder. From Middle English really, realy, rialliche, equivalent to real + -ly.

examples.text: She thanked him for all his help.

translations.de: Sie dankte ihm für all seine Hilfe.
translations.fr: Elle le remercia pour toute son aide.
translations.pt: Ela lhe agradeceu toda a ajuda.

examples.text: I thank you with all my heart.

translations.de: Ich danke dir von ganzem Herzen.
translations.fr: Je vous remercie de tout cœur.
translations.pt: Agradeço de todo o coração.

examples.text: I'm fine, thanks for asking!

translations.de: Es geht mir gut. Danke der Nachfrage!
translations.fr: Je vais bien, merci de me le demander !
translations.pt: Estou bem, obrigado por perguntar.

examples.text: From the bottom of my heart, thank you.

translations.de: Ich danke Ihnen von ganzem Herzen.
translations.fr: Je vous remercie du fond du cœur.
translations.pt: Eu vos agradeço de coração.

more.definition: To express appreciation or gratitude toward (someone or something).; In the future tense in the form one will thank someone to do something, chiefly expressing a command or criticism: to request that (someone) do something.; To respond to (someone) out of, or as if out of, appreciation or gratitude.
more.etymology: From Middle English thanken (“to express gratitude, give thanks; to congratulate, rejoice with, or wish joy to; to extol; to hold responsible for”), from Old English þancian, þoncian (“to thank”), from Proto-West Germanic *þankōn, from Proto-Germanic *þankōną (“to thank”), from *þankaz (see etymology 1) + *-ōną (suffix forming infinitives of verbs from nouns).

examples.text: We're trying to find some answers.

translations.de: Wir versuchen, einige Antworten zu finden.
translations.fr: Nous essayons de trouver des réponses.
translations.pt: Estamos tentando encontrar algumas respostas.

examples.text: I'm going to buy some water.

translations.de: Ich werde jetzt etwas Wasser kaufen.
translations.fr: Je vais acheter de l'eau.
translations.pt: Vou comprar água.

examples.text: This article contains some genuinely new ideas.

translations.de: Dieser Artikel enthält einige wirklich neue Ideen.
translations.fr: Cet article contient certaines idées vraiment nouvelles.
translations.pt: Este artigo contém algumas ideias genuinamente novas.

examples.text: Would you answer some questions for me?

translations.de: Würdest du mir ein paar Fragen beantworten?
translations.fr: Pourriez-vous répondre à quelques questions ?
translations.pt: Poderias responder-me algumas perguntas?

more.definition: Of a measurement: approximately, roughly.
more.etymology: From Middle English som, sum, from Old English sum (“some, a certain one”), from Proto-West Germanic *sum, from Proto-Germanic *sumaz (“some, a certain one”), from Proto-Indo-European *sem- (“one, whole”).

examples.text: I'll get you some more coffee.

translations.de: Ich bringe dir noch etwas Kaffee.
translations.fr: Je vais vous chercher du café.
translations.pt: Vou lhe trazer mais café.

examples.text: There's some milk in the fridge.

translations.de: Es gibt Milch im Kühlschrank.
translations.fr: Il y a du lait dans le réfrigérateur.
translations.pt: Há leite na geladeira.

examples.text: Tom put some butter on his toast.

translations.de: Tom strich sich Butter aufs Brot.
translations.fr: Tom a beurré sa tartine.
translations.pt: O Tom colocou manteiga na torrada.

examples.text: I want to learn some French songs.

translations.fr: Tu étais censé regarder le film aussi.
translations.pt: Você também deveria ter visto aquele filme.

examples.text: You mustn't use too many hyphens.

translations.de: Du darfst nicht zu viele Bindestriche benutzen.
translations.fr: Il ne faut pas utiliser trop de tirets.
translations.pt: Você não deve usar tantos hífens.

examples.text: This sweater is too tight for me.

translations.de: Dieser Pulli ist mir zu eng.
translations.fr: Ce pull est trop moulant pour moi.
translations.pt: Esta camisola é muito apertada para mim.

more.definition: Likewise.; Also, in addition marks a statement as equally valid as the preceding one.; To an excessive degree, more than enough indicates that the degree of a quality is more than what is needed or wanted.
more.etymology: From Middle English to (“also, in addition to”), from Old English tō (“furthermore, also, besides”), adverbial use of preposition tō (“to, into”). The sense of "in addition, also" deriving from the original meaning of "apart, separately" (compare Old English prefix tō- (“apart”)). Doublet of to; see there for more.

examples.text: What do you hope to find here?

translations.de: Was hoffen Sie hier zu finden?
translations.fr: Qu'espères-tu trouver ici ?
translations.pt: O que você espera encontrar aqui?

examples.text: I hope nobody finds out what we did.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, es findet niemand heraus, was wir getan haben.
translations.fr: J'espère que personne ne découvre ce que nous avons fait.
translations.pt: Espero que ninguém descubra o que fizemos.

examples.text: I figured I'd find you here.

translations.de: Dachte ich mir doch, dass ich dich hier fände!
translations.fr: J'ai songé que je te trouverais là.
translations.pt: Eu imaginei que te encontraria aqui.

examples.text: Did you find that on the internet?

translations.de: Hast du das im Internet gefunden?
translations.fr: Avez-vous trouvé ça sur Internet ?
translations.pt: Você encontrou isso na Internet?

more.definition: Anything that is found (usually valuable), as objects on an archeological site or a person with talent.; The act of finding.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *pent-der. Inherited from Middle English fynden, from Old English findan, from Proto-West Germanic *finþan, from Proto-Germanic *finþaną, a secondary verb from Proto-Indo-European *pent- (“to go, pass; path bridge”).

examples.text: Where can I find a newspaper, please?

translations.de: Wo kann ich eine Zeitung finden, bitte?
translations.fr: Où puis-je trouver un journal, s'il vous plaît ?
translations.pt: Onde eu posso encontrar um jornal, por favor?

examples.text: He finds fault with everything I say.

translations.de: Er kritisiert alles, was ich sage.
translations.fr: Il critique tout ce que je dis.
translations.pt: Ele critica tudo o que eu digo.

examples.text: I need to find my own rhythm.

translations.de: Ich muss meinen eigenen Rhythmus finden.
translations.fr: Je dois trouver mon propre rythme.
translations.pt: Eu preciso encontrar o meu próprio ritmo.

examples.text: Could you help me find my dog?

translations.de: Könntest du mir meinen Hund suchen helfen?
translations.fr: Pourriez-vous m'aider à retrouver mon chien ?
translations.pt: Você poderia me ajudar a procurar o meu cachorro?

more.definition: To encounter or discover by accident; to happen upon.; To encounter or discover something being searched for; to locate.; To locate on behalf of another.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *pent-der. Inherited from Middle English fynden, from Old English findan, from Proto-West Germanic *finþan, from Proto-Germanic *finþaną, a secondary verb from Proto-Indo-European *pent- (“to go, pass; path bridge”).

examples.text: Tom was the last student to leave.

translations.de: Tom war der letzte Student, der wegging.
translations.fr: Tom fut le dernier étudiant à partir.
translations.pt: Tom foi o último estudante a sair.

examples.text: Please leave a message after the beep.

translations.de: Sprechen Sie bitte nach dem Piepston.
translations.fr: Veuillez laisser un message après le bip.
translations.pt: Por favor, deixe uma mensagem após o sinal.

examples.text: Don't leave the bedroom window open.

translations.de: Lass das Schlafzimmerfenster nicht offen.
translations.fr: Ne laisse pas la fenêtre de la chambre ouverte.
translations.pt: Não deixe a janela do quarto aberta.

examples.text: You have to leave the country today.

translations.de: Du sollst heute das Land verlassen.
translations.fr: Tu dois quitter le pays aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Vocês têm de deixar o país hoje.

more.definition: The action of the batsman not attempting to play at the ball.; The arrangement of balls in play that remains after a shot is made (which determines whether the next shooter — who may be either the same player, or an opponent — has good options, or only poor ones).; The tiles remaining on a player's rack after his or her turn.
more.etymology: From Middle English leven, from Old English lǣfan (“to leave”), from Proto-West Germanic *laibijan, from Proto-Germanic *laibijaną (“to let stay, leave”), causative of *lībaną (“to stay, remain”), from Proto-Indo-European *leyp- (“to stick; fat”).

examples.text: Our plane is leaving in two hours.

translations.de: Unser Flugzeug fliegt in zwei Stunden ab.
translations.fr: Notre avion part dans deux heures.
translations.pt: Nosso avião parte dentro de duas horas.

examples.text: In winter I leave home at nine.

translations.de: Im Winter gehe ich um neun aus dem Haus.
translations.fr: En hiver, je quitte la maison à neuf heures.
translations.pt: No inverno, saio de casa às nove.

examples.text: She left the tin on the table.

translations.de: Sie ließ die Dose auf dem Tisch.
translations.fr: Elle laissa la boîte sur la table.
translations.pt: Ela deixou a lata na mesa.

examples.text: Two of the players left the match.

translations.de: Zwei der Spieler verließen die Partie.
translations.fr: Deux des joueurs ont quitté le match.
translations.pt: Dois dos jogadores deixaram a partida.

more.definition: To cause or allow (something) to remain as available; to refrain from taking (something) away; to stop short of consuming or otherwise depleting (something) entirely.; To cause, to result in.; To put; to place; to deposit; to deliver, with a sense of withdrawing oneself.
more.etymology: From Middle English leven, from Old English lǣfan (“to leave”), from Proto-West Germanic *laibijan, from Proto-Germanic *laibijaną (“to let stay, leave”), causative of *lībaną (“to stay, remain”), from Proto-Indo-European *leyp- (“to stick; fat”).

examples.text: Are you scared to talk to girls?

translations.de: Hast du Angst davor, Mädchen anzusprechen?
translations.fr: Tu as peur de parler aux filles ?
translations.pt: Você tem medo de falar com garotas?

examples.text: Don't talk while you're eating.

translations.de: Beim Essen spricht man nicht!
translations.fr: Ne parle pas en mangeant !
translations.pt: Não fale enquanto estiver comendo.

examples.text: I still need to talk to Tom.

translations.de: Ich muss noch immer mit Tom reden.
translations.fr: J'ai encore besoin de parler à Tom.
translations.pt: Eu ainda preciso falar com o Tom.

examples.text: Tom prefers not to talk about it.

translations.de: Tom zieht es vor, nicht darüber zu sprechen.
translations.fr: Tom préfère ne pas en parler.
translations.pt: Tom prefere não falar sobre isso.

more.definition: A conversation or discussion; usually serious, but informal.; A lecture.; Gossip; rumour.
more.etymology: From Middle English talk, talke (“conversation; discourse”), from the verb (see above).

examples.text: Tom talked to Mary on the phone.

translations.de: Tom hat mit Maria telefoniert.
translations.fr: Tom parlait à Marie au téléphone.
translations.pt: Tom falou com Mary pelo telefone.

examples.text: Are we talking about the same Tom?

translations.de: Sprechen wir über denselben Tom?
translations.fr: Parlons-nous du même Tom ?
translations.pt: Estamos falando sobre o mesmo Tom?

examples.text: I want to talk to your uncle.

translations.de: Ich will mit deinem Onkel reden.
translations.fr: Je veux parler à ton oncle.
translations.pt: Quero falar com teu tio.

examples.text: I prefer to not talk about it.

translations.de: Darüber möchte ich lieber nicht reden.
translations.fr: Je préfère ne pas en parler.
translations.pt: Prefiro não falar sobre isso.

more.definition: To communicate, usually by means of speech.; To discuss; to talk about.; To speak (a certain language).
more.etymology: From Middle English talken, talkien, from Old English *tealcian (“to talk, chat”), from Proto-West Germanic *talkōn, from Proto-Germanic *talkōną (“to talk, chatter”), frequentative form of Proto-Germanic *talōną (“to count, recount, tell”), from Proto-Indo-European *dol-, *del- (“to aim, calculate, adjust, count”), equivalent to tell + -k. Cognates Cognate with Low German taalken (“to chatter, gossip, talk”).

examples.text: This sentence shall not be translated.

translations.de: Dieser Satz darf nicht übersetzt werden.
translations.fr: Cette phrase ne sera pas traduite.
translations.pt: Esta frase não deve ser traduzida.

examples.text: Tomorrow we shall go from Frankfurt to Munich.

translations.de: Morgen werden wir von Frankfurt nach München fahren.
translations.fr: Demain nous partirons de Francfort pour Munich.
translations.pt: Amanhã iremos de Frankfurt para Munique.

examples.text: Where shall we have breakfast today?

translations.de: Wo frühstücken wir heute?
translations.fr: Où petit-déjeunerons-nous aujourd'hui ?
translations.pt: Onde vamos tomar café hoje?

examples.text: When shall I return the book?

translations.de: Wann soll ich das Buch zurückgeben?
translations.fr: Quand dois-je restituer le livre ?
translations.pt: Quando devo devolver o livro?

more.definition: Used before a verb to indicate the simple future tense in the first person singular or plural.; Used similarly to indicate determination or obligation in the second and third persons singular or plural.; Used in questions with the first person singular or plural to suggest a possible future action.
more.etymology: From Middle English schal (infinitive schulen), from Old English sċeal (infinitive sċulan (“should, must”)), from Proto-West Germanic *skulan, from Proto-Germanic *skal (infinitive *skulaną), from Proto-Indo-European *skel- (“to owe, be under obligation”).

examples.text: Don't forget to call your mom.

translations.de: Vergiss nicht, deine Mutter anzurufen!
translations.fr: N'oublie pas d'appeler ta maman !
translations.pt: Não se esqueça de ligar para a sua mãe.

examples.text: I wanted to make some telephone calls.

translations.de: Ich wollte einige Telefonate führen.
translations.fr: Je voulais effectuer quelques appels téléphoniques.
translations.pt: Eu queria fazer algumas chamadas telefônicas.

examples.text: Tom is waiting for a telephone call.

translations.de: Tom erwartet einen Telefonanruf.
translations.fr: Tom attend un appel téléphonique.
translations.pt: Tom está aguardando uma ligação telefônica.

examples.text: I'm going to call for help.

translations.de: Ich werde um Hilfe rufen.
translations.fr: Je vais appeler de l'aide.
translations.pt: Eu vou pedir ajuda.

more.definition: A cry or shout.; The characteristic cry of a bird or other animal.; A beckoning or summoning.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *gels-der. Proto-Germanic *kalzazder. Old English cealliander. From Middle English callen, from Old English ċeallian (“to call, shout”) and Old Norse kalla (“to call; shout; refer to as; name”); both from Proto-Germanic *kalzōną (“to call, shout”), from Proto-Indo-European *golH-so- (“voice, cry”), from *gel(H)- (“to vocalize, call, shout”). * Albanian gjuhë (“language, tongue”).

examples.text: What's the capital of Brazil called?

translations.de: Wie heißt die Hauptstadt von Brasilien?
translations.fr: Comment s'appelle la capitale du Brésil ?
translations.pt: Como se chama a capital do Brasil?

examples.text: I'm calling from my cell phone.

translations.de: Ich rufe von meinem Mobiltelefon aus an.
translations.fr: J'appelle de mon téléphone cellulaire.
translations.pt: Eu estou ligando do meu celular.

examples.text: Why didn't you call the police?

translations.de: Warum hast du nicht die Polizei gerufen?
translations.fr: Pourquoi n'as-tu pas appelé la police ?
translations.pt: Por que você não chamou a polícia?

examples.text: My boss called me into his office.

translations.de: Mein Chef hat mich in sein Büro gerufen.
translations.fr: Mon patron m'a convoqué dans son bureau.
translations.pt: O patrão me chamou ao seu escritório.

more.definition: To request, summon, or beckon.; To cry or shout.; To utter in a loud or distinct voice.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *gels-der. Proto-Germanic *kalzazder. Old English cealliander. From Middle English callen, from Old English ċeallian (“to call, shout”) and Old Norse kalla (“to call; shout; refer to as; name”); both from Proto-Germanic *kalzōną (“to call, shout”), from Proto-Indo-European *golH-so- (“voice, cry”), from *gel(H)- (“to vocalize, call, shout”). * Albanian gjuhë (“language, tongue”).

examples.text: I love the roar of the sea.

translations.de: Ich liebe das Brausen des Meeres.
translations.fr: J'aime le bruit de la mer.
translations.pt: Eu adoro o rugido do mar.

examples.text: Tom loves to play with my dog.

translations.de: Tom mag mit meinem Hund spielen.
translations.fr: Tom aime jouer avec mon chien.
translations.pt: Tom adora brincar com o meu cachorro.

examples.text: She was the love of my life.

translations.de: Sie war die Liebe meines Lebens.
translations.fr: Elle a été l'amour de ma vie.
translations.pt: Ela foi o amor da minha vida.

examples.text: Mary was the love of my life.

translations.de: Maria war die Liebe meines Lebens.
translations.fr: Marie était l'amour de ma vie.
translations.pt: A Maria foi o amor da minha vida.

more.definition: A deep caring for the existence of another.; A profound and caring affection towards someone.; Affectionate, benevolent concern or care for other people or beings, and for their well-being.
more.etymology: From Middle English love, luve, from Old English lufu, from Proto-West Germanic *lubu, from Proto-Germanic *lubō, from Proto-Indo-European *lewbʰ- (“love, care, desire”). The close of a letter sense is presumably a truncation of With love or the like. Eclipsed non-native English amour (“love”), borrowed from Norman amour (“love”).

examples.text: I love the smell of morning coffee.

translations.de: Ich liebe den Geruch von Kaffee am Morgen.
translations.fr: J'aime l'odeur du café le matin.
translations.pt: Amo o aroma do café da manhã.

examples.text: The cat loves playing in the garden.

translations.de: Die Katze mag es, im Garten zu spielen.
translations.fr: Le chat aime jouer dans le jardin.
translations.pt: O gato adora brincar no jardim.

examples.text: Tom loved Mary and Mary loved him.

translations.de: Tom liebte Maria, und Maria liebte ihn.
translations.fr: Tom aimait Marie et Marie l'aimait.
translations.pt: Tom amava Mary e Mary o amava.

examples.text: He was the love of her life.

translations.de: Er war die Liebe ihres Lebens.
translations.fr: Il était l'amour de sa vie.
translations.pt: Ele era o amor da sua vida.

more.definition: To have a strong affection for (someone or something).; To need, thrive on.; To be strongly inclined towards something; an emphatic form of like.
more.etymology: The verb sense is from Middle English loven, luvien, from Old English lufian (“to love”), from Proto-West Germanic *lubōn (“to love”), derived from the noun.

examples.text: Where is he going to settle down?

translations.de: Wo wird er sich niederlassen?
translations.fr: Où est-ce qu'il va s'installer ?
translations.pt: Onde ele vai se instalar?

examples.text: I have written down his phone number.

translations.de: Ich habe seine Telefonnummer aufgeschrieben.
translations.fr: J'ai noté son numéro de téléphone.
translations.pt: Eu anotei o telefone dele.

examples.text: They will cut down on their expenses.

translations.de: Sie werden ihre Ausgaben reduzieren.
translations.fr: Ils réduiront leurs dépenses.
translations.pt: Eles vão reduzir suas despesas.

examples.text: He sat down to read a novel.

translations.de: Er hat sich hingesetzt, um einen Roman zu lesen.
translations.fr: Il s'est assis pour lire un roman.
translations.pt: Sentou-se para ler um romance.

more.definition: Facing downwards.; At a lower level than before.; Sad, unhappy, depressed, feeling low.
more.etymology: From Middle English doun, doune (“down”), from Old English dūne (“down”), aphetic form of adūne (“down, downward”), from earlier ofdūne (“down”, literally “off the hill”), from of (“of, off of”) + dūn (“hill, mount, dune, down”). More at Etymology 2 below.

examples.text: I slipped and fell down the stairs.

translations.de: Ich bin ausgerutscht und die Treppe hinuntergefallen.
translations.fr: J'ai glissé et je suis tombé dans les escaliers.
translations.pt: Escorreguei e caí escada abaixo.

examples.text: The quality of rice is going down.

translations.de: Die Qualität des Reises verschlechtert sich.
translations.fr: La qualité du riz diminue.
translations.pt: A qualidade do arroz está caindo.

examples.text: The price of coffee has come down.

translations.de: Der Kaffeepreis ist gefallen.
translations.fr: Le prix du café a baissé.
translations.pt: O preço do café baixou.

examples.text: She turned down our offer of help.

translations.de: Sie lehnte unser Angebot, ihr zu helfen, ab.
translations.fr: Elle rejeta notre proposition de l'aider.
translations.pt: Ela recusou a nossa ajuda.

more.definition: From a higher position to a lower one; downwards.; To or towards what is considered the bottom of something, irrespective of whether this is presently physically lower.; At a lower or further place or position along a set path.
more.etymology: From Middle English doun, doune (“down”), from Old English dūne (“down”), aphetic form of adūne (“down, downward”), from earlier ofdūne (“down”, literally “off the hill”), from of (“of, off of”) + dūn (“hill, mount, dune, down”). More at Etymology 2 below.

examples.text: I heard him go down the stairs.

translations.de: Ich hörte ihn die Treppe hinuntergehen.
translations.fr: Je l'entendis descendre les escaliers.
translations.pt: Eu ouvi ele descer as escadas.

examples.text: In life there are ups and downs.

translations.de: Im Leben gibt es Höhen und Tiefen.
translations.fr: Dans la vie il y a des hauts et des bas.
translations.pt: Há altos e baixos na vida.

examples.text: A drunk man fell down the stairs.

translations.de: Ein betrunkener Mann fiel die Treppe hinunter.
translations.fr: Un homme ivre est tombé des escaliers.
translations.pt: Um bêbado caiu pelas escadas.

examples.text: I closed my eyes to calm down.

translations.de: Ich schloss meine Augen, um mich zu beruhigen.
translations.fr: J'ai fermé les yeux pour me calmer.
translations.pt: Fechei os olhos para me acalmar.

more.definition: A negative aspect; a downer, a downside.; A downer, depressant.; An act of swallowing an entire drink at once.
more.etymology: From Middle English doun, doune (“down”), from Old English dūne (“down”), aphetic form of adūne (“down, downward”), from earlier ofdūne (“down”, literally “off the hill”), from of (“of, off of”) + dūn (“hill, mount, dune, down”). More at Etymology 2 below.

examples.text: Would you mind turning down the music?

translations.de: Könntest du bitte die Musik leiser stellen?
translations.fr: Pourriez-vous baisser la musique ?
translations.pt: Você se importaria de recusar a música?

examples.text: The spiders climbed down from the ceiling.

translations.de: Die Spinnen kletterten von der Decke herunter.
translations.fr: Les araignées sont descendues du plafond.
translations.pt: As aranhas desceram do teto.

examples.text: Tom wrote down Mary's telephone number.

translations.de: Tom notierte sich Marias Telefonnummer.
translations.fr: Tom nota le numéro de téléphone de Marie.
translations.pt: Tom anotou o número de telefone de Mary.

examples.text: Maria came down from the seventh floor.

translations.de: Maria kam aus dem siebten Stock herunter.
translations.fr: Marie est descendue du septième étage.
translations.pt: Maria desceu do sétimo andar.

more.definition: From the higher end to the lower of.; From north to south of.; Towards the mouth of (a river); in the direction of flow of.
more.etymology: From Middle English doun, doune (“down”), from Old English dūne (“down”), aphetic form of adūne (“down, downward”), from earlier ofdūne (“down”, literally “off the hill”), from of (“of, off of”) + dūn (“hill, mount, dune, down”). More at Etymology 2 below.

examples.text: The sun went down behind the mountains.

translations.de: Die Sonne ging hinter den Bergen unter.
translations.fr: Le soleil s'est couché derrière les montagnes.
translations.pt: O Sol se pôs por detrás das montanhas.

examples.text: Life is full of ups and downs.

translations.de: Das Leben ist voller Hochs und Tiefs.
translations.fr: La vie est pleine de hauts et de bas.
translations.pt: A vida é cheia de altos e baixos.

examples.text: Tom sat down at the kitchen table.

translations.de: Tom setzte sich an den Küchentisch.
translations.fr: Tom s'assit à la table de la cuisine.
translations.pt: Tom sentou-se à mesa da cozinha.

examples.text: This day will go down in history.

translations.de: Dieser Tag wird in die Geschichte eingehen.
translations.fr: Ce jour entrera dans l'histoire.
translations.pt: Este dia vai ficar para a história.

more.definition: To knock (someone or something) down; to cause to come down; to fell.; Specifically, to cause (something in the air) to fall to the ground; to bring down (with a missile etc.).; To lower; to put (something) down.
more.etymology: From Middle English doun, doune (“down”), from Old English dūne (“down”), aphetic form of adūne (“down, downward”), from earlier ofdūne (“down”, literally “off the hill”), from of (“of, off of”) + dūn (“hill, mount, dune, down”). More at Etymology 2 below.

examples.text: I work at a hotel in Boston.

translations.de: Ich arbeite in einem Bostoner Hotel.
translations.fr: Je travaille dans un hôtel à Boston.
translations.pt: Trabalho num hotel em Boston.

examples.text: I don't know how this works.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, wie das funktioniert.
translations.fr: J'ignore comment ceci fonctionne.
translations.pt: Não sei como isto funciona.

examples.text: Do you have to work on Sundays?

translations.de: Müssen Sie sonntags arbeiten?
translations.fr: Devez-vous travailler le dimanche ?
translations.pt: Deveis trabalhar aos domingos?

examples.text: Tomorrow is my first day of work.

translations.de: Morgen ist mein erster Arbeitstag.
translations.fr: Demain est mon premier jour de travail.
translations.pt: Amanhã é o meu primeiro dia de trabalho.

more.definition: Labour, occupation, job.; The place where one is employed.; One's employer.
more.etymology: From Middle English work, werk, from Old English weorc, from Proto-West Germanic *werk, from Proto-Germanic *werką (“work”), from Proto-Indo-European *wérǵom (“work”), from Proto-Indo-European *werǵ- (“to make”).

examples.text: I don't want to work tomorrow.

translations.de: Ich will morgen nicht arbeiten.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas travailler demain.
translations.pt: Não quero trabalhar amanhã.

examples.text: I'm working on a new book.

translations.de: Ich arbeite an einem neuen Buch.
translations.fr: Je travaille sur un nouveau livre.
translations.pt: Estou escrevendo um novo livro.

examples.text: I don't know how it works.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, wie das funktioniert.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas comment ça marche.
translations.pt: Eu não sei como funciona.

examples.text: I didn't know you worked here.

translations.de: Ich wusste nicht, dass du hier arbeitest.
translations.fr: Je ne savais pas que tu travaillais ici.
translations.pt: Eu não sabia que você trabalhava aqui.

more.definition: To do a specific task by employing physical or mental powers.; Said of one's workplace (building), or one's department, or one's trade (sphere of business) [with in or at].; Said of one's job title [with as].
more.etymology: From Middle English werken and worchen, from Old English wyrċan and wircan (Mercian), from Proto-Germanic *wurkijaną (“to work”), from Proto-Indo-European *wr̥ǵyéti (“to be working, to be at work”), from the root *werǵ-.

examples.text: I'm a little under the weather.

translations.de: Ich bin nicht ganz auf Höhe.
translations.fr: Je ne me sens pas trop dans mon assiette.
translations.pt: Estou um pouco indisposto.

examples.text: This example is a little more complex.

translations.de: Dieses Beispiel ist etwas komplexer.
translations.fr: Cet exemple est un peu plus compliqué.
translations.pt: Este exemplo é um pouco mais complexo.

examples.text: Can you lend me a little money?

translations.de: Kannst du mir etwas Geld leihen?
translations.fr: Pouvez-vous me prêter un peu d'argent?
translations.pt: Você pode me emprestar um dinheiro?

examples.text: May I tell you a little secret?

translations.de: Darf ich dir ein kleines Geheimnis anvertrauen?
translations.fr: Puis-je te dire un petit secret?
translations.pt: Posso te contar um segredo?

more.definition: Small, not large, limited, particularly; Small, limited in size.; Short, limited in extent.
