examples.text: These oaks are over a hundred years old.

translations.de: Diese Eichen sind über hundert Jahre alt.
translations.fr: Ces chênes ont plus de cent ans.
translations.pt: Estes carvalhos têm mais de cem anos.

examples.text: I've been walking for over four hours.

translations.de: Ich bin schon seit über vier Stunden unterwegs.
translations.fr: Je marche depuis plus de quatre heures.
translations.pt: Eu estou correndo há mais de quatro horas.

more.etymology: From Middle English over, from Old English ofer, ofor, ouer, from Proto-West Germanic *obar, from Proto-Germanic *uber (“over”), from Proto-Indo-European *upér (“above; over”).

examples.text: He was arrested because he stole money.

translations.de: Er wurde festgenommen, weil er Geld gestohlen hatte.
translations.fr: Il a été arrêté parce qu'il a volé de l'argent.
translations.pt: Ele foi preso porque roubou dinheiro.

examples.text: It's because you're a girl.

translations.de: Es liegt daran, dass du ein Mädchen bist.
translations.fr: C'est parce que t'es une nana.
translations.pt: É porque você é mulher.

examples.text: He was absent because of the storm.

translations.de: Er fehlte aufgrund des Sturmes.
translations.fr: Il n'était pas là à cause de l'orage.
translations.pt: Ele faltou por causa da tempestade.

examples.text: I'm going because I want to.

translations.de: Ich gehe, weil ich gehen will.
translations.fr: J'y vais parce que j'en ai envie.
translations.pt: Eu vou porque eu quero.

more.definition: On account, for sake [with of].
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₁ep-der. Proto-Indo-European *h₁épsder. Proto-Indo-European *h₁épider. Latin causalbor. Old French causebor. From Middle English bi cause, from bi (“by”) + cause, modelled on Old French par cause.

examples.text: I cannot sleep because of the noise.

translations.de: Ich kann wegen des Lärms nicht schlafen.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas dormir à cause du bruit.
translations.pt: Não posso dormir por causa do barulho.

examples.text: I stayed home because I was sick.

translations.de: Ich bin zu Hause geblieben, da ich krank war.
translations.fr: Je suis resté chez moi parce que j'étais malade.
translations.pt: Fiquei em casa porque estava doente.

examples.text: I fixed the house because of you.

translations.de: Ich habe das Haus für dich repariert.
translations.fr: J'ai réparé la maison pour vous.
translations.pt: Consertei a casa por sua causa.

examples.text: They were late because of the storm.

translations.de: Sie verspäteten sich aufgrund des Sturms.
translations.fr: Ils ont été en retard à cause de la tempête.
translations.pt: Eles chegaram atrasados por causa da tempestade.

more.definition: By or for the cause that; on this account that; for the reason that.; As is known, inferred, or determined from the fact that.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₁ep-der. Proto-Indo-European *h₁épsder. Proto-Indo-European *h₁épider. Latin causalbor. Old French causebor. From Middle English bi cause, from bi (“by”) + cause, modelled on Old French par cause.

examples.text: I'm still angry because of her.

translations.de: Ich bin ihretwegen noch immer sauer.
translations.fr: Je suis encore en colère à cause d'elle.
translations.pt: Ainda estou zangado por causa dela.

examples.text: I stayed home because it was raining.

translations.de: Ich blieb zu Hause, weil es regnete.
translations.fr: Je suis resté chez moi car il pleuvait.
translations.pt: Fiquei em casa porque estava chovendo.

examples.text: I do it because I have to.

translations.de: Ich tue es, weil ich muss.
translations.fr: Je le fais parce que je le dois.
translations.pt: Faço-o porque preciso.

examples.text: She's absent because she's sick.

translations.de: Sie fehlt krankheitshalber.
translations.fr: Elle est absente car elle est malade.
translations.pt: Ela não veio porque está doente.

more.definition: Used alone to refuse to provide a full answer to a question begun with "why", usually taken as an anapodoton of the elided full phrase "Because I said so".
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₁ep-der. Proto-Indo-European *h₁épsder. Proto-Indo-European *h₁épider. Latin causalbor. Old French causebor. From Middle English bi cause, from bi (“by”) + cause, modelled on Old French par cause.

examples.text: I will do it because she said.

translations.de: Ich werde es machen, weil sie es sagte.
translations.fr: Je vais le faire parce qu'elle l'a dit.
translations.pt: Eu o farei porque ela disse.

examples.text: I like Tom because he's honest.

translations.de: Ich mag Tom, weil er ehrlich ist.
translations.fr: J'aime Tom parce qu'il est honnête.
translations.pt: Gosto do Tom porque ele é honesto.

examples.text: I do it because I want to.

translations.de: Ich tue es, weil ich es will.
translations.fr: Je le fais car j'en ai envie.
translations.pt: Eu faço isso porque quero.

examples.text: He was late because of the snow.

translations.de: Er verspätete sich aufgrund des Schnees.
translations.fr: Il fut en retard à cause de la neige.
translations.pt: Ele atrasou-se por causa da neve.

more.definition: On account of, because of.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₁ep-der. Proto-Indo-European *h₁épsder. Proto-Indo-European *h₁épider. Latin causalbor. Old French causebor. From Middle English bi cause, from bi (“by”) + cause, modelled on Old French par cause.

examples.text: What are you guys going to do?

translations.de: Was gedenkt ihr zu tun?
translations.fr: Vous allez faire quoi, vous ?
translations.pt: O que vocês vão fazer?

examples.text: I don't like the new guy.

translations.de: Ich mag den Neuen nicht.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas le nouveau.
translations.pt: Eu não gosto do cara novo.

examples.text: That guy stole my wallet! Stop him!

translations.de: Der Kerl hat meinen Geldbeutel geklaut! Haltet ihn!
translations.fr: Ce type a volé mon portefeuille ! Arrêtez-le !
translations.pt: Aquele cara roubou minha carteira! Pare-o!

examples.text: Tom is a decent sort of guy.

translations.de: Tom ist ein anständiger Typ.
translations.fr: Tom est un garçon convenable.
translations.pt: Tom é um cara decente.

more.definition: An effigy of a man burned on a bonfire on the anniversary of the Gunpowder Plot (5th November).; A man or boy; a fellow.; A person (see usage notes).
more.etymology: Coined by semantic widening from the name of Guy Fawkes (1570–1606), an English Catholic executed for his role in the Gunpowder Plot, which also came to refer to effigies of his image burned annually on Guy Fawkes Night.

examples.text: What do you guys want to eat?

translations.de: Was wollt ihr essen?
translations.fr: Qu'est-ce que je vous sers ?
translations.pt: Que é que vocês querem comer?

examples.text: Who do you think that guy is?

translations.de: Was glaubst du, wer der Typ da ist?
translations.fr: Qui crois-tu que ce type soit ?
translations.pt: Quem você acha que esse cara é?

examples.text: Who does that guy think he is?

translations.de: Für wen hält sich der Kerl eigentlich?
translations.fr: Il se prend pour qui, ce type ?
translations.pt: Quem esse cara pensa que é?

examples.text: Do you know who that guy is?

translations.de: Wisst ihr, wer der Kerl ist?
translations.fr: Vous savez qui est ce mec ?
translations.pt: Você sabe quem é aquele cara?

more.definition: To exhibit an effigy of Guy Fawkes around the 5th November.; To make fun of, to ridicule with wit or innuendo.; To equip with a support cable.
more.etymology: Coined by semantic widening from the name of Guy Fawkes (1570–1606), an English Catholic executed for his role in the Gunpowder Plot, which also came to refer to effigies of his image burned annually on Guy Fawkes Night.

examples.text: Could you bring us the bill, please?

translations.de: Die Rechnung, bitte.
translations.fr: J'aimerais la note, je vous prie.
translations.pt: Você pode nos trazer a conta, por favor?

examples.text: Could you please speak a little slower?

translations.de: Könnt ihr ein bisschen langsamer sprechen?
translations.fr: Pourrais-tu parler un peu plus lentement ?
translations.pt: Poderia falar um pouco mais devagar, por favor?

examples.text: Sing a song in your language, please!

translations.de: Singt bitte ein Lied in eurer Sprache!
translations.fr: Chante une chanson dans ta langue, s'il te plaît !
translations.pt: Cante uma música no seu idioma, por favor!

examples.text: I found it difficult to please her.

translations.de: Ich fand es schwierig, sie zufriedenzustellen.
translations.fr: Je trouvai difficile de la satisfaire.
translations.pt: Achei difícil satisfazê-la.

more.definition: Used to make a polite request.
more.etymology: Short for if you please, an intransitive, ergative form taken from if it please you which is a calque of French s'il vous plaît, which replaced pray. If it please you is a present subjunctive form, but most current uses of please are not parsed that way.

examples.text: Write the translation of the text, please.

translations.de: Schreiben Sie bitte die Übersetzung des Textes.
translations.fr: Écris la traduction du texte, s'il te plaît.
translations.pt: Escrevam a tradução do texto, por favor.

examples.text: Put the chair near the window, please.

translations.de: Stellen Sie den Stuhl bitte ans Fenster.
translations.fr: Mettez la chaise près de la fenêtre, s'il vous plaît.
translations.pt: Coloque a cadeira perto da janela, por favor.

examples.text: Can you switch the radio on, please?

translations.de: Kannst du bitte das Radio einschalten?!
translations.fr: Peux-tu allumer la radio, s'il te plaît ?
translations.pt: Você pode ligar o rádio, por favor?

examples.text: May I speak to Tom Jackson, please?

translations.de: Dürfte ich bitte mit Tom Johannsen sprechen?
translations.fr: Puis-je parler à Tom Jackson, s'il vous plaît ?
translations.pt: Posso falar com o Tom Jackson, por favor?

more.definition: Used as an affirmative to an offer.; An expression of annoyance, impatience, or exasperation.; Said as a request to repeat information.
more.etymology: Short for if you please, an intransitive, ergative form taken from if it please you which is a calque of French s'il vous plaît, which replaced pray. If it please you is a present subjunctive form, but most current uses of please are not parsed that way.

examples.text: Could you please turn off the TV?

translations.de: Kannst du bitte den Fernseher ausschalten?
translations.fr: Tu peux éteindre la télé s'il te plaît ?
translations.pt: Poderia desligar a tevê, por favor?

examples.text: Tom is a hard person to please.

translations.de: Es ist schwer, es Tom recht zu machen.
translations.fr: Tom est quelqu'un de difficile à satisfaire.
translations.pt: Tom é uma pessoa difícil de agradar.

examples.text: Can we have a moment alone, please?

translations.de: Könnten wir bitte kurz allein sein?
translations.fr: Pouvons-nous avoir un moment seuls, s'ils vous plaît ?
translations.pt: Podemos ficar um momento a sós, por favor?

examples.text: If the address changes, please contact us.

translations.de: Wenn sich die Adresse ändert, melden Sie sich bitte bei uns.
translations.fr: En cas de changement d'adresse, veuillez-nous contacter.
translations.pt: Se o endereço mudar, favor entrar em contato conosco.

more.definition: To make happy or satisfy; to give pleasure to.; To desire; to will; to be pleased by.
more.etymology: From Middle English plesen, plaisen, borrowed from Old French plaise, conjugated form of plaisir or plaire, from Latin placeō (“to please, to seem good”), from the Proto-Indo-European *pleHk- (“pleasingness, permission”). In this sense, displaced native Old English līcian, whence Modern English like.

examples.text: Hey, look, a three-headed monkey!

translations.de: Hey, schau' mal, ein Affe mit drei Köpfen!
translations.fr: Eh regarde, un singe à trois têtes !
translations.pt: Ei, olhe, um macaco de três cabeças!

examples.text: A lot of people are dealing with hay fever now.

translations.de: Viele Leute haben momentan mit Heuschnupfen zu tun.
translations.fr: De nombreuses personnes ont des problèmes de rhume des foins, actuellement.
translations.pt: Muitas pessoas estão agora a encarar a alergia ao pólen.

examples.text: Hey, what's going on?

translations.de: Hey, was ist los?
translations.fr: Eh, qu'est-ce qu'il y a ?
translations.pt: Ei, o que está acontecendo?

examples.text: Hey, don't do that!

translations.de: Hey, mach das nicht!
translations.fr: Hé, ne fais pas ça !
translations.pt: Ei, não faça isso!

more.definition: An exclamation to get attention.; A protest or reprimand.; An expression of surprise.
more.etymology: From Middle English hey, hei, also without h- in ey, from Old English *hē, ēa (interjection), attested as first element in hēlā, ēalā (“O!, alas!, oh!, lo!”). Cognate with Dutch hé, hei (“hi, hey”), German hei (“hey, wow”), Danish and Swedish hej (“hello, hey”), Faroese hey (“hey, hello”), Old Norse, Icelandic and Norwegian hei (“hey”), Polish hej (“hey, hello”), Romanian hei, Russian эй (ej, “hey”); see heigh.

examples.text: Hey, you two! What are you doing?

translations.de: Hallo, ihr zwei! Was treibt ihr?
translations.fr: Hé, vous deux ! Que faites-vous ?
translations.pt: Ei, vocês dois! Que é que estão fazendo?

examples.text: Hey, you! No running by the pool!

translations.de: He, du! Beim Schwimmbecken nicht rennen!
translations.fr: Hé toi ! Ne cours pas autour de la piscine !
translations.pt: Ei! Você, não corra perto da piscina.

examples.text: Hey, let me tell you something.

translations.de: Hey, lass mich dir mal was sagen.
translations.fr: Hé, laisse-moi te dire quelque chose.
translations.pt: Ei! Deixa eu te contar um negócio.

examples.text: Hey, Mimi! How's it going?

translations.de: Hallo Mimi! Wie geht es?
translations.fr: Salut, Mimi ! Comment ça va ?
translations.pt: Oi, Mimi! Como vai?

more.definition: A choreographic figure in which three or more dancers weave between one another, passing by left and right shoulder alternately.
more.etymology: From French haie (“hedge”), with reference to the weaving patterns used in hedgelaying. Doublet of hedge and quay.

examples.text: A lot of people are dealing with hay fever now.

translations.de: Viele Leute haben momentan mit Heuschnupfen zu tun.
translations.fr: De nombreuses personnes ont des problèmes de rhume des foins, actuellement.
translations.pt: Muitas pessoas estão agora a encarar a alergia ao pólen.

examples.text: Hey, you! What are you doing?

translations.de: Hey, ihr! Was macht ihr denn da?
translations.fr: Hé, vous ! Qu'est-ce que vous faites ?
translations.pt: Ei, você! Que está fazendo?

examples.text: I have hay fever.

translations.de: Ich habe Heuschnupfen.
translations.fr: J'ai le rhume des foins.
translations.pt: Estou com a febre do feno.

examples.text: Hey, Tom, forget about your worries.

translations.de: He, Tom, vergiss deine Bekümmernisse!
translations.fr: Hé, Tom, oublie tes préoccupations.
translations.pt: Ei, Tom, esqueça suas preocupações.

more.definition: To greet with a "hey"
more.etymology: From Middle English hey, hei, also without h- in ey, from Old English *hē, ēa (interjection), attested as first element in hēlā, ēalā (“O!, alas!, oh!, lo!”). Cognate with Dutch hé, hei (“hi, hey”), German hei (“hey, wow”), Danish and Swedish hej (“hello, hey”), Faroese hey (“hey, hello”), Old Norse, Icelandic and Norwegian hei (“hey”), Polish hej (“hey, hello”), Romanian hei, Russian эй (ej, “hey”); see heigh.

examples.text: I can't take my glasses off.

translations.de: Ich kann meine Brille nicht abnehmen.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas enlever mes lunettes.
translations.pt: Eu não posso tirar os óculos.

examples.text: I thought Tom had a day off.

translations.de: Ich dachte, Tom hätte einen Tag frei.
translations.fr: Je pensais que Tom avait un jour de congé.
translations.pt: Achei que Tom tinha um dia de folga.

examples.text: I forgot to turn off the light.

translations.de: Ich habe vergessen, das Licht auszumachen.
translations.fr: J'ai oublié de fermer la lumière.
translations.pt: Eu esqueci de apagar a luz.

examples.text: I grabbed a book off the shelf.

translations.de: Ich nahm ein Buch aus dem Regal.
translations.fr: J'ai attrapé un livre sur l'étagère.
translations.pt: Peguei um livro da estante.

more.definition: Inoperative, disabled.; Cancelled; not happening.; Not fitted; not being worn.
more.etymology: From Middle English of, from Old English of, af, æf (“from, off, away”), from Proto-West Germanic *ab, from Proto-Germanic *ab (“from”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epo (“from, off, back”). Doublet of of.

examples.text: He cut off a slice of meat.

translations.de: Er schnitt eine Scheibe Fleisch ab.
translations.fr: Il découpa une tranche de viande.
translations.pt: Ele cortou uma fatia de carne.

examples.text: He forgot to turn off the light.

translations.de: Er vergaß, das Licht auszumachen.
translations.fr: Il a oublié d'éteindre la lumière.
translations.pt: Ele se esqueceu de apagar a luz.

examples.text: That plane will take off at five.

translations.de: Das Flugzeug wird um 5 Uhr abheben.
translations.fr: Cet avion s'envolera à cinq heures.
translations.pt: Esse avião irá decolar às cinco.

examples.text: See if the gas is turned off.

translations.de: Schau nach, ob das Gas abgedreht ist.
translations.fr: Regarde si le gaz est coupé.
translations.pt: Veja se o gás está desligado.

more.definition: In a direction away from the speaker or other reference point.; Into a state of non-operation or non-existence.; So as to remove or separate, or be removed or separated.
more.etymology: From Middle English of, from Old English of, af, æf (“from, off, away”), from Proto-West Germanic *ab, from Proto-Germanic *ab (“from”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epo (“from, off, back”). Doublet of of.

examples.text: Tom is taking a few days off.

translations.de: Tom nimmt sich ein paar Tage frei.
translations.fr: Tom prend quelques jours de congé.
translations.pt: O Tom tirou alguns dias de folga.

examples.text: Israel should be wiped off the map.

translations.de: Israel soll von der Karte verschwinden.
translations.fr: Israël doit être rayé de la carte.
translations.pt: Israel deveria ser varrido do mapa.

examples.text: The plane took off exactly at six.

translations.de: Exakt um sechs hob das Flugzeug ab.
translations.fr: L'avion a décollé à six heures exactement.
translations.pt: O avião decolou às seis em ponto.

examples.text: She happened to have the day off.

translations.de: Sie hatte an diesem Tag zufällig frei.
translations.fr: Elle avait justement ce jour-là de libre.
translations.pt: Ela por acaso teve o dia livre.

more.definition: Beginning; starting point.
more.etymology: From Middle English of, from Old English of, af, æf (“from, off, away”), from Proto-West Germanic *ab, from Proto-Germanic *ab (“from”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epo (“from, off, back”). Doublet of of.

examples.text: The police have blocked off the area.

translations.de: Die Polizei hat die Gegend abgesperrt.
translations.fr: La police a bloqué l'accès à la zone.
translations.pt: A polícia tem bloqueado a área.

examples.text: Why did you switch the light off?

translations.de: Warum hast du das Licht ausgeschaltet?
translations.fr: Pourquoi as-tu éteint la lumière ?
translations.pt: Por que você desligou a luz?

examples.text: Mary dropped the children off at school.

translations.de: Maria setzte die Kinder an der Schule ab.
translations.fr: Mary a déposé les enfants à l'école.
translations.pt: Maria deixou as crianças na escola.

examples.text: She cut the crusts off her sandwich.

translations.de: Sie hat die Kruste von ihrem Butterbrot abgeschnitten.
translations.fr: Elle a enlevé la croûte de son sandwich.
translations.pt: Ela cortou as cascas do sanduíche dela.

more.definition: Not positioned upon; away from a position upon.; Detached, separated, excluded or disconnected from; away from a position of attachment or connection to.; Outside the area or region of.
more.etymology: From Middle English of, from Old English of, af, æf (“from, off, away”), from Proto-West Germanic *ab, from Proto-Germanic *ab (“from”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epo (“from, off, back”). Doublet of of.

examples.text: I dropped her off at the airport.

translations.de: Ich habe sie am Flughafen abgesetzt.
translations.fr: Je l'ai déposée à l'aéroport.
translations.pt: Eu deixei ela no aeroporto.

examples.text: The plane still hasn't taken off.

translations.de: Das Flugzeug hat noch nicht abgehoben.
translations.fr: L'avion n'a toujours pas décollé.
translations.pt: O avião ainda não decolou.

examples.text: The flowers give off a strong odor.

translations.de: Die Blumen verströmen einen starken Geruch.
translations.fr: Les fleurs dégagent une forte odeur.
translations.pt: As flores exalam um forte odor.

examples.text: The old lady got off the bus.

translations.de: Die alte Dame stieg aus dem Bus aus.
translations.fr: La vieille dame est descendue du bus.
translations.pt: A velha senhora desceu do ônibus.

more.definition: To kill.; To switch off.
more.etymology: From Middle English of, from Old English of, af, æf (“from, off, away”), from Proto-West Germanic *ab, from Proto-Germanic *ab (“from”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epo (“from, off, back”). Doublet of of.

examples.text: Today is the International Day of Friendship.

translations.de: Heute ist der Internationale Tag der Freundschaft.
translations.fr: Aujourd'hui, c'est la Journée Internationale de l'Amitié.
translations.pt: Hoje é o Dia Internacional da Amizade.

examples.text: You can't trust anyone these days.

translations.de: Heutzutage kann man niemandem mehr vertrauen.
translations.fr: On ne peut faire confiance à personne de nos jours.
translations.pt: Você não pode confiar em ninguém hoje em dia.

examples.text: I'm leaving the day after tomorrow.

translations.de: Ich reise übermorgen ab.
translations.fr: Je pars après-demain.
translations.pt: Vou embora depois de amanhã.

examples.text: Did you come the day before yesterday?

translations.de: Bist du vorgestern gekommen?
translations.fr: Es-tu venue avant-hier ?
translations.pt: Você veio antes de ontem?

more.definition: The time when the Sun is above the horizon and it lights the sky.; A period of time equal or almost equal to a full day-night cycle, being 24 hours long.; The time taken for the Sun to seem to be in the same place in the sky twice; a solar day.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English day, from Old English dæġ, from Proto-West Germanic *dag, from Proto-Germanic *dagaz (“day”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰegʷʰ- (“to burn”).

examples.text: Do you watch the news every day?

translations.de: Siehst du jeden Tag die Nachrichten?
translations.fr: Regardez-vous les informations tous les jours ?
translations.pt: Você assiste ao noticiário todos os dias?

examples.text: Can you stay for a few days?

translations.de: Kannst du ein paar Tage bleiben?
translations.fr: Peux-tu rester quelques jours ?
translations.pt: Você pode ficar por alguns dias?

examples.text: Tom has been working all day long.

translations.de: Tom arbeitet schon den ganzen Tag.
translations.fr: Tom a travaillé toute la journée.
translations.pt: Tom tem trabalhado o dia todo.

examples.text: I speak with my mother every day.

translations.de: Ich spreche jeden Tag mit meiner Mutter.
translations.fr: Je parle à ma mère tous les jours.
translations.pt: Eu falo com a minha mãe todo dia.

more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English day, from Old English dæġ, from Proto-West Germanic *dag, from Proto-Germanic *dagaz (“day”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰegʷʰ- (“to burn”).

examples.text: True friendships are even rarer than diamonds.

translations.de: Wahre Freundschaften sind seltener noch als Diamanten.
translations.fr: Une véritable amitié est encore plus rare qu'un diamant.
translations.pt: Amizades verdadeiras são ainda mais raras que diamantes.

examples.text: It is cold there, even in summer.

translations.de: Es ist kalt dort, sogar im Sommer.
translations.fr: Il fait froid, là-bas, même en été !
translations.pt: É frio lá, mesmo no verão.

examples.text: He doesn't even know my name.

translations.de: Er kennt nicht einmal meinen Namen.
translations.fr: Il ne sait pas même mon nom.
translations.pt: Ele nem sequer sabe meu nome.

examples.text: Tom doesn't even know my name.

translations.de: Tom kennt nicht einmal meinen Namen.
translations.fr: Tom ne connaît même pas mon nom.
translations.pt: Tom nem sequer sabe o meu nome.

more.definition: Flat and level.; Without great variation.; Equal in proportion, quantity, size, etc.
more.etymology: From Middle English even, from Old English efn (“flat; level, even, equal”), from Proto-West Germanic *ebn, from Proto-Germanic *ebnaz, from Proto-Indo-European *(h₁)em-no- (“equal, straight; flat, level, even”).

examples.text: I didn't even think about that.

translations.de: Daran habe ich überhaupt nicht gedacht.
translations.fr: Je n'y ai même pas pensé.
translations.pt: Eu nem sequer pensei nisso.

examples.text: I don't even have a boyfriend.

translations.de: Ich habe noch nicht einmal einen Freund.
translations.fr: Je n'ai même pas de petit ami.

examples.text: She wouldn't even look at me.

more.definition: In reality (used to imply an extreme example in the case mentioned).; Used to emphasise a comparative.; Used to indicate a further degree of comparison.

examples.text: Cats can see even in dark places.

translations.de: Katzen können selbst an dunklen Orten etwas sehen.

examples.text: The investigation hasn't progressed even one step.

translations.de: Die Ermittlungen sind keinen Schritt weitergekommen.

translations.pt: A investigação não progrediu nem mesmo um passo.

examples.text: She didn't even let me kiss her.

translations.de: Sie erlaubte mir nicht einmal, sie zu küssen.
translations.fr: Elle ne m'a même pas laissé l'embrasser.
translations.pt: Nem mesmo permitiu que eu a beijasse.

examples.text: They are not coming even if they can.

translations.de: Sie werden nicht kommen, selbst wenn sie es könnten.
translations.fr: Ils ne viennent pas, même s'ils le peuvent.
translations.pt: Eles não vêm, mesmo que possam.

more.definition: An even number.
more.etymology: From Middle English even, from Old English efn (“flat; level, even, equal”), from Proto-West Germanic *ebn, from Proto-Germanic *ebnaz, from Proto-Indo-European *(h₁)em-no- (“equal, straight; flat, level, even”).

examples.text: I didn't even know his name.

translations.de: Ich kannte nicht einmal seinen Namen.
translations.fr: J'ignorais même son nom.
translations.pt: Eu nem sequer sabia o nome dele.

examples.text: It didn't even cross my mind.

translations.de: Das ist mir nicht einmal eingefallen.
translations.fr: Ça ne m'a même pas traversé l'esprit.
translations.pt: Isso nem passou por minha cabeça.

examples.text: Tom doesn't even know I exist.

translations.de: Tom weiß nicht einmal, dass es mich gibt.
translations.fr: Tom ne sait même pas que j'existe.
translations.pt: Tom nem sequer sabe que eu existo.

examples.text: She wouldn't even speak to him.

translations.de: Sie spricht nicht einmal mit ihm.
translations.fr: Elle ne voudrait même pas lui parler.
translations.pt: Ela nem falaria com ele.

more.definition: To make flat and level.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *(h₁)ém-no-der. Inherited from Middle English evenen, from Old English efnian, from Proto-West Germanic *ebnōn, from Proto-Germanic *ebnōną, from *ebnaz (“even”) + *-ōną (factitive suffix).

examples.text: I'm sorry, but the answer is no.

translations.de: Es tut mir leid, aber die Antwort lautet „Nein!“
translations.fr: Je suis désolé, mais la réponse est « non ».
translations.pt: Sinto muito, mas a resposta é não.

examples.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear you.

translations.de: Entschuldige! Ich habe dich nicht gehört.
translations.fr: Je suis désolé, je ne t'ai pas entendu.
translations.pt: Me desculpe, eu não te ouvi.

examples.text: I'm sorry about last night.

translations.de: Das gestern Abend tut mir leid.
translations.fr: Je suis désolé pour hier soir.
translations.pt: Sinto muito por ontem à noite.

examples.text: I'm very sorry, but I can't.

translations.de: Ich bedaure sehr, aber ich kann nicht.
translations.fr: Je regrette beaucoup, mais je ne peux pas.
translations.pt: Sinto muito, mas não posso.

more.definition: Of a person, regretful or apologetic for one's actions.; Of a person, grieved or saddened, especially by the loss of something or someone.; Poor, pitifully sad or regrettable.
more.etymology: From Middle English sory, from Old English sāriġ (“feeling or expressing grief, sorry, grieved, sorrowful, sad, mournful, bitter”), from Proto-West Germanic *sairag, from Proto-Germanic *sairagaz (“sad”), from Proto-Indo-European *seh₂yro (“hard, rough, painful”).

examples.text: I'm sorry, the flight is full.

translations.de: Tut mir leid, der Flug ist voll.
translations.fr: Je suis désolé, ce vol est plein.
translations.pt: Sinto muito, o voo está lotado.

examples.text: I'm sorry I was so rude.

translations.de: Es tut mir leid, dass ich so grob war.
translations.fr: Je suis désolé d'avoir été si grossier.
translations.pt: Lamento ter sido tão grosseiro.

examples.text: I'm sorry to have disturbed you.

translations.de: Es tut mir leid, dass ich Sie gestört habe.
translations.fr: Je suis désolé de t'avoir dérangé.
translations.pt: Desculpe por tê-lo incomodado.

examples.text: I'm sorry but your excuses are unacceptable.

translations.de: Es tut mir leid, aber Ihre Ausreden sind inakzeptabel.
translations.fr: Je suis désolé mais vos excuses sont inacceptables.
translations.pt: Sinto muito, mas suas desculpas são inaceitáveis.

more.definition: Expresses regret, remorse, or sorrow.; Said as a request to excuse one's unintentional behaviors.; Said as a request to pass somebody.
more.etymology: From Middle English sory, from Old English sāriġ (“feeling or expressing grief, sorry, grieved, sorrowful, sad, mournful, bitter”), from Proto-West Germanic *sairag, from Proto-Germanic *sairagaz (“sad”), from Proto-Indo-European *seh₂yro (“hard, rough, painful”).

examples.text: I'm sorry, I don't dance.

translations.de: Tut mir leid, ich tanze nicht.
translations.fr: Désolée, je ne danse pas.
translations.pt: Desculpe, eu não danço.

examples.text: I'm sorry that I disappointed you.

translations.de: Es tut mir leid, daß ich Sie enttäuscht habe.
translations.fr: Je suis désolé de t'avoir déçu.
translations.pt: Me desculpe por ter te desapontado.

examples.text: I'm sorry about what happened today.

translations.de: Es tut mir leid, was heute passiert ist.
translations.fr: Je suis désolé de ce qui est arrivé aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Lamento pelo que aconteceu hoje.

examples.text: I want to say I'm sorry.

translations.de: Ich möchte sagen, es tut mir leid.
translations.fr: Je veux dire que je suis désolé.
translations.pt: Quero dizer que sinto muito.

more.definition: The act of saying sorry; an apology.
more.etymology: From Middle English sory, from Old English sāriġ (“feeling or expressing grief, sorry, grieved, sorrowful, sad, mournful, bitter”), from Proto-West Germanic *sairag, from Proto-Germanic *sairagaz (“sad”), from Proto-Indo-European *seh₂yro (“hard, rough, painful”).

examples.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand.

translations.de: Tut mir leid, ich versteh das nicht.
translations.fr: Je suis désolé, je ne comprends pas.
translations.pt: Desculpe, não compreendo.

examples.text: I'm sorry I yelled at you.

translations.de: Es tut mir leid, dass ich Sie angeschrien habe!
translations.fr: Je suis désolé de t'avoir crié après.
translations.pt: Desculpe eu ter gritado com você.

examples.text: I'm sorry for the late response.

translations.de: Ich möchte mich für die späte Antwort entschuldigen.
translations.fr: Je suis désolé de la réponse tardive.
translations.pt: Sinto muito pela resposta tardia.

examples.text: I'm sorry, but it's impossible.

translations.de: Es tut mir leid, aber das ist unmöglich.
translations.fr: Je suis désolé mais c'est impossible.
translations.pt: Sinto muito, mas é impossível.

more.etymology: From Middle English sory, from Old English sāriġ (“feeling or expressing grief, sorry, grieved, sorrowful, sad, mournful, bitter”), from Proto-West Germanic *sairag, from Proto-Germanic *sairagaz (“sad”), from Proto-Indo-European *seh₂yro (“hard, rough, painful”).

examples.text: Don't try to make me angry.

translations.de: Versuch nicht, mich zu ärgern!
translations.fr: N'essayez pas de m'énerver.
translations.pt: Não tente me deixar nervoso.

examples.text: You have to try to stay awake.

translations.de: Du musst versuchen, wach zu bleiben.
translations.fr: Tu dois essayer de rester éveillé.
translations.pt: Você precisa tentar ficar acordado.

examples.text: I've always wanted to try it.

translations.de: Ich wollte es schon immer mal probieren.
translations.fr: J'ai toujours voulu l'essayer.
translations.pt: Eu sempre quis experimentar.

examples.text: At least try to come on time.

translations.de: Versuche wenigstens, pünktlich zu sein!
translations.fr: Essaie au moins de venir à l'heure !
translations.pt: Pelo menos, tente ser pontual.

more.etymology: From Middle English trye, trie, probably from Old French trié, past participle of Old French trier (“to try”).

examples.text: Don't try to change the subject.

translations.de: Versuch nicht, das Thema zu wechseln!
translations.fr: N'essayez pas de changer de sujet.
translations.pt: Não tente mudar de assunto.

examples.text: I think that we should try again.

translations.de: Ich glaube, wir sollten es noch mal versuchen.
translations.fr: Je crois que nous devrions encore essayer.
translations.pt: Acho que devemos tentar de novo.

examples.text: We must try to protect the environment.

translations.de: Wir müssen versuchen, unsere Umwelt zu schützen.
translations.fr: Nous devons essayer de protéger l'environnement.
translations.pt: Devemos tentar proteger o meio ambiente.

examples.text: Let's try to understand one another.

translations.de: Lass uns versuchen, einander zu verstehen.
translations.fr: Essayons de nous comprendre l'un l'autre.
translations.pt: Tentemos entender um ao outro.

more.definition: An attempt.; An act of tasting or sampling.; A score in rugby league and rugby union, analogous to a touchdown in American football.
more.etymology: From Middle English trien (“to separate out, sift, choose, select, evaluate, try a legal case”), from Anglo-Norman trier, triher, triere (“to divide, separate, choose, select, prove, determine, try a case”), Old French trier (“to choose, pick out or separate from others, sift, cull”), of uncertain origin. Cognate with Occitan triar (“to choose, sort, scrutinise, peel”), Catalan triar (“to pick, choose, decide”).

examples.text: The weasel tries to grab the mice.

translations.de: Das Wiesel versucht, sich die Mäuse zu schnappen.
translations.fr: La belette essaie d'attraper les souris.
translations.pt: A doninha tenta pegar os ratos.

examples.text: My father is trying to stop drinking.

translations.de: Mein Vater versucht, mit dem Trinken aufzuhören.
translations.fr: Mon père essaie d'arrêter de boire.
translations.pt: Meu pai está tentando parar de beber.

examples.text: I'll try to keep you informed.

translations.de: Ich werde versuchen, dich auf dem Laufenden zu halten.
translations.fr: Je vais essayer de te tenir informé.
translations.pt: Vou tentar te manter informado.

examples.text: I tried to stop that from happening.

translations.de: Ich wollte verhindern, dass das geschähe.
translations.fr: J'ai essayé d'empêcher cela.
translations.pt: Eu tentei impedir que isso acontecesse.

more.definition: To attempt; to endeavour. Followed by infinitive.; To make an experiment. Usually followed by a present participle.; To put to test.
more.etymology: From Middle English trien (“to separate out, sift, choose, select, evaluate, try a legal case”), from Anglo-Norman trier, triher, triere (“to divide, separate, choose, select, prove, determine, try a case”), Old French trier (“to choose, pick out or separate from others, sift, cull”), of uncertain origin. Cognate with Occitan triar (“to choose, sort, scrutinise, peel”), Catalan triar (“to pick, choose, decide”).

examples.text: Do you have any books in French?

translations.de: Hast du französischsprachige Bücher?
translations.fr: As-tu des livres en français ?
translations.pt: Você tem algum livro em francês?

examples.text: I don't understand any of this.

examples.text: Don't pay any attention to him.

translations.de: Beachte ihn gar nicht!
translations.fr: Ne fais pas attention à lui.
translations.pt: Não dê atenção a ele.

more.definition: To even the slightest extent; at all.; Used before different, before comparatives with more and less, and idiomatically before other comparatives, generally in interrogative, hypothetical, or negative contexts.; Used to modify a verb, generally a finite verb or a non-finite verb in object position.
more.etymology: From Middle English any, eny, ony, ani, aniȝ, eniȝ, æniȝ, from Old English ǣniġ (“any”), from Proto-West Germanic *ainīg, *ainag, from Proto-Germanic *ainagaz, from Proto-Germanic *ainaz (“one”), equivalent to one + -y.

examples.text: Cheeky children don't get any sweets!

translations.de: Freche Kinder bekommen keine Bonbons!

examples.text: I don't wear glasses any more.

translations.de: Ich trage keine Brille mehr.
translations.fr: Je ne porte plus de lunettes.
translations.pt: Não uso mais óculos.

examples.text: I didn't get any messages yesterday.

translations.de: Ich habe gestern keine Nachrichten erhalten.

translations.pt: Ontem eu não recebi nenhuma mensagem.

translations.fr: Je ne parle aucune langue romane.
translations.pt: Não sei falar nenhuma língua românica.

more.definition: One at all; at least one; at least one kind of; some; a positive quantity of.; A/an, each or some, no matter its/their identity or nature.; An unspecified but imminent (second, minute, day etc.).
more.etymology: From Middle English any, eny, ony, ani, aniȝ, eniȝ, æniȝ, from Old English ǣniġ (“any”), from Proto-West Germanic *ainīg, *ainag, from Proto-Germanic *ainagaz, from Proto-Germanic *ainaz (“one”), equivalent to one + -y.

examples.text: I don't have any other options.

translations.de: Ich mag Weihnachten nicht mehr.

examples.text: Do any of you have a pencil?

more.definition: Any thing(s) or person(s).
more.etymology: From Middle English any, eny, ony, ani, aniȝ, eniȝ, æniȝ, from Old English ǣniġ (“any”), from Proto-West Germanic *ainīg, *ainag, from Proto-Germanic *ainagaz, from Proto-Germanic *ainaz (“one”), equivalent to one + -y.

examples.text: I don't need your help anymore.

translations.de: Ich brauche deine Hilfe nicht mehr.

examples.text: I'm glad I could help you.

more.definition: A cry of distress or an urgent request for assistance.; A way to signal uncontrollable laughter; implying the risk of dying of laughter and needing assistance.
more.etymology: From Middle English helpen, from Old English helpan (“to help, aid, assist, benefit, relieve, cure”), from Proto-West Germanic *helpan, Proto-Germanic *helpaną (“to help”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱelb-, *ḱelp- (“to help”).

examples.text: I can't help you with that.

translations.de: Ich kann dir dabei nicht helfen.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas t'aider avec ça.

examples.text: The medicine didn't help at all.

translations.de: Das Medikament hat überhaupt nicht geholfen.
translations.fr: Les médicaments n'ont pas du tout aidé.
translations.pt: O remédio não ajudou nada.

examples.text: We won't need your help today.

translations.de: Wir werden deine Hilfe heute nicht brauchen.
translations.fr: Nous n'aurons pas besoin de ton aide, aujourd'hui.

examples.text: I don't want to help you.

translations.de: Ich will dir nicht helfen.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas vous aider.
translations.pt: Não quero te ajudar.

more.definition: Action given to provide assistance; aid.; Something or someone which provides assistance with a task.; Documentation provided with computer software that could be accessed using the computer.
more.etymology: From Middle English help, from Old English help (“help, aid, assistance, relief”), from Proto-Germanic *helpō (“help”), *hilpiz, *hulpiz, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱelb-, *ḱelp- (“to help”).

examples.text: I don't need anyone's help.

translations.de: Ich brauche niemandes Hilfe.
translations.fr: Je n'ai besoin de l'aide de personne.
translations.pt: Eu não preciso da ajuda de ninguém.

examples.text: The frogs' croaking helped me fall asleep.

translations.de: Das Quaken der Frösche half mir beim Einschlafen.
translations.fr: Le coassement des grenouilles m'aida à m'endormir.
translations.pt: O coaxo dos sapos me ajudou a adormecer.

examples.text: You can always ask me for help.

translations.de: Du kannst mich immer um Hilfe bitten.
translations.fr: Vous pouvez toujours me demander de l'aide.
translations.pt: Você pode sempre me pedir ajuda.

examples.text: I said that I would help her.

translations.de: Ich sagte, dass ich ihr helfen würde.
translations.fr: J'ai dit que je l'aiderais.
translations.pt: Disse que a ajudaria.

examples.text: Can you help me, please?

translations.de: Kannst du mir bitte helfen?
translations.fr: Peux-tu m'aider, s'il te plaît ?
translations.pt: Você pode me ajudar, por favor?

examples.text: He helped his sister with the move.

translations.de: Er hat seiner Schwester beim Umzug geholfen.
translations.fr: Il a aidé sa sœur à déménager.
translations.pt: Ele ajudou a irmã com a mudança.

more.definition: To provide assistance to (someone or something).; To assist (a person) in getting something, especially food or drink at table; used with to.; To contribute in some way to.
collocations: help yourself — take what you want
more.etymology: From Middle English helpen, from Old English helpan (“to help, aid, assist, benefit, relieve, cure”), from Proto-West Germanic *helpan, Proto-Germanic *helpaną (“to help”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱelb-, *ḱelp- (“to help”).

examples.text: I can't wait to meet him.

translations.de: Ich kann es kaum erwarten, ihn kennenzulernen.
translations.fr: Je suis impatient de le rencontrer.
translations.pt: Não vejo a hora de conhecê-lo.

examples.text: I don't usually wait for anybody.

translations.de: Ich warte gewöhnlich auf niemanden.
translations.fr: Je n'attends habituellement personne.
translations.pt: Não costumo esperar por ninguém.

examples.text: I want you to wait for me.

translations.de: Ich möchte, dass du auf mich wartest.
translations.fr: Je veux que tu m'attendes.
translations.pt: Quero que você me espere.

examples.text: We can't wait for the weekend.

translations.de: Wir können nicht auf das Wochenende warten.
translations.fr: Nous sommes impatients d'être en week-end.
translations.pt: Não podemos esperar o fim de semana.

more.definition: Tells the other speaker to stop talking, typing etc. for a moment, often to allow clarification.
more.etymology: From Middle English waiten, from Anglo-Norman waiter, waitier (compare French guetter from Old French gaitier, guaitier), from Frankish *wahtwēn (“to watch, guard”), derivative of Frankish *wahtu (“guard, watch”), from Proto-Germanic *wahtwō (“guard, watch”), from Proto-Indo-European *weǵ- (“to be fresh, cheerful, awake”).

examples.text: I'll wait at the bus stop.

translations.de: Ich warte an der Bushaltestelle.

translations.pt: Eu vou esperar no ponto de ônibus.

examples.text: Let's wait until it stops raining.

translations.de: Warten wir, bis es aufhört zu regnen!
translations.fr: Attendons que la pluie cesse.
translations.pt: Vamos esperar até a chuva parar.

examples.text: I'll wait for you in here.

translations.de: Ich warte hier drinnen auf dich.
translations.fr: Je vous attends ici.
translations.pt: Eu vou te esperar aqui.

examples.text: Why don't you wait till morning?

translations.de: Warum wartest du nicht bis zum Morgen?
translations.fr: Pourquoi n'attends-tu pas jusqu'au matin ?
translations.pt: Por que vocês não esperam até de manhã?

more.definition: A delay.; An ambush.; Ellipsis of wait state.
more.etymology: From Middle English waiten, from Anglo-Norman waiter, waitier (compare French guetter from Old French gaitier, guaitier), from Frankish *wahtwēn (“to watch, guard”), derivative of Frankish *wahtu (“guard, watch”), from Proto-Germanic *wahtwō (“guard, watch”), from Proto-Indo-European *weǵ- (“to be fresh, cheerful, awake”).

examples.text: You have to wait in the queue.

translations.de: Sie müssen sich anstellen.
translations.fr: Il faut que vous fassiez la queue.
translations.pt: Tem que esperar na fila.

examples.text: I'm just waiting for a friend.

translations.de: Ich warte gerade auf einen Freund.
translations.fr: J'attends juste une amie.
translations.pt: Estou só à espera de um amigo.

examples.text: She waited for you for two hours.

translations.de: Sie hat zwei Stunden auf dich gewartet.
translations.fr: Elle vous a attendu pendant deux heures.
translations.pt: Ela te esperou por duas horas.

examples.text: Can you wait two minutes for me?

translations.de: Kannst du zwei Minuten auf mich warten?
translations.fr: Pouvez-vous m'attendre deux minutes ?
translations.pt: Podes esperar por mim dois minutos?

examples.text: I am waiting for the bus.

translations.de: Ich warte auf den Bus.
translations.fr: J'attends le bus.
translations.pt: Estou esperando o ônibus.

examples.text: We waited an hour for you.

translations.de: Wir haben eine Stunde auf dich gewartet.
translations.fr: Nous t'avons attendu pendant une heure.
translations.pt: Esperamos uma hora por você.

more.definition: To delay movement or action until some event or time; to remain neglected or in readiness.; To wait tables; to serve customers in a restaurant or other eating establishment.; To remain faithful to one’s partner or betrothed during a prolonged period of absence.

examples.text: The two friends drank seven beers together.

examples.text: Last year I read two hundred books.

translations.pt: No ano passado, eu li duzentos livros.

examples.text: How long have you two been married?

more.definition: A numerical value equal to 2; the number following one and preceding three.; Describing a set or group with two elements.

examples.text: I should've expected that to happen.

examples.text: I wanted to see what would happen.

translations.de: Ich wollte sehen, was geschehen würde.
translations.fr: Je voulais voir ce qui arriverait.
translations.pt: Eu queria ver o que aconteceria.

examples.text: A lot can happen in a year.

translations.de: In einem Jahr kann viel passieren.
translations.fr: Beaucoup peut arriver en une année.
translations.pt: Muita coisa pode acontecer em um ano.

more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *kob-der. Proto-Germanic *hampijanąder. Proto-Germanic *hampijanąder. examples.text: We don't want that to happen.

examples.text: Nothing interesting happens in this small town.

more.definition: To occur or take place.; To do or occur by chance or unexpectedly.; To encounter by chance.

examples.text: I feel bad about lying to him.

translations.de: Ich habe ein schlechtes Gewissen, dass ich ihn belogen habe.
translations.fr: Ça me met mal à l'aise de lui mentir.
translations.pt: Eu me sinto mal em mentir para ele.

examples.text: This toilet paper feels like sandpaper.

translations.de: Das Toilettenpapier hier fühlt sich wie Schleifpapier an.
translations.fr: Ce papier toilette est comme du papier émeri.
translations.pt: Este papel higiênico parece lixa.

examples.text: I really don't feel like talking.

translations.de: Ich bin wirklich nicht in Redelaune.
translations.fr: Je n'ai vraiment pas envie de parler.
translations.pt: Eu não estou com vontade de conversar.

examples.text: I don't feel like answering questions.

translations.de: Mir ist nicht danach, Fragen zu beantworten.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas envie de répondre à des questions.

more.definition: A perception experienced mainly or solely through the sense of touch.; A vague mental impression.; An act of fondling.

examples.text: I feel young and full of energy.

translations.pt: Eu me sinto jovem e cheio de energia.

examples.text: She felt something crawl up her leg.

translations.de: Sie spürte, wie etwas ihr Bein hinaufkrabbelte.
translations.fr: Elle sentit quelque chose lui grimper le long de la jambe.
translations.pt: Ela sentiu algo subindo na perna dela.

examples.text: The tongue of a cat feels rough.

translations.de: Die Zunge einer Katze fühlt sich rau an.

translations.pt: A língua de um gato é áspera.

examples.text: I feel a whole lot better today.

translations.de: Es geht mir heute schon sehr viel besser.
translations.fr: Je me sens beaucoup mieux aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Estou me sentindo bem melhor hoje.

more.definition: To become aware of through the skin; to use the sense of touch on.; To find one's way (literally or figuratively) by touching or using cautious movements.; To receive information by touch or by any neurons other than those responsible for sight, smell, taste, or hearing.
more.etymology: From Middle English felen, from Old English fēlan, from Proto-West Germanic *fōlijan. Cognate with Dutch voelen and German fühlen.

examples.text: She may be proud of her daughter.

translations.de: Sie kann stolz auf ihre Tochter sein.
translations.fr: Elle peut être fière de sa fille.

examples.text: He may not be able to come.

examples.text: Tom may choose whichever color he likes.

translations.de: Tom darf sich jegliche Farbe aussuchen, die ihm gefällt.
translations.fr: Tom peut choisir la couleur que bon lui semble.
translations.pt: O Tom pode escolher a cor que ele quiser.

examples.text: You may bring whoever wants to come.

translations.de: Wer kommen möchte, den bring ruhig mit!
translations.fr: Tu peux emmener qui veut venir.
translations.pt: Você pode trazer quem quiser vir.

more.definition: The hawthorn bush or its blossoms.

examples.text: Your package might arrive later than expected.

translations.de: Ihr Paket könnte später als erwartet ankommen.
translations.fr: Votre colis pourrait arriver plus tard que prévu.
translations.pt: Seu pacote pode chegar mais tarde do que o esperado.

examples.text: Excuse me, may I have a spoon?

translations.de: Entschuldigen Sie! Könnte ich wohl einen Löffel bekommen?
translations.fr: Excusez-moi, est-ce que je pourrais avoir une cuillère ?
translations.pt: Por favor, quer me trazer uma colher?

examples.text: It may take longer than we expected.

translations.de: Es kann länger dauern als erwartet.
translations.fr: Cela peut prendre plus de temps que prévu.
translations.pt: Pode demorar mais do que esperávamos.

examples.text: I thought it might be a possibility.

translations.de: Ich hielt es für eine Möglichkeit.
translations.fr: Je pensais que cela pourrait être une possibilité.
translations.pt: Achei que poderia ser uma possibilidade.

more.definition: To be able to go.; To have permission to, be allowed. Used in granting permission and in questions to make polite requests.; Expressing a present possibility; possibly.
more.etymology: From Middle English magen, mauen, mawe, mawen, mayen, maȝen, mouin, mow, mowen, moȝen, mugen, from Old English magan, from Proto-West Germanic *magan, from Proto-Germanic *maganą (“to be able, may”), from Proto-Indo-European *(me)mógʰe (“to be able”), from *megʰ- (“to be able”).

examples.text: I'm pretty sure Tom can win.

translations.de: Ich bin mir ziemlich sicher, dass Tom gewinnen kann.
translations.fr: Je suis presque sûr que Tom peut gagner.
translations.pt: Tenho quase certeza de que Tom pode vencer.

examples.text: I'm not too sure about that.

translations.fr: Je n'en suis pas si sûre.
translations.pt: Não tenho muita certeza sobre isso.

examples.text: I'm sure that wasn't intentional.

translations.de: Das war sicher nicht mit Absicht.
translations.fr: Je suis sûr que ce n'était pas intentionnel.
translations.pt: Eu tenho certeza de que isso não foi intencional.

examples.text: I'm sure you have other skills.

translations.de: Du hast sicher andere Begabungen.
translations.fr: Tu as sûrement d'autres talents.

more.definition: Physically secure and certain, non-failing, reliable.; Certain in one's knowledge or belief.; Certain to act or be a specified way.
more.etymology: From Middle English sure, seur, sur, from Middle French sur or Old French seür, from Latin sēcūrus (“secure”, literally “carefree”), from sē- (“apart”) + cūra (“care”) (compare Old English orsorg (“carefree”), from or- (“without”) + sorg (“care”)). See cure. Doublet of secure and the now obsolete or dialectal sicker (“certain, safe”).

examples.text: I'm not sure of it either.

translations.fr: Je n'en suis pas sûr non plus.
translations.pt: Não tenho certeza, também.

examples.text: I'm sure you're very busy.

translations.de: Du wirst bestimmt Erfolg haben.
translations.fr: Je suis sûr que tu vas réussir.
translations.pt: Tenho certeza que você conseguirá.

more.definition: Without doubt, certainly.
more.etymology: From Middle English sure, seur, sur, from Middle French sur or Old French seür, from Latin sēcūrus (“secure”, literally “carefree”), from sē- (“apart”) + cūra (“care”) (compare Old English orsorg (“carefree”), from or- (“without”) + sorg (“care”)). examples.text: I'm going to make sure of that.

more.etymology: From Middle English sure, seur, sur, from Middle French sur or Old French seür, from Latin sēcūrus (“secure”, literally “carefree”), from sē- (“apart”) + cūra (“care”) (compare Old English orsorg (“carefree”), from or- (“without”) + sorg (“care”)). translations.de: Wie viele Äpfel hast du heute gegessen?

more.etymology: From Middle English many, mani, moni, from Old English maniġ, moniġ, maneġ (“many”), from Proto-West Germanic *manag, from Proto-Germanic *managaz (“many; much”), from Proto-Indo-European *menegʰ-, *mengʰ- (“many, sufficient”) or Proto-Indo-European *méǵh₂- (“big, great”).

examples.text: This house was built a year ago.

examples.text: Failures are always a part of life.

translations.de: Misserfolge gehören immer zum Leben dazu.

examples.text: You are the sunshine of my life.

translations.de: Du bist der Sonnenschein meines Lebens.

translations.de: Sein Privatleben interessiert mich nicht.

examples.text: Tom isn't used to city life.

translations.fr: Il est l'amour de ma vie.

translations.de: Er erzählte mir seine Lebensgeschichte.
translations.fr: Il me conta l'histoire de sa vie.

more.definition: The state of organisms preceding their death, characterized by biological processes such as metabolism and reproduction and distinguishing them from inanimate objects; the state of being alive and living.; The status possessed by any of a number of entities, including animals, plants, fungi, bacteria, and sometimes viruses, which have the properties of replication and metabolism.; The animating principle or force that keeps an inorganic thing or concept metaphorically alive (dynamic, relevant, etc) and makes it a "living document", "living constitution", etc.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *leyp-der. Proto-Germanic *lībanąder. From Middle English lyf, from Old English līf, from Proto-West Germanic *līb, from Proto-Germanic *lībą (“life, body”), from *lībaną (“to remain, stay, be left”), from Proto-Indo-European *leyp- (“to stick, glue”).

examples.text: Sami destroyed the life of his children.

translations.de: Sami hat das Leben seiner Kinder zerstört.
translations.fr: Sami a détruit la vie de ses enfants.

translations.pt: Não existe vida na Lua.

more.definition: To replace components whose operational lifetime has expired.

examples.text: Do you love each other very much?

translations.de: Liebt ihr euch sehr?
translations.fr: Vous aimez-vous beaucoup l'un l'autre ?
translations.pt: Vocês se amam muito?

examples.text: California and Nevada border on each other.

translations.de: Kalifornien und Nevada grenzen aneinander.
translations.fr: La Californie et le Nevada se jouxtent.
translations.pt: Califórnia e Nevada fazem fronteira entre si.

examples.text: The twins are indistinguishable from each other.

translations.de: Die Zwillinge lassen sich nicht auseinanderhalten.
translations.fr: Les jumeaux sont indifférenciables entre eux.

examples.text: I saw her just the other day.

translations.de: Ich habe sie erst neulich gesehen.
translations.fr: Je l'ai vue l'autre jour.
translations.pt: Eu vi ela no outro dia.

more.definition: See other (determiner) below.; Second.; Alien.
more.etymology: From Middle English other, from Old English ōþer (“other, second”), from Proto-West Germanic *ą̄þar, *anþar, from Proto-Germanic *anþeraz (“other, second”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énteros (“other”).

examples.text: One boy is taller than the other.

translations.de: Der eine Junge ist größer als der andere.
translations.fr: Un garçon est plus grand que l'autre.
translations.pt: Um menino é mais alto do que o outro.

examples.text: When can we see each other again?

translations.de: Wann können wir uns das nächstemal treffen?
translations.fr: Quand pourrons-nous nous revoir ?
translations.pt: Quando poderemos nos ver de novo?

examples.text: One's new. The other's old.

translations.de: Eines ist neu. Das Andere ist alt.
translations.fr: L'un est neuf, l'autre est ancien.
translations.pt: Um é novo. O outro é velho.

examples.text: How long have you known each other?

translations.de: Wie lange kennen Sie sich schon?
translations.fr: Depuis combien de temps vous vous connaissez ?
translations.pt: Há quanto tempo vocês se conhecem?

more.etymology: From Middle English other, from Old English ōþer (“other, second”), from Proto-West Germanic *ą̄þar, *anþar, from Proto-Germanic *anþeraz (“other, second”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énteros (“other”).

examples.text: I'm not like the other girls.

translations.de: Ich bin nicht wie die anderen Mädchen.
translations.fr: Je ne suis pas comme les autres filles.
translations.pt: Não sou como as outras garotas,

examples.text: We see each other once a month.

translations.de: Wir sehen uns einmal im Monat.
translations.fr: On se voit une fois par mois.
translations.pt: A gente se vê uma vez por mês.

examples.text: I think the other path is safer.

translations.de: Ich glaube, der andere Weg ist sicherer.
translations.fr: Je pense que l'autre chemin est plus sûr.
translations.pt: Eu acho que o outro caminho é mais seguro.

examples.text: We've spoken to each other before.

translations.de: Wir haben schon einmal miteinander gesprochen.
translations.fr: Nous nous sommes déjà entretenus.
translations.pt: Nós já nos falamos antes.

more.definition: Not the one or ones previously referred to.
more.etymology: From Middle English other, from Old English ōþer (“other, second”), from Proto-West Germanic *ą̄þar, *anþar, from Proto-Germanic *anþeraz (“other, second”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énteros (“other”).

examples.text: Don't worry about what others say.

translations.de: Scher dich nicht darum, was andere sagen.
translations.fr: Ne te soucie pas de ce que les autres disent.
translations.pt: Não se preocupe com o que os outros dizem.

examples.text: I saw your brother the other day.

translations.de: Ich habe letztens deinen Bruder gesehen.
translations.fr: J'ai vu ton grand frère l'autre jour.
translations.pt: Eu vi seu irmão outro dia desse.

examples.text: We have known each other since childhood.

translations.de: Wir kennen uns schon seit unserer Kindheit.
translations.fr: Nous nous connaissons depuis l'enfance.
translations.pt: Nós nos conhecemos desde a infância.

examples.text: The two ladies smiled at each other.

translations.de: Die zwei Damen lächelten einander an.
translations.fr: Les deux femmes se sourirent.
translations.pt: As duas moças sorriram entre si.

more.definition: An other, another (person, etc), more often rendered as another.; The other one; the second of two.
more.etymology: From Middle English other, from Old English ōþer (“other, second”), from Proto-West Germanic *ą̄þar, *anþar, from Proto-Germanic *anþeraz (“other, second”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énteros (“other”).

examples.text: Why aren't you with the others?

translations.de: Warum bist du denn nicht bei den anderen?
translations.fr: Pourquoi n'es-tu pas avec les autres ?
translations.pt: Por que você não está com os outros?

examples.text: All the other boys laughed at him.

translations.de: Alle anderen Jungen haben ihn ausgelacht.
translations.fr: Tous les autres garçons riaient de lui.
translations.pt: Todos os outros garotos riam dele.

examples.text: I bought this book the other day.

translations.de: Ich habe mir neulich dieses Buch gekauft.
translations.fr: J'ai acheté ce livre l'autre jour.
translations.pt: Comprei esse livro um dia desses.

examples.text: Some people like cats, others prefer dogs.

translations.de: Manche Leute mögen Katzen, andere eher Hunde.
translations.fr: Certains aiment les chats, d'autres préfèrent les chiens.
translations.pt: Algumas pessoas gostam de gatos, outras preferem cães.

more.definition: To regard, label, or treat as an "other", as not part of the same group; to view as different and alien.; To treat as different or separate; segregate; ostracise.
more.etymology: From Middle English other, from Old English ōþer (“other, second”), from Proto-West Germanic *ą̄þar, *anþar, from Proto-Germanic *anþeraz (“other, second”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énteros (“other”).

examples.text: I don't really want to stop.

translations.de: Ich will eigentlich nicht aufhören.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas vraiment m'arrêter.
translations.pt: Eu realmente não quero parar.

examples.text: This train stops at all stations.

translations.de: Dieser Zug hält an allen Bahnhöfen.
translations.fr: Ce train s'arrête à toutes les stations.
translations.pt: Esse trem para em todas as estações.

examples.text: I can't stop thinking about Tom.

translations.de: Ich kann nicht aufhören, an Tom zu denken.
translations.fr: Je n'arrive pas à ne pas penser à Tom.
translations.pt: Não consigo parar de pensar em Tom.

examples.text: Tom can't stop looking at Mary.

translations.de: Tom kann nicht aufhören, Maria anzusehen.
translations.fr: Tom ne peut pas cesser de contempler Marie.
translations.pt: Tom não consegue parar de olhar para a Mary.

more.definition: A (usually marked) place where buses, trams or trains halt to let passengers get on and off, usually smaller than a station.; An action of stopping; interruption of travel.; That which stops, impedes, or obstructs; an obstacle; an impediment.
more.etymology: From Middle English stoppen, stoppien, from Old English stoppian (“to stop, close”), from Proto-West Germanic *stoppōn, from Proto-Germanic *stuppōną (“to stop, close”), *stuppijaną (“to push, pierce, prick”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tewp-, *(s)tewb- (“to push; stick”), from *(s)tew- (“to bump; impact; butt; push; beat; strike; hit”).

examples.text: The elevator stopped on the second floor.

translations.de: Der Aufzug hielt im zweiten Stock an.
translations.fr: L'ascenseur s’arrêta au deuxième étage.
translations.pt: O elevador parou no segundo andar.

examples.text: How are you going to stop Tom?

translations.de: Wie willst du Tom aufhalten?
translations.fr: Comment vas-tu stopper Tom ?
translations.pt: Como você vai parar o Tom?

examples.text: Don't open before the train stops.

translations.de: Nicht öffnen, bevor der Zug hält.
translations.fr: Ne pas ouvrir avant l'arrêt du train.
translations.pt: Não abra antes do trem parar.

examples.text: Right at that instant, the bus stopped.

translations.de: Genau in dem Moment hielt der Bus an.
translations.fr: Juste à ce moment-là, le bus s'arrêta.
translations.pt: Exatamente naquele momento o ônibus parou.

more.definition: To cease moving.; Not to continue.; To cause (something) to cease moving or progressing.
more.etymology: From Middle English stoppen, stoppien, from Old English stoppian (“to stop, close”), from Proto-West Germanic *stoppōn, from Proto-Germanic *stuppōną (“to stop, close”), *stuppijaną (“to push, pierce, prick”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tewp-, *(s)tewb- (“to push; stick”), from *(s)tew- (“to bump; impact; butt; push; beat; strike; hit”).

examples.text: That's all I need to hear.

translations.de: Mehr muss ich nicht hören.
translations.fr: C'est tout ce que j'ai besoin d'entendre.
translations.pt: É tudo que preciso ouvir.

examples.text: I want to hear it from you.

translations.de: Ich will es von euch hören.
translations.fr: Je veux t'entendre le dire.
translations.pt: Quero escutar isso de você.

examples.text: I don't want to hear it.

translations.de: Ich will das nicht hören.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas entendre ça.
translations.pt: Eu não quero escutar.

examples.text: I was glad to hear the news.

translations.de: Ich habe mich über die Nachricht gefreut.
translations.fr: J'étais content d'entendre la nouvelle.
translations.pt: Fiquei contente em ouvir a notícia.

more.definition: you hear me
more.etymology: From Middle English har, heoren, her, here, heren, from Old English hēran, hīeran, hīran, hȳran (“to hear”), from Proto-West Germanic *hauʀijan, from Proto-Germanic *hauzijaną (“to hear”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ḱh₂owsyéti (“to be sharp-eared”), from *h₂eḱ- (“sharp”) + *h₂ows- (“ear”) + *-yéti (denominative suffix).

examples.text: I want to hear the whole story.

translations.de: Ich will die ganze Geschichte hören.
translations.fr: Je veux entendre toute l'histoire.
translations.pt: Eu quero ouvir a estória toda.

examples.text: I think I need a hearing aid.

translations.de: Ich glaube, ich brauche ein Hörgerät.
translations.fr: Je pense que j'ai besoin d'une aide auditive.
translations.pt: Acho que preciso de aparelho auditivo.

examples.text: That's not what I've heard.

translations.de: Das ist nicht, was ich gehört habe.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas ce que j'ai entendu.
translations.pt: Não foi isso o que eu ouvi.

examples.text: I always wanted to hear that piece.

translations.de: Das Stück wollte ich schon immer mal hören.
translations.fr: J'ai toujours voulu entendre ce morceau.
translations.pt: Sempre quis ouvir essa peça.

more.definition: To perceive sounds through the ear.; To perceive (a sound, or something producing a sound) with the ear, to recognize (something) in an auditory way.; To exercise this faculty intentionally; to listen to.
more.etymology: From Middle English har, heoren, her, here, heren, from Old English hēran, hīeran, hīran, hȳran (“to hear”), from Proto-West Germanic *hauʀijan, from Proto-Germanic *hauzijaną (“to hear”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ḱh₂owsyéti (“to be sharp-eared”), from *h₂eḱ- (“sharp”) + *h₂ows- (“ear”) + *-yéti (denominative suffix).

examples.text: The teacher split the students into groups.

translations.de: Der Lehrer teilte die Schüler in Gruppen ein.
translations.fr: Le professeur a séparé les étudiants en groupes.
translations.pt: O professor separou os estudantes em grupos.

examples.text: I translated everything Tom wrote into French.

translations.de: Ich habe alles, was Tom geschrieben hat, ins Französische übersetzt.
translations.fr: J'ai traduit en français tout ce que Tom a écrit.
translations.pt: Eu traduzi tudo o que Tom escreveu para o francês.

examples.text: I saw Tom going into the cave.

translations.de: Ich habe Tom in die Höhle gehen sehen.
translations.fr: J'ai vu Tom entrer dans la grotte.
translations.pt: Vi o Tom indo para a caverna.

examples.text: Tom and Mary got into their car.

translations.de: Tom und Maria stiegen ins Auto.
translations.fr: Tom et Mary sont montés dans leur voiture.
translations.pt: Tom e Maria entraram no carro.

more.definition: To or towards the inside of.; To or towards the region of.; To the condition or state.
more.etymology: From Middle English in-to, from Old English intō, equivalent to in + to. Cognate with Scots intae.

examples.text: We can't keep on fooling ourselves.

translations.de: Wir müssen aufhören, uns selbst etwas vorzumachen.
translations.fr: Nous ne pouvons pas continuer à nous abuser.
translations.pt: Não podemos continuar nos enganando.

examples.text: I'll go crazy if this keeps up.

translations.de: Ich werde noch verrückt, wenn das so weitergeht.
translations.fr: Je deviendrai fou si ça continue.
translations.pt: Ficarei doido se isto continuar.

translations.de: Tom kann nicht den Mund halten.
translations.fr: Tom ne peut pas fermer sa gueule.
translations.pt: Tom não consegue ficar calado.

translations.de: Ich habe ein Kaninchen als Haustier.
translations.fr: J'ai un lapin comme animal de compagnie.
translations.pt: Tenho um coelho como animal de estimação.

more.definition: The main tower of a castle or fortress, located within the castle walls.; The food or money required to keep someone alive and healthy; one's support, maintenance.; The state of being kept; hence, the resulting condition; case.
more.etymology: From Middle English kepe, kep, from the verb (see above).

examples.text: You can't keep doing this, Tom.

translations.de: Du kannst nicht so weitermachen, Tom!
translations.fr: Tu ne peux pas continuer comme ça, Tom.
translations.pt: Você não pode continuar fazendo isto, Tom.

examples.text: Why have you kept it a secret?

translations.de: Warum hast du das geheimgehalten?
translations.fr: Pourquoi l'as-tu gardé secret ?
translations.pt: Por que você o(a) manteve como um segredo?

examples.text: She keeps on making the same mistakes.

translations.de: Sie macht immer wieder dieselben Fehler.
translations.fr: Elle continue à faire les mêmes erreurs.
translations.pt: Ela continua cometendo os mesmos erros.

examples.text: Stay here and keep the doors locked.

translations.de: Bleib hier und halte die Türen geschlossen!
translations.fr: Reste ici et garde les portes verrouillées.
translations.pt: Fique aqui e deixe as portas trancadas.

more.definition: To continue in (a course or mode of action); to not intermit or fall from; to uphold or maintain.; To remain faithful to a given promise or word.; To maintain possession of.

examples.text: At first, I thought Tom was joking.

translations.de: Anfangs glaubte ich, Tom scherze.
translations.fr: Au début, je croyais que Tom plaisantait.
translations.pt: No início, eu achava que Tom estava brincando.

examples.text: The first round is on the house.

translations.de: Die erste Runde geht aufs Haus.
translations.fr: La première tournée est pour la maison.
translations.pt: A primeira rodada é por conta da casa.

examples.text: Tom was the first person to arrive.

translations.de: Tom war der Erste, der ankam.
translations.fr: Tom fut la première personne à arriver.
translations.pt: Tom foi a primeira pessoa a chegar.

examples.text: It's his first day at school.

translations.de: Es ist sein erster Schultag.
translations.fr: C'est son premier jour à l'école.
translations.pt: É o seu primeiro dia na escola.

more.definition: Preceding all others of a series or kind; the ordinal of one; earliest.; Most eminent or exalted; most excellent; chief; highest.; Of or belonging to a first family.

translations.fr: La première femme de Tom s'appelait Marina.

examples.text: The library is on the first floor.

translations.de: Die Bibliothek ist im ersten Stock.
translations.fr: La bibliothèque est au premier étage.
translations.pt: A biblioteca fica no primeiro andar.

examples.text: Welcome to our first class in Italian.

translations.de: Willkommen zu unserer ersten Italienischstunde!
translations.fr: Bienvenue à notre premier cours en italien.
translations.pt: Sejam bem-vindos à nossa primeira aula de italiano.

examples.text: I was the first to begin speaking.

translations.de: Ich war der Erste, der zu sprechen begann.
translations.fr: Je fus le premier à prendre la parole.
translations.pt: Eu falei primeiro.

more.definition: Before anything else; firstly.; For the first time.
more.etymology: From Middle English first, furst, ferst, fyrst, from Old English fyrest, from Proto-West Germanic *furist, from Proto-Germanic *furistaz (“first, foremost”), superlative of Proto-Germanic *furai, *furi (“before”), from Proto-Indo-European *preh₂- (“before”), from *per- (“before; first”), equivalent to fore + -est.

examples.text: What was the first capital of Portugal?

translations.de: Was war die erste Hauptstadt Portugals?
translations.fr: Quelle fut la première capitale du Portugal ?
translations.pt: Qual foi a primeira capital de Portugal?

examples.text: Who will score the first goal tonight?

translations.de: Wer macht heute Abend das erste Tor?
translations.fr: Qui marquera le premier but ce soir ?
translations.pt: Quem vai marcar o primeiro gol esta noite?

examples.text: She didn't like him at first.

translations.de: Sie mochte ihn zuerst nicht.

translations.pt: A princípio ela não gostava dele.

examples.text: What is Mr. Johnson's first name?

translations.de: Wie lautet der Vorname von Herrn Johnson?
translations.fr: Comment M. Johnson se prénomme-t-il?
translations.pt: Qual é o primeiro nome do Sr. Johnson?

more.definition: The person or thing in the first position.; The first gear of an engine.; Something that has never happened before; a new occurrence.
more.etymology: From Middle English first, furst, ferst, fyrst, from Old English fyrest, from Proto-West Germanic *furist, from Proto-Germanic *furistaz (“first, foremost”), superlative of Proto-Germanic *furai, *furi (“before”), from Proto-Indo-European *preh₂- (“before”), from *per- (“before; first”), equivalent to fore + -est.

examples.text: At first, they didn't believe him.

translations.de: Zunächst glaubten sie ihm nicht.
translations.fr: Au début, ils ne le crurent pas.
translations.pt: No princípio, não acreditavam nele.

examples.text: He was the first person to arrive.

translations.de: Er war der Erste, der ankam.
translations.fr: Il est le premier à être arrivé.
translations.pt: Ele foi a primeira pessoa a chegar.

examples.text: Let's begin with the first chapter.

translations.de: Lasst uns mit Kapitel 1 beginnen.
translations.fr: Commençons par le premier chapitre.
translations.pt: Comecemos com o primeiro capítulo.

examples.text: My brother is a first-year student.

translations.de: Mein Bruder studiert im ersten Jahr.
translations.fr: Mon frère est étudiant de première année.
translations.pt: Meu irmão é estudante do primeiro ano.

more.etymology: From Middle English first, furst, ferst, fyrst, from Old English fyrest, from Proto-West Germanic *furist, from Proto-Germanic *furistaz (“first, foremost”), superlative of Proto-Germanic *furai, *furi (“before”), from Proto-Indo-European *preh₂- (“before”), from *per- (“before; first”), equivalent to fore + -est.

examples.text: I didn't ask to be born!

translations.de: Ich habe nicht darum gebeten, geboren zu werden!
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas demandé à naître !
translations.pt: Eu não pedi para nascer!

examples.text: She gives him everything he asks for.

translations.de: Sie gibt ihm alles, um was er sie bittet.
translations.fr: Elle lui donne tout ce qu'il demande.
translations.pt: Ela lhe dá tudo o que pede.

examples.text: I did not ask to be born!

translations.de: Ich habe nicht darum gebeten, geboren zu werden!
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas demandé à naître !
translations.pt: Eu não pedi para nascer!

examples.text: I'll ask my father for money.

translations.de: Ich werde meinen Vater um Geld bitten.
translations.fr: Je demanderai de l'argent à mon père.
translations.pt: Eu pedirei dinheiro ao meu pai.

more.definition: An act or instance of asking.; Something asked or asked for.; An asking price.

examples.text: By asking, you get to the city.

translations.de: Indem Sie fragen, gelangen Sie in die Stadt.
translations.fr: En demandant, vous arrivez en ville.
translations.pt: Perguntando, você chega à cidade.

examples.text: He asked his boss for a raise.

translations.de: Er bat seinen Chef um eine Gehaltserhöhung.
translations.fr: Il a demandé une augmentation à son patron.
translations.pt: Ele pediu ao seu chefe um aumento.

examples.text: I'll ask my mother for money.

translations.de: Ich werde meine Mutter um Geld bitten.
translations.fr: Je demanderai de l'argent à ma mère.
translations.pt: Eu pedirei dinheiro à minha mãe.

examples.text: Here are the books you asked for.

translations.de: Hier sind die Bücher, die Sie erbaten.
translations.fr: Voici les livres que vous avez demandés.
translations.pt: Aqui estão os livros que você pediu.

more.definition: To request (information, or an answer to a question).; To request or enquire of (a person).; To request (an item or service) (see also ask for).
more.etymology: From Middle English asken, axen, from Old English āscian, from Proto-West Germanic *aiskōn, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eys- (“to wish; request”).

examples.text: I still don't have a plan.

translations.de: Ich habe noch keinen Plan.
translations.fr: Je n'ai toujours pas de plan.
translations.pt: Ainda não tenho um plano.

examples.text: Your name is still on the list.

translations.de: Ihr Name ist immer noch auf der Liste.
translations.fr: Ton nom est toujours sur la liste.
translations.pt: Seu nome ainda está na lista.

examples.text: Tom is still working at his computer.

translations.de: Tom arbeitet immer noch an seinem Computer.
translations.fr: Tom travaille encore sur son ordinateur.

translations.de: Tom ist immer noch unverheiratet, nicht wahr?

translations.pt: Você ainda mora com os seus pais?

examples.text: Tom still doesn't know what happened.

translations.pt: Tom ainda não sabe o que aconteceu.

examples.text: You still haven't answered my question.

more.definition: Without motion.; Up to a time, as in the preceding time.; To an even greater degree. Used to modify comparative adjectives or adverbs.
more.etymology: From Middle English stille (“motionless, stationary”), from Old English stille (“still, quiet”), from Proto-West Germanic *stillī, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)telH- (“to be silent; to be still”).

examples.text: There's still blood on the wall.

translations.de: Es ist immer noch Blut an der Wand.
translations.fr: Il y a encore du sang sur le mur.
translations.pt: Ainda há sangue na parede.

examples.text: Are you still afraid of the dark?

translations.de: Hast du noch Angst im Dunkeln?
translations.fr: Est-ce que tu as encore peur du noir ?
translations.pt: Você ainda tem medo do escuro?
