translations.pt: O Tom ainda não pagou o aluguel.

examples.text: I think Tom is still in Boston.

translations.de: Ich glaube, Tom ist noch immer in Boston.
translations.fr: Je pense que Tom est toujours à Boston.
translations.pt: Eu acho que Tom ainda está em Boston.

more.definition: A period of calm or silence.; A photograph, as opposed to movie footage.; A single frame from a film.
more.etymology: From Middle English stille (“motionless, stationary”), from Old English stille (“still, quiet”), from Proto-West Germanic *stillī, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)telH- (“to be silent; to be still”).

examples.text: We still have a lot to do.

translations.de: Wir haben noch viel zu tun.
translations.fr: Nous avons encore beaucoup à faire.
translations.pt: Ainda temos muito o que fazer.

examples.text: I still haven't found my keys.

translations.de: Ich habe meine Schlüssel immer noch nicht gefunden.
translations.fr: Je n'ai toujours pas trouvé mes clés.
translations.pt: Ainda não encontrei as minhas chaves.

examples.text: I still don't know the rules.

translations.de: Ich kenne die Regeln immer noch nicht.
translations.fr: Je ne connais toujours pas les règles.
translations.pt: Eu ainda não conheço as regras.

examples.text: Ken still hasn't washed the car.

translations.de: Ken hat das Auto immer noch nicht gewaschen.
translations.fr: Ken n'a toujours pas lavé la voiture.
translations.pt: O Ken ainda não lavou o carro.

more.definition: To calm down, to quiet.; To cause to fall by drops.; To expel spirit from by heat, or to evaporate and condense in a refrigeratory; to distill.
more.etymology: Inherited from Old English stillan.

examples.text: I don't have anything to eat.

translations.de: Ich habe nichts zu essen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai rien à manger.
translations.pt: Não tenho nada para comer.

examples.text: Tom doesn't know anything about computers.

translations.de: Tom versteht nichts von Computern.
translations.fr: Tom ne connaît rien aux ordinateurs.
translations.pt: Tom não sabe nada sobre computadores.

examples.text: I don't know anything about that.

examples.text: I've never seen anything like this.

translations.de: So etwas habe ich noch nie gesehen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai jamais rien vu de tel.
translations.pt: Nunca vi nada assim.

more.definition: In any way, any extent or any degree.
more.etymology: From Middle English anything, enything, onything, onythynge, from Old English ǣniġe þinga, ǣnġi þinga (literally “by any of things”), from ǣniġe, instrumental form of ǣniġ (“any”) + þinga, genitive plural of þing (“thing”).

examples.text: You can ask me anything you like.

translations.de: Sie können mich fragen, was immer Sie wollen.
translations.fr: Tu peux me demander tout ce que tu veux.
translations.pt: Podes perguntar-me o que quiseres.

examples.text: We don't have anything to do.

translations.de: Wir haben nichts zu tun.
translations.fr: On n'a rien à faire.
translations.pt: Não temos nada para fazer.

examples.text: I'll buy you anything you want.

translations.de: Ich kaufe dir, was immer du willst.
translations.fr: Je t'achèterai tout ce que tu veux.
translations.pt: Eu vou comprar o que você quiser.

examples.text: Tom didn't know anything about Mary.

translations.de: Tom wusste nichts über Maria.
translations.fr: Tom ne savait rien à propos de Mary.
translations.pt: Tom não sabia nada sobre Mary.

more.definition: Someone or something of importance.
more.etymology: From Middle English anything, enything, onything, from Late Old English aniþing, from earlier ǣniġ þing (literally “any thing”), equivalent to any + thing.

examples.text: I value our friendship more than anything.

translations.de: Ich achte unsere Freundschaft höher als alles andere.
translations.fr: J'accorde davantage de valeur à notre amitié qu'à quoi que ce soit d'autre.
translations.pt: Eu prezo por nossa amizade mais do que tudo.

examples.text: I can't see anything from here.

translations.de: Ich sehe von hier aus nichts.
translations.fr: Je n'arrive à rien voir d'ici.
translations.pt: Não consigo ver nada daqui.

examples.text: Let me know if you need anything.

translations.de: Lassen Sie mich wissen, wenn Sie etwas brauchen!
translations.fr: Dis-moi si tu as besoin de quelque chose.
translations.pt: Me diga se precisar de alguma coisa.

examples.text: I will do anything that you ask.

translations.de: Ich werde alles tun, was du verlangst.
translations.fr: Je ferai tout ce que vous demanderez.
translations.pt: Farei qualquer coisa que pedir.

more.definition: Any object, act, state, event, or fact whatsoever; a thing of any kind; something or other.; Expressing an indefinite comparison.
more.etymology: From Middle English anything, enything, onything, from Late Old English aniþing, from earlier ǣniġ þing (literally “any thing”), equivalent to any + thing.

examples.text: I don't have anything to add.

translations.de: Ich habe dem nichts hinzuzufügen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai rien à ajouter.
translations.pt: Não tenho nada a acrescentar.

examples.text: Tom isn't interested in anything else.

translations.de: Tom interessiert sich für nichts anderes.
translations.fr: Tom ne s'intéresse à rien d'autre.
translations.pt: Tom não está interessado em mais nada.

examples.text: Are you thinking of anything in particular?

translations.de: Denkst du an etwas Bestimmtes?
translations.fr: Tu penses à quelque chose en particulier?
translations.pt: Você está pensando em algo em particular?

examples.text: I love my family more than anything.

translations.de: Ich liebe meine Familie mehr als alles andere.
translations.fr: J'aime ma famille plus que tout.
translations.pt: Eu amo minha família mais do que qualquer coisa.

more.definition: Used as a placeholder verb for any verb out of a set of related verbs.
more.etymology: From Middle English anything, enything, onything, from Late Old English aniþing, from earlier ǣniġ þing (literally “any thing”), equivalent to any + thing.

examples.text: My husband's going to kill me.

translations.de: Mein Mann wird mich umbringen.
translations.fr: Mon mari va me tuer.
translations.pt: Meu marido vai me matar.

examples.text: My brother's going to kill me.

translations.de: Mein Bruder hat vor, mich umzubringen.
translations.fr: Mon frère va me tuer.
translations.pt: Meu irmão vai me matar.

examples.text: My wife's going to kill me.

translations.de: Meine Frau wird mich umbringen.
translations.fr: Ma femme va me tuer.
translations.pt: Minha mulher vai me matar.

examples.text: My sister's going to kill me.

translations.de: Meine Schwester wird mich umbringen.
translations.fr: Ma sœur va me tuer.
translations.pt: Minha irmã vai me matar.

more.definition: The act of killing.; Specifically, the death blow.; The result of killing; that which has been killed.
more.etymology: From Middle English killen, kyllen, cüllen (“to strike, beat, cut”), of obscure origin. Cognate with Scots kele, keil (“to kill”). * Perhaps from unattested Old English *cyllan, from Proto-West Germanic *kwulljan, from Proto-Germanic *kwuljaną, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷelH- (“to throw, hit, hurt by throwing”). * Or, possibly a variant of Old English cwellan (“to kill, murder, execute”) (see quell).

examples.text: Will artificial intelligence grow to kill humankind?

translations.de: Wird die künstliche Intelligenz irgendwann die Menschheit töten?
translations.fr: L'intelligence artificielle va-t-elle grandir pour tuer l'humanité ?
translations.pt: A inteligência artificial virá a matar a humanidade?

examples.text: I don't know who killed Tom.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, wer Tom getötet hat.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas qui a tué Tom.
translations.pt: Eu não sei quem matou Tom.

examples.text: He got killed in an automobile accident.

translations.de: Er kam bei einem Autounfall ums Leben.
translations.fr: Il perdit la vie dans un accident de voiture.
translations.pt: Ele foi morto num acidente automobilístico.

examples.text: My father is going to kill me.

translations.de: Mein Vater wird mich umbringen.
translations.fr: Mon père va me tuer.
translations.pt: O meu pai vai me matar.

more.definition: To put to death; to extinguish the life of.; To render inoperative.; To stop, cease, or render void; to terminate.
more.etymology: From Middle English killen, kyllen, cüllen (“to strike, beat, cut”), of obscure origin. Cognate with Scots kele, keil (“to kill”). * Perhaps from unattested Old English *cyllan, from Proto-West Germanic *kwulljan, from Proto-Germanic *kwuljaną, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷelH- (“to throw, hit, hurt by throwing”). * Or, possibly a variant of Old English cwellan (“to kill, murder, execute”) (see quell).

examples.text: She has nothing in common with him.

translations.de: Sie hat mit ihm nichts gemein.
translations.fr: Elle n'a rien de commun avec lui.
translations.pt: Ela não tem nada em comum com ele.

examples.text: The soldiers could do nothing until spring.

translations.de: Die Soldaten konnten bis zum Frühling nichts unternehmen.
translations.fr: Les soldats ne purent rien entreprendre jusqu'au printemps.
translations.pt: Os soldados não podiam fazer nada até a primavera.

examples.text: This has nothing to do with me.

translations.de: Das hat nichts mit mir zu tun.
translations.fr: Ça n'a rien à voir avec moi.
translations.pt: Isso não tem nada a ver comigo.

examples.text: It's nothing, don't be afraid!

translations.de: Es ist nichts, hab keine Angst!
translations.fr: Ce n'est rien, n'aie pas peur !
translations.pt: Não é nada, não tenha medo!

more.definition: Completely unimportant.; Lacking effort or commitment.
more.etymology: From Middle English nothyng, noon thing, non thing, na þing, nan thing, nan þing, from Old English nāþing, nān þing (“nothing”, literally “not any thing”), equivalent to no + thing. Compare Old English nāwiht (“nothing”, literally “no thing”), Swedish ingenting (“nothing”, literally “not any thing, no thing”).

examples.text: I've got nothing to do today.

translations.de: Ich habe heute nichts zu tun.
translations.fr: Je n'ai rien à faire aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Hoje eu não tenho nada para fazer.

examples.text: I had nothing to do with it.

translations.de: Ich hatte nichts damit zu tun.
translations.fr: Je n'avais rien à y faire.
translations.pt: Não tenho nada a ver com isso.

examples.text: I have nothing to add to that.

translations.de: Dem habe ich nichts hinzuzufügen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai rien à ajouter à cela.
translations.pt: Não tenho nada a acrescentar.

examples.text: That has nothing to do with him.

translations.de: Das hat nichts mit ihm zu tun.
translations.fr: Ça n'a rien à voir avec lui.
translations.pt: Isso não tem nada a ver com ele.

more.definition: Used to dismiss a previous statement.
more.etymology: From Middle English nothyng, noon thing, non thing, na þing, nan thing, nan þing, from Old English nāþing, nān þing (“nothing”, literally “not any thing”), equivalent to no + thing. Compare Old English nāwiht (“nothing”, literally “no thing”), Swedish ingenting (“nothing”, literally “not any thing, no thing”).

examples.text: I've got nothing in my fridge.

translations.de: Ich habe nichts in meinem Kühlschrank.
translations.fr: Je n'ai rien dans mon frigo.
translations.pt: Eu não tenho nada na geladeira.

examples.text: I have nothing to say to you.

translations.de: Ich habe dir nichts zu sagen.

translations.pt: Não tenho nada a lhe dizer.

translations.de: Ich schätze, ich habe nichts zu verlieren.

more.definition: Never mind; it's not important; forget what I said.
more.etymology: From Middle English nothyng, noon thing, non thing, na þing, nan thing, nan þing, from Old English nāþing, nān þing (“nothing”, literally “not any thing”), equivalent to no + thing. Compare Old English nāwiht (“nothing”, literally “no thing”), Swedish ingenting (“nothing”, literally “not any thing, no thing”).

examples.text: I've got nothing else to do.

translations.de: Ich habe sonst nichts zu tun.

examples.text: There's nothing we can't do.

translations.de: Es gibt nichts, was wir nicht können.
translations.fr: Il n'y a rien d'impossible pour nous.

translations.fr: J'ai cliqué sur le lien, mais il ne s'est rien passé.
translations.pt: Cliquei no link mas nada aconteceu.

more.definition: Something trifling, or of no consequence or importance.; A trivial remark especially in the term sweet nothings.; A nobody (insignificant person).
more.etymology: From Middle English nothyng, noon thing, non thing, na þing, nan thing, nan þing, from Old English nāþing, nān þing (“nothing”, literally “not any thing”), equivalent to no + thing. Compare Old English nāwiht (“nothing”, literally “no thing”), Swedish ingenting (“nothing”, literally “not any thing, no thing”).

examples.text: There's nothing as precious as love.

translations.de: Nichts ist so kostbar wie die Liebe.
translations.fr: Rien n'a autant de valeur que l'amour.
translations.pt: Não há nada tão valioso quanto o amor.

translations.de: Die Mannschaft hat nur starke Spieler.

translations.de: Er ist nichts weiter als ein Feigling.
translations.fr: Il n'est rien d'autre qu'un lâche.

examples.text: He looked as if nothing had happened.

more.definition: Not any thing; no thing.; An absence of anything, including empty space, brightness, darkness, matter, or a vacuum.
more.etymology: From Middle English nothyng, noon thing, non thing, na þing, nan thing, nan þing, from Old English nāþing, nān þing (“nothing”, literally “not any thing”), equivalent to no + thing. Compare Old English nāwiht (“nothing”, literally “no thing”), Swedish ingenting (“nothing”, literally “not any thing, no thing”).

translations.de: Er stemmte die Hände in die Hüften.

more.definition: Ellipsis of put option (“right to sell something at a predetermined price”); The act of putting; an action; a movement; a thrust; a push.; An old card game.
more.etymology: From Middle English putten, pitten, pytten, puten, poten, from Old English putian, *pūtian ("to push, put out"; attested by derivative putung (“pushing, impulse, instigation, urging”)) and potian (“to push, thrust, strike, butt, goad”), both from Proto-West Germanic *putōn, from Proto-Germanic *putōną (“to stick, stab”), which is of uncertain origin.

examples.text: I'll put this in the fridge.

translations.de: Ich werde das in den Kühlschrank legen.
translations.fr: Je vais le mettre au réfrigérateur.

examples.text: Tom seldom puts sugar in his coffee.

examples.text: She's putting the children to bed.

translations.de: Sie bringt die Kinder ins Bett.
translations.fr: Elle est en train de coucher les enfants.
translations.pt: Ela está pondo as crianças para dormir.

examples.text: Tom put the vase on the table.

translations.de: Tom hat die Vase auf den Tisch gestellt.
translations.fr: Tom posa le vase sur la table.
translations.pt: Tom colocou o vaso sobre a mesa.

more.definition: To physically place (something or somebody, in, at, around, etc. someplace); To place in abstract; to attach or attribute; to assign.; To bring or set (into a certain relation, state or condition).
more.etymology: From Middle English putten, pitten, pytten, puten, poten, from Old English putian, *pūtian ("to push, put out"; attested by derivative putung (“pushing, impulse, instigation, urging”)) and potian (“to push, thrust, strike, butt, goad”), both from Proto-West Germanic *putōn, from Proto-Germanic *putōną (“to stick, stab”), which is of uncertain origin.

examples.text: Hundreds of people have lost their livelihoods.

translations.de: Hunderte Menschen haben ihre Lebensgrundlage verloren.
translations.fr: Des centaines de personnes ont perdu leurs gagne-pain.
translations.pt: Centenas de pessoas perderam os seus sustentos.

examples.text: They've started believing their own lies.

translations.de: Die fangen an, ihre eigenen Lügen zu glauben.
translations.fr: Ils se mettent à croire à leurs propres mensonges.
translations.pt: Eles começaram a acreditar em suas próprias mentiras.

examples.text: They're happy with their new flat.

translations.de: Sie sind mit ihrer neuen Wohnung zufrieden.
translations.fr: Ils sont contents de leur nouvel appartement.
translations.pt: Eles estão felizes com o seu novo apartamento.

examples.text: They brush their teeth twice a day.

translations.de: Sie putzen sich zweimal am Tag die Zähne.
translations.fr: Ils se brossent les dents deux fois par jour.
translations.pt: Eles escovam os dentes duas vezes por dia.

more.definition: Belonging to, from, of, or relating to, them (plural).; Belonging to someone (one person, singular), or occasionally to something.
more.etymology: Old Norse þeirader. From Old Norse þeira, þeirra. Replaced native Old English heora.

examples.text: He uses bitcoins to purchase illicit drugs.

translations.de: Er benutzt Bitcoin, um illegale Drogen zu kaufen.
translations.fr: Il utilise des bitcoins pour acheter des drogues illégales.
translations.pt: Ele usa bitcoins para comprar drogas ilícitas.

examples.text: Freedom is useless unless you use it.

translations.de: Freiheit ist nutzlos, wenn du sie nicht nutzt.
translations.fr: La liberté est inutile, sauf si vous l'utilisez.
translations.pt: A liberdade é inútil a menos que você a use.

examples.text: Which online dictionary do you use most?

translations.de: Welches Netzwörterbuch verwendest du am meisten?
translations.fr: Quel dictionnaire en ligne emploies-tu le plus ?
translations.pt: Qual dicionário online você usa mais?

examples.text: Don't use this apparatus near water.

translations.de: Dieses Gerät nicht in Wassernähe benutzen!
translations.fr: N'utilisez pas cet appareil près de l'eau.
translations.pt: Não use este aparelho perto da água.

more.definition: The act of using.; The act of consuming alcohol or narcotics.; Usefulness, utility, benefit; purpose, point.
more.etymology: Old French usbor. Inherited from Middle English use, from Old French us, from Latin ūsus (“use, custom, skill, habit”), from past participle stem of ūtor (“use”). Displaced native Middle English note (“use”) (see note) from Old English notu; Middle English nutte (“use”) from Old English nytt; as well as Old English fricu and Old English sidu.

examples.text: The child must get used to school.

translations.de: Das Kind muss sich an die Schule gewöhnen.
translations.fr: L'enfant doit s'habituer à l'école.
translations.pt: A criança tem de se habituar à escola.

examples.text: The iron uses a lot of electricity.

translations.de: Das Bügeleisen verbraucht viel Strom.
translations.fr: Le fer à repasser utilise beaucoup d'électricité.
translations.pt: O ferro de passar consome bastante energia elétrica.

examples.text: I like people who use language beautifully.

translations.de: Ich mag Menschen, die sich gepflegt ausdrücken.
translations.fr: J'aime les gens qui utilisent le langage magnifiquement.
translations.pt: Eu gosto das pessoas que usam a língua de uma maneira bela.

examples.text: I'm not used to the heat.

translations.de: Ich bin die Hitze nicht gewohnt.
translations.fr: Je ne suis pas habitué à la chaleur.
translations.pt: Não estou acostumado com o calor.

more.definition: To employ; to apply; to utilize.; To expend; to consume by employing.; To exploit.

Displaced native Middle English noten, nutten (“to use”) (from Old English notian, nēotan, nyttian) and Middle English brouken, bruken (“to use, enjoy”) (from Old English brūcan).

examples.text: My room is almost six meters long.

translations.de: Mein Zimmer ist fast sechs Meter lang.
translations.fr: Ma chambre fait presque six mètres de long.
translations.pt: Meu quarto tem quase seis metros de comprimento.

examples.text: In general, women live longer than men.

translations.de: Frauen leben im Allgemeinen länger als Männer.
translations.fr: En général, les femmes vivent plus longtemps que les hommes.
translations.pt: Em geral, as mulheres vivem mais que os homens.

examples.text: We'll know the truth before long.

translations.de: Bald erfahren wir die Wahrheit.
translations.fr: Avant peu nous connaîtrons la vérité.
translations.pt: Nós logo saberemos a verdade.

examples.text: How long have you been in England?

translations.de: Wie lange bist du schon in England?
translations.fr: Depuis combien de temps êtes-vous en Angleterre ?
translations.pt: Há quanto tempo você está na Inglaterra?

more.definition: Having much distance in space from one end to the other.; Specifically, having much distance in a horizontal dimension (see also Usage Notes below).; Travelling a great distance.
more.etymology: From Middle English long, lang, from Old English long, lang (“long, tall, lasting”), from Proto-West Germanic *lang, from Proto-Germanic *langaz (“long”), from Proto-Indo-European *dlongʰos (“long”).

examples.text: It's not going to be long.

translations.de: Es wird nicht lange dauern.
translations.fr: Ça ne sera pas long.
translations.pt: Não vai demorar.

examples.text: I was unable to stand any longer.

translations.de: Ich konnte nicht mehr stehen.
translations.fr: Je fus incapable de me tenir debout plus longtemps.
translations.pt: Fui incapaz de ficar mais.

examples.text: I had a long talk with Tom.

translations.de: Ich hatte ein langes Gespräch mit Tom.
translations.fr: J'ai eu une longue conversation avec Tom.
translations.pt: Eu tive uma longa conversa com Tom.

examples.text: How long did you stay in Boston?

translations.de: Wie lange blieben Sie in Boston?
translations.fr: Combien de temps es-tu resté à Boston ?
translations.pt: Por quanto tempo você ficou em Boston?

translations.pt: Farei o que estiver ao meu alcance.

examples.text: When I'm sleeping, everything is fine.

translations.de: Wenn ich schlafe, ist alles in Ordnung.
translations.fr: Quand je dors, tout va bien.
translations.pt: Quando estou dormindo, está tudo bem.

examples.text: My computer crashed and I lost everything.

translations.de: Mein Computer ist abgestürzt und alle Daten sind weg.
translations.fr: Mon ordi a planté et j'ai tout perdu.
translations.pt: Meu computador quebrou e eu perdi tudo.

examples.text: You seem to know everything about this.

translations.de: Du scheinst darüber alles zu wissen.
translations.fr: Vous semblez tout savoir là-dessus.
translations.pt: Vocês parecem saber tudo sobre isto.

more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English every thing; univerbation of every + thing.

examples.text: I cannot live far from the ocean.

translations.de: Ich kann nicht weit vom Meer entfernt leben.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas vivre loin de la mer.
translations.pt: Eu não posso viver longe do mar.

examples.text: I don't live in Boston anymore.

translations.de: Ich wohne nicht mehr in Boston.
translations.fr: Je n’habite plus à Boston.
translations.pt: Eu não moro mais em Boston.

examples.text: Few people live to be a hundred.

translations.de: Kaum jemand wird hundert Jahre alt.
translations.fr: Peu de gens vivent jusqu'à cent ans.
translations.pt: Poucas pessoas vivem até os cem anos de idade.

examples.text: I'd like to live in Brazil.

translations.de: Ich möchte in Brasilien leben.
translations.fr: Je voudrais vivre au Brésil.
translations.pt: Eu gostaria de morar no Brasil.

more.definition: Having life; that is alive.; Being in existence; actual.; Having active properties; being energized.
more.etymology: An apheretic form of alive.

examples.text: He doesn't live far from here.

translations.de: Er wohnt nicht weit weg.
translations.fr: Il n'habite pas loin d'ici.
translations.pt: Ele não mora longe daqui.

examples.text: Mary doesn't live in my neighborhood.

translations.de: Maria wohnt nicht in meiner Nachbarschaft.
translations.fr: Marie n'habite pas dans mon quartier.
translations.pt: Mary não mora no meu bairro.

examples.text: I'd like to live in Italy.

translations.de: Ich würde gerne in Italien leben.
translations.fr: J'aimerais vivre en Italie.
translations.pt: Eu gostaria de morar na Itália.

examples.text: Tom and Mary live near the library.

translations.de: Tom und Maria wohnen nahe der Bibliothek.
translations.fr: Tom et Mary habitent près de la bibliothèque.
translations.pt: Tom e Maria moram perto da biblioteca.

more.definition: Of an event, as it happens; in real time; direct.; Of making a performance or speech, in person.
more.etymology: An apheretic form of alive.

examples.text: Where does the president of Brazil live?

translations.de: Wo lebt der Präsident von Brasilien?
translations.fr: Où habite le président du Brésil ?
translations.pt: Onde mora o presidente do Brasil?

examples.text: The dead are useful to the living.

translations.de: Die Toten sind den Lebenden nützlich.
translations.fr: Les morts sont utiles aux vivants.
translations.pt: Os mortos são úteis aos vivos.

examples.text: I lived in Australia for three years.

translations.de: Ich habe drei Jahre in Australien gelebt.
translations.fr: J'ai vécu trois ans en Australie.
translations.pt: Eu morei na Austrália por três anos.

examples.text: He slept on the living room couch.

translations.de: Er schlief auf der Couch im Wohnzimmer.
translations.fr: Il dormit sur le canapé du salon.
translations.pt: Ele dormiu no sofá da sala.

more.definition: To be alive; to have life.; To have permanent residence somewhere, to inhabit, to reside.; (of an object) to have its proper place; to normally be stored.
more.etymology: From Middle English lefe, lifen, libbe, libben, live, luvien, lyven, from Old English libban, lifian (“to live; be alive”), from Proto-West Germanic *libbjan, from Proto-Germanic *libjaną (“to live”), from Proto-Indo-European *leyp- (“to stick”).

examples.text: When did man start to use tools?

translations.de: Wann begann der Mensch Werkzeuge zu gebrauchen?
translations.fr: Depuis quand l'être humain a-t-il commencé à faire usage des outils ?
translations.pt: Quando o homem começou a utilizar-se de ferramentas?

examples.text: We may as well start at once.

translations.de: Wir können auch gleich anfangen.
translations.fr: On pourrait aussi commencer de suite.
translations.pt: Vamos começar logo de uma vez.

examples.text: You should start as early as possible.

translations.de: Du solltest so früh wie möglich anfangen.
translations.fr: Vous devriez commencer aussi tôt que possible.
translations.pt: Você deve começar o mais cedo possível.

examples.text: We'll start whenever you are ready.

translations.de: Wir fangen an, sobald du fertig bist.
translations.fr: Nous commencerons dès que tu es prêt.
translations.pt: Começaremos quando você estiver pronto.

more.etymology: Variant of stark.

examples.text: When did you start wearing contact lenses?

translations.de: Wann hast du angefangen Kontaktlinsen zu tragen?
translations.fr: Quand as-tu commencé à porter des lentilles de contact ?
translations.pt: Quando você começou a usar lentes de contato?

examples.text: The word starts with a consonant.

translations.de: Das Wort beginnt mit einem Konsonanten.
translations.fr: Le mot commence par une consonne.
translations.pt: A palavra começa por consoante.

examples.text: It's never too late to start.

translations.de: Es ist nie zu spät, um anzufangen.
translations.fr: Il n'est jamais trop tard pour commencer.
translations.pt: Nunca é tarde demais para começar.

examples.text: I don't know where to start.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, wo ich anfangen soll.
translations.fr: Je ne sais par où commencer.
translations.pt: Não sei por onde começar.

more.definition: The beginning of an activity.; A sudden involuntary movement.; The beginning point of a race, a board game, etc.
more.etymology: Middle English stertendeverb. From Middle English stert, from the verb sterten (“to start, startle”). See below.

examples.text: Let's start with the easy questions.

translations.de: Lasst uns mit leichten Fragen beginnen.
translations.fr: Commençons par les questions faciles.
translations.pt: Vamos começar com as perguntas fáceis.

examples.text: The fire started in Tom's room.

translations.de: Der Brand begann in Toms Zimmer.
translations.fr: L'incendie a pris dans la chambre de Tom.
translations.pt: O incêndio começou na casa de Tom.

examples.text: I'm starting to lose my patience.

translations.de: Ich fange an, die Geduld zu verlieren.
translations.fr: Je commence à perdre patience.
translations.pt: Estou começando a perder a paciência.

examples.text: The movie starts at ten o'clock.

translations.de: Der Film fängt um 10 Uhr an.
translations.fr: Le film commence à dix heures.
translations.pt: O filme começa às dez em ponto.

more.definition: To set in motion.; To begin.; To ready the operation of a vehicle or machine.
more.etymology: From Middle English sterten (“to leap up suddenly, rush out”), from Old English styrtan (“to leap up, start”), from Proto-West Germanic *sturtijan (“to startle, move, set in motion”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ter- (“to be stiff”).

examples.text: Tom always drinks tea in the morning.

translations.de: Tom trinkt des Morgens immer Tee.
translations.fr: Tomas boit toujours du thé le matin.
translations.pt: O Tom sempre toma chá de manhã.

examples.text: I've always wanted to visit Turkey.

translations.de: Ich wollte schon immer die Türkei besuchen.
translations.fr: J'ai toujours eu envie de visiter la Turquie.
translations.pt: Eu sempre quis visitar a Turquia.

examples.text: The simplest solutions are always the best.

translations.de: Die einfachen Lösungen sind immer die schönsten.
translations.fr: Les solutions les plus simples sont toujours les meilleures.
translations.pt: As soluções mais simples são sempre as melhores.

examples.text: I've always dreamed of living abroad.

translations.de: Ich habe schon immer davon geträumt, im Ausland zu leben.
translations.fr: J'ai toujours rêvé de vivre à l'étranger.
translations.pt: Eu sempre sonhei em viver no exterior.

more.definition: At all times; throughout all time; since the beginning.; Constantly during a certain period, or regularly at stated intervals (opposed to sometimes or occasionally).; if necessary, or if there is no better option; in any event.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *weǵʰ-der. From Middle English alweyes, alwayes, alweys, a variant of Middle English alwey, alway (“always”), from Old English ealneġ, ealne weġ (“always, perpetually”, literally “all the way, all the while, continuously”), from ealne + weġ (accusative case), equivalent to alway + -s. Cognate with Scots always (“always”), Low German allerwegens (“very often”, literally “all ways'”).

examples.text: The goal is always the maximum profit.

translations.de: Das Ziel ist immer der maximale Gewinn.
translations.fr: Le but est toujours le profit maximum.
translations.pt: O objetivo é sempre o lucro máximo.

examples.text: I always had trouble earning a living.

translations.de: Ich hatte immer Schwierigkeiten damit, mir meinen Lebensunterhalt zu verdienen.
translations.fr: J'ai toujours eu du mal à gagner ma vie.
translations.pt: Sempre tive dificuldade em ganhar a vida.

examples.text: Mary is always in a bad mood.

translations.de: Maria hat immer schlechte Laune.
translations.fr: Mary est toujours de mauvaise humeur.
translations.pt: Mary está sempre de mau humor.

examples.text: She's always in a bad mood.

translations.de: Sie hat immer schlechte Laune.
translations.fr: Elle est toujours de mauvaise humeur.
translations.pt: Ela está sempre de mau humor.

more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *weǵʰ-der. From Middle English alweyes, alwayes, alweys, a variant of Middle English alwey, alway (“always”), from Old English ealneġ, ealne weġ (“always, perpetually”, literally “all the way, all the while, continuously”), from ealne + weġ (accusative case), equivalent to alway + -s. Cognate with Scots always (“always”), Low German allerwegens (“very often”, literally “all ways'”).

examples.text: I'm going to miss this place.

translations.de: Diesen Ort werde ich vermissen.
translations.fr: Cet endroit va me manquer.
translations.pt: Eu vou sentir falta deste lugar.

examples.text: We went to some incredible places.

translations.de: Wir gingen zu einigen unglaublichen Orten.
translations.fr: Nous sommes allés dans des endroits incroyables.
translations.pt: Fomos a alguns lugares incríveis.

examples.text: This isn't a place for kids.

translations.de: Das ist kein Platz für Kinder.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas un endroit pour les enfants.
translations.pt: Isto não é lugar para crianças.

examples.text: Store in a cool and dry place.

translations.de: Kühl und trocken lagern.
translations.fr: Conserver dans un endroit frais et sec.
translations.pt: Armazene num lugar seco e frio.

more.definition: An open space, particularly a city square, market square, or courtyard.; A street, sometimes but not always surrounding a public place, square, or plaza of the same name.; An inhabited area: a village, town, or city.
more.etymology: From Middle English place, conflation of Old English plæċe (“place, an open space, street”) and Old French place (“place, an open space”), both from Latin platēa (“plaza, wide street”), from Ancient Greek πλατεῖα (plateîa), shortening of πλατεῖα ὁδός (plateîa hodós, “broad way”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleth₂- (“to spread”), extended form of *pleh₂- (“flat”).

examples.text: I'm ready to leave this place.

translations.de: Ich bin bereit, von hier zu verschwinden.
translations.fr: Je suis prêt à quitter cet endroit.
translations.pt: Eu estou pronto para sair deste lugar.

examples.text: He placed the book on the shelf.

translations.de: Er stellte das Buch ins Regal.
translations.fr: Il plaça le livre sur l'étagère.
translations.pt: Ele colocou o livro na prateleira.

examples.text: Moss grows in damp, dark places.

translations.de: Moos wächst an feuchten, dunklen Plätzen.
translations.fr: La mousse pousse dans les endroits humides et sombres.
translations.pt: Os musgos crescem em lugares úmidos e sombrios.

examples.text: Tom came out of his hiding place.

translations.de: Tom kam aus seinem Versteck hervor.
translations.fr: Tom est sorti de sa cachette.
translations.pt: Tom saiu do esconderijo dele.

more.definition: To put (someone or something) in a specific location.; To earn a given spot in a competition; to rank at a certain position ((often followed by an ordinal)).; To finish second, especially of horses or dogs.
more.etymology: From Middle English placen, from the noun (see above).

examples.text: She wasn't able to meet him.

translations.de: Sie konnte sich nicht mit ihm treffen.
translations.fr: Elle fut dans l'incapacité de le rencontrer.
translations.pt: Ela não pôde encontrá-lo.

examples.text: I would like to meet his father.

translations.de: Ich würde gerne seinen Vater treffen.
translations.fr: Je voudrais rencontrer son père.
translations.pt: Gostaria de conhecer o pai dela.

examples.text: I don't meet him so often.

translations.de: Ich treffe ihn nicht so oft.
translations.fr: Je ne le rencontre pas si souvent.
translations.pt: Eu não o encontro com muita frequência.

examples.text: I'm going to meet him tomorrow.

translations.de: Ich treffe mich morgen mit ihm.
translations.fr: Je vais le rencontrer demain.
translations.pt: Eu vou encontrar ele amanhã.

more.etymology: From Middle English mete, imete, from Old English ġemǣte (“suitable, having the same measurements”), from the Proto-Germanic *gamētijaz, *mētiz (“reasonable; estimable”) (cognate with Dutch meten (“measure”), German gemäß (“suitable”) etc.), itself from collective prefix *ga- + Proto-Indo-European *med- (“to measure”).

examples.text: Priscilla, I'm glad to meet you.

translations.de: Priscilla, ich freue mich, Sie kennenzulernen.
translations.fr: Priscilla, je suis ravie de vous rencontrer.
translations.pt: Priscila, prazer em conhecê-la.

examples.text: He meets foreigners during his travels.

translations.de: Auf seinen Reisen trifft er Ausländer.
translations.fr: Il rencontre des étrangers lors de ses voyages.
translations.pt: Ele conhece estrangeiros durante suas viagens.

examples.text: I'd like to meet his father.

translations.de: Ich würde gerne seinen Vater treffen.
translations.fr: J'aimerais rencontrer son père.
translations.pt: Eu gostaria de conhecer seu pai.

examples.text: I meet people like you every day.

translations.de: Ich treffe jeden Tag Leute wie dich.
translations.fr: Je rencontre des gens comme toi tous les jours.
translations.pt: Conheço pessoas como você todos os dias.

more.definition: A sports competition, especially for track and field or swimming.; A gathering of riders, horses and hounds for foxhunting; a field meet for hunting.; A meeting of two trains in opposite directions on a single track, when one is put into a siding to let the other cross.
more.etymology: From Middle English meten, from Old English mētan (“to meet, find, encounter”), from Proto-West Germanic *mōtijan (“to meet”), from Proto-Germanic *mōtijaną (“to meet”), from Proto-Indo-European *meh₂d- (“to come, meet”).

examples.text: I'm glad to have met you.

translations.de: Ich bin froh, dich getroffen zu haben.
translations.fr: Je suis content de t'avoir croisé.
translations.pt: Estou contente por ter te encontrado.

examples.text: Tom wants Mary to meet his mother.

translations.de: Tom möchte, dass Mary seine Mutter trifft.
translations.fr: Tom veut que Mary rencontre sa mère.
translations.pt: Tom quer que Mary conheça sua mãe.

examples.text: I met a friend at the airport.

translations.de: Ich habe einen Freund am Flughafen getroffen.
translations.fr: J'ai rencontré un ami à l'aéroport.
translations.pt: Me encontrei com um amigo no aeroporto.

examples.text: I'd like to meet with her.

translations.de: Ich würde sie gerne treffen.
translations.fr: J'aimerais la rencontrer.
translations.pt: Gostaria de me encontrar com ela.

more.definition: To come face to face with by accident; to encounter.; To come face to face with someone by arrangement.; To get acquainted with someone.
more.etymology: From Middle English meten, from Old English mētan (“to meet, find, encounter”), from Proto-West Germanic *mōtijan (“to meet”), from Proto-Germanic *mōtijaną (“to meet”), from Proto-Indo-European *meh₂d- (“to come, meet”).

examples.text: The destruction of the environment is big.

translations.de: Die Umweltzerstörung ist groß.
translations.fr: La destruction de l'environnement est grande.
translations.pt: A destruição do meio ambiente é grande.

examples.text: Our city is getting bigger and bigger.

translations.de: Unsere Stadt wird immer größer.
translations.fr: Notre ville devient de plus en plus grande.
translations.pt: Nossa cidade está ficando cada vez maior.

examples.text: Mary has beautiful eyes, big and blue.

translations.de: Maria hat schöne große blaue Augen.
translations.fr: Marie a de beaux yeux, grands et bleus.
translations.pt: Maria tem olhos lindos, grandes e azuis.

examples.text: It's not that big a deal.

translations.de: Es ist nicht so wichtig.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas si grave.
translations.pt: Não é para tanto.

examples.text: They live in a big city.

translations.de: Sie wohnen in einer großen Stadt.
translations.fr: Ils habitent dans une grande ville.
translations.pt: Eles moram em uma cidade grande.

examples.text: This shirt is too big for me.

translations.de: Dieses Hemd ist mir zu groß.
translations.fr: Cette chemise est trop grande pour moi.
translations.pt: Esta camisa é grande demais para mim.

more.definition: Of great size, large.; Fat.; Large with young; pregnant; swelling; ready to give birth or produce.
collocations: big deal — something important (often ironic)
more.etymology: Inherited from Northern Middle English big, bigge (“powerful, strong”), possibly from a dialect of Old Norse. Ultimately perhaps a derivative of Proto-Germanic *bugja- (“swollen up, thick”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰew-, *bu- (“to swell”), in which case big would be related to bogey, bugbear, and bug. Compare dialectal Norwegian bugge (“great man”), Low German Bögge, Boggelmann.

examples.text: I don't like visiting big cities.

translations.de: Ich besichtige nicht gerne große Städte.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas visiter les grandes villes.
translations.pt: Não gosto de visitar cidades grandes.

examples.text: That box is bigger than this one.

translations.de: Die Schachtel dort ist größer als diese.
translations.fr: Cette boîte-là est plus grande que celle-ci.
translations.pt: Aquela caixa é maior do que essa.

examples.text: A big earthquake occurred in India yesterday.

translations.de: Gestern hat sich in Indien ein großes Erdbeben ereignet.
translations.fr: Un gros tremblement de terre a secoué l'Inde hier.
translations.pt: Um grande terremoto ocorreu na Índia ontem.

examples.text: This dress is too big for me.

translations.de: Dieses Kleid ist mir zu groß.
translations.fr: Cette robe est trop grande pour moi.
translations.pt: Este vestido é muito grande para mim.

more.definition: In a loud manner.; In a boasting manner.; In a large amount or to a large extent.
more.etymology: Inherited from Northern Middle English big, bigge (“powerful, strong”), possibly from a dialect of Old Norse. Ultimately perhaps a derivative of Proto-Germanic *bugja- (“swollen up, thick”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰew-, *bu- (“to swell”), in which case big would be related to bogey, bugbear, and bug. Compare dialectal Norwegian bugge (“great man”), Low German Bögge, Boggelmann.

examples.text: This hat is too big for me.

translations.de: Dieser Hut ist mir zu groß.
translations.fr: Ce chapeau est trop grand pour moi.
translations.pt: Este chapéu é muito grande para mim.

examples.text: Belgium is not as big as France.

translations.de: Belgien ist nicht so groß wie Frankreich.
translations.fr: La Belgique n'est pas aussi grande que la France.
translations.pt: A Bélgica não é tão grande quanto a França.

examples.text: Is the room big enough for you?

translations.de: Ist das Zimmer groß genug für Sie?
translations.fr: La pièce est-elle assez grande pour vous ?
translations.pt: O quarto é espaçoso o suficiente para você?

examples.text: They were afraid of the big dog.

translations.de: Sie hatten Angst vor dem großen Hund.
translations.fr: Ils avaient peur du gros chien.
translations.pt: Tinham medo do cachorro grande.

more.definition: Someone or something that is large in stature.; An important or powerful person; a celebrity; a big name.; The big leagues, big time.
more.etymology: Inherited from Northern Middle English big, bigge (“powerful, strong”), possibly from a dialect of Old Norse. Ultimately perhaps a derivative of Proto-Germanic *bugja- (“swollen up, thick”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰew-, *bu- (“to swell”), in which case big would be related to bogey, bugbear, and bug. Compare dialectal Norwegian bugge (“great man”), Low German Bögge, Boggelmann.

examples.text: We call New York the Big Apple.

translations.de: Wir bezeichnen New York als den „dicken Apfel“.
translations.fr: Nous appelons New York, la grosse pomme.
translations.pt: Chamamos Nova York de "a Grande Maçã".

examples.text: Capital cities are big and noisy.

translations.de: Hauptstädte sind groß und laut.
translations.fr: Les capitales sont grandes et bruyantes.
translations.pt: As capitais são grandes e barulhentas.

examples.text: A big car needs a lot of fuel.

translations.de: Ein großes Auto braucht viel Sprit.
translations.fr: Une grosse voiture a besoin de beaucoup de carburant.
translations.pt: Um carro grande precisa de muito combustível.

examples.text: My dad bought me a big yellow bicycle.

translations.de: Mein Vater kaufte mir ein großes gelbes Fahrrad.
translations.fr: Mon père m'a acheté un gros vélo jaune.
translations.pt: Meu pai me comprou uma grande bicicleta amarela.

more.etymology: From Middle English biggen, byggen, from Old Norse byggja, byggva (“to build, dwell in, inhabit”), a secondary form of Old Norse búa (“to dwell”), related to Old English būan (“to dwell”). Cognate with Danish bygge, Swedish bygga.

examples.text: Tom is three years older than you.

translations.de: Tom ist drei Jahre älter als du.
translations.fr: Tom a trois ans de plus que vous.
translations.pt: Tom é três anos mais velho que você.

examples.text: How old do you think Tom is?

translations.de: Für wie alt haltet ihr Tom?
translations.fr: Quel âge donnerais-tu à Tom ?
translations.pt: Quantos anos você acha que o Tom tem?

examples.text: Tom is not much older than me.

translations.de: Tom ist nicht viel älter als ich.
translations.fr: Tom n'est pas beaucoup plus vieux que moi.
translations.pt: Tom não é muito mais velho do que eu.

examples.text: Tom and Mary are older than John.

translations.de: Tom und Maria sind älter als Johannes.
translations.fr: Tom et Mary sont plus vieux que John.
translations.pt: Tom e Maria são mais velhos do que João.

more.definition: Of an object, concept, relationship, etc., having existed for a relatively long period of time.; Of a living being, having lived for most of the expected years.; Of a perishable item, having existed for most of, or more than, its shelf life.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English old, oold, from Old English ald, eald (“old, aged, ancient, antique, primeval”), from Proto-West Germanic *ald, from Proto-Germanic *aldaz (“grown-up”), originally a participle form, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eltós (“grown, tall, big”).

examples.text: My father is a bit old fashioned.

translations.de: Mein Vater ist ein bisschen altmodisch.
translations.fr: Mon père est un peu ringard.
translations.pt: Meu pai é um pouco antiquado.

examples.text: They were talking together like old pals.

translations.de: Sie unterhielten sich wie alte Freunde.
translations.fr: Ils se parlaient comme de vieux copains.
translations.pt: Eles estavam conversando como velhos amigos.

examples.text: Tom and Mary both like old movies.

translations.de: Tom und Maria mögen beide alte Filme.
translations.fr: Tom et Marie aiment les vieux films.
translations.pt: Tanto Tom como Mary gostam de filmes antigos.

examples.text: We still have an old tube television.

translations.de: Wir haben noch einen alten Röhrenfernseher.
translations.fr: Nous avons encore un vieux téléviseur à lampe.
translations.pt: Nós ainda temos uma televisão de tubo velha.

more.definition: People who are old; old beings; the older generation, taken as a group.; A person older than oneself, especially an adult in relation to a teenager.; One's parents.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English old, oold, from Old English ald, eald (“old, aged, ancient, antique, primeval”), from Proto-West Germanic *ald, from Proto-Germanic *aldaz (“grown-up”), originally a participle form, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eltós (“grown, tall, big”).

examples.text: The woman is wearing a black dress.

translations.de: Die Frau trägt ein schwarzes Kleid.
translations.fr: La femme porte une robe noire.
translations.pt: A mulher está usando um vestido preto.

examples.text: I don't like women like that.

translations.de: Solche Frauen mag ich nicht.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas les femmes comme ça.
translations.pt: Não gosto de mulheres assim.

examples.text: The woman eats fish and drinks wine.

translations.de: Die Frau ißt Fisch und trinkt Wein.
translations.fr: La femme mange du poisson et boit du vin.
translations.pt: A mulher come peixe e bebe vinho.

examples.text: The vampire bit the woman's neck.

translations.de: Der Vampir biss der Frau in den Hals.
translations.fr: Le vampire a mordu la femme au cou.
translations.pt: O vampiro mordeu o pescoço da mulher.

more.definition: An adult female human.; All female humans collectively; womankind.; A female person, usually an adult: a (generally adult) female sentient being, whether human, supernatural, elf, alien, etc.
more.etymology: From Middle English womman, from earlier wimman, wifman, from Old English wīfmann (“woman”, literally “female person”), a compound of wīf (“woman, female”, whence English wife) + mann (“person, human being”, whence English man). For details on the pronunciation and spelling history, see the usage notes below.

examples.text: You're the woman of my dreams.

translations.de: Du bist meine Traumfrau.
translations.fr: Tu es la femme de mes rêves.
translations.pt: Você é a mulher dos meus sonhos.

examples.text: You are the woman of my dreams.

translations.de: Du bist die Frau meiner Träume.
translations.fr: Tu es la femme de mes rêves.
translations.pt: Você é a mulher dos meus sonhos.

examples.text: Did Marika dress like a Japanese woman?

translations.de: Kleidete sich Marika wie eine Japanerin?
translations.fr: Marika s'est-elle habillée comme une Japonaise ?
translations.pt: A Marika se vestia como uma japonesa?

examples.text: I think she's an honest woman.

translations.de: Ich halte sie für eine ehrliche Frau.
translations.fr: Je crois que c'est une femme honnête.
translations.pt: Acho que ela é uma mulher honesta.

more.definition: To staff with female labor.; To make effeminate or womanish.; To furnish with, or unite to, a woman.
more.etymology: From Middle English womman, from earlier wimman, wifman, from Old English wīfmann (“woman”, literally “female person”), a compound of wīf (“woman, female”, whence English wife) + mann (“person, human being”, whence English man). For details on the pronunciation and spelling history, see the usage notes below.

examples.text: Tom often borrowed money from his friends.

translations.de: Tom lieh sich oftmals Geld von seinen Freunden.
translations.fr: Tom empruntait souvent de l'argent à ses amis.
translations.pt: De vez em quando, Tom pegava dinheiro emprestado dos amigos dele.

examples.text: Tom lost all the money he had.

translations.de: Tom verlor alles Geld, das er besaß.
translations.fr: Tom a perdu tout l'argent qu'il avait.
translations.pt: Tom perdeu todo o dinheiro que ele tinha.

examples.text: I'm not doing this for money.

translations.de: Ich tue das nicht um des Geldes willen.
translations.fr: Je ne fais pas ça pour l'argent.
translations.pt: Não estou fazendo isso por dinheiro.

examples.text: I'm in dire need of money.

translations.de: Ich brauche dringend Geld.
translations.fr: J'ai un besoin urgent d'argent.
translations.pt: Estou desesperadamente necessitando de dinheiro.

more.definition: Cool; excellent.
more.etymology: Anglo-Norman muneiebor. From Middle English moneye, moneie, money, borrowed from Anglo-Norman muneie (“money”), from Latin monēta (“money, a place for coining money, coin, mint”), from the name of the temple of Juno Moneta in Rome, where a mint was. In this sense, displaced native Old English feoh, whence English fee.

examples.text: Are you carrying a lot of money?

translations.de: Hast du viel Geld dabei?
translations.fr: As-tu beaucoup d'argent avec toi ?
translations.pt: Você está carregando muito dinheiro?

examples.text: Here's the money I owe you.

translations.de: Hier ist das Geld, das ich dir schulde.
translations.fr: Voici l'argent que je te dois.
translations.pt: Aqui está o dinheiro que te devo.

examples.text: Mary hid the money in her bra.

translations.de: Maria versteckte das Geld in ihrem BH.
translations.fr: Marie cacha l'argent dans son soutien-gorge.
translations.pt: Mary escondeu o dinheiro no sutiã.

examples.text: I bought it with my own money.

translations.de: Ich habe es von meinem eigenen Geld gekauft.
translations.fr: Je l'ai acheté avec mon propre argent.
translations.pt: Comprei-o com meu próprio dinheiro.

more.definition: A generally accepted means of exchange.; A currency maintained by a state or other entity which can guarantee its value (such as a monetary union).; Hard cash in the form of banknotes and coins, as opposed to cheques, credit cards, or credit more generally.
more.etymology: Anglo-Norman muneiebor. From Middle English moneye, moneie, money, borrowed from Anglo-Norman muneie (“money”), from Latin monēta (“money, a place for coining money, coin, mint”), from the name of the temple of Juno Moneta in Rome, where a mint was. In this sense, displaced native Old English feoh, whence English fee.

examples.text: There are around sixty species of hornbill.

translations.de: Es gibt etwa sechzig Arten von Nashornvögeln.
translations.fr: Il existe une soixantaine d'espèces de calaos.
translations.pt: Existem cerca de sessenta espécies de calaus.

examples.text: Julien wears round glasses, like John Lennon.

translations.de: Julien trägt runde Brillengläser, wie John Lennon.
translations.fr: Julien a des lunettes rondes, comme John Lennon.
translations.pt: Julien usa óculos redondos, como John Lennon.

examples.text: American films are popular around the world.

translations.de: Amerikanische Filme erfreuen sich weltweiter Beliebtheit.
translations.fr: Les films américains ont du succès dans le monde entier.
translations.pt: Os filmes americanos são populares no mundo todo.

examples.text: Is there a public beach around here?

translations.de: Gibt es hier in der Nähe einen öffentlichen Strand?
translations.fr: Y a-t-il une plage publique près d'ici ?
translations.pt: Há alguma praia pública aqui perto?

more.definition: Present in the vicinity.; Alive; existing.
more.etymology: From Middle English around, arounde, from a- (from Old English a- (“on, at”)) + Middle English round (“circle, round”) borrowed from French, equivalent to a- + round. Cognate with Scots aroond, aroon (“around”). Displaced earlier Middle English umbe, embe (“around”) (from Old English ymbe (“around”)).

examples.text: They built a fence around the farm.

translations.de: Sie bauten einen Zaun um den Bauernhof.
translations.fr: Ils ont construit une clôture autour de la ferme.
translations.pt: Eles ergueram uma cerca ao redor da fazenda.

examples.text: Strictly speaking, the earth is not round.

translations.de: Genau genommen ist die Erde nicht rund.
translations.fr: La Terre n’est pas ronde stricto sensu.
translations.pt: Estritamente falando, a Terra não é redonda.

examples.text: I want to travel around the world.

translations.de: Ich möchte um die Welt reisen.
translations.fr: Je veux voyager à travers le monde.
translations.pt: Quero viajar ao redor do mundo.

examples.text: I will show you around the city.

translations.de: Ich werde dir die Stadt zeigen.
translations.fr: Je te ferai visiter la ville.
translations.pt: Eu vou te mostrar a cidade.

more.definition: So as to form a circle or trace a circular path, or approximation thereof.; So as to surround or be near.; Nearly; approximately; about.
more.etymology: From Middle English around, arounde, from a- (from Old English a- (“on, at”)) + Middle English round (“circle, round”) borrowed from French, equivalent to a- + round. Cognate with Scots aroond, aroon (“around”). Displaced earlier Middle English umbe, embe (“around”) (from Old English ymbe (“around”)).

examples.text: We've walked all around the lake.

translations.de: Wir wanderten einmal um den See herum.
translations.fr: Nous avons marché tout autour du lac.
translations.pt: Nós caminhamos ao redor de todo o lago.

examples.text: He believed that the earth was round.

translations.de: Er glaubte, dass die Erde rund ist.
translations.fr: Il croyait que la Terre était ronde.
translations.pt: Ele acreditava que a Terra era redonda.

examples.text: I lost my key somewhere around here.

translations.de: Ich habe hier irgendwo meinen Schlüssel verloren.
translations.fr: J'ai perdu ma clef quelque part par ici.
translations.pt: Perdi minha chave em algum lugar por aqui.

examples.text: A mouse is running around the room.

translations.de: Eine Maus läuft im Zimmer herum.
translations.fr: Une souris court autour de la pièce.
translations.pt: Um rato está correndo pelo quarto.

more.definition: Forming a circle or closed curve containing (something).; Centred upon; surrounding; regarding.; Following the perimeter of a specified area and returning to the starting point.
more.etymology: From Middle English around, arounde, from a- (from Old English a- (“on, at”)) + Middle English round (“circle, round”) borrowed from French, equivalent to a- + round. Cognate with Scots aroond, aroon (“around”). Displaced earlier Middle English umbe, embe (“around”) (from Old English ymbe (“around”)).

examples.text: I think we should stay and fight.

translations.de: Ich finde, wir sollten bleiben und kämpfen.
translations.fr: Je pense que nous devrions rester et nous battre.
translations.pt: Acho que deveríamos ficar e lutar.

examples.text: I decided to stay one more day.

translations.de: Ich beschloss, noch einen Tag zu bleiben.
translations.fr: J'ai décidé de rester un jour de plus.
translations.pt: Eu decidi ficar mais um dia.

examples.text: I wish I could stay with you.

translations.de: Ich wünschte, ich könnte bei dir bleiben!
translations.fr: J'aimerais pouvoir rester avec toi.
translations.pt: Queria poder ficar com você.

examples.text: Tom, I want to stay with you.

translations.de: Tom, ich möchte bei dir bleiben.
translations.fr: Tom, je veux rester avec toi.
translations.pt: Tom, eu quero ficar com você.

more.etymology: From Middle English *steȝe, from Old English *stǣġe, an apocopated variant of stǣġel (“steep, abrupt”), from Proto-West Germanic *staigil (“steep”), see sty.

examples.text: I want to stay here with you.

translations.de: Ich möchte hier bei dir bleiben.
translations.fr: Je veux rester ici avec toi.
translations.pt: Eu quero ficar aqui com você.

examples.text: I don't want to stay here.

translations.de: Ich will nicht hierbleiben.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas rester ici.
translations.pt: Eu não quero ficar aqui.

examples.text: I'll stay here until you return.

translations.de: Ich bleibe hier, bis du wiederkommst.
translations.fr: Je resterai ici jusqu'à votre retour.
translations.pt: Ficarei aqui até vocês voltarem.

examples.text: How long will you stay in Japan?

translations.de: Wie lange wirst du in Japan bleiben?
translations.fr: Combien de temps vas-tu rester au Japon ?
translations.pt: Por quanto tempo você vai ficar no Japão?

more.etymology: From Middle English *steȝe, from Old English *stǣġe, an apocopated variant of stǣġel (“steep, abrupt”), from Proto-West Germanic *staigil (“steep”), see sty.

examples.text: I hope the weather stays this way.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, das Wetter bleibt so.
translations.fr: J'espère que le temps va rester comme ça.
translations.pt: Espero que o tempo continue assim.

examples.text: How long do you plan to stay?

translations.de: Wie lange haben Sie vor zu bleiben?
translations.fr: Combien de temps comptes-tu rester ?
translations.pt: Quanto tempo você pretende ficar?

examples.text: Can't you stay a little longer?

translations.de: Kannst du nicht noch etwas länger bleiben?
translations.fr: Tu ne peux pas rester un peu plus longtemps ?
translations.pt: Você não pode ficar um pouco mais?

examples.text: Whatever happens, you have to stay calm.

translations.de: Was auch passiert, du musst ruhig bleiben.
translations.fr: Quoi qu'il arrive, tu dois rester calme.
translations.pt: Não importa o que aconteça, você deve permanecer calmo.

more.definition: Continuance or a period of time spent in a place; abode for an indefinite time.; A postponement, especially of an execution or other punishment.; A fixed state; fixedness; stability; permanence.
more.etymology: From Middle English steyen, staien, from Old French estayer, estaier (“to fix, prop up, support, stay”), from estaye, estaie (“a prop, stay”), from Middle Dutch staeye (“a prop, stay”), a contracted form of staede, stade (“a prop, stay, help, aid”) (compare Middle Dutch staeyen, staeden (“to make firm, stay, support, hold still, stabilise”)), from Proto-West Germanic *stadi (“a site, place, location, standing”), …

examples.text: I want you to stay with me.

translations.de: Ich will, dass du bei mir bleibst.
translations.fr: Je veux que tu restes avec moi.
translations.pt: Quero que fiques comigo.

examples.text: How long will you stay in Tokyo?

translations.de: Wie lange wirst du in Tokio bleiben?
translations.fr: Combien de temps resteras-tu à Tokyo ?
translations.pt: Quanto tempo ficará em Tóquio?

examples.text: Will you stay here for a while?

translations.de: Wirst du eine Weile hier bleiben?
translations.fr: Resterez-vous ici pendant quelque temps ?
translations.pt: Você pode ficar aqui por um tempo?

examples.text: I think I'd better stay here.

translations.de: Ich denke, ich bleibe besser hier.
translations.fr: Je pense que je ferais mieux de rester ici.
translations.pt: Acho que é melhor eu ficar aqui.

more.definition: Aspect marker indicating frequency or permanence.
more.etymology: From Middle English stay, from Old French estaye, estaie (“a prop, a stay”), from Middle Dutch staeye (“a prop, stay”), a contracted form of staede, stade ("a prop, stay, help, aid"; compare Middle Dutch staeyen, staeden (“to make firm, stay, support, hold still, stabilise”)), from Old Dutch *stad (“a site, place, location, standing”), from Proto-Germanic *stadiz (“a standing, place”), from Proto-Indo-European …

examples.text: Tom stayed in Boston for three years.

translations.de: Tom blieb drei Jahre in Boston.
translations.fr: Tom est resté trois ans à Boston.
translations.pt: Tom ficou em Boston por três anos.

examples.text: I'm used to staying up late.

translations.de: Ich bin es gewohnt, spät ins Bett zu gehen.
translations.fr: Je suis habitué à rester debout tard.
translations.pt: Estou acostumado a ficar acordado até tarde.

examples.text: You may go or stay at will.

translations.de: Du kannst gehen oder bleiben, wie es dir beliebt.
translations.fr: Tu peux partir ou rester selon ton bon plaisir.
translations.pt: Se quiser ir ou ficar, sinta-se à vontade.

examples.text: We stayed at a three-star hotel.

translations.de: Wir wohnten in einem Drei-Sterne-Hotel.
translations.fr: Nous avons séjourné dans un hôtel trois étoiles.
translations.pt: Ficamos num hotel três estrelas.

more.definition: To remain in a particular place, especially for a definite or short period of time; sojourn; abide.; To continue to have a particular quality.; To prop; support; sustain; hold up; steady.
more.etymology: From Middle English steyen, staien, from Old French estayer, estaier (“to fix, prop up, support, stay”), from estaye, estaie (“a prop, stay”), from Middle Dutch staeye (“a prop, stay”), a contracted form of staede, stade (“a prop, stay, help, aid”) (compare Middle Dutch staeyen, staeden (“to make firm, stay, support, hold still, stabilise”)), from Proto-West Germanic *stadi (“a site, place, location, standing”), …

examples.text: My favorite TV show's been canceled.

translations.de: Meine Lieblingssendung wurde abgesetzt.
translations.fr: Mon programme télé préféré a été annulé.
translations.pt: O meu seriado favorito foi cancelado.

examples.text: He shows me the way to the airport.

translations.de: Er zeigt mir den Weg zum Flughafen.
translations.fr: Il me montre le chemin de l'aéroport.
translations.pt: Ele está me mostrando o caminho para o aeroporto.

examples.text: I've got to show you something.

translations.de: Ich muss Ihnen etwas zeigen.
translations.fr: Je dois te montrer quelque chose.
translations.pt: Eu tenho que te mostrar uma coisa.

examples.text: What did you want to show me?

translations.de: Was wolltest du mir zeigen?
translations.fr: Que vouliez-vous me montrer ?
translations.pt: O que você queria me mostrar?

more.definition: A play, dance, or other entertainment.; An exhibition of items.; A broadcast program, especially a light entertainment program.
more.etymology: From Middle English schewe, from the verb (schewen).

examples.text: Have you shown this letter to anybody?

translations.de: Hast du diesen Brief irgend jemandem gezeigt?
translations.fr: Avez-vous montré cette lettre à quelqu'un ?
translations.pt: Vocês mostraram esta carta para alguém?

examples.text: I don't usually show my feelings.

translations.de: Ich zeige meine Gefühle für gewöhnlich nicht.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas l'habitude de montrer mes sentiments.
translations.pt: Eu geralmente não exteriorizo meus sentimentos.

examples.text: Tom showed Mary's letter to me.

translations.de: Tom zeigte mir den Brief von Maria.
translations.fr: Tom m'a montré la lettre de Mary.
translations.pt: Tom me mostrou a carta de Maria.

examples.text: Sometimes I can't help showing emotions.

translations.de: Manchmal kann ich es nicht vermeiden, Gefühle zu zeigen.
translations.fr: Parfois je ne peux pas m'empêcher de montrer des émotions.
translations.pt: Às vezes não consigo me segurar ao mostrar minhas emoções.

more.definition: To display, convey or exhibit; to have something available for others to see; to direct attention to something.; To indicate; to convey facts that lead to a conclusion.; To guide or escort; to show the way.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewh₁-der. From Middle English schewen, from Old English scēawian (“to look, look at, exhibit, display”), from Proto-West Germanic *skauwōn, from Proto-Germanic *skawwōną (“to look, see”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewh₁- (“to heed, look, feel, take note of”); see haw, gaum, caveat, caution.

examples.text: I know a lot of French songs.

translations.de: Ich kenne viele französische Lieder.
translations.fr: Je connais beaucoup de chansons françaises.
translations.pt: Conheço muitas músicas francesas.

examples.text: Leaking taps waste a lot of water.

translations.de: Tropfende Wasserhähne vergeuden viel Wasser.
translations.fr: Les robinets qui fuient gâchent beaucoup d'eau.
translations.pt: Torneiras que pingam desperdiçam muita água.

examples.text: I made a lot of stupid mistakes.

translations.de: Ich habe viele dumme Fehler gemacht.
translations.fr: J'ai fait beaucoup d'erreurs idiotes.
translations.pt: Eu fiz muitos erros estúpidos.

examples.text: I've got a lot to do.

translations.de: Ich habe viel zu tun.
translations.fr: J'ai beaucoup à faire.
translations.pt: Eu tenho muito que fazer.

more.definition: A large quantity or number; a great deal.; A separate, appropriated portion; a quantized, subdivided set consisting a whole.; One or more items auctioned or sold as a unit, separate from other items.
more.etymology: From Middle English lot, from Old English hlot (“portion, choice, decision”), from Proto-West Germanic *hlut, from Proto-Germanic *hlutą. Cognate with North Frisian lod, Saterland Frisian Lot, West Frisian lot, Dutch lot, French lot, German Low German Lott, Middle High German luz. Doublet of lotto. Related also to German Los.

examples.text: Historians usually read a lot of books.

translations.de: Historiker lesen normalerweise viele Bücher.
translations.fr: Les historiens lisent généralement beaucoup de livres.
translations.pt: Os historiadores costumam ler muitos livros.

examples.text: We swim a lot and enjoy it.

translations.de: Wir schwimmen viel und gerne.
translations.fr: Nous nageons beaucoup et nous aimons ça.
translations.pt: Nadamos muito e temos prazer nisso.

examples.text: I have read a lot of books.

translations.de: Ich habe viele Bücher gelesen.
translations.fr: J'ai lu beaucoup de livres.
translations.pt: Eu li muitos livros.

examples.text: Do Germans eat a lot of pork?

translations.de: Essen die Deutschen viel Schweinefleisch?
translations.fr: Les Allemands mangent-ils beaucoup de porc ?
translations.pt: Os alemães comem muita carne de porco?

more.etymology: From Middle English lot, from Old English hlot (“portion, choice, decision”), from Proto-West Germanic *hlut, from Proto-Germanic *hlutą. Cognate with North Frisian lod, Saterland Frisian Lot, West Frisian lot, Dutch lot, French lot, German Low German Lott, Middle High German luz. Doublet of lotto. Related also to German Los.

examples.text: I don't want to play golf.

translations.de: Ich habe keine Lust auf Golf.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas jouer au golf.
translations.pt: Eu não quero jogar golfe.

examples.text: He plays the piano better than me.

translations.de: Er spielt besser Klavier als ich.
translations.fr: Il joue mieux du piano que moi.
translations.pt: Ele toca piano melhor que eu.

examples.text: Do you want to play with Tom?

translations.de: Willst du mit Tom spielen?
translations.fr: Voulez-vous jouer avec Tom ?
translations.pt: Você quer brincar com Tom?

examples.text: Your dad wants you to play soccer.

translations.de: Dein Vater will, daß du Fußball spielst.
translations.fr: Ton père veut que tu joues au foot.
translations.pt: Seu pai quer que você jogue futebol.

more.definition: Activity for amusement only, especially among the young.; Similar activity in young animals, as they explore their environment and learn new skills.; The conduct, or course, of a game.
more.etymology: From Middle English pleyen (verb) and Middle English pleye (noun), from Old English plegian and plegan, plagian (“to play, exercise, etc.”), from Proto-West Germanic *plehan (“to care about, be concerned with”) and Proto-West Germanic *plegōn (“to engage, move”), of uncertain origin.

examples.text: The singer sings while playing the piano.

translations.de: Der Sänger singt, während er Klavier spielt.
translations.fr: La chanteuse chante en jouant du piano.
translations.pt: A cantora canta acompanhando-se ao piano.

examples.text: I'm going to play tennis tomorrow.

translations.de: Ich spiele morgen Tennis.
translations.fr: Je vais jouer au tennis demain.
translations.pt: Irei jogar tênis amanhã.

examples.text: Tom played the piano and Mary sang.

translations.de: Tom spielte Klavier und Maria sang.
translations.fr: Tom jouait du piano et Marie chantait.
translations.pt: Tom tocou piano e Maria cantou.

examples.text: Tom plays the piano better than Mary.

translations.de: Tom spielt besser Klavier als Maria.
translations.fr: Tom joue mieux du piano que Marie.
translations.pt: Tom toca piano melhor do que Maria.

more.definition: To act in a manner such that one has fun; to engage in activities expressly for the purpose of recreation or entertainment.; To toy or trifle; to act with levity or thoughtlessness; to be careless.; To perform in (a sport); to participate in (a game).
more.etymology: From Middle English pleyen (verb) and Middle English pleye (noun), from Old English plegian and plegan, plagian (“to play, exercise, etc.”), from Proto-West Germanic *plehan (“to care about, be concerned with”) and Proto-West Germanic *plegōn (“to engage, move”), of uncertain origin.

examples.text: All parents want their kids to be happy.

translations.de: Alle Eltern wollen, dass ihre Kinder glücklich sind.
translations.fr: Tous les parents veulent que leurs enfants soient heureux.
translations.pt: Todos os pais querem que os seus filhos sejam felizes.

examples.text: Tom isn't a kid anymore.

translations.de: Tom ist kein Kind mehr.
translations.fr: Tom n'est plus un enfant.
translations.pt: Tom não é mais criança.

examples.text: The kindergarten is full of kids.

translations.de: Der Kindergarten ist voller Kinder.
translations.fr: Le jardin d'enfants est plein d'enfants.
translations.pt: O jardim de infância está cheio de crianças.

examples.text: The kids ran toward the playground.

translations.de: Die Kinder rannten zum Spielplatz.
translations.fr: Les enfants ont couru vers l'aire de jeux.
translations.pt: As crianças correram em direção ao parquinho.

more.definition: A child, adolescent, or (loosely) a young adult.; A person whose childhood took place in a particular time period or area.; One's son or daughter, regardless of age.
more.etymology: From Middle English kide, from Old Norse kið (“young goat”), from Proto-Germanic *kidją, *kittīną (“goatling, kid”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *gʰaydn-, *ǵʰaydn- (“goat”) or Proto-Indo-European *gidʰ- (“kid, goatling, little goat”). Compare Swedish and Danish kid, German Kitz and Kitze, Albanian kedh and kec. The sense of child has been in use since the 1590s as slang, and since the 1840s in informal use.

examples.text: You are kidding me, aren't you?

translations.de: Du veräppelst mich, oder?
translations.fr: Vous êtes un petit farceur, hein ?
translations.pt: Você está brincando comigo, não é?

examples.text: Tom is taking care of the kids.

translations.de: Tom kümmert sich um die Kinder.
translations.fr: Tom prend soin des enfants.
translations.pt: Tom está cuidando das crianças.

examples.text: She bought a toy for the kid.

translations.de: Sie kaufte dem Kind ein Spielzeug.
translations.fr: Elle a acheté un jouet pour le gosse.
translations.pt: Ela comprou um brinquedo para a criança.

examples.text: Don't treat me like a kid.

translations.de: Behandel mich nicht wie ein Kind.
translations.fr: Ne me traite pas comme un gamin.
translations.pt: Não me trate como a uma criança.

more.definition: To dupe or deceive.; To deceive or dupe as a joke.; To deceive oneself by having unrealistic expectations.
more.etymology: From Middle English kide, from Old Norse kið (“young goat”), from Proto-Germanic *kidją, *kittīną (“goatling, kid”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *gʰaydn-, *ǵʰaydn- (“goat”) or Proto-Indo-European *gidʰ- (“kid, goatling, little goat”). Compare Swedish and Danish kid, German Kitz and Kitze, Albanian kedh and kec. The sense of child has been in use since the 1590s as slang, and since the 1840s in informal use.

examples.text: I don't believe in the Devil.

translations.de: Ich glaube nicht an den Teufel.
translations.fr: Je ne crois pas au diable.
translations.pt: Não acredito no diabo.

examples.text: Tom believed that John was his brother.

translations.de: Tom glaubte, Johannes sei sein Bruder.
translations.fr: Tom croyait que John était son frère.
translations.pt: Tom pensava que João era seu irmão.

examples.text: Mary believes in the power of love.

translations.de: Maria glaubt an die Macht der Liebe.
translations.fr: Marie croit au pouvoir de l'amour.
translations.pt: Mary acredita no poder do amor.

examples.text: I know Tom won't believe me.

translations.de: Ich weiß, daß Tom mir nicht glauben wird.
translations.fr: Je sais que Tom ne va pas me croire.
translations.pt: Eu sei que Tom não vai acreditar em mim.

more.definition: To accept as true, particularly without absolute certainty (i.e., as opposed to knowing).; To accept that someone is telling the truth.; To have been convinced by rational means to accept the truth of a proposition.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₁ep-der. Proto-Indo-European *h₁épsder. Proto-Indo-European *h₁épider. Proto-Germanic *bider. Proto-Indo-European *lewbʰ-der. From Middle English beleven, bileven, from Old English belīefan (“to believe”), from Proto-West Germanic *bilaubijan (“to believe”), equivalent to be- + leave (“to give leave or permission to, permit, allow, grant”).

examples.text: Could you bring me a Japanese newspaper?

translations.de: Können Sie mir eine japanische Zeitung bringen?
translations.fr: Pourriez-vous m'apporter un journal japonais ?
translations.pt: Você pode me trazer um jornal japonês?

examples.text: Did you bring an umbrella with you?

translations.de: Hast du einen Regenschirm mitgebracht?
translations.fr: As-tu pris un parapluie avec toi ?
translations.pt: Trouxe um guarda-chuva com você?

examples.text: May the new year bring you happiness!

translations.de: Möge dir das neue Jahr Glück bringen!
translations.fr: Puisse la nouvelle année t'apporter la joie.
translations.pt: Que o novo ano te traga felicidade!

examples.text: Please bring me two pieces of chalk.

translations.de: Bring mir bitte zwei Kreidestücke.
translations.fr: S'il vous plaît, apportez-moi deux morceaux de craie.
translations.pt: Por favor, traga-me dois gizes.

more.definition: The sound of a telephone ringing.
more.etymology: Onomatopoeia.

examples.text: Don't forget to bring a camera.

translations.de: Vergiss nicht, die Kamera mitzubringen.
translations.fr: N'oublie pas de prendre un appareil photo avec toi.
translations.pt: Não se esqueça de trazer uma câmera.

examples.text: She brought me a cup of tea.

translations.de: Sie brachte mir eine Tasse Tee.
translations.fr: Elle m'apporta une tasse de thé.
translations.pt: Ela me trouxe uma xícara de chá.

examples.text: The child brings them to me.

translations.de: Das Kind bringt sie zu mir.
translations.fr: L'enfant me les apporte.
translations.pt: A criança os traz para mim.

examples.text: She brought up the three children alone.

translations.de: Sie zog die drei Kinder alleine groß.
translations.fr: Elle éleva les trois enfants seule.
translations.pt: Ela criou três filhos por conta própria.

more.definition: To transport toward somebody/somewhere.; To supply or contribute.; To occasion or bring about.
more.etymology: From Middle English bryngen, from Old English bringan, from Proto-West Germanic *bringan, from Proto-Germanic *bringaną (“to bring”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰrenk-, possibly based on *bʰer-.

examples.text: Have you ever heard someone speaking French?

translations.de: Hast du schon einmal jemanden Französisch sprechen hören?
translations.fr: As-tu déjà entendu quelqu'un parler français ?
translations.pt: Você já ouviu alguém falando francês?

examples.text: Don't you ever clean your room?

translations.de: Machst du eigentlich nie dein Zimmer sauber?
translations.fr: Ne nettoies-tu jamais ta chambre ?
translations.pt: Você nunca limpa o seu quarto?

examples.text: I don't believe Atlantis ever existed.

translations.de: Ich glaube nicht, dass Atlantis je existierte.
translations.fr: Je ne crois pas que l'Atlantide ait jamais existé.
translations.pt: Eu não acredito que a Atlântida tenha existido.

examples.text: Don't ever lie to me again.

translations.de: Lüge mich nie wieder an!
translations.fr: Ne me mentez jamais plus.
translations.pt: Nunca mais minta para mim.

more.definition: Occurring at any time, occurring even but once during a timespan.
more.etymology: From Middle English ever, from Old English ǣfre, originally a phrase whose first element undoubtedly consists of Old English ā (“ever, always”) + in (“in”) + an element possibly from feorh (“life, existence”) (dative fēore). Compare Old English ā tō fēore (“ever in life”), Old English feorhlīf (“life”) from feorh (“life”) + līf (“life”).

examples.text: If anybody was ever wise, Cato was.

translations.de: Wenn jemals jemand weise war, dann war es Cato.
translations.fr: Si quelqu'un a jamais été sage, c'est bien Caton.
translations.pt: Se já houve alguém sábio, Catão o foi.

examples.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with asthma?

translations.de: Wurde bei Ihnen schon einmal Asthma disgnostiziert?
translations.fr: A-t-on déjà diagnostiqué chez toi de l'asthme ?
translations.pt: Alguma vez você foi diagnosticado com asma?

examples.text: Don't you ever say that again.

translations.de: Sag das bloß nie wieder.
translations.fr: Ne répétez plus jamais ça !
translations.pt: Nunca mais diga isso!

examples.text: No one ever escapes from this prison.

translations.de: Aus diesem Gefängnis entkommt nie jemand.
translations.fr: Personne ne s'évade jamais de cette prison.
translations.pt: Ninguém nunca escapa desta prisão.

more.definition: Continuously, constantly, all the time (for the complete duration).; At any time.; As intensifier following an interrogative word.
more.etymology: From Middle English ever, from Old English ǣfre, originally a phrase whose first element undoubtedly consists of Old English ā (“ever, always”) + in (“in”) + an element possibly from feorh (“life, existence”) (dative fēore). Compare Old English ā tō fēore (“ever in life”), Old English feorhlīf (“life”) from feorh (“life”) + līf (“life”).

examples.text: Have you ever forgotten your phone number?

translations.de: Hast du schon einmal deine Telefonnummer vergessen?
translations.fr: As-tu déjà oublié ton numéro de téléphone ?
translations.pt: Você já esqueceu o seu número de telefone?
