examples.text: I promise never to promise anything ever again.

translations.de: Ich verspreche, dass ich niemals mehr irgendetwas versprechen werde.
translations.fr: Je promets que je ne promettrai plus jamais quelque chose.
translations.pt: Eu prometo que nunca mais prometerei o que quer que seja.

examples.text: She was the only woman I ever loved.

translations.de: Sie war die einzige Frau, die ich je geliebt hatte.
translations.fr: Elle était la seule femme que j'aie jamais aimée.
translations.pt: Ela foi a única mulher que eu amei.

examples.text: Did Greece ever have a king?

translations.de: Hatte Griechenland jemals einen König?
translations.fr: La Grèce a-t-elle jamais eu un roi ?
translations.pt: A Grécia já teve rei?

more.etymology: From Middle English ever, from Old English ǣfre, originally a phrase whose first element undoubtedly consists of Old English ā (“ever, always”) + in (“in”) + an element possibly from feorh (“life, existence”) (dative fēore). Compare Old English ā tō fēore (“ever in life”), Old English feorhlīf (“life”) from feorh (“life”) + līf (“life”).

examples.text: My pen has run out of ink.

translations.de: In meinem Füller ist keine Tinte mehr.
translations.fr: Mon stylo n'a plus d'encre.
translations.pt: A tinta da minha caneta acabou.

examples.text: The pen has run out of ink.

translations.de: Dem Füller ist die Tinte ausgegangen.
translations.fr: Le stylo n'a plus d'encre.
translations.pt: A caneta ficou sem tinta.

examples.text: Tom allowed his dog to run free.

translations.de: Tom ließ seinen Hund frei laufen.
translations.fr: Tom autorisa son chien à courir librement.
translations.pt: Tom deixou o seu cachorro correr livre.

examples.text: In general, men run faster than women.

translations.de: Männer können in der Regel schneller laufen als Frauen.
translations.fr: En général, les hommes courent plus vite que les femmes.
translations.pt: No geral, os homens correm mais rápidos do que as mulheres.

more.definition: In a liquid state; melted or molten.; Cast in a mould.; Exhausted; depleted (especially with "down" or "out").
more.etymology: From Middle English runnen, rennen (“to run”), alteration (due to the past participle runne, runnen, yronne) of Middle English rinnen (“to run”), from Old English rinnan, iernan (“to run”) and Old Norse rinna (“to run”), both from Proto-Germanic *rinnaną (“to run”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃reyH- (“to boil, churn”).

examples.text: Sometimes he runs, sometimes he walks.

translations.de: Manchmal rennt er, manchmal geht er.
translations.fr: Parfois il court, parfois il marche.
translations.pt: Às vezes ele corre, às vezes ele caminha.

examples.text: My nose runs whenever I have a cold.

translations.de: Immer wenn ich eine Erkältung habe, läuft meine Nase.
translations.fr: Chaque fois que j'ai un rhume, mon nez coule.
translations.pt: Meu nariz sempre escorre quando estou resfriado.

examples.text: She runs faster than I do.

translations.de: Sie läuft schneller als ich.
translations.fr: Elle court plus vite que moi.
translations.pt: Ela corre mais rápido que eu.

examples.text: He runs as fast as you.

translations.de: Er läuft genauso schnell wie du.
translations.fr: Il court aussi vite que toi.
translations.pt: Ele corre tão rápido quanto você.

more.definition: Act or instance of running, of moving rapidly using the feet.; Act or instance of hurrying (to or from a place) (not necessarily on foot); dash or errand, trip.; A pleasure trip.
more.etymology: From Middle English runnen, rennen (“to run”), alteration (due to the past participle runne, runnen, yronne) of Middle English rinnen (“to run”), from Old English rinnan, iernan (“to run”) and Old Norse rinna (“to run”), both from Proto-Germanic *rinnaną (“to run”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃reyH- (“to boil, churn”).

examples.text: He runs in the park every day.

translations.de: Er joggt jeden Tag im Park.
translations.fr: Il court chaque jour dans le parc.
translations.pt: Ele corre no parque todo dia.

examples.text: Who is that boy running toward us?

translations.de: Wer ist der Junge, der da auf uns zugerannt kommt?
translations.fr: Qui est le garçon qui vient en courant vers nous ?
translations.pt: Quem é o menino que está correndo em nossa direção?

examples.text: He runs a supermarket in the town.

translations.de: Er betreibt in der Stadt einen Supermarkt.
translations.fr: Il gère un supermarché en ville.
translations.pt: Ele administra um supermercado na cidade.

examples.text: These shoes are not suitable for running.

translations.de: Diese Schuhe sind nicht zum Laufen geeignet.
translations.fr: Ces chaussures ne sont pas adaptées à la course.
translations.pt: Estes tênis não são apropriados para correr.

more.definition: To move forward quickly upon two feet by alternately making a short jump off either foot.; To go at a fast pace; to move quickly.; To cover (a course or a distance) by running.
more.etymology: From Middle English runnen, rennen (“to run”), alteration (due to the past participle runne, runnen, yronne) of Middle English rinnen (“to run”), from Old English rinnan, iernan (“to run”) and Old Norse rinna (“to run”), both from Proto-Germanic *rinnaną (“to run”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃reyH- (“to boil, churn”).

examples.text: Could you move the chair a bit?

translations.de: Könntest du den Stuhl ein wenig verschieben?
translations.fr: Pourrais-tu bouger un peu la chaise ?
translations.pt: Você pode mover um pouco a cadeira?

examples.text: Don't make abrupt moves.

translations.de: Mach keine brüsken Bewegungen.
translations.fr: Ne fais pas de mouvements brusques.
translations.pt: Não faça movimentos bruscos.

examples.text: She decided to move to Belgium.

translations.de: Sie beschloss, nach Belgien zu ziehen.
translations.fr: Elle a décidé de s'installer en Belgique.
translations.pt: Decidiu mudar-se para a Bélgica.

examples.text: Please move away from the door.

translations.de: Bitte gehen Sie von der Tür weg.
translations.fr: Veuillez vous éloigner de la porte.
translations.pt: Afastem-se da porta, por favor.

more.definition: The act of moving; a movement.; An act for the attainment of an object; a step in the execution of a plan or purpose.; A formalized or practiced action used in athletics, dance, physical exercise, self-defense, hand-to-hand combat, etc.
more.etymology: Old Northern French moverbor. From Middle English moven, moeven, meven, borrowed from Old Northern French mover, moveir and Old French mouver, moveir (“to move”) (compare modern French mouvoir from Old French movoir), from Latin movēre (“move; change, exchange, go in or out, quit”), from Proto-Indo-European *m(y)ewh₁- (“to move, drive”).

examples.text: I'm going to move next month.

translations.de: Ich werde nächsten Monat umziehen.
translations.fr: Je vais déménager le mois prochain.
translations.pt: Eu vou me mudar próximo mês.

examples.text: He moved to Istanbul with his wife.

translations.de: Er ist mit seiner Frau nach Istanbul gezogen.
translations.fr: Il a déménagé à Istanbul avec sa femme.
translations.pt: Ele se mudou com a esposa para Istambul.

examples.text: The boy tried moving the heavy sofa.

translations.de: Der Junge versuchte, das schwere Sofa zu bewegen.
translations.fr: Le garçon a essayé de déplacer le canapé lourd.
translations.pt: O menino tentou mover o sofá pesado.

examples.text: The dogs bark, but the caravan moves on.

translations.de: Die Hunde bellen, aber die Karawane zieht unbeirrt ihres Weges.
translations.fr: Les chiens aboient, la caravane passe.
translations.pt: Os cães ladram, mas a caravana passa.

more.definition: To change place or posture; to go, in any manner, from one place or position to another.; To act; to take action; to begin to act; To change residence, for example from one house, town, or state, to another; to go and live at another place; similarly to change the location of another establishment such as a business. See also move out and move in.
more.etymology: Old Northern French moverbor. From Middle English moven, moeven, meven, borrowed from Old Northern French mover, moveir and Old French mouver, moveir (“to move”) (compare modern French mouvoir from Old French movoir), from Latin movēre (“move; change, exchange, go in or out, quit”), from Proto-Indo-European *m(y)ewh₁- (“to move, drive”).

examples.text: That's probably not a bad idea.

translations.de: Das ist vermutlich keine schlechte Idee.
translations.fr: Ce n'est sans doute pas une mauvaise idée.
translations.pt: Provavelmente isso não é uma má ideia.

examples.text: I feel bad about what I said.

translations.de: Es reut mich, was ich gesagt habe.
translations.fr: Je me sens mal au sujet de ce que j'ai dit.
translations.pt: Eu me senti mal pelo que disse.

examples.text: Eating meat is bad for the environment.

translations.de: Fleischkonsum ist schlecht für die Umwelt.
translations.fr: Manger de la viande est mauvais pour l'environnement.
translations.pt: Comer carne prejudica o meio.

examples.text: The weather's bad, isn't it?

translations.de: Das Wetter ist schlecht, nicht wahr?
translations.fr: Le temps est mauvais, non ?
translations.pt: O tempo está ruim, não é?

more.definition: Of low quality.; Inaccurate; incorrect; Unfavorable; negative; not good.
more.etymology: From Middle English bad, badde (“wicked, evil, depraved”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps a shortening of Old English bæddel (“hermaphrodite”) (for loss of -el compare Middle English muche from Old English myċel, and Middle English wenche from Old English wenċel), or at least related to it and/or to bǣ̆dan (“to defile”), compare Old High German pad (“hermaphrodite”).

examples.text: She has never had a bad experience.

translations.de: Sie hat nie schlechte Erfahrungen gemacht.
translations.fr: Elle n'a jamais eu de mauvaise expérience.
translations.pt: Ela nunca teve uma experiência ruim.

examples.text: I think my German is really bad.

translations.de: Mein Deutsch ist, denke ich, äußerst schlecht.
translations.fr: Je pense que mon allemand est vraiment mauvais.
translations.pt: Acho que meu alemão é mesmo ruim.

examples.text: I'm in a bad mood today.

translations.de: Ich bin heute schlechter Laune.
translations.fr: Je suis de mauvaise humeur aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Hoje estou de mau humor.

examples.text: He attributes his poverty to bad luck.

translations.de: Er schreibt seine Armut seinem schlechten Aussehen zu.
translations.fr: Il attribue sa pauvreté à la malchance.
translations.pt: Ele atribui sua pobreza ao azar.

more.definition: Badly; poorly.; Badly; severely, extremely, passionately, eagerly.
more.etymology: From Middle English bad, badde (“wicked, evil, depraved”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps a shortening of Old English bæddel (“hermaphrodite”) (for loss of -el compare Middle English muche from Old English myċel, and Middle English wenche from Old English wenċel), or at least related to it and/or to bǣ̆dan (“to defile”), compare Old High German pad (“hermaphrodite”).

examples.text: I had a bad dream last night.

translations.de: Letzte Nacht hatte ich einen schlechten Traum.
translations.fr: Hier soir j'ai fait un cauchemar.
translations.pt: Ontem à noite eu tive um pesadelo.

examples.text: I'm suffering from a bad headache.

translations.de: Ich habe schreckliche Kopfschmerzen.
translations.fr: J'ai un terrible mal de crâne.
translations.pt: Estou com uma terrível dor de cabeça.

examples.text: Telling lies is a very bad habit.

translations.de: Lügen ist eine sehr schlechte Angewohnheit.
translations.fr: Raconter des mensonges, est une très vilaine habitude.
translations.pt: Contar mentiras é um hábito muito ruim.

examples.text: Do you think it a bad thing?

translations.de: Hältst du es für etwas Schlechtes?
translations.fr: Penses-tu que ce soit une mauvaise chose ?
translations.pt: Você acha que isso é ruim?

more.definition: Used to scold a misbehaving child or pet.
more.etymology: From Middle English bad, badde (“wicked, evil, depraved”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps a shortening of Old English bæddel (“hermaphrodite”) (for loss of -el compare Middle English muche from Old English myċel, and Middle English wenche from Old English wenċel), or at least related to it and/or to bǣ̆dan (“to defile”), compare Old High German pad (“hermaphrodite”).

examples.text: It's bad luck to say that.

translations.de: Es bringt Pech, das zu sagen.
translations.fr: Ça porte malheur de dire ça.
translations.pt: Dá azar dizer isso.

examples.text: You must rid yourself of bad habits.

translations.de: Du musst von deinen schlechten Angewohnheiten loskommen.
translations.fr: Tu dois te débarrasser des mauvaises habitudes.
translations.pt: Você deve se livrar de maus hábitos.

examples.text: The bad people are in prison.

translations.de: Die Bösen sind im Gefängnis.
translations.fr: Les mauvais éléments sont en prison.
translations.pt: As pessoas más estão na prisão.

examples.text: The coat is not bad, I like it.

translations.de: Der Mantel ist nicht schlecht, gefällt mir.
translations.fr: Le manteau n'est pas mal, j'aime bien.
translations.pt: O casaco não é mau, eu gosto.

more.definition: Something that is bad; a harm or evil.; Error; mistake.; An item (or kind of item) of merchandise with negative value; an unwanted good.
more.etymology: From Middle English bad, badde (“wicked, evil, depraved”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps a shortening of Old English bæddel (“hermaphrodite”) (for loss of -el compare Middle English muche from Old English myċel, and Middle English wenche from Old English wenċel), or at least related to it and/or to bǣ̆dan (“to defile”), compare Old High German pad (“hermaphrodite”).

examples.text: The bad harvest caused massive food shortages.

translations.de: Die schlechte Ernte verursachte eine massive Lebensmittelknappheit.
translations.fr: La mauvaise récolte a provoqué des pénuries alimentaires massives.
translations.pt: A colheita ruim provocou grande escassez de comida.

examples.text: He came in spite of bad weather.

translations.de: Er kam trotz des schlechten Wetters.
translations.fr: Il est venu en dépit du mauvais temps.
translations.pt: Ele veio, mesmo com todo o mau tempo.

examples.text: He was suffering from a bad headache.

translations.de: Er hatte starke Kopfschmerzen.
translations.fr: Il souffrait de maux de tête.
translations.pt: Ele estava sofrendo de uma terrível dor de cabeça.

examples.text: The situation went from bad to worse.

translations.de: Die Situation wurde immer schlimmer.
translations.fr: La situation allait de pire en pire.
translations.pt: A situação foi de má a pior.

more.etymology: From Middle English bad, from Old English bæd, first- and third-person singular indicative past tense of biddan (“to ask”).

examples.text: Isn't that a boy's name?

translations.de: Ist das nicht der Name eines Jungen?
translations.fr: N'est-ce pas le nom d'un garçon ?
translations.pt: Isso é o nome de um menino?

examples.text: There's a new boy in school.

translations.de: Es gibt einen neuen Jungen in der Schule.
translations.fr: Il y a un nouveau garçon à l'école.
translations.pt: Há um menino novo na escola.

examples.text: Tom is a shy and lonely boy.

translations.de: Tom ist ein scheuer, einsamer Bub.
translations.fr: Tom est un garçon timide et solitaire.
translations.pt: Tom é moço tímido e solitário.

examples.text: She has a crush on this boy.

translations.de: Sie steht auf diesen Jungen.
translations.fr: Elle en pince pour ce garçon.
translations.pt: Ela está caidinha por este moço.

more.definition: Exclamation of surprise, pleasure or longing.
more.etymology: From Middle English boy /boye (“servant, commoner, knave, boy”), from Old English *bōia (“boy”), from Proto-West Germanic *bōjō, from Proto-Germanic *bōjô (“younger brother, young male relation”), from Proto-Germanic *bō- (“brother, close male relation”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰā-, *bʰāt- (“father, elder brother, brother”).

examples.text: The boy didn't change his opinion.

translations.de: Der Junge änderte seine Meinung nicht.
translations.fr: Le garçon ne changea pas d'avis.
translations.pt: O rapaz não mudou de opinião.

examples.text: She is very popular among the boys.

translations.de: Sie ist bei den Jungs sehr beliebt.
translations.fr: Elle a beaucoup de succès auprès des garçons.
translations.pt: Ela é muito popular entre os garotos.

examples.text: George seems to be a good boy.

translations.de: George scheint ein guter Junge zu sein.
translations.fr: George semble être un bon garçon.
translations.pt: George parece ser um bom garoto.

examples.text: She gave birth to a baby boy.

translations.de: Sie hat einen Jungen bekommen.
translations.fr: Elle donna naissance à un garçon.
translations.pt: Ela deu à luz um menino.

more.definition: A male child.; A young man.; A son of any age.
more.etymology: From Middle English boy /boye (“servant, commoner, knave, boy”), from Old English *bōia (“boy”), from Proto-West Germanic *bōjō, from Proto-Germanic *bōjô (“younger brother, young male relation”), from Proto-Germanic *bō- (“brother, close male relation”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰā-, *bʰāt- (“father, elder brother, brother”).

examples.text: The boy got lost in the forest.

translations.de: Der Junge verirrte sich im Wald.
translations.fr: Le garçon se perdit dans la forêt.
translations.pt: O menino se perdeu na floresta.

examples.text: All the boys are the same age.

translations.de: Alle Jungen sind gleich alt.
translations.fr: Tous les garçons sont du même âge.
translations.pt: Todos os meninos têm a mesma idade.

examples.text: The boy was afraid of the dark.

translations.de: Der Junge hatte Angst im Dunkeln.
translations.fr: Le garçon avait peur du noir.
translations.pt: O menino tinha medo da escuridão.

examples.text: The boy asked his mother a question.

translations.de: Der Sohn stellte seiner Mutter eine Frage.
translations.fr: Le fils posa une question à sa mère.
translations.pt: O filho fez uma pergunta à mãe.

more.definition: To act as a boy (in allusion to the former practice of boys acting women's parts on the stage).
more.etymology: From Middle English boy /boye (“servant, commoner, knave, boy”), from Old English *bōia (“boy”), from Proto-West Germanic *bōjō, from Proto-Germanic *bōjô (“younger brother, young male relation”), from Proto-Germanic *bō- (“brother, close male relation”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰā-, *bʰāt- (“father, elder brother, brother”).

examples.text: My father is getting better and better.

translations.de: Meinem Vater geht es immer besser.
translations.fr: Mon père va de mieux en mieux.
translations.pt: O meu pai está a ficar cada vez melhor.

examples.text: You're going to be a father.

translations.de: Du wirst ein Vater sein.
translations.fr: Vous allez être père.
translations.pt: Você vai ser pai.

examples.text: I'm going to be a father.

translations.de: Ich werde Vater.
translations.fr: Je vais devenir père.
translations.pt: Eu vou ser pai.

examples.text: I'm proud to be your father.

translations.de: Ich bin stolz, dein Vater zu sein.
translations.fr: Je suis fier d'être ton père.
translations.pt: Estou orgulhoso de ser seu pai.

more.definition: A male parent, especially of a human; a male who parents a child (which he has sired, adopted, fostered, etc.).; A male ancestor more remote than a parent; a progenitor; especially, a first ancestor.; A term of respectful address for an elderly man.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English fader, from Old English fæder, from Proto-West Germanic *fader, from Proto-Germanic *fadēr, from Proto-Indo-European *ph₂tḗr, possibly from *peh₂- + *-tḗr. Doublet of ayr, faeder, athair, padre, pater, and père.

examples.text: My wife's father has dark hair.

translations.de: Mein Schwiegervater hat dunkle Haare.
translations.fr: Mon beau-père a les cheveux noirs.
translations.pt: Meu sogro tem cabelo escuro.

examples.text: My father's sisters are my aunts.

translations.de: Die Schwestern meines Vaters sind meine Tanten.
translations.fr: Les sœurs de mon père sont mes tantes.
translations.pt: As irmãs de meu pai são minhas tias.

examples.text: He's the father of the bride.

translations.de: Er ist der Vater der Braut.
translations.fr: Il est le père de la mariée.
translations.pt: Ele é o pai da noiva.

examples.text: Do you want to become a father?

translations.de: Möchtest du Vater werden?
translations.fr: Voulez-vous devenir père ?
translations.pt: Você deseja vir a ser pai?

more.definition: To be a father to; to sire.; To give rise to.; To act as a father; to support and nurture.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English fader, from Old English fæder, from Proto-West Germanic *fader, from Proto-Germanic *fadēr, from Proto-Indo-European *ph₂tḗr, possibly from *peh₂- + *-tḗr. Doublet of ayr, faeder, athair, padre, pater, and père.

examples.text: Tom thought he was going to die.

translations.de: Tom glaubte, er müsse sterben.
translations.fr: Tom pensait qu'il allait mourir.
translations.pt: Tom pensou que ia morrer.

examples.text: I don't want him to die.

translations.de: Er soll nicht sterben.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas qu'il meure.
translations.pt: Eu não quero que ele morra.

examples.text: I thought I was going to die.

translations.de: Ich dachte, ich müsse sterben.
translations.fr: Je pensais que j'allais mourir.
translations.pt: Eu pensei que ia morrer.

examples.text: I know I'm going to die.

translations.de: Ich weiß, dass ich sterben werde.
translations.fr: Je sais que je vais mourir.
translations.pt: Eu sei que eu vou morrer.

more.definition: per day
more.etymology: Borrowed from Latin die (“[in a] day”), locative of Latin dies (“day”).

examples.text: It's a pity when somebody dies.

translations.de: Es ist schade, wenn jemand stirbt.
translations.fr: C'est dommage quand quelqu'un meurt.
translations.pt: É uma pena quando alguém morre.

examples.text: God doesn't play dice with the universe.

translations.de: Gott würfelt nicht mit dem Universum.
translations.fr: Dieu ne joue pas aux dés avec l'univers.
translations.pt: Deus não joga dados com o Universo.

examples.text: If the wind dies down, we'll go.

translations.de: Wir gehen, wenn sich der Wind gelegt hat.
translations.fr: Si le vent faiblit, nous irons.
translations.pt: Se o vento diminuir, nós iremos.

examples.text: The Guard dies, but it does not surrender!

translations.de: Die Garde stirbt, aber sie ergibt sich nicht.
translations.fr: La Garde meurt mais ne se rend pas !
translations.pt: A Guarda morre, mas não se rende!

more.definition: The cubical part of a pedestal; a plinth.; A device for cutting into a specified shape.; A device used to cut an external screw thread. (Internal screw threads are cut with a tap.)
more.etymology: From Middle English dee, from Old French de (Modern French dé), from Latin datum, from datus (“given”), the past participle of dō (“to give”), from Proto-Indo-European *deh₃- (“to lay out, to spread out”). Doublet of datum. Replaced Old English tasul, tesul (“die”), from Latin tessella (“die, cube”).

examples.text: Princess Diana died in a car crash.

translations.de: Prinzessin Diana kam bei einem Autounfall ums Leben.
translations.fr: La princesse Diana est décédée dans un accident de voiture.
translations.pt: A princesa Diana morreu em um acidente de carro.

examples.text: The addict died from a drug overdose.

translations.de: Der Drogenabhängige starb an einer Überdosis.
translations.fr: Le drogué est mort d'une surdose.
translations.pt: O viciado morreu de overdose.

examples.text: My father died before I was born.

translations.de: Mein Vater ist vor meiner Geburt gestorben.
translations.fr: Mon père est mort avant ma naissance.
translations.pt: Meu pai morreu antes de eu nascer.

examples.text: He died fighting in the Vietnam War.

translations.de: Er fiel im Vietnamkrieg.
translations.fr: Il est mort au combat pendant la guerre du Vietnam.
translations.pt: Ele morreu lutando durante a Guerra do Vietnã.

more.definition: To stop living; to become dead; to undergo death.; followed by of as an indication of direct cause; general use; followed by from as an indication of direct cause; general use, though somewhat more common in the context of medicine or the sciences
more.etymology: From Middle English deyen, probably from Old Norse deyja, from Proto-Germanic *dawjaną (“to die”). Displaced native Old English sweltan, whence Modern English swelt, and Old English steorfan, whence modern starve.

examples.text: I think you should listen to me.

translations.de: Ich finde, du solltest mir zuhören.
translations.fr: Je pense que tu devrais m'écouter.
translations.pt: Eu acho que você deveria me ouvir.

examples.text: He never listens to me. Why?

translations.de: Er hört mir nie zu. Warum?
translations.fr: Il ne m'écoute jamais. Pourquoi ?
translations.pt: Ele nunca me dá ouvidos. Por quê?

examples.text: He doesn't listen to his teachers.

translations.de: Er hört nicht auf seine Lehrer.
translations.fr: Il n'écoute pas ses professeurs.
translations.pt: Ele não escuta os seus professores.

examples.text: I want you to listen to me.

translations.de: Ich möchte, dass du mir zuhörst.
translations.fr: Je veux que vous m'écoutiez.
translations.pt: Eu quero que você me escute.

more.definition: An instance of listening.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *ḱlew-der. From Middle English listenen, listnen, alteration (due to Middle English listen (“to listen, give heed to”)) of Old English hlysnan (“to listen”), from Proto-Germanic *hlusnijaną, *hlusnōną (compare Middle High German lüsenen), from Proto-Germanic *hlusēną (compare Old High German hlosēn), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱlew- (“to hear”). Cognate with Swedish lyssna (“to listen”).

examples.text: I relax while listening to classical music.

translations.de: Ich entspanne mich, während ich klassische Musik höre.
translations.fr: Je me détends en écoutant de la musique classique.
translations.pt: Eu relaxo a escutar música clássica.

examples.text: We have to pay attention and listen.

translations.de: Wir müssen aufpassen und zuhören.
translations.fr: Nous devons être attentifs et écouter.
translations.pt: Nós temos que prestar atenção e escutar.

examples.text: I hope that she listens to me.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, sie hört auf mich.
translations.fr: J'espère qu'elle m'écoute.
translations.pt: Espero que ela me escute.

examples.text: I listened to some CDs last night.

translations.de: Ich habe gestern Abend ein paar CDs gehört.
translations.fr: J'ai écouté quelques CD la nuit dernière.
translations.pt: Ontem à noite escutei vários CDs.

more.definition: To use one's sense of hearing and auditory cognition in an intentional way; to make deliberate use of one's ears; to pay attention to or wait for a specific sound.; To accept advice or obey instruction; to agree or assent.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *ḱlew-der. From Middle English listenen, listnen, alteration (due to Middle English listen (“to listen, give heed to”)) of Old English hlysnan (“to listen”), from Proto-Germanic *hlusnijaną, *hlusnōną (compare Middle High German lüsenen), from Proto-Germanic *hlusēną (compare Old High German hlosēn), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱlew- (“to hear”). Cognate with Swedish lyssna (“to listen”).

examples.text: Most people nowadays don't understand friendship.

translations.de: Die meisten wissen heute gar nicht mehr, was Freundschaft ist.
translations.fr: La plupart des gens de nos jours ne comprennent pas l'amitié.
translations.pt: A maioria das pessoas de hoje em dia não entende amizade.

examples.text: I pretended that I didn't understand.

translations.de: Ich tat, als würde ich es nicht verstehen.
translations.fr: J'ai prétendu ne pas comprendre.
translations.pt: Eu fingi que não entendi.

examples.text: I think Tom didn't understand you.

translations.de: Ich denke, Tom hat dich nicht verstanden.
translations.fr: Je pense que Tom ne t'a pas compris.
translations.pt: Eu acho que o Tom não te entendeu.

examples.text: Tom didn't understand Mary's joke.

translations.de: Tom verstand Marys Witz nicht.
translations.fr: Tom n'a pas compris la plaisanterie de Marie.
translations.pt: Tom não entendeu a piada de Mary.

more.definition: Uh-huh, I see; a way to acknowledge something said by the other speaker.
more.etymology: From Middle English understanden, from Old English understandan (“to understand”), from Proto-West Germanic *understandan (“to stand between, understand”), from Proto-Germanic *understandaną (“to stand between, understand”), equivalent to Old English under- (“between, inter-”) + standan (“to stand”) (Modern English under- + stand).

examples.text: Does he understand what he's saying?

translations.de: Begreift er, was er da sagt?
translations.fr: Comprend-il ce qu'il dit ?
translations.pt: Ele entende o que está dizendo?

examples.text: Only a few understood what he said.

translations.de: Nur ein paar wenige verstanden, was er sagte.
translations.fr: Quelques personnes seulement comprirent ce qu'il disait.
translations.pt: Poucos entenderam o que ele disse.

examples.text: They translate the text without understanding its meaning.

translations.de: Sie übersetzen den Text, ohne seine Bedeutung zu verstehen.
translations.fr: Ils traduisent le texte sans en comprendre le sens.
translations.pt: Eles traduzem o texto sem lhe entender o significado.

examples.text: When I speak German, only Tom understands me.

translations.de: Wenn ich Deutsch spreche, versteht mich nur Tom.
translations.fr: Quand je parle allemand, seul Tom me comprend.
translations.pt: Quando falo Alemão, só o Tom me entende.

more.definition: To know the meaning of; to parse or have parsed correctly; to comprehend.; To know the meaning of.; To be thoroughly familiar with; to be able to undertake properly.
more.etymology: From Middle English understanden, from Old English understandan (“to understand”), from Proto-West Germanic *understandan (“to stand between, understand”), from Proto-Germanic *understandaną (“to stand between, understand”), equivalent to Old English under- (“between, inter-”) + standan (“to stand”) (Modern English under- + stand).

examples.text: I don't know which one to choose.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, welche ich nehmen soll.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas laquelle choisir.
translations.pt: Eu não sei qual escolher.

examples.text: Tom doesn't know which color to choose.

translations.de: Tom weiß nicht, welche Farbe zu wählen ist.
translations.fr: Tom ne sait pas quelle couleur choisir.
translations.pt: Tom não sabe qual cor escolher.

examples.text: This is a doll which she made herself.

translations.de: Das ist eine Puppe, die sie selbst gemacht hat.
translations.fr: C'est une poupée qu'elle a fabriquée elle-même.
translations.pt: Esta é uma boneca que ela mesma fez.

examples.text: Do you know which book sells well now?

translations.de: Weißt du, welches Buch sich zurzeit gut verkauft?
translations.fr: Sais-tu quel livre se vend bien en ce moment ?
translations.pt: Você sabe que livro vende bem atualmente?

more.etymology: From Middle English which, hwic, wilche, hwilch, whilk, hwilc, from Old English hwelċ (“which”), from Proto-Germanic *hwilīkaz (“what kind”, literally “like what”), derived from *hwaz.

examples.text: That which is easily acquired is easily lost.

translations.de: Wie gewonnen, so zerronnen.
translations.fr: Ce qui est facilement gagné est facilement perdu.
translations.pt: O que facilmente se ganha, facilmente se perde.

examples.text: In which folder did you save the file?

translations.de: In welchen Ordner hast du die Datei gespeichert?
translations.fr: Dans quel dossier as-tu enregistré le fichier ?
translations.pt: Em qual pasta você salvou o arquivo?

examples.text: Let each one practice the branch which he knows.

translations.de: Jeder soll den Zweig praktizieren, den er kennt.
translations.fr: Que chacun pratique la branche qu'il connaît.
translations.pt: Que cada um pratique o ramo que conhece.

examples.text: Do other planets exist, on which life can exist?

translations.de: Existieren andere Planeten, auf denen Leben existieren kann?
translations.fr: Existe-t-il d'autres planètes sur lesquelles la vie puisse exister ?
translations.pt: Existem outros planetas nos quais possa existir vida?

more.definition: What, of those mentioned or implied.; The/Any ... that; whichever.; Designates the one(s) previously mentioned.
more.etymology: From Middle English which, hwic, wilche, hwilch, whilk, hwilc, from Old English hwelċ (“which”), from Proto-Germanic *hwilīkaz (“what kind”, literally “like what”), derived from *hwaz.

examples.text: This is the letter which I wrote.

translations.de: Das ist der Brief, den ich geschrieben habe.
translations.fr: C'est la lettre que j'ai écrite.
translations.pt: Esta é a carta que escrevi.

examples.text: I don't know which to choose.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, welche ich nehmen soll.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas lequel choisir.
translations.pt: Eu não sei qual escolher.

examples.text: All that which is invented, is true.

translations.de: Alles Erfundene ist wahr.
translations.fr: Tout ce qui est inventé est vrai.
translations.pt: Tudo que já foi inventado é verdadeiro.

examples.text: Tom didn't know which bus to take.

translations.de: Tom wusste nicht, welchen Bus er nehmen sollte.
translations.fr: Tom ne savait pas quel bus prendre.
translations.pt: O Tom não sabia qual ônibus tomar.

more.definition: What one or ones (of those mentioned or implied).; The/Any ones that; whichever.; Referring to a preceding noun.
more.etymology: From Middle English which, hwic, wilche, hwilch, whilk, hwilc, from Old English hwelċ (“which”), from Proto-Germanic *hwilīkaz (“what kind”, literally “like what”), derived from *hwaz.

examples.text: He promised not to be late again.

translations.de: Er versprach, nicht wieder zu spät zu sein.
translations.fr: Il a promis de ne pas être encore en retard.
translations.pt: Ele prometeu não se atrasar de novo.

examples.text: He will regret it sooner or later.

translations.de: Früher oder später wird er es bereuen.
translations.fr: Il le regrettera tôt ou tard.
translations.pt: Ele vai se arrepender mais cedo ou mais tarde.

examples.text: The train is ten minutes late today.

translations.de: Der Zug hat heute 10 Minuten Verspätung.
translations.fr: Le train est aujourd'hui dix minutes en retard.
translations.pt: O trem está com dez minutos de atraso hoje.

examples.text: Don't be late to school again.

translations.de: Sei nicht wieder zu spät zur Schule.
translations.fr: Ne sois pas en retard à l'école à nouveau.
translations.pt: Não se atrase de novo para a escola.

more.definition: Near the end of a period of time.; Specifically, near the end of the day.; Associated with the end of a period.
more.etymology: From Middle English late, lat, from Old English læt (“slow; slack, lax, negligent; late”), from Proto-West Germanic *lat, from Proto-Germanic *lataz (“slow, lazy”). By surface analysis, deverbal from let.

examples.text: A few minutes later, the telephone rang.

translations.de: Einige Minuten später klingelte das Telefon.
translations.fr: Quelques minutes plus tard, le téléphone sonna.
translations.pt: Poucos minutos depois, o telefone tocou.

examples.text: I might be a few minutes late.

translations.de: Ich komme vielleicht ein paar Minuten später.
translations.fr: Je pourrai avoir quelques minutes de retard.
translations.pt: Talvez eu chegue um pouco atrasado.

examples.text: It's never too late to learn.

translations.de: Es ist nie zu spät zum Lernen.
translations.fr: Tu n'es pas trop vieux pour apprendre.
translations.pt: Nunca é tarde demais para aprender.

examples.text: It's too late to apologize now.

translations.de: Es ist zu spät, um sich jetzt noch zu entschuldigen.
translations.fr: Il est trop tard pour t'excuser maintenant.
translations.pt: Já é muito tarde para pedir desculpas.

more.definition: After a deadline has passed, past a designated time.; Formerly, especially in the context of service in a military unit.; Not long ago; just now, recently.
more.etymology: From Middle English late, lat, from Old English læt (“slow; slack, lax, negligent; late”), from Proto-West Germanic *lat, from Proto-Germanic *lataz (“slow, lazy”). By surface analysis, deverbal from let.

examples.text: I hope it's not too late.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, es ist noch nicht zu spät.
translations.fr: J'espère qu'il n'est pas trop tard.
translations.pt: Tomara que não seja tarde demais.

examples.text: You don't want to be late.

translations.de: Du kannst dir nicht erlauben, zu spät zu kommen.
translations.fr: Vous ne voulez pas être en retard.
translations.pt: Não queiram se atrasar.

examples.text: I hope I'm not too late.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, ich bin nicht zu spät.
translations.fr: J'espère ne pas être trop en retard.
translations.pt: Espero não estar demasiado atrasado.

examples.text: I hope we're not too late.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, wir sind nicht zu spät.
translations.fr: J'espère que nous ne sommes pas trop en retard.
translations.pt: Espero que não estejamos atrasados demais.

more.definition: A shift (scheduled work period) that takes place late in the day or at night.
more.etymology: From Middle English late, lat, from Old English læt (“slow; slack, lax, negligent; late”), from Proto-West Germanic *lat, from Proto-Germanic *lataz (“slow, lazy”). By surface analysis, deverbal from let.

examples.text: She's got a nice ass.

translations.de: Sie hat einen hübschen Arsch.
translations.fr: Elle a un joli cul.
translations.pt: Ela tem um belo cu.

examples.text: Some people are nicer than others.

translations.de: Manche Leute sind netter als andere.
translations.fr: Certaines personnes sont plus gentilles que d'autres.
translations.pt: Algumas pessoas são mais agradáveis do que outras.

examples.text: The weather is getting nice again.

translations.de: Das Wetter wird wieder schön.
translations.fr: Le temps se remet au beau.
translations.pt: O tempo está ficando bom de novo.

examples.text: My neighbors are very nice people.

translations.de: Meine Nachbarn sind sehr nette Leute.
translations.fr: Mes voisins sont des gens très gentils.
translations.pt: Meus vizinhos são pessoas muito agradáveis.

more.definition: Pleasant, satisfactory, complimentary.; Of a person: friendly, attractive.; Respectable; virtuous.
more.etymology: From Middle English nyce, nice, nys, from Old French nice, niche, nisce (“simple, foolish, ignorant”), from Latin nescius (“ignorant, not knowing”); compare nesciō (“to know not, be ignorant of”), from ne (“not”) + sciō (“to know”).

examples.text: In my opinion, the weather is nice.

translations.de: Meiner Meinung nach ist das Wetter schön.
translations.fr: À mon avis, le temps est agréable.
translations.pt: Na minha opinião, o tempo está bom.

examples.text: I wish people were nicer to each other.

translations.de: Ich wünschte, die Menschen wären netter zueinander.
translations.fr: J'aimerais que les gens soient plus gentils les uns avec les autres.
translations.pt: Gostaria que as pessoas fossem mais gentis umas com as outras.

examples.text: I think Tom is a nice name.

translations.de: Tom ist, finde ich, ein schöner Name.
translations.fr: Je pense que Tom est un joli nom.
translations.pt: Acho que Tom é um nome legal.

examples.text: I discovered a very nice place today.

translations.de: Ich habe heute einen sehr schönen Ort entdeckt.
translations.fr: J'ai découvert un endroit tout à fait charmant aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Conheci um lugar muito bonito hoje.

more.definition: Nicely.
more.etymology: From Middle English nyce, nice, nys, from Old French nice, niche, nisce (“simple, foolish, ignorant”), from Latin nescius (“ignorant, not knowing”); compare nesciō (“to know not, be ignorant of”), from ne (“not”) + sciō (“to know”).

examples.text: How long will this nice weather last?

translations.de: Wie lange wird dieses schöne Wetter anhalten?
translations.fr: Combien de temps va durer ce beau temps ?
translations.pt: Até quando vai durar esse bom tempo?

examples.text: How nice to see you again, Tom.

translations.de: Wie schön, dich wiederzusehen, Tom!
translations.fr: C'est super de te revoir, Tom !
translations.pt: Como é bom vê-lo novamente, Tom.

examples.text: The Greek doctor was very nice.

translations.de: Der griechische Arzt war sehr nett.
translations.fr: Le médecin grec était très gentil.
translations.pt: O médico grego foi muito atencioso.

examples.text: I feel nice doing something good.

translations.de: Ich fühle mich gut dabei, etwas Gutes zu tun.
translations.fr: Je me sens bien en faisant quelque chose de bien.
translations.pt: Sinto-me bem fazendo algo de bom.

more.definition: Used to signify a job well done.; Used to signify approval.
more.etymology: From Middle English nyce, nice, nys, from Old French nice, niche, nisce (“simple, foolish, ignorant”), from Latin nescius (“ignorant, not knowing”); compare nesciō (“to know not, be ignorant of”), from ne (“not”) + sciō (“to know”).

examples.text: Tom's a nice guy. Everyone likes him.

translations.de: Tom ist ein netter Typ. Jeder hat ihn gern.
translations.fr: Tom est un mec sympa. Tout le monde l'aime.
translations.pt: Tom é um cara bacana. Todo mundo gosta dele.

examples.text: She's a really nice person.

translations.de: Sie ist wirklich eine sympathische Person.
translations.fr: C'est vraiment une chic fille.
translations.pt: Ela é realmente uma pessoa legal.

examples.text: It's nice of you to help me.

translations.de: Es ist nett, daß du mir hilfst!
translations.fr: C'est gentil de ta part de m'aider.
translations.pt: É gentil da sua parte me ajudar.

examples.text: Thank you for this nice present.

translations.de: Ich danke dir für das schöne Geschenk.
translations.fr: Merci pour ce beau cadeau.
translations.pt: Obrigado por esse belo presente.

more.definition: niceness.
more.etymology: From Middle English nyce, nice, nys, from Old French nice, niche, nisce (“simple, foolish, ignorant”), from Latin nescius (“ignorant, not knowing”); compare nesciō (“to know not, be ignorant of”), from ne (“not”) + sciō (“to know”).

examples.text: You look nice with your hair short.

translations.de: Du siehst gut aus mit kurzen Haaren.
translations.fr: Les cheveux courts vous vont bien.
translations.pt: Você fica bem de cabelo curto.

examples.text: I bought her a nice Christmas present.

translations.de: Ich kaufte ihr ein schönes Weihnachtsgeschenk.
translations.fr: Je lui ai acheté un beau cadeau de Noël.
translations.pt: Comprei-lhe um belo presente de Natal.

examples.text: It was very nice seeing you again.

translations.de: Es war nett, dich wiederzusehen.
translations.fr: C'était un plaisir de vous revoir.
translations.pt: Foi muito bom te ver de novo.

examples.text: This coat is nice, but too expensive.

translations.de: Dieser Mantel ist schön, aber zu teuer.
translations.fr: Ce manteau est beau, mais trop cher.
translations.pt: Esse casaco é bonito, mas muito caro.

more.definition: To run a process with a specified (usually lower) priority.
more.etymology: Name of a Unix program used to invoke a script or program with a specified priority, with the implication that running at a lower priority is "nice" (kind, etc.) because it leaves more resources for others.

examples.text: That's just fine with me.

translations.de: Das ist für mich in Ordnung.
translations.fr: Ça me convient parfaitement.
translations.pt: Por mim tudo bem.

examples.text: I'm fine. How about you?

translations.de: Mir geht’s gut. Und dir?
translations.fr: Je vais bien, et vous ?
translations.pt: Estou bem, e você?

examples.text: Everything will be fine now.

translations.de: Jetzt wird alles gut.
translations.fr: Tout ira bien maintenant.
translations.pt: Tudo vai ficar bem agora.

examples.text: I said I'm fine.

translations.de: Ich sagte, es geht mir gut.
translations.fr: J'ai dit que j'allais bien.
translations.pt: Eu disse que estou bem.

more.definition: Of superior quality.; Impressively bad, inappropriate, or unsatisfactory.; Being acceptable, adequate, passable, or satisfactory; having one's well-being be no cause for concern.
more.etymology: From Middle English fin, fyn, from Old French fin (“fine, minute, exact”), of obscure origin, but probably derived from Latin fīnīre (“to finish”) or fīnis (“boundary, limit, end”), with an abstract sense of fine or thin also arising in many Romance languages (compare Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish fino). Doublet of fino.

examples.text: We're going to be fine.

translations.de: Uns geht es gut.
translations.fr: Tout va bien se passer.
translations.pt: Nós vamos ficar bem.

examples.text: I'm fine, thanks for asking.

translations.de: Es geht mir gut. Danke der Nachfrage!
translations.fr: Je vais bien, merci de me le demander !
translations.pt: Estou bem, obrigado por perguntar.

examples.text: It's a fine day today.

translations.de: Heute ist ein schöner Tag.
translations.fr: Aujourd'hui est un beau jour.
translations.pt: Hoje está um belo dia.

examples.text: Everything's going to be fine.

translations.de: Es wird alles gut werden.
translations.fr: Tout va bien se passer.
translations.pt: Vai ficar tudo bem.

more.definition: Well, nicely, in a positive, agreeable way.; In a manner so that the driven ball strikes the object ball so far to one side as to be barely deflected, the object ball being driven to one side.
more.etymology: From Middle English fin, fyn, from Old French fin (“fine, minute, exact”), of obscure origin, but probably derived from Latin fīnīre (“to finish”) or fīnis (“boundary, limit, end”), with an abstract sense of fine or thin also arising in many Romance languages (compare Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish fino). Doublet of fino.

examples.text: Don't worry. Everything'll be fine.

translations.de: Mach dir keine Sorgen! Es wird alles gut gehen.
translations.fr: Ne t'en fais pas ! Tout ira bien.
translations.pt: Não se preocupe. Tudo ficará bem.

examples.text: Where is the Palace of Fine Arts?

translations.de: Wo ist der „Palast der schönen Künste“?
translations.fr: Où est le Palais des Beaux-Arts ?
translations.pt: Onde fica o Palácio de Belas Artes?

examples.text: I hope it'll be fine tomorrow.

translations.de: Hoffentlich wird es morgen heiter.
translations.fr: J'espère que ça ira demain.
translations.pt: Eu espero que esteja melhor amanhã.

examples.text: Everything is fine. Don't worry.

translations.de: Alles ist in Ordnung. Mach dir keine Sorgen.
translations.fr: Tout va bien. Ne t'en fais pas.
translations.pt: Está tudo bem. Não se preocupe.

more.definition: Expression of (typically) reluctant agreement.; Expression of (typically) reluctant acceptance, without further argument or discussion, of another person's viewpoint.
more.etymology: From Middle English fin, fyn, from Old French fin (“fine, minute, exact”), of obscure origin, but probably derived from Latin fīnīre (“to finish”) or fīnis (“boundary, limit, end”), with an abstract sense of fine or thin also arising in many Romance languages (compare Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish fino). Doublet of fino.

examples.text: I'm fine with it.

translations.de: Ich bin damit einverstanden.
translations.fr: Ça colle pour moi.
translations.pt: Estou bem com isso.

examples.text: I've paid parking fines a number of times myself.

translations.de: Ich habe selbst schon mehrmals Bußgelder für widerrechtliches Parken bezahlt.
translations.fr: J'ai moi-même payé des tas de fois des amendes pour stationnement interdit.
translations.pt: Eu mesmo já paguei multas por estacionamento proibido algumas vezes.

examples.text: There's a fine line between genius and insanity.

translations.de: Genie und Wahnsinn liegen dicht beieinander.
translations.fr: La frontière qui sépare le génie de la folie est ténue.
translations.pt: Existe uma fina linha entre genialidade e insanidade.

examples.text: I'm fine, thank you!

translations.de: Mir geht's gut, danke!
translations.fr: Je vais bien, merci.
translations.pt: Eu estou bem, obrigado.

more.definition: Fine champagne; French brandy.; Something that is fine; fine particles.; A fee levied as punishment for breaking the law.
more.etymology: From Middle English fin, fyn, from Old French fin (“fine, minute, exact”), of obscure origin, but probably derived from Latin fīnīre (“to finish”) or fīnis (“boundary, limit, end”), with an abstract sense of fine or thin also arising in many Romance languages (compare Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish fino). Doublet of fino.

examples.text: I am fine, thank you.

translations.de: Mir geht’s gut. Danke!
translations.fr: Je vais bien, merci.
translations.pt: Eu vou bem, obrigado.

examples.text: My family is fine, thanks.

translations.de: Meiner Familie geht es gut, danke.
translations.fr: Ma famille va bien, merci.
translations.pt: Minha família vai bem, obrigado.

examples.text: Perhaps the weather is fine.

translations.de: Vielleicht ist das Wetter schön.
translations.fr: Peut-être que le temps est au poil.
translations.pt: Talvez o tempo esteja bom.

examples.text: I'm fine, thank you.

translations.de: Es geht mir gut, danke.
translations.fr: Je vais bien, merci.
translations.pt: Eu estou bem, obrigado.

more.definition: To make finer, purer, or cleaner; to purify or clarify.; To become finer, purer, or cleaner.; To make finer, or less coarse, as in bulk, texture, etc.
more.etymology: From Middle English fin, fyn, from Old French fin (“fine, minute, exact”), of obscure origin, but probably derived from Latin fīnīre (“to finish”) or fīnis (“boundary, limit, end”), with an abstract sense of fine or thin also arising in many Romance languages (compare Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish fino). Doublet of fino.

examples.text: What kind of car does he drive?

translations.de: Was für einen Wagen fährt er?
translations.fr: Quel genre de voiture conduit-il ?
translations.pt: Que tipo de carro ele dirige?

examples.text: That kind of story appeals to me.

translations.de: Solche Geschichten gefallen mir.
translations.fr: Ce genre d'histoire me plaît.
translations.pt: Esse tipo de estória me interessa.

examples.text: I'll do any kind of work.

translations.de: Ich werde jede Art von Arbeit machen.
translations.fr: Je suis prêt à faire n'importe quel type de travail.
translations.pt: Eu farei qualquer tipo de trabalho.

examples.text: He's always been kind to me.

translations.de: Er war immer freundlich zu mir.
translations.fr: Il a toujours été bon avec moi.
translations.pt: Ele sempre foi gentil comigo.

more.definition: Having a benevolent, courteous, friendly, generous, gentle, liberal, sympathetic, or warm-hearted nature or disposition, marked by consideration for – and service to – others.; Affectionate.; Favorable.
more.etymology: From Middle English kynde, kinde, from Old English cynde, ġecynde (“innate, natural, native”), from Old English cynd, ġecynd (“nature, kind”).

examples.text: What kind of game are you playing?

translations.de: Was für ein Spiel spielst du?
translations.fr: À quelle sorte de jeu jouez-vous ?
translations.pt: Que espécie de jogo você está jogando?

examples.text: Those kinds of things don't happen here.

translations.de: So was gibt’s hier nicht.
translations.fr: Ce genre de choses n'arrive pas ici.
translations.pt: Esse tipo de coisa não acontece aqui.

examples.text: This is a new kind of melon.

translations.de: Das ist eine neue Melonenart.
translations.fr: C'est une nouvelle espèce de melon.
translations.pt: Este é um novo tipo de melão.

examples.text: Why are you being so kind to me?

translations.de: Warum bist du so lieb zu mir?
translations.fr: Pourquoi êtes-vous si gentil avec moi ?
translations.pt: Por que é que estás sendo tão boa comigo?

more.definition: A type, race or category; a group of entities that have common characteristics such that they may be grouped together.; A makeshift or otherwise atypical specimen.; Goods or services used as payment, as e.g. in barter.
more.etymology: From Middle English kynde, kinde, from Old English cynd, ġecynd (“inherent nature, disposition, kind, gender, generation, race”), from Proto-West Germanic *kundi, from Proto-Germanic *kinþiz, related to Proto-Germanic *kunją (“race, kin”) and Old English cennan (“to bear, give birth”). Cognate with Old High German gikunt (“nature, kind”), Icelandic kind (“race, species, kind”). Doublet of gens, genesis, and jati.

examples.text: I built a shed behind my house.

translations.de: Ich stellte einen Schuppen hinter meinem Haus auf.
translations.fr: J'ai construit un abri de jardin derrière ma maison.
translations.pt: Construí um galpão atrás de casa.

examples.text: There are several churches near my house.

translations.de: Es gibt mehrere Kirchen bei mir in der Nähe.
translations.fr: Il y a plusieurs églises près de chez moi.
translations.pt: Há várias igrejas perto da minha casa.

examples.text: Tom's house was almost completely destroyed.

translations.de: Toms Haus war beinah vollständig zerstört.
translations.fr: La maison de Tom a presque été entièrement détruite.
translations.pt: A casa do Tom foi quase completamente destruída.

examples.text: I want to build my own house.

translations.de: Ich möchte mein eigenes Haus bauen.
translations.fr: Je veux construire ma propre maison.
translations.pt: Eu quero construir minha própria casa.

examples.text: The house has a big yard.

translations.de: Das Haus hat einen großen Garten.
translations.fr: La maison a un grand jardin.
translations.pt: A casa tem um jardim grande.

examples.text: There are many old houses on this street.

translations.de: In dieser Straße stehen viele alte Häuser.
translations.fr: Il y a beaucoup de vieilles maisons dans cette rue.
translations.pt: Há muitas casas antigas nesta rua.

more.definition: A structure built or serving as an abode of human beings.; An apartment building within a public housing estate.; A container; a thing which houses another.
collocations: on the house — free, paid by the owner
more.etymology: From Middle English hous, hus, from Old English hūs (“dwelling, shelter, house”), from Proto-West Germanic *hūs, from Proto-Germanic *hūsą (“house”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kews-, from *(s)kewH- (“to cover, hide”). More at hose. Eclipsed non-native Middle English mees, meson, measoun (“house”), borrowed from Anglo-Norman mes, mies, meis, maisun (“house”).

examples.text: Tom has a house near the beach.

translations.de: Tom hat ein Haus in Strandnähe.
translations.fr: Tom a une maison près de la plage.
translations.pt: O Tom tem uma casa perto da praia.

examples.text: The zombies had totally surrounded the house.

translations.de: Die Zombies hatten das Haus vollständig umzingelt.
translations.fr: Les zombies avaient complètement encerclé la maison.
translations.pt: Os zumbis tinham cercado totalmente a casa.

examples.text: There is a pharmacy near my house.

translations.de: In der Nähe meines Hauses gibt es eine Apotheke.
translations.fr: Il y a une pharmacie près de chez moi.
translations.pt: Há uma farmácia perto da minha casa.

examples.text: We have a house in the countryside.

translations.de: Wir haben ein Haus auf dem Lande.
translations.fr: Nous avons une maison à la campagne.
translations.pt: Nós temos uma casa no campo.

more.definition: To keep within a structure or container.; To admit to residence; to harbor.; To take shelter or lodging; to abide; to lodge.
more.etymology: From Middle English housen, from Old English hūsian, from Proto-Germanic *hūsōną (“to house, live, dwell”), from the noun (see above). Compare Dutch huizen (“to live, dwell, reside”), German Low German husen (“to live, dwell, reside”), German hausen (“to live, dwell, reside”), Norwegian Nynorsk husa (“to house”), Faroese húsa (“to house”), Icelandic húsa (“to shelter, house”).

examples.text: I wanted to say hello to Tom.

translations.de: Ich wollte Tom guten Tag sagen.
translations.fr: Je voulais dire bonjour à Tom.
translations.pt: Eu queria dizer oi para o Tom.

examples.text: Say hello to your parents from me.

translations.de: Grüße deine Eltern von mir.
translations.fr: Saluez vos parents de ma part.
translations.pt: Mande um oi aos seus pais por mim.

examples.text: Please say hello to him for me.

translations.de: Grüßen Sie ihn bitte von mir.
translations.fr: Dis-lui bonjour de ma part s'il te plaît.
translations.pt: Por favor, diga olá a ele por mim.

examples.text: She doesn't say hello to her neighbours.

translations.de: Sie grüßt ihre Nachbarn nicht.
translations.fr: Elle ne salue pas ses voisins.
translations.pt: Ela não cumprimenta os vizinhos.

more.definition: A greeting (salutation) said when meeting someone or acknowledging someone’s arrival or presence.; A greeting used when answering the telephone.; A call for response if it is not clear if anyone is present or listening, or if a telephone conversation may have been disconnected.
more.etymology: First attested in 1826. From holla, hollo (attested 1588). This variant of hallo is often credited to Thomas Edison as a coinage for telephone use, but its appearance in print predates the invention of the telephone by several decades. Ultimately from a variant of Old English ēalā, such as hēlā, which was used colloquially at the time similarly to how hey and (in some dialects) hi are used nowadays.

examples.text: Say hello to your mum for me.

translations.de: Grüß deine Mama von mir.
translations.fr: Dis bonjour à ta maman de ma part.
translations.pt: Mande um alô para a sua mãe por mim.

examples.text: Please say hello to your family.

translations.de: Bitte grüße deine Familie.
translations.fr: Dis bonjour à ta famille, s'il te plaît.
translations.pt: Por favor, diga olá para sua família.

examples.text: Tom wants to say hello.

translations.de: Tom möchte Hallo sagen.
translations.fr: Tom a envie de dire bonjour.
translations.pt: Tom quer dizer oi.

examples.text: Hello, I'm Tomoko Sato from Japan.

translations.de: Hallo, ich bin Tomoko Sato aus Japan.
translations.fr: Bonjour, je suis Tomoko Sato, je viens du Japon.
translations.pt: Oi, eu sou Tomoko Sato, do Japão.

more.definition: "Hello!" or an equivalent greeting.
more.etymology: First attested in 1826. From holla, hollo (attested 1588). This variant of hallo is often credited to Thomas Edison as a coinage for telephone use, but its appearance in print predates the invention of the telephone by several decades. Ultimately from a variant of Old English ēalā, such as hēlā, which was used colloquially at the time similarly to how hey and (in some dialects) hi are used nowadays.

examples.text: Please say hello to your wife.

translations.de: Grüßen Sie Ihre Frau!
translations.fr: Dis bonjour à ta femme, s'il te plaît.
translations.pt: Por favor, dê um alô à sua mulher.

examples.text: Say hello to your friends.

translations.de: Grüß deine Freunde von mir.
translations.fr: Dis bonjour à tes amis.
translations.pt: Diga oi para as suas amigas.

examples.text: Tom said hello.

translations.de: Tom sagte Hallo.
translations.fr: Tom dit bonjour.
translations.pt: Tom mandou lembranças.

examples.text: Hello! I'm a new user.

translations.de: Hallo! Ich bin ein neuer Benutzer.
translations.fr: Salut ! Je suis un nouvel utilisateur.
translations.pt: Olá, eu sou um usuário novo.

more.definition: To greet (someone) with "hello".
more.etymology: First attested in 1826. From holla, hollo (attested 1588). This variant of hallo is often credited to Thomas Edison as a coinage for telephone use, but its appearance in print predates the invention of the telephone by several decades. Ultimately from a variant of Old English ēalā, such as hēlā, which was used colloquially at the time similarly to how hey and (in some dialects) hi are used nowadays.

examples.text: Go tell those fibs to someone else.

translations.de: Erzähl diese Schwindeleien doch jemand anders.
translations.fr: Va raconter ces bobards à quelqu'un d'autre.
translations.pt: Vá contar essas mentiras a outro.

examples.text: I need someone who can speak French.

translations.de: Ich brauche jemanden, der Französisch sprechen kann.
translations.fr: J'ai besoin de quelqu'un qui parle français.
translations.pt: Eu preciso de alguém que saiba falar francês.

examples.text: There's someone hiding in the closet.

translations.de: Jemand hält sich im Schrank versteckt.
translations.fr: Quelqu'un se cache dans le placard.
translations.pt: Tem alguém se escondendo no armário.

examples.text: I know someone who lives in Boston.

translations.de: Ich kenne jemanden, der in Boston wohnt.
translations.fr: Je connais quelqu'un qui habite à Boston.
translations.pt: Eu conheço alguém que mora em Boston.

more.definition: A partially specified but unnamed person.; An important person.
more.etymology: From Middle English sum on, sum one, sum oon, equivalent to some + one.

examples.text: Do you want to talk to someone?

translations.de: Willst du mit jemandem reden?
translations.fr: Est-ce que tu veux parler à quelqu'un ?
translations.pt: Quer falar com alguém?

examples.text: You can't make someone like you.

translations.de: Man kann niemanden dazu zwingen, einen zu mögen.
translations.fr: Tu ne peux pas forcer quelqu'un à t'aimer.
translations.pt: Você não pode obrigar alguém a gostar de você.

examples.text: She mixed him up with someone else.

translations.de: Sie verwechselte ihn mit jemand anderem.
translations.fr: Elle le prit pour quelqu'un d'autre.
translations.pt: Ela confundiu ele com outra pessoa.

examples.text: These red apples belong to someone.

translations.de: Diese roten Äpfel gehören jemandem.
translations.fr: Ces pommes rouges appartiennent à quelqu'un.
translations.pt: Estas maçãs vermelhas são de alguém.

more.definition: One or some person of unspecified or indefinite identity.
more.etymology: From Middle English sum on, sum one, sum oon, equivalent to some + one.

examples.text: Mary wiped her hands on her apron.

translations.de: Maria wischte sich die Hände an ihrer Schürze ab.
translations.fr: Mary s'est essuyée les mains sur son tablier.
translations.pt: Mary limpou as mãos no avental.

examples.text: I really want to hold your hand.

translations.de: Ich hielte sehr gerne deine Hand.
translations.fr: Je veux vraiment te tenir la main.
translations.pt: Eu quero mesmo segurar a sua mão.

examples.text: Don't forget to wash your hands.

translations.de: Vergiss nicht, dir die Hände zu waschen!
translations.fr: N'oublie pas de te laver les mains.
translations.pt: Não esqueça de lavar as mãos.

examples.text: She had a flower in her hand.

translations.de: Sie hielt eine Blume in der Hand.
translations.fr: Elle avait une fleur dans la main.
translations.pt: Ela segurava na mão uma flor.

more.definition: The part of the forelimb below the forearm or wrist in humans and other primates, and the corresponding part in many other animals.; A limb of certain animals, such as the foot of a hawk, or any one of the four extremities of a monkey.; An index or pointer on a dial; such as the hour and minute hands on the face of an analog clock, which are used to indicate the time of day.
more.etymology: From Middle English hond, hand, from Old English hand, from Proto-West Germanic *handu, from Proto-Germanic *handuz. See also Dutch and Swedish hand (“hand”), Danish hånd, German Hand, West Frisian hân.

examples.text: Tom handed Mary a bottle of water.

translations.de: Tom reichte Maria eine Flasche Wasser.
translations.fr: Tom tendit une bouteille d'eau à Mary.
translations.pt: Tom entregou a Mary uma garrafa de água.

examples.text: She cut her hand with a knife.

translations.de: Sie hat sich mit einem Messer in die Hand geschnitten.
translations.fr: Elle s'est coupé la main avec un couteau.
translations.pt: Ela se cortou na mão com uma faca.

examples.text: Some people eat sushi with their hands.

translations.de: Manche Leute essen Sushi mit den Händen.
translations.fr: Certaines personnes mangent les sushis avec les doigts.
translations.pt: Algumas pessoas comem sushi com as mãos.

examples.text: Tom caught the ball with one hand.

translations.de: Tom fing den Ball mit einer Hand.
translations.fr: Tom a attrapé la balle d'une main.
translations.pt: Tom pegou a bola com uma mão.

more.definition: To give, pass or transmit with the hand, literally or figuratively.; To lead, guide, or assist with the hand; to conduct.; To furl (a sail).
more.etymology: From Middle English handen, honden, from the noun (see above); and also from henden (> English hend), from Old English *hendan, ġehendan (“to seize by hand, grasp, hold”), from Proto-West Germanic *handijan, from Proto-Germanic *handijaną (“to take by hand, grasp”), from the noun (see above).

examples.text: You're going to miss the train.

translations.de: Sie werden den Zug verpassen.
translations.fr: Vous allez rater le train.
translations.pt: Vocês vão perder o trem.

examples.text: She misses him, especially on rainy days.

translations.de: Er fehlt ihr, besonders an regnerischen Tagen.
translations.fr: Il lui manque, particulièrement les jours de pluie.
translations.pt: Ela sente falta dele, especialmente em dias chuvosos.

examples.text: I'm going to miss your cooking.

translations.de: Mir werden eure Kochkünste fehlen.
translations.fr: Ta cuisine me manquera.
translations.pt: Eu vou sentir falta do jeito que você cozinha.

examples.text: I'm beginning to miss my girlfriend.

translations.de: Langsam fehlt mir meine Freundin.
translations.fr: Je commence à m'ennuyer de ma petite amie.
translations.pt: Estou começando a sentir falta de minha namorada.

more.definition: A failure to physically hit.; A failure to obtain or accomplish something; a failure to succeed.; An act of avoidance (usually used with the verb give).
more.etymology: Verb from Middle English missen, from Old English missan (“to miss, escape the notice of a person”), from Proto-West Germanic *missijan, from Proto-Germanic *missijaną (“to miss, go wrong, fail”), from Proto-Indo-European *meyth₂- (“to change, exchange, trade”).

examples.text: I missed the beginning of the movie.

translations.de: Ich habe den Anfang des Films verpasst.
translations.fr: J'ai raté le début du film.
translations.pt: Eu perdi o começo do filme.

examples.text: She is looking for her missing wallet.

translations.de: Sie sucht nach ihrer verlorenen Geldbörse.
translations.fr: Elle cherche le portefeuille qu'elle a perdu.
translations.pt: Ela está procurando a carteira que ela perdeu.

examples.text: He suddenly noticed his wallet was missing.

translations.de: Plötzlich bemerkte er, dass seine Brieftasche fehlte.
translations.fr: Il s'aperçut soudain que son portefeuille avait disparu.
translations.pt: De repente, sentiu falta de sua carteira.

examples.text: More than a hundred people are still missing.

translations.de: Über einhundert Personen werden noch vermisst.
translations.fr: Plus d'une centaine de personnes sont toujours portées disparues.
translations.pt: Mais de uma centena de pessoas ainda estão desaparecidas.

more.definition: To fail to hit, catch, grasp, etc.; To avoid hitting.; To fail to achieve or attain.
more.etymology: Verb from Middle English missen, from Old English missan (“to miss, escape the notice of a person”), from Proto-West Germanic *missijan, from Proto-Germanic *missijaną (“to miss, go wrong, fail”), from Proto-Indo-European *meyth₂- (“to change, exchange, trade”).

examples.text: I have given every child three candies.

translations.de: Ich habe jedem Kind drei Bonbons gegeben.
translations.fr: J'ai donné 3 bonbons à chaque enfant.
translations.pt: Eu dei três doces a cada criança.

examples.text: I speak French every day at work.

translations.de: Ich spreche jeden Tag auf der Arbeit Französisch.
translations.fr: Je parle le français tous les jours au travail.
translations.pt: Falo francês todos os dias no trabalho.

examples.text: She wakes up at six every morning.

translations.de: Sie steht jeden Morgen um sechs Uhr auf.
translations.fr: Elle se réveille à six heures tous les matins.
translations.pt: Ela acorda às seis horas toda manhã.

examples.text: I go to the movies every week.

translations.de: Ich gehe jede Woche ins Kino.
translations.fr: Je vais au cinéma toutes les semaines.
