examples.text: What the hell is wrong with you?

translations.de: Geht’s noch?
translations.fr: C’est quoi ton problème, à la fin ?
translations.pt: O que diabos há de errado com você?

examples.text: Is it possible that you're wrong?

translations.de: Ist es möglich, dass du dich irrst?
translations.fr: Est-ce possible que tu aies tort ?
translations.pt: É possível que você esteja errado?

more.definition: Incorrect or untrue.; Asserting something incorrect or untrue.; Immoral, not good, bad.
more.etymology: Old Norse rangrinflu. Old Norse rangrinflu. From Middle English wrong, from Old English wrang (“wrong, twisted, uneven”), from Old Norse rangr, vrangr (“crooked, wrong”), from Proto-Germanic *wrangaz (“crooked, twisted, turned awry”), from Proto-Indo-European *werḱ-, *wrengʰ- (“to twist, weave, tie together”), from *wer- (“to turn, bend”).

examples.text: It's clear that you're wrong.

translations.de: Es ist eindeutig, dass du falsch liegst.
translations.fr: Il est évident que tu as tort.
translations.pt: Claramente você está errado.

examples.text: Who said that? It's totally wrong!

translations.de: Wer hat das gesagt? Das ist völlig falsch!
translations.fr: Qui a dit ça ? C'est complètement faux !
translations.pt: Quem disse isso? Está completamente errado!

examples.text: You are playing the wrong notes.

translations.de: Du spielst die falschen Noten.
translations.fr: Vous jouez les mauvaises notes.
translations.pt: Você está tocando as notas erradas.

examples.text: Which of the two is wrong?

translations.de: Was von beidem ist falsch?
translations.fr: Lequel des deux a tort ?
translations.pt: Qual dos dois está errado?

more.definition: In a way that isn't right; incorrectly, wrongly.
more.etymology: Old Norse rangrinflu. Old Norse rangrinflu. From Middle English wrong, from Old English wrang (“wrong, twisted, uneven”), from Old Norse rangr, vrangr (“crooked, wrong”), from Proto-Germanic *wrangaz (“crooked, twisted, turned awry”), from Proto-Indo-European *werḱ-, *wrengʰ- (“to twist, weave, tie together”), from *wer- (“to turn, bend”).

examples.text: Something's wrong with my e-mail.

translations.de: Etwas ist mit meiner E-Mail nicht in Ordnung.
translations.fr: Quelque chose ne va pas dans mon courriel.
translations.pt: Há algo errado com meu e-mail.

examples.text: You're barking up the wrong tree.

translations.de: Du bist auf dem Holzweg.
translations.fr: Tu fais fausse route.
translations.pt: Estás muito enganado.

examples.text: There's something wrong with this machine.

translations.de: Mit dieser Maschine ist irgendetwas nicht in Ordnung.
translations.fr: Cette machine a un problème.
translations.pt: Há algo errado com esta máquina.

examples.text: This answer may not necessarily be wrong.

translations.de: Diese Antwort muss nicht notwendigerweise falsch sein.
translations.fr: Cette réponse n'est pas nécessairement fausse.
translations.pt: Esta resposta não está necessariamente errada.

more.definition: Something that is immoral or not good.; An instance of wronging someone (sometimes with possessive to indicate the wrongdoer).; The incorrect or unjust position or opinion.
more.etymology: Old Norse rangrinflu. Old Norse rangrinflu. From Middle English wrong, from Old English wrang (“wrong, twisted, uneven”), from Old Norse rangr, vrangr (“crooked, wrong”), from Proto-Germanic *wrangaz (“crooked, twisted, turned awry”), from Proto-Indo-European *werḱ-, *wrengʰ- (“to twist, weave, tie together”), from *wer- (“to turn, bend”).

examples.text: Whatever can go wrong will go wrong.

translations.de: Alles, was schiefgehen kann, wird auch schiefgehen.
translations.fr: Tout ce qui peut foirer foirera.
translations.pt: O que puder dar errado, dará errado.

examples.text: You're going in the wrong direction.

translations.de: Du gehst in die verkehrte Richtung.
translations.fr: Tu vas dans la mauvaise direction.
translations.pt: Você está indo na direção errada.

examples.text: It's obvious that you're wrong.

translations.de: Es ist offensichtlich, dass du unrecht hast.
translations.fr: Il est évident que vous avez tort.
translations.pt: É óbvio que você está equivocado.

examples.text: There is something wrong with my car.

translations.de: Irgendetwas stimmt nicht mit meinem Auto.
translations.fr: Il y a quelque chose qui cloche avec ma voiture.
translations.pt: Tem alguma coisa errada com o meu carro.

more.definition: To treat unjustly; to injure or harm; to do wrong by.; To deprive of some right, or to withhold some act of justice.; To slander; to impute evil to unjustly.
more.etymology: Old Norse rangrinflu. Old Norse rangrinflu. From Middle English wrong, from Old English wrang (“wrong, twisted, uneven”), from Old Norse rangr, vrangr (“crooked, wrong”), from Proto-Germanic *wrangaz (“crooked, twisted, turned awry”), from Proto-Indo-European *werḱ-, *wrengʰ- (“to twist, weave, tie together”), from *wer- (“to turn, bend”).

examples.text: Good morning, sir! A merry Christmas to you!

translations.de: Guten Morgen, mein Herr! Frohe Weihnachten für Sie!
translations.fr: Bonjour monsieur ! Joyeux Noël à vous !
translations.pt: Bom dia, senhor! Um feliz Natal para o senhor!

examples.text: Are you going to need the paper bag, sir?

translations.de: Werden Sie die Papiertüte brauchen, Sir?
translations.fr: Allez-vous avoir besoin du sac en papier, monsieur ?
translations.pt: Vai precisar do saco de papel, senhor?

examples.text: Sir, yes, sir!

translations.de: Jawohl, Sir!
translations.fr: Oui mon caporal !
translations.pt: Sim, meu major!

examples.text: Sir, please fill out this form.

translations.de: Mein Herr, füllen Sie bitte dieses Formular aus.
translations.fr: Monsieur, complétez ce formulaire s'il vous plaît.
translations.pt: Senhor, por favor, preencha este formulário.

more.definition: A man of a higher rank or position.; A respectful term of address to a man of higher rank or position, particularly; to a knight or other low member of the peerage.
more.etymology: From Middle English sir, unstressed form of sire, borrowed from Old French sire (“master, sir, lord”), from Latin senior (“older, elder”), from senex (“old”). Doublet of seigneur, seignior, senhor, senior, señor, senyor, signore, and sire.

examples.text: Anything else, sir?

translations.de: Sonst noch etwas, mein Herr?
translations.fr: Quelque chose d'autre, Monsieur ?
translations.pt: Algo mais, senhor?

examples.text: Sir, you are not allowed to park your car here.

translations.de: Sie dürfen hier nicht parken, mein Herr.
translations.fr: Monsieur, vous n’avez pas le droit de garer votre voiture ici.
translations.pt: Cavalheiro, não é permitido estacionar o carro aqui.

examples.text: Good morning, sir! A merry Christmas to you!

translations.de: Guten Morgen, mein Herr! Frohe Weihnachten für Sie!
translations.fr: Bonjour monsieur ! Joyeux Noël à vous !
translations.pt: Bom dia, senhor! Um feliz Natal para o senhor!

examples.text: Are you going to need the paper bag, sir?

translations.de: Werden Sie die Papiertüte brauchen, Sir?
translations.fr: Allez-vous avoir besoin du sac en papier, monsieur ?
translations.pt: Vai precisar do saco de papel, senhor?

more.definition: To address another individual using "sir".
more.etymology: From Middle English sir, unstressed form of sire, borrowed from Old French sire (“master, sir, lord”), from Latin senior (“older, elder”), from senex (“old”). Doublet of seigneur, seignior, senhor, senior, señor, senyor, signore, and sire.

examples.text: I don't care about anyone else!

translations.de: Alle anderen sind mir egal!
translations.fr: Je ne me soucie de personne d'autre !
translations.pt: Eu não me importo com mais ninguém!

examples.text: The only thing he cares about is himself.

translations.de: Er interessiert sich nur für sich selbst.
translations.fr: La seule chose dont il se préoccupe, c'est lui-même.
translations.pt: A única coisa com que se preocupa é ele mesmo.

examples.text: I took care of it for you.

translations.de: Ich habe darauf für dich aufgepasst.
translations.fr: J'en ai pris soin pour toi.
translations.pt: Eu tomei conta para você.

examples.text: I'll take care of it personally.

translations.de: Ich werde mich persönlich darum kümmern.
translations.fr: Je m'en occuperai personnellement.
translations.pt: Vou cuidar disso pessoalmente.

more.definition: Close attention; concern; responsibility.; Worry.; Maintenance, upkeep.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *ǵeh₂r-der. From Middle English care, from Old English caru, ċearu (“care, concern, anxiety, sorrow, grief, trouble”), from Proto-West Germanic *karu, from Proto-Germanic *karō (“care, sorrow, cry”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵeh₂r- (“shout, call”).

examples.text: I can take care of that immediately.

translations.de: Ich kann mich sogleich darum kümmern.
translations.fr: Je peux m'occuper de cela immédiatement.
translations.pt: Posso cuidar disso imediatamente.

examples.text: No one cares about your conscience.

translations.de: Niemand kümmert sich um Ihr Gewissen.
translations.fr: Personne ne se soucie de votre conscience.
translations.pt: Ninguém se importa com tua consciência.

examples.text: He never cared much for me.

translations.de: Ich war ihm immer herzlich egal gewesen.
translations.fr: Il ne s'est jamais beaucoup préoccupé de moi.
translations.pt: Ele nunca se importou muito comigo.

examples.text: I'm taking care of my grandfather.

translations.de: Ich kümmere mich um meinen Großvater.
translations.fr: Je prends soin de mon grand-père.
translations.pt: Estou cuidando do meu avô.

more.definition: To be concerned (about), to have an interest (in); to feel concern (about).; To want, to desire; to like; to be inclined towards or interested in.; To be affected by, to treat as relevant for a subsequent course of action.
more.etymology: From Middle English caren, carien, from Old English carian (“to sorrow, grieve, be troubled, be anxious, to care for, heed”), from Proto-West Germanic *karōn (“to care”), from Proto-Germanic *karōną (“to care”).

examples.text: My mother's going to kill me.

translations.de: Meine Mutter wird mich umbringen.
translations.fr: Ma mère va me tuer.
translations.pt: Minha mãe vai me matar.

examples.text: My mother set the table for dinner.

translations.de: Meine Mutter deckte den Tisch fürs Abendessen.
translations.fr: Ma mère mit la table pour le dîner.
translations.pt: Minha mãe pôs a mesa para o jantar.

examples.text: My mother allowed me to go abroad.

translations.de: Meine Mutter erlaubte mir, ins Ausland zu gehen.
translations.fr: Ma mère m'autorisa à aller à l'étranger.
translations.pt: Minha mãe me autorizou a ir ao exterior.

examples.text: One should love one's mother tongue.

translations.de: Man sollte seine Muttersprache lieben.
translations.fr: Il faut aimer sa langue maternelle.
translations.pt: Devemos amar nossa língua materna.

more.definition: A female parent, especially of a human; a female who parents a child (which she has given birth to, adopted, fostered, etc).; A pregnant female; mother-to-be; a female who gestates a baby.; A female who donates a fertilized egg or donates a body cell which has resulted in a clone.
more.etymology: From Middle English moder, from Old English mōdor, from Proto-West Germanic *mōder, from Proto-Germanic *mōdēr, from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂tēr. Doublet of Madeira, mata, mater, matrix, and matter. Some have proposed that the "dregs" sense is from Middle Dutch modder (“filth”), from Proto-Germanic *muþraz (“sediment”), but modder is not known in this meaning.

examples.text: I forgot Russian was your mother tongue.

translations.de: Ich vergaß, dass Russisch deine Muttersprache ist.
translations.fr: J'avais oublié que le russe était ta langue maternelle.
translations.pt: Eu esqueci que o russo era sua língua materna.

examples.text: That gold ring belonged to my mother.

translations.de: Der Goldring gehörte meiner Mutter.
translations.fr: Cette bague d'or appartenait à ma mère.
translations.pt: Esse anel de ouro pertenceu a minha mãe.

examples.text: He worries about his mother's health.

translations.de: Er macht sich Sorgen um die Gesundheit seiner Mutter.
translations.fr: Il se fait du souci pour la santé de sa mère.
translations.pt: Ele está preocupado com a saúde da mãe.

examples.text: Have you ever lied to your mother?

translations.de: Hast du deine Mutter je angelogen?
translations.fr: As-tu déjà menti à ta mère ?
translations.pt: Você já mentiu para a sua mãe?

more.definition: To give birth to or produce (as its female parent) a child. (Compare father.); To treat as a mother would be expected to treat her child; to nurture.; To cause to contain mother (“that substance which develops in fermenting alcohol and turns it into vinegar”).
more.etymology: From Middle English modren, from the noun (see above).

examples.text: A circle has three hundred sixty degrees.

translations.de: Ein Kreis hat dreihundertsechzig Grad.
translations.fr: Un cercle a trois cent soixante degrés.
translations.pt: O círculo tem trezentos e sessenta graus.

examples.text: The square root of nine is three.

translations.de: Die Quadratwurzel aus neun ist drei.
translations.fr: La racine carrée de neuf est trois.
translations.pt: A raiz quadrada de nove é três.

examples.text: I was born in nineteen thirty-three.

translations.de: Ich wurde 1933 geboren.
translations.fr: Je suis né en mille neuf cent trente-trois.
translations.pt: Eu nasci em mil novecentos e trinta e três.

examples.text: I have three brothers and four sisters.

translations.de: Ich habe drei Brüder und vier Schwestern.
translations.fr: J'ai trois frères et quatre sœurs.
translations.pt: Eu tenho três irmãos e quatro irmãs.

more.definition: The digit/figure 3.; Anything measuring three units, as length.; A person who is three years old.
more.etymology: From Middle English thre, threo, thrie, thri, from Old English þrī, from Proto-West Germanic *þrīʀ, from Proto-Germanic *þrīz, from Proto-Indo-European *tréyes. Doublet of tres and trey. Cognate with German drei, Albanian tre, Armenian երեք (erekʻ), Latin trēs, Latvian trīs, Lithuanian trỹs, Greek τρεῖς (treís), Old Church Slavonic трьѥ (trĭje), and others.

examples.text: I paid three dollars for that book.

translations.de: Ich habe drei Dollar für das Buch bezahlt.
translations.fr: J'ai payé trois dollars pour ce livre.
translations.pt: Paguei três dólares por esse livro.

examples.text: I planted this tree three years ago.

translations.de: Ich habe diesen Baum vor drei Jahren gepflanzt.
translations.fr: J'ai planté cet arbre il y a trois ans.
translations.pt: Plantei esta árvore há três anos.

examples.text: We closed the restaurant three years ago.

translations.de: Wir haben das Restaurant vor drei Jahren geschlossen.
translations.fr: Nous avons fermé le restaurant il y a trois ans.
translations.pt: Nós fechamos o restaurante faz três anos.

examples.text: You're three years younger than Tom.

translations.de: Du bist drei Jahre jünger als Tom.
translations.fr: Tu as trois ans de moins que Tom.
translations.pt: Você é três anos mais novo do que Tom.

more.definition: A numerical value equal to 3; the number following two and preceding four.; Describing a set or group with three elements.
more.etymology: From Middle English thre, threo, thrie, thri, from Old English þrī, from Proto-West Germanic *þrīʀ, from Proto-Germanic *þrīz, from Proto-Indo-European *tréyes. Doublet of tres and trey. Cognate with German drei, Albanian tre, Armenian երեք (erekʻ), Latin trēs, Latvian trīs, Lithuanian trỹs, Greek τρεῖς (treís), Old Church Slavonic трьѥ (trĭje), and others.

examples.text: Tom is wearing a blue sweater today.

translations.de: Tom trägt heute einen blauen Pullover.
translations.fr: Tom porte un pull-over bleu aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Tom está vestindo um suéter azul hoje.

examples.text: I was planning on telling you today.

translations.de: Ich wollte es dir eigentlich heute sagen.
translations.fr: J'avais l'intention de te le dire aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Eu estava planejando te contar hoje.

examples.text: Tom is in a good mood today.

translations.de: Tom ist heute guter Laune.
translations.fr: Tom est de bonne humeur aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Tom está de bom humor hoje.

examples.text: What did you learn at school today?

translations.de: Was hast du heute in der Schule gelernt?
translations.fr: Qu'as-tu appris à l'école aujourd'hui ?
translations.pt: O que você aprendeu na escola hoje?

more.definition: Current; up to date.
more.etymology: From Middle English today, to-daie, todæig, from Old English tōdæġ, tō dæġe (“today”, literally “on [the/this] day, [this] day forward”), equivalent to to + day. Compare Saterland Frisian däälich (“today”), Dutch vandaag (“today”), Old Saxon hindag (“today”, literally “[this] day forward”), German Low German vandage, vandaag (“today”), Swedish i dag, idag (“today”).

examples.text: She has to be feeling better today.

translations.de: Sie muss sich heute besser fühlen.
translations.fr: Elle doit se sentir mieux aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Ela deve estar se sentindo melhor hoje.

examples.text: I've already read today's paper.

translations.de: Ich habe die Zeitung von heute schon gelesen.
translations.fr: J'ai déjà lu le journal d'aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Já li o jornal de hoje.

examples.text: Do I have to do that today?

translations.de: Muss ich das heute machen?
translations.fr: Est-ce que je dois faire ça aujourd'hui ?
translations.pt: Tenho de fazer isso hoje?

examples.text: Aren't you going to school today?

translations.de: Gehst du heute nicht zur Schule?
translations.fr: Ne vas-tu pas à l'école aujourd'hui ?
translations.pt: Você não vai para a escola hoje?

more.definition: On the current day or date.; In the current era; nowadays; these days.; On the day of a recurring cycle or event which is currently happening.
more.etymology: From Middle English today, to-daie, todæig, from Old English tōdæġ, tō dæġe (“today”, literally “on [the/this] day, [this] day forward”), equivalent to to + day. Compare Saterland Frisian däälich (“today”), Dutch vandaag (“today”), Old Saxon hindag (“today”, literally “[this] day forward”), German Low German vandage, vandaag (“today”), Swedish i dag, idag (“today”).

examples.text: What are we going to do today?

translations.de: Was werden wir heute machen?
translations.fr: Que faisons-nous aujourd'hui ?
translations.pt: O que nós vamos fazer hoje?

examples.text: I don't want to study today.

translations.de: Ich will heute nicht lernen.
translations.fr: Aujourd'hui je n'ai pas envie d'étudier.
translations.pt: Eu não quero estudar hoje.

examples.text: Do you think it'll rain today?

translations.de: Denkst du, dass es heute regnet?
translations.fr: Penses-tu qu'il va pleuvoir aujourd'hui ?
translations.pt: Você acha que vai chover hoje?

examples.text: I'm not going to school today.

translations.de: Heute gehe ich nicht zur Schule.
translations.fr: Je ne vais pas à l'école aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Não vou à escola hoje.

more.definition: The current day or date.; The 24-hour period beginning at 5 or 6 a.m. or sunrise of the current day.; The present era; nowadays.
more.etymology: From Middle English today, to-daie, todæig, from Old English tōdæġ, tō dæġe (“today”, literally “on [the/this] day, [this] day forward”), equivalent to to + day. Compare Saterland Frisian däälich (“today”), Dutch vandaag (“today”), Old Saxon hindag (“today”, literally “[this] day forward”), German Low German vandage, vandaag (“today”), Swedish i dag, idag (“today”).

examples.text: There's a shortage of car parts.

translations.de: Es besteht ein Mangel an Autoersatzteilen.
translations.fr: Il y a une pénurie de pièces automobiles.
translations.pt: Há uma escassez de peças de automóvel.

examples.text: He has two cars in his garage.

translations.de: In seiner Garage stehen zwei Autos.
translations.fr: Il a deux voitures dans son garage.
translations.pt: Ele tem dois carros na garagem.

examples.text: I am going to rent a car.

translations.de: Ich werde ein Auto mieten.
translations.fr: Je vais louer une voiture.
translations.pt: Vou alugar um carro.

examples.text: Do you know whose car that is?

translations.de: Wissen Sie, wem das dort Auto gehört?
translations.fr: Sais-tu à qui est cette voiture ?
translations.pt: Você sabe de quem é esse carro?

more.definition: A wheeled vehicle that moves independently, with at least three wheels, powered mechanically, steered by a driver and mostly for personal transportation but relatively smaller than a truck/lorry and a bus.; An unpowered unit in a railroad train, used to hold either passengers or cargo.; A similar vehicle used in special contexts, such as mines, quarries, and mills.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English carre, borrowed from Anglo-Norman carre, from Old Northern French (compare Old French char), from Latin carrus (“two-wheeled baggage wagon”), from Gaulish *karros, from Proto-Celtic *karros (“wagon”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱr̥sós (“vehicle”). Doublet of carrus and horse.

examples.text: Let me sleep for another ten minutes.

translations.de: Lass mich noch zehn Minuten schlafen.
translations.fr: Laisse-moi dormir encore dix minutes.
translations.pt: Deixe-me dormir por mais dez minutos.

examples.text: The waiter went to get another glass.

translations.de: Der Kellner ging ein anderes Glas holen.
translations.fr: Le serveur alla chercher un autre verre.
translations.pt: O garçom foi buscar outro copo.

examples.text: I think everybody should learn another language.

translations.de: Ich finde, dass jeder eine andere Sprache lernen sollte.
translations.fr: Je pense que tout le monde devrait apprendre une autre langue.
translations.pt: Acho que todo mundo deve aprender um segundo idioma.

examples.text: I asked the bartender for another beer.

translations.de: Ich bat den Barmann um ein weiteres Bier.
translations.fr: J'ai demandé une autre bière au barman.
translations.pt: Pedi outra cerveja ao barman.

more.definition: One more further, in addition to the quantity by then; a second or additional one, similar in likeness or in effect.; Not the same; different.; Any or some other, similar in likeness or in effect, instead.
more.etymology: From Middle English another. By surface analysis, an + other.

examples.text: I'm going to order another beer.

translations.de: Ich bestelle mir noch ein Bier.
translations.fr: Je vais commander une autre bière.
translations.pt: Vou pedir mais uma cerveja.

examples.text: Do you have this in another colour?

translations.de: Haben Sie das hier in einer anderen Farbe?
translations.fr: As-tu cela dans une autre couleur ?
translations.pt: Você tem isso em outra cor?

examples.text: Can I have another piece of cake?

translations.de: Kann ich noch ein Stück Kuchen haben?
translations.fr: Puis-je avoir une autre part de gâteau ?
translations.pt: Posso comer mais um pedaço de bolo?

examples.text: Puns are often untranslatable into another language.

translations.de: Wortwitze können oft nicht in andere Sprachen übersetzt werden.
translations.fr: Les jeux de mots sont souvent intraduisibles dans une autre langue.
translations.pt: Os trocadilhos são, muitas vezes, intraduzíveis em outro idioma.

more.definition: An additional one of the same kind.; One that is different from the current one.; One of a group of things of the same kind.
more.etymology: From Middle English another. By surface analysis, an + other.

examples.text: I'll be there in a minute.

translations.de: Ich werde in einer Minute da sein.
translations.fr: J'arrive immédiatement.
translations.pt: Estarei aí em um minuto.

examples.text: Will you help me for a minute?

translations.de: Kannst du mir mal kurz helfen?
translations.fr: Veux-tu m'aider une minute ?
translations.pt: Você me ajuda um minuto?

examples.text: I'm leaving in one minute.

translations.de: Ich gehe in einer Minute.
translations.fr: Je pars dans une minute.
translations.pt: Estou saindo em um minuto.

examples.text: Can I borrow your book for a minute?

translations.de: Kann ich dein Buch für eine Minute ausleihen?
translations.fr: Je peux emprunter ton livre une minute ?
translations.pt: Pode me emprestar seu livro por um momento?

more.definition: Very small.; Very careful and exact, giving small details.
more.etymology: Borrowed from Latin minūtus (“small", "petty”), perfect passive participle of minuō (“make smaller”).

examples.text: I'll be ready in ten minutes.

translations.de: Ich bin in zehn Minuten soweit.
translations.fr: Je serai prêt dans dix minutes.
translations.pt: Estarei pronto em dez minutos.

examples.text: Let's take a ten-minute break.

translations.de: Machen wir zehn Minuten Pause.
translations.fr: Faisons une pause de dix minutes.
translations.pt: Vamos dar uma pausa de dez minutos.

examples.text: There are sixty seconds in a minute.

translations.de: Eine Minute umfasst sechzig Sekunden.
translations.fr: Il y a soixante secondes dans une minute.
translations.pt: Há sessenta segundos em um minuto.

examples.text: He will be back in ten minutes.

more.definition: Of an event, to write in a memo or the minutes of a meeting.; To set down a short sketch or note of; to jot down; to make a minute or a brief summary of.
more.etymology: From Middle English mynute, minute, mynet, from Old French minute, from Medieval Latin minūta (“60th of an hour; note”). Doublet of menu and menudo.

examples.text: Please hold the line a moment.

more.etymology: From Middle English hold, holde, from Old English hold (“gracious, friendly, kind”), from Proto-West Germanic *holþ, from Proto-Germanic *hulþaz (“favourable, gracious, loyal”), from Proto-Indo-European *kel- (“to tend, incline, bend, tip”).

examples.text: That auditorium holds two thousand people.

examples.text: Can I hold your hand?

examples.text: May I hold your hand?

more.definition: A grasp or grip.; An act or instance of holding.; A place where animals are held for safety
more.etymology: Derived from Middle English holden, derived from Old English healdan, derived from Proto-West Germanic *haldan, derived from Proto-Germanic *haldaną (“to tend, herd”), maybe derived from Proto-Indo-European *kel- (“to drive”). examples.text: The fat woman was holding a monkey.

examples.text: Rio's carnival is held in February.

examples.text: I couldn't hold back my anger.

translations.de: Ich konnte meine Wut nicht zügeln.

more.definition: To grasp or grip.; To contain or store.; To have and keep possession of something.

examples.text: The world has no need for me.

examples.text: I'm a citizen of the world.

more.definition: The subjective human experience, regarded collectively; human collective existence; existence in general; the reality we live in.; The subjective human experience, regarded individually.; A majority of people.
more.etymology: From Middle English world, from Old English weorold (“world”), from Proto-West Germanic *weraldi, from Proto-Germanic *weraldiz (“lifetime, human existence, world”, literally “age/era of man”), equivalent to wer (“man”) + eld (“age”). examples.text: Magnus Carlsen is the world chess champion.

translations.fr: Magnus Carlsen est le champion du monde d'échecs.

examples.text: Tom travels the world looking for adventure.

translations.de: Tom bereist die Welt auf der Suche nach Abenteuer.
translations.fr: Tom parcourt le monde en quête d'aventure.
translations.pt: Tom viaja pelo mundo em busca de aventura.

examples.text: I'm too beautiful for this world.

translations.de: Ich bin zu schön für diese Welt.
translations.fr: Je suis trop beau pour ce monde.
translations.pt: Eu sou muito bonito para este mundo.

examples.text: Tom thinks he can save the world.

translations.de: Tom denkt, er könne die Welt retten.
translations.fr: Tom pense qu'il peut sauver le monde.

more.definition: To consider or cause to be considered from a global perspective; to consider as a global whole, rather than making or focusing on national or other distinctions; compare globalize.; To make real; to make worldly.
more.etymology: From Middle English world, from Old English weorold (“world”), from Proto-West Germanic *weraldi, from Proto-Germanic *weraldiz (“lifetime, human existence, world”, literally “age/era of man”), equivalent to wer (“man”) + eld (“age”). examples.text: Hindi and Urdu are the same language.

translations.fr: Le hindi et l'ourdou sont la même langue.
translations.pt: Hindi e Urdu são o mesmo idioma.

examples.text: Tom and Mary are the same height.

examples.text: We played on the same soccer team.

translations.pt: Nós jogávamos no mesmo time.

examples.text: Many people have made the same mistake.

translations.de: Viele haben denselben Fehler gemacht.
translations.fr: Beaucoup de personnes ont fait la même erreur.
translations.pt: Muitas pessoas cometeram o mesmo erro.

more.definition: Not different or other; not another or others; not different as regards self; selfsame; identical.; Lacking variety from; indistinguishable.; Similar, alike.
more.etymology: From Middle English same, from Old Norse samr (“same”) and/or Old English same, sama (“same”) in the phrase swā same (swā) (“in like manner, in the same way (as)”), both from Proto-Germanic *samaz (“same”), from Proto-Indo-European *somHós (“same”). Doublet of some and -some.

examples.text: We're all in the same boat.

translations.fr: Nous sommes tous sur le même bateau.

examples.text: You'd do the same for me.

more.definition: The same way; in the same manner; to the same extent, unchanged; equally.
more.etymology: From Middle English same, from Old Norse samr (“same”) and/or Old English same, sama (“same”) in the phrase swā same (swā) (“in like manner, in the same way (as)”), both from Proto-Germanic *samaz (“same”), from Proto-Indo-European *somHós (“same”). Doublet of some and -some.

examples.text: Don't make the same mistake again.

examples.text: It's all the same to me.

more.etymology: From Middle English efd, had, hafd, heafd, hed, heed, hefet, heid, het, hevd, heved, hevid, hiede, hæfd, hæfedd, from Old English hēafod (“head; top; leader; origin”), from Proto-West Germanic *haubud, from Proto-Germanic *haubudą (“head”), from Proto-Indo-European *káput (“head”), from *kap- (“head; bowl, cup”).

translations.pt: Ela terá um filho no mês que vem.

examples.text: I'm going to Spain next week.

translations.de: Nächste Woche fahre ich nach Spanien.
translations.fr: Je vais en Espagne la semaine prochaine.
translations.pt: Vou à Espanha na semana que vem.

more.definition: In a time, place, rank or sequence closest or following.; So as to follow in time or sequence something previously mentioned.; On the first subsequent occasion.
more.etymology: From Middle English nexte, nexste, nixte, from Old English nīehsta, nīehste, etc., inflected forms of nīehst (“nearest, next”), superlative form of nēah (“nigh”) (the comparative would become near), corresponding to Proto-Germanic *nēhwist (“nearest, closest”); equivalent to nigh + -est.

examples.text: He will be very busy next month.

translations.de: Er wird im nächsten Monat sehr beschäftigt sein.
translations.fr: Il sera très occupé le mois prochain.
translations.pt: Ele estará muito ocupado no mês que vem.

examples.text: She will have a baby next month.

translations.de: Sie bekommt nächsten Monat ein Baby.
translations.fr: Elle va avoir un bébé le mois prochain.
translations.pt: Ela terá um bebê no mês que vem.

examples.text: I want to learn Chinese next year.

translations.de: Nächstes Jahr will ich Chinesisch lernen.
translations.fr: Je veux apprendre le chinois l'année prochaine.
translations.pt: Quero aprender chinês no ano que vem.

examples.text: What time does the next train leave?

translations.de: Wann fährt der nächste Zug ab?
translations.fr: À quelle heure part le prochain train ?
translations.pt: A que horas sai o próximo trem?

more.definition: Denotes the one immediately following the current or most recent one.; Closest in the future, or closest but one if the closest is very soon; of days, sometimes thought to specifically refer to the instance closest to seven days (one week) in the future.
more.etymology: From Middle English nexte, nexste, nixte, from Old English nīehsta, nīehste, etc., inflected forms of nīehst (“nearest, next”), superlative form of nēah (“nigh”) (the comparative would become near), corresponding to Proto-Germanic *nēhwist (“nearest, closest”); equivalent to nigh + -est.

examples.text: Ask him when the next plane leaves.

translations.de: Frag ihn, wann der nächste Flug geht!
translations.fr: Demande-lui quand part le prochain vol !
translations.pt: Pergunte-lhe quando sai o próximo avião.

examples.text: I want to go abroad next year.

translations.de: Nächstes Jahr will ich ins Ausland gehen.
translations.fr: Je veux aller à l'étranger l'année prochaine.
translations.pt: Quero viajar para fora no ano que vem.

examples.text: We will visit our teacher next week.

translations.de: Wir werden nächste Woche unseren Lehrer besuchen.
translations.fr: Nous rendrons visite à notre professeur la semaine prochaine.
translations.pt: Visitaremos nosso professor semana que vem.

examples.text: The wedding will take place next spring.

translations.de: Die Hochzeit findet im nächsten Frühjahr statt.
translations.fr: Le mariage aura lieu au printemps prochain.
translations.pt: O casamento acontecerá na próxima primavera.

more.definition: The one that follows after this one.; Next match
more.etymology: From Middle English nexte, nexste, nixte, from Old English nīehsta, nīehste, etc., inflected forms of nīehst (“nearest, next”), superlative form of nēah (“nigh”) (the comparative would become near), corresponding to Proto-Germanic *nēhwist (“nearest, closest”); equivalent to nigh + -est.

examples.text: I want to study abroad next year.

translations.de: Ich möchte nächstes Jahr im Ausland studieren.
translations.fr: Je veux étudier à l'étranger l'année prochaine.
translations.pt: Quero estudar fora no ano que vem.

examples.text: She will give a party next week.

translations.de: Sie wird nächste Woche eine Party veranstalten.
translations.fr: Elle donnera une fête la semaine prochaine.
translations.pt: Ela dará uma festa semana que vem.

examples.text: She leaves for New York next Sunday.

translations.de: Nächsten Sonntag fährt sie nach New York ab.
translations.fr: Elle part pour New-York dimanche prochain.
translations.pt: Ela vai para Nova York no próximo domingo.

examples.text: New stamps will be issued next month.

translations.de: Nächste Woche werden neue Briefmarken herausgegeben.
translations.fr: De nouveaux timbres seront émis le mois prochain.
translations.pt: Novos selos serão emitidos no mês que vem.

more.etymology: From Middle English nexte, nexste, nixte, from Old English nīehsta, nīehste, etc., inflected forms of nīehst (“nearest, next”), superlative form of nēah (“nigh”) (the comparative would become near), corresponding to Proto-Germanic *nēhwist (“nearest, closest”); equivalent to nigh + -est.

examples.text: I've already made up my mind.

translations.de: Ich habe mich bereits entschieden.
translations.fr: J'ai déjà pris ma décision.
translations.pt: Eu já me decidi.

examples.text: Chess is a battle between two creative minds.

translations.de: Schach ist ein Kampf zwischen zwei kreativen Geister.
translations.fr: Les échecs sont une bataille entre deux esprits créatifs.
translations.pt: O xadrez é uma batalha entre duas mentes criativas.

examples.text: Would you mind speaking a little louder?

translations.de: Könnten Sie vielleicht etwas lauter sprechen?
translations.fr: Pourrais-tu parler un peu plus fort ?
translations.pt: Quer falar um pouco mais alto, por favor?

examples.text: I think I'm losing my mind.

translations.de: Ich denke, ich verliere den Verstand.
translations.fr: Je pense que je perds l'esprit.
translations.pt: Acho que estou perdendo a cabeça.

more.definition: The capability for rational thought.; The ability to be aware of things.; The ability to remember things.
more.etymology: From Middle English minde, munde, imynde, imunde, ȝemynde, ȝemunde, from Old English mynd, ġemynd (“mind, memory”), from Proto-West Germanic *mundi, *gamundi, from Proto-Germanic *mundiz, *gamundiz (“memory, remembrance”), from Proto-Indo-European *méntis (“thought”) (compare also mantis, via Greek), from the root *men- (“to think”).

examples.text: Do you mind if I come in?

translations.de: Hättest du etwas dagegen, wenn ich hereinkäme?
translations.fr: Vois-tu un inconvénient à ce que j'entre ?
translations.pt: Se importa se eu entrar?

examples.text: Superstition is the religion of feeble minds.

translations.de: Aberglaube ist die Religion der schwachen Geister.
translations.fr: La superstition est la religion des esprits faibles.
translations.pt: Superstição é a religião das mentes fracas.

examples.text: Keep in mind what I tell you.

translations.de: Merke dir, was ich dir sage!
translations.fr: Garde à l'esprit ce que je te dis.
translations.pt: Lembre-se do que eu lhe digo.

examples.text: Have you made up your mind yet?

translations.de: Hast du dich schon entschieden?
translations.fr: Est-ce que tu t'es déjà décidé ?
translations.pt: Vocês já se decidiram?

more.definition: To bring or recall to mind; to remember; bear or keep in mind.; To remember.; To turn one's mind to; to observe; to notice.
more.etymology: From Middle English minde, munde, imynde, imunde, ȝemynde, ȝemunde, from Old English mynd, ġemynd (“mind, memory”), from Proto-West Germanic *mundi, *gamundi, from Proto-Germanic *mundiz, *gamundiz (“memory, remembrance”), from Proto-Indo-European *méntis (“thought”) (compare also mantis, via Greek), from the root *men- (“to think”).

examples.text: Tom said he didn't drink coffee.

translations.de: Tom sagte, er trinke keinen Kaffee.
translations.fr: Tom dit qu'il ne buvait pas de café.
translations.pt: Tom disse que não bebeu café.

examples.text: Tom drank a glass of orange juice.

translations.de: Tom trank ein Glas Orangensaft.
translations.fr: Thomas a bu un verre de jus d'orange.
translations.pt: Tom tomou um copo de suco de laranja.

examples.text: A man who drinks water is always healthy.

translations.de: Wer Wasser trinkt, ist immer gesund.
translations.fr: Un homme qui boit de l'eau est toujours en bonne santé.
translations.pt: Quem bebe água está sempre saudável.

examples.text: What I drink the most is coffee.

translations.de: Was ich am meisten trinke, ist Kaffee.
translations.fr: Ce que je bois le plus, c'est du café.
translations.pt: O que eu mais bebo é café.

more.definition: A beverage.; Drinks in general; something to drink.; A type of beverage (usually mixed).
more.etymology: From Middle English drink, drinke (also as drinche, drunch), from Old English drynċ, from Proto-Germanic *drunkiz, *drankiz.

examples.text: Do people in Boston drink tap water?

translations.de: Trinken die Leute in Boston Leitungswasser?
translations.fr: Les gens boivent-ils de l'eau du robinet à Boston ?
translations.pt: As pessoas tomam água da torneira em Boston?

examples.text: I've been drinking too much coffee.

translations.de: Ich habe zu viel Kaffee getrunken.
translations.fr: J'ai bu trop de café.
translations.pt: Eu tenho tomado muito café.

examples.text: He made a mistake and drank poison.

translations.de: Er machte einen Fehler und trank Gift.
translations.fr: Il s'est trompé et a bu du poison.
translations.pt: Ele fez um erro e bebeu veneno.

examples.text: I drink coconut water in the morning.

translations.de: Morgens trinke ich Kokosnussmilch.
translations.fr: Je bois de l'eau de coco le matin.
translations.pt: Eu bebo água de coco de manhã.

more.definition: To consume (a liquid) through the mouth.; To consume the liquid contained within (a bottle, glass, etc.).; To consume alcoholic beverages.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English drynken, drinken, from Old English drincan (“to drink, swallow up, engulf”), from Proto-West Germanic *drinkan, from Proto-Germanic *drinkaną (“to drink”), of uncertain origin; possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dʰrenǵ- (“to draw into one's mouth, sip, gulp”), nasalised variant of *dʰreǵ- (“to draw, glide”). Cognates include German trinken, Norwegian Bokmål drikke, and Italian trincare.

examples.text: I've got a job for you.

translations.de: Ich habe Arbeit für dich.
translations.fr: J'ai un boulot pour toi.
translations.pt: Tenho um trabalho para você.

examples.text: Are you thinking about getting a job?

translations.de: Hast du vor, dir einen Job zu suchen?
translations.fr: Penses-tu à obtenir un emploi ?
translations.pt: Você está pensando sobre pegar o emprego?

examples.text: He was looking for a good job.

translations.de: Er hat einen guten Job gesucht.
translations.fr: Il recherchait un bon travail.
translations.pt: Ele estava procurando um bom emprego.

examples.text: There is no future in his job.

translations.de: Seine Arbeit hat keine Zukunft.
translations.fr: Son métier n'a pas d'avenir.
translations.pt: Não há futuro nesse emprego.

more.definition: A task.; An economic role for which a person is paid.; Plastic surgery.
more.etymology: From the phrase jobbe of work (“piece of work”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from a variant of Middle English gobbe (“mass, lump”); or perhaps related to Middle English jobben (“to jab, thrust, peck”), or Middle English choppe (“piece, bargain”). More at gob, jab, chop.

examples.text: Tom has started looking for a job.

translations.de: Tom hat begonnen, sich nach einen Job umzuschauen.
translations.fr: Tom a commencé à chercher un travail.
translations.pt: Tom começou a procurar trabalho.

examples.text: Why don't you get a job?

translations.de: Such dir doch Arbeit!
translations.fr: Pourquoi ne prends-tu pas un emploi ?
translations.pt: Por que você não arruma um emprego?

examples.text: I have a job interview tomorrow morning.

translations.de: Ich habe morgen früh ein Vorstellungsgespräch.
translations.fr: J'ai un entretien d'embauche demain matin.
translations.pt: Eu terei uma entrevista de emprego amanhã de manhã.

examples.text: I wasn't interested in the job.

translations.de: Ich hatte kein Interesse an dem Job.
translations.fr: Le travail ne m'intéressait pas.
translations.pt: Eu não estava interessado no trabalho.

more.definition: To do odd jobs or occasional work for hire.; To work as a jobber.; To take the loss, usually in a demeaning or submissive manner.
more.etymology: From the phrase jobbe of work (“piece of work”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from a variant of Middle English gobbe (“mass, lump”); or perhaps related to Middle English jobben (“to jab, thrust, peck”), or Middle English choppe (“piece, bargain”). More at gob, jab, chop.

examples.text: I can't change who I am.

translations.de: Ich kann nicht ändern, wer ich bin.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas changer ce que je suis.
translations.pt: Eu não posso mudar quem eu sou.

examples.text: Intelligence is the ability to adjust to changes.

translations.de: Intelligenz ist die Fähigkeit, sich an Veränderungen anzupassen.
translations.fr: L'intelligence est la capacité de s'adapter aux changements.
translations.pt: Inteligência é a habilidade de se adaptar às mudanças.

examples.text: In autumn, leaves change color and fall.

translations.de: Im Herbst verändern die Blätter ihre Farbe und fallen ab.
translations.fr: En automne, les feuilles changent de couleur et tombent.
translations.pt: No outono, as folhas mudam de cor e caem.

examples.text: Do you have change for a dollar?

translations.de: Kannst du auf einen Dollar herausgeben?
translations.fr: As-tu la monnaie d'un dollar ?
translations.pt: Você tem troco para um dólar?

more.definition: The process or result of becoming different.; Small denominations of money given in exchange for a larger denomination.; A replacement.
more.etymology: Proto-Celtic *kambosder. Gaulish cambionbor. Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Late Latin cambiāreder. Old French changierder. Anglo-Norman chaungerbor.

examples.text: There's been a change of plans.

translations.de: Es gab eine Planänderung.
translations.fr: Il y a eu un changement de plan.
translations.pt: Houve uma mudança de planos.

examples.text: I have to get changed for work.

translations.de: Ich muß mich für die Arbeit umziehen.
translations.fr: Il faut que je me change pour le travail.
translations.pt: Preciso me trocar para trabalhar.

examples.text: Wait until the light changes to green.

translations.de: Warte bis das Licht grün wird.
translations.fr: Attendez jusqu'à ce que le feu passe au vert.
translations.pt: Espere até a luz mudar para o verde.

examples.text: Artificial intelligence is changing the world.

translations.de: Künstliche Intelligenz verändert die Welt.
translations.fr: L'intelligence artificielle change le monde.
translations.pt: A inteligência artificial está mudando o mundo.

more.definition: To become something different.; To make something into something else.; To replace.
more.etymology: Proto-Celtic *kambosder. Gaulish cambionbor. Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Late Latin cambiāreder. Old French changierder. Anglo-Norman chaungerbor.

examples.text: They want to see you dead.

translations.de: Sie wollen dich tot sehen.
translations.fr: Elles veulent te voir mort.
translations.pt: Eles querem ver você morto.

examples.text: Today I dreamed I was dead.

translations.de: Heute träumte ich davon, dass ich tot wäre.
translations.fr: Aujourd'hui, j'ai rêvé que j'étais mort.
translations.pt: Hoje sonhei que tinha morrido.

examples.text: I thought Tom and Mary were both dead.

translations.de: Ich dachte, Tom und Mary wären beide tot.
translations.fr: Je pensais que Tom et Mary étaient tous les deux morts.
translations.pt: Pensei que Tom e Mary estivessem mortos.

examples.text: They are probably all dead now.

translations.de: Wahrscheinlich sind nun alle tot.
translations.fr: Ils sont probablement tous morts, à l'heure qu'il est.
translations.pt: Eles provavelmente estão todos mortos agora.
