more.etymology: From Middle English ded, deed, from Old English dēad, from Proto-West Germanic *daud, from Proto-Germanic *daudaz. Compare West Frisian dead, dea, Dutch dood, German tot, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål død, Norwegian Nynorsk daud, Swedish död.

examples.text: I'm glad he's dead.

translations.de: Ich bin froh, dass er tot ist.
translations.fr: Je suis content qu'il soit mort.
translations.pt: Folgo que ele tenha morrido.

examples.text: The king is dead. Long live the king!

translations.de: Der König ist tot. Lang lebe der König!
translations.fr: Le roi est mort. Longue vie au roi !
translations.pt: O rei está morto. Vida longa ao rei!

examples.text: My phone battery is almost dead.

translations.de: Mein Handyakku ist fast leer.
translations.fr: La batterie de mon téléphone est presque vide.
translations.pt: A bateria do meu telefone está quase acabando.

examples.text: They're probably all dead now.

translations.de: Wahrscheinlich sind nun alle tot.
translations.fr: Ils sont probablement tous morts, à l'heure qu'il est.
translations.pt: Eles provavelmente estão todos mortos agora.

more.definition: Exactly.; Very, absolutely, extremely.; Suddenly and completely.
more.etymology: From Middle English ded, deed, from Old English dēad, from Proto-West Germanic *daud, from Proto-Germanic *daudaz. Compare West Frisian dead, dea, Dutch dood, German tot, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål død, Norwegian Nynorsk daud, Swedish död.

examples.text: He has been dead for three years.

translations.de: Er ist seit drei Jahren tot.
translations.fr: Il est mort il y a trois ans.
translations.pt: Ele está morto há três anos.

examples.text: I suddenly thought of my dead mother.

translations.de: Ich dachte plötzlich an meine verstorbene Mutter.
translations.fr: Soudain, j'ai pensé à ma mère décédée.
translations.pt: De repente, pensei em minha falecida mãe.

examples.text: I often think of my dead mother.

translations.de: Ich denke oft an meine verstorbene Mutter.
translations.fr: Je pense souvent à ma mère morte.
translations.pt: Penso com frequência na minha falecida mãe.

examples.text: I'm dead set against the plan.

translations.de: Ich bin absolut gegen den Plan.
translations.fr: Je suis fermement opposé au plan.
translations.pt: Eu sou absolutamente contrário ao plano.

more.definition: Time when coldness, darkness, or stillness is most intense.; Those who have died: dead people.; (usually in the plural) Sterile mining waste, often present as many large rocks stacked inside the workings.
more.etymology: From Middle English ded, deed, from Old English dēad, from Proto-West Germanic *daud, from Proto-Germanic *daudaz. Compare West Frisian dead, dea, Dutch dood, German tot, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål død, Norwegian Nynorsk daud, Swedish död.

examples.text: Tom was found dead in his bed.

translations.de: Tom wurde tot in seinem Bett aufgefunden.
translations.fr: Tom a été retrouvé mort dans son lit.
translations.pt: Tom foi encontrado morto em sua cama.

examples.text: I didn't know he was dead.

translations.de: Ich wusste nicht, dass er tot war.
translations.fr: Je ne savais pas qu'il était mort.
translations.pt: Eu não sabia que ele tinha morrido.

examples.text: She was watching the dead leaves falling.

translations.de: Sie sah zu, wie die welken Blätter herabfielen.
translations.fr: Elle regardait les feuilles mortes tomber.
translations.pt: Ela estava observando as folhas secas caírem.

examples.text: He has been dead for five years.

translations.de: Er ist seit fünf Jahren tot.
translations.fr: Il est mort depuis cinq ans.
translations.pt: Ele está morto há cinco anos.

more.definition: To prevent by disabling; to stop.; To make dead; to deaden; to deprive of life, force, or vigour.; To kill.
more.etymology: From Middle English ded, deed, from Old English dēad, from Proto-West Germanic *daud, from Proto-Germanic *daudaz. Compare West Frisian dead, dea, Dutch dood, German tot, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål død, Norwegian Nynorsk daud, Swedish död.

examples.text: I can't get the door open.

translations.de: Ich kriege die Tür nicht auf.
translations.fr: Je n'arrive pas à ouvrir la porte.
translations.pt: Não consigo abrir a porta.

examples.text: The museum isn't open on Sundays.

translations.de: Das Museum hat sonntags nicht geöffnet.
translations.fr: Le musée n'est pas ouvert les dimanches.
translations.pt: O museu não abre aos domingos.

examples.text: The banks aren't open on Saturdays.

translations.de: Banken sind samstags nicht geöffnet.
translations.fr: Les banques ne sont pas ouvertes le samedi.
translations.pt: Os bancos não abrem aos sábados.

examples.text: Do I have to open the window?

translations.de: Muss ich das Fenster öffnen?
translations.fr: Dois-je ouvrir la fenêtre ?
translations.pt: Devo abrir a janela?

more.definition: Able to have something pass through or along it.; Not covered, sealed, etc.; having an opening or aperture showing what is inside.; Not physically drawn together, folded or contracted.
more.etymology: Adjective from Middle English open, from Old English open (“open”), from Proto-West Germanic *opan, from Proto-Germanic *upanaz (“open”), from Proto-Indo-European *upo (“up from under, over”).

examples.text: We had to break open the door.

translations.de: Wir mussten die Tür aufbrechen.
translations.fr: On a dû enfoncer la porte.
translations.pt: Tivemos que arrombar a porta.

examples.text: I didn't leave the door open.

translations.de: Ich habe die Tür nicht offengelassen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas laissé la porte ouverte.
translations.pt: Eu não deixei a porta aberta.

examples.text: I can't get this suitcase open.

translations.de: Ich kriege diesen Koffer nicht auf.
translations.fr: Je ne parviens pas à ouvrir cette valise.
translations.pt: Não posso abrir esta mala.

examples.text: Can you open the door for me?

translations.de: Kannst du mir die Türe öffnen?
translations.fr: Peux-tu m'ouvrir la porte ?
translations.pt: Você pode abrir a porta para mim?

more.definition: Open or unobstructed space; an exposed location.; Public knowledge or scrutiny; full view.; A defect in an electrical circuit preventing current from flowing.
more.etymology: Adjective from Middle English open, from Old English open (“open”), from Proto-West Germanic *opan, from Proto-Germanic *upanaz (“open”), from Proto-Indo-European *upo (“up from under, over”).

examples.text: If you get bored, open a book!

translations.de: Wenn dir langweilig wird, schlag ein Buch auf!
translations.fr: Si tu t'ennuies, ouvre un livre !
translations.pt: Se ficares entediado, abre um livro!

examples.text: The mechanic opens his workshop at seven.

translations.de: Der Mechaniker öffnet seine Werkstatt um sieben Uhr.
translations.fr: Le mécanicien ouvre son atelier à sept heures.
translations.pt: O mecânico abre sua oficina às sete.

examples.text: I opened a bottle of red wine.

translations.de: Ich habe eine Flasche Rotwein geöffnet.
translations.fr: J'ouvris une bouteille de vin rouge.
translations.pt: Abri uma garrafa de vinho tinto.

examples.text: Please open the window. I'm suffocating.

translations.de: Mach bitte das Fenster auf. Ich ersticke.
translations.fr: S'il te plait, ouvre la fenêtre, j'étouffe.
translations.pt: Por favor, abra a janela. Estou morrendo sufocado.

more.definition: To make or become accessible or clear for passage by moving from a shut position.; To make or become clear by removal of objects and obstructions, so as to allow passage, access, or visibility.; To unseal or uncover, or become unsealed or uncovered.
more.etymology: Adjective from Middle English open, from Old English open (“open”), from Proto-West Germanic *opan, from Proto-Germanic *upanaz (“open”), from Proto-Indo-European *upo (“up from under, over”).

examples.text: His family emigrated to the United States.

translations.de: Seine Familie wanderte in die Vereinigten Staaten aus.
translations.fr: Sa famille émigra aux États-Unis d'Amérique.
translations.pt: Sua família emigrou para os Estados Unidos.

examples.text: Why don't you have a family?

translations.de: Warum hast du keine Familie?
translations.fr: Pourquoi n'as-tu pas de famille ?
translations.pt: Por que você não tem família?

examples.text: His family did not have much money.

translations.de: Seine Familie hatte nicht viel Geld.
translations.fr: Sa famille ne disposait pas de beaucoup d'argent.
translations.pt: A família dele não tinha muito dinheiro.

examples.text: The family is watching a movie together.

translations.de: Die Familie schaut sich zusammen einen Film an.
translations.fr: La famille regarde un film.
translations.pt: A família está assistindo um filme junta.

more.definition: Suitable for children and adults.; Homosexual.
more.etymology: From Late Middle English famylye, from Latin familia (“a household”). Displaced native Old English hīred and hād. Doublet of familia.

examples.text: I'll spend Christmas with my family.

translations.de: Ich werde Weihnachten mit meiner Familie zusammen verbringen.
translations.fr: Je passerai Noël avec ma famille.
translations.pt: Eu vou passar o Natal com a minha família.

examples.text: There are five people in our family.

translations.de: Wir sind in unserer Familie zu fünft.
translations.fr: Il y a cinq personnes dans notre famille.
translations.pt: Há cinco pessoas em nossa família.

examples.text: I'm doing this for my family.

translations.de: Ich tue das für meine Familie.
translations.fr: Je le fais pour ma famille.
translations.pt: Estou fazendo isso pela minha família.

examples.text: I grew up in a poor family.

translations.de: Ich bin in einer armen Familie groß geworden.
translations.fr: J'ai grandi dans une famille pauvre.
translations.pt: Eu cresci numa família pobre.

more.definition: A group of people who are closely related to one another (by blood, marriage or adoption); kin; in particular, a set of parents and their children; an immediate family.; A group of related animals, usually a mother and offspring, a mating pair or larger lineages in some species.; An extended family: a group of people who are related to one another by blood or marriage.
more.etymology: From Late Middle English famylye, from Latin familia (“a household”). Displaced native Old English hīred and hād. Doublet of familia.

examples.text: Mr. Yoshida never breaks his promise.

translations.de: Herr Yoshida bricht nie sein Versprechen.
translations.fr: M. Yoshida ne rompt jamais ses promesses.
translations.pt: O Sr. Yoshida nunca quebra as suas promessas.

examples.text: During summer breaks, I ate dinner at midnight.

translations.de: Während der Sommerferien habe ich um Mitternacht Abendessen gegessen.
translations.fr: Pendant les vacances d’été, je prenais mon dîner à minuit.
translations.pt: Durante as férias de verão, eu jantava à meia-noite.

examples.text: It really breaks my heart.

translations.de: Das bricht mir wirklich das Herz.
translations.fr: Ça me brise vraiment le cœur.
translations.pt: Isso realmente parte meu coração.

examples.text: A man who breaks his promises cannot be trusted.

translations.de: Einem Mann, der seine Versprechen bricht, kann man nicht trauen.
translations.fr: Un homme qui ne tient pas ses promesses n'est pas crédible.
translations.pt: Um homem que quebra a promessa não pode ser confiado.

more.definition: An instance of breaking something into two or more pieces.; A physical space that opens up in something or between two things.; An interruption of continuity; departure from or rupture with something.
more.etymology: From Middle English breken, from Old English brecan (“to break”), from Proto-West Germanic *brekan, from Proto-Germanic *brekaną (“to break”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰreg- (“to break”). Doublet of bray.

examples.text: I think I have a broken rib.

translations.de: Ich glaube, ich habe mir eine Rippe gebrochen.
translations.fr: Je crois que j'ai une côte cassée.
translations.pt: Eu acho que estou com uma costela quebrada.

examples.text: He's always breaking into our conversation.

translations.de: Er mischt sich immer in unser Gespräch ein.
translations.fr: Il se mêle toujours de notre conversation.
translations.pt: Ele está sempre se intrometendo em nossas conversas.

examples.text: She breaks a dish every time she washes dishes.

translations.de: Jedes Mal, wenn sie Geschirr spült, zerbricht sie ein Teil.
translations.fr: Elle casse une assiette chaque fois qu'elle fait la vaisselle.
translations.pt: Sempre que lava pratos, ela quebra algum.

examples.text: I think I've broken my arm.

translations.de: Ich glaube, ich habe mir den Arm gebrochen.
translations.fr: Je pense que je me suis cassé le bras.
translations.pt: Acho que quebrei o braço.

more.definition: To separate into two or more pieces, to fracture or crack, by a process that cannot easily be reversed for reassembly.; To crack or fracture (bone) under a physical strain.; To make the first shot; to scatter the balls from the initial neat arrangement.
more.etymology: From Middle English breken, from Old English brecan (“to break”), from Proto-West Germanic *brekan, from Proto-Germanic *brekaną (“to break”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰreg- (“to break”). Doublet of bray.

examples.text: I have a plan. Don't worry.

translations.de: Ich habe einen Plan. Mach dir keine Sorgen.
translations.fr: J'ai un plan. Ne t'en fais pas.
translations.pt: Tenho um plano. Não se preocupe.

examples.text: He worries about the result.

translations.de: Er sorgt sich um das Ergebnis.
translations.fr: Il se préoccupe du résultat.
translations.pt: Preocupa-se com o resultado.

examples.text: Don't you worry about a thing.

translations.de: Mache dir um nichts Sorgen!
translations.fr: Ne vous souciez de rien !
translations.pt: Não se preocupe com nada.

examples.text: I don't want you to worry.

translations.de: Ich will nicht, dass Sie sich sorgen.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas que tu te fasses de souci.
translations.pt: Não quero que você se preocupe.

more.definition: A strong feeling of anxiety.; An instance or cause of such a feeling.; A person who causes worry.
more.etymology: From Middle English worien (“to choke, strangle”), from Old English wyrġan, from Proto-West Germanic *wurgijan, from Proto-Germanic *wurgijaną, from Proto-Indo-European *werǵʰ- (“bind, squeeze”). Cognate with Dutch worgen, wurgen, German würgen.

examples.text: Where've you been? I was worried.

translations.de: Wo bist du gewesen? Ich habe mir Sorgen gemacht.
translations.fr: T'étais où ? J'étais inquiète.
translations.pt: Onde você estava? Fiquei preocupado.

examples.text: You don't need to worry anymore.

translations.de: Du musst dir keine Sorgen mehr machen.
translations.fr: Tu n'as plus besoin de t'en faire.
translations.pt: Não deves mais te preocupar.

examples.text: That's what's worrying me.

translations.de: Das ist was mich beunruhigt.
translations.fr: C'est ce qui me soucie.
translations.pt: Isso é o que está me preocupando.

examples.text: Don't worry. We're safe here.

translations.de: Keine Sorge! Hier sind wir sicher.
translations.fr: Ne t'en fais pas ! Nous sommes en sécurité, ici.
translations.pt: Não se preocupem. Estamos seguros aqui.

more.definition: To be troubled; to give way to mental anxiety or doubt.; Disturb the peace of mind of; afflict with mental agitation or distress; to exercise.; To harass; to irritate or distress.
more.etymology: From Middle English worien (“to choke, strangle”), from Old English wyrġan, from Proto-West Germanic *wurgijan, from Proto-Germanic *wurgijaną, from Proto-Indo-European *werǵʰ- (“bind, squeeze”). Cognate with Dutch worgen, wurgen, German würgen.

examples.text: You shouldn't leave the baby alone.

translations.de: Du solltest das Kind nicht allein lassen.
translations.fr: Tu ne devrais pas laisser le bébé seul.
translations.pt: Você não deveria deixar o bebê sozinho.

examples.text: Bringing up a baby is hard work.

translations.de: Ein Kind zu erziehen ist eine schwere Arbeit.
translations.fr: Élever un bébé est un travail difficile.
translations.pt: Criar um bebê é um trabalho difícil.

examples.text: We are going to have a baby.

translations.de: Wir bekommen ein Kind.
translations.fr: Nous allons avoir un bébé.
translations.pt: Nós vamos ter um bebê.

examples.text: Their daughter plays with the baby.

translations.de: Ihre Tochter spielt mit dem Baby.
translations.fr: Leur fille joue avec le bébé.
translations.pt: A filha deles brinca com o bebê.

more.definition: Picked when small and immature (as in baby corn, baby potatoes).; Newest (overall, or in some group or state); most inexperienced.; Like or pertaining to a baby, in size or youth; small, young.
more.etymology: Proto-Germanic *bō-redup. From Middle English baby, babie (“baby”), a diminutive form of babe (“babe, baby”), equivalent to babe + -y/-ie (“endearing and diminutive suffix”). Perhaps ultimately imitative of baby talk (compare babble).

examples.text: A baby flamingo's feathers are grey.

translations.de: Die Federn eines Flamingokükens sind grau.
translations.fr: Les plumes d'un bébé flamant sont grises.
translations.pt: As penas de um filhote de flamingo são cinzentas.

examples.text: They're sleeping like babies.

translations.de: Sie schlafen wie Babys.
translations.fr: Ils dorment comme des bébés.
translations.pt: Estão dormindo como bebês.

examples.text: The baby is sleeping in his crib.

translations.de: Das Kind schläft in der Wiege.
translations.fr: Le bébé dort dans son berceau.
translations.pt: O bebê está dormindo no berço.

examples.text: The baby seemed to be fast asleep.

translations.de: Das Baby schien tief und fest zu schlafen.
translations.fr: Le bébé semblait dormir à poings fermés.
translations.pt: O bebê parecia estar dormindo profundamente.

more.definition: A very young human, particularly from birth to a couple of years old or until walking is fully mastered.; A very young human, even if not yet born.; Any very young animal, especially a vertebrate; many species have specific names for their babies, such as kittens for the babies of cats, puppies for the babies of dogs, and chicks for the babies of birds. See :Category:Baby animals for more.
more.etymology: Proto-Germanic *bō-redup. From Middle English baby, babie (“baby”), a diminutive form of babe (“babe, baby”), equivalent to babe + -y/-ie (“endearing and diminutive suffix”). Perhaps ultimately imitative of baby talk (compare babble).

examples.text: Who will take care of the baby?

translations.de: Wer wird sich um das Baby kümmern?
translations.fr: Qui va s'occuper du bébé ?
translations.pt: Quem tomará conta do bebê?

examples.text: My wife had a baby last week.

translations.de: Meine Frau hat in der vergangenen Woche ein Kind bekommen.
translations.fr: Ma femme a eu un bébé la semaine dernière.
translations.pt: A minha mulher teve um filho na semana passada.

examples.text: The baby was sleeping in the cradle.

translations.de: Das Baby schlief in der Wiege.
translations.fr: Le bébé dormait dans le berceau.
translations.pt: O bebê estava dormindo no berço.

examples.text: A baby is sleeping in the cradle.

translations.de: Ein Baby schläft in der Wiege.
translations.fr: Un bébé dort dans le berceau.
translations.pt: Um bebê está dormindo no berço.

more.definition: To coddle; to pamper somebody like an infant.; To tend (something) with care; to be overly attentive to (something), fuss over.
more.etymology: Proto-Germanic *bō-redup. From Middle English baby, babie (“baby”), a diminutive form of babe (“babe, baby”), equivalent to babe + -y/-ie (“endearing and diminutive suffix”). Perhaps ultimately imitative of baby talk (compare babble).

examples.text: Entry to the operating room is prohibited.

translations.de: Das Betreten des Operationssaals ist untersagt.
translations.fr: L'accès à la salle d'opération est interdit.
translations.pt: A entrada na sala de cirurgia é proibida.

examples.text: I'm quite comfortable in this room.

translations.de: Ich fühle mich recht wohl in diesem Zimmer.
translations.fr: Je suis plutôt à l'aise dans cette pièce.
translations.pt: Estou muito cômodo neste quarto.

examples.text: Here's the key to your room.

translations.de: Hier ist der Schlüssel zu deinem Zimmer.
translations.fr: Voici la clé de ta chambre.
translations.pt: Aqui está a chave do seu quarto.

examples.text: My flat has a large living room.

translations.de: Meine Wohnung hat ein großes Wohnzimmer.
translations.fr: Mon appartement a une grande salle de séjour.
translations.pt: Meu apartamento tem uma sala de estar grande.

more.etymology: From Middle English roum, rom, rum, from Old English rūm (“roomy, spacious, ample, extensive, large, open, unencumbered, unoccupied, temporal, long, extended, great, liberal, unrestricted, unfettered, clear, loose, free from conditions, free from occupation, not restrained within due limits, lax, far-reaching, abundant, noble, august”), from Proto-Germanic *rūmaz (“roomy, spacious”), from Proto-Indo-European *rewh₁- …

examples.text: I want a room with a view.

translations.de: Ich will ein Zimmer mit Aussicht.
translations.fr: Je veux une chambre avec vue.
translations.pt: Quero um quarto com vista.

examples.text: What was she doing in his room?

translations.de: Was machte sie in seinem Zimmer?
translations.fr: Que faisait-elle dans sa chambre ?
translations.pt: O que ela estava fazendo no quarto dele?

examples.text: I have to book a hotel room.

translations.de: Ich muss ein Hotelzimmer buchen.
translations.fr: Je dois réserver une chambre d'hôtel.
translations.pt: Tenho que fazer uma reserva em um hotel.

examples.text: Mary is now studying in her room.

translations.de: Mary studiert gerade in ihrem Zimmer.
translations.fr: Marie étudie dans sa chambre.
translations.pt: Mary está estudando no quarto dela.

more.definition: Off from the wind.
more.etymology: From Middle English rome, from Old English rūme (“widely, spaciously, roomily, far and wide, so as to extend over a wide space, liberally, extensively, amply, abundantly, in a high degree, without restriction or encumbrance, without the pressure of care, light-heartedly, without obstruction, plainly, clearly, in detail”). Cognate with Dutch ruim (“amply”, adverb).

examples.text: I had my brother clean my room.

translations.de: Ich ließ meinen Bruder mein Zimmer sauber machen.
translations.fr: J'ai fait ranger ma chambre à mon frère.
translations.pt: Eu fiz meu irmão limpar meu quarto.

examples.text: Tom has a house with two rooms.

translations.de: Tom hat ein Haus mit zwei Zimmern.
translations.fr: Tom a une maison de deux chambres.
translations.pt: Tom tem uma casa de dois quartos.

examples.text: What are you doing in my room?

translations.de: Was machst du in meinem Zimmer?
translations.fr: Que fais-tu dans ma chambre ?
translations.pt: O que você está fazendo no meu quarto?

examples.text: This giant table occupies the entire room.

translations.de: Dieser riesige Tisch nimmt das ganze Zimmer ein.
translations.fr: Cette immense table occupe toute la pièce.
translations.pt: Esta mesa gigante ocupa a sala inteira.

more.definition: Space for something, or to carry out an activity.; Sufficient space for or to do something.; A space between the timbers of a ship's frame.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *(H)rewH-der. From Middle English roum (“room, space”), from Old English rūm (“room, space”), from Proto-West Germanic *rūm (“room”), from Proto-Germanic *rūmą (“room”), from Proto-Indo-European *(H)rewH- (“to root; to rip, tear”), from *Hrew- (“to tear out, open”).

examples.text: What're you doing in my room?

translations.de: Was machst du in meinem Zimmer?
translations.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu fais dans ma chambre ?
translations.pt: O que você está fazendo no meu quarto?

examples.text: I want a room with two beds.

translations.de: Ich hätte gern ein Zweibettzimmer.
translations.fr: Je désire une chambre à deux lits.
translations.pt: Eu quero um quarto com duas camas.

examples.text: Tom was sitting alone in his room.

translations.de: Tom saß allein auf seinem Zimmer.
translations.fr: Tom était assis seul dans sa chambre.
translations.pt: Tom estava sentado sozinho em seu quarto.

examples.text: She lit some candles in her room.

translations.de: Sie hat in ihrem Zimmer Kerzen angezündet.
translations.fr: Elle a allumé des bougies dans sa chambre.
translations.pt: Ele acendeu algumas velas no quarto.

more.definition: To reside, especially as a boarder or tenant.; To assign to a room; to allocate a room to.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *(H)rewH-der. From Middle English roum (“room, space”), from Old English rūm (“room, space”), from Proto-West Germanic *rūm (“room”), from Proto-Germanic *rūmą (“room”), from Proto-Indo-European *(H)rewH- (“to root; to rip, tear”), from *Hrew- (“to tear out, open”).

examples.text: I probably won't watch TV tonight.

translations.de: Ich werde heute Abend wahrscheinlich nicht fernsehen.
translations.fr: Je ne vais probablement pas regarder la télévision ce soir.
translations.pt: Eu provavelmente não assistirei à TV esta noite.

examples.text: I don't want to watch television.

translations.de: Ich will nicht fernsehen.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas regarder la télé.
translations.pt: Eu não quero assistir televisão.

examples.text: I found this watch at the station.

translations.de: Ich habe auf dem Bahnhof diese Uhr gefunden.
translations.fr: J’ai trouvé cette montre à la gare.
translations.pt: Achei este relógio na estação.

examples.text: He doesn't watch TV at all.

translations.de: Er guckt überhaupt kein Fernsehen.
translations.fr: Il ne regarde pas du tout la télé.
translations.pt: Ele nunca assiste televisão.

more.definition: A portable or wearable timepiece.; The act of guarding and observing someone or something.; A particular time period when guarding is kept.
more.etymology: As a noun, from Middle English wacche, from Old English wæċċe. See below for verb form.

examples.text: Last Sunday, we watched a soccer game.

translations.de: Letzten Sonntag haben wir ein Fußballspiel gesehen.
translations.fr: Dimanche dernier, nous avons regardé un match de football.
translations.pt: No domingo passado, assistimos a um jogo de futebol.

examples.text: Give me your wallet and your watch.

translations.de: Gib mir deinen Geldbeutel und deine Uhr!
translations.fr: File-moi ton portefeuille et ta montre.
translations.pt: Dê-me sua carteira e seu relógio.

examples.text: I'm watching the game on TV.

translations.de: Ich schaue das Spiel im Fernsehen.
translations.fr: Je regarde le match à la télé.
translations.pt: Estou assistindo ao jogo na tevê.

examples.text: My mother seldom watches TV at night.

translations.de: Meine Mutter sieht des Abends selten fern.
translations.fr: Ma mère regarde rarement la télévision le soir.
translations.pt: Minha mãe raramente assiste à TV à noite.

more.definition: To look at, see, or view for a period of time.; To observe over a period of time; to notice or pay attention.; To mind, attend, or guard.
more.etymology: From Middle English wacchen, from Old English wæċċan, from Proto-West Germanic *wakkjan, from Proto-Germanic *wakjaną. Cognate with Dutch wekken, German wecken, Danish vække, Norwegian Bokmål vekke, Norwegian Nynorsk vekkja, Swedish väcka, Faroese and Icelandic vekja.

examples.text: I am a duck. I speak English.

translations.de: Ich bin eine Ente. Ich spreche Englisch.
translations.fr: Je suis un canard. Je parle anglais.
translations.pt: Eu sou um pato. Eu falo inglês.

examples.text: Tom speaks French better than his classmates.

translations.de: Tom spricht besser Französisch als seine Klassenkameraden.
translations.fr: Tom parle mieux français que ses camarades de classe.
translations.pt: Tom fala francês melhor do que seus colegas de classe.

examples.text: It's not difficult to speak French.

translations.de: Es ist nicht schwer, Französisch zu sprechen.
translations.fr: Il n'est pas difficile de parler français.
translations.pt: Não é difícil falar francês.

examples.text: Tom knows Mary doesn't speak French.

translations.de: Tom weiß, dass Maria kein Französisch spricht.
translations.fr: Tom sait que Maria ne parle pas français.
translations.pt: Tom sabe que Maria não fala francês.

more.definition: Language, jargon, or terminology used uniquely in a particular environment or group.; Speech, conversation.; Clipping of speaker point.
more.etymology: From Middle English speke, speken (“to speak”), from Old English specan (“to speak”). This is usually taken to be an irregular alteration of earlier sprecan, spreocan (“to speak”), from Proto-West Germanic *sprekan, from Proto-Germanic *sprekaną (“to speak, make a sound”), from Proto-Indo-European *spreg- (“to make a sound, utter, speak”).

examples.text: I can speak neither French nor English.

translations.de: Ich kann weder Französisch noch Englisch.
translations.fr: Je ne parle ni français ni anglais.
translations.pt: Eu não falo nem francês nem inglês.

examples.text: When Tom spoke, they all remained silent.

translations.de: Wenn Tom sprach, schwiegen alle.
translations.fr: Quand Tom parla, ils restèrent tous silencieux.
translations.pt: Quando Tom falou, todos ficaram em silêncio.

examples.text: He speaks English with a Russian accent.

translations.de: Er spricht Englisch mit einem russischen Akzent.
translations.fr: Il parle anglais avec un accent russe.
translations.pt: Ele fala inglês com sotaque russo.

examples.text: It is not difficult to speak French.

translations.de: Es ist nicht schwer, Französisch zu sprechen.
translations.fr: Il n'est pas difficile de parler français.
translations.pt: Não é difícil falar francês.

more.definition: To communicate with one's voice, to say words out loud.; To have a conversation.; To communicate or converse by some means other than orally, such as writing or facial expressions.
more.etymology: From Middle English speke, speken (“to speak”), from Old English specan (“to speak”). This is usually taken to be an irregular alteration of earlier sprecan, spreocan (“to speak”), from Proto-West Germanic *sprekan, from Proto-Germanic *sprekaną (“to speak, make a sound”), from Proto-Indo-European *spreg- (“to make a sound, utter, speak”).

examples.text: In the end, they approved the proposal.

translations.de: Schließlich haben sie den Vorschlag angenommen.
translations.fr: Finalement, ils ont approuvé la proposition.
translations.pt: No final, eles aprovaram a proposta.

examples.text: The novel ends with the heroine's death.

translations.de: Der Roman endet mit dem Tod der Heldin.
translations.fr: Le roman se termine par la mort de l'héroïne.
translations.pt: A novela termina com a morte da heroína.

examples.text: Where is the end of this line?

translations.de: Wo ist das Ende dieser Linie?
translations.fr: Où est la fin de cette ligne ?
translations.pt: Onde é o fim dessa linha?

examples.text: That is somewhat explained at the end.

translations.de: Das ist am Ende einigermaßen erklärt.
translations.fr: C'est un peu expliqué à la fin.
translations.pt: Isso é mais ou menos explicado no fim.

more.definition: The terminal point of something in space or time.; Share of joint responsibility.; The cessation of an effort, activity, state, or motion.
more.etymology: From Middle English ende, from Old English ende, from Proto-West Germanic *andī, from Proto-Germanic *andijaz (“end”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂entíos (“forehead; front”), from *h₂ent- (“face; forehead; front”), from *h₂en- (“on, onto”).

examples.text: All good things come to an end.

translations.de: Alle guten Dinge müssen einmal enden.
translations.fr: Toutes les bonnes choses ont une fin.
translations.pt: Tudo o que é bom acaba.

examples.text: Most Hollywood movies have a happy ending.

translations.de: Die meisten Hollywoodfilme haben ein glückliches Ende.
translations.fr: La plupart des films hollywoodiens ont une fin heureuse.
translations.pt: A maioria dos filmes de Hollywood têm um final feliz.

examples.text: The game ended in a draw.

translations.de: Das Spiel endete unentschieden.
translations.fr: La rencontre s'est terminée par un match nul.
translations.pt: A partida resultou num empate.

examples.text: All's well that ends well.

translations.de: Ende gut, alles gut.
translations.fr: Tout est bien qui finit bien.
translations.pt: Bem está o que bem acaba.

more.definition: To come to an end.; To conclude; to bring something to an end.; To finish, terminate.
more.etymology: From Middle English ende, from Old English ende, from Proto-West Germanic *andī, from Proto-Germanic *andijaz (“end”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂entíos (“forehead; front”), from *h₂ent- (“face; forehead; front”), from *h₂en- (“on, onto”).

examples.text: The child has gloves and a scarf.

translations.de: Das Kind hat Handschuhe und ein Halstuch.
translations.fr: L'enfant a des gants et une écharpe.
translations.pt: A criança tem luvas e um cachecol.

examples.text: The children are playing in the park.

translations.de: Die Kinder spielen im Park.
translations.fr: Les enfants jouent dans le parc.
translations.pt: As crianças estão brincando no parque.

examples.text: The child doesn't want to sleep.

translations.de: Das Kind möchte nicht schlafen.
translations.fr: L'enfant ne veut pas dormir.
translations.pt: A criança não quer dormir.

examples.text: Tom wants his children to learn French.

translations.de: Tom will, dass seine Kinder Französisch lernen.
translations.fr: Tom veut que ses enfants apprennent le français.
translations.pt: Tom quer que os filhos aprendam francês.

examples.text: The child is playing in the park.

translations.de: Das Kind spielt im Park.
translations.fr: L'enfant joue dans le parc.
translations.pt: A criança está brincando no parque.

examples.text: The children are at school.

translations.de: Die Kinder sind in der Schule.
translations.fr: Les enfants sont à l'école.
translations.pt: As crianças estão na escola.

more.definition: A person who has not yet reached adulthood, whether natural (puberty), cultural (initiation), or legal (majority).; A youth aged 1 to 9 years, whereas neonates are aged 0 to 1 month, infants are aged 1 to 12 months, and adolescents are aged 10 to 20 years.; One's direct descendant by birth, regardless of age; one's offspring; a son or daughter.
collocations: only child — a child with no brothers or sisters
more.etymology: From Middle English child, from Old English ċild, from Proto-West Germanic *kilþ, *kelþ, from Proto-Germanic *kelþaz (“womb; fetus”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵelt- (“womb”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to ball up, amass”).

examples.text: I heard a knock at the door.

translations.de: Ich hörte ein Klopfen an der Tür.
translations.fr: J'ai entendu frapper à la porte.
translations.pt: Eu ouvi uma batida na porta.

examples.text: Almost all the doors were closed.

translations.de: Fast alle Türen waren geschlossen.
translations.fr: Presque toutes les portes étaient fermées.
translations.pt: Quase todas portas estavam fechadas.

examples.text: An ugly man knocked on my door.

translations.de: Ein hässlicher Mann klopfte an meiner Tür.
translations.fr: Un homme laid frappa à ma porte.
translations.pt: Um homem feio bateu na minha porta.

examples.text: Please lock the door when you leave.

translations.de: Bitte schließ die Tür ab, wenn du gehst.
translations.fr: Verrouille la porte lorsque tu pars.
translations.pt: Por favor, tranque a porta quando sair.

more.definition: A portal of entry into a building, room, or vehicle, typically consisting of a rigid plane movable on a hinge. It may have a handle to help open and close, a latch to hold it closed, and a lock that ensures it cannot be opened without a key.; A building with a door, especially a house.; Any flap, etc., that opens like a door.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *dʰwer-der. From Middle English dore, dor, from Old English duru (“door”), dor (“gate”), from Proto-West Germanic *dur, from Proto-Germanic *durz, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰwṓr, from *dʰwer- (“doorway, door, gate”).

examples.text: I forgot to lock the front door.

translations.de: Ich habe vergessen, die Haustür abzuschließen.
translations.fr: J'ai oublié de verrouiller la porte d'entrée.
translations.pt: Eu esqueci de trancar a porta da frente.

examples.text: They locked the doors and windows.

translations.de: Sie verschlossen die Türen und Fenster.
translations.fr: Ils ont verrouillé les portes et fenêtres.
translations.pt: Trancaram as portas e as janelas.

examples.text: This door is locked from the inside.

translations.de: Diese Tür ist von innen verschlossen.
translations.fr: Cette porte est verrouillée de l'intérieur.
translations.pt: Esta porta está trancada por dentro.

examples.text: The door of the office is yellow.

translations.de: Die Bürotür ist gelb.
translations.fr: La porte du bureau est jaune.
translations.pt: A porta do escritório é amarela.

examples.text: I hope I didn't offend anyone.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, ich habe niemanden beleidigt.
translations.fr: J'espère n'avoir offensé personne.
translations.pt: Espero não ter ofendido ninguém.

examples.text: Let's hope that common sense prevails.

translations.de: Hoffen wir, dass die Vernunft obsiegt.
translations.fr: Espérons que le bon sens l'emporte.
translations.pt: Vamos esperar que o senso comum prevaleça.

examples.text: I hope that I can do it.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, dass ich das kann.
translations.fr: J'espère pouvoir le faire.
translations.pt: Espero que eu possa fazer isso.

examples.text: I hope this isn't a mistake.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, dass das kein Fehler ist.
translations.fr: J'espère que ce n'est pas une erreur.
translations.pt: Espero que isto não seja um erro.

more.definition: The feeling of trust, confidence, belief or expectation that something wished for can or will happen.; The actual thing wished for.; A person or thing that is a source of hope.
more.etymology: Proto-West Germanic *tōhopōnder. From Middle English hope, from Old English hopa (“hope, expectation”), from the same source as the verb hope. Eclipsed non-native early modern English esperance, borrowed from Middle French esperance.

examples.text: I hope you'll answer me soon.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, dass ihr mir bald antworten werdet.
translations.fr: J'espère que vous me répondrez bientôt.
translations.pt: Espero que você me responda logo.

examples.text: I had hoped we might become friends.

translations.de: Ich hatte gehofft, wir könnten Freunde werden.
translations.fr: J'avais espéré que nous pourrions devenir amis.
translations.pt: Eu esperava que pudéssemos nos tornar amigos.

examples.text: I was hoping you'd say that.

translations.de: Ich hoffte, Sie würden das sagen.
translations.fr: J'espérais que tu dirais ça.
translations.pt: Eu estava esperando que você dissesse isso.

examples.text: I hope that nobody steals my stuff.

translations.de: Hoffentlich klaut mir niemand mein Zeug.
translations.fr: J'espère que personne ne me volera mes affaires.
translations.pt: Espero que ninguém roube minhas coisas.

more.definition: To want (something) to happen, with a sense of expectation that it might [with that (+ clause); or (informal) with clause; or with so or (negative) not].; To intend to do something and look forward to the prospect of having done it [with to (+ infinitive)].; To expect optimistically that one might get something (either a change in circumstance or an object) [with for].
more.etymology: From Middle English hopen, from Old English hopian (“hope”), from Proto-West Germanic *hopōn; further etymology unclear.

examples.text: Don't forget to send the letter.

translations.de: Vergiss nicht, den Brief zu versenden.
translations.fr: N'oublie pas de poster la lettre.
translations.pt: Não se esqueça de enviar a carta.

examples.text: Tom keeps every letter his mother sends him.

translations.de: Tom bewahrt jeden Brief auf, den ihm seine Mutter schickt.
translations.fr: Tom garde chaque lettre que lui envoie sa mère.
translations.pt: Tom guarda todas as cartas que lhe manda a mãe.

examples.text: Please send me a picture of yourself.

translations.de: Bitte schicke mir ein Bild von dir.
translations.fr: Veuillez m'envoyer une photo de vous.
translations.pt: Me manda uma foto sua, por favor.

examples.text: The smile you send out returns to you.

translations.de: Das Lächeln, das du aussendest, kehrt zu dir zurück.
translations.fr: Le sourire que tu envoies revient vers toi.
translations.pt: O sorriso que envias retorna a ti.

more.definition: An operation in which data is transmitted.; An icon (usually on a computer screen and labeled with the word "Send") on which one clicks (with a mouse or its equivalent) or taps to transmit an email or other electronic message.; A messenger, especially one sent to fetch the bride.
more.etymology: From Middle English senden, from Old English sendan (“to send, cause to go”), from Proto-West Germanic *sandijan, from Proto-Germanic *sandijaną, from Proto-Indo-European *sont-eye-ti (“to cause to go”), causative of *sent- (“to walk, travel”). The noun derives from the verb.

examples.text: I shouldn't have sent that email.

translations.de: Ich hätte diese Mail nicht abschicken sollen.
translations.fr: Je n'aurais pas dû envoyer ce courriel.
translations.pt: Eu não devia ter mandado aquele e-mail.

examples.text: Reread your email before sending it.

translations.de: Lies dir die Netznachricht vor dem Versenden noch einmal durch.
translations.fr: Relis ton courriel avant de l'envoyer.
translations.pt: Releia seu e-mail antes de enviá-lo.

examples.text: Can you send me a screenshot?

translations.de: Kannst du mir einen Bildschirmausdruck senden?
translations.fr: Peux-tu m'envoyer une capture d'écran ?
translations.pt: Você pode me enviar um print?

examples.text: My brother sends you his regards.

translations.de: Schönen Gruß von meinem Bruder.
translations.fr: Mon frère vous envoie ses amitiés.
translations.pt: Meu irmão manda lembranças.

more.definition: To make something (such as an object or message) go from one place to another (or to someone).; To get one going; move to excitement or rapture; to delight or thrill.; To amuse greatly or otherwise stun by absurdity.
more.etymology: From Middle English senden, from Old English sendan (“to send, cause to go”), from Proto-West Germanic *sandijan, from Proto-Germanic *sandijaną, from Proto-Indo-European *sont-eye-ti (“to cause to go”), causative of *sent- (“to walk, travel”). The noun derives from the verb.

examples.text: I haven't actually slept with him.

translations.fr: Je n'ai pas réellement couché avec lui.
translations.pt: Eu, na verdade, não dormi com ele.

examples.text: I actually don't work here.

translations.de: Eigentlich arbeite ich hier nicht.
translations.fr: Je ne travaille en fait pas ici.
translations.pt: Na verdade, eu não trabalho aqui.

examples.text: He isn't actually the manager.

translations.de: Eigentlich ist er gar nicht der Manager.
translations.fr: Il n'est pas vraiment le gérant.

examples.text: Did you actually see the accident?

translations.de: Hast du den Unfall tatsächlich gesehen?
translations.fr: Avez-vous réellement vu l'accident ?
translations.pt: Você realmente viu o acidente?

more.definition: In act or in fact; really; in truth; positively.; Currently; at the time.
more.etymology: From Middle English actually, actuelly, equivalent to actual + -ly.

examples.text: Juggling is actually a lot easier than it looks.

translations.de: Jonglieren ist in Wirklichkeit bei weitem einfacher, als es aussieht.
translations.fr: Jongler est en fait beaucoup plus facile que cela en a l'air.
translations.pt: Na verdade, malabarismo é muito mais fácil do que parece.

examples.text: We actually saw the accident.

translations.de: Wir haben den Unfall tatsächlich gesehen.
translations.fr: Nous avons réellement vu l'accident.
translations.pt: Nós realmente vimos o acidente.

examples.text: You're actually right.

translations.de: Du hast tatsächlich Recht.
translations.fr: En fait, tu as raison.
translations.pt: Na verdade você tem razão.

examples.text: I actually enjoyed that.

translations.de: Ich habe es in der Tat genossen.
translations.fr: J'y ai vraiment pris plaisir.
translations.pt: Eu gostei disso.

more.definition: Indicating affirmation, agreement.
more.etymology: A calque of Tagalog talaga.

examples.text: She spoke to him about the matter.

translations.de: Sie sprach mit ihm über die Angelegenheit.
translations.fr: Elle lui a parlé de l'affaire.
translations.pt: Ela falou com ele sobre o assunto.

examples.text: Isn't that what really matters?

translations.de: Ist es nicht eigentlich das, was wirklich wichtig ist?
translations.fr: N'est-ce pas là l'essentiel ?
translations.pt: Não é isso o que realmente importa?

examples.text: I spoke with him about the matter.

translations.de: Ich habe mit ihm über die Sache geredet.
translations.fr: Je me suis entretenu avec lui à ce sujet.
translations.pt: Eu falei com ele sobre o assunto.

examples.text: This is a matter of supreme importance.

translations.de: Das ist eine Sache von höchster Bedeutung.
translations.fr: C'est là une question d'une importance cruciale.
translations.pt: Esta é uma questão de suma importância.

more.definition: Anything with mass and volume.; Matter made up of normal particles, not antiparticles.; A kind of substance.
more.etymology: Ancient Greek ὕλη (húlē)sl. Latin māteriader. Anglo-Norman materebor. From Middle English matere, mater, from Anglo-Norman matere, materie, from Old French materie, matiere, from Latin māteria (“wood”), from māter (“mother”), in which case cognate with Old Armenian մայր (mayr, “cedar”) and մայրի (mayri, “forest”). Doublet of Madeira, mata, mater, matrix, and mother.

examples.text: All that matters is to be happy.

translations.de: Alles was zählt, ist glücklich zu sein.
translations.fr: Tout ce qui compte c'est d'être heureux.
translations.pt: Tudo o que importa é ser feliz.

examples.text: I guess it doesn't matter anymore.

translations.de: Ich glaube, es spielt keine Rolle mehr.
translations.fr: Je suppose que ça n'a plus d'importance.
translations.pt: Acho que não importa mais.

examples.text: It wouldn't have mattered anyway.

translations.de: Es hätte sowieso keine Rolle gespielt.
translations.fr: De toute façon, ça n'aurait rien changé.
translations.pt: De qualquer forma, isso não teria mudado nada.

examples.text: It's only a matter of time.

translations.de: Es ist nur eine Frage der Zeit.
translations.fr: Ce n'est qu'une question de temps.
translations.pt: É só uma questão de tempo.

more.definition: To be important.; To care about, to mind; to find important.
more.etymology: Ancient Greek ὕλη (húlē)sl. Latin māteriader. Anglo-Norman materebor. From Middle English matere, mater, from Anglo-Norman matere, materie, from Old French materie, matiere, from Latin māteria (“wood”), from māter (“mother”), in which case cognate with Old Armenian մայր (mayr, “cedar”) and մայրի (mayri, “forest”). examples.text: Doesn't it seem strange to you?

translations.de: Kommt es dir nicht komisch vor?
translations.fr: Ça ne te paraît-il pas étrange ?
translations.pt: Isso não parece estranho para você?

examples.text: It seems that he's a student.

translations.de: Anscheinend ist er ein Schüler.
translations.fr: Il semble être étudiant.
translations.pt: Parece que ele é um estudante.

examples.text: Tom seemed to be worried about Mary.

translations.de: Tom schien um Maria besorgt zu sein.
translations.fr: Tom semblait inquiet pour Marie.
translations.pt: Tom parecia estar preocupado com a Mary.

examples.text: You seem to be in a hurry.

translations.de: Du scheinst es eilig zu haben.
translations.fr: Tu as l'air d'être pressée.
translations.pt: Você parece estar com pressa.

more.definition: To appear; to look outwardly; to be perceived as.
more.etymology: From Middle English semen (“to seem, befit, be becoming”), from Old Norse sœma (“to conform to, beseem, befit”), from Proto-Germanic *sōmijaną (“to unite, fit”), from Proto-Indo-European *sem- (“one; whole”). Cognate with Scots seme (“to be fitting; beseem”), Danish sømme (“to beseem”), Old Swedish søma, Faroese søma (“to be proper”).

examples.text: Carol studies very hard. So does Henry.

translations.de: Carol studiert sehr hart. Henry auch.
translations.fr: Carole étudie très fort. Henri aussi.
translations.pt: Carol estuda bastante. Henry também.

examples.text: It's a lot harder than it looks.

translations.de: Das ist viel schwerer, als es aussieht.
translations.fr: C'est beaucoup plus difficile qu'il n'y paraît.
translations.pt: É muito mais difícil do que parece.

examples.text: All the boys in class worked hard.

translations.de: Alle Jungen in der Klasse haben hart gearbeitet.
translations.fr: Tous les garçons de la classe ont travaillé dur.
translations.pt: Todos os meninos na classe trabalharam duro.

examples.text: This city is hard to live in.

translations.de: Es ist schwer, in dieser Stadt zu leben.
translations.fr: Il est difficile de vivre dans cette ville.
translations.pt: Essa cidade é difícil de se viver.

more.definition: Solid and firm.; Resistant to pressure; difficult to break, cut, or penetrate.; Strong.
more.etymology: From Middle English hard, from Old English heard, from Proto-West Germanic *hard(ī), from Proto-Germanic *harduz, from Proto-Indo-European *kort-ús, from *kret- (“strong, powerful”).

examples.text: French is pretty hard, isn't it?

translations.de: Französisch ist recht schwer, oder?
translations.fr: Le français est plutôt difficile, n'est-ce pas ?
translations.pt: Francês é bem difícil, não?

examples.text: Life is hard, but I am harder.

translations.de: Das Leben ist hart, aber ich bin härter.
translations.fr: La vie est dure, mais je suis encore plus dur.
translations.pt: A vida é dura, mas eu sou mais duro.

examples.text: I know it's hard to believe.

translations.de: Ich weiß, dass es kaum zu glauben ist.
translations.fr: Je sais que c'est difficile à croire.
translations.pt: Eu sei que é difícil acreditar.

examples.text: Don't be too hard on yourself.

translations.de: Sei nicht zu hart zu dir selbst.
translations.fr: Ne sois pas trop dur avec toi-même.
translations.pt: Não seja muito duro consigo mesmo.

more.definition: With much force or effort.; With difficulty.; Compactly.
more.etymology: From Middle English hard, from Old English heard, from Proto-West Germanic *hard(ī), from Proto-Germanic *harduz, from Proto-Indo-European *kort-ús, from *kret- (“strong, powerful”).

examples.text: It's hard to understand his ideas.

translations.de: Es ist schwer, seine Gedanken zu verstehen.
translations.fr: Il est difficile de comprendre ses idées.
translations.pt: É difícil entender as suas ideias.

examples.text: Don't be so hard on yourself.

translations.de: Sei nicht so streng zu dir!
translations.fr: Ne sois pas si dur avec toi-même.
translations.pt: Não seja rigoroso demais consigo mesmo!

examples.text: Nickel is a hard, bright silver metal.

translations.de: Nickel ist ein hartes, hell silbernes Metall.
translations.fr: Le nickel est un métal dur, d'une lueur argentée.
translations.pt: O níquel é um metal duro, brilhante e prata.

examples.text: English is pretty hard, isn't it?

translations.de: Englisch ist ziemlich schwierig, oder?

more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English yet, yit, from Old English ġīet, gȳta, from Proto-West Germanic *jūta, from Proto-Germanic *juta (compare West Frisian jit, jitte (“yet”), Dutch ooit (“ever”), German jetzt (“now”)), compound of (1) *ju (“already”, adverb), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂yew-, accusative of *h₂óyu (“long time”) and (2) the Proto-Germanic *ta (“to, towards”), from Proto-Indo-European *do.

examples.text: I haven't downloaded the file yet.

translations.de: Ich habe die Datei noch nicht heruntergeladen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas encore téléchargé le fichier.
translations.pt: Eu ainda não baixei o arquivo.

examples.text: The boss doesn't know it yet.

translations.de: Der Chef weiß es noch nicht.
translations.fr: Le patron ne le sait pas encore.
translations.pt: O chefe ainda não sabe.

examples.text: Why haven't you cooked dinner yet?

translations.de: Warum hast du das Abendessen noch nicht zubereitet?
translations.fr: Pourquoi n'as-tu pas encore préparé le dîner ?
translations.pt: Por que você ainda não preparou o jantar?

examples.text: Tom doesn't know the truth yet.

translations.de: Tom weiß noch nicht die Wahrheit.
translations.fr: Tom ne sait pas encore la vérité.
translations.pt: O Tom ainda não sabe da verdade.

more.definition: Nevertheless; however; but; despite that.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English yet, yit, from Old English ġīet, gȳta, from Proto-West Germanic *jūta, from Proto-Germanic *juta (compare West Frisian jit, jitte (“yet”), Dutch ooit (“ever”), German jetzt (“now”)), compound of (1) *ju (“already”, adverb), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂yew-, accusative of *h₂óyu (“long time”) and (2) the Proto-Germanic *ta (“to, towards”), from Proto-Indo-European *do.

examples.text: Have you finished your French homework yet?

translations.de: Hast du deine Französisch-Hausaufgaben schon fertig?
translations.fr: As-tu déjà terminé tes devoirs de français ?
translations.pt: Você já terminou a sua tarefa de francês?

examples.text: I haven't downloaded the files yet.

translations.de: Ich habe die Dateien noch nicht heruntergeladen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas encore téléchargé les fichiers.
translations.pt: Eu ainda não baixei os arquivos.

examples.text: I can't tell you that yet.

translations.de: Ich kann es Ihnen noch nicht sagen.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas encore vous le dire.
translations.pt: Eu não posso te dizer isso ainda.

examples.text: Have you bought your Christmas gifts yet?

translations.de: Hast du schon Weihnachtsgeschenke besorgt?
translations.fr: As-tu déjà acheté tes cadeaux de Noël ?
translations.pt: Você já comprou seus presentes de Natal?

more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English yeten, from Old English ġēotan (“to flow, pour”), from Proto-West Germanic *geutan, from Proto-Germanic *geutaną (“to flow, pour”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰewd- (“to pour”). Cognate with Scots yat (“to pour, yet”), West Frisian jitte (“to scatter, shed, pour”), Dutch gieten (“to pour, cast, mould”), German gießen (“to pour, cast, mould”), Swedish gjuta (“to pour, cast”).

examples.text: I haven't watched that video yet.

translations.de: Ich habe mir das Video noch nicht angeschaut.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas encore regardé cette vidéo.
translations.pt: Eu ainda não assisti a esse vídeo.

examples.text: Tom hasn't read the book yet.

translations.de: Tom hat das Buch noch nicht gelesen.
translations.fr: Tom n'a pas encore lu le livre.
translations.pt: Tom ainda não leu o livro.

examples.text: The body hasn't yet been identified.

translations.de: Die Leiche ist noch nicht identifiziert worden.
translations.fr: Le corps n'a pas encore été identifié.
translations.pt: O corpo ainda não foi identificado.

examples.text: Haven't you washed the dishes yet?

translations.de: Hast du das Geschirr noch nicht gespült?
translations.fr: Tu n'as pas encore fait la vaisselle ?
translations.pt: Você ainda não lavou os pratos?

more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English yeten, from Old English ġēotan (“to flow, pour”), from Proto-West Germanic *geutan, from Proto-Germanic *geutaną (“to flow, pour”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰewd- (“to pour”). Cognate with Scots yat (“to pour, yet”), West Frisian jitte (“to scatter, shed, pour”), Dutch gieten (“to pour, cast, mould”), German gießen (“to pour, cast, mould”), Swedish gjuta (“to pour, cast”).

examples.text: I spent the whole day thinking about Tom.

translations.de: Ich dachte den ganzen Tag an Tom.
translations.fr: J'ai passé la journée entière à penser à Tom.
translations.pt: Eu passei o dia todo pensando em Tom.

examples.text: He made up the whole story.

translations.de: Er hat sich die ganze Geschichte ausgedacht.
translations.fr: Il a fabriqué toute cette histoire.
translations.pt: Ele inventou a história inteira.

examples.text: Did you read the whole book?

translations.de: Hast du das ganze Buch gelesen?
translations.fr: Aviez-vous lu le livre en entier ?
translations.pt: Você lera o livro inteiro?

examples.text: The storm destroyed the whole town.

translations.de: Der Sturm zerstörte die ganze Stadt.
translations.fr: La tempête a détruit toute la ville.
translations.pt: A tempestade destruiu toda a cidade.

more.definition: Entire, undivided.; Used as an intensifier.; Sound, uninjured, healthy.
more.etymology: From Middle English whol, hol, hole (“healthy, unhurt, whole”), from Old English hāl (“healthy, safe”), from Proto-West Germanic *hail, from Proto-Germanic *hailaz (“whole, safe, sound”), from Proto-Indo-European *kéh₂ilos (“healthy, whole”). The spelling with wh-, attested since ca. 1400, represents an excrescent /w/, which developed in words with initial /(h)ɔː/, /(h)oː/ in southwestern dialects of Middle English.

examples.text: She is the joy of the whole family.

translations.de: Sie ist die Freude der ganzen Familie.
translations.fr: Elle fait la joie de toute la famille.
translations.pt: Ela é a alegria de toda a família.

examples.text: I spent the whole day cleaning my room.

translations.de: Ich habe den ganzen Tag mein Zimmer aufgeräumt.
translations.fr: J'ai passé toute la journée à nettoyer ma chambre.
translations.pt: Eu passei o dia limpando o meu quarto.

examples.text: The rain lasted the whole night.

translations.de: Der Regen währte die ganze Nacht.
translations.fr: La pluie a duré toute la nuit.
translations.pt: A chuva durou a noite toda.

examples.text: We have waited for you the whole day.

translations.de: Wir warten schon den ganzen Tag auf dich.
translations.fr: Nous vous avons attendu toute la journée.
translations.pt: Nós esperamos por você o dia todo.

more.definition: In entirety; entirely; wholly.
more.etymology: From Middle English whol, hol, hole (“healthy, unhurt, whole”), from Old English hāl (“healthy, safe”), from Proto-West Germanic *hail, from Proto-Germanic *hailaz (“whole, safe, sound”), from Proto-Indo-European *kéh₂ilos (“healthy, whole”). The spelling with wh-, attested since ca. 1400, represents an excrescent /w/, which developed in words with initial /(h)ɔː/, /(h)oː/ in southwestern dialects of Middle English.

examples.text: The whole family was sick in bed.

translations.de: Die ganze Familie lag krank im Bett.
translations.fr: Toute la famille était malade au lit.
translations.pt: Toda a família estava doente de cama.

examples.text: The whole class laughed at his joke.

translations.de: Die ganze Klasse lachte über seinen Witz.
translations.fr: Toute la classe a ri de sa blague.
translations.pt: A turma toda riu da piada dele.

examples.text: The whole country was covered with snow.

translations.de: Das ganze Land war schneebedeckt.
translations.fr: Le pays en entier était couvert de neige.
translations.pt: O país todo estava coberto de neve.

examples.text: On the whole, the Japanese are conservative.

translations.de: Japaner sind im Allgemeinen konservativ.
translations.fr: Dans l'ensemble, les Japonais sont plutôt conservateurs.
translations.pt: Em geral, os japoneses são conservadores.

more.definition: Something complete, without any parts missing.; An entirety.
more.etymology: From Middle English whol, hol, hole (“healthy, unhurt, whole”), from Old English hāl (“healthy, safe”), from Proto-West Germanic *hail, from Proto-Germanic *hailaz (“whole, safe, sound”), from Proto-Indo-European *kéh₂ilos (“healthy, whole”). The spelling with wh-, attested since ca. 1400, represents an excrescent /w/, which developed in words with initial /(h)ɔː/, /(h)oː/ in southwestern dialects of Middle English.

examples.text: I won't be back for a while.

translations.de: Ich werde eine Zeit lang nicht da sein.
translations.fr: Je ne reviendrai pas avant un moment.
translations.pt: Eu não voltarei por um tempo.

examples.text: I fell asleep while I was watching TV.

translations.de: Ich bin beim Fernsehen eingeschlafen.
translations.fr: Je me suis endormie en regardant la télé.
translations.pt: Adormeci enquanto via televisão.

examples.text: You should get out once in a while.

translations.de: Du solltest ab und an mal nach draußen gehen.
translations.fr: Tu devrais sortir de temps en temps.
translations.pt: Você deveria sair de vez em quando.

examples.text: Let's play cards a while.

translations.de: Lass uns etwas Karten spielen!
translations.fr: Jouons un peu aux cartes.
translations.pt: Vamos jogar cartas por enquanto.

more.definition: During the same time that.; Although.; Until.
more.etymology: From Middle English whyle, from Old English hwīl, from Proto-West Germanic *hwīlu, from Proto-Germanic *hwīlō (compare Dutch wijl, Low German Wiel, German Weile, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål hvile (“rest”), Norwegian Nynorsk kvila (“rest”), Swedish vila (“rest”), Faroese and Icelandic hvíla (“rest”)) from Proto-Indo-European *kʷyeh₁- (“to rest”).

examples.text: I fell asleep while reading a book.

translations.de: Ich schlief beim Lesen eines Buches ein.
translations.fr: Je me suis endormi en lisant un livre.
translations.pt: Adormeci enquanto lia um livro.

examples.text: He wrote a book while in China.

translations.de: Als er in China war, schrieb er ein Buch.
translations.fr: En Chine il a écrit un livre.
translations.pt: Ele escreveu um livro na China.

examples.text: He drowned while swimming in the river.

translations.de: Er ertrank beim Schwimmen im Fluss.
translations.fr: Il s'est noyé en nageant dans la rivière.
translations.pt: Ele afogou-se enquanto nadava no rio.

examples.text: He came back home a while ago.

translations.de: Er kam vor einer Weile nach Hause zurück.
translations.fr: Il est rentré chez lui il y a un moment.
translations.pt: Ele voltou para casa há alguns instantes.

more.definition: An uncertain duration of time, a period of time.; An uncertain long period of time; An uncertain short moment.
more.etymology: From Middle English whyle, from Old English hwīl, from Proto-West Germanic *hwīlu, from Proto-Germanic *hwīlō (compare Dutch wijl, Low German Wiel, German Weile, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål hvile (“rest”), Norwegian Nynorsk kvila (“rest”), Swedish vila (“rest”), Faroese and Icelandic hvíla (“rest”)) from Proto-Indo-European *kʷyeh₁- (“to rest”).

examples.text: We go fishing once in a while.

translations.de: Wir gehen hin und wieder angeln.
translations.fr: Nous allons pêcher occasionnellement.
translations.pt: Vamos pescar de vez em quando.

examples.text: I like to sing while taking a shower.

translations.de: Ich singe gerne beim Duschen.
translations.fr: J'aime chanter en prenant une douche.
translations.pt: Eu gosto de cantar enquanto tomo banho.

examples.text: It is difficult to remain aware while dreaming.

translations.de: Es ist schwierig, während des Träumens bei Bewusstsein zu bleiben.
translations.fr: Il est difficile de rester conscient en rêvant.
translations.pt: É difícil permanecer consciente durante o sonho.

examples.text: She left a little while ago.

translations.de: Sie ist vor einiger Zeit gegangen.
translations.fr: Elle est partie il y a peu de temps.
translations.pt: Ela saiu há pouco.

more.definition: Until.
more.etymology: From Middle English whyle, from Old English hwīl, from Proto-West Germanic *hwīlu, from Proto-Germanic *hwīlō (compare Dutch wijl, Low German Wiel, German Weile, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål hvile (“rest”), Norwegian Nynorsk kvila (“rest”), Swedish vila (“rest”), Faroese and Icelandic hvíla (“rest”)) from Proto-Indo-European *kʷyeh₁- (“to rest”).

examples.text: I watch birds while walking in the forest.

translations.de: Beim Waldspaziergang beobachte ich Vögel.
translations.fr: J'observe les oiseaux en marchant dans la forêt.
translations.pt: Observo os pássaros enquanto ando pela floresta.

examples.text: He had a problem while parking.

translations.de: Er hatte ein Problem beim Parken.
translations.fr: Il a eu un problème en se garant.
translations.pt: Ele teve um problema ao estacionar.

examples.text: My wallet was stolen while I was asleep.

translations.de: Mein Portemonnaie wurde mir im Schlaf gestohlen.
translations.fr: Mon portefeuille a été volé pendant que je dormais.
translations.pt: Minha carteira foi roubada enquanto eu estava dormindo.

examples.text: He wrote a letter while listening to music.

translations.de: Er schrieb einen Brief während er Musik hörte.
translations.fr: Il a écrit une lettre en écoutant de la musique.
translations.pt: Ele escreveu uma carta enquanto escutava música.

more.definition: To pass (time) idly.; To occupy or entertain (someone) in order to let time pass.
more.etymology: From Middle English whyle, from Old English hwīl, from Proto-West Germanic *hwīlu, from Proto-Germanic *hwīlō (compare Dutch wijl, Low German Wiel, German Weile, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål hvile (“rest”), Norwegian Nynorsk kvila (“rest”), Swedish vila (“rest”), Faroese and Icelandic hvíla (“rest”)) from Proto-Indo-European *kʷyeh₁- (“to rest”).

examples.text: She has been sick since last week.

translations.de: Sie ist seit voriger Woche krank.
translations.fr: Elle est malade depuis la semaine dernière.
translations.pt: Ela está doente desde a semana passada.

examples.text: Ten years have passed since he died.

translations.de: Seit er starb, sind zehn Jahre vergangen.
translations.fr: Dix ans ont passé depuis qu'il est mort.
translations.pt: Dez anos se passaram desde a sua morte.

examples.text: It has been raining since last Sunday.

translations.de: Es regnet seit letztem Sonntag.
translations.fr: Il pleut depuis dimanche dernier.
translations.pt: Está chovendo desde domingo.

examples.text: Two years have passed since we parted.

translations.de: Zwei Jahre sind seit unserer Trennung vergangen.
translations.fr: Deux ans ont passé depuis que nous nous sommes séparés.
translations.pt: Dois anos se passaram desde que nos separamos.

more.definition: From a specified time in the past.
more.etymology: From Middle English syns, synnes, contraction of earlier sithens, sithence, from sithen (“after, since”) ( + -s, adverbial genitive suffix), from Old English sīþþan, from the phrase sīþ þǣm (“after/since that (time)”), from sīþ (“since, after”) + þǣm dative singular of þæt. Cognate with Dutch sinds (“since”), German seit (“since”), Danish siden (“since”), Icelandic síðan (“since”) Scots syne (“since”).

examples.text: I haven't eaten anything since yesterday morning.

translations.de: Seit gestern Morgen habe ich nichts gegessen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai rien mangé depuis hier matin.
translations.pt: Não comi nada desde ontem de manhã.

examples.text: I haven't seen him since.

translations.de: Ich habe ihn seither nicht gesehen.
translations.fr: Je ne l'ai pas vu depuis.
translations.pt: Não o tenho visto de lá para cá.

examples.text: I haven't done this since high school.

translations.de: Das habe ich schon seit meiner Schulzeit nicht mehr gemacht.
translations.fr: Je n'ai plus fait ça depuis le lycée.
translations.pt: Eu não fiz isso desde o ensino médio.

examples.text: Ten years have gone by since her death.

translations.de: Zehn Jahre sind seit ihrem Tod vergangen.
translations.fr: Dix ans ont passé depuis son décès.
translations.pt: Dez anos se passaram desde a sua morte.

more.definition: From the time that.; Because.
more.etymology: From Middle English syns, synnes, contraction of earlier sithens, sithence, from sithen (“after, since”) ( + -s, adverbial genitive suffix), from Old English sīþþan, from the phrase sīþ þǣm (“after/since that (time)”), from sīþ (“since, after”) + þǣm dative singular of þæt. Cognate with Dutch sinds (“since”), German seit (“since”), Danish siden (“since”), Icelandic síðan (“since”) Scots syne (“since”).

examples.text: It's been raining since last night.

translations.de: Es regnet schon seit gestern Abend.
translations.fr: Il pleut depuis la nuit dernière.
translations.pt: Está chovendo desde ontem à noite.

examples.text: Nothing has changed since the dawn of humanity.

translations.de: Seit Anfang der Menschheit hat sich nichts geändert.
translations.fr: Rien n'a changé depuis le début de l'humanité.
translations.pt: Nada mudou desde o início da humanidade.

examples.text: I've been working since six this morning.

translations.de: Ich arbeite seit 6:00 Uhr morgens.
translations.fr: Je travaille depuis six heures ce matin.
translations.pt: Eu estive trabalhando desde às seis essa manhã.

examples.text: I haven't done that since last year.

translations.de: Das habe ich seit letztem Jahr nicht mehr getan.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas fait ça depuis l'année dernière.
translations.pt: Tenho feito isso desde o ano passado.

more.definition: Continuously during that period of time.; At certain points during that period of time.
more.etymology: From Middle English syns, synnes, contraction of earlier sithens, sithence, from sithen (“after, since”) ( + -s, adverbial genitive suffix), from Old English sīþþan, from the phrase sīþ þǣm (“after/since that (time)”), from sīþ (“since, after”) + þǣm dative singular of þæt. Cognate with Dutch sinds (“since”), German seit (“since”), Danish siden (“since”), Icelandic síðan (“since”) Scots syne (“since”).

examples.text: I don't have a cell phone.

translations.de: Ich habe kein Mobiltelefon.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas de portable.
translations.pt: Eu não tenho celular.

examples.text: How many phones does she have?

translations.de: Wie viele Telefonnummern hat sie?
translations.fr: Combien de téléphones a-t-elle ?
translations.pt: Quantos telefones ela tem?

examples.text: I need to make a phone call.

translations.de: Ich muss einen Anruf tätigen.
translations.fr: Je dois passer un coup de téléphone.
translations.pt: Eu preciso fazer uma ligação.

examples.text: He asked me for my phone number.

translations.de: Er fragte mich nach meiner Telefonnummer.
translations.fr: Il m'a demandé mon numéro de téléphone.
translations.pt: Ele pediu meu número de telefone.

more.definition: A device for transmitting conversations and other sounds in real time across distances, now often a small portable unit also capable of running software etc.; A person's telephone number (as a means of contact); digits.; A speech segment that possesses distinct physical or perceptual properties, considered as a physical event without regard to its place in the phonology of a language.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *kʷelh₁-der. Ancient Greek τῆλε (têle)lbor. Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂-der. Ancient Greek φωνή (phōnḗ)der. French téléphonebor. English telephoneclip. Clipping of telephone; first attested in 1884.

examples.text: I need to charge my cell phone.

translations.de: Ich muss mein Handy aufladen.
translations.fr: Il faut que je recharge mon téléphone portable.
translations.pt: Preciso carregar meu celular.

examples.text: You've neither written nor phoned.

translations.de: Du hast weder geschrieben noch angerufen.
translations.fr: Vous n'avez ni écrit, ni téléphoné.
translations.pt: Você nem escreveu, nem ligou.

examples.text: I'm calling from a cell phone.

translations.de: Ich rufe von meinem Mobiltelefon aus an.
translations.fr: J'appelle d'un téléphone portable.
translations.pt: Estou ligando de um celular.

examples.text: She gave me a fake phone number.

translations.de: Sie hat mir eine falsche Telefonnummer gegeben.
translations.fr: Elle me donna un faux numéro de téléphone.
translations.pt: Ela me deu um número de telefone falso.

more.definition: To call (someone) using a telephone.; To say via telephone.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *kʷelh₁-der. Ancient Greek τῆλε (têle)lbor. Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂-der. Ancient Greek φωνή (phōnḗ)der. French téléphonebor. English telephoneclip. Clipping of telephone; first attested in 1884.

examples.text: Today, I'm not going to school.

translations.de: Heute gehe ich nicht zur Schule.
translations.fr: Aujourd'hui, je ne vais pas à l'école.
translations.pt: Hoje eu não vou para a escola.

examples.text: How many different schools have you attended?

translations.de: Wie viele verschiedene Schulen hast du besucht?
translations.fr: Combien d'écoles différentes as-tu fréquentées ?
translations.pt: Em quantas escolas diferentes você já esteve?

examples.text: Tom is at school, isn't he?

translations.de: Tom ist in der Schule, nicht wahr?
translations.fr: Tom est à l'école, n'est-ce pas ?
translations.pt: Tom está na escola, não está?

examples.text: This school has a zero tolerance policy.

translations.de: An dieser Schule herrscht das Nulltoleranzprinzip.
translations.fr: Cette école pratique la tolérance zéro.
translations.pt: Esta escola tem uma política de tolerância zero.

more.definition: An institution dedicated to teaching and learning; an educational institution.; An educational institution providing primary and secondary education, prior to tertiary education (college or university).; At Eton College, a period or session of teaching.
more.etymology: From Middle English scole, from Old English scōl (“place of education”), from Proto-West Germanic *skōlu, from Late Latin schola, scola (“learned discussion or dissertation, lecture, school”), from Ancient Greek σχολή (skholḗ, “spare time, leisure”), from Proto-Indo-European *seǵʰ- (“to hold, have, possess”).
