examples.text: I'm a student of this school.

translations.de: Ich besuche diese Schule.
translations.fr: Je suis un étudiant de cette école.
translations.pt: Sou um aluno dessa escola.

examples.text: Why do our schools look like prisons?

translations.de: Warum sehen unsere Schulen aus wie Gefängnisse?
translations.fr: Pourquoi nos écoles ont-elles l'air de prisons ?
translations.pt: Por que as nossas escolas parecem prisões?

examples.text: I don't like going to school.

translations.de: Ich gehe nicht gern zur Schule.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas aller à l'école.
translations.pt: Eu não gosto de ir à escola.

examples.text: I won't go to school tomorrow.

translations.de: Ich werde morgen nicht zur Schule gehen.
translations.fr: Je n'irai pas à l'école demain.
translations.pt: Amanhã não vou para a escola.

more.definition: To educate, teach, or train (often, but not necessarily, in a school).; To defeat emphatically, to teach an opponent a harsh lesson.; To control, or compose, one’s expression.
more.etymology: From Middle English scole, from Old English scōl (“place of education”), from Proto-West Germanic *skōlu, from Late Latin schola, scola (“learned discussion or dissertation, lecture, school”), from Ancient Greek σχολή (skholḗ, “spare time, leisure”), from Proto-Indo-European *seǵʰ- (“to hold, have, possess”). Doublet of schola and shul.

examples.text: I'll sleep on the couch tonight.

translations.de: Ich werde heute Abend auf dem Sofa schlafen.
translations.fr: Je vais dormir sur le canapé ce soir.
translations.pt: Vou dormir no sofá esta noite.

examples.text: I like to sleep on my stomach.

translations.de: Ich schlafe gern auf dem Bauch.
translations.fr: J'aime dormir sur le ventre.
translations.pt: Eu gosto de dormir de bruços.

examples.text: I want to go home and sleep.

translations.de: Ich will nach Hause und schlafen.
translations.fr: Je veux aller chez moi et dormir.
translations.pt: Eu quero ir para casa dormir.

examples.text: I don't have time to sleep.

translations.de: Ich habe keine Zeit, um zu schlafen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas le temps de dormir.
translations.pt: Eu não tenho tempo para dormir.

more.definition: The state of reduced consciousness during which a human or animal rests in a daily rhythm.; An act or instance of sleeping.; A night.
more.etymology: From Middle English slepe, sleep, sleepe, from Old English slǣp (“sleep”), from Proto-West Germanic *slāp, from Proto-Germanic *slēpaz (“sleep”).

examples.text: The cat is sleeping on the couch.

translations.de: Die Katze schläft auf der Couch.
translations.fr: Le chat dort sur le canapé.
translations.pt: O gato está dormindo no sofá.

examples.text: I shouldn't have slept with her.

translations.de: Ich hätte nicht mit ihr schlafen sollen.
translations.fr: Je n'aurais pas dû coucher avec elle.
translations.pt: Não deveria ter dormido com ela.

examples.text: I want to sleep with your wife.

translations.de: Ich will mit Ihrer Frau schlafen.
translations.fr: Je veux coucher avec ta femme.
translations.pt: Eu quero dormir com a sua esposa.

examples.text: A sleeping child is like an angel.

translations.de: Ein schlafend Kind gleicht einem Engel.
translations.fr: Un enfant endormi est comme un ange.
translations.pt: Uma criança que dorme é como um anjo.

more.definition: To rest in a state of reduced consciousness.; To have sexual intercourse (see sleep with).; To accommodate in beds.
more.etymology: From Middle English slepen, from Anglian Old English slēpan (West Saxon Old English slǣpan), from Proto-West Germanic *slāpan, from Proto-Germanic *slēpaną (“to sleep”).

examples.text: Life is a fight against death.

translations.de: Das Leben ist ein Kampf gegen den Tod.
translations.fr: La vie est un combat contre la mort.
translations.pt: A vida é uma luta contra a morte.

examples.text: The best gladiator fights today.

translations.de: Der beste Gladiator wird heute kämpfen.
translations.fr: Le meilleur gladiateur se battra aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: O melhor gladiador luta hoje.

examples.text: Why don't they fight for their rights?

translations.de: Warum kämpfen sie nicht für ihre Rechte?
translations.fr: Pourquoi ne se battent-ils pas pour leurs droits ?
translations.pt: Por que não lutam por seus direitos?

examples.text: Don't let the children fight.

translations.de: Lass die Kinder nicht kämpfen.
translations.fr: Ne laisse pas les enfants se battre.
translations.pt: Não deixe as crianças brigarem.

more.definition: An occasion of fighting.; A physical confrontation or combat between two or more people or groups.; A boxing or martial arts match.
more.etymology: From Middle English fight, feyght, fiȝt, fecht, from Old English feoht, ġefeoht (“fight”), from Proto-West Germanic *fehtan (“to fight”), from Proto-Germanic *fehtą, *gafehtą (“fight, struggle”), from Proto-Germanic *fehtaną (“to struggle with”). Cognate with Dutch gevecht (“fight”), German Gefecht (“fight”).

examples.text: Gladiators fought to death inside the Colosseum.

translations.de: Im Kolosseum kämpften die Gladiatoren bis zum Tode.
translations.fr: Les gladiateurs se battaient à mort dans le Colisée.
translations.pt: No Coliseu, os gladiadores lutavam até a morte.

examples.text: The doctor is fighting against the disease.

translations.de: Der Arzt kämpft gegen die Krankheit.
translations.fr: Le médecin se bat contre la maladie.
translations.pt: O médico está lutando contra a enfermidade.

examples.text: They combined forces to fight the enemy.

translations.de: Sie vereinigten ihre Kräfte, um den Feind zu bekämpfen.
translations.fr: Ils combinèrent leurs forces pour combattre l'ennemi.
translations.pt: Eles combinaram forças para combater o inimigo.

examples.text: Mary fights constantly with her parents.

translations.de: Maria streitet sich ständig mit ihren Eltern.
translations.fr: Mary se dispute constamment avec ses parents.
translations.pt: Mary briga constantemente com seus pais.

more.definition: To engage in combat with; to oppose physically, to contest with.; To conduct or engage in (battle, warfare, a cause, etc.).; To contend in physical conflict, either singly or in war, battle, etc.
more.etymology: From Middle English fighten (“to fight”), from Old English feohtan (“to fight, combat, strive”), from Proto-West Germanic *fehtan (“to fight”), from Proto-Germanic *fehtaną (“to comb, tease, shear, struggle with”), from Proto-Indo-European *peḱ- (“to comb, shear”).

examples.text: I couldn't stand the noise anymore.

translations.de: Ich konnte den Lärm nicht mehr vertragen.
translations.fr: Je ne pouvais plus supporter le bruit.
translations.pt: Não podia aguentar mais esse barulho.

examples.text: The woman stands before the library.

translations.de: Die Frau steht vor der Bücherei.
translations.fr: La femme se tient devant la bibliothèque.
translations.pt: A mulher está em frente à biblioteca.

examples.text: I can't stand it any longer.

translations.de: Ich kann es nicht mehr ertragen.
translations.fr: Je ne puis le supporter davantage.
translations.pt: Não aguento mais.

examples.text: You don't need to stand up.

translations.de: Du brauchst nicht aufzustehen.
translations.fr: Tu n'as pas besoin de te lever.
translations.pt: Você não precisa se levantar.

more.definition: The act of standing.; A defensive position or effort.; A resolute, unwavering position; firm opinion; action for a purpose in the face of opposition.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-der. From Middle English stonden, standen (verb) and stand, stond (noun, from the verb), from Old English standan (“to stand, occupy a place”), from Proto-West Germanic *standan, from Proto-Germanic *standaną (“to stand”), from Pre-Germanic *sth₂-n-t-´, an innovative extended n-infixed form of Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-.

examples.text: The audience gave Tom a standing ovation.

translations.de: Das Publikum erhob sich vor Tom applaudierend von den Sitzen.
translations.fr: Le public a fait une standing ovation pour Tom.
translations.pt: Tom foi aplaudido de pé pelo auditório.

examples.text: I can't stand that noise anymore.

translations.de: Ich halte diesen Lärm nicht mehr aus!
translations.fr: Je ne peux plus supporter ce bruit.
translations.pt: Eu não suporto mais esse barulho.

examples.text: She stood in front of the mirror.

translations.de: Sie stand vor dem Spiegel.
translations.fr: Elle se tenait debout devant le miroir.
translations.pt: Ela ficou parada diante do espelho.

examples.text: Do you know what UNESCO stands for?

translations.de: Wissen Sie was UNESCO bedeutet?
translations.fr: Savez-vous ce que UNESCO veut dire ?
translations.pt: Você sabe o que significa "UNESCO"?

examples.text: I have been standing in line for an hour.

translations.de: Ich stehe seit einer Stunde in der Schlange.
translations.fr: Je suis debout dans la file depuis une heure.
translations.pt: Estou em pé na fila há uma hora.

examples.text: We stood in front of the door.

translations.de: Wir standen vor der Tür.
translations.fr: Nous nous tenions devant la porte.
translations.pt: Nós ficamos em pé em frente à porta.

more.definition: To support oneself on the feet in an erect position.; To rise to one’s feet; to stand up.; To remain motionless.
collocations: stand up — to rise to your feet
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-der. From Middle English stonden, standen (verb) and stand, stond (noun, from the verb), from Old English standan (“to stand, occupy a place”), from Proto-West Germanic *standan, from Proto-Germanic *standaną (“to stand”), from Pre-Germanic *sth₂-n-t-´, an innovative extended n-infixed form of Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-.

examples.text: I'll buy it for you tomorrow.

translations.de: Morgen kaufe ich sie dir.
translations.fr: Je l'achèterai pour toi demain.
translations.pt: Vou comprar isso para você amanhã.

examples.text: I'm afraid it'll rain tomorrow.

translations.de: Ich befürchte es wird morgen regnen.
translations.fr: Je crains qu'il ne pleuve demain.
translations.pt: Estou achando que vai chover amanhã.

examples.text: It's going to be hot tomorrow.

translations.de: Morgen wird es heiß.
translations.fr: Il va faire chaud demain.
translations.pt: O dia vai ser quente amanhã.

examples.text: I'll do that tomorrow. I promise.

translations.de: Ich tu’s morgen. Versprochen!
translations.fr: Je le ferai demain. Je le promets.
translations.pt: Amanhã eu faço. Prometo.

more.definition: On the day after the present day.; At some point in the future; later on
more.etymology: From Middle English tomorwe, tomorwen, from Old English tō morgne (“tomorrow”, adverb), from tō (“at, on”) + morgne (dative of morgen (“morning”)), from Proto-Germanic *murganaz (“morning”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *mergʰ- (“to blink, to twinkle”), equivalent to to- + morrow. Compare French demain, Dutch morgen, German morgen, Swedish imorgon or Danish i morgen.

examples.text: What are we going to do tomorrow?

translations.de: Was machen wir morgen?
translations.fr: Qu'allons nous faire demain ?
translations.pt: O que vocês vão fazer amanhã?

examples.text: Can I go to the movies tomorrow?

translations.de: Darf ich morgen ins Kino?
translations.fr: Puis-je aller au cinéma demain ?
translations.pt: Posso ir ao cinema amanhã?

examples.text: Where do you want to go tomorrow?

translations.de: Wohin willst du morgen gehen?
translations.fr: Où voulez-vous aller demain ?
translations.pt: Aonde a senhora quer ir amanhã?

examples.text: I'll do it tomorrow. I promise.

translations.de: Ich tu’s morgen. Versprochen!
translations.fr: Je le ferai demain. Je le promets.
translations.pt: Amanhã eu faço. Prometo.

more.definition: The day after the present day.; A future period or time.
more.etymology: From Middle English tomorwe, tomorwen, from Old English tō morgne (“tomorrow”, adverb), from tō (“at, on”) + morgne (dative of morgen (“morning”)), from Proto-Germanic *murganaz (“morning”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *mergʰ- (“to blink, to twinkle”), equivalent to to- + morrow. Compare French demain, Dutch morgen, German morgen, Swedish imorgon or Danish i morgen.

examples.text: Tom teaches me French twice a week.

translations.de: Tom bringt mir zweimal die Woche Französisch bei.
translations.fr: Tom me montre le français deux fois par semaine.
translations.pt: Tom me ensina francês duas vezes por semana.

examples.text: I took that picture a week ago.

translations.de: Ich habe das Foto vor einer Woche geschossen.
translations.fr: J'ai pris cette photo il y a une semaine.
translations.pt: Tirei essa foto há uma semana.

examples.text: In one week there are seven days.

translations.de: Eine Woche sind sieben Tage.
translations.fr: Il y a sept jours dans une semaine.
translations.pt: Em uma semana há sete dias.

examples.text: We have four French classes a week.

translations.de: Wir haben in der Woche vier Mal Französischunterricht.
translations.fr: Nous avons quatre cours de français par semaine.
translations.pt: Nós temos quatro aulas de francês por semana.

more.definition: The squeal of a pig.
more.etymology: Imitative.

examples.text: Tom went to Boston a week ago.

translations.de: Tom ist vor einer Woche nach Boston gefahren.
translations.fr: Tom est allé à Boston il y a une semaine.
translations.pt: Tom foi a Boston há uma semana.

examples.text: Tom was away for three weeks.

translations.de: Tom war drei Wochen lang weg.
translations.fr: Tom était absent pendant trois semaines.
translations.pt: Tom esteve fora por três semanas.

examples.text: I was in hospital for a week.

translations.de: Ich war eine Woche im Krankenhaus.
translations.fr: J'étais à l'hôpital pendant une semaine.
translations.pt: Fiquei no hospital por uma semana.

examples.text: What day of the week is it?

translations.de: Welcher Wochentag ist heute?
translations.fr: On est quel jour de la semaine ?
translations.pt: Qual dia da semana é hoje?

more.definition: Any period of seven consecutive days.; A period of seven days beginning with Sunday or Monday.; A period of five days beginning with Monday.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *weyg-der. From Middle English wyke, weke, from Old English wice, wucu (“week”), from Proto-West Germanic *wikā, from Proto-Germanic *wikǭ (“sequence; week”), from Proto-Indo-European *weyg-, *weyk- (“to bend, curve”). Related to weak and dialectal English wick (“corner”); see Proto-Germanic *wīk(w)aną (“to bend, yield, cease”).

examples.text: How about going out to eat tonight?

translations.de: Was hältst du davon, heute Abend essen zu gehen?
translations.fr: Que dirais-tu d'aller manger dehors ce soir ?
translations.pt: Que tal comermos fora esta noite?

examples.text: Do you have any plans for tonight?

translations.de: Hast du Pläne für heute Abend?
translations.fr: Avez-vous des projets pour la soirée ?
translations.pt: Você tem planos para hoje à noite?

examples.text: It's raining cats and dogs tonight.

translations.de: Heute Abend regnet es in Strömen.
translations.fr: Il pleut des cordes ce soir.
translations.pt: Está chovendo muito hoje.

examples.text: He promised to come home early tonight.

translations.de: Er versprach, heute Abend früh nach Hause zu kommen.
translations.fr: Il a promis de rentrer tôt ce soir.
translations.pt: Ele prometeu voltar cedo para casa esta noite.

more.definition: During the night following the current day; during the evening of today.
more.etymology: From Middle English tonyght, to niȝt, from Old English tō niht.

examples.text: I wonder if he'll come tonight.

translations.de: Ich frage mich, ob er heute Abend kommen wird.
translations.fr: Je me demande s'il viendra ce soir.
translations.pt: Será que ele virá hoje à noite?

examples.text: Are you going to the theater tonight?

translations.de: Gehen Sie heute Abend ins Theater?
translations.fr: Allez-vous au théâtre ce soir ?
translations.pt: Você vai ao teatro hoje à noite?

examples.text: A full moon can be seen tonight.

translations.de: Heute Abend kann man den Vollmond sehen.
translations.fr: Une pleine lune peut être vue ce soir.
translations.pt: Esta noite pode-se ver a Lua cheia.

examples.text: I have no place to sleep tonight.

translations.de: Ich habe keinen Schlafplatz für diese Nacht.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas d'endroit où dormir cette nuit.
translations.pt: Não tenho lugar para dormir esta noite.

more.definition: The nighttime of the current day or date; this night.
more.etymology: From Middle English tonyght, to niȝt, from Old English tō niht.

examples.text: Almost everyone I know can speak French.

translations.de: Fast jeder, den ich kenne, spricht Französisch.
translations.fr: Presque tous ceux que je connais savent parler français.
translations.pt: Quase todo mundo que conheço sabe falar francês.

examples.text: He kissed me in front of everyone.

translations.de: Er küsste mich vor allen Leuten.
translations.fr: Il m'a embrassée devant tout le monde.
translations.pt: Ele me beijou na frente de todos.

examples.text: I detest everyone, and everyone detests me.

translations.de: Ich hasse alle und alle hassen mich.
translations.fr: Je déteste tout le monde et tout le monde me déteste.
translations.pt: Detesto toda a gente e toda a gente me detesta.

examples.text: When he finished speaking, everyone was silent.

translations.de: Als er zu reden aufhörte, waren alle still.
translations.fr: Lorsqu'il acheva de parler, tout le monde était silencieux.
translations.pt: Quando ele acabou de falar, todo mundo estava quieto.

more.definition: Every individual in a set; every person.
more.etymology: An alteration of earlier everychone after every, from Middle English everichon. By surface analysis, every + one.

examples.text: I am just going for a walk.

translations.de: Ich mache bloß einen Spaziergang.
translations.fr: Je vais juste faire une promenade.
translations.pt: Só vou dar um passeio.

examples.text: My sister usually walks to school.

translations.de: Meine Schwester geht gewöhnlich zu Fuß zur Schule.
translations.fr: D'habitude ma sœur va à l'école à pied.
translations.pt: Minha irmã normalmente anda até a escola.

examples.text: My father takes a walk every day.

translations.de: Vater geht jeden Tag spazieren.
translations.fr: Mon père se promène tous les jours.
translations.pt: O meu pai faz uma caminhada todo dia.

examples.text: We took a walk along the river.

translations.de: Wir machten einen Spaziergang den Fluss entlang.
translations.fr: Nous nous sommes promenés le long de la rivière.
translations.pt: Nós fizemos uma caminhada ao longo do rio.

more.definition: A trip made by walking.; A distance walked.; An Olympic Games track event requiring that the heel of the leading foot touch the ground before the toe of the trailing foot leaves the ground.
more.etymology: From Middle English walc, walk, walke, from Old English *wealc (as in Old English wealcspinl) and ġewealc (“rolling, turning; motion, surging”), from Proto-Germanic *walką. Cognate with Icelandic volk (“difficulty, hardship, trouble”).

examples.text: Wait. I can't walk that fast.

translations.de: Warte! Ich kann nicht so schnell gehen.
translations.fr: Attends. Je ne peux pas marcher aussi vite.
translations.pt: Espere. Não posso caminhar tão ligeiro assim.

examples.text: He walked into the lion's den.

translations.de: Er begab sich in die Höhle des Löwen.
translations.fr: Il s'est jeté dans la gueule du loup.
translations.pt: Ele adentrou o covil do leão.

examples.text: Tom isn't accustomed to walking barefooted.

translations.de: Tom ist es nicht gewohnt, barfuß zu gehen.
translations.fr: Tom n'est pas habitué à marcher pieds nus.
translations.pt: Tom não está acostumado a andar descalço.

examples.text: Let's go out for a walk.

translations.de: Lass uns spazieren gehen.
translations.fr: Allons nous promener.
translations.pt: Vamos sair para caminhar.

more.definition: To move on the feet by alternately setting each foot (or pair or group of feet: in the case of some non-human animals with four or more feet) forward, with at least one foot on the ground at all times. Compare run.; To "walk free", i.e. to win, or avoid, a criminal court case, particularly when actually guilty.; Of an object, to go missing or be stolen.
more.etymology: From Middle English walk, walke, walken, walkyn, wolken (“to roll, toss, or turn; to walk; to move; to be living; to beat or full; to perform”), a conflation of Old English wealcan (“to move around; to revolve; to roll; to fluctuate; to discuss”) (ġewealcan (“to go, traverse; to roll”)) and Old English wealcian (“to curl, roll up, twist; to wrinkle”); both from Proto-West Germanic *walkan, from Proto-Germanic …

examples.text: Tom and Mary are in the classroom.

translations.de: Tom und Maria sind im Klassenzimmer.
translations.fr: Tom et Marie sont dans la classe.
translations.pt: Tom e Mary estão na sala de aula.

examples.text: Tom kissed Mary on the Ferris wheel.

translations.de: Tom küsste Maria auf dem Riesenrad.
translations.fr: Tom a embrassé Marie sur la grande roue.
translations.pt: O Tom beijou a Mary na roda-gigante.

examples.text: Tom knew that Mary was in Boston.

translations.de: Tom wusste, dass Maria in Boston war.
translations.fr: Tom savait que Marie était à Boston.
translations.pt: Tom sabia que Mary estava em Boston.

examples.text: Tom doesn't respect Mary's opinion.

translations.de: Tom respektiert Marias Meinung nicht.
translations.fr: Tom ne respecte pas l'opinion de Marie.
translations.pt: Tom não respeita as opiniões de Maria.

more.etymology: From Middle English Marie, referring to Mary, the Virgin Mary. Mid-14th century.

examples.text: Tom was married to Mary's sister.

translations.de: Tom war mit Marias Schwester verheiratet.
translations.fr: Tom était marié à la sœur de Mary.
translations.pt: Tom era casado com a irmã de Mary.

examples.text: I don't want to marry you.

translations.de: Ich möchte dich nicht heiraten.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas t'épouser.
translations.pt: Não quero me casar com você.

examples.text: Tom is married to a famous actress.

translations.de: Tom ist mit einer berühmten Schauspielerin verheiratet.
translations.fr: Tom est marié à une célèbre actrice.
translations.pt: Tom é casado com uma atriz famosa.

examples.text: I was already married at your age.

translations.de: In deinem Alter war ich bereits verheiratet.
translations.fr: À votre âge, j'étais déjà mariée.
translations.pt: Eu já era casado à sua idade.

more.definition: To enter into the conjugal or connubial state; to take a husband or a wife.; To enter into marriage with one another.; To take as husband or wife.
more.etymology: From Middle English marien, from Anglo-Norman marïer, from Latin marītāre (“to wed”), from marītus (“husband, suitor”), from mās (“man, male”), of uncertain origin. Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *méryos (“young man”), same source as Sanskrit मर्य (márya, “suitor, young man”).

examples.text: Do you wanna talk?

translations.de: Wollen Sie reden?
translations.fr: Tu veux parler ?
translations.pt: Queres conversar?

examples.text: We're going to the beach. Wanna come?

translations.de: Wir gehen an den Strand. Willst du mitkommen?
translations.fr: Nous allons à la plage. Tu veux venir ?
translations.pt: Nós vamos à praia. Queres vir também?

examples.text: It's getting late. I don't wanna go home alone.

translations.de: Es wird schon spät. Ich möchte nicht alleine nach Hause gehen.
translations.fr: Il se fait tard. Je ne veux pas rentrer à la maison seul.
translations.pt: Está ficando tarde. Não quero ir para casa sozinho.

examples.text: I've got two tickets for the concert. Wanna come?

translations.de: Ich habe zwei Karten für das Konzert. Willst du mit?
translations.fr: J'ai deux billets pour le concert. Tu veux venir ?
translations.pt: Eu tenho duas entradas para o concerto. Quer ir?

more.definition: Represents a contracted pronunciation of want to.; Represents a contracted pronunciation of want a.
more.etymology: Contractions. Attested as early as 1824.

examples.text: Ah! If I were rich, I'd buy myself a house in Spain.

translations.de: Ah! Wenn ich reich wäre, würde ich mir ein Haus in Spanien kaufen.

translations.pt: Ah! Se eu fosse rico, compraria uma casa na Espanha.

examples.text: Ah, I forgot my mobile phone.

translations.de: Ach, ich habe mein Handy vergessen.
translations.fr: Ah non, j'ai oublié mon cellulaire.

examples.text: Ah, the coffee is really hot!

translations.de: Oh, der Kaffee ist wirklich heiß!
translations.fr: Ah, le café est vraiment chaud !

translations.pt: Ah, isto é muito melhor.

more.definition: Marks a yes–no tag question prompting the listener to clarify or confirm something.; Reinforces a short, non-rhetorical wh-question.; Emphasizes the need for absolute confirmation, permission or acknowledgment.
more.etymology: From Hokkien 啊 (--a, a) and Teochew 啊 (a⁷), reinforced by Tamil -ஆ (-ā, etymology 3, particle sense 1) among Tamil speakers (Baskaran, 1988).

examples.text: Ah, that's much better.

translations.de: Ah, das ist viel besser!
translations.fr: Ah, c'est bien meilleur.
translations.pt: Ah, isto é muito melhor.

examples.text: Ah! If I were rich, I'd buy myself a house in Spain.

translations.de: Ah! Wenn ich reich wäre, würde ich mir ein Haus in Spanien kaufen.
translations.fr: Ah ! Si j'étais riche, je m'achèterais une maison en Espagne.
translations.pt: Ah! Se eu fosse rico, compraria uma casa na Espanha.

examples.text: Ah, I forgot my mobile phone.

translations.de: Ach, ich habe mein Handy vergessen.
translations.fr: Ah non, j'ai oublié mon cellulaire.
translations.pt: Oh, esqueci o celular.

examples.text: Ah, the coffee is really hot!

translations.de: Oh, der Kaffee ist wirklich heiß!
translations.fr: Ah, le café est vraiment chaud !
translations.pt: Ai, o café está muito quente!

more.definition: To give a cry of "ah".
more.etymology: From Middle English ah, aa, a (“ah”), of imitative origin, or from Old English ēa, *eah (“oh, alas”), from Proto-West Germanic *a, *ah (“ah”). Earliest recorded use is circa 1175 in the Ormulum: A, Maȝȝstre! icc wat tatt tu full wiss Arrt Godess Sune ("Ah, Master! I know for sure that thou art God's Son").

examples.text: Is this your second trip to France?

translations.de: Ist dies Ihre zweite Reise nach Frankreich?
translations.fr: C'est ton second voyage en France ?
translations.pt: É a sua segunda viagem à França?

examples.text: Elizabeth II is the Queen of England.

translations.de: Elisabeth II. ist die Königin von England.
translations.fr: Elisabeth II est la Reine d'Angleterre.
translations.pt: Elizabeth II é a rainha da Inglaterra.

examples.text: The library is on the second floor.

translations.de: Die Bibliothek ist im ersten Stock.
translations.fr: La bibliothèque est au premier étage.
translations.pt: A biblioteca fica no segundo andar.

examples.text: We live on the second floor.

translations.de: Wir wohnen im zweiten Stock.
translations.fr: Nous habitons au second étage.
translations.pt: Nós moramos no segundo andar.

more.definition: Number-two; following after the first one with nothing between them. The ordinal number corresponding to the cardinal number two.; Next to the first in value, power, excellence, dignity, or rank; secondary; subordinate; inferior.; Being of the same kind as one that has preceded; another.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ-der. Latin secunduslbor. Old French secondbor. From Middle English secunde, second, secound, secund, borrowed from Old French second, seond, from Latin secundus (“following, next in order”), from root of sequor (“to follow”), from Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ- (“to follow”). Doublet of secund and secundo.

examples.text: Every second house has a car.

translations.de: Jedes zweite Haus hat ein Auto.
translations.fr: Il y a une voiture pour deux maisons.
translations.pt: Para cada duas casas há um carro.

examples.text: Ramses II was an Egyptian pharaoh.

translations.de: Ramses II. war ein ägyptischer Pharaoh.
translations.fr: Ramsès II était un pharaon égyptien.
translations.pt: Ramses II foi um faraó egípcio.

examples.text: She only buys second-hand clothing.

translations.de: Sie kauft nur gebrauchte Kleidung.
translations.fr: Elle n'achète que des vêtements d'occasion.
translations.pt: Ela compra apenas roupas usadas.

examples.text: My grandfather died in the Second World War.

translations.de: Mein Großvater ist im Zweiten Weltkrieg gestorben.
translations.fr: Mon grand-père est mort pendant la Seconde Guerre mondiale.
translations.pt: Meu avô morreu na Segunda Guerra Mundial.

more.definition: After the first; at the second rank.; After the first occurrence but before the third.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ-der. Latin secunduslbor. Old French secondbor. From Middle English secunde, second, secound, secund, borrowed from Old French second, seond, from Latin secundus (“following, next in order”), from root of sequor (“to follow”), from Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ- (“to follow”). Doublet of secund and secundo.

examples.text: It's snowing and it's cold.

translations.de: Es schneit und es ist kalt.
translations.fr: Il neige et il fait froid.
translations.pt: Está nevando e fazendo frio.

examples.text: It's windy and it's raining.

translations.de: Es ist windig und es regnet.
translations.fr: Il y a du vent et il pleut.
translations.pt: Está ventando e chovendo.

examples.text: There's a stone in my shoe.

translations.de: Es ist ein Stein in meinem Schuh.
translations.fr: J'ai une pierre dans mon soulier.
translations.pt: Há uma pedra em meu sapato.

examples.text: She's going to write a letter.

translations.de: Sie wird einen Brief schreiben.
translations.fr: Elle écrira une lettre.
translations.pt: Ela vai escrever uma carta.

more.definition: Something that is number two in a series.; Something that is next in rank, quality, precedence, position, status, or authority.; The place that is next below or after first in a race or contest.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ-der. Latin secunduslbor. Old French secondbor. From Middle English secunde, second, secound, secund, borrowed from Old French second, seond, from Latin secundus (“following, next in order”), from root of sequor (“to follow”), from Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ- (“to follow”). Doublet of secund and secundo.

examples.text: Can I talk to you for a second?

translations.de: Kann ich kurz mit euch reden?
translations.fr: Puis-je te parler une seconde ?
translations.pt: Posso falar com você por um segundo?

examples.text: The fight lasted three seconds.

translations.de: Der Kampf dauerte drei Sekunden.
translations.fr: Le combat a duré trois secondes.
translations.pt: A luta durou três segundos.

examples.text: Germany was allied with Italy in World War II.

translations.de: Im Zweiten Weltkrieg war Deutschland mit Italien verbündet.
translations.fr: L'Allemagne était alliée avec l'Italie durant la deuxième guerre mondiale.
translations.pt: A Alemanha estava aliada à Itália durante a Segunda Guerra Mundial.

examples.text: The second lesson is very easy.

translations.de: Lektion zwei ist sehr leicht.
translations.fr: La deuxième leçon est très facile.
translations.pt: A segunda lição é muito fácil.

more.definition: To agree as a second person to (a proposal), usually to reach a necessary quorum of two. (See etymology 3 for translations.); To follow in the next place; to succeed.; To climb after a lead climber.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ-der. Latin secunduslbor. Old French secondbor. From Middle English secunde, second, secound, secund, borrowed from Old French second, seond, from Latin secundus (“following, next in order”), from root of sequor (“to follow”), from Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ- (“to follow”). Doublet of secund and secundo.

examples.text: I want to talk with Tom alone.

translations.de: Ich will allein mit Tom sprechen.
translations.fr: Je veux parler avec Tom seul à seul.
translations.pt: Eu quero falar com o Tom a sós.

examples.text: I just want to be left alone.

translations.de: Ich will einfach nur in Ruhe gelassen werden.
translations.fr: Je veux juste qu'on me laisse tranquille.
translations.pt: Eu só quero que me deixem sozinho.

examples.text: I'm getting used to eating alone.

translations.de: Ich gewöhne mich daran, allein zu essen.
translations.fr: Je m'habitue à manger seule.
translations.pt: Estou acostumado a comer sozinho.

examples.text: Tom is too young to travel alone.

translations.de: Tom ist zu jung, um allein zu verreisen.
translations.fr: Tom est trop jeune pour voyager seul.
translations.pt: Tom é jovem demais para viajar sozinho.

more.definition: By oneself, solitary.; Not involved in a romantic relationship.; Lacking peers who share one's beliefs, experiences, practices, etc.
more.etymology: From Middle English allone, from earlier all oon (literally “all one”), contracted from the Old English phrase eall ān (“completely alone”), equivalent to al- (“all”) + one. Cognate with Scots alane (“alone”), Saterland Frisian alleene (“alone”), West Frisian allinne (“alone”), Dutch alleen (“alone”), Low German alleen (“alone”), German allein (“alone”), Danish alene (“alone”), Swedish allena (“alone”).

examples.text: I shouldn't have left you alone.

translations.de: Ich hätte Sie nicht allein lassen sollen.
translations.fr: Je n'aurais pas dû te laisser seul.
translations.pt: Eu não devia tê-la deixado sozinha.

examples.text: She was alone on Valentine's Day.

translations.de: Sie war allein am Valentinstag.
translations.fr: Elle était seule le jour de la Saint-Valentin.
translations.pt: Ela estava sozinha no dia dos namorados.

examples.text: Tom just wants to be left alone.

translations.de: Tom will einfach nur allein gelassen werden.
translations.fr: Tom veut juste qu'on le laisse seul.
translations.pt: Tom só quer ser deixado em paz.

examples.text: I have to deal with this alone.

translations.de: Ich muss allein damit fertig werden.
translations.fr: Je dois gérer ceci toute seule.
translations.pt: Tenho que lidar com isso sozinho.

more.definition: By oneself; apart from, or exclusive of, others; solo.; Without outside help.; Not permitting anything further; exclusively.
more.etymology: From Middle English allone, from earlier all oon (literally “all one”), contracted from the Old English phrase eall ān (“completely alone”), equivalent to al- (“all”) + one. Cognate with Scots alane (“alone”), Saterland Frisian alleene (“alone”), West Frisian allinne (“alone”), Dutch alleen (“alone”), Low German alleen (“alone”), German allein (“alone”), Danish alene (“alone”), Swedish allena (“alone”).

examples.text: I talk to myself all the time.

translations.de: Ich rede ständig mit mir selbst.
translations.fr: Je me parle tout le temps.
translations.pt: Eu falo sozinho o tempo todo.

examples.text: I can't do it by myself.

translations.de: Allein schaff’ ich’s nicht.
translations.fr: Je ne peux le faire seul.
translations.pt: Não posso fazer isso sozinho.

examples.text: I'll have to do it myself.

translations.de: Ich werde es selbst tun müssen.
translations.fr: Je devrai le faire moi-même.
translations.pt: Terei de fazer isso eu mesmo.

examples.text: I don't like talking about myself.

translations.de: Ich rede nicht gern über mich selbst.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas parler de moi.
translations.pt: Eu não gosto de falar sobre mim mesmo.

more.definition: Me, as direct or indirect object the speaker as the object of a verb or preposition, when the speaker is also the subject.; Personally, for my part; used in apposition to I, sometimes for simple emphasis and sometimes with implicit exclusion of any others performing the activity described.; In my normal state of body or mind.
more.etymology: From Middle English myself, meself, from Old English mē selfum and similar phrases, equivalent to me + self, later partly reinterpreted as my + self / -self. Cognate with Scots mysel, mysell (“myself”), West Frisian mysels (“myself”), Dutch mijzelf (“myself”), German mich selbst, mir selbst (“myself”), Norwegian Bokmål meg selv (“myself”).

examples.text: What's the worst-case scenario?

translations.de: Was ist das Worst-Case-Szenario?
translations.fr: Que se passe-t-il dans le pire des cas ?
translations.pt: Qual é a pior das hipóteses?

examples.text: In that case, we've got a problem...

translations.de: In dem Fall haben wir ein Problem...
translations.fr: Dans ce cas, nous avons un problème ...
translations.pt: Nesse caso, temos um problema...

examples.text: In case you want, I will do it.

translations.de: Im Falle, dass du es möchtest, werde ich es tun.
translations.fr: Si vous voulez, je le ferai.
translations.pt: Caso você queira, fá-lo-ei.

examples.text: Can we apply this rule in this case?

translations.de: Können wir die Regel in diesem Fall anwenden?
translations.fr: Peut-on appliquer cette règle dans ce cas ?
translations.pt: Podemos empregar esta regra nesse caso?

more.definition: The last remaining card of a particular rank.
more.etymology: From Middle English case, from Old Northern French casse (compare Old French chasse (“box, chest, case”)), from Latin capsa (“box, bookcase”), from capiō (“to take, seize, hold”). Doublet of cash, chase, and chasse. Compare Spanish caja, Asturian caxa, Portuguese caixa.

examples.text: In case of emergency, call the police.

translations.de: Benachrichtigen Sie im Notfall die Polizei!
translations.fr: En cas d'urgence, appelle la police.
translations.pt: Em caso de emergência, chame a polícia.

examples.text: I wish that were the case.

translations.de: Ich wünschte, dass das der Fall wäre.
translations.fr: J'aimerais que ce soit le cas.
translations.pt: Eu gostaria de que esse fosse o caso.

examples.text: You're wrong. That's not the case.

translations.de: Du irrst dich, das ist nicht der Fall.
translations.fr: Tu te trompes, ce n'est pas le cas.
translations.pt: Você está enganado; esse não é o caso.

examples.text: That's not always the case.

translations.de: Das ist nicht immer der Fall.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas toujours le cas.
translations.pt: Esse não é sempre o caso.

more.definition: An actual event, situation, or fact.; A specific matter or piece of work, specifically defined within a profession, usually in respect of a specific person and/or event; the set of tasks involved in addressing one such matter.; An instance or event as a topic of study.
more.etymology: From Middle English cas, from Old French cas (“an event”), from Latin cāsus (“a falling, a fall; accident, event, occurrence; occasion, opportunity; noun case”), perfect passive participle of cadō (“to fall, to drop”).

examples.text: Break the glass in case of emergency.

translations.de: Im Notfall Scheibe einschlagen.

translations.pt: Em caso de emergência, quebre o vidro.

examples.text: That isn't the case in Japan.

translations.de: In Japan ist das nicht der Fall.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas le cas au Japon.
translations.pt: Não é assim no Japão.

examples.text: In case of fire, push the button.

translations.de: Im Brandfall Knopf drücken!
translations.fr: En cas d'incendie, appuyez sur le bouton.
translations.pt: Em caso de incêndio, aperte o botão.

examples.text: Unfortunately, that's not the case.

translations.de: Das ist leider nicht der Fall.
translations.fr: Malheureusement, ce n'est pas le cas.
translations.pt: Infelizmente, esse não é o caso.

more.definition: To place (an item or items of manufacture) into a box, as in preparation for shipment.; To cover or protect with, or as if with, a case; to enclose.; To survey (a building or other location) surreptitiously, as in preparation for a robbery.
more.etymology: From Middle English cas, from Old French cas (“an event”), from Latin cāsus (“a falling, a fall; accident, event, occurrence; occasion, opportunity; noun case”), perfect passive participle of cadō (“to fall, to drop”).

examples.text: I've got to go back and check.

translations.de: Ich muss noch einmal zurückgehen und nachsehen.
translations.fr: Il faut que j'y retourne et que je vérifie.
translations.pt: Preciso voltar e checar.

examples.text: Can I pay for the book by check?

translations.de: Kann ich das Buch mit Scheck zahlen?

translations.pt: Vamos verificar o mapa.

examples.text: I'd like to pay by check.

translations.de: Ich möchte per Scheck zahlen.
translations.fr: Je veux payer par chèque.
translations.pt: Gostaria de pagar com cheque.

examples.text: I just wanted to check my email.

translations.de: Ich wollte nur meine E-Mails abrufen.

translations.de: Er muss unsere Pässe überprüfen.

examples.text: I'll check in the basement.

translations.de: Ich sehe mal im Keller nach.
translations.fr: Je vais vérifier au sous-sol.
translations.pt: Vou verificar no porăo.

more.definition: An expression showing that a requirement has been satisfied.; An expression that indicates that the speaker wishes to pay the bill (e.g. in a restaurant).

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, Lass mich mal nachsehen!

examples.text: I have one thousand dollars in travelers' checks and five hundred in cash.

translations.de: Ich habe eintausend Dollar in Reiseschecks und fünfhundert in bar.
translations.fr: J'ai mille dollars en chèques de voyage et cinq cents dollars en liquide.
translations.pt: Eu tenho mil dólares em traveler checks e quinhentos em dinheiro.

examples.text: I'll need to check my schedule.

translations.de: Ich muss in meinem Terminkalender nachsehen.
translations.fr: Il va falloir que je vérifie mon agenda.
translations.pt: Eu terei de consultar a minha agenda.

From Middle English chek, chekke, borrowed from Old French eschec, eschek, eschac, from Medieval Latin scaccus, borrowed from Arabic شَاه (šāh, “king or check at chess, shah”), borrowed from Classical Persian شَاه (šāh, “king”), from Middle Persian 𐭬𐭫𐭪𐭠 (mlkʾ /⁠šāh⁠/), from Old Persian 𐏋 (XŠ /⁠xšāyaθiya⁠/, “king”), from …

examples.text: The doctor checked the patient's pulse.

translations.de: Der Arzt überprüfte den Puls des Patienten.

translations.pt: O médico examinou o pulso do paciente.

examples.text: I'd like to open a checking account.

translations.de: Ich möchte ein Girokonto öffnen.
translations.fr: Je souhaite ouvrir un compte courant.
translations.pt: Gostaria de abrir uma conta corrente.

examples.text: Sue checked in at the Royal Hotel.

translations.de: Sue meldete sich im Royal Hotel an.
translations.fr: Sue s'est enregistrée au Royal Hotel.
translations.pt: Sue deu entrada no Royal Hotel.

examples.text: Have you checked under the couch?

translations.de: Hast du mal unter dem Sofa nachgesehen?
translations.fr: Est-ce que tu as vérifié sous le canapé ?
translations.pt: Vocês olharam debaixo do sofá?

more.definition: To inspect; to examine.; To verify the accuracy of a text or translation, usually making some corrections (proofread) or many (copyedit).; To mark items on a list (with a checkmark or by crossing them out) that have been chosen for keeping or removal or that have been dealt with (for example, completed or verified as correct or satisfactory).

examples.text: This is where my dad works.

translations.de: Hier ist es, wo mein Papa arbeitet.
translations.fr: C'est là que travaille mon père.
translations.pt: É aqui que meu pai trabalha.

examples.text: Tom doesn't have a dad.

translations.de: Tom hat keinen Vater.
translations.fr: Tom n'a pas de père.
translations.pt: Tom não tem pai.

examples.text: My dad cheated on my mom.

translations.de: Mein Vater hat meine Mutter betrogen.
translations.fr: Mon père a trompé ma mère.
translations.pt: O meu pai traiu a minha mãe.

examples.text: My dad taught me how to do it.

translations.de: Das hat mir mein Papa beigebracht.

translations.pt: Meu pai me ensinou como fazê-lo.

more.definition: A father, a male parent.; Used to address one's father; often capitalized.; Used to address an older adult male.

examples.text: This was my dad's favorite tie.

translations.de: Das war die Lieblingskrawatte meines Vaters.
translations.fr: Celle-ci était la cravate préférée de mon père.
translations.pt: Esta era a gravata favorita de meu pai.

examples.text: Why don't you answer your dad?

translations.de: Warum antwortest du deinem Vater nicht?
translations.fr: Pourquoi ne réponds-tu pas à ton papa ?
translations.pt: Por que não responde ao seu pai?

examples.text: Tom's dad is a university professor.

translations.de: Toms Vater ist Universitätsprofessor.
translations.fr: Le père de Tom est professeur à l'université.
translations.pt: O pai de Tom é professor universitário.

examples.text: My dad doesn't like football.

translations.de: Mein Vater mag Fußball nicht.
translations.fr: Mon père n'aime pas le foot.
translations.pt: Meu pai não gosta de futebol.

more.definition: To be a father to; to parent.; To act like a dad.; To throw against something; to dash.
more.etymology: From Early Modern English dadd, dadde (circa 1500), undoubtedly older, from unrecorded Middle English *dadde, of uncertain ultimate origin. Compare West Frisian deite (“dad, daddy”), Swabian Dede (“Godfather”).

examples.text: It'll soon be three o'clock.

translations.de: Es wird bald drei Uhr sein.

translations.pt: Já são quase três horas.

examples.text: My package arrived sooner than expected.

translations.de: Mein Paket kam früher als erwartet an.
translations.fr: Mon colis est arrivé plus tôt que prévu.
translations.pt: Meu pacote chegou mais cedo do que o esperado.

examples.text: I'd better get to bed soon.

translations.de: So langsam muss ich ins Bett.
translations.fr: Je ferais mieux d'aller tôt au lit.
translations.pt: É melhor eu ir logo dormir.

examples.text: He soon accustomed himself to cold weather.

translations.de: Er gewöhnte sich schnell an kaltes Wetter.
translations.fr: Il s'habitua bientôt au temps froid.
translations.pt: Ele logo se acostumou ao tempo frio.

more.definition: Short in length of time from the present.; Used as an alternative to express 'to be going to' in the form 'to be soon to'.
more.etymology: From Middle English sone, from Old English sōna (“immediately, at once”), from Proto-West Germanic *sān(ō), from Proto-Germanic *sēna, *sēnô (“immediately, soon, then”), from *sa (demonstrative pronoun), from Proto-Indo-European *só (demonstrative pronoun).

examples.text: You'll soon get used to it.

translations.de: Du wirst dich schnell daran gewöhnen.

translations.pt: Logo você vai se acostumar.

translations.fr: La justice vient toujours, tôt ou tard.
translations.pt: Cedo ou tarde, a justiça sempre chega.

examples.text: We will soon have no more petrol.

translations.de: Wir haben bald kein Benzin mehr.
translations.fr: Nous n'aurons bientôt plus d'essence.
translations.pt: Em breve não teremos mais petróleo.

examples.text: I think I'll come back soon.

translations.de: Ich denke, dass ich bald zurückkommen werde.
translations.fr: Je pense que je serai bientôt de retour.
translations.pt: Acho que voltarei logo.

more.definition: Within a short time; quickly.; Readily; willingly; used with would, or some other word expressing will.
more.etymology: From Middle English sone, from Old English sōna (“immediately, at once”), from Proto-West Germanic *sān(ō), from Proto-Germanic *sēna, *sēnô (“immediately, soon, then”), from *sa (demonstrative pronoun), from Proto-Indo-European *só (demonstrative pronoun).

examples.text: What's the point of your question?

examples.text: I need to ask you some questions.

translations.fr: Je dois vous poser quelques questions.
