more.definition: To forgive; to pardon; to overlook.; To allow to leave, or release from any obligation.; To provide an excuse for; to justify.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Latin excūsāreder. Old French escuserder. Latin excūsāreder. Old French excuseder. From Middle English excusen (verb) and excuse (noun), borrowed from Old French escuser (verb) and excuse (noun), from Latin excūsō, excūsāre (“to excuse, allege in excuse, literally, free from a charge”), from ex (“out”) + causa (“a charge”); see cause, accuse and recuse.

examples.text: Tom moved to Boston three years ago.

translations.de: Tom zog vor drei Jahren nach Boston.
translations.fr: Tom a déménagé à Boston il y a trois ans.
translations.pt: Tom se mudou para Boston há três anos.

examples.text: I gave up smoking a year ago.

translations.de: Ich habe vor einem Jahr mit dem Rauchen aufgehört.
translations.fr: J'ai arrêté de fumer il y a un an.
translations.pt: Deixei de fumar um ano atrás.

examples.text: He came to Japan seven years ago.

translations.de: Er kam vor sieben Jahren nach Japan.
translations.fr: Il est venu au Japon il y a sept ans.
translations.pt: Ele veio para o Japão sete anos atrás.

examples.text: He gave up smoking two years ago.

translations.de: Er hat vor zwei Jahren aufgehört zu rauchen.
translations.fr: Il a arrêté de fumer il y a deux ans.
translations.pt: Ele deixou de fumar há dois anos.

more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₁-der. From Middle English ago, agon (“passed”), past participle of agon (“to depart, escape, pass”), from Old English āgān (“to go away, pass away, go forth, come to pass”), from Proto-Germanic *uz- (“out”), *gāną (“to go”), equivalent to a- + gone, and by surface analysis, a- + go. Cognate with German ergehen (“to come to pass, fare, go forth”).

examples.text: I went to France two years ago.

translations.de: Ich ging vor zwei Jahren nach Frankreich.
translations.fr: Je suis allé en France il y a deux ans.
translations.pt: Eu fui para a França há dois anos.

examples.text: This picture is from three years ago.

translations.de: Dieses Foto ist drei Jahre alt.
translations.fr: Cette photo date d'il y a trois ans.
translations.pt: Esta foto é de três anos atrás.

examples.text: Tom started studying French three years ago.

translations.de: Tom hat vor drei Jahren angefangen, Französisch zu lernen.
translations.fr: Tom commença à étudier le français il y a trois ans.
translations.pt: O Tom começou a estudar francês há três anos.

examples.text: I taught Tom French three years ago.

translations.de: Ich habe Tom vor drei Jahren in Französisch unterrichtet.
translations.fr: J'ai enseigné le français à Tom il y a 3 ans.
translations.pt: Há três anos, ensinei Tom a falar francês.

more.definition: Before now, before the present time
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₁-der. From Middle English ago, agon (“passed”), past participle of agon (“to depart, escape, pass”), from Old English āgān (“to go away, pass away, go forth, come to pass”), from Proto-Germanic *uz- (“out”), *gāną (“to go”), equivalent to a- + gone, and by surface analysis, a- + go. Cognate with German ergehen (“to come to pass, fare, go forth”).

examples.text: Do you suppose it will rain today?

translations.de: Meinst du, dass es heute regnen wird?
translations.fr: Penses-tu qu'il va pleuvoir aujourd'hui ?
translations.pt: Você acha que vai chover hoje?

examples.text: Am I supposed to read it right now?

translations.de: Soll ich es jetzt lesen?
translations.fr: Suis-je censé le lire maintenant ?
translations.pt: Devo lê-lo agora mesmo?

examples.text: Who am I supposed to be looking for?

translations.de: Nach wem soll ich eigentlich suchen?
translations.fr: Qui suis-je censé chercher ?
translations.pt: Quem eu deveria procurar?

examples.text: Is that supposed to scare me?

translations.de: Soll mir das Angst einjagen?
translations.fr: Est-ce censé me faire peur ?
translations.pt: Isso deveria me assustar?

more.definition: To take for granted; to conclude, with less than absolute supporting data; to believe.; To theorize or hypothesize.; To imagine; to believe; to receive as true.
more.etymology: From Middle English supposen, borrowed from Old French supposer, equivalent to prefix sub- (“under”) + poser (“to place”); corresponding in meaning to Latin supponere (“to put under, to substitute, falsify, counterfeit”), suppositum. See pose.

examples.text: I wouldn't wish that on anyone.

translations.de: Das würde ich niemandem wünschen.
translations.fr: Je ne souhaite cela à personne.
translations.pt: Eu não desejaria isso para ninguém.

examples.text: I don't know anyone in Boston.

translations.de: Ich kenne niemanden in Boston.
translations.fr: Je ne connais personne à Boston.
translations.pt: Não conheço ninguém em Boston.

examples.text: Don't tell anyone I'm here.

translations.de: Verrate keinem, dass ich hier bin.
translations.fr: Ne dites à personne que je suis ici.
translations.pt: Não diga a ninguém que estou aqui.

examples.text: I've never told this to anyone.

translations.de: Ich habe das noch nie jemandem gesagt.
translations.fr: Je ne l'ai jamais dit à personne.
translations.pt: Eu nunca contei isso a ninguém.

more.definition: Any person; anybody.
more.etymology: From Middle English eny on, ony one. By surface analysis, any + one.

examples.text: I'll love you until I die.

translations.de: Ich werde dich lieben, bis ich sterbe.
translations.fr: Je t'aimerai jusqu'à ma mort.
translations.pt: Te amarei até morrer.

examples.text: She ignored him until he became rich.

translations.de: Sie ignorierte ihn so lange, bis er reich wurde.
translations.fr: Elle l'ignora jusqu'à ce qu'il devienne riche.
translations.pt: Ela o ignorou até ele ficar rico.

examples.text: We talked until two in the morning.

translations.de: Wir haben uns bis zwei Uhr früh unterhalten.
translations.fr: Nous avons discuté jusqu'à deux heures du matin.
translations.pt: Nós conversamos até as duas da madrugada.

examples.text: Class doesn't begin until eight-thirty.

translations.de: Der Unterricht fängt erst um halb neun an.
translations.fr: La classe ne commence pas avant huit heures et demie.
translations.pt: A aula não começa até as oito e meia.

more.definition: Up to the time that (a condition becomes true).; Before (a condition becoming true).
more.etymology: From Middle English vntil, until, untill, ontil, ontill, perhaps representing a northern variant of Middle English unto (see Modern English unto). By surface analysis, un- (“against; toward; up to”) + till.

examples.text: At our school, we have classes until three.

translations.de: An unserer Schule haben wir Unterricht bis drei Uhr.
translations.fr: Dans notre école, nous avons des cours jusqu'à trois heures.
translations.pt: Na nossa escola, temos aulas até às três.

examples.text: We'll stay until the end.

translations.de: Wir bleiben bis zum Ende.
translations.fr: Nous resterons jusqu'à la fin.
translations.pt: Vamos ficar até o final.

examples.text: The library is open until nine.

translations.de: Die Bibliothek ist bis neun Uhr geöffnet.
translations.fr: La bibliothèque est ouverte jusqu'à neuf heures.
translations.pt: A biblioteca está aberta até as nove.

examples.text: I'll wait here until you get back.

translations.de: Ich werde hier warten, bis du wiederkommst.
translations.fr: J'attendrai ici jusqu'à ce que tu reviennes.
translations.pt: Vou esperar aqui até você voltar.

more.definition: Up to the time of (something happening); pending.; Up to (a certain place); Before (a time).
more.etymology: From Middle English vntil, until, untill, ontil, ontill, perhaps representing a northern variant of Middle English unto (see Modern English unto). By surface analysis, un- (“against; toward; up to”) + till.

examples.text: Tom's goal is to become famous.

translations.de: Toms Ziel ist es, berühmt zu werden.
translations.fr: Devenir célèbre, c'est le but de Tom.
translations.pt: A meta do Tom é se tornar famoso.

examples.text: That's the reason he became angry.

translations.de: Das ist der Grund, warum er wütend wurde.
translations.fr: C'est la raison pour laquelle il s'est mis en colère.
translations.pt: Foi por isso que ele ficou com raiva.

examples.text: She abandoned her hope of becoming a doctor.

translations.de: Sie hat die Hoffnung aufgegeben, Ärztin zu werden.
translations.fr: Elle a abandonné l'espoir d'être médecin.
translations.pt: Ela abandonou a esperança de se tornar médica.

examples.text: Tom wants to become rich and famous.

translations.de: Tom möchte reich und berühmt werden.
translations.fr: Tom veut devenir riche et célèbre.
translations.pt: Tom quer ficar rico e famoso.

more.definition: begin to be; turn into (often with permanent states).; To come about; happen; come into being; arise.; To be appropriate for.
more.etymology: A compound of the sources of be- + come. From Middle English becomen, bicumen, from Old English becuman (“to come (to), approach, arrive, enter, meet with, fall in with; happen, befall; befit”), from Proto-Germanic *bikwemaną (“to come around, come about, come across, come by”), equivalent to be- (“about, around”) + come.

examples.text: The police could not control the mob.

translations.de: Die Polizei konnte die Menge nicht unter Kontrolle halten.
translations.fr: La police ne pouvait contrôler la foule.
translations.pt: A polícia não pôde conter a multidão.

examples.text: The police informed us of the accident.

translations.de: Die Polizei hat uns über den Unfall informiert.
translations.fr: La police nous a informés de l'accident.
translations.pt: A polícia nos informou acerca do acidente.

examples.text: Go away, or I'm calling the police!

translations.de: Geh weg, oder ich rufe die Polizei!
translations.fr: Partez, ou j'appelle la police !
translations.pt: Vá embora ou chamo a polícia!

examples.text: The police officer arrested him for drink-driving.

translations.de: Der Polizist verhaftete ihn wegen Trunkenheit am Steuer.
translations.fr: Le policier l'a arrêté pour conduite en état d'ivresse.
translations.pt: O policial o prendeu por dirigir alcoolizado.

more.definition: A constituted body of officers representing the civil authority of government, empowered to maintain public order and safety, enforce the law, and prevent, detect, and investigate crime.; A department of local (usually municipal) government responsible for general law enforcement.; A branch of the Home Office responsible for general law enforcement within a specific territory.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-tósder. Ancient Greek πολῑτείᾱ (polīteíā)bor. Latin politialbor. Middle French policeder. From Middle French police, from Latin polītīa (“state, government”), from Ancient Greek πολιτεία (politeía). Doublet of policy, polis (“police”), and polity.

examples.text: She drove to the nearest police station.

translations.de: Sie fuhr zum nächsten Polizeirevier.
translations.fr: Elle roula jusqu'au prochain poste de police.
translations.pt: Ela dirigiu até a delegacia mais próxima.

examples.text: Why are people afraid of the police?

translations.de: Warum haben die Leute Angst vor der Polizei?
translations.fr: Pourquoi les gens ont-ils peur de la police ?
translations.pt: Por que as pessoas têm medo da polícia?

examples.text: Go back home and call the police!

translations.de: Gehe zurück nach Hause und rufe die Polizei!
translations.fr: Rentre à la maison, et appelle la police !
translations.pt: Volte para casa e chame a polícia!

examples.text: Tom is being hunted by the police.

translations.de: Tom wird von der Polizei gejagt.
translations.fr: Tom est poursuivi par la police.
translations.pt: Tom está sendo perseguido pela polícia.

more.definition: To enforce the law and keep order among (a group).; To clean up an area.; To enforce norms or standards upon.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-tósder. Ancient Greek πολῑτείᾱ (polīteíā)bor. Latin politialbor. Middle French policeder. From Middle French police, from Latin polītīa (“state, government”), from Ancient Greek πολιτεία (politeía). Doublet of policy, polis (“police”), and polity.

examples.text: Toki Pona is a charming young lady.

translations.de: Toki Pona ist eine charmante Jungfrau.
translations.fr: Le toki pona est une jeune femme charmante.
translations.pt: Toki Pona é uma jovem encantadora.

examples.text: I'm a lot younger than Tom.

translations.de: Ich bin viel jünger als Tom.
translations.fr: Je suis beaucoup plus jeune que Tom.
translations.pt: Eu sou muito mais novo que Tom.

examples.text: His youngest son is five years old.

translations.de: Sein jüngster Sohn ist fünf Jahre alt.
translations.fr: Son plus jeune enfant a cinq ans.
translations.pt: O caçula dela tem cinco anos.

examples.text: You're too young to get married.

translations.de: Du bist zu jung, um zu heiraten.
translations.fr: Tu es trop jeune pour te marier.
translations.pt: Você é jovem demais para se casar.

more.definition: In the early part of growth or life; born not long ago.; At an early stage of existence or development; having recently come into existence.; advanced in age; (far towards or) at a specified stage of existence or age.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English yong, yonge, from Old English ġeong, from Proto-West Germanic *jung, from Proto-Germanic *jungaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂yuHn̥ḱós, from *h₂yuh₁en- (“young”).

examples.text: The shop was crowded with young people.

translations.de: Das Geschäft war voll mit jungen Leuten.
translations.fr: Le magasin était plein de jeunes gens.
translations.pt: A loja estava lotada por adolescentes.

examples.text: The Beatles are popular among young people.

translations.de: Die Beatles sind populär unter der Jugend.
translations.fr: Les Beatles sont connus des jeunes gens.
translations.pt: Os Beatles são populares entre os jovens.

examples.text: Rock is the music of the young.

translations.de: Rock ist die Musik der Jungen.
translations.fr: Le rock est la musique des jeunes.
translations.pt: O rock é a música dos jovens.

examples.text: Dozens of young people attended the demonstration.

translations.de: Dutzende Jugendlicher nahmen an der Demonstration teil.
translations.fr: Des dizaines de jeunes ont assisté à la manifestation.
translations.pt: Dezenas de jovens assistiram a demonstração.

more.definition: Offspring, especially the immature offspring of animals.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English yong, yonge, from Old English ġeong, from Proto-West Germanic *jung, from Proto-Germanic *jungaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂yuHn̥ḱós, from *h₂yuh₁en- (“young”).

examples.text: He likes being surrounded by young people.

translations.de: Es gefällt ihm, von jungen Leuten umgeben zu sein.
translations.fr: Il aime être entouré de jeunes.
translations.pt: Ele gosta de estar rodeado por pessoas jovens.

examples.text: His novels are popular among young people.

translations.de: Seine Romane sind bei jungen Leuten beliebt.
translations.fr: Ses romans sont prisés par les jeunes gens.
translations.pt: Seus romances são populares entre os jovens.

examples.text: I did smoke when I was young.

translations.de: Ich rauchte, als ich jung war.
translations.fr: Je fumais quand j'étais jeune.
translations.pt: Eu fumava quando eu era jovem.

examples.text: You are too young to travel alone.

translations.de: Du bist zu jung, um alleine zu reisen.
translations.fr: Tu es trop jeune pour voyager seul.
translations.pt: Você é jovem demais para viajar sozinha.

more.definition: To become or seem to become younger.; To cause to appear younger.; To exhibit younging.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English yong, yonge, from Old English ġeong, from Proto-West Germanic *jung, from Proto-Germanic *jungaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂yuHn̥ḱós, from *h₂yuh₁en- (“young”).

examples.text: Did you hear about the fire yesterday?

translations.de: Hast du von dem Brand gestern gehört?
translations.fr: As-tu entendu parler de l'incendie d'hier ?
translations.pt: Você ouviu sobre o incêndio de ontem?

examples.text: We make the fire with wood.

translations.de: Wir machen das Feuer mit Holz.
translations.fr: Nous faisons le feu avec du bois.
translations.pt: Fazemos o fogo com madeira.

examples.text: There is fire under the bridge.

translations.de: Es ist Feuer unter der Brücke.
translations.fr: Il y a du feu sous le pont.
translations.pt: Há fogo debaixo da ponte.

examples.text: The fire got out of control.

translations.de: Das Feuer ist außer Kontrolle geraten.
translations.fr: Le feu est devenu incontrôlable.
translations.pt: O fogo saiu de controle.

more.definition: Amazing; excellent.
more.etymology: From Middle English fyr, from Old English fȳr (“fire”), from Proto-West Germanic *fuir, from *fuïr, a regularised form of Proto-Germanic *fōr (“fire”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *péh₂wr̥.

examples.text: It's dangerous to play with fire.

translations.de: Es ist gefährlich, mit dem Feuer zu spielen.
translations.fr: Il est dangereux de jouer avec le feu.
translations.pt: É perigoso brincar com fogo.

examples.text: The soldiers set fire to the barn.

translations.de: Die Soldaten haben die Scheune angezündet.
translations.fr: Les soldats ont mis le feu à la grange.
translations.pt: Os soldados atearam fogo ao celeiro.

examples.text: Why do you think animals dread fire?

translations.de: Warum denkst du, dass Tiere Angst vor Feuer haben?
translations.fr: Pourquoi pensez-vous que les animaux craignent le feu ?
translations.pt: Por que tu achas que os animais temem o fogo?

examples.text: Where there is smoke, there is fire.

translations.de: Es gibt keinen Rauch ohne ein Feuer.
translations.fr: Il ne peut y avoir de fumée sans feu.
translations.pt: Onde se eleva fumaça aí se encontra fogo.

more.definition: Command to shoot with firearms.
more.etymology: From Middle English firen, fyren, furen, from Old English fȳrian (“to make a fire”), from the noun (see above). Cognate with Old Frisian fioria (“to light a fire”), Saterland Frisian fjuurje (“to fire”), Middle Dutch vûren, vueren, vieren (“to set fire”), Dutch vuren (“to fire, shoot”), Old High German fiuren (“to ignite, set on fire”), German feuern (“to fire”).

examples.text: Tom's car is on fire.

translations.de: Toms Auto brennt.
translations.fr: La voiture de Tom brûle.
translations.pt: O carro de Tom está em chamas.

examples.text: Look! The car is on fire!

translations.de: Sieh nur! Der Wagen brennt!
translations.fr: Regarde ! La voiture est en feu !
translations.pt: Olha! O carro está pegando fogo!

examples.text: She set fire to a tent.

translations.de: Sie hat ein Zelt angezündet.
translations.fr: Elle a mis le feu à une tente.
translations.pt: Ela ateou fogo a uma barraca.

examples.text: Tom's house is on fire.

translations.de: Toms Haus steht in Flammen.
translations.fr: La maison de Tom est en feu.
translations.pt: A casa do Tom está pegando fogo.

more.definition: A (usually self-sustaining) chemical reaction involving the bonding of oxygen with carbon or other fuel, with the production of heat and the presence of flame or smouldering.; An instance of this chemical reaction, especially when intentionally created and maintained in a specific location to a useful end (such as a campfire or a hearth fire).; The occurrence, often accidental, of fire in a certain place, causing damage and danger.
more.etymology: From Middle English fyr, from Old English fȳr (“fire”), from Proto-West Germanic *fuir, from *fuïr, a regularised form of Proto-Germanic *fōr (“fire”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *péh₂wr̥.

examples.text: Another mistake, and he will be fired.

translations.de: Noch ein Fehler und er wird gefeuert.
translations.fr: Une autre erreur et il sera renvoyé.
translations.pt: Mais um erro e ele será demitido.

examples.text: Please keep the fire from going out.

translations.de: Gib bitte acht, dass das Feuer nicht erlischt!
translations.fr: Veille à ce que le feu ne s'éteigne pas, s'il te plaît.
translations.pt: Por favor, não deixe o fogo se apagar.

examples.text: It only adds fuel to the fire.

translations.de: Das gießt nur Öl ins Feuer.
translations.fr: Ça ne fait qu'ajouter de l'huile sur le feu.
translations.pt: Só bota palha na fogueira.

examples.text: The origin of the fire is unknown.

translations.de: Der Ursprung des Feuers ist unbekannt.
translations.fr: L'origine de l'incendie est inconnue.
translations.pt: A origem do incêndio é desconhecida.

more.definition: To set (something, often a building) on fire.; To heat as with fire, but without setting on fire, as ceramic, metal objects, etc.; To drive away by setting a fire.
more.etymology: From Middle English firen, fyren, furen, from Old English fȳrian (“to make a fire”), from the noun (see above). Cognate with Old Frisian fioria (“to light a fire”), Saterland Frisian fjuurje (“to fire”), Middle Dutch vûren, vueren, vieren (“to set fire”), Dutch vuren (“to fire, shoot”), Old High German fiuren (“to ignite, set on fire”), German feuern (“to fire”).

examples.text: You're part of the family.

translations.de: Du bist Teil der Familie.
translations.fr: Tu fais partie de la famille.
translations.pt: Vocês são parte da família.

examples.text: Music is a part of me.

translations.de: Die Musik ist ein Teil von mir.
translations.fr: La musique fait partie de moi.
translations.pt: A música faz parte de mim.

examples.text: I have a part-time job.

translations.de: Ich habe eine Teilzeitstelle.
translations.fr: J'ai un travail à temps partiel.
translations.pt: Tenho um emprego de meio período.

examples.text: Shut up! We'll miss the best part.

translations.de: Halt den Mund! Wir verpassen den besten Teil.
translations.fr: Tais-toi ! On va rater le meilleur.
translations.pt: Cale-se! Perderemos a melhor parte.

more.definition: Fractional; partial.
more.etymology: From Middle English part, from the noun.

examples.text: Do you have a part-time job?

translations.de: Hast du eine Teilzeitstelle?
translations.fr: As-tu un travail à temps partiel ?
translations.pt: Você tem um emprego de meio período?

examples.text: Tom acted the part of a sailor.

translations.de: Tom spielte die Rolle eines Matrosen.
translations.fr: Tom jouait le rôle d'un marin.
translations.pt: O Tom fez o papel de um marinheiro.

examples.text: That's the part I liked best.

translations.de: Dies ist der Teil, der mir am besten gefallen hat.
translations.fr: C'est la partie que j'ai préférée.
translations.pt: Essa é a parte de que eu mais gostei.

examples.text: Where is the northern part of the city?

translations.de: Wo ist der nördliche Teil der Stadt?
translations.fr: Où se trouve la partie nord de la ville ?
translations.pt: Onde fica a parte norte da cidade?

more.definition: Partly; partially; fractionally.; to a partial degree.
more.etymology: From Middle English part, from the noun.

examples.text: Death is an integral part of life.

translations.de: Der Tod ist ein fester Bestandteil des Lebens.
translations.fr: La mort est une part intégrante de la vie.
translations.pt: A morte é uma parte integral da vida.

examples.text: Divide this line into twenty equal parts.

translations.de: Teile diese Strecke in zwanzig gleiche Teile.
translations.fr: Divisez cette droite en vingt segments égaux.
translations.pt: Divida esta linha em vinte partes iguais.

examples.text: What part of Canada are you from?

translations.de: Aus welchem Teil von Kanada kommst du?
translations.fr: De quelle partie du Canada es-tu ?
translations.pt: De qual parte do Canadá você é?

examples.text: He took part in the Olympic Games.

translations.de: Er hat an den Olympischen Spielen teilgenommen.
translations.fr: Il a participé aux Jeux olympiques.
translations.pt: Ele participou dos Jogos Olímpicos.

more.definition: A fraction of a whole.; A distinct element of something larger.; A group inside a larger group.
more.etymology: Old French partbor. Latin partembor. From Middle English part, from Old English part (“part”) and Old French part (“part”); both from Latin partem, accusative of pars (“piece, portion, share, side, party, faction, role, character, lot, fate, task, lesson, part, member”), from Proto-Indo-European *par-, *per- (“to sell, exchange”). Akin to Latin portiō (“a portion, part”), parāre (“to make ready, prepare”).

examples.text: What part of Australia are you from?

translations.de: Aus welchem Teil Australiens kommst du?
translations.fr: De quel coin de l'Australie viens-tu ?
translations.pt: De qual parte da Austrália você é?

examples.text: All Gaul is divided into three parts.

translations.de: Ganz Gallien ist in drei Teile geteilt.
translations.fr: Toute la Gaule est divisée en trois parties.
translations.pt: Toda a Gália está dividida em três partes.

examples.text: I hate this part of the movie.

translations.de: Ich hasse diesen Teil des Films.
translations.fr: Je déteste cette partie du film.
translations.pt: Odeio esta parte do filme.

examples.text: I like being part of this group.

translations.de: Ich gehöre gern zu dieser Gruppe.
translations.fr: J'aime faire partie de ce groupe.
translations.pt: Eu gosto de ser parte deste grupo.

more.definition: To leave the company of (each other, or someone/something [with with or from]).; To divide in two.; To cut hair with a parting.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-yétider. Old French partirbor. Inherited from Middle English parten, borrowed from Old French partir.

examples.text: Tom and I were business partners.

translations.de: Tom und ich waren Geschäftspartner.
translations.fr: Tom et moi étions associés.
translations.pt: Tom e eu éramos sócios.

examples.text: I'm in town on business.

translations.de: Ich bin geschäftlich in der Stadt.
translations.fr: Je suis en ville pour affaires.
translations.pt: Estou na cidade a negócios.

examples.text: I'm not here on business.

translations.de: Ich bin nicht geschäftlich hier.
translations.fr: Je ne suis pas ici pour affaires.
translations.pt: Não estou aqui a negócios.

examples.text: This is none of your business.

translations.de: Das hier geht dich nichts an!
translations.fr: Ce ne sont pas tes affaires.
translations.pt: Isto não é da vossa conta.

more.definition: Of, to, pertaining to, or used for purposes of conducting trade, commerce, governance, advocacy or other professional purposes.; Professional, businesslike, having concern for good business practice.; Supporting business, conducive to the conduct of business.
more.etymology: From Middle English busines, busynes, businesse, bisynes, from Old English bisiġnes (“business, busyness”), equivalent to busy + -ness. Doublet of busyness. Sense 17 (something very good, top quality), possibly derives from "the bee's knees"

examples.text: He inherited the business from his father.

translations.de: Er erbte das Geschäft von seinem Vater.
translations.fr: Il hérita le commerce de son père.
translations.pt: Ele herdou o negócio do seu pai.

examples.text: He is planning to launch his business.

translations.de: Er beabsichtigt sein Geschäft zu eröffnen.
translations.fr: Il projette de lancer son entreprise.
translations.pt: Ele está pensando em começar seu próprio negócio.

examples.text: It's none of our business.

translations.de: Das geht dich nichts an.
translations.fr: Cela ne nous regarde pas.
translations.pt: Não é da nossa conta.

examples.text: That's none of our business.

translations.de: Das geht uns nichts an.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas notre problème.
translations.pt: Isso não é de nossa conta.

more.definition: A specific commercial enterprise or establishment.; A person's occupation, work, or trade.; Commercial, industrial, or professional activity.
more.etymology: From Middle English busines, busynes, businesse, bisynes, from Old English bisiġnes (“business, busyness”), equivalent to busy + -ness. Doublet of busyness. Sense 17 (something very good, top quality), possibly derives from "the bee's knees"

examples.text: I haven't found a doctor yet.

translations.de: Ich habe noch keinen Arzt gefunden.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas encore trouvé de médecin.
translations.pt: Ainda não encontrei um médico.

examples.text: The doctors heal many sick people.

translations.de: Die Ärzte heilen viele Kranke.
translations.fr: Les médecins guérissent de nombreux malades.
translations.pt: Os médicos curam muitos doentes.

examples.text: She thought that I was a doctor.

translations.de: Sie dachte, dass ich Ärztin sei.
translations.fr: Elle pensait que j'étais toubib.
translations.pt: Ela pensava que eu era um médico.

examples.text: An uncle of mine is a doctor.

translations.de: Ein Onkel von mir ist Arzt.
translations.fr: Un oncle à moi est médecin.
translations.pt: Um tio meu é médico.

more.definition: A physician; a member of the medical profession; one who is trained and licensed to heal the sick or injured. The final examination and qualification may award a doctor degree in which case the post-nominal letters are DO, DPM, MD, DMD, or DDS in the US, or MBBS or BDS in the UK.; A person who has attained a doctorate, such as a Ph.D. or Th.D. or one of many other terminal degrees conferred by a college or university.; A veterinarian; a medical practitioner who treats non-human animals.
more.etymology: Ancient Greek διδάσκω (didáskō)sl. Latin doctorlbor. Anglo-Norman doctourder. From Middle English doctor, doctour (“an expert, authority on a subject”), from Anglo-Norman doctour, from Latin doctor (“teacher”), from doceō (“to teach”).

examples.text: The doctor treated the patient with antibiotics.

translations.de: Der Arzt behandelte den Patienten mit Antibiotika.
translations.fr: Le médecin soigna le patient avec des antibiotiques.
translations.pt: O médico tratou a paciente com antibióticos.

examples.text: Tom spoke to the doctors in French.

translations.de: Tom sprach mit den Ärzten französisch.
translations.fr: Tom parla aux médecins en français.
translations.pt: Tom conversou com os médicos em francês.

examples.text: I know you're not a doctor.

translations.de: Ich weiß, dass du kein Arzt bist.
translations.fr: Je sais que tu n'es pas médecin.
translations.pt: Eu sei que você não é médico.

examples.text: Christiaan Barnard was a South African doctor.

translations.de: Christiaan Barnard war ein südafrikanischer Arzt.
translations.fr: Christiaan Barnard était un médecin sud-africain.
translations.pt: Christiaan Barnard foi um médico sul-africano.

more.definition: To act as a medical doctor to.; To act as a medical doctor.; To make (someone) into an (academic) doctor; to confer a doctorate upon.
more.etymology: Ancient Greek διδάσκω (didáskō)sl. Latin doctorlbor. Anglo-Norman doctourder. From Middle English doctor, doctour (“an expert, authority on a subject”), from Anglo-Norman doctour, from Latin doctor (“teacher”), from doceō (“to teach”).

examples.text: It is too good to be true.

translations.de: Das ist zu schön, um wahr zu sein.
translations.fr: C'est trop beau pour être vrai.
translations.pt: É bom demais para ser verdade.

examples.text: That's too good to be true.

translations.de: Das ist zu schön, um wahr zu sein.
translations.fr: C'est trop beau pour être vrai.
translations.pt: Isso é bom demais para ser verdade.

examples.text: What they told you is not true.

translations.de: Was sie dir erzählt haben, ist nicht wahr.
translations.fr: Ce qu'ils vous ont dit n'est pas vrai.
translations.pt: O que eles te contaram não é verdade.

examples.text: Her dream will one day come true.

translations.de: Ihr Traum wird eines Tages wahr werden.
translations.fr: Un jour ses rêves se réaliseront.
translations.pt: O sonho dela um dia se realizará.

more.definition: Conforming to the actual state of reality or fact; factually correct.; As an ellipsis of "(while) it is true (that)", used to start a sentence; Conforming to a rule or pattern; exact; accurate.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *drewH-der. From Middle English treowe, trew, trewe, triwe, true, trwe, from Old English trēowe, trīewe (“faithful, true”), from Proto-Germanic *triwwiz (“faithful, true”), from pre-Germanic *drewh₂yos, from Proto-Indo-European *drewH- (“firm, hard, true”).

examples.text: Her dream has come true at last.

translations.de: Ihr Traum wurde endlich wahr.
translations.fr: Son rêve s'est enfin réalisé.
translations.pt: O sonho dela se tornou realidade finalmente.

examples.text: What he said yesterday is not true.

translations.de: Was er gestern gesagt hat, stimmt nicht.
translations.fr: Ce qu'il a dit hier n'est pas vrai.
translations.pt: O que ele disse ontem não é verdade.

examples.text: A true friend would've helped me.

translations.de: Ein echter Freund hätte mir geholfen.
translations.fr: Un véritable ami m'aurait aidé.
translations.pt: Um amigo de verdade teria me ajudado.

examples.text: It's time my dream came true.

translations.de: Es ist Zeit, dass sich mein Traum erfüllte.
translations.fr: Il est temps que mon rêve se réalise.
translations.pt: É a hora do meu sonho se tornar realidade.

more.definition: Accurately; in alignment.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *drewH-der. From Middle English treowe, trew, trewe, triwe, true, trwe, from Old English trēowe, trīewe (“faithful, true”), from Proto-Germanic *triwwiz (“faithful, true”), from pre-Germanic *drewh₂yos, from Proto-Indo-European *drewH- (“firm, hard, true”).

examples.text: A true sacrifice is a false sacrifice.

translations.de: Ein echtes Opfer ist ein falsches Opfer.
translations.fr: Un vrai sacrifice est un faux sacrifice.
translations.pt: Um verdadeiro sacrifício é um falso sacrifício.

examples.text: Is it true Tom won the race?

translations.de: Stimmt es, dass Tom das Rennen gewonnen hat?
translations.fr: Est-il vrai que Tom a gagné la course ?
translations.pt: É verdade que Tom venceu a corrida?

examples.text: People used to think that was true.

translations.de: Die Menschen hielten das einst für wahr.
translations.fr: Les gens pensaient que c'était vrai.
translations.pt: As pessoas pensavam que isso fosse verdade.

examples.text: I don't think it's true.

translations.de: Ich halte es nicht für wahr.
translations.fr: Je ne pense pas que ce soit vrai.
translations.pt: Não acho que isso seja verdade.

more.definition: The state of being in alignment.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *drewH-der. From Middle English treowe, trew, trewe, triwe, true, trwe, from Old English trēowe, trīewe (“faithful, true”), from Proto-Germanic *triwwiz (“faithful, true”), from pre-Germanic *drewh₂yos, from Proto-Indo-European *drewH- (“firm, hard, true”).

examples.text: I can't believe it's true.

translations.de: Ich kann nicht glauben, dass das stimmt.
translations.fr: Je n'arrive pas à croire que ce soit vrai.
translations.pt: Não consigo acreditar que seja verdade.

examples.text: It's true that Americans love pizza.

translations.de: Es stimmt, dass Amerikaner Pizza lieben.
translations.fr: C'est vrai que les américains adorent la pizza.
translations.pt: É verdade que os americanos adoram pizza.

examples.text: It seemed too good to be true.

translations.de: Es schien zu schön, um wahr zu sein.
translations.fr: Il sembla trop bien pour être vrai.
translations.pt: Parecia bom demais para ser verdade.

examples.text: I believe what you said is true.

translations.de: Ich glaube, was du gesagt hast, ist wahr.
translations.fr: Je crois que ce que tu as dit est vrai.
translations.pt: Creio que o que você disse é verdade.

more.definition: To straighten (something that is supposed to be straight).; To make even, level, symmetrical, or accurate, align; adjust (often followed by up).
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *drewH-der. From Middle English treowe, trew, trewe, triwe, true, trwe, from Old English trēowe, trīewe (“faithful, true”), from Proto-Germanic *triwwiz (“faithful, true”), from pre-Germanic *drewh₂yos, from Proto-Indo-European *drewH- (“firm, hard, true”).

examples.text: Can you will yourself to fall asleep?

translations.de: Kannst du dich dazu zwingen einzuschlafen?
translations.fr: Est-ce que tu peux te forcer à dormir ?
translations.pt: Você pode se forçar a dormir?

examples.text: I heard something fall to the ground.

translations.de: Ich hörte etwas auf den Boden fallen.
translations.fr: J'ai entendu quelque chose tomber par terre.
translations.pt: Ouvi algo cair no chão.

examples.text: I dream as soon as I fall asleep.

translations.de: Ich träume, sobald ich einschlafe.
translations.fr: Je rêve dès que je m'endors.
translations.pt: Eu sonho assim que adormeço.

examples.text: We fall and we get up.

translations.de: Wir fallen und wir stehen auf.
translations.fr: On tombe et on se relève.
translations.pt: Nós caímos e nos levantamos.

more.definition: The cry given when a whale is sighted, or harpooned.
more.etymology: Perhaps from the north-eastern Scottish pronunciation of whale.

examples.text: Three climbers were killed in a rock fall.

translations.de: Drei Bergsteiger kamen bei einem Steinschlag ums Leben.
translations.fr: Trois grimpeurs ont été tués lors d'une chute de pierres.
translations.pt: Três alpinistas foram mortos em uma queda de pedras.

examples.text: Christmas falls on Sunday this year.

translations.de: Weihnachten fällt dieses Jahr auf einen Sonntag.
translations.fr: Noël tombe un dimanche cette année.
translations.pt: O Natal cai num domingo este ano.

examples.text: I didn't fall in love.

translations.de: Ich habe mich nicht verliebt.
translations.fr: Je ne suis pas tombé amoureux.
translations.pt: Eu não me apaixonei.

examples.text: He was lame after the fall.

translations.de: Er erlahmte durch den Sturz.
translations.fr: Il boitait après la chute.
translations.pt: Ele ficou coxo depois da queda.

more.definition: The act of moving to a lower position under the effect of gravity.; A reduction in quantity, pitch, etc.; A waterfall.
more.etymology: Verb from Middle English fallen, from Old English feallan (“to fall, fail, decay, die, attack”), from Proto-West Germanic *fallan (“to fall”), from Proto-Germanic *fallaną (“to fall”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃elh₁- (“to collapse, fall; to destroy”).

examples.text: Three hundred millimeters of precipitation fell overnight.

translations.de: Über Nacht fielen dreihundert Millimeter Niederschlag.
translations.fr: Trois cent millimètres de précipitation sont tombés pendant la nuit.
translations.pt: Trezentos milímetros de precipitação caíram durante a noite.

examples.text: In the autumn, leaves fall from trees.

translations.de: Im Herbst fallen die Blätter von den Bäumen.
translations.fr: En automne, les feuilles tombent des arbres.
translations.pt: No outono, as folhas caem das árvores.

examples.text: I've fallen in love with you.

translations.de: Ich habe mich in Sie verliebt.
translations.fr: Je suis tombé amoureux de toi.
translations.pt: Eu me apaixonei por você.

examples.text: I think I'm falling in love.

translations.de: Ich glaube, ich bin dabei, mich zu verlieben.
translations.fr: Je pense que je suis en train de tomber amoureux.
translations.pt: Acho que estou me apaixonando.

more.definition: To move to a lower position under the effect of gravity.; To come down, to drop or descend.; To come as if by dropping down.
more.etymology: Verb from Middle English fallen, from Old English feallan (“to fall, fail, decay, die, attack”), from Proto-West Germanic *fallan (“to fall”), from Proto-Germanic *fallaną (“to fall”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃elh₁- (“to collapse, fall; to destroy”).

examples.text: Do you have plans for this weekend?

translations.de: Hast du Pläne für dieses Wochenende?
translations.fr: Vous avez des projets pour ce week-end ?
translations.pt: Você tem planos para esse fim de semana?

examples.text: I'm assuming you have a plan.

translations.de: Ich nehme an, du hast einen Plan.
translations.fr: Je suppose que tu disposes d'un plan.
translations.pt: Eu estou assumindo que você tem um plano.

examples.text: What are your plans for the weekend?

translations.de: Was hast du am Wochenende vor?
translations.fr: Quels sont tes plans pour le week-end ?
translations.pt: Quais são os seus planos para o fim de semana?

examples.text: Do you plan to buy that car?

translations.de: Hast du vor, dieses Auto zu kaufen?
translations.fr: Prévois-tu d'acheter cette voiture ?
translations.pt: Você planeja comprar esse carro?

more.definition: A drawing showing technical details of a building, machine, etc., with unwanted details omitted, and often using symbols rather than detailed drawing to represent doors, valves, etc.; A set of intended actions, usually mutually related, through which one expects to achieve a goal.; A two-dimensional drawing of a building as seen from above with obscuring or irrelevant details such as roof removed, or of a floor of a building, revealing the internal layout; as distinct from the elevation.
more.etymology: Borrowed from French plan (“flat surface, ground plot, map”), from Latin plānus. Some sources also argue for influence or alteration of French plant, from plantar, from Latin plantāre (“set, fix in place”). Doublet of llano, piano, plane, and plain.

examples.text: Do you have any plans for tomorrow?

translations.de: Hast du für morgen etwas geplant?
translations.fr: Tu as quelque chose de prévu, demain ?
translations.pt: Você tem planos para amanhã?

examples.text: This plan had little chance of success.

translations.de: Dieser Plan hatte geringe Erfolgschancen.
translations.fr: Ce plan avait peu de chance de réussite.
translations.pt: Este plano tinha poucas chances de ser bem-sucedido.

examples.text: What you're planning to do is dangerous.

translations.de: Das, was Sie vorhaben, ist gefährlich.
translations.fr: Ce que tu prévois de faire est dangereux.
translations.pt: O que você está planejando fazer é perigoso.

examples.text: The workers are against the new plan.

translations.de: Die Arbeiter sind gegen den neuen Plan.
translations.fr: Les employés sont contre le nouveau plan.
translations.pt: Os trabalhadores são contras o novo plano.

more.definition: To design (a building, machine, etc.).; To create a plan for.; To intend.
more.etymology: Borrowed from French plan (“flat surface, ground plot, map”), from Latin plānus. Some sources also argue for influence or alteration of French plant, from plantar, from Latin plantāre (“set, fix in place”). Doublet of llano, piano, plane, and plain.

examples.text: You can't save me.

translations.de: Du kannst mich nicht retten.
translations.fr: Tu ne peux pas me sauver.
translations.pt: Você não pode me salvar.

examples.text: I tried to save you.

translations.de: Ich habe versucht, Sie zu retten.
translations.fr: J'ai tenté de te sauver.
translations.pt: Eu tentei te salvar.

examples.text: I can't save you.

translations.de: Ich kann Sie nicht retten.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas te sauver.
translations.pt: Não posso salvá-lo.

examples.text: Can we save the planet?

translations.de: Können wir den Planeten retten?
translations.fr: Pouvons-nous sauver la planète ?
translations.pt: Podemos salvar o planeta?

more.definition: Unless; except.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *solh₂-der. Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Old French sauverbor. From Middle English saven, sauven, a borrowing from Old French sauver, from Late Latin salvāre (“to save”). Displaced native Old English nerian.

examples.text: I must save her at all costs.

translations.de: Ich muss sie retten, koste es, was es wolle.
translations.fr: Je dois à tout prix la sauver.
translations.pt: Eu devo salvá-la a qualquer custo.

examples.text: This highway saves us a lot of time.

translations.de: Diese Autobahn spart uns eine Menge Zeit.
translations.fr: Cette autoroute nous fait gagner beaucoup de temps.
translations.pt: Esta rodovia nos economiza muito tempo.

examples.text: I'm here to save you.

translations.de: Ich bin hier, um dich zu retten.
translations.fr: Je suis ici pour te sauver.
translations.pt: Estou aqui para te salvar.

examples.text: Tom always flies economy class to save money.

translations.de: Um Geld zu sparen, fliegt Tom immer dritter Klasse.
translations.fr: Tom prend toujours des avions en classe économique pour économiser de l'argent.
translations.pt: Tom sempre voa na classe econômica para economizar dinheiro.

more.definition: An instance of preventing (further) harm or difficulty.; In various sports, a block that prevents an opponent from scoring.; A successful attempt by a relief pitcher to preserve the win of another pitcher on one's team.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *solh₂-der. Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Old French sauverbor. From Middle English saven, sauven, a borrowing from Old French sauver, from Late Latin salvāre (“to save”). Displaced native Old English nerian.

examples.text: I've come to save the princess.

translations.de: Ich bin gekommen, um die Prinzessin zu retten.
translations.fr: Je suis venu sauver la princesse.
translations.pt: Eu vim para salvar a princesa.

examples.text: She risked her life to save him.

translations.de: Sie riskierte ihr Leben, um ihn zu retten.
translations.fr: Elle risqua sa vie pour le sauver.
translations.pt: Ela arriscou sua vida para salvá-lo.

examples.text: Nothing but peace can save the world.

translations.de: Nur Frieden kann die Welt retten.
translations.fr: Seule la paix peut sauver le monde.
translations.pt: Somente a paz pode salvar o mundo.

examples.text: I had hoped to save more money.

translations.de: Ich hatte gehofft, mehr Geld zu sparen.
translations.fr: J'avais espéré épargner davantage d'argent.
translations.pt: Queria ter poupado mais dinheiro.

more.definition: Except; with the exception of.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *solh₂-der. Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Old French sauverbor. From Middle English saven, sauven, a borrowing from Old French sauver, from Late Latin salvāre (“to save”). Displaced native Old English nerian.

examples.text: The policeman saved the child from drowning.

translations.de: Der Polizist rettete das Kind vor dem Ertrinken.
translations.fr: Le policier a sauvé l'enfant de la noyade.
translations.pt: O policial salvou o menino do afogamento.

examples.text: I'm trying to save money.

translations.de: Ich versuche, Geld zu sparen.
translations.fr: J'essaie d'économiser de l'argent.
translations.pt: Estou tentando guardar dinheiro.

examples.text: The dog saved the girl's life.

translations.de: Der Hund hat dem Mädchen das Leben gerettet.
translations.fr: Le chien a sauvé la vie de la fille.
translations.pt: O cachorro salvou a vida da menina.

examples.text: How could I have saved them?

translations.de: Wie hätte ich sie retten können?
translations.fr: Comment aurais-je pu les sauver ?
translations.pt: Como eu poderia tê-los salvo?

more.definition: To help (somebody) to survive, or rescue (somebody or something) from harm.; To keep (something) safe; to safeguard.; To spare (somebody) (from effort, or from something undesirable).
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *solh₂-der. Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Old French sauverbor. From Middle English saven, sauven, a borrowing from Old French sauver, from Late Latin salvāre (“to save”). Displaced native Old English nerian.

examples.text: They sat across from each other.

translations.de: Sie setzten sich einander gegenüber.
translations.fr: Ils se sont assis l'un en face de l'autre.
translations.pt: Eles se sentaram um em frente ao outro.

examples.text: We'll see each other tonight?

translations.de: Wir sehen uns heute Abend?
translations.fr: On se verra ce soir ?
translations.pt: Hoje à noite nos veremos?

examples.text: Tom and Mary love each other very much.

translations.de: Tom und Maria lieben sich sehr.
translations.fr: Tom et Mary s'aiment beaucoup.
translations.pt: Tom e Mary querem-se muito.

examples.text: I think we need each other.

translations.de: Ich glaube, wir brauchen einander.
translations.fr: Je pense que nous avons besoin l'un de l'autre.
translations.pt: Acho que precisamos um do outro.

more.definition: For one; apiece; per.; Individually; separately; used in a sentence with a plural subject to indicate that the action or state described by the verb applies to all members of the described group individually, rather than collectively to the entire group.
more.etymology: From Middle English ech, eche, elche, ilch, from Old English ǣlċ, contraction of ǣġhwelċ. Comparable to aye + alike. Compare Scots ilk, elk (“each, every”), Saterland Frisian älk (“each”), West Frisian elk, elts (“each”), Dutch elk (“each”), Low German elk, ellik (“each”), German Low German elk, elke (“each, every”), German jeglicher (“any”). By surface analysis, Old English ā + which.

examples.text: Tom and Mary are seeing each other secretly.

translations.de: Tom und Maria treffen sich heimlich.
translations.fr: Tom et Marie ont une liaison secrète.
translations.pt: Tom e Mary estão se vendo em segredo.

examples.text: We're meant for each other.

translations.de: Wir sind füreinander bestimmt.
translations.fr: Nous sommes faits l'un pour l'autre.
translations.pt: Fomos feitos um para o outro.

examples.text: We'll see each other again.

translations.de: Wir werden uns wiedersehen.
translations.fr: Nous nous reverrons.
translations.pt: Nós nos veremos novamente.

examples.text: Do you guys know each other?

translations.de: Kennt ihr euch?
translations.fr: Vous vous connaissez ?
translations.pt: Vocês se conhecem?

more.definition: All; every; qualifying a singular noun, indicating all examples of the thing so named seen as individual or separate items (compare every).
more.etymology: From Middle English ech, eche, elche, ilch, from Old English ǣlċ, contraction of ǣġhwelċ. Comparable to aye + alike. Compare Scots ilk, elk (“each, every”), Saterland Frisian älk (“each”), West Frisian elk, elts (“each”), Dutch elk (“each”), Low German elk, ellik (“each”), German Low German elk, elke (“each, every”), German jeglicher (“any”). By surface analysis, Old English ā + which.

examples.text: We were meant for each other.

translations.de: Wir waren füreinander bestimmt.
translations.fr: Nous étions faits l'un pour l'autre.
translations.pt: Fomos feitos um para o outro.

examples.text: Do you two know each other?

translations.de: Kennt ihr beiden euch?
translations.fr: Vous vous connaissez toutes les deux ?
translations.pt: Vocês dois se conhecem?

examples.text: You guys love each other, don't you?

translations.de: Ihr liebt einander, nicht wahr?

more.definition: An individual item: the least quantitative unit in a grouping.
more.etymology: From Middle English ech, eche, elche, ilch, from Old English ǣlċ, contraction of ǣġhwelċ. Comparable to aye + alike. Compare Scots ilk, elk (“each, every”), Saterland Frisian älk (“each”), West Frisian elk, elts (“each”), Dutch elk (“each”), Low German elk, ellik (“each”), German Low German elk, elke (“each, every”), German jeglicher (“any”). By surface analysis, Old English ā + which.

more.definition: Every one/thing individually or one by one.
more.etymology: From Middle English ech, eche, elche, ilch, from Old English ǣlċ, contraction of ǣġhwelċ. Comparable to aye + alike. Compare Scots ilk, elk (“each, every”), Saterland Frisian älk (“each”), West Frisian elk, elts (“each”), Dutch elk (“each”), Low German elk, ellik (“each”), German Low German elk, elke (“each, every”), German jeglicher (“any”). By surface analysis, Old English ā + which.

more.definition: Comfortable; at ease.; Requiring little skill or effort.; Causing ease; giving comfort, or freedom from care or labour.

more.definition: In a relaxed or casual manner.; In a manner without strictness or harshness; gently; softly.; Handily; at the very least.

examples.text: What's the point of doing that?

more.definition: The mistress of a household.; A woman of breeding or higher class, a woman of authority.; A woman who behaves in a polite way.

From Middle English lady, laddy, lafdi, lavedi, from Old English hlǣfdīġe (“mistress of a household, wife of a lord, lady”, literally “bread-kneader”), from hlāf (“bread, loaf”) + dǣġe (“kneader”), related to Old English dǣġe (“maker of dough”) (whence dey (“dairymaid”)). Compare also lord. More at loaf, dairy, dough. Unrelated to lad.

examples.text: It's the story of an unparalleled love.

examples.text: Tom is good at telling stories.

examples.text: I've been busy writing a short story.

more.definition: To tell as a story; to relate or narrate about.; To post a story (chronological collection of pictures or short videos) on an application or website.

more.definition: The physical structure of a human or animal seen as one single organism.; The fleshly or corporeal nature of a human, as opposed to the spirit or soul.; A corpse.
more.etymology: From Middle English body, bodi, bodiȝ, from Old English bodiġ, bodeġ (“body, trunk, chest, torso, height, stature”), from Proto-West Germanic *bodag (“body, trunk”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰewdʰ- (“to be awake, observe”). Cognate with Old High German botah (“body, corpse, trunk, torso”) (whence Swabian Bottich (“body, torso”), Bavarian Bottich (“body, torso, carcass; lower part of a shirt or jacket”)).

examples.text: I had an out-of-body experience.

more.definition: To give body or shape to something.; To construct the bodywork of a car.; To embody.

more.etymology: From Middle English dryven, from Old English drīfan (“to drive, force, move”), from Proto-West Germanic *drīban, from Proto-Germanic *drībaną (“to drive”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰreybʰ- (“to drive, push”).

more.definition: To put (something) down, to rest.; To attach or affix (something) to something else, or in or upon a certain place.; To put in a specified condition or state; to cause to be.

more.definition: The amount by which an actual total is less than the expected or required amount.; Something having a particular property that is low or too low.; A bet that a particular sporting statistic, such as points scored in a game, will be below a certain stated value.
more.etymology: From Middle English under, from Old English under, from Proto-West Germanic *undar, from Proto-Germanic *under, from a merger of Proto-Indo-European *(H)n̥dʰér (“under”) and *h₁entér (“inside”).

examples.text: There is a monster under my bed.

translations.fr: Rien de nouveau sous le soleil.

more.definition: Beneath; below; at or to the bottom of, or the area covered or surmounted by.; Below the surface of.; From one side of to the other, passing beneath.
more.etymology: From Middle English under, from Old English under, from Proto-West Germanic *undar, from Proto-Germanic *under, from a merger of Proto-Indo-European *(H)n̥dʰér (“under”) and *h₁entér (“inside”).

examples.text: Tell me how to play the game.

translations.de: Verrate mir, wie man das spielt!
translations.fr: Dis-moi comment jouer au jeu.

examples.text: The game is about to start.

examples.text: You won't win this game.

translations.de: Du wirst dieses Spiel nicht gewinnen.
translations.fr: Vous ne gagnerez pas ce jeu.
translations.pt: Você não vencerá este jogo.

examples.text: Yesterday I learned a new game.

translations.de: Gestern habe ich ein neues Spiel gelernt.
translations.fr: Hier, j'ai appris un nouveau jeu.
translations.pt: Ontem eu aprendi um novo jogo.

more.definition: Willing and able to participate.; That shows a tendency to continue to fight against another animal, despite being wounded, often severely.; Persistent, especially in senses similar to the above.
more.etymology: From Middle English game, gamen, gammen, from Old English gamen (“sport, joy, mirth, pastime, game, amusement, pleasure”), from Proto-West Germanic *gaman, from Proto-Germanic *gamaną (“amusement, pleasure, game", literally "participation, communion, people together”), from *ga- (collective prefix) + *mann- (“man”); or alternatively from *ga- + a root from Proto-Indo-European *men- (“to think, have in mind”).

examples.text: Pawns are the lifeblood of the game.

translations.de: Bauern sind das Lebenselixier des Spiels.
translations.fr: Les pions sont la pierre angulaire du jeu.

examples.text: The Olympic Games were born in Greece.

translations.de: Die Olympischen Spiele wurden in Griechenland geboren.
translations.fr: Les Jeux olympiques sont nés en Grèce.

examples.text: Football's not a game of chess.

translations.de: Fußball ist kein Schachspiel.

translations.pt: O futebol não é um jogo de xadrez.

examples.text: Without humility, courage is a dangerous game.

translations.de: Ohne Demut ist Mut ein gefährliches Unterfangen.

translations.pt: Sem humildade, a coragem é um jogo perigoso.

more.definition: A playful activity that may be unstructured; an amusement or pastime.; An activity described by a set of rules, especially for the purpose of entertainment, often competitive or having an explicit goal.; A school subject during which sports are practised.
more.etymology: From Middle English game, gamen, gammen, from Old English gamen (“sport, joy, mirth, pastime, game, amusement, pleasure”), from Proto-West Germanic *gaman, from Proto-Germanic *gamaną (“amusement, pleasure, game", literally "participation, communion, people together”), from *ga- (collective prefix) + *mann- (“man”); or alternatively from *ga- + a root from Proto-Indo-European *men- (“to think, have in mind”).

examples.text: Cricket is a game that takes skill.

examples.text: All of my friends like computer games.

translations.de: Alle meine Freunde mögen Computerspiele.
translations.fr: Tous mes amis aiment les jeux vidéo.
translations.pt: Todos os meus amigos gostam de jogos de computador.

examples.text: We watched the soccer game on TV.

translations.de: Wir haben das Fußballspiel im Fernsehen gesehen.
translations.fr: Nous avons vu le match de football à la télévision.

examples.text: I wish we had won the game.

more.definition: To gamble.; To play card games, board games, or video games.; To exploit loopholes in a system or bureaucracy in a way which defeats or nullifies the spirit of the rules in effect, usually to obtain a result which otherwise would be unobtainable.
more.etymology: From Middle English game, gamen, gammen, from Old English gamen (“sport, joy, mirth, pastime, game, amusement, pleasure”), from Proto-West Germanic *gaman, from Proto-Germanic *gamaną (“amusement, pleasure, game", literally "participation, communion, people together”), from *ga- (collective prefix) + *mann- (“man”); or alternatively from *ga- + a root from Proto-Indo-European *men- (“to think, have in mind”).

examples.text: I want everybody to be happy.

examples.text: Is everybody ready for the trip?

translations.de: Ich wäre gerne als Kanadier geboren worden.

examples.text: We wanted to wish you good luck.

examples.text: Weasels eat great numbers of rodents.

translations.de: Wiesel fressen eine große Anzahl von Nagetieren.

examples.text: One and three are odd numbers.

translations.de: Eins und drei sind ungerade Zahlen.
translations.fr: Un et trois sont des nombres impairs.
translations.pt: Um e três são números ímpares.

examples.text: Two and four are even numbers.

translations.de: Zwei und vier sind gerade Zahlen.

translations.fr: Deux, quatre, six, et huit sont des nombres pairs.
translations.pt: Dois, quatro, seis e oito são números pares.

more.definition: Quantity of countable things.; An abstract entity used to describe quantity.; A numeral: a symbol for a non-negative integer.
more.etymology: Anglo-Norman noumbrebor. Inherited from Middle English number, nombre, numbre, noumbre, from Anglo-Norman noumbre, Old French nombre, from Latin numerus (“number”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *nem- (“to distribute, to give, to take”).

examples.text: One, three, and five are odd numbers.

translations.de: Eins, drei und fünf sind ungerade Zahlen.
translations.fr: 1, 3 et 5 sont des nombres impairs.
translations.pt: Um, três e cinco são números ímpares.

examples.text: He is numbered among the greatest scientists in the world.

translations.de: Er wird zu den größten Wissenschaftlern der Welt gezählt.
translations.fr: Il compte parmi les plus grands scientifiques mondiaux.

examples.text: There are no arguments against numbers.

translations.de: Es gibt keine Argumente gegen Zahlen.

examples.text: Toki Pona only has words for small numbers.

translations.de: Toki Pona hat nur Wörter für kleine Zahlen.
translations.fr: Toki Pona n'a de mots que pour les petits nombres.
translations.pt: Toki Pona só tem palavras para números pequenos.

more.definition: To total or count; to amount to.; To limit to a certain number; to reckon (as by fate) to be few in number.; To label (items) with numbers; to assign numbers to (items).
more.etymology: Anglo-Norman noumbrebor. Inherited from Middle English number, nombre, numbre, noumbre, from Anglo-Norman noumbre, Old French nombre, from Latin numerus (“number”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *nem- (“to distribute, to give, to take”).

examples.text: You can say whatever you want.

translations.de: Du kannst sagen, was auch immer du willst.
translations.fr: Tu peux dire tout ce que tu veux.

examples.text: I will lend you whatever book you need.

translations.de: Ich werde dir jedes Buch borgen, das du brauchst.
translations.fr: Je te prêterai tous les livres dont tu as besoin.
translations.pt: Vou te emprestar qualquer livro que precise.

more.definition: Unexceptional or unimportant; blah.
more.etymology: From Middle English whatever. By surface analysis, what + -ever.

examples.text: He can do whatever he likes with the money.

translations.de: Er kann mit dem Geld machen, was er will.
translations.fr: Il peut faire avec son argent tout ce qu'il veut.

examples.text: Take whatever cake you want.

more.definition: At all; in any way; whatsoever.; In what way; to what extent.
more.etymology: From Middle English whatever. By surface analysis, what + -ever.

examples.text: I'll do whatever I have to.

translations.de: Ich werde tun, was immer nötig ist.
translations.fr: Je ferai ce que je dois faire.
translations.pt: Eu farei o que for preciso.

examples.text: You can do whatever you want to.

translations.de: Du kannst tun, was immer du willst.
translations.fr: Tu peux faire ce qui te chante.
translations.pt: Você pode fazer o que quiser.

examples.text: You can write whatever you want.

translations.de: Du kannst schreiben, was du willst.

examples.text: Do whatever you want. I don't care.

translations.fr: Fais ce que tu veux. Je m'en fiche.

more.definition: What ever; emphatic form of 'what'.; Regardless of the ... that; for any ... that.; Any ... that; of no matter what type or kind that.
more.etymology: From Middle English whatever. By surface analysis, what + -ever.

examples.text: I give whatever I can to the poor children.

translations.de: Ich gebe den armen Kindern, was ich kann.

translations.pt: Eu dou o que posso às crianças pobres.

examples.text: You can do whatever you want to, of course.

translations.de: Du kannst natürlich tun, was immer dir beliebt.
translations.fr: Tu peux faire tout ce qui te chante, bien sûr.
translations.pt: Você pode fazer o que quiser, claro.

examples.text: I'll be whatever you want me to be.

translations.de: Ich werde sein, was immer du willst.

translations.pt: Eu serei qualquer um que você quer que eu seja.

examples.text: He believes whatever I say.

translations.de: Er glaubt alles, was ich sage.
translations.fr: Il croit tout ce que je dis.
translations.pt: Acredita em tudo que digo.

more.definition: A holophrastic expression used to dismiss something that the speaker doesn't care about, doesn't think important, or doesn't want to consider or discuss any further. Sometimes conceived as an ellipsis of whatever you say, implying feigned deference: whatever you say [apparently must be true].
more.etymology: From Middle English whatever. By surface analysis, what + -ever.

examples.text: Do whatever you think is best.

translations.de: Tu, was du für am besten hältst.
translations.fr: Fais ce que tu penses être le mieux.
translations.pt: Faça o que achar melhor.

examples.text: You'll do whatever I say.

translations.de: Du wirst tun, was ich sage.
translations.fr: Tu feras ce que je dis.
translations.pt: Você fará o que eu disser.

examples.text: Tom may do whatever he wants.

examples.text: I'll do whatever you want.

translations.de: Ich werde tun, was immer du willst.
translations.fr: Je ferai tout ce que tu veux.
translations.pt: Farei o que vocês quiserem.

more.definition: A thing or person whose actual name is unknown or forgotten.; Something whose exact kind or nature is unimportant; a thingy.
more.etymology: From Middle English whatever. By surface analysis, what + -ever.

examples.text: Do whatever it takes.

translations.de: Tun Sie, was immer notwendig ist.
translations.fr: Faites ce qui est nécessaire !
translations.pt: Faça o que for preciso.

examples.text: You can do whatever you want to do, of course.

translations.de: Du kannst natürlich tun, was immer dir beliebt.
translations.fr: Tu peux faire tout ce qui te chante, bien sûr.
translations.pt: Você pode fazer o que quiser, claro.

examples.text: Do whatever you like.

translations.de: Tu, was auch immer du willst.

examples.text: Whatever you do, don't forget this.

translations.de: Was auch immer du tust, vergiss das nicht.

translations.pt: Faça o que fizer, não se esqueça disto.

more.definition: What ever; emphasised form of 'what', used to ask which thing, event, circumstance, etc.; Regardless of anything that.; Anything that; all that.
more.etymology: From Middle English whatever. By surface analysis, what + -ever.

examples.text: I don't know what to answer.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, was ich erwidern soll.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas quoi répondre.
translations.pt: Eu não sei o que responder.

examples.text: One of these two answers is right.

translations.de: Eine dieser beiden Antworten ist korrekt.
translations.fr: Une de ces deux réponses est correcte.
translations.pt: Uma destas duas respostas está certa.

examples.text: I'd like to have an answer.

translations.de: Ich möchte eine Antwort haben.
translations.fr: J'aimerais avoir une réponse.
translations.pt: Gostaria de ter uma resposta.

examples.text: There is no answer to your question.

translations.de: Es gibt keine Antwort auf Ihre Frage.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas de réponse à ta question.
translations.pt: Não há resposta à sua pergunta.

more.definition: A response or reply; something said or done in reaction to a statement or question.; A solution to a problem.; Someone or something that fills a similar role or position.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₂éntsder. Proto-Indo-European *swer-der. examples.text: Do I have to answer in English?

translations.de: Muss ich auf Englisch antworten?
translations.fr: Dois-je répondre en anglais ?
translations.pt: Tenho de responder em Inglês?

examples.text: He hasn't answered my letter yet.

translations.de: Er hat meinen Brief noch nicht beantwortet.
translations.fr: Il n'a pas encore répondu à ma lettre.
translations.pt: Ele ainda não respondeu a minha carta.

examples.text: Compare your answers with the teacher's.

translations.de: Vergleiche deine Antworten mit denen des Lehrers.
translations.fr: Compare tes réponses avec celles du professeur.
translations.pt: Compare suas respostas com as do professor.

examples.text: I was able to answer the question.

translations.de: Ich konnte die Frage beantworten.
translations.fr: J'ai été capable de répondre à la question.
translations.pt: Eu consegui responder à pergunta.

more.definition: To make a reply or response to.; To speak in defence against; to reply to in defence.; To respond to a call by someone at a door or telephone, or other similar piece of equipment.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₂éntsder. Proto-Indo-European *swer-der. From Middle English answeren, andswaren, answerien, from Old English andswarian, answarien (“to answer, to respond, to deny an allegation under oath”), from Proto-Germanic *andaswarōną, *andaswarjaną (“to answer, to give a response, to rebut”), from *anda- (“against”) + *swarjaną, *swarōną (“to swear an oath, to answer, to respond”), from …

examples.text: All the apple trees were cut down.

translations.de: Alle Apfelbäume wurden gefällt.

examples.text: I used the knife to cut the cake.

translations.de: Ich habe den Kuchen mit dem Messer geschnitten.

examples.text: Tom cut the wire and defused the bomb.

translations.de: Tom schnitt das Kabel durch und entschärfte die Bombe.

examples.text: Tom cut the slice of bread diagonally.

translations.de: Tom schnitt die Brotscheibe diagonal durch.

more.etymology: From Middle English cutten, of North Germanic origin, from Old Norse *kytja, *kutta, from Proto-Germanic *kutjaną, *kuttaną (“to cut”), of uncertain origin, perhaps related to Proto-Germanic *kwetwą (“meat, flesh”) (compare Old Norse kvett (“meat”)). more.definition: The act of cutting.; An attack made with a chopping motion of the blade, landing with its edge or point.; A time period when one attempts to lose fat while retaining muscle mass.
more.etymology: From Middle English cutten, of North Germanic origin, from Old Norse *kytja, *kutta, from Proto-Germanic *kutjaną, *kuttaną (“to cut”), of uncertain origin, perhaps related to Proto-Germanic *kwetwą (“meat, flesh”) (compare Old Norse kvett (“meat”)). examples.text: I got my hair cut yesterday.

translations.de: Ich habe mir gestern die Haare schneiden lassen.

translations.pt: Eu cortei o cabelo ontem.

examples.text: He cut the apple in half.

examples.text: I must bite the sour apple.

translations.de: Ich muss in den sauren Apfel beißen.

examples.text: Our dog seldom bites.

translations.de: Unser Hund beißt nur selten.

translations.fr: Mon chien ne mord pas.

examples.text: Never bite the hand that feeds you.

translations.de: Beiß nie die Hand, die dich füttert.

examples.text: The man was bitten by a dog.

translations.de: Der Mann wurde von einem Hund gebissen.

examples.text: I have mosquito bites all over my arm.

translations.de: Mein Arm ist mit Mückenstichen übersät.

translations.pt: Eu tenho picadas de mosquito no meu braço inteiro.

examples.text: She has a habit of biting her nails.

translations.de: Sie hat die Angewohnheit, ihre Nägel zu kauen.

more.definition: To cut into something by clamping the teeth.; To hold something by clamping one's teeth.; To attack with the teeth.
more.etymology: From Middle English biten, from Old English bītan (“bite”), from Proto-West Germanic *bītan, from Proto-Germanic *bītaną (“bite”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeyd- (“split”).

examples.text: I promise it won't happen again.

translations.de: Ich verspreche, das wird nicht wieder passieren.
translations.fr: Je promets que cela ne se reproduira plus.
translations.pt: Prometo que isso não vai acontecer novamente.

examples.text: I can't make you any promises.

translations.de: Ich kann dir nichts versprechen.
translations.fr: Je ne peux rien vous promettre.

examples.text: I promise you I'll come early.

translations.de: Ich verspreche dir, früh zu kommen.
translations.fr: Je vous promets de venir tôt.

translations.de: Ich will, dass du dein Versprechen hältst.

translations.pt: Eu quero que você mantenha a sua promessa.

examples.text: He did what he promised to do.

translations.de: Er hat getan, was er versprochen hat.
translations.fr: Il a fait ce qu'il a promis.
translations.pt: Ele fez o que prometeu fazer.

examples.text: He forgot his promise to go there.

translations.de: Er vergaß sein Versprechen dorthin zu gehen.
translations.fr: Il oublia sa promesse de s'y rendre.
translations.pt: Ele esqueceu a promessa de ir até lá.

examples.text: I've always kept my promises.

translations.fr: J'ai toujours tenu mes promesses.

examples.text: I promised him to keep it secret.

translations.de: Ich versprach ihm, es geheim zu halten.
translations.fr: Je lui ai promis de garder ça secret.

more.definition: To commit to (some action or outcome), or to assure (a person) of such commitment; to make an oath or vow.; To give grounds for expectation, especially of something good.
more.etymology: From Middle English promis, promisse, borrowed from Old French promesse, from Medieval Latin prōmissa, Latin prōmissum (“a promise”), feminine and neuter past participles of prōmittō (“to send forth, to say beforehand, to promise”), from pro (“forth”) + mittere (“to send”); see mission. examples.text: You arrived at the moment I left.

examples.text: I want to live beautiful moments.

examples.text: How many users are active at the moment?

examples.text: She's having a bath at the moment.

translations.de: Sie badet sich gerade.
translations.fr: Elle est en train de se baigner.

more.definition: A particular point of space; a spot.; A particular point of time; an instant.; A brief, unspecified amount of time.
more.etymology: From Middle English moment, from Old French moment, from Latin mōmentum. Doublet of momentum and movement.

examples.text: I know that this doesn't interest you.

translations.fr: Il ne s'intéresse pas à la politique.
translations.pt: Ele não se interessa por política.

examples.text: I have an interest in cello and piano.

translations.de: Ich interessiere mich für Cello und Piano.
translations.fr: Je m'intéresse au violoncelle et au piano.
translations.pt: Interessam-me o violoncelo e o piano.

more.definition: The price paid for obtaining, or price received for providing, money or goods in a credit transaction, calculated as a fraction of the amount or value of what was borrowed.; Any excess over and above an exact equivalent; A great attention and concern from someone or something; intellectual curiosity.

examples.text: Aren't you interested in foreign languages?

examples.text: The goldfinch is a very interesting bird.

examples.text: That doesn't interest me anymore.

translations.fr: Cela ne m'intéresse plus.

translations.de: Ich interessiere mich wirklich nicht für Geschichte.

examples.text: The groom hid inside the wedding cake.

translations.fr: Le marié s'est caché dans la pièce montée.

more.definition: Of or pertaining to the inner surface, limit or boundary.; Nearer to the interior or centre of something.; Originating from, arranged by, or being someone inside an organisation.

examples.text: Do you want to come inside?

translations.de: Möchtest du hereinkommen?

examples.text: We need to find what's inside these boxes.

examples.text: Why aren't you inside?

examples.text: He lives inside an apple.

translations.de: Er lebt in einem Apfel.

more.definition: The interior or inner part.; The left-hand side of a road if one drives on the left, or right-hand side if one drives on the right.; The side of a curved road, racetrack etc. that has the shorter arc length; the side of a racetrack nearer the interior of the course or some other point of reference.
more.etymology: From Middle English ynneside; equivalent to in- + side. Compare German Innenseite (“inside”), Danish inderside (“inside”), Swedish insida (“inside”), Dutch binnenzijde (“inside”), German Low German Binnensied, Binnersied (“inside”), Saterland Frisian Binnersiede (“inside”).

examples.text: Remove your hat when you go inside.

translations.fr: Enlève ton chapeau quand tu entres.

examples.text: Ancient coins were found inside the mysterious tomb.

more.definition: Within the interior of, closest to the center or to a specific point of reference; on the interior side of.; To the interior of.; Within (a period of time).

more.definition: Not the same; exhibiting a difference.; Various, assorted, diverse.; Distinct, separate; used for emphasis after numbers and other determiners of quantity.
