examples.text: Why does the US government let people have guns?

translations.de: Warum lässt die US-Regierung zu, dass Menschen Waffen besitzen dürfen?
translations.fr: Pourquoi le gouvernement américain laisse-t-il les gens posséder des armes ?
translations.pt: Por que será que o governo dos Estados Unidos permite que as pessoas portem armas?

examples.text: Tom's fingerprints were on the gun.

translations.de: Toms Fingerabdrücke befanden sich auf der Waffe.
translations.fr: Les empreintes digitales de Tom étaient sur le pistolet.
translations.pt: As digitais de Tom estavam na arma.

examples.text: Guns don't kill people. People kill people.

translations.de: Waffen töten keine Menschen. Menschen töten Menschen.
translations.fr: Ce ne sont pas les armes qui tuent les hommes, ce sont les hommes qui tuent les hommes.
translations.pt: Armas não matam pessoas. Pessoas matam pessoas.

examples.text: And where are the aliens, the flying saucers, and the laser guns?

translations.de: Und wo sind nun die Außerirdischen, die fliegenden Untertassen und die Strahlenwaffen?
translations.fr: Et où sont maintenant passées les extra-terrestres, les soucoupes volantes et les armes à rayons laser ?
translations.pt: E onde estão os alienígenas, os discos voadores e as armas laser?

more.definition: A device for shooting projectiles or ditto (a shooter), functioning through stored energy: a firearm, cannon, harpoon gun/spear gun, raygun, etc, not a bow and arrow, or slingshot.; A very portable, short firearm, for hand use, which fires bullets or projectiles, such as a handgun, revolver, pistol, or Derringer.; A less portable, long firearm that fires bullets or projectiles; a rifle, either manual, automatic or semi-automatic; a flintlock, musket or shotgun.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *kelh₂-der. Old Norse Gunnhildrder. From Middle English gunne, gonne, possibly from Gunnhild, a female given name formerly used as a nickname for engines of war (compare Nordic Gunn, a female name meaning “battle”). The name is composed of the Norse elements gunnr and hildr, both meaning "battle".

examples.text: I don't really have a gun.

translations.de: Ich habe wirklich kein Gewehr.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas vraiment d'arme.
translations.pt: Eu realmente não tenho uma arma.

examples.text: Why does the US government let people have guns?

translations.de: Warum lässt die US-Regierung zu, dass Menschen Waffen besitzen dürfen?
translations.fr: Pourquoi le gouvernement américain laisse-t-il les gens posséder des armes ?
translations.pt: Por que será que o governo dos Estados Unidos permite que as pessoas portem armas?

examples.text: My screw gun is making weird noises.

translations.de: Mein Akkuschrauber macht seltsame Geräusche.
translations.fr: Ma visseuse fait des bruits bizarres.
translations.pt: Minha parafusadeira está fazendo uns barulhos estranhos.

examples.text: Watch out, the man has a gun.

translations.de: Pass auf, der Typ hat ein Gewehr.
translations.fr: Attention, l'homme a un pistolet.
translations.pt: Cuidado, o homem tem uma arma.

more.definition: To shoot with a gun.; To cause to speed up.; To offer vigorous support to (a person or cause).
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *kelh₂-der. Old Norse Gunnhildrder. From Middle English gunne, gonne, possibly from Gunnhild, a female given name formerly used as a nickname for engines of war (compare Nordic Gunn, a female name meaning “battle”). The name is composed of the Norse elements gunnr and hildr, both meaning "battle".

examples.text: I could have sworn I saw somebody.

translations.de: Ich hätte schwören können, dass ich jemanden gesehen habe.
translations.fr: J'aurais pu jurer avoir vu quelqu'un.
translations.pt: Eu poderia jurar que vi alguém.

examples.text: I want somebody to love me.

translations.de: Ich möchte, dass mich jemand liebt.
translations.fr: Je veux que quelqu'un m'aime.
translations.pt: Eu quero que alguém me ame.

examples.text: I know somebody who speaks French very well.

translations.de: Ich kenne jemanden, der sehr gut Französisch spricht.
translations.fr: Je connais quelqu'un qui parle très bien français.
translations.pt: Eu conheço alguém que fala francês muito bem.

examples.text: I need somebody to talk to.

translations.de: Ich brauche jemanden, mit dem ich reden kann.
translations.fr: J'ai besoin de quelqu'un à qui parler.
translations.pt: Preciso de alguém com quem conversar.

more.definition: Any person.; A recognised or important person, a celebrity.
more.etymology: From Middle English sum body, equivalent to some + body.

examples.text: I would like to marry somebody like her.

translations.de: Ich würde gern jemanden wie sie heiraten.
translations.fr: J'aimerais épouser quelqu'un comme elle.
translations.pt: Gostaria de me casar com alguém como ela.

examples.text: I really need to hit somebody.

translations.de: Ich habe wirklich das Bedürfnis, jemanden zu schlagen.
translations.fr: J'ai vraiment besoin de frapper quelqu'un.
translations.pt: Eu realmente preciso bater em alguém.

examples.text: Did somebody mention my name?

translations.de: Erwähnte jemand meinen Namen?
translations.fr: Quelqu'un a-t-il mentionné mon nom ?
translations.pt: Alguém mencionou o meu nome?

examples.text: Can somebody please help me?

translations.de: Kann mir bitte jemand helfen?
translations.fr: Quelqu'un peut-il m'aider, je vous prie ?
translations.pt: Alguém pode me ajudar, por favor?

more.definition: Some unspecified person.; Synonym of someone; an important person.
more.etymology: From Middle English sum body, equivalent to some + body.

examples.text: He is my cousin on the father's side.

translations.de: Er ist mein Cousin väterlicherseits.
translations.fr: C'est mon cousin paternel.
translations.pt: Ele é meu primo por parte de pai.

examples.text: She sat down on the side of the bed.

translations.de: Sie setzte sich auf die Seite des Bettes.
translations.fr: Elle s'est assise sur le côté du lit.
translations.pt: Ela se sentou ao lado da cama.

examples.text: They live on the other side of the river.

translations.de: Sie leben auf der anderen Seite des Flusses.
translations.fr: Ils vivent de l'autre côté de la rivière.
translations.pt: Eles moram do outro lado do rio.

examples.text: She has a mysterious side.

translations.de: Sie hat eine geheimnisvolle Seite.
translations.fr: Elle a un côté mystérieux.
translations.pt: Ela tem um lado misterioso.

more.definition: Being on the left or right, or toward the left or right; lateral.; Indirect; oblique; incidental.; Far; distant.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *seh₁-der. From Middle English side, from Old English sīde (“side, flank”), from Proto-Germanic *sīdǭ (“side, flank, edge, shore”), derived from *sīdaz, probably from Proto-Indo-European *seh₁- (“long, lasting”).

examples.text: There are trees on either side of the river.

translations.de: Auf beiden Seiten des Flusses stehen Bäume.
translations.fr: Il y a des arbres de chaque côté de la rivière.
translations.pt: Tem árvores em cada lado do rio.

examples.text: He's on our side.

translations.de: Er ist auf unserer Seite.
translations.fr: Il est de notre côté.
translations.pt: Ele está do nosso lado.

examples.text: They walked side-by-side.

translations.de: Sie schritten Seite an Seite.
translations.fr: Ils ont marché côte à côte.
translations.pt: Eles andaram lado a lado.

examples.text: Whose side are you on?

translations.de: Auf wessen Seite stehst du?
translations.fr: De quel côté êtes-vous ?
translations.pt: De que lado você está?

more.etymology: From Middle English side, syde, syd, from Old English sīd (“wide, broad, spacious, ample, extensive, vast, far-reaching”), from Proto-West Germanic *sīd, from Proto-Germanic *sīdaz (“drooping, hanging, low, excessive, extra”), from Proto-Indo-European *sēy- (“to send, throw, drop, sow, deposit”).

examples.text: The newspaper is by your side.

translations.de: Die Zeitung liegt neben dir.
translations.fr: Le journal est de ton côté.
translations.pt: O jornal está ao seu lado.

examples.text: A hexagon has six sides.

translations.de: Ein Sechseck hat sechs Seiten.
translations.fr: Un hexagone a six côtés.
translations.pt: Um hexágono tem seis lados.

examples.text: This medicine has no side effects.

translations.de: Diese Medizin hat keine Nebenwirkungen.
translations.fr: Ce médicament n'a pas d'effets secondaires.
translations.pt: Este remédio não tem efeitos colaterais.

examples.text: She is my cousin on my mother's side.

translations.de: Sie ist meine Cousine mütterlicherseits.
translations.fr: C'est ma cousine du côté de ma mère.
translations.pt: Ela é minha prima por parte de mãe.

more.definition: A bounding straight edge of a two-dimensional shape.; A flat surface of a three-dimensional object; a face.; One half (left or right, top or bottom, front or back, etc.) of something or someone.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *seh₁-der. From Middle English side, from Old English sīde (“side, flank”), from Proto-Germanic *sīdǭ (“side, flank, edge, shore”), derived from *sīdaz, probably from Proto-Indo-European *seh₁- (“long, lasting”).

examples.text: She always stayed by my side.

translations.de: Sie stand stets an meiner Seite.
translations.fr: Elle s'est toujours tenue à mon côté.
translations.pt: Ela sempre ficava ao meu lado.

examples.text: A square has four equal sides.

translations.de: Ein Quadrat hat vier gleiche Seiten.
translations.fr: Un carré a quatre côtés égaux.
translations.pt: Um quadrado tem quatro lados iguais.

examples.text: I want you to be by my side.

translations.de: Ich möchte gerne, dass du bei mir bist.
translations.fr: Je veux que tu sois à mon côté.
translations.pt: Quero você do meu lado.

examples.text: He sat down by my side.

translations.de: Er setzte sich neben mich.
translations.fr: Il s'est assis à côté de moi.
translations.pt: Ele sentou-se ao meu lado.

more.definition: To ally oneself, be in an alliance, usually with "with" or rarely "in with"; To lean on one side.; To work (a timber or rib) to a certain thickness by trimming the sides.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *seh₁-der. From Middle English side, from Old English sīde (“side, flank”), from Proto-Germanic *sīdǭ (“side, flank, edge, shore”), derived from *sīdaz, probably from Proto-Indo-European *seh₁- (“long, lasting”).

examples.text: I had a strange dream last night.

translations.de: Ich hatte letzte Nacht einen seltsamen Traum.
translations.fr: J'ai eu un rêve étrange la nuit dernière.
translations.pt: Tive um sonho estranho ontem à noite.

examples.text: My dream is to be a firefighter.

translations.de: Mein Traum ist es, Feuerwehrmann zu sein.
translations.fr: Mon rêve est d'être pompier.
translations.pt: Meu sonho é ser bombeiro.

examples.text: Some day my dream will come true.

translations.de: Eines Tages wird mein Traum wahr werden.
translations.fr: Un jour, mon rêve deviendra réalité.
translations.pt: Algum dia meu sonho se tornará realidade.

examples.text: I hope my dream will come true.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, mein Traum wird in Erfüllung gehen.
translations.fr: J'espère que mon rêve se réalisera.
translations.pt: Espero que meu sonho se realize.

more.definition: Ideal; perfect.
more.etymology: From Middle English dream, dreem, dreeme, drem, dreme, dræm, from Old English drēam, drēm, drīm (“joy; melody, music; frenzy”), from Proto-West Germanic *draum, from Proto-Germanic *draumaz (“dream”), from earlier *draugmaz, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰrowgʰ-mos, from *dʰrewgʰ- (“to deceive”).

examples.text: I'll see you in my dreams.

translations.de: Ich werde dich in meinen Träumen sehen.
translations.fr: Je te verrai dans mes rêves.
translations.pt: Eu te verei em meus sonhos.

examples.text: My dream is to become a pilot.

translations.de: Es ist mein Traum, Pilot zu werden.
translations.fr: Mon rêve est de devenir pilote.
translations.pt: Meu sonho é de virar piloto.

examples.text: You're the girl of my dreams.

translations.de: Du bist das Mädchen meiner Träume.
translations.fr: Tu es la fille de mes rêves.
translations.pt: Você é a garota dos meus sonhos.

examples.text: Mary is the woman of my dreams.

translations.de: Mary ist die Frau meiner Träume.
translations.fr: Mary est la femme de mes rêves.
translations.pt: Maria é a mulher dos meus sonhos.

more.definition: Imaginary events seen in the mind while sleeping.; A hope or wish.; A visionary scheme; a wild conceit; an idle fancy.
more.etymology: From Middle English dream, dreem, dreeme, drem, dreme, dræm, from Old English drēam, drēm, drīm (“joy; melody, music; frenzy”), from Proto-West Germanic *draum, from Proto-Germanic *draumaz (“dream”), from earlier *draugmaz, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰrowgʰ-mos, from *dʰrewgʰ- (“to deceive”).

examples.text: My dog is dreaming of a cat.

translations.de: Mein Hund träumt von einer Katze.
translations.fr: Mon chien rêve d'une chatte.
translations.pt: Meu cachorro está sonhando com um gato.

examples.text: Tom is the man of my dreams.

translations.de: Tom ist der Mann meiner Träume.
translations.fr: Tom est l'homme de mes rêves.
translations.pt: Tom é o homem dos meus sonhos.

examples.text: I had a horrible dream last night.

translations.de: Ich hatte letzte Nacht einen furchtbaren Traum.
translations.fr: J'ai fait un horrible rêve, la nuit dernière.
translations.pt: Eu tive um sonho horrível na noite passada.

examples.text: I dreamt I was a horse.

translations.de: Ich träumte, dass ich ein Pferd war.
translations.fr: J'ai rêvé que j'étais un cheval.
translations.pt: Sonhei que eu era um cavalo.

more.definition: To see imaginary events in one's mind while sleeping.; To hope, to wish.; To daydream.
more.etymology: From Middle English dream, dreem, dreeme, drem, dreme, dræm, from Old English drēam, drēm, drīm (“joy; melody, music; frenzy”), from Proto-West Germanic *draum, from Proto-Germanic *draumaz (“dream”), from earlier *draugmaz, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰrowgʰ-mos, from *dʰrewgʰ- (“to deceive”).

examples.text: There's no reason to be afraid.

translations.de: Es gibt keinen Grund zur Angst.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas de quoi avoir peur.
translations.pt: Não há razão para ter medo.

examples.text: I had good reasons to do that.

translations.de: Ich hatte gute Gründe, das zu tun.
translations.fr: J'ai eu de bonnes raisons de le faire.
translations.pt: Tive boas razões para fazer isso.

examples.text: Hope is the reason for life.

translations.de: Hoffnung ist der Grund des Lebens.
translations.fr: L'espoir est la raison de la vie.
translations.pt: A esperança é a razão da vida.

examples.text: That's the most important reason.

translations.de: Das ist der wichtigste Grund.
translations.fr: C'est la raison la plus importante.
translations.pt: Essa é a razão mais importante.

more.definition: That which causes something: an efficient cause, a proximate cause.; A motive for an action or a determination.; An excuse: a thought or a consideration offered in support of a determination or an opinion; that which is offered or accepted as an explanation.
more.etymology: From Middle English resoun, reson, from Anglo-Norman raisun (Old French raison), from Latin ratiō, from ratus, past participle of reor (“reckon”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂reh₁- (“to think”), reanalysed root of *h₂er- (“to put together”).

examples.text: A smart dog never barks for no reason.

translations.de: Ein kluger Hund bellt nie ohne Grund.
translations.fr: Un chien intelligent n'aboie jamais sans raison.
translations.pt: Um cachorro esperto nunca late sem razão.

examples.text: Tom had reasons to be angry.

translations.de: Tom hatte Grund, verärgert zu sein.
translations.fr: Tom avait des raisons d'être énervé.
translations.pt: Tom tinha razões para estar irritado.

examples.text: That's the reason I bought this book.

translations.de: Deswegen habe ich mir dieses Buch gekauft.
translations.fr: C'est la raison pour laquelle j'ai acheté ce livre.
translations.pt: É por isso que comprei este livro.

examples.text: Children always find a reason to make friends.

translations.de: Kinder finden immer einen Grund, Freundschaften zu schließen.
translations.fr: Les enfants trouvent toujours une raison de se faire des amis.
translations.pt: As crianças sempre encontram um motivo para travar uma amizade.

more.definition: To deduce or come to a conclusion by being rational.; To perform a process of deduction or of induction, in order to convince or to confute; to argue.; To arrange and present the reasons for or against; to examine or discuss by arguments; to debate or discuss.
more.etymology: From Middle English resoun, reson, from Anglo-Norman raisun (Old French raison), from Latin ratiō, from ratus, past participle of reor (“reckon”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂reh₁- (“to think”), reanalysed root of *h₂er- (“to put together”).

examples.text: We don't have to follow Tom.

translations.de: Wir müssen Tom nicht folgen.
translations.fr: Nous n'avons pas à suivre Tom.
translations.pt: Não temos que seguir o Tom.

examples.text: His dog follows him wherever he goes.

translations.de: Sein Hund folgt ihm, wo auch immer er hingeht.
translations.fr: Son chien le suit où qu'il aille.
translations.pt: O cachorro dele o segue aonde ele for.

examples.text: I'll follow you wherever you go.

translations.de: Ich werde dir folgen, wohin du auch gehen wirst.
translations.fr: Où que tu ailles, je te suivrai.
translations.pt: Onde quer que você vá, eu o seguirei.

examples.text: My dog follows me wherever I go.

translations.de: Mein Hund folgt mir überall hin.
translations.fr: Mon chien me suit partout où je vais.
translations.pt: Meu cachorro me acompanha para onde quer que eu vá.

more.definition: In billiards and similar games, a stroke causing a ball to follow another ball after hitting it.; The act of following another user's online activity.
more.etymology: From Middle English folwen, folȝen, folgen, from Old English folgian (“to follow, pursue”), from Proto-West Germanic *folgēn, from Proto-Germanic *fulgāną (“to follow”).

examples.text: A dog followed me to my school.

translations.de: Ein Hund lief mir nach bis zur Schule.
translations.fr: Un chien m'a suivi jusqu'à l'école.
translations.pt: Um cachorro me seguiu até minha escola.

examples.text: I will follow you wherever you go.

translations.de: Wohin du auch gehst, ich werde dir folgen.
translations.fr: Je te suivrai partout où tu iras.
translations.pt: Onde quer que você vá, eu o seguirei.

examples.text: The dog follows me wherever I go.

translations.de: Der Hund folgt mir überall hin.
translations.fr: Le chien me suit où que j'aille.
translations.pt: O cachorro me segue aonde quer que eu vá.

examples.text: I made sure no one was following me.

translations.de: Ich habe zugesehen, dass mich keiner verfolgt hat.
translations.fr: Je me suis assuré que personne ne me suivait.
translations.pt: Certifiquei-me de que ninguém estava me seguindo.

more.definition: To go after; to pursue; to move behind in the same path or direction, especially with the intent of catching.; To go or come after in a sequence.; To carry out (orders, instructions, etc.).
more.etymology: From Middle English folwen, folȝen, folgen, from Old English folgian (“to follow, pursue”), from Proto-West Germanic *folgēn, from Proto-Germanic *fulgāną (“to follow”).

examples.text: I'm afraid that you misunderstood me.

translations.de: Ich befürchte, du hast mich missverstanden.
translations.fr: Je crains que tu m'aies mal comprise.
translations.pt: Acho que vocês me entenderam mal.

examples.text: I'm afraid you've misunderstood me.

translations.de: Ihr habt mich leider mißverstanden.
translations.fr: Je crains que vous ne m'ayez mal compris.
translations.pt: Infelizmente, você me entendeu mal.

examples.text: I'm not afraid of snakes anymore.

translations.de: Ich habe keine Angst mehr vor Schlangen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai plus peur des serpents.
translations.pt: Eu não tenho mais medo de cobras.

examples.text: She's afraid of getting sick again.

translations.de: Sie hat Angst davor, wieder zu erkranken.
translations.fr: Elle a peur de retomber malade.
translations.pt: Ela está com medo de ficar doente de novo.

more.definition: Impressed with fear or apprehension; in fear.; Regretful, sorry; expressing a reluctance to face an unpleasant situation.; Worried about, feeling concern for, fearing for (someone or something).
more.etymology: From Middle English affrayed, affraied, past participle of afraien (“to affray”), from Anglo-Norman afrayer (“to terrify, disquiet, disturb”), from Old French effreer, esfreer (“to disturb, remove the peace from”), from es- (“out”) + freer (“to secure, secure the peace”), from Frankish *friþu (“security, peace”), from Proto-Germanic *friþuz (“peace”), from Proto-Germanic *frijōną (“to free; to love”), from …

examples.text: Images are the books of the illiterate.

translations.de: Bilder sind die Bücher der Analphabeten.
translations.fr: Les images sont les livres des illettrés.
translations.pt: Imagens são os livros dos analfabetos.

examples.text: I've read a lot of books.

translations.de: Ich habe viele Bücher gelesen.
translations.fr: J'ai lu beaucoup de livres.
translations.pt: Eu li muitos livros.

examples.text: What kind of books do you like?

translations.de: Was für Bücher lesen Sie gerne?
translations.fr: Quel genre de livres aimez-vous ?
translations.pt: De que tipo de livro você gosta?

examples.text: Tom has a lot of French books.

translations.de: Tom hat viele französische Bücher.
translations.fr: Tom a beaucoup de livres français.
translations.pt: O Tom tem muitos livros em francês.

examples.text: I am reading a book about history.

translations.de: Ich lese ein Buch über Geschichte.
translations.fr: Je lis un livre sur l'histoire.
translations.pt: Estou lendo um livro sobre história.

examples.text: These books belong to the library.

translations.de: Diese Bücher gehören der Bibliothek.
translations.fr: Ces livres appartiennent à la bibliothèque.
translations.pt: Estes livros pertencem à biblioteca.

more.definition: A collection of sheets of paper bound together to hinge at one edge, containing printed or written material, pictures, etc.; A long work fit for publication, typically prose, such as a novel or textbook, and typically published as such a bound collection of sheets, but now sometimes electronically as an e-book.; A major division of a long work.
collocations: by the book — strictly following the rules
more.etymology: From Middle English bok, book, from Old English bōc, from Proto-West Germanic *bōk, from Proto-Germanic *bōks. Bookmaker sense by clipping.

examples.text: I've booked a table for four.

translations.de: Ich habe einen Tisch für vier Personen bestellt.
translations.fr: J'ai réservé une table pour quatre personnes.
translations.pt: Reservei uma mesa para quatro.

examples.text: They are reading books in the library.

translations.de: Sie lesen Bücher in der Bibliothek.
translations.fr: Ils lisent des livres dans la bibliothèque.
translations.pt: Eles estão lendo livros na biblioteca.

examples.text: Do you enjoy reading books in French?

translations.de: Liest du gerne Bücher auf Französisch?
translations.fr: Tu aimes lire des livres en français ?
translations.pt: Você gosta de ler livros em francês?

examples.text: What type of books do you read?

translations.de: Was für Bücher liest du?
translations.fr: Quel sorte de livre vous lisez ?
translations.pt: Que tipo de livros você lê?

more.definition: To reserve (something) for future use.; To write down, to register or record in a book or as in a book.; To add a name to the list of people who are participating in something.
more.etymology: From Middle English booken, boken, from Old English bōcian, ġebōcian, from the noun (see above).

examples.text: Remember your humanity, and forget the rest.

translations.de: Erinnern Sie sich an Ihre Menschlichkeit, und vergessen Sie den Rest.
translations.fr: Souvenez-vous de votre humanité, oubliez le reste.
translations.pt: Lembre da sua humanidade e esqueça o resto.

examples.text: Let's stop and take a rest.

translations.de: Lasst uns anhalten und eine Pause machen.
translations.fr: Arrêtons-nous et faisons une pause.
translations.pt: Vamos parar e descansar.

examples.text: You're sick. You have to rest.

translations.de: Du bist krank, du musst dich ausruhen.
translations.fr: Tu es malade, tu dois te reposer.
translations.pt: Estás doente, tu precisas repousar.

examples.text: Grandma cannot come along, because she needs rest.

translations.de: Oma kann nicht mitkommen, weil sie Erholung braucht.
translations.fr: Mamie ne peut venir, parce qu'elle a besoin de repos.
translations.pt: Vovó não pode vir, porque precisa descansar.

more.definition: Relief from work or activity by sleeping; sleep.; Any relief from exertion; a state of quiet and relaxation.; Peace; freedom from worry, anxiety, annoyances; tranquility.

more.definition: To cease from action, motion, work, or performance of any kind; stop; desist; be without motion.; To come to a pause or an end; end.; To be free from that which harasses or disturbs; be quiet or still; be undisturbed.

examples.text: A chessboard has sixty-four squares.

more.definition: A numerical value equal to 4; the number following three and preceding five.; Describing a set or group with four elements.

examples.text: I guess I haven't made myself clear.

translations.de: Ich denke, ich war nicht klar genug.

examples.text: It was a bright and clear Sunday morning.

translations.de: Es war ein heller und klarer Sonntagmorgen.
translations.fr: C'était un dimanche matin clair et lumineux.
translations.pt: Era uma manhã brilhante e clara de domingo.

examples.text: The sky is not clear.

translations.fr: Le ciel n'est pas clair.

examples.text: A clear conscience creates harmony.

translations.de: Ein reines Gewissen schafft Harmonie.

translations.pt: Uma consciência tranquila gera harmonia.

more.definition: Transparent in colour.; Bright; luminous; not dark or obscured.; Free of obstacles.
more.etymology: Old French clerbor. From Middle English clere, from Anglo-Norman cler, from Old French cler (Modern French clair), from Latin clarus.

examples.text: I want to be clear about that.

translations.de: Da will ich Klarheit schaffen.
translations.fr: Je tiens à ce que ce soit clair.
translations.pt: Eu quero ser claro sobre isso.

examples.text: You must steer clear of that gang.

translations.de: Du musst dich von dieser Gang fernhalten.

examples.text: It is clear what must be done.

translations.de: Es ist klar, was getan werden muss.
translations.fr: Ce qui doit être fait est clair.
translations.pt: Está claro o que tem que ser feito.

examples.text: The sky is clear almost every day.

translations.de: Der Himmel ist fast täglich klar.
translations.fr: Le ciel est dégagé quasiment tous les jours.
translations.pt: O céu está limpo quase todo dia.

more.definition: All the way; entirely.; Not near something or touching it.; Free (or separate) from others.
more.etymology: Old French clerbor. From Middle English clere, from Anglo-Norman cler, from Old French cler (Modern French clair), from Latin clarus.

examples.text: Suddenly, it all became clear.

translations.de: Plötzlich wurde alles klar.
translations.fr: Soudain, tout devint clair.
translations.pt: De repente, tudo ficou claro.

examples.text: The cause of the accident is still not clear.

translations.de: Die Unfallursache ist noch immer nicht klar.
translations.fr: La cause de l'accident n'est toujours pas claire.
translations.pt: A causa do acidente ainda não está clara.

examples.text: The sky's clear today.

translations.de: Der Himmel ist heute klar.
translations.fr: Le ciel est clair aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: O céu está limpo hoje.

examples.text: Have I made myself clear?

translations.de: Habe ich mich klar ausgedrückt?
translations.fr: Me suis-je fait comprendre ?
translations.pt: Fui claro?

more.definition: Empty or open area.; Full extent; distance between extreme limits; especially; the distance between the nearest surfaces of two bodies, or the space between walls.; The completion of a stage or challenge, or of the whole game.
more.etymology: Old French clerbor. From Middle English clere, from Anglo-Norman cler, from Old French cler (Modern French clair), from Latin clarus.

examples.text: Let's try to clear up this misunderstanding.

translations.fr: Essayons de dissiper ce malentendu.
translations.pt: Vamos tentar esclarecer este mal-entendido.

examples.text: The DNA test cleared him of all charges.

translations.de: Der DNA-Test befreite ihn von allen Anklagen.
translations.fr: Le test ADN l'a blanchi de toutes les accusations.
translations.pt: O exame de DNA o isentou de todas as acusações.

examples.text: The mist is clearing.

translations.de: Der Nebel löst sich auf.
translations.fr: La brume se dissipe.
translations.pt: A névoa está desaparecendo.

examples.text: It's best to steer clear of him.

translations.de: Mit dem ist nicht gut Kirschen essen.
translations.fr: Il vaut mieux rester à l'écart de lui.
translations.pt: É melhor evitá-lo.

more.definition: To remove obstructions, impediments or other unwanted items from.; To remove (items or material) so as to leave something unobstructed or open.; To leave abruptly; to clear off or clear out.
more.etymology: Old French clerbor. From Middle English clere, from Anglo-Norman cler, from Old French cler (Modern French clair), from Latin clarus.

examples.text: I am quite comfortable in this room.

translations.de: Ich fühle mich recht wohl in diesem Zimmer.
translations.fr: Je suis plutôt à l'aise dans cette pièce.

examples.text: You know quite a lot about sumo.

translations.de: Du weißt ziemlich viel über Sumo.
translations.fr: Tu en sais beaucoup sur le sumo.
translations.pt: Voê sabe bastante sobre sumô.

examples.text: It's quite an old building.

translations.de: Es ist ein ziemlich altes Gebäude.
translations.fr: C'est un bâtiment assez ancien.
translations.pt: É um edifício bastante antigo.

examples.text: The thieves made off with quite a haul.

translations.de: Die Diebe machten sich mit ordentlich Beute davon.
translations.fr: Les voleurs sont partis avec un sacré butin.

more.definition: With verbs, especially past participles.; With prepositional phrases and spatial adverbs.; With predicative adjectives.

examples.text: It's not quite as simple as that.

translations.de: Ganz so einfach ist das nicht.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas aussi simple que ça.

examples.text: I've never seen anything quite like this.

translations.fr: Je n'ai jamais rien vu de tel.
translations.pt: Nunca vi algo parecido com isso.

examples.text: Tom plays the accordion quite well.

translations.de: Tom spielt ziemlich gut Akkordeon.
translations.fr: Tom joue assez bien de l'accordéon.

examples.text: Although she is rich, she dresses quite simply.

translations.de: Obwohl sie reich ist, kleidet sie sich sehr einfach.

translations.pt: Apesar de ser rica, ela se veste com bastante simplicidade.

more.definition: Indicates agreement; exactly so.

examples.text: He started going bald quite young.

translations.de: Er bekam schon sehr jung eine Glatze.
translations.fr: Il a commencé à perdre ses cheveux très jeune.

more.definition: A series of passes made with the cape to distract the bull.
more.etymology: From Spanish quite.

examples.text: Studying French is a lot of fun.

examples.text: We are not here to have fun.

more.etymology: From Middle English fonne, fon (“foolish, simple, silly”) or fonnen (“make a fool of”), from Middle English fonne (“a fool, dupe”), probably of North Germanic origin, related to Swedish fånig (“foolish”), Swedish fåne (“a fool”), from Old Norse fáni (“vain person, swaggerer”), but of unknown ultimate origin. translations.fr: C'est plus marrant que de boire du thé.
translations.pt: É mais divertido do que beber chá.

examples.text: He hates me. And I hate him!

translations.de: Er hasst mich und ich hasse ihn!
translations.fr: Il me déteste et je le déteste !
translations.pt: Ele me odeia. E eu odeio ele!

examples.text: She hates fish and never eats any.

translations.de: Sie hasst Fisch und isst niemals welchen.

examples.text: I told you I hated that shirt.

translations.de: Ich habe dir doch gesagt, dass ich das Hemd hasse.
translations.fr: Je t'ai dit que je détestais cette chemise.
translations.pt: Eu te disse que odiava essa camisa.

translations.de: Sie hasst ihre Schwiegermutter.

more.etymology: From Middle English haate, hat, hate (noun), probably from Old English hatian (“to hate”, verb) and/or Old Norse hatr (“hate”, noun). Merged with Middle English het, hete (“hate”), from Old English hete, from Proto-West Germanic *hati, from Proto-Germanic *hataz (“hate”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱeh₂d- (“angriness, hatred”).

examples.text: Why are you protesting against the government?

translations.de: Warum protestierst du gegen die Regierung?

translations.de: Alle Studenten waren gegen den Krieg.
translations.fr: Tous les étudiants étaient contre la guerre.
translations.pt: Todos os estudantes eram contra a guerra.

translations.de: Bist du für oder gegen den Plan?
translations.fr: Es-tu pour ou contre notre plan ?
translations.pt: Você é contra ou a favor do plano?

examples.text: The rain beats against the window pane.

translations.de: Der Regen klopft an die Fensterscheiben.
translations.fr: La pluie bat contre le carreau.

translations.de: Tom drückte sein Ohr gegen die Wand.

translations.de: Die Studenten gingen gegen den Vietnamkrieg auf die Straßen.

more.definition: In a contrary direction to.; In physical opposition to; in collision with.; In physical contact with, so as to abut or be supported by.

translations.de: Ihr Mann lebt jetzt in Tokio.

more.etymology: Latin posseder. Anglo-Norman poerbor. From Middle English power, poer, from Old French poeir, from Vulgar Latin potēre, from Latin posse, whence English potent. Compare French pouvoir. Displaced the native Old English anweald.

translations.de: Die Wissenschaft prägt unseren Lebensstil.

more.definition: Despite the fact that; although.

more.definition: The act of throwing something.; A move in which one lifts or unbalances one’s opponent and then brings him down to the ground.; One’s ability to throw.

examples.text: He threw a stone at the dog.

translations.de: Er warf einen Stein auf den Hund.

examples.text: I hardly ever throw food away.

translations.de: Ich werfe fast nie Lebensmittel weg.
translations.fr: Je ne jette quasiment jamais de nourriture.
translations.pt: Eu quase nunca jogo comida fora.

examples.text: I feel like throwing up.

more.definition: To hurl; to release (an object) with some force from one’s hands, an apparatus, etc. so that it moves rapidly through the air.; To eject or cause to fall off.; To move to another position or condition; to displace.
more.etymology: From Middle English throwen, thrawen, from Old English þrāwan (“to turn, twist”), from Proto-West Germanic *þrāan, from Proto-Germanic *þrēaną (“to twist, turn”), from Proto-Indo-European *terh₁- (“to rub, rub by twisting, twist, turn”).

examples.text: The bicycle is between the cars.

more.definition: A kind of needle, shorter than a sharp, with a small rounded eye, used for making fine stitches on heavy fabrics.
more.etymology: PIE word *dwóh₁ From Middle English betwene, from Old English betwēonum (“between, among”, dative plural, literally “by the two, near both”), from Proto-Germanic *bi- (“be-”) + *twīhnaz (“two each”), corresponding to be- + twain. examples.text: I see someone between the trees.

examples.text: What's the difference between fission and fusion?

examples.text: There isn't much difference between the two.

translations.de: Es besteht kein großer Unterschied zwischen den beiden.

translations.pt: Não tem muita diferença entre os dois.

examples.text: There's not much difference between the two.

translations.de: Es besteht kein großer Unterschied zwischen den beiden.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas beaucoup de différence entre les deux.
translations.pt: Não tem muita diferença entre os dois.

more.definition: In the position or interval that separates (two things), or intermediate in quantity or degree. (See Usage notes below.); Done together or reciprocally.; Shared in confidence.
more.etymology: PIE word *dwóh₁ From Middle English betwene, from Old English betwēonum (“between, among”, dative plural, literally “by the two, near both”), from Proto-Germanic *bi- (“be-”) + *twīhnaz (“two each”), corresponding to be- + twain. examples.text: My client has been charged with murder.

translations.de: Mein Mandant ist des Mordes angeklagt worden.
translations.fr: Mon client est accusé de meurtre.
translations.pt: Meu cliente foi acusado de assassinato.

examples.text: There were two murders this month.

translations.de: In diesem Monat gab es zwei Morde.
translations.fr: Il y a eu deux meurtres ce mois-ci.
translations.pt: Houve dois assassinatos este mês.

examples.text: Tom and Mary attempted to murder John.

translations.de: Tom und Mary versuchten John zu ermorden.
translations.fr: Tom et Mary ont tenté de tuer John.
translations.pt: Tom e Mary tentaram assassinar John.

examples.text: Jealousy was the motive for the murder.

translations.de: Das Mordmotiv war Eifersucht.
translations.fr: Le mobile du meurtre était la jalousie.
translations.pt: O motivo para o assassinato foi o ciúme.

more.definition: An act of killing a person unlawfully, especially with predetermination.; The crime of killing a person unlawfully, especially with predetermination.; Short for felony murder, the act of committing or abetting a crime that results in the killing of a person, regardless of intent, even if the perpetrator did not directly kill the victim.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *mer-der. From Middle English murder, murdre, mourdre, alteration of earlier murthre (“murder”) (see murther), from Old English morþor (“secret slaying, unlawful killing”) and Old English myrþra (“murder, homicide”), both from Proto-West Germanic *morþr, from Proto-Germanic *murþrą (“death, killing, murder”), from Proto-Indo-European *mr̥tro- (“killing”), from Proto-Indo-European *mer-, *mor-, …

examples.text: The police think Tom murdered Mary.

translations.de: Die Polizei glaubt, dass Tom Mary ermordet hat.
translations.fr: La police pense que Tom a tué Mary.
translations.pt: A polícia pensa que Tom matou Mary.

examples.text: I'm being charged with murder.

translations.de: Ich bin des Mordes angeklagt.
translations.fr: Je suis accusé de meurtre.
translations.pt: Estou sendo acusado de assassinato.

examples.text: To everyone's surprise, Fadil quickly confessed to the murders.

translations.de: Zur allgemeinen Überraschung hat Fadil die Morde schnell gestanden.
translations.fr: À la surprise de générale, Fadil avoua rapidement les meurtres.
translations.pt: Para surpresa de todos, Fadil confessou rapidamente os homicídios.

examples.text: The murder weapon wasn't found.

translations.de: Die Mordwaffe wurde nicht gefunden.
translations.fr: L'arme du crime n'a pas été retrouvée.
translations.pt: A arma do crime não foi encontrada.

more.definition: To illegally kill (a person or persons) with intent, especially with predetermination; To kill violently.; To defeat decisively.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *mer-der. From Middle English murder, murdre, mourdre, alteration of earlier murthre (“murder”) (see murther), from Old English morþor (“secret slaying, unlawful killing”) and Old English myrþra (“murder, homicide”), both from Proto-West Germanic *morþr, from Proto-Germanic *murþrą (“death, killing, murder”), from Proto-Indo-European *mr̥tro- (“killing”), from Proto-Indo-European *mer-, *mor-, …

examples.text: Could you please pass me the salt?

translations.de: Kannst du mir bitte das Salz reichen?
translations.fr: Pouvez-vous me passer le sel, s’il vous plait ?
translations.pt: Por favor, você poderia me passar o sal?

examples.text: Time passes by quickly.

translations.de: Die Zeit vergeht schnell.

examples.text: Could you pass me the salt, please?

examples.text: Would you pass me the salt, please?

translations.de: Gibst du mir mal bitte das Salz?!
translations.fr: Pouvez-vous me passer le sel, s’il vous plait ?
translations.pt: Poderia passar-me o sal, por favor?

more.definition: An opening, road, or track, available for passing; especially, one through or over some dangerous or otherwise impracticable barrier such as a mountain range; a passageway; a defile; a ford.; A channel connecting a river or body of water to the sea, for example at the mouth (delta) of a river.; A single movement, especially of a hand, at, over, or along anything.
more.etymology: From Middle English pas, pase, pace, from passen (“to pass”).

examples.text: Mary passed the test with flying colors.

translations.de: Maria hat die Prüfung mit Bravour bestanden.
translations.fr: Marie a passé l'examen avec brio.
translations.pt: Mary passou na prova com distinção.

examples.text: Could you please pass me the pepper?

translations.de: Würden Sie mir bitte den Pfeffer reichen?
translations.fr: Pourriez-vous me passer le poivre ?
translations.pt: Você podia me passar a pimenta?

examples.text: He amazed everyone by passing his driving test.

translations.de: Er verblüffte alle mit dem Bestehen seiner Fahrprüfung.
translations.fr: Tous furent épatés qu'il eût réussi à l'examen du permis de conduire.
translations.pt: Ele impressionou todos ao passar no teste de direção.

examples.text: Neither of his students passed the exam.

translations.de: Keiner seiner beiden Schüler bestand die Prüfung.
translations.fr: Aucun de ses étudiants n'a réussi l'examen.
translations.pt: Nenhum dos seus alunos passou no exame.

more.definition: To move or be moved from one place to another.; To go past, by, over, or through; to proceed from one side to the other of; to move past.; To cause to move or go; to send; to transfer from one person, place, or condition to another.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *peth₂-der. Latin -ereinflu. Old French passerbor. From Middle English passen, from Old French passer (“to step, walk, pass”), from Vulgar Latin *passāre (“step, walk, pass”), derived from Latin passus (“a step”), from Proto-Italic *pat-s-tus, from Proto-Indo-European *peth₂- (“to spread, stretch out”). Cognate with Old English fæþm (“armful, fathom”). More at fathom.

examples.text: It's cool after the rain.

translations.de: Nach dem Regen ist es kalt.
translations.fr: Il fait frais après la pluie.
translations.pt: Fica fresco após a chuva.

examples.text: Keep it in a cool place.

translations.de: Bewahre es an einem kühlen Ort auf.
translations.fr: Garde-le dans un endroit frais.
translations.pt: Guarde isso num lugar frio.

examples.text: It is cool after the rain.

translations.de: Nach dem Regen ist es kalt.
translations.fr: Il fait frais après la pluie.
translations.pt: Fica fresco após a chuva.

examples.text: I want to be cool.

translations.de: Ich will cool sein.
translations.fr: Je veux être cool.
translations.pt: Quero ser legal.

more.definition: Of a mildly low temperature.; Allowing or suggesting heat relief.; Of a color, in the range of violet to green.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *gel-der. Proto-Germanic *kalanąder. From Middle English cool, from Old English cōl (“cool, cold, tranquil, calm”), from Proto-West Germanic *kōl(ī), from Proto-Germanic *kōluz (“cool”), from *kalaną (“to be cold, to freeze”), Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to be cold, to freeze”).

examples.text: It's really cool here.

translations.de: Es ist echt cool hier.
translations.fr: C'est vraiment frais, ici.
translations.pt: Aqui é bem legal.

examples.text: It was very cool.

translations.de: Es war sehr kühl.
translations.fr: C'était très sympa.
translations.pt: Foi muito legal.

examples.text: Your parents are cool.

translations.de: Deine Eltern sind cool.
translations.fr: Tes parents sont sympas.
translations.pt: Seus pais são legais.

examples.text: Your mom is cool.

translations.de: Deine Mama ist cool.
translations.fr: Ta mère est cool.

more.definition: A moderate or refreshing state of cold; moderate temperature of the air between hot and cold; coolness.; A calm temperament.; The property of being cool, popular or in fashion.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *gel-der. Proto-Germanic *kalanąder. From Middle English cool, from Old English cōl (“cool, cold, tranquil, calm”), from Proto-West Germanic *kōl(ī), from Proto-Germanic *kōluz (“cool”), from *kalaną (“to be cold, to freeze”), Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to be cold, to freeze”).

examples.text: My love for him has already cooled.

Cognate with Dutch koelen (“to cool”), German kühlen (“to cool”), Swedish kyla (“to cool, refrigerate”).

more.definition: To apply a force to (an object) so that it comes toward the person or thing applying the force.; To gather with the hand, or by drawing toward oneself; to pluck or pick (flowers, fruit, etc.).; To attract or net; to pull in.
more.etymology: Verb from Middle English pullen, from Old English pullian (“to pull, draw, tug, pluck off”), of uncertain ultimate origin. examples.text: Tom has decided to sell his car.

translations.de: Tom hat sich dazu entschieden, sein Auto zu verkaufen.
translations.fr: Tom a décidé de vendre sa voiture.
translations.pt: Tom decidiu vender o carro dele.

examples.text: All the old magazines are sold out.

translations.de: Alle die alten Zeitschriften sind ausverkauft.

examples.text: He buys and sells used cars.

more.definition: To transfer goods or provide services in exchange for money.; To be sold.; To promote (a product or service) although not being paid in any direct way or at all.
more.etymology: From Middle English sellen, from Old English sellan (“give; give up for money”), from Proto-West Germanic *salljan, from Proto-Germanic *saljaną, from Proto-Indo-European *selh₁-.

examples.text: I don't know where to begin.

translations.pt: Não sei por onde começar.

examples.text: Tom doesn't know where to begin.

translations.de: Tom weiß nicht, wo er anfangen soll.
translations.fr: Tom ne sait pas par où commencer.
translations.pt: Tom não sabe por onde começar.

examples.text: Let's begin our work at once.

translations.de: Beginnen wir sofort mit der Arbeit.

more.definition: To start, to initiate or take the first step into something.; To come into existence.
more.etymology: From Middle English beginnen, from Old English beginnan (“to begin”), from Proto-West Germanic *biginnan, from Proto-Germanic *biginnaną (“to begin”), from be- + base verb *ginnaną also found in Old English onginnan.

examples.text: I think that she knows the truth.

translations.pt: A verdade é que contei uma mentira.

examples.text: I have to tell you the truth.

translations.de: Ich muss dir die Wahrheit sagen.
translations.fr: Je dois te dire la vérité.
translations.pt: Eu tenho que te dizer a verdade.

examples.text: You should've told me the truth.

translations.de: Du hättest mir die Wahrheit sagen sollen.
translations.fr: Tu aurais dû me dire la vérité.
translations.pt: Você devia ter me contado a verdade.

examples.text: I want to tell you the truth.

translations.pt: Eu quero te dizer a verdade.

more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *welh₁-der. From Middle English welcome, wolcume, wulcume, wilcume, from Old English wilcuma (“a wished-for guest”; compare also wilcume (“welcome!”, interjection)), from Proto-West Germanic *willjakwemō, from Proto-Germanic *wiljakwemô (“a wished-for arrival or guest”), possibly from *wiljakwemaną (“to be welcome”), equivalent to will (“desire”) + come (“comer, arrival”).

more.definition: To affirm or greet the arrival of someone, especially by saying "Welcome!".; To accept something willingly or gladly.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *welh₁-der. From Middle English welcome, wolcume, wulcume, wilcume, from Old English wilcuma (“a wished-for guest”; compare also wilcume (“welcome!”, interjection)), from Proto-West Germanic *willjakwemō, from Proto-Germanic *wiljakwemô (“a wished-for arrival or guest”), possibly from *wiljakwemaną (“to be welcome”), equivalent to will (“desire”) + come (“comer, arrival”).

more.definition: A visible fact that shows that something exists or may happen.; An omen.; A property of the body that indicates a disease and, unlike a symptom, can be detected objectively by someone other than the patient.
more.etymology: From Middle English signe, sygne, syng, seine, sine, syne, from Old English seġn (“sign; mark; token”) and Old French signe, seing (“sign; mark; signature”); both from Latin signum (“a mark; sign; token”); root uncertain. Doublet of signum and signal. Partially displaced native token.

translations.de: Sie hätten kein Geständnis unterschreiben sollen.

examples.text: Tom refused to sign the document.

examples.text: I'm not signing anything.

translations.de: Ich werde nichts unterschreiben.

examples.text: There were no signs of life on the island.

translations.de: Es gab kein Zeichen von Leben auf der Insel.

more.definition: To mark, to put or leave a mark on.; To validate or ratify (a document) by writing one's signature on it.; More generally, to write one's signature on (something) as a means of identification etc.
more.etymology: From Middle English signen, seinen, seinien, partly from Old English seġnian (“to mark; sign”) and partly from Anglo-Norman seigner, seiner et al., Old French signer et al., and their source Latin signāre (“to mark, seal, indicate, signify”); all from Latin signum (“a mark, sign”); see Etymology 1, above. Compare sain.

examples.text: She's the cutest girl in town.

more.definition: A settlement; an area with residential districts, shops and amenities, and its own local government; especially one larger than a village and smaller than a city, historically enclosed by a fence or walls, with total populations ranging from several hundred to more than a hundred thousand (as of the early 21st century); Any more urbanized centre than the place of reference.; A rural settlement in which a market was held at least once a week.
more.etymology: Proto-Celtic *dūnombor. Inherited from Middle English toun, from Old English tūn, from Proto-West Germanic *tūn, from Proto-Germanic *tūną, borrowed from Proto-Celtic *dūnom (“stronghold, rampart”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *duh₂-nós (“lasting, durable”), from *dewh₂- (“to last”) + *-nós.

examples.text: We couldn't get in touch with him.

more.definition: An act of touching, especially with the hand or finger.; The faculty or sense of perception by physical contact.; The style or technique with which one plays a musical instrument.
more.etymology: From Middle English touchen, tochen, from Old French tochier (“to touch”) (whence Modern French toucher; compare French doublet toquer (“to offend, bother, harass”)), from Vulgar Latin *tuccō (“to knock, strike, offend”), from Frankish *tukkōn (“to knock, strike, touch”), from Proto-Germanic *tukkōną (“to tug, grab, grasp”), from Proto-Indo-European *dewk- (“to draw, pull, lead”).

more.definition: To make physical contact with; to bring the hand, finger or other part of the body into contact with.; To come into (involuntary) contact with; to meet or intersect.; To come into physical contact, or to be in physical contact.
more.etymology: From Middle English touchen, tochen, from Old French tochier (“to touch”) (whence Modern French toucher; compare French doublet toquer (“to offend, bother, harass”)), from Vulgar Latin *tuccō (“to knock, strike, offend”), from Frankish *tukkōn (“to knock, strike, touch”), from Proto-Germanic *tukkōną (“to tug, grab, grasp”), from Proto-Indo-European *dewk- (“to draw, pull, lead”).

examples.text: I didn't want to scare you.

more.definition: Characterized by declining prices in securities markets or by belief that the prices will fall.

more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *bʰerH-der. Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰwer-der. From Middle English bere, from Old English bera, from Proto-West Germanic *berō, from Proto-Germanic *berô (“bear”).

examples.text: He was as ravenous as a bear.

translations.de: Er war wild wie ein Bär.
translations.fr: Il avait une faim de loup.

examples.text: The university bears the name of its founder.

translations.de: Die Universität trägt den Namen ihres Gründers.
translations.fr: L'université porte le nom de son fondateur.

examples.text: Your conduct is beyond bearing.

examples.text: I hope your efforts will bear fruit.

more.definition: To endeavour to depress the price of, or prices in.; To carry or convey, literally or figuratively.; To carry (weapons, flags or symbols of rank, office, etc.) upon one's person, especially visibly; to be equipped with (weapons, etc.).
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *bʰerH-der. Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰwer-der. From Middle English bere, from Old English bera, from Proto-West Germanic *berō, from Proto-Germanic *berô (“bear”).

examples.text: Dogs are not allowed in his city.

translations.de: Hunde sind in seiner Stadt verboten.
translations.fr: Les chiens sont interdits dans sa ville.
translations.pt: Cachorros são proibidos na cidade dele.

examples.text: Boston is one of my favorite cities.

translations.de: Boston ist eine meiner Lieblingsstädte.
translations.fr: Boston est l'une de mes villes préférées.
translations.pt: Boston é uma das minhas cidades favoritas.

examples.text: The city was damaged during the war.

translations.de: Die Stadt wurde während des Krieges beschädigt.
translations.fr: La ville a été endommagée pendant la guerre.
translations.pt: A cidade foi danificada durante a guerra.

examples.text: The capital city of Serbia is Belgrade.

translations.de: Die Hauptstadt Serbiens ist Belgrad.
translations.fr: La capitale de Serbie est Belgrade.
translations.pt: A capital da Sérvia é Belgrado.

more.definition: A large settlement, bigger than a town; sometimes with a specific legal definition, depending on the place.; A settlement granted special status by royal charter or letters patent; traditionally, a settlement with a cathedral regardless of size.; The central business district; downtown.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *ḱey-der. Old French citetbor. Inherited from Middle English cite, derived from Old French cite, derived from Late Latin cīvitātem (“city”), in Classical Latin "citizenry", derived from cīvis (“fellow-citizen”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱey- (“lie down; settle”). Cognate with Old English hīwan pl (“members of one's household, servants”). See hewe. Doublet of civitas.

examples.text: I think that this fact is very serious.

translations.de: Ich denke, dass diese Tatsache sehr schwer wiegt.
translations.fr: Je pense que ce fait est très grave.
translations.pt: Acho que este fato é seriíssimo.

examples.text: The fact is that my cat is shy.

translations.de: Fakt ist, dass meine Katze scheu ist.
translations.fr: Le fait est que mon chat est timide.
translations.pt: O fato é que meu gato é tímido.

examples.text: As a matter of fact, it is true.

translations.de: Fakt ist, es ist wahr.
translations.fr: En fait, c'est vrai.
translations.pt: De fato, é verdade.

examples.text: I know it for a fact.

translations.de: Ich weiß es mit Sicherheit.
translations.fr: Je le sais pertinemment.
translations.pt: Tenho certeza absoluta.

more.definition: Used before making a statement to introduce it as a trustworthy one.
more.etymology: From Old French fact, from Latin factum (“an act, deed, feat, etc.”); also Medieval Latin for “state, condition, circumstance”; neuter of factus (“done or made”), perfect passive participle of faciō (“do, make”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to put, place, set”). Old/Middle French later evolved it into faict and fait. Doublet of feat.

examples.text: The fact is, he broke the window.

translations.de: Um die Wahrheit zu sagen, hat er die Fensterscheibe kaputtgemacht.
translations.fr: Le fait est qu'il a cassé la fenêtre.
translations.pt: O fato é que ele quebrou a janela.

examples.text: His conclusion is based on these facts.

translations.de: Seine Schlußfolgerung stützt sich auf diese Tatsachen.
translations.fr: Sa conclusion est fondée sur ces faits.
translations.pt: A sua conclusão é baseada nesses factos.

examples.text: The fact remains that he is guilty.

translations.de: Die Tatsache, dass er schuldig ist, bleibt bestehen.
translations.fr: Il n'en reste pas moins qu'il est coupable.
translations.pt: É incontestável que ele é culpado.

examples.text: It's a fact of life.

translations.de: Es ist eine Tatsache des Lebens.
translations.fr: C'est une réalité.
translations.pt: É um fato da vida.

more.definition: Something actual as opposed to invented.; Something which is real.; Something concrete used as a basis for further interpretation.
more.etymology: From Old French fact, from Latin factum (“an act, deed, feat, etc.”); also Medieval Latin for “state, condition, circumstance”; neuter of factus (“done or made”), perfect passive participle of faciō (“do, make”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to put, place, set”). Old/Middle French later evolved it into faict and fait. Doublet of feat.

examples.text: I know that Tom is fast.

translations.de: Ich weiß, dass Tom schnell ist.
translations.fr: Je sais que Tom est rapide.
translations.pt: Eu sei que o Tom é rápido.

examples.text: My car is faster than yours.

translations.de: Mein Wagen ist schneller als deiner.
translations.fr: Ma voiture est plus rapide que la tienne.
translations.pt: Meu carro é mais rápido que o seu.

examples.text: We've got to act fast.

translations.de: Wir müssen schnell handeln.
translations.fr: Il nous faut agir vite.
translations.pt: Tivemos que agir rápido.

examples.text: My watch is two minutes fast.

translations.de: Meine Uhr geht zwei Minuten vor.
translations.fr: Ma montre avance de deux minutes.
translations.pt: Meu relógio está dois minutos adiantado.

more.definition: Firm against attack; fortified by nature or art; impregnable; strong.; Steadfast, with unwavering feeling. (Now mostly in set phrases like fast friend(s).); Moving with great speed, or capable of doing so; swift, rapid; light.
more.etymology: From Middle English fast, fest, from Old English fæst (“firm, secure”), from Proto-West Germanic *fast, from Proto-Germanic *fastuz; see it for cognates and further etymology. The development of “rapid” from an original sense of “secure” apparently happened first in the adverb and then transferred to the adjective; compare hard in expressions like “to run hard”.

examples.text: How fast can a year go by!

translations.de: Wie schnell kann ein Jahr vorübergehen!
translations.fr: Comme une année peut passer vite !
translations.pt: Como um ano pode passar rápido!

examples.text: He ran faster than his brother did.

translations.de: Er rannte schneller als sein Bruder.
translations.fr: Il courait plus vite que son frère.
translations.pt: Ele correu mais rápido do que seu irmão.

examples.text: The cheetah is the fastest animal.

translations.de: Der Gepard ist das schnellste Tier.
translations.fr: Le guépard est l'animal le plus rapide.
translations.pt: O guepardo é o animal mais rápido.

examples.text: I'm not as fast as you.

translations.de: Ich bin nicht so schnell wie ihr.
translations.fr: Je ne suis pas aussi rapide que toi.
translations.pt: Não sou tão rápido como vocês.

more.definition: In a firm or secure manner, securely; in such a way as not to be moved; safe, sound .; Deeply or soundly .; Immediately following in place or time; close, very near .
more.etymology: From Middle English fast, faste, from Old English fæste, from fæst + -e (adverb-forming suffix).

examples.text: I ran as fast as I could.

translations.de: Ich rannte so schnell ich konnte.
translations.fr: J'ai couru aussi vite que j'ai pu.
translations.pt: Corri tão rápido quanto eu pude.

examples.text: I'm tired of eating fast food.

translations.de: Ich habe es satt, Fastfood zu essen.

examples.text: You are fast, we are slow.

examples.text: Why are you walking so fast?

translations.fr: Pourquoi marches-tu si vite ?
translations.pt: Por que você está andando tão rápido?

more.definition: A train that calls at only some stations it passes between its origin and destination, typically just the principal stations.; The act or practice of fasting, religious abstinence from food.; Any of the fasting periods in the liturgical year.
more.etymology: From Middle English fast, fest, from Old English fæst (“firm, secure”), from Proto-West Germanic *fast, from Proto-Germanic *fastuz; see it for cognates and further etymology. examples.text: She ran as fast as she could.

examples.text: He ran as fast as he could.

translations.de: Er rannte, so schnell er konnte.

translations.pt: Ele correu o mais rápido que pôde.

more.definition: To practice religious abstinence, especially from food.; To reduce or limit one's nutrition intake for medical or health reasons, to diet.; To cause (a person or animal) to abstain, especially from eating.
more.etymology: From Middle English fasten, from Old English fæstan (“to fast”), from Proto-West Germanic *fastēn, from Proto-Germanic *fastāną (“to fast”), from the same root as Proto-Germanic *fastijaną (“to fasten”), derived from *fastuz, and thereby related to Etymology 1. The religious sense is presumably introduced in the Gothic church, from Gothic 𐍆𐌰𐍃𐍄𐌰𐌽 (fastan, “hold fast (viz. to the rule of abstinence)”).

examples.text: My name's Tom. What's yours?

translations.de: Ich heiße Tom. Und du?

examples.text: My watch is more accurate than yours.

translations.de: Meine Uhr ist genauer als deine.

translations.pt: Meu relógio é mais preciso que o seu.

more.definition: That or those belonging to you; the possessive second-person singular pronoun used without a following noun.; Your house or home.; Written at the end of a letter, before the signature.

examples.text: I'd like to dance with you.

translations.de: Ich würde gerne mit dir tanzen.
translations.fr: Je voudrais danser avec toi.
translations.pt: Gostaria de dançar contigo.

examples.text: He knows many folk dances.

translations.de: Er kennt viele Volkstänze.
translations.fr: Il connaît de nombreuses danses folkloriques.
translations.pt: Ele conhece muitas danças folclóricas.

examples.text: Why didn't you dance with him?

translations.de: Warum hast du mit ihm nicht getanzt?
translations.fr: Pourquoi n'as-tu pas dansé avec lui ?
translations.pt: Por que você não dançou com ele?

examples.text: Would you like to dance with me?

translations.de: Willst du mit mir tanzen?
translations.fr: Voudrais-tu danser avec moi ?

examples.text: I don't feel much like dancing.

examples.text: The gypsies danced around the bonfire.

examples.text: She sings and dances very well.

Displaced native Old English sealtian, Old English frīcian, and partially displaced Old English hlēapan (“to leap, dance, run”, whence modern leap). Doublet of danza.

examples.text: She tried to hide her anger.

translations.de: Sie versuchte, ihren Ärger zu verbergen.
translations.fr: Elle tenta de dissimuler sa colère.
translations.pt: Ela tentou esconder a sua raiva.

examples.text: Let's play hide and seek.

more.definition: The skin of an animal.; One's own life or personal safety, especially when in peril.; (mainly British) A covered structure from which hunters, birdwatchers, etc can observe animals without scaring them.
more.etymology: From Middle English hyde, from Old English hȳd, from Proto-West Germanic *hūdi, from Proto-Germanic *hūdiz, from Proto-Indo-European *kéw(H)tis (“skin, hide”) (compare Latin cutis (“skin, rind, hide”)), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kew(H)- (“to cover”), ultimately the same root as the above etymology. More at sky.

examples.text: I hid it in my sock drawer.

translations.de: Ich habe es in meiner Sockenschublade versteckt.
translations.fr: Je l'ai caché dans mon tiroir à chaussettes.
translations.pt: Escondi-o na minha gaveta de meias.

examples.text: I still think Tom is hiding something.

translations.de: Ich glaube noch immer, dass Tom etwas verheimlicht.
translations.fr: Je pense toujours que Tom cache quelque chose.

examples.text: We will hide away where no one knows.

translations.fr: Nous nous cacherons là où personne ne le saura.
translations.pt: Esconderemo-nos onde ninguém conhece.

translations.de: Die Spielsachen sind in der roten Kiste versteckt.
translations.fr: Les jouets sont cachés dans la boîte rouge.
translations.pt: Os brinquedos estão escondidos na caixa vermelha.

more.definition: To put (something) in a place where it will be out of sight or harder to discover.; To put oneself in a place where one will be out of sight or harder to find.; To beat with a whip made from hide.
more.etymology: From Middle English hiden, huden, from Old English hȳdan (“to hide, conceal, preserve”), from Proto-West Germanic *huʀdijan (“to conceal”), from Proto-Germanic *huzdijaną (“to hoard”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewdʰ- (“to cover, wrap, encase”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewH- (“to cover”). examples.text: Half for you and half for me.

more.etymology: From Middle English half, halfe from Old English healf (“half”); as a noun, 'half', 'side', 'part', from Proto-West Germanic *halb, from Proto-Germanic *halbaz. more.definition: A call reminding performers that the performance will begin in thirty minutes.
more.etymology: From Middle English half, halfe from Old English healf (“half”); as a noun, 'half', 'side', 'part', from Proto-West Germanic *halb, from Proto-Germanic *halbaz. examples.text: I gave my half to him.

examples.text: I'll be back in half an hour.

more.definition: Half past; a half-hour (30 minutes) after the last hour.

translations.de: Sie ließ mich eine halbe Stunde warten.

examples.text: She cut the apple in half.

translations.de: Sie halbierte den Apfel.

more.definition: To halve.

examples.text: One drop makes the glass overflow.

translations.de: Ein Tropfen bringt das Fass zum Überlaufen.

examples.text: My dad drops in on me from time to time.

translations.fr: Mon père apparaît de temps en temps.
translations.pt: Meu pai vem me visitar de vez em quando.

examples.text: It's a mere drop in the ocean.

translations.de: Das ist nur ein Tropfen auf den heißen Stein.
translations.fr: Ce n'est qu'une goutte d'eau dans l'océan.
translations.pt: É uma simples gota no oceano.

examples.text: A jug fills drop by drop.

translations.de: Tropfen um Tropfen füllt sich der Krug.
translations.fr: Une cruche se remplit goutte à goutte.
translations.pt: Um jarro se enche gota a gota.

more.definition: A small quantity of liquid, just large enough to hold its own rounded shape through surface tension, especially one that falls from a source of liquid.; A dose of liquid medicine in the form of a drop (sense 1).; A liquid medicine that is intended to be administered in drops (sense 1).
more.etymology: From Late Middle English droppe, Middle English drope (“small quantity of liquid; small or least amount of something; pendant jewel; dripping of a liquid; a shower; nasal flow, catarrh; speck, spot; blemish; disease causing spots on the skin”) [and other forms], from Old English dropa (“a drop”), from Proto-West Germanic *dropō (“drop (of liquid)”), from Proto-Germanic *drupô (“drop (of liquid)”),, from *dreupaną …

examples.text: I'd like to buy eye drops.

translations.de: Ich hätte gerne Augentropfen.
translations.fr: Je voudrais acheter des gouttes pour les yeux.
translations.pt: Eu gostaria de comprar colírio.

examples.text: A ripe apple dropped from the tree.

translations.de: Ein reifer Apfel fiel vom Baum.
translations.fr: Une pomme mûre tomba de l'arbre.
translations.pt: Uma maçã madura caiu da árvore.

examples.text: Please drop me off at the station.

translations.de: Bitte setze mich am Bahnhof ab.
translations.fr: Dépose-moi à la gare s'il te plaît.
translations.pt: Deixe-me na estação, por favor.

examples.text: A coin dropped out of his pocket.

translations.de: Eine Münze fiel aus seiner Tasche.
translations.fr: Une pièce est tombée de sa poche.
translations.pt: Caiu uma moeda do bolso dele.

more.definition: Of a liquid: to fall in drops or droplets.; To fall (straight down) under the influence of gravity, like a drop of liquid.; Of an item: To appear for the player to pick up, usually after an enemy has been defeated.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *dʰrebʰ-der. From Middle English droppen, dropen (“to fall in drops, drip or trickle down; to scatter, sprinkle; to be covered with a liquid; to give off moisture; of an object: to drop, fall; of a living being: to fall to the ground”) [and other forms], from Old English droppian, dropian (“to drop”), from Proto-West Germanic *dropōn, from Proto-Germanic *drupōną (“to fall in drops, drip”), …

examples.text: My father is still ill in bed.

translations.de: Mein Vater liegt noch immer krank im Bett.
translations.fr: Mon père est toujours malade, il est dans son lit.
translations.pt: Meu pai ainda está de cama.

examples.text: She is in bed with a cold.

translations.de: Sie ist im Bett, erkältet.
translations.fr: Elle est au lit, enrhumée.

examples.text: He's in bed with the flu.

translations.de: Er liegt mit Grippe im Bett.
translations.fr: La grippe le cloue au lit.

examples.text: He measured the length of the bed.

translations.de: Er maß die Länge des Bettes ab.
translations.fr: Il mesura la longueur du lit.
translations.pt: Ele mediu o comprimento da cama.

more.definition: A piece of furniture, usually flat and soft, on which to rest or sleep.; A mattress.; A bedframe.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English bed, bedde, from Old English bedd, from Proto-West Germanic *badi, from Proto-Germanic *badją (“resting-place, plot of ground”).

examples.text: There is a window above the bed.

translations.de: Über dem Bett ist ein Fenster.
translations.fr: Il y a une fenêtre au-dessus du lit.
translations.pt: Há uma janela acima da cama.

examples.text: Tell the maid to make the beds.

translations.de: Sage dem Hausmädchen, dass es die Betten herrichten soll!
translations.fr: Dis à la bonne de faire les lits.
translations.pt: Diga à camareira para fazer as camas.

examples.text: The girl is jumping on the bed.

translations.de: Das Mädchen springt auf dem Bett herum.
translations.fr: La fille saute sur le lit.
translations.pt: A menina está pulando em cima da cama.

examples.text: I want to go to my bed!

translations.de: Ich will in mein Bett!
translations.fr: Je veux aller dans mon lit !
translations.pt: Quero ir para a minha cama!

more.definition: To go to bed; to put oneself to sleep.; To place in a bed.; To furnish with a bed or bedding.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English bed, bedde, from Old English bedd, from Proto-West Germanic *badi, from Proto-Germanic *badją (“resting-place, plot of ground”).

examples.text: I don't know him either.

translations.fr: Je ne sais pas vraiment non plus.

examples.text: She doesn't understand me, either.

translations.de: Sie versteht mich auch nicht.
translations.fr: Elle ne me comprend pas non plus.

examples.text: I don't know either of his brothers.

more.etymology: From Middle English either, from Old English ǣġhwæþer, from Proto-West Germanic *aiw + *gahwaþar. Akin to Old Saxon eogihwethar, iahwethar (Low German jeed); Old Dutch *iogewether, *iowether, *iother (Dutch ieder); Old High German eogihwedar, iegihweder, ieweder (German jeder).

examples.text: This song makes me want to cry.

translations.de: Bei diesem Lied möchte ich am liebsten weinen.
translations.fr: Cette chanson me donne envie de pleurer.

translations.de: Er weint fast jeden Tag.

examples.text: What is the population of the country?

translations.de: Dieses Land ist reich an natürlichen Ressourcen.
translations.fr: Ce pays est riche en ressources naturelles.
translations.pt: Este país é rico em recursos naturais.

more.definition: From or in the countryside, connected with it, or typical of it.; Of or connected to country music.; Originating in India rather than being imported from abroad.

examples.text: What is the location of the country?

examples.text: His name is known throughout this country.

translations.de: Sein Name ist bekannt im ganzen Lande.
translations.fr: Son nom est connu de tous dans ce pays.
translations.pt: Seu nome é conhecido em todo o país.

more.definition: The territory of a nation; a sovereign state or a region once independent and still distinct in institutions, language, etc.; A large area regarded as distinct from other areas, e.g. because it is inhabited by a specific group of people; An area of land of undefined extent; a region, a district.

Inherited from Middle English contre, borrowed from Old French contree, from Vulgar Latin *(terra) contrāta (“facing land”), from Latin contrā (“against”) + -āta (noun-forming suffix). examples.text: I saw the figure of a man.

translations.fr: J'ai vu la silhouette d'un homme.

translations.de: Sie hat eine gute Figur.

more.definition: A drawing or diagram conveying information.; The representation of any form, as by drawing, painting, modelling, carving, embroidering, etc.; especially, a representation of the human body.; A person, thing, or action representative of another

translations.de: Ich habe die Wahrheit herausgefunden.

translations.pt: Eu descobri a verdade.

examples.text: I need to figure out what I'm doing wrong.

translations.de: Ich muss dahinterkommen, was ich falsch mache.
translations.fr: Je dois découvrir ce que je fais mal.
translations.pt: Eu preciso descobrir o que eu estou fazendo errado.

examples.text: I figured I could be of some help.

translations.de: Ich dachte mir, ich könnte ein bisschen helfen.
translations.fr: J'ai pensé que je pourrais être utile.

more.definition: Used to summon a worker on duty, such as a bellhop.

examples.text: I've locked the front door.
