examples.text: The fronts of the houses were hung with flags.

translations.de: Die Häuserfronten waren mit Fahnen behangen.
translations.fr: Les façades des maisons étaient ornées de drapeaux.
translations.pt: Das fachadas das casas suspendiam-se bandeiras.

examples.text: Tom often forgets to lock the front door.

translations.de: Tom vergisst häufig, die Haustür abzuschließen.
translations.fr: Tom oublie souvent de fermer à clé la porte d'entrée.
translations.pt: Tom sempre esquece de trancar a porta da frente.

examples.text: He stood in front of me.

translations.de: Er stand vor mir.
translations.fr: Il se planta devant moi.
translations.pt: Ele ficou na minha frente.

more.definition: The foremost side of something or the end that faces the direction it normally moves.; The side of a building with the main entrance.; A field of activity.
more.etymology: Old French frontbor. From Middle English front, frunt, frount, from Old French front, frunt, from Latin frōns, frontem (“forehead”). Doublet of frons.

examples.text: We have a garden in front of our house.

translations.de: Wir haben einen Garten vor unserem Haus.
translations.fr: Nous avons un jardin devant notre maison.
translations.pt: Nós temos um jardim na frente de nossa casa.

examples.text: There is a lake in front of my house.

translations.de: Vor meinem Haus liegt ein See.
translations.fr: Devant ma maison se trouve un lac.
translations.pt: Há um lago em frente à minha casa.

examples.text: Go to the front desk to ask for some information.

translations.de: Gehen Sie zur Rezeption, um Informationen zu erhalten.
translations.fr: Va à l'accueil pour demander des renseignements.
translations.pt: Vá até a recepção para pedir informações.

examples.text: Marie is drying her hair in front of the mirror.

translations.de: Marie trocknet ihr Haar vor dem Spiegel.
translations.fr: Marie sèche ses cheveux devant le miroir.
translations.pt: Maria está secando o cabelo diante do espelho.

more.definition: To face, be opposite to.; To face up to, to meet head-on, to confront.; To adorn with, at the front; to put on the front.
more.etymology: Old French frontbor. From Middle English front, frunt, frount, from Old French front, frunt, from Latin frōns, frontem (“forehead”). Doublet of frons.

examples.text: Mary knew that she'd win.

translations.de: Mary wusste, sie würde gewinnen.
translations.fr: Mary savait qu'elle gagnerait.
translations.pt: Mary sabia que venceria.

examples.text: No matter what game he plays, he always wins.

translations.de: Ganz gleich, welches Spiel er spielt, er gewinnt immer.
translations.fr: Qu'importe le jeu auquel il joue, il gagne toujours.
translations.pt: Não importa qual jogo ele jogue, sempre vence.

examples.text: The truth doesn't always win.

translations.de: Nicht immer siegt die Wahrheit.
translations.fr: La vérité ne l'emporte pas toujours.
translations.pt: A verdade nem sempre prevalece.

examples.text: Who do you want to win?

translations.de: Wer soll gewinnen?
translations.fr: Qui veux-tu voir gagner ?
translations.pt: Quem você quer que ganhe?

more.definition: An individual victory.; A feat carried out successfully; a victorious achievement.; Pleasure; joy; delight.
more.etymology: From Middle English winn, winne, from Old English winn (“toil, labor, trouble, hardship; profit, gain; conflict, strife, war”), from Proto-Germanic *winną (“labour, struggle, fight”), from Proto-Indo-European *wenh₁- (“to strive, desire, wish, love”). Cognate with German Gewinn (“profit, gain”), Dutch gewin (“profit, gain”).

examples.text: He was lucky and won the competition.

translations.de: Er hatte Glück und gewann den Wettkampf.
translations.fr: Il eut de la chance et remporta la compétition.
translations.pt: Ele teve sorte de ganhar a competição.

examples.text: I didn't really want to win.

translations.de: Ich wollte nicht wirklich gewinnen.
translations.fr: Je ne voulais pas vraiment gagner.
translations.pt: Eu não queria realmente vencer.

examples.text: Tell Tom I won't be there.

translations.de: Sag Tom, dass ich nicht da sein werde.
translations.fr: Dis à Tom que je n'y serai pas.
translations.pt: Diga ao Tom que não estarei lá.

examples.text: I swear I won't tell anyone.

translations.de: Ich schwöre, ich werde es niemandem sagen.
translations.fr: Je jure que je ne le dirai à personne.
translations.pt: Eu juro não dizer a ninguém.

more.definition: To reach some destination or object, despite difficulty or toil (now usually intransitive, with preposition or locative adverb).; To triumph or achieve victory in (a game, a war, etc.).; To gain (a prize) by succeeding in competition or contest.
more.etymology: From Middle English winnen, from Old English winnan (“to labour, swink, toil,”) (compare Old English ġewinnan (“conquer, obtain, gain; endure, bear, suffer; be ill”)), from Proto-West Germanic *winnan, from Proto-Germanic *winnaną (“to swink, labour, win, gain, fight”), from Proto-Indo-European *wenh₁- (“to strive, wish, desire, love”).

examples.text: Whoa! Where did that come from?

translations.de: Oh! Wo kommt das her?
translations.pt: Opa! De onde isso veio?

examples.text: Whoa, this is getting weird.

translations.de: Herrje, jetzt wird’s bizarr.
translations.pt: Ei, isso tá ficando estranho.

examples.text: Woah, look! The sky's bright red. Let's take a picture.
Whoa! I'm going to be a father!

translations.pt: Ual! Eu vou ser pai!

more.definition: Stop (especially when commanding a horse or imitative thereof); calm down; slow down.; An expression of surprise.; Used as a meaningless filler in song lyrics.
more.etymology: Whoa (c. 1843) is a variant of woa (c. 1840), itself a variant of wo (c. 1787), from who (c. 1450), ultimately from Middle English ho, hoo (interjection), probably from Old Norse hó! (interjection, also, a shepherd's call). Compare German ho, Old French ho ! (“hold!, halt!”).

examples.text: Whoa! Where did that come from?

translations.de: Oh! Wo kommt das her?
translations.pt: Opa! De onde isso veio?

examples.text: Whoa, this is getting weird.

translations.de: Herrje, jetzt wird’s bizarr.
translations.pt: Ei, isso tá ficando estranho.

examples.text: Woah, I think I just had deja vu.
Woah, are you serious?

more.definition: To attempt to slow (an animal) by crying "whoa".
more.etymology: Whoa (c. 1843) is a variant of woa (c. 1840), itself a variant of wo (c. 1787), from who (c. 1450), ultimately from Middle English ho, hoo (interjection), probably from Old Norse hó! (interjection, also, a shepherd's call). Compare German ho, Old French ho ! (“hold!, halt!”).

examples.text: We had no choice but to return home.

translations.de: Wir hatten keine andere Wahl, als nach Hause zurückzukehren.
translations.fr: Nous n'avons eu d'autre choix que de rentrer chez nous.
translations.pt: Não tínhamos escolha senão voltar para casa.

examples.text: What do you want in return?

translations.de: Was willst du als Gegenleistung?
translations.fr: Que souhaitez-vous en retour ?
translations.pt: O que você quer em troca?

examples.text: I hope to return to France.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, nach Frankreich zurückzukehren.
translations.fr: J'espère retourner en France.
translations.pt: Eu espero retornar à França.

examples.text: Why don't you return to your quarters?

translations.de: Warum gehen Sie nicht zurück in Ihr Quartier?
translations.fr: Pourquoi ne réintègres-tu pas tes quartiers ?
translations.pt: Por que não volta para seus aposentos?

more.definition: The act of returning.; A return ticket.; An item that is returned, e.g. due to a defect.
more.etymology: From Middle English returnen, retornen, from Anglo-Norman returner, from Old French retourner, retorner, from Medieval Latin retornare (“to turn back”), from re- + tornare (“to turn”). By surface analysis, re- + turn. Compare beturn. Displaced native Old English eftċierran, literally "eft-char".

examples.text: I want you to return to Boston.

translations.de: Ich möchte, dass du nach Boston zurückkommst.
translations.fr: Je veux que tu reviennes à Boston.
translations.pt: Eu quero que você retorne a Boston.

examples.text: She returned the book to the library.

translations.de: Sie brachte das Buch zurück in die Bücherei.
translations.fr: Elle restitua le livre à la bibliothèque.
translations.pt: Ela devolveu o livro à biblioteca.

examples.text: I remember returning the book to the library.

translations.de: Ich erinnere mich, der Bibliothek das Buch zurückgegeben zu haben.
translations.fr: Je me souviens avoir rendu le livre à la bibliothèque.
translations.pt: Lembro-me de ter devolvido o livro à biblioteca.

examples.text: As soon as he returns, I will tell you.

translations.de: Sobald er zurückkehrt, sage ich es dir.
translations.fr: Dès qu'il reviendra, je vous le dirai.
translations.pt: Assim que ele retornar, eu te contarei.

more.definition: To come or go back (to a place or person).; To go back in thought, narration, or argument.; To recur; to come again.
more.etymology: From Middle English returnen, retornen, from Anglo-Norman returner, from Old French retourner, retorner, from Medieval Latin retornare (“to turn back”), from re- + tornare (“to turn”). By surface analysis, re- + turn. Compare beturn. Displaced native Old English eftċierran, literally "eft-char".

examples.text: I wonder if it will rain tomorrow.

translations.de: Ich frage mich, ob es morgen regnen wird.
translations.fr: Je me demande s'il pleuvra demain.
translations.pt: Será que choverá amanhã?

examples.text: I wonder what has become of him.

translations.de: Ich frage mich, was aus ihm geworden ist.
translations.fr: Je me demande ce qu'il est devenu.
translations.pt: Eu me pergunto o que aconteceu com ele.

examples.text: I wonder whose scissors these are.

translations.de: Wem gehört wohl diese Schere?
translations.fr: Je me demande à qui appartiennent ces ciseaux.
translations.pt: Pergunto-me de quem será essa tesoura.

examples.text: I wonder where Tom studied French.

translations.de: Ich frage mich, wo Tom wohl Französisch gelernt hat.
translations.fr: Je me demande où Tom a étudié le français.
translations.pt: Onde será que Tom estudou francês?

more.definition: A sense of awe, astonishment and curiosity, inspired by unexpected events, novel experiences and inexplicable circumstances, sometimes accompanied by surprise, shock or reverence.; Something that causes amazement or awe; a marvel.; Fortunate circumstances.
more.etymology: From Middle English wonder, wunder, from Old English wundor (“wonder, miracle, marvel”), from Proto-West Germanic *wundr, from Proto-Germanic *wundrą.

examples.text: I wonder if there's a connection.

translations.de: Ich frage mich, ob es da einen Zusammenhang gibt.
translations.fr: Je me demande s'il y a une relation.
translations.pt: Será que há uma conexão?

examples.text: We were all wondering why you were late.

translations.de: Wir fragten uns schon alle, warum du wohl so spät kommest.
translations.fr: Nous nous demandions pourquoi tu es arrivé tard.
translations.pt: Todos estávamos nos perguntando por que você estava atrasado.

examples.text: One wonders how it's possible.

translations.de: Man möchte gerne wissen, wie das möglich ist.
translations.fr: On se demande comment c'est possible.
translations.pt: Pergunta-se como é possível.

examples.text: She wondered where she had lost her purse.

translations.de: Sie fragte sich, wo sie wohl ihre Handtasche verloren hatte.
translations.fr: Elle se demanda où elle avait perdu son sac à main.
translations.pt: Ela ficou imaginando onde teria perdido sua bolsa.

more.definition: To be affected with surprise or admiration; to be struck with astonishment; to be amazed; to marvel; often followed by at.; To ponder; to feel doubt and curiosity; to query in the mind.
more.etymology: From Middle English wonder, wunder, from Old English wundor (“wonder, miracle, marvel”), from Proto-West Germanic *wundr, from Proto-Germanic *wundrą.

examples.text: An honest man never steals money.

translations.de: Ein ehrlicher Mann stiehlt nie Geld.
translations.fr: Un honnête homme ne vole jamais d'argent.
translations.pt: Um homem honesto nunca rouba dinheiro.

examples.text: He steals stuff.

translations.de: Er stiehlt Sachen.
translations.fr: Il vole des trucs.
translations.pt: Ele rouba.

examples.text: Tom steals stuff.

translations.de: Tom stiehlt.
translations.fr: Tom vole des choses.
translations.pt: Tom rouba coisas.

examples.text: Did you really steal this food?

translations.de: Hast du dieses Essen wirklich gestohlen?
translations.fr: Avez-vous réellement volé cette nourriture ?
translations.pt: É verdade que você furtou esta comida?

more.definition: The act of stealing.; A piece of merchandise available at a very low, attractive price; the act of buying it.; A situation in which a defensive player actively takes possession of the ball or puck from the opponent's team.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English stelen, from Old English stelan, from Proto-West Germanic *stelan, from Proto-Germanic *stelaną.

examples.text: Tom stole all of Mary's money.

translations.de: Tom hat Maria all ihr Geld gestohlen.
translations.fr: Tom a volé tout l'argent de Mary.
translations.pt: Tom roubou todo o dinheiro de Mary.

examples.text: She accused him of stealing her money.

translations.de: Sie beschuldigte ihn, ihr Geld gestohlen zu haben.
translations.fr: Elle l'a accusé de lui avoir volé de l'argent.
translations.pt: Ela o acusou de ter roubado seu dinheiro.

examples.text: My watch was stolen last night.

translations.de: Gestern Nacht stahl man mir meine Uhr.
translations.fr: Ma montre a été volée la nuit dernière.
translations.pt: O meu relógio foi roubado ontem à noite.

examples.text: She accused me of stealing her money.

translations.de: Sie bezichtigte mich, ihr Geld gestohlen zu haben.
translations.fr: Elle m'a accusé de lui avoir volé son argent.
translations.pt: Ele me acusou de ter roubado o dinheiro dela.

more.definition: To take illegally, or without the owner's permission, something owned by someone else without intending to return it.; To appropriate without giving credit or acknowledgement.; To get or effect surreptitiously or artfully.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English stelen, from Old English stelan, from Proto-West Germanic *stelan, from Proto-Germanic *stelaną.

examples.text: The bee is an insect and it eats honey.

translations.de: Die Biene ist ein Insekt und frisst Honig.
translations.fr: L'abeille est un insecte et elle mange du miel.
translations.pt: A abelha é um inseto e come mel.

examples.text: The bear is eating honey.

translations.de: Der Bär frisst Honig.
translations.fr: L'ours mange du miel.
translations.pt: O urso está comendo mel.

examples.text: Bees provide us with honey.

translations.de: Bienen geben uns Honig.
translations.fr: Les abeilles nous fournissent en miel.
translations.pt: As abelhas nos dão mel.

examples.text: Bees provide honey for us.

translations.de: Bienen versorgen uns mit Honig.
translations.fr: Les abeilles nous fournissent du miel.
translations.pt: As abelhas nos fornecem mel.

more.definition: Involving or resembling honey.; Of a pale yellow to brownish-yellow color, like most types of honey.; Honey-sweet.
more.etymology: From Middle English hony, honi, from Old English huniġ, from Proto-West Germanic *hunag, from Proto-Germanic *hunagą (compare Saterland Frisian Hunich, West Frisian hunich, German Low German Honnig, German Honig), from earlier *hunangą (compare North Frisian honning, hönning, West Frisian huning, Dutch honing, Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk honning, Swedish honung, Faroese hunangur, Icelandic …

examples.text: The woman drinks the tea with sugar or with honey.

translations.de: Die Frau trinkt den Tee mit Zucker oder mit Honig.
translations.fr: La femme boit le thé avec du sucre ou du miel.
translations.pt: A mulher bebe o chá com açúcar ou com mel.

examples.text: Are you sleepy, honey?

translations.de: Bist du schläfrig, Schatz?
translations.fr: As-tu sommeil, ma biche ?
translations.pt: Você está com sono, amor?

examples.text: Don't lie, Honey.

translations.de: Lüg nicht, Liebling.
translations.fr: Ne mens pas, chéri.
translations.pt: Não minta, querido.

examples.text: Hot lemon with honey is a good remedy for colds.

translations.de: Heiße Zitrone mit Honig ist ein gutes Mittel gegen Erkältung.
translations.fr: Du citron chaud avec du miel est un bon remède contre les rhumes.
translations.pt: Limão quente com mel é um bom remédio para resfriados.

more.definition: A sweet, viscous, gold-colored fluid produced from plant nectar by bees, and often consumed by humans.; A variety of this substance.; Something sweet or desirable.
more.etymology: From Middle English hony, honi, from Old English huniġ, from Proto-West Germanic *hunag, from Proto-Germanic *hunagą (compare Saterland Frisian Hunich, West Frisian hunich, German Low German Honnig, German Honig), from earlier *hunangą (compare North Frisian honning, hönning, West Frisian huning, Dutch honing, Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk honning, Swedish honung, Faroese hunangur, Icelandic …

examples.text: Yesterday, I put honey in my tea.

translations.de: Gestern habe ich Honig in meinen Tee getan.
translations.fr: Hier, j'ai mis du miel dans mon thé.
translations.pt: Ontem pus mel no meu chá.

examples.text: I dipped my finger into the honey.

translations.de: Ich stippte meinen Finger in den Honig.
translations.fr: J'ai trempé le doigt dans le miel.
translations.pt: Mergulhei o dedo no mel.

examples.text: Your kiss is sweeter than honey.

translations.de: Dein Kuss ist süßer als Honig.
translations.fr: Ton baiser est plus doux que du miel.
translations.pt: Seu beijo é mais doce que mel.

examples.text: He uses honey instead of sugar.

translations.de: Er verwendet statt Zucker Honig.
translations.fr: Il met du miel à la place du sucre.
translations.pt: Ele usa mel em vez de açúcar.

more.definition: To sweeten; to make agreeable.; To add honey to.; To be gentle, agreeable, or coaxing; to talk fondly; to use endearments.
more.etymology: From Middle English hony, honi, from Old English huniġ, from Proto-West Germanic *hunag, from Proto-Germanic *hunagą (compare Saterland Frisian Hunich, West Frisian hunich, German Low German Honnig, German Honig), from earlier *hunangą (compare North Frisian honning, hönning, West Frisian huning, Dutch honing, Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk honning, Swedish honung, Faroese hunangur, Icelandic …

examples.text: I beat him at chess.

translations.de: Ich habe ihn im Schach geschlagen.
translations.fr: Je l'ai battu aux échecs.
translations.pt: Eu o venci no xadrez.

examples.text: Ken beat me at chess.

translations.de: Ken hat mich beim Schach besiegt.
translations.fr: Ken m'a battu aux échecs.
translations.pt: Ken me venceu no xadrez.

examples.text: He won't beat me.

translations.de: Er wird mich nicht schlagen.
translations.fr: Il ne me battra pas.
translations.pt: Ele não vai me pegar.

examples.text: We beat three teams.

translations.de: Wir haben drei Mannschaften geschlagen.
translations.fr: Nous avons battu trois équipes.
translations.pt: Vencemos três equipes.

more.definition: Exhausted.; Dilapidated, beat up.; Having impressively attractive makeup.
more.etymology: From Middle English bet (simple past of beten "to beat"), from Old English bēot (simple past of bēatan "to beat"). Middle English bet would regularly yield *beet; the modern form is influenced by the present stem and the past participle beaten, perhaps by analogy with the Early Modern English paradigm eat:eat (“ate”):eaten.

examples.text: Don't beat around the bush.

translations.de: Rede nicht um den heißen Brei herum!
translations.fr: Ne tourne pas autour du pot.
translations.pt: Pare de enrolar.

examples.text: My wife beats me.

translations.de: Meine Frau schlägt mich.
translations.fr: Ma femme me bat.
translations.pt: A minha mulher me bate.

examples.text: You can't beat me.

translations.de: Du kannst mich nicht schlagen.
translations.fr: Tu ne peux pas me battre.
translations.pt: Você não pode me bater.

examples.text: We need to band together to beat the enemy.

translations.de: Wir müssen uns vereinigen, um den Feind zu schlagen.
translations.fr: Nous devons nous unir pour battre l'ennemi.
translations.pt: Devemos nos unir para derrotar o inimigo.

more.definition: A stroke; a blow.; A pulsation or throb.; A pulse on the beat level, the metric level at which pulses are heard as the basic unit. Thus a beat is the basic time unit of a piece.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English beten, from Old English bēatan (“to beat, pound, strike, lash, dash, thrust, hurt, injure”), from Proto-West Germanic *bautan, from Proto-Germanic *bautaną (“to push, strike”).

examples.text: If you can't beat them, join them.

translations.de: Wenn du sie nicht besiegen kannst, schließe dich ihnen an.
translations.fr: Si tu ne peux pas les battre, allie-toi avec eux.
translations.pt: Se não pode vencê-los, junte-se a eles.

examples.text: His heart was beating wildly.

translations.de: Sein Herz schlug wie wild.
translations.fr: Son cœur battait frénétiquement.
translations.pt: Seu coração batia desenfreadamente.

examples.text: Tom beats his wife.

translations.de: Tom schlägt seine Frau.
translations.fr: Thomas bat sa femme.
translations.pt: Tom bate na mulher.

examples.text: Tom's heart suddenly began to beat faster.

translations.de: Toms Herz begann plötzlich, schneller zu schlagen.
translations.fr: Le cœur de Tom se mit soudain à battre plus vite.
translations.pt: O coração de Tom começou a bater mais forte de repente.

more.definition: To hit; to strike.; To strike or pound repeatedly, usually in some sort of rhythm.; To strike repeatedly; to inflict repeated blows; to knock vigorously or loudly.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English beten, from Old English bēatan (“to beat, pound, strike, lash, dash, thrust, hurt, injure”), from Proto-West Germanic *bautan, from Proto-Germanic *bautaną (“to push, strike”).

examples.text: I know you think I'm stupid.

translations.de: Ich weiß, dass du mich für blöd hältst.
translations.fr: Je sais que tu penses que je suis stupide.
translations.pt: Eu sei que você acha que eu sou estúpido.

examples.text: This is the stupidest thing I have ever heard.

translations.de: Das ist das Dümmste, was ich je gehört habe.
translations.fr: C'est la chose la plus bête que j'aie jamais entendue.
translations.pt: Essa é a coisa mais estúpida que eu já ouvi na vida.

examples.text: It was just a stupid mistake.

translations.de: Das war einfach ein dummer Fehler.
translations.fr: C'était juste une erreur stupide.
translations.pt: Só foi um erro bobo.

examples.text: I refuse to answer such a stupid question.

translations.de: Ich weigere mich, eine so dumme Frage zu beantworten.
translations.fr: Je refuse de répondre à une question aussi stupide.
translations.pt: Eu me nego a responder a uma pergunta tão idiota.

more.definition: Lacking in intelligence.; Exhibiting the quality of having been done by someone lacking in intelligence.; Unpleasant; annoying to the speaker. This sense can be used alongside obscene words.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-der. Latin stupidusder. Middle French stupideder. From Middle French stupide, from Latin stupidus (“struck senseless, amazed”), from stupeō (“be amazed or confounded, be struck senseless”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tup-, *(s)tewp- (“to push, stick”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tew- (“to push, hit”). Cognate with Old High German stubarōn (“to be astonished, be stunned, be blocked”).

examples.text: Who are you calling stupid?

translations.de: Wen nennst du hier einen Dummkopf?
translations.fr: De qui dis-tu qu'il est stupide ?
translations.pt: Quem você está chamando de burro?

examples.text: No one is born wise, but many die stupid.

translations.de: Niemand wird klug geboren, doch viele sterben dumm.
translations.fr: Personne ne naît sage, mais beaucoup meurent stupides.
translations.pt: Ninguém nasce sábio, mas muitos morrem estúpidos.

examples.text: Tom did something very stupid.

translations.de: Tom hat etwas sehr Dummes getan.
translations.fr: Tom fit quelque chose de très stupide.
translations.pt: Tom fez algo muito estúpido.

examples.text: It was a stupid joke.

translations.de: Das war ein blöder Witz.
translations.fr: C'était une blague idiote.
translations.pt: Foi uma piada burra.

more.definition: Extremely.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-der. Latin stupidusder. Middle French stupideder. From Middle French stupide, from Latin stupidus (“struck senseless, amazed”), from stupeō (“be amazed or confounded, be struck senseless”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tup-, *(s)tewp- (“to push, stick”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tew- (“to push, hit”). Cognate with Old High German stubarōn (“to be astonished, be stunned, be blocked”).

examples.text: Do you think I'm stupid?

translations.de: Denkst du, ich bin blöd?
translations.fr: Penses-tu que je sois idiot ?

examples.text: My last husband was really stupid.

translations.de: Ich würde an deiner Stelle anders handeln.
translations.fr: J'agirais différemment à votre place.
translations.pt: Eu agiria de outra forma, em seu lugar.

examples.text: He acts quickly.

translations.de: Er handelt schnell.
translations.fr: Il agit rapidement.
translations.pt: Ele age rapidamente.

examples.text: I will act on your advice.

translations.de: Ich werde deinem Rat folgen.
translations.fr: J'agirai selon tes conseils.
translations.pt: Vou seguir o seu conselho.

examples.text: We have to act fast.

translations.de: Wir müssen schnell handeln.
translations.fr: Il faut faire vite.
translations.pt: Temos de agir rápido.

more.definition: Something done, a deed.; Something done once and for all, as distinguished from a work.; A product of a legislative body, a statute.
more.etymology: Old French actbor. From Middle English acte, from Old French acte, from Latin ācta (“register of events”), plural of āctum (“decree, law”), from agere (“to do, to act”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵeti. Compare German Akte (“file”). Partially displaced deed, from Old English dǣd (“act, deed”).

examples.text: In an emergency, do you act quickly?

translations.de: Reagierst du schnell in einer Krise?
translations.fr: En cas d'urgence, agissez-vous rapidement ?
translations.pt: Numa emergência, você age com rapidez?

examples.text: This director doesn't know anything about acting.

translations.de: Dieser Regisseur hat keine Ahnung von Schauspielerei.
translations.fr: Ce directeur ne connaît rien à la comédie.
translations.pt: Este diretor não sabe nada sobre atuação.

examples.text: She acted like she didn't know me.

translations.de: Sie tat so, als ob sie mich nicht kennen würde.
translations.fr: Elle s'est comportée comme si elle ne me connaissait pas.
translations.pt: Ela agiu como se não me conhecesse.

examples.text: Tobacco acts on the brain.

translations.de: Tabak wirkt auf das Gehirn.
translations.fr: Le tabac agit sur le cerveau.
translations.pt: O tabaco age sobre o cérebro.

more.definition: To do something.; To perform a theatrical role.; Of a play: to be acted out (well or badly).
more.etymology: Old French actbor. From Middle English acte, from Old French acte, from Latin ācta (“register of events”), plural of āctum (“decree, law”), from agere (“to do, to act”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵeti. Compare German Akte (“file”). Partially displaced deed, from Old English dǣd (“act, deed”).

examples.text: Why didn't you say so earlier?

translations.de: Warum hast du das nicht früher gesagt?
translations.fr: Pourquoi tu ne l'as pas dit plus tôt ?
translations.pt: Por que não disse logo?

examples.text: The apple trees blossomed early this year.

translations.de: Die Apfelbäume haben dieses Jahr früh geblüht.
translations.fr: Les pommiers ont fleuri tôt cette année.
translations.pt: As macieiras floresceram cedo este ano.

examples.text: The earliest civilizations arose in Mesopotamia.

translations.de: Die ersten Zivilisationen entstanden in Mesopotamien.
translations.fr: Les civilisations premières apparurent en Mésopotamie.
translations.pt: As primeiras civilizações surgiram na Mesopotâmia.

examples.text: These flowers bloom earlier than others do.

translations.de: Diese Blumen blühen früher als andere.
translations.fr: Ces fleurs fleurissent plus tôt que les autres.
translations.pt: Essas flores desabrocham mais cedo do que outras.

more.definition: At a time in advance of the usual or expected event.; Arriving a time before expected; sooner than on time.; After but close to the start of a period of time.
more.etymology: From Middle English erly, erlich, earlich, from Old English ǣrlīċ (“early”, adjective), equivalent to ere + -ly.

examples.text: You should've thought of that earlier.

translations.de: Das hättest du dir eher überlegen sollen.
translations.fr: Il fallait y penser plus tôt.
translations.pt: Você deveria ter pensado nisso antes.

examples.text: What is your earliest memory from childhood?

translations.de: Was ist deine früheste Kindheitserinnerung?
translations.fr: Quel sont vos premiers souvenirs d'enfance ?
translations.pt: Qual é a sua lembrança mais antiga da infância?

examples.text: She's accustomed to getting up early.

translations.de: Sie ist es gewohnt, früh aufzustehen.
translations.fr: Elle est habituée à se lever tôt.
translations.pt: Ela está acostumada a levantar cedo.

examples.text: John got up much earlier than usual.

translations.de: John ist viel früher als gewohnt aufgestanden.
translations.fr: John s'est levé beaucoup plus tôt que d'habitude.
translations.pt: João se levantou muito antes do que de costume.

more.definition: At a time before expected; sooner than usual.; Soon; in good time; seasonably.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der. Proto-Germanic *līkąder. From Middle English erly, orely, arely, erliche, arliche, from Old English ǣrlīċe, ārlīċe (“early; early in the morning”, adverb), equivalent to ere + -ly. Cognate with Old Norse árliga, árla ( > Danish årle, Swedish arla, Norwegian årle, Faroese árla).

examples.text: She's used to getting up early.

translations.de: Sie ist frühes Aufstehen gewohnt.
translations.fr: Elle est habituée à se lever tôt.
translations.pt: Ela está acostumada a levantar cedo.

examples.text: It's too early to get up.

translations.de: Es ist zu früh, um aufzustehen.
translations.fr: Il est trop tôt pour se lever.
translations.pt: É muito cedo para levantar da cama.

examples.text: I've never woken up this early.

translations.de: Ich bin nie so früh aufgewacht.
translations.fr: Je ne me suis jamais réveillé si tôt.
translations.pt: Nunca acordei tão cedo.

examples.text: I'm used to getting up early.

translations.de: Ich bin es gewohnt, früh aufzustehen.
translations.fr: J'ai l'habitude de me lever tôt.
translations.pt: Estou acostumada a me levantar cedo.

more.definition: A shift (scheduled work period) that takes place early in the day.
more.etymology: From Middle English erly, erlich, earlich, from Old English ǣrlīċ (“early”, adjective), equivalent to ere + -ly.

examples.text: Forgive me, I'm a bit nervous.

translations.de: Verzeihung, ich bin ein bisschen nervös.
translations.fr: Pardon, je suis un peu nerveux.
translations.pt: Perdoe-me, estou um pouco nervoso.

examples.text: Tom is a bit older than Mary.

translations.de: Tom ist etwas älter als Maria.
translations.fr: Tom est un peu plus vieux que Mary.
translations.pt: O Tom é um pouco mais velho que a Mary.

examples.text: He's a bit older than me.

translations.de: Er ist etwas älter als ich.
translations.fr: Il est un peu plus vieux que moi.
translations.pt: Ele é um pouco mais velho que eu.

examples.text: My father is a bit old-fashioned.

translations.de: Mein Vater ist ein wenig altmodisch.
translations.fr: Mon père est un peu ringard.
translations.pt: Meu pai tem um gosto antigo.

more.definition: Having been bitten.
more.etymology: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form. See bite. Replaced a former strong past tense, seen in Middle English bot and Old English bāt.

examples.text: There were bits of broken glass on the floor.

translations.de: Auf dem Fußboden lagen Glasscherben.
translations.fr: Il y avait des morceaux de verre cassé sur le sol.
translations.pt: Havia cacos de vidro no chão.

examples.text: He is getting better bit by bit.

translations.de: Er verbessert sich nach und nach.
translations.fr: Il s'améliore petit à petit.
translations.pt: Ele está melhorando aos poucos.

examples.text: A dog bit her on the leg.

translations.de: Ein Hund biss ihr ins Bein.
translations.fr: Un chien l'a mordue à la jambe.
translations.pt: Um cachorro mordeu a perna dela.

examples.text: The dog bit me in the hand.

translations.de: Der Hund biss mich in die Hand.
translations.fr: Le chien me mordit la main.
translations.pt: O cachorro mordeu-me na mão.

more.definition: A small amount of something.; A piece of metal placed in a horse's mouth and connected to the reins to direct the animal.; A rotary cutting tool, fitted to a drill, brace, or router, used to bore or drill holes or to remove material from the profile of the workpiece.
more.etymology: From Middle English bitte, bite, from Old English bita (“bit; fragment; morsel”) and bite (“a bite; cut”), from Proto-Germanic *bitô and *bitiz; both from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeyd- (“to split”). More at bite. Cognates Cognate with West Frisian bit, Saterland Frisian Bit, Dutch bit, German Low German Beet, Biet, German Biss and Bissen, Danish bid, Swedish bit, Icelandic biti.

examples.text: You bit the hand that fed you.

translations.de: Du hast die Hand gebissen, die dich gefüttert hat.
translations.fr: Tu as mordu la main qui te nourrissait.
translations.pt: Você mordeu a mão que lhe deu de comer.

examples.text: There were bits of broken glass on the floor.

translations.de: Auf dem Fußboden lagen Glasscherben.
translations.fr: Il y avait des morceaux de verre cassé sur le sol.
translations.pt: Havia cacos de vidro no chão.

examples.text: I think she is just a bit tired.

translations.de: Ich glaube, sie ist nur ein bisschen müde.
translations.fr: Je pense qu'elle est juste un peu fatiguée.
translations.pt: Acho que ela está apenas um pouco cansada.

examples.text: I want to lose a bit of weight.

translations.de: Ich möchte etwas abnehmen.
translations.fr: Je veux perdre un peu de poids.
translations.pt: Quero perder um pouco de peso.

more.definition: To put a bridle upon; to put the bit in the mouth of (a horse).
more.etymology: From Middle English bitte, bite, from Old English bita (“bit; fragment; morsel”) and bite (“a bite; cut”), from Proto-Germanic *bitô and *bitiz; both from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeyd- (“to split”). More at bite. Cognates Cognate with West Frisian bit, Saterland Frisian Bit, Dutch bit, German Low German Beet, Biet, German Biss and Bissen, Danish bid, Swedish bit, Icelandic biti.

examples.text: This picture has a very interesting history.

translations.de: Das Foto hat eine sehr interessante Geschichte.
translations.fr: Cette photo a une histoire très intéressante.
translations.pt: Esta foto tem uma história muito interessante.

examples.text: His hobby is painting pictures of flowers.

translations.de: Sein Hobby ist Blumenbilder zu malen.
translations.fr: Son passe-temps est de peindre des tableaux de fleurs.
translations.pt: O passatempo dele é pintar quadros de flores.

examples.text: The picture is in black and white.

translations.de: Das Bild ist schwarzweiß.
translations.fr: La photo est en noir et blanc.
translations.pt: O quadro está em preto e branco.

examples.text: The girl in the picture is smiling.

translations.de: Das Mädchen auf dem Bild lächelt.
translations.fr: La fille de la photo sourit.
translations.pt: A garota na foto está sorrindo.

more.definition: A representation of anything (as a person, a landscape, a building) upon canvas, paper, or other surface, by drawing, painting, printing, photography, etc.; An image; a representation as in the imagination.; A painting.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English picture, from Latin pictūra (“the art of painting, a painting”), from pingō (“to paint”). Doublet of pictura.

examples.text: Who's the girl in this picture?

translations.de: Wer ist das Mädchen auf diesem Bild?
translations.fr: Qui est la fille sur la photo ?
translations.pt: Quem é a garota da foto?

examples.text: There are many pictures in this book.

translations.de: In diesem Buch sind viele Bilder.
translations.fr: Ce livre a beaucoup d'images.
translations.pt: Há muitas figuras neste livro.

examples.text: It's a black-and-white picture.

translations.de: Das ist ein Schwarzweißbild.
translations.fr: C'est une photo en noir et blanc.
translations.pt: É uma foto em preto e branco.

examples.text: What did you take a picture of?

translations.de: Wovon hast du ein Bild gemacht?
translations.fr: De quoi as-tu pris une photo ?
translations.pt: Você tirou foto do quê?

more.definition: To represent in or with a picture.; To imagine or envision.; To depict or describe vividly.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English picture, from Latin pictūra (“the art of painting, a painting”), from pingō (“to paint”). Doublet of pictura.

examples.text: Bye for now.

translations.de: Wiedersehen.
translations.fr: Au revoir.
translations.pt: Até a vista!

examples.text: I have to go now. Bye!

translations.de: Ich muss jetzt gehen. Tschüss!
translations.fr: Je dois y aller maintenant. Salut !

examples.text: Good-bye, Sayoko!

translations.fr: Sayonara, Sayoko !
translations.pt: Adeus, Sayoko!

examples.text: Thanks for the ride. I really appreciate it. Bye.

translations.de: Danke, daß du mich hergefahren hast! Dafür bin ich dir wirklich dankbar! Mach’s gut!
translations.pt: Obrigado pela carona. Fico muito agradecido. Tchau.

more.definition: Out of the way; remote.; Secondary; supplementary.
more.etymology: Variant form of by, from Old English bī (“being near”).

examples.text: Bye for now.

translations.de: Wiedersehen.
translations.fr: Au revoir.
translations.pt: Até a vista!

examples.text: She hung up without saying good-bye.

translations.de: Sie hängte auf, ohne sich zu verabschieden.
translations.fr: Elle a raccroché sans même dire au revoir.

examples.text: He went out without saying good-bye.

translations.de: Er ging hinaus, ohne auf Wiedersehen zu sagen.
translations.fr: Il est parti sans dire au revoir.

examples.text: She waved good-bye to me.

translations.de: Sie winkte mir zum Abschied.
translations.fr: D'un signe, elle me dit "au revoir".

more.definition: Goodbye.; An exclamation of disbelief or dismissal.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *wíterosder. Old English wiþerclip. Proto-Indo-European *uswísder. English goodinflu. English goodbyeclip. Shortened form of goodbye.

examples.text: Bye for now.

translations.de: Wiedersehen.
translations.fr: Au revoir.
translations.pt: Até a vista!

examples.text: It is high time we said good-bye.

translations.fr: Il est grand temps qu'on dise au revoir.
translations.pt: Já passou da hora de nos despedirmos.

examples.text: Good bye and thanks a lot, Little Venusian says.

translations.de: „Auf Wiedersehen und vielen Dank!“ sagt der kleine Venusianer.
translations.fr: Au revoir et merci bien ! dit Petit Vénusien.

examples.text: She went out without saying good-bye.

translations.de: Sie ging hinaus, ohne auf Wiedersehen zu sagen.
translations.fr: Elle s'en alla sans dire au revoir.

more.definition: The position of a person or team in a tournament or competition who draws no opponent in a particular round so advances to the next round unopposed, or is awarded points for a win in a league table; also the phantom opponent of such a person or team.; An extra scored when the batsmen take runs after the ball has passed the striker without hitting either the bat or the batsman.; An unspecified way or place.
more.etymology: Variant form of by, from Old English bī (“being near”).

examples.text: How long does it take on foot?

translations.de: Wie lange braucht man zu Fuß?
translations.fr: Combien de temps cela prend-il à pied ?
translations.pt: Quanto tempo leva para ir a pé?

examples.text: I've got blisters on my feet.

translations.de: Ich habe Blasen an den Füßen.
translations.fr: J'ai des ampoules aux pieds.
translations.pt: Eu tenho bolhas nos meus pés.

examples.text: Do you go to school on foot?

translations.de: Geht ihr zu Fuß zur Schule?
translations.fr: Allez-vous à l'école à pied ?
translations.pt: Você vai a pé para a escola?

examples.text: These shoes don't fit my feet.

translations.de: Diese Schuhe passen mir nicht.
translations.fr: Ces chaussures ne me vont pas.
translations.pt: Estes sapatos não me servem.

more.definition: A biological structure found in many animals that is used for locomotion and that is frequently a separate organ at the terminal part of the leg.; Specifically, a human foot, which is found below the ankle and is used for standing and walking.; Travel by walking.
more.etymology: From Middle English fot, fote, foot, from Old English fōt, from Proto-West Germanic *fōt, from Proto-Germanic *fōts, from Proto-Indo-European *pṓds. The plural feet is the result of i-umlaut in Proto-West Germanic *fōti, see more at Old English fōt. Doublet of pes, pie (“Spanish unit of length”), and pous.

examples.text: He goes to work on foot.

translations.de: Er geht zu Fuß zur Arbeit.
translations.fr: Il va au travail à pied.
translations.pt: Ele vai para o trabalho a pé.

examples.text: Tom goes to school by foot.

translations.de: Tom geht zu Fuß zur Schule.
translations.fr: Tom se rend à l'école à pied.
translations.pt: Tom vai à escola a pé.

examples.text: He hurt his left foot when he fell.

translations.de: Er hat sich am linken Fuß verletzt, als er hingefallen ist.
translations.fr: Il s'est blessé au pied gauche en tombant.
translations.pt: Ele machucou o pé esquerdo quando caiu.

examples.text: Are you going on foot?

translations.de: Gehst du zu Fuß?
translations.fr: Tu y vas à pied ?
translations.pt: Vocês vão a pé?

more.definition: To use the foot to kick (usually a ball).; To pay (a bill).; To tread to measure of music; to dance; to trip; to skip.
more.etymology: From Middle English fot, fote, foot, from Old English fōt, from Proto-West Germanic *fōt, from Proto-Germanic *fōts, from Proto-Indo-European *pṓds. The plural feet is the result of i-umlaut in Proto-West Germanic *fōti, see more at Old English fōt. Doublet of pes, pie (“Spanish unit of length”), and pous.

examples.text: I sometimes have a pain in my stomach.

translations.de: Manchmal habe ich Magenschmerzen.
translations.fr: J'ai parfois une douleur à l'estomac.
translations.pt: Às vezes tenho dor na barriga.

examples.text: She sometimes has her mother cut her hair.

translations.de: Sie lässt sich manchmal von ihrer Mutter die Haare schneiden.
translations.fr: Elle se fait parfois couper les cheveux par sa mère.
translations.pt: A mãe dela corta o seu cabelo algumas vezes.

examples.text: He is sometimes absent from school.

translations.de: Er fehlt manchmal in der Schule.
translations.fr: Il est quelquefois absent de l'école.
translations.pt: Ele falta à escola de vez em quando.

examples.text: He sometimes comes to see me.

translations.de: Er besucht mich manchmal.
translations.fr: Il me rend parfois visite.
translations.pt: Às vezes ele vem me ver.

more.etymology: From Middle English sumtymes, somtymes, som tymes, equivalent to sometime + -s (adverbial suffix). Compare West Frisian somstiden (“sometimes”), Dutch somtijds, somwijlen (“sometimes”).

examples.text: Patience is sometimes the most effective weapon.

translations.de: Geduld ist manchmal die wirkungsvollste Waffe.
translations.fr: La patience est parfois l'arme la plus efficace.
translations.pt: A paciência, às vezes, é a arma mais eficiente.

examples.text: The old man sometimes talks to himself.

translations.de: Der alte Mann führt manchmal Selbstgespräche.
translations.fr: Le vieil homme se parle parfois à lui-même.
translations.pt: O velho homem às vezes fala consigo mesmo.

examples.text: I sometimes go home for lunch.

translations.de: Manchmal gehe ich zum Mittagessen nach Hause.
translations.fr: Parfois, je rentre à la maison pour le déjeuner.
translations.pt: Às vezes vou para casa almoçar.

examples.text: People are sometimes resistant to change.

translations.de: Die Leute stellen sich Veränderungen manchmal entgegen.
translations.fr: Les gens sont parfois réfractaires au changement.
translations.pt: As pessoas às vezes são tão resistentes a mudanças.

more.definition: On some occasions, over some periods, or in certain circumstances, but not always.
more.etymology: From Middle English sumtymes, somtymes, som tymes, equivalent to sometime + -s (adverbial suffix). Compare West Frisian somstiden (“sometimes”), Dutch somtijds, somwijlen (“sometimes”).

examples.text: He was dragged along by the current.

translations.de: Er wurde von der Strömung mitgerissen.
translations.fr: Il a été entraîné par le courant.
translations.pt: Ele foi arrastado pela correnteza.

examples.text: I get along with my younger brother.

translations.de: Ich verstehe mich mit meinem jüngeren Bruder.
translations.fr: Je m'entends bien avec mon petit frère.
translations.pt: Eu me dou bem com o meu irmão caçula.

examples.text: Would you mind if I came along?

translations.de: Hättest du etwas dagegen, wenn ich dich begleitete?
translations.fr: Cela te dérangerait-il que je t'accompagne ?
translations.pt: Você se importa se eu for junto?

examples.text: They must have known it all along.

translations.de: Sie müssen es die ganze Zeit über gewusst haben.
translations.fr: Ils doivent l'avoir su tout le temps.
translations.pt: Eles deviam saber disso o tempo todo.

more.definition: In company; together.; Onward, forward, with progressive action.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₂éntsder. From Middle English, from Old English andlang, from prefix and- + lang (“long”). Doublet of endlong.

examples.text: I didn't get along with her.

translations.de: Ich habe mich mit ihr nicht gut verstanden.
translations.fr: Je ne m'entendais pas avec elle.
translations.pt: Eu não me dava bem com ela.

examples.text: Do you get along with your boss?

translations.de: Verstehst du dich gut mit deinem Chef?
translations.fr: T'entends-tu bien avec ton patron ?
translations.pt: Você se relaciona bem com seu chefe?

examples.text: That's what I said all along.

translations.de: Das habe ich die ganze Zeit gesagt.
translations.fr: C'est ce que je disais depuis le début.
translations.pt: É isso que eu disse o tempo todo.

examples.text: Come along with me and go fishing.

translations.de: Kommen Sie mit mir angeln.
translations.fr: Viens pêcher avec moi.
translations.pt: Venha pescar comigo.

more.definition: By the length of; in a line with the length of; lengthwise next to.; In a line with, with a progressive motion on; onward on; forward on.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₂éntsder. From Middle English, from Old English andlang, from prefix and- + lang (“long”). Doublet of endlong.

examples.text: All's fair in love and war.

translations.de: In der Liebe und im Krieg ist alles erlaubt.
translations.fr: En amour comme à la guerre, tous les coups sont permis.
translations.pt: No amor e na guerra vale tudo.

examples.text: They supplied the war victims with food.

translations.de: Sie versorgten die Kriegsopfer mit Nahrung.
translations.fr: Ils dispensèrent de la nourriture aux victimes de guerre.
translations.pt: Eles forneceram comida para as vítimas da guerra.

examples.text: She lost her son in the war.

translations.de: Sie hat ihren Sohn im Krieg verloren.
translations.fr: Elle a perdu son fils à la guerre.
translations.pt: Ela perdeu o filho na guerra.

examples.text: My grandfather was wounded in the war.

translations.de: Mein Großvater wurde im Krieg verletzt.
translations.fr: Mon grand-père a été blessé à la guerre.
translations.pt: O meu avô foi ferido na guerra.

more.definition: Organized, large-scale, armed conflict between countries or between national, ethnic, or other sizeable groups, usually but not always involving active engagement of military forces.; A particular conflict of this kind.; A sustained campaign against a social problem, idea, set of values, etc.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *wers-der. Frankish *werʀubor. Old Northern French guerreder. Inherited from Middle English werre, from Late Old English werre /wyrre (“armed conflict”), from Anglo-Norman and Old Northern French guerre /werre (compare modern French guerre), from Medieval Latin werra, from Frankish *werʀu (“confusion; quarrel”), from Proto-Indo-European *wers- (“to mix up, confuse, beat, thresh”).

examples.text: The city was destroyed during the war.

translations.de: Die Stadt wurde während des Krieges zerstört.
translations.fr: La ville a été détruite pendant la guerre.
translations.pt: A cidade foi destruída durante a guerra.

examples.text: We've been through three wars.

translations.de: Wir haben drei Kriege durchgemacht.
translations.fr: Nous avons traversé trois guerres.
translations.pt: Nós passamos por três guerras.

examples.text: If you want peace, prepare for war.

translations.de: Willst du Frieden, bereite dich zum Krieg.
translations.fr: Si tu veux la paix, prépare la guerre.
translations.pt: Se desejas paz, prepara a guerra.

examples.text: Our son was killed in the war.

translations.de: Unser Sohn ist im Krieg umgekommen.
translations.fr: Notre fils a été tué à la guerre.
translations.pt: Nosso filho foi morto na guerra.

more.definition: To engage in conflict (may be followed by "with" to specify the foe).; To carry on, as a contest; to wage.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *wers-der. Frankish *werʀubor. Old Northern French guerreder. examples.text: I don't feel safe here.

translations.fr: Je ne me sens pas en sécurité, ici.
translations.pt: Eu não me sinto seguro aqui.

examples.text: We're safe in here, aren't we?

translations.de: Hier drinnen sind wir sicher, oder nicht?
translations.fr: Nous sommes en sécurité ici, n'est-ce pas ?
translations.pt: Estamos seguros aqui, não estamos?

examples.text: You won't be safe anywhere.

translations.de: Ihr werdet nirgendwo sicher sein.
translations.fr: Vous ne serez en sécurité nulle part.
translations.pt: Você não estará seguro em lugar nenhum.

more.definition: To make something safe.
more.etymology: From Middle English sauf, safe, saf, saaf, from Old French sauf, saulf, salf (“safe”), from Latin salvus (“whole, safe”), from Proto-Italic *salawos, from Proto-Indo-European *solh₂- (“whole, every”). Displaced Old English sicor (“secure, sure”).

examples.text: We'll eat at six o'clock.

translations.de: Wir werden um sechs Uhr essen.
translations.fr: Nous mangerons à 6 heures.
translations.pt: Nós comeremos às dezoito horas.

examples.text: He lived in Ankara for six years.

translations.de: Er lebte sechs Jahre in Ankara.
translations.fr: Il a vécu à Ankara pendant six ans.
translations.pt: Ele viveu em Ancara durante seis anos.

examples.text: We have a reservation for six-thirty.

translations.de: Wir haben eine Reservierung für halb sieben.
translations.fr: Nous avons réservé pour dix-huit heures trente.
translations.pt: Temos uma reserva para seis e meia.

examples.text: She has a dog and six cats.

translations.de: Sie hat einen Hund und sechs Katzen.
translations.fr: Elle a un chien et six chats.
translations.pt: Ela tem um cachorro e seis gatos.

more.definition: A group or set with six elements.; The digit or figure 6.; A playing card featuring six pips.
more.etymology: PIE word *swéḱs From Middle English six, from Old English six, from Proto-West Germanic *sehs, from Proto-Germanic *sehs, from Proto-Indo-European *swéḱs. Compare West Frisian seis, Dutch zes, Low German söss, sess, German sechs, Norwegian and Danish seks, also Latin sex, Ancient Greek ἕξ (héx), Sanskrit षष् (ṣaṣ). Doublet of sice. Toilet sense predates military usage.

examples.text: He has a dog and six cats.

translations.de: Er hat einen Hund und sechs Katzen.
translations.fr: Il a un chien et six chats.
translations.pt: Ele tem um cachorro e seis gatos.

examples.text: I wake him at six every morning.

translations.de: Ich wecke ihn jeden Morgen um sechs.
translations.fr: Je le réveille à 6 heures chaque matin.
translations.pt: Eu o acordo todos os dias às seis.

examples.text: They wake up at six every morning.

translations.de: Sie wachen jeden Morgen um sechs Uhr auf.
translations.fr: Ils se lèvent à six heures tous les matins.
translations.pt: Eles se levantam às seis todas as manhãs.

examples.text: God created the world in six days.

translations.de: Gott erschuf die Welt in sechs Tagen.
translations.fr: Dieu créa le monde en six jours.
translations.pt: Deus criou o mundo em seis dias.

more.definition: A numerical value equal to 6; the number following five and preceding seven. This number of dots: (••••••).
more.etymology: PIE word *swéḱs From Middle English six, from Old English six, from Proto-West Germanic *sehs, from Proto-Germanic *sehs, from Proto-Indo-European *swéḱs. Compare West Frisian seis, Dutch zes, Low German söss, sess, German sechs, Norwegian and Danish seks, also Latin sex, Ancient Greek ἕξ (héx), Sanskrit षष् (ṣaṣ). Doublet of sice. Toilet sense predates military usage.

examples.text: We had a brief discussion about human rights.

translations.de: Wir hatten eine kleine Meinungsverschiedenheit bezüglich der Menschenrechte.
translations.fr: Nous avons eu une brève discussion sur les droits de l'homme.
translations.pt: Nós tivemos uma breve discussão sobre direitos humanos.

examples.text: The two poems express human suffering.

translations.de: Die beiden Gedichte drücken das menschliche Leid aus.
translations.fr: Les deux poèmes expriment la souffrance humaine.
translations.pt: Os dois poemas exprimem o sofrimento humano.

examples.text: The human heart is analogous to a pump.

translations.de: Das menschliche Herz gleicht einer Pumpe.
translations.fr: Le cœur humain est analogue à une pompe.
translations.pt: O coração humano é análogo a uma bomba.

examples.text: Creativity is an important aspect of human development.

translations.de: Die Kreativität ist ein wichtiger Aspekt für die Entwicklung des Menschen.
translations.fr: La créativité est une chose importante pour le développement de l’être humain.
translations.pt: A criatividade é um importante aspecto do desenvolvimento humano.

more.definition: Of or belonging to the species Homo sapiens or its closest relatives.; Having the nature or attributes of a human being.; Compassionate.
more.etymology: Latin hūmānuslbor. Middle French humainbor. From Late Middle English humaigne, humayne, humain, from Middle French humain, from Old French humain, umain (“of or belonging to man”, adjective), from Latin hūmānus m (“of man, human”, adjective); see there for further details. Spelling human has been predominant since the early 18th century. Compare man, to which it is possibly related.

examples.text: All human beings are born equal.

translations.de: Alle Menschen sind von Geburt an gleichberechtigt.
translations.fr: Tous les hommes naissent égaux.
translations.pt: Todos os homens nascem iguais.

examples.text: We are humans and we are from Earth.

translations.de: Wir sind Menschen und kommen von der Erde.
translations.fr: Nous sommes des êtres humains, et nous venons de la Terre.
translations.pt: Nós somos humanos e somos da Terra.

examples.text: The false alarm was caused by human error.

translations.de: Der Fehlalarm wurde durch ein menschliches Versehen ausgelöst.
translations.fr: La fausse alerte a été causée par une erreur humaine.
translations.pt: O alarme falso foi causado por um erro humano.

examples.text: The dog is the human's best friend.

translations.de: Der Hund ist der beste Freund des Menschen.
translations.fr: Le chien est le meilleur ami de l'homme.
translations.pt: O cão é o melhor amigo do homem.

more.definition: A highly intelligent ape with fine and short body hair; the most abundant species of primate, with members found on every continent (Homo sapiens).; A human as contrasted from superficially similar but typically more powerful humanoid creatures; a member of the human race.; A term of address for any human, often implying the listener's species is their only noteworthy trait.
more.etymology: Latin hūmānuslbor. Middle French humainbor. From Late Middle English humaigne, humayne, humain, from Middle French humain, from Old French humain, umain (“of or belonging to man”, adjective), from Latin hūmānus m (“of man, human”, adjective); see there for further details. Spelling human has been predominant since the early 18th century. Compare man, to which it is possibly related.

examples.text: A parrot can imitate the human voice.

translations.de: Ein Papagei kann die menschliche Stimme imitieren.
translations.fr: Un perroquet peut imiter la voix humaine.
translations.pt: O papagaio pode imitar a voz humana.

examples.text: Monkeys are closely related to humans.

translations.de: Affen sind nahe Verwandte des Menschen.
translations.fr: Les singes sont des parents proches des humains.
translations.pt: Os macacos são parentes próximos dos humanos.

examples.text: To err is human, to forgive divine.

translations.de: Irren ist menschlich, vergeben göttlich.
translations.fr: Se tromper est humain, pardonner, divin.
translations.pt: Errar é humano; perdoar é divino.

examples.text: Will artificial intelligence supplant human intelligence?

translations.de: Wird künstliche Intelligenz die menschliche Intelligenz verdrängen?
translations.fr: L'intelligence artificielle supplantera-t-elle l'intelligence humaine ?
translations.pt: A inteligência artificial irá suplantar a inteligência humana?

more.etymology: Latin hūmānuslbor. Middle French humainbor. From Late Middle English humaigne, humayne, humain, from Middle French humain, from Old French humain, umain (“of or belonging to man”, adjective), from Latin hūmānus m (“of man, human”, adjective); see there for further details. Spelling human has been predominant since the early 18th century. Compare man, to which it is possibly related.

examples.text: Don't be late for the train.

translations.de: Verpassen Sie Ihren Zug nicht.
translations.fr: Ne sois pas en retard pour le train.
translations.pt: Não se atrase para o trem.

examples.text: There aren't as many trains at night.

translations.de: Nachts fahren nicht so viele Züge.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas autant de trains la nuit.
translations.pt: Não tem muitos trens de noite.

examples.text: She left her umbrella in the train.

translations.de: Sie hat ihren Schirm im Zug gelassen.
translations.fr: Elle a laissé son parapluie dans le train.
translations.pt: Ela deixou o seu guarda-chuva no trem.

examples.text: I left my umbrella on the train.

translations.de: Ich habe meinen Regenschirm im Zug vergessen.
translations.fr: J'ai laissé mon parapluie dans le train.
translations.pt: Eu deixei o meu guarda-chuva no trem.

examples.text: The train leaves at eight.

translations.de: Der Zug fährt um acht Uhr ab.
translations.fr: Le train part à huit heures.
translations.pt: O trem parte às oito.

examples.text: The trains are often late in winter.

translations.de: Im Winter haben die Züge oft Verspätung.
translations.fr: Les trains sont souvent en retard en hiver.
translations.pt: Os trens costumam atrasar no inverno.

more.definition: The elongated back portion of a dress or skirt (or an ornamental piece of material added to similar effect), which drags along the ground.; A trail or line of something, especially gunpowder.; The tail of a bird.
collocations: catch a train — to get on it in time
more.etymology: Old French traïnerder. Old French trainder. From Middle English trayne (“train”), from Old French train (“a delay, a drawing out”), from traïner (“to pull out, to draw”), from Vulgar Latin *traginō, from *tragō, from Latin trahō (“to pull, to draw”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *tregʰ- (“to pull, draw, drag”). The verb was derived from the noun in Middle English.

examples.text: France is training eagles to intercept drones.

translations.de: In Frankreich werden Adler abgerichtet, Dronen abzufangen.
translations.fr: La France entraîne des aigles à intercepter des drones.
translations.pt: A França está a treinar águias para intercetar drones.

examples.text: I will go to Australia by train.

translations.de: Ich werde mit dem Zug nach Australien reisen.
translations.fr: J'irai en Australie par le train.
translations.pt: Vou à Austrália de trem.

examples.text: The next three trains go to the North.

translations.de: Die nächsten drei Züge fahren nach Norden.
translations.fr: Les trois prochains trains partent vers le Nord.
translations.pt: Os próximos três trens vão para o Norte.

examples.text: Is there a train station near here?

translations.de: Gibt es hier in der Nähe einen Bahnhof?
translations.fr: Y a-t-il une gare près d'ici ?
translations.pt: Há alguma estação de trem perto daqui?

more.definition: To practice an ability.; To teach and form (someone) by practice; to educate (someone).; To feed data into an algorithm, usually based on a neural network, to create a machine learning model that can perform some task.
more.etymology: Old French traïnerder. Old French trainder. From Middle English trayne (“train”), from Old French train (“a delay, a drawing out”), from traïner (“to pull out, to draw”), from Vulgar Latin *traginō, from *tragō, from Latin trahō (“to pull, to draw”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *tregʰ- (“to pull, draw, drag”). The verb was derived from the noun in Middle English.

examples.text: People say that he's still alive.

translations.de: Er soll noch am Leben sein.
translations.fr: Les gens disent qu'il est encore en vie.
translations.pt: Dizem que ele ainda está vivo.

examples.text: Almost all of the dogs are alive.

translations.de: Fast alle Hunde sind am Leben.
translations.fr: Presque tous les chiens sont en vie.
translations.pt: Quase todos cachorros estão vivos.

examples.text: We won't get off this island alive.

translations.de: Wir werden nicht lebend von dieser Insel kommen.
translations.fr: Nous ne sortirons pas vivants de cette île.
translations.pt: Não sairemos vivos desta ilha.

examples.text: I can't believe I'm still alive.

translations.de: Ich kann nicht glauben, dass ich noch immer lebe.
translations.fr: Je n'arrive pas à croire que je sois encore en vie.
translations.pt: Eu não acredito que ainda estou vivo.

more.definition: Having life; living; not dead.; In a state of action; in force or operation; existent.; Busy with activity of many living beings; swarming; thronged; busy.
more.etymology: From Middle English alyve, alive, alife, olive, olife, on live, on life, from Old English on līfe (“alive”, literally “in life" or "in (the) body”), from on (“on, in”) + līfe, dative singular of līf (“life”). In this sense, replaced Old English cwic (whence English quick). Equivalent to a- + life. Compare Dutch in leven (“alive”, literally “in life”), German am Leben (“alive”, literally “at life" or "at living”).

examples.text: Where does this street lead to?

translations.de: Wohin führt diese Straße?
translations.fr: Où conduit cette rue ?
translations.pt: Onde sai essa rua?

examples.text: This is as heavy as lead.

translations.de: Das ist so schwer wie Blei.
translations.fr: C'est aussi lourd que du plomb.
translations.pt: Isto pesa como chumbo.

examples.text: Which is heavier, lead or gold?

translations.de: Was ist schwerer, Blei oder Gold?
translations.fr: Qu'est-ce qui est le plus lourd, le plomb ou l'or ?
translations.pt: O que é mais pesado, chumbo ou ouro?

examples.text: Where does that road lead?

translations.de: Wohin führt die Straße?
translations.fr: Où mène cette rue ?
translations.pt: Aonde vai ter essa estrada?

more.definition: Foremost.; Main, principal, primary, first, chief, foremost.
more.etymology: From Middle English leden, from Old English lǣdan (“to lead”), from Proto-West Germanic *laidijan, from Proto-Germanic *laidijaną (“to cause one to go, lead”), causative of Proto-Germanic *līþaną (“to go”), from Proto-Indo-European *leyt- (“to leave, die”).

examples.text: Not all roads lead to Rome.

translations.de: Nicht alle Wege führen nach Rom.
translations.fr: Tous les chemins ne mènent pas à Rome.
translations.pt: Nem todos os caminhos levam a Roma.

examples.text: After all, the wrong road always leads somewhere.

translations.de: Immerhin führt der falsche Weg immer irgendwo hin.
translations.fr: Après tout, le mauvais chemin mène toujours quelque part.
translations.pt: Afinal, o caminho errado sempre leva a algum lugar.

examples.text: In his hand, lead became gold.

translations.de: In seiner Hand wurde Blei zu Gold.
translations.fr: Dans sa main le plomb se transforma en or.
translations.pt: Na mão dele, chumbo se transformava em ouro.

examples.text: Nicolas Flamel dreamed of turning lead into gold.

translations.de: Nicolas Flamel träumte davon, Blei in Gold zu verwandeln.
translations.fr: Nicolas Flamel rêvait de transformer le plomb en or.
translations.pt: Nicolas Flamel sonhou em transformar o chumbo em ouro.

more.definition: A heavy, pliable, inelastic metal element, having a bright, bluish color, but easily tarnished; both malleable and ductile, though with little tenacity. It is easily fusible, forms alloys with other metals, and is an ingredient of solder and type metal. Atomic number 82.; A plummet or mass of lead attached to a line, used in sounding depth at sea or to estimate velocity in knots.; A thin strip of type metal, used to separate lines of type in printing.
more.etymology: From Middle English led, leed, from Old English lēad (“lead”), from Proto-West Germanic *laud (“lead”), possibly borrowed from Proto-Celtic *ɸloudom, from Proto-Indo-European *plewd- (“to flow”).

examples.text: California condors are endangered by lead poisoning.

translations.de: Kalifornische Kondore sind durch Bleivergiftung gefährdet.
translations.fr: Les condors de Californie sont menacés par le saturnisme.
translations.pt: Os condores da Califórnia estão ameaçados de envenenamento pelo chumbo.

examples.text: And so one thing leads to another.

translations.de: Und so führt eins zum anderen.
translations.fr: Et c'est ainsi qu'une chose mène à l'autre.
translations.pt: E uma coisa leva à outra.

examples.text: What led up to the war in Ukraine?

translations.de: Was hat zum Krieg in der Ukraine geführt?
translations.fr: Qu'est-ce qui a mené à la guerre en Ukraine ?
translations.pt: O que levou à guerra na Ucrânia?

examples.text: China is the world's leading producer of rice.

translations.de: China ist der weltgrößte Reisproduzent.
translations.fr: La Chine est le premier producteur mondial de riz.
translations.pt: A China é o maior produtor mundial de arroz.

more.definition: To cover, fill, or affect with lead.; To place leads between the lines of.; To guide or conduct with the hand, or by means of some physical contact connection.
more.etymology: From Middle English led, leed, from Old English lēad (“lead”), from Proto-West Germanic *laud (“lead”), possibly borrowed from Proto-Celtic *ɸloudom, from Proto-Indo-European *plewd- (“to flow”).

examples.text: He doesn't live with his parents.

translations.de: Er wohnt nicht bei seinen Eltern.
translations.fr: Il n'habite pas avec ses parents.
translations.pt: Ele não mora com os pais.

examples.text: Both of my parents can speak French.

translations.de: Meine Eltern können beide Französisch.
translations.fr: Mes deux parents parlent français.
translations.pt: Meu pai e minha mãe sabem falar francês.

examples.text: My parents want me to study medicine.

translations.de: Meine Eltern wollen, dass ich Medizin studiere.
translations.fr: Mes parents veulent que je fasse des études de médecine.
translations.pt: Meus pais querem que eu estude medicina.

examples.text: You should ask your parents for permission.

translations.de: Ihr solltet eure Eltern um Erlaubnis bitten.
translations.fr: Tu devrais demander la permission à tes parents.
translations.pt: Você deveria pedir permissão aos seus pais.

more.definition: A person who raises a child (which they have made, adopted, fostered, taken as their own, etc.).; A person who has had a baby; this person in relation to their child or children.; A surrogate parent.
more.etymology: From Middle English parent, borrowed from Anglo-Norman parent, Middle French parent, from Latin parentem, accusative of parēns (“parent”), present participle of pariō (“to breed, bring forth”).

examples.text: Do you know the bride's parents?

translations.de: Kennen Sie die Eltern der Braut?
translations.fr: Connaissez-vous les parents de la mariée ?
translations.pt: Vocês conhecem os pais da noiva?

examples.text: My parents don't like my girlfriend.

translations.de: Meine Eltern mögen meine Freundin nicht.
translations.fr: Mes parents n'aiment pas ma petite amie.
translations.pt: Meus pais não gostam de minha namorada.

examples.text: My parents will be proud of me.

translations.de: Meine Eltern werden stolz auf mich sein.
translations.fr: Mes parents seront fiers de moi.
translations.pt: Meus pais vão ficar orgulhosos de mim.

examples.text: My parents were opposed to our marriage.

translations.de: Meine Eltern waren gegen unsere Heirat.
translations.fr: Mes parents étaient opposés à notre mariage.
translations.pt: Meus pais eram contra o nosso casamento.

more.definition: To act as parent, to raise or rear.; To provide a parent object for one or more other objects, which become the children.
more.etymology: From Middle English parent, borrowed from Anglo-Norman parent, Middle French parent, from Latin parentem, accusative of parēns (“parent”), present participle of pariō (“to breed, bring forth”).

examples.text: I have to clean the bathroom.

translations.de: Ich muss die Toilette säubern.
translations.fr: Je dois nettoyer la salle de bain.
translations.pt: Eu tenho que limpar o banheiro.

examples.text: Tom's room wasn't clean.

translations.de: Toms Zimmer war nicht aufgeräumt.
translations.fr: La chambre de Tom n'était pas propre.
translations.pt: O quarto de Tom não estava limpo.

examples.text: I don't like to clean.

translations.de: Ich reinige nicht gerne.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas nettoyer.
translations.pt: Eu não gosto de limpar.

examples.text: You should keep this machine clean and lubed.

translations.de: Sie sollten diese Maschine sauber und geölt halten.
translations.fr: Il faut tenir cette machine propre et lubrifiée.
translations.pt: Você deveria manter esta máquina limpa e lubrificada.

more.definition: Free of dirt, filth, or impurities (extraneous matter); not dirty, filthy, or soiled.; Of metal, having relatively few impurities.; Not muscular due to steroid use.
more.etymology: From Middle English clene, from Old English clāne, clǣne (“clean; pure; clear”), from Proto-West Germanic *klainī (“dainty, fine, small; clean”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *glēy- (“gleaming”), from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to gleam”).

examples.text: We need to invest in clean, renewable energy.

translations.de: Wir müssen in eine saubere und erneuerbare Energieform investieren.
translations.fr: Nous devons investir dans une énergie propre et renouvelable.
translations.pt: Precisamos de investir em energia limpa e renovável.

examples.text: She made him clean his room.

translations.de: Sie ließ ihn sein Zimmer aufräumen.
translations.fr: Elle lui fit nettoyer sa chambre.
translations.pt: Ela o fez limpar seu quarto.

examples.text: Could you please bring me a clean knife?

translations.de: Könnten Sie mir bitte ein sauberes Messer bringen?
translations.fr: Pourriez-vous, s'il vous plait, m'apporter un couteau propre ?
translations.pt: Você pode me trazer uma faca limpa, por favor?

examples.text: You have to clean your room.

translations.de: Du musst dein Zimmer sauber machen.
translations.fr: Tu dois ranger ta chambre.
translations.pt: Você tem que limpar teu quarto.

more.definition: Fully and completely.
more.etymology: From Middle English clene, from Old English clāne, clǣne (“clean; pure; clear”), from Proto-West Germanic *klainī (“dainty, fine, small; clean”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *glēy- (“gleaming”), from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to gleam”).

examples.text: I have to clean up my apartment.

translations.de: Ich muss meine Wohnung aufräumen.
translations.fr: Je dois ranger mon appartement.
translations.pt: Tenho que limpar o meu apartamento.

examples.text: I helped my mother clean the kitchen.

translations.de: Ich half meiner Mutter, die Küche zu putzen.
translations.fr: J'ai aidé ma mère à nettoyer la cuisine.
translations.pt: Ajudei minha mãe a limpar a cozinha.

examples.text: The locker room of the girls is clean.

translations.de: Die Umkleidekabine der Mädchen ist sauber.
translations.fr: Le vestiaire des filles est propre.
translations.pt: O vestiário das meninas está limpo.

examples.text: Tom's room was very clean.

translations.de: Toms Zimmer war sehr aufgeräumt.
translations.fr: La chambre de Tom était très propre.
translations.pt: O quarto de Tom estava limpíssimo.

more.definition: A removal of dirt.; The first part of the event clean and jerk in which the weight is brought from the ground to the shoulders.; Of heavy metal, clear vocals, contrasted with death growls and screams.
more.etymology: From Middle English clene, from Old English clāne, clǣne (“clean; pure; clear”), from Proto-West Germanic *klainī (“dainty, fine, small; clean”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *glēy- (“gleaming”), from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to gleam”).

examples.text: She cleaned the house all by herself.

translations.de: Sie hat das Haus alleine geputzt.
translations.fr: Elle a nettoyé la maison toute seule.
translations.pt: Ela fez a limpeza da casa sozinha.

examples.text: Have you finished cleaning your room yet?

translations.de: Bist du schon fertig mit Zimmeraufräumen?
translations.fr: Tu as terminé de nettoyer ta chambre ?
translations.pt: Você já terminou de limpar seu quarto?

examples.text: The shirt is clean and dry.

translations.de: Das Shirt ist sauber und trocken.
translations.fr: La chemise est propre et sèche.
translations.pt: A camisa está limpa e seca.

examples.text: Have you already cleaned your room?

translations.de: Hast du schon dein Zimmer aufgeräumt?
translations.fr: As-tu déjà nettoyé ta chambre ?
translations.pt: Você já limpou seu quarto?

more.definition: To remove dirt from a place or object.; To tidy up, make a place neat.; To make things clean in general.
more.etymology: From Middle English clene, from Old English clāne, clǣne (“clean; pure; clear”), from Proto-West Germanic *klainī (“dainty, fine, small; clean”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *glēy- (“gleaming”), from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to gleam”).

examples.text: I've got a big hoo-ha.

translations.fr: J’ai une grosse zézette.

examples.text: Ha ha ha, very funny.

translations.de: Hahaha! Sehr lustig!

examples.text: Mwa, ha, ha, ha, ha! Your soul will be mine!

translations.pt: Mua, ha, ha, ha! Tua alma será minha!

examples.text: Ha! You should've thought of that earlier!
