translations.fr: La banque a prêté un million de dollars à l'entreprise.
translations.pt: O banco emprestou à empresa um milhão de dólares.

more.definition: A team; a group of people who work together for a common purpose.; A group of performing artists who put on shows together.; The crew of a ship.
more.etymology: From Middle English companye (“a team; companionship”), from Old French compaignie (“companionship”) (Modern French: compagnie), possibly from Late Latin *compania, but this word is not attested. Old French compaignie is equivalent to Old French compaignon (Modern French: compagnon) + -ie. More at companion. Displaced native Old English werod, gefer, getæl, and hired.

examples.text: Tom's company imports coffee from Brazil.

translations.de: Toms Firma führt Kaffee aus Brasilien ein.
translations.fr: La compagnie de Tom importe du café du Brésil.
translations.pt: A companhia de Tom importa café do Brasil.

examples.text: What are your thoughts on the company?

translations.de: Was haltet ihr von der Firma?
translations.fr: Quelles sont vos réflexions sur l'entreprise ?
translations.pt: O que você pensa sobre a companhia?

examples.text: What is the company's competitive advantage?

translations.de: Was ist der Wettbewerbsvorteil des Unternehmens?
translations.fr: Quel est l'avantage concurrentiel de l'entreprise ?
translations.pt: Qual é a vantagem competitiva da empresa?

examples.text: The company claims that the delay was unintentional.

translations.de: Das Unternehmen behauptet, dass die Verzögerung unbeabsichtigt war.
translations.fr: La société affirme que le retard n'était pas intentionnel.
translations.pt: A empresa afirma que o atraso foi involuntário.

more.etymology: From Middle English companye (“a team; companionship”), from Old French compaignie (“companionship”) (Modern French: compagnie), possibly from Late Latin *compania, but this word is not attested. Old French compaignie is equivalent to Old French compaignon (Modern French: compagnon) + -ie. More at companion. Displaced native Old English werod, gefer, getæl, and hired.

examples.text: Don't step on the broken glass.

translations.de: Nicht auf die Glasscherben treten!
translations.fr: Ne marchez pas sur les éclats de verre.
translations.pt: Não pise no vidro quebrado.

examples.text: The boy counted his steps as he walked.

translations.de: Der Junge zählte seine Schritte, während er ging.
translations.fr: Le garçon comptait ses pas en marchant.
translations.pt: O menino contava os passos enquanto andava.

examples.text: I can't walk another step.

translations.de: Ich kann keinen einzigen Schritt mehr gehen.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas faire un pas de plus.
translations.pt: Não posso dar nem mais um passo.

examples.text: The first step is the hardest.

translations.de: Der erste Schritt ist der schwerste.
translations.fr: Le premier pas est le plus difficile.
translations.pt: O primeiro passo é o mais difícil.

more.definition: An advance or movement made from one foot to the other; a pace.; A rest, or one of a set of rests, for the foot in ascending or descending, as a stair, or a rung of a ladder.; The part of a spade, digging stick or similar tool that a digger's foot rests against and presses on when digging; an ear, a foot-rest.
more.etymology: Proto-Germanic *stappōnąbf. From Middle English steppen, from Old English steppan (“to step, go, proceed, advance”), stepe (“step”), from Proto-West Germanic *stappjan, from Proto-Germanic *stapjaną (“to step”), *stapiz (“step”), from Proto-Indo-European *stebʰ- (“to support, stomp, curse, be amazed”).

examples.text: Don't step on the dog's tail.

translations.de: Tritt dem Hund nicht auf den Schwanz.
translations.fr: Ne marchez pas sur la queue du chien.
translations.pt: Não pise no rabo do cachorro.

examples.text: You almost stepped on the dog's tail.

translations.de: Du hättest fast auf den Schwanz des Hundes getreten.
translations.fr: Tu as presque marché sur la queue du chien.
translations.pt: Você quase pisou no rabo do cachorro.

examples.text: I always used to count the steps while going up.

translations.de: Ich habe immer beim Aufstieg die Schritte gezählt.
translations.fr: Je comptais toujours les marches en montant.
translations.pt: Eu sempre contava os degraus enquanto subia.

examples.text: I almost stepped on a skunk last night.

translations.de: Ich wäre gestern Abend fast auf ein Stinktier getreten.
translations.fr: J'ai failli marcher sur une moufette hier soir.
translations.pt: Quase tropecei num gambá noite passada.

more.definition: To move the foot in walking; to advance or recede by raising and moving one of the feet to another resting place, or by moving both feet in succession.; To don with a stepping action.; To walk; to go (on foot, especially) a little distance.
more.etymology: Proto-Germanic *stappōnąbf. From Middle English steppen, from Old English steppan (“to step, go, proceed, advance”), stepe (“step”), from Proto-West Germanic *stappjan, from Proto-Germanic *stapjaną (“to step”), *stapiz (“step”), from Proto-Indo-European *stebʰ- (“to support, stomp, curse, be amazed”).

examples.text: I would like to report a theft.

translations.de: Ich möchte einen Diebstahl melden.
translations.fr: Je voudrais déclarer un vol.
translations.pt: Gostaria de denunciar um roubo.

examples.text: I'd like to report a theft.

translations.de: Ich möchte einen Diebstahl melden.
translations.fr: Je voudrais déclarer un vol.
translations.pt: Gostaria de denunciar um roubo.

examples.text: I spent all night working on this report.

translations.de: Ich habe die ganze Nacht an diesem Bericht gearbeitet.
translations.fr: J'ai passé toute la nuit à travailler sur ce rapport.
translations.pt: Eu passei a noite inteira trabalhando nesse relatório.

examples.text: I read the report you wrote.

translations.de: Ich habe den Bericht gelesen, den du geschrieben hast.
translations.fr: J'ai lu le rapport que tu as écrit.
translations.pt: Eu li o relatório que você escreveu.

more.definition: A piece of information describing, or an account of certain events given or presented to someone, with the most common adpositions being by (referring to creator of the report) and on (referring to the subject).; Reputation.; The sharp, loud sound of a gunshot or explosion.
more.etymology: From Middle English reporten, from Anglo-Norman reporter, from Latin reportāre (“to carry back, return, remit, refer”), from re- + portāre.

examples.text: We need that report by tomorrow.

translations.de: Wir brauchen diesen Bericht bis morgen.
translations.fr: Nous avons besoin de ce rapport pour demain.
translations.pt: Precisamos desse relatório para amanhã.

examples.text: She will report directly to me.

translations.de: Sie wird mir direkt Bericht erstatten.
translations.fr: Elle me sera directement rattachée.
translations.pt: Ela vai reportar diretamente para mim.

examples.text: Make a copy of this report.

translations.de: Mach eine Kopie von diesem Bericht.
translations.fr: Fais une copie de ce rapport.
translations.pt: Faça uma cópia deste relatório.

examples.text: The report revealed that many teenagers are alcoholics.

translations.de: Der Bericht zeigte auf, dass viele Jugendliche alkoholabhängig sind.
translations.fr: Du rapport, il apparaît que de nombreux adolescents sont dépendants de l'alcool.
translations.pt: O repórter revelou que muitos adolescentes são alcoólatras.

more.definition: To relate details of (an event or incident); to recount, describe (something).; To repeat (something one has heard), to retell; to pass on, convey (a message, information etc.).; To notify someone of (particular intelligence, suspicions, illegality, misconduct etc.); to make notification to relevant authorities; to submit a formal report of.
more.etymology: From Middle English reporten, from Anglo-Norman reporter, from Latin reportāre (“to carry back, return, remit, refer”), from re- + portāre.

examples.text: Is everything alright?

translations.de: Ist alles in Ordnung?
translations.fr: Est-ce que tout va bien ?
translations.pt: Está tudo em ordem?

examples.text: Everything is alright.

translations.de: Es ist alles in Ordnung.
translations.fr: Tout est en ordre.
translations.pt: Está tudo certo.

examples.text: Don't worry. Everything will be alright!

translations.de: Mach dir keine Sorgen. Alles wird gut!
translations.fr: Ne t'inquiète pas ! Tout ira bien !

examples.text: I've heard a scream. Is everything alright?

translations.de: Ich habe einen Schrei gehört. Ist alles in Ordnung?
translations.fr: J'ai entendu un cri. Tout est en règle ?

more.definition: Used to indicate acknowledgement or acceptance; OK.; An expression of happiness.; A generic greeting; hello; how are you.
more.etymology: Univerbation of all + right. Compare Old English eallriht (“all-right, just, exactly”) (from eall + riht), equivalent to al- (“all”) + right.

examples.text: There are nine million bicycles in Beijing.

translations.de: In Peking gibt es neun Millionen Fahrräder.
translations.fr: Il y a neuf millions de vélos à Pékin.
translations.pt: Há nove milhões de bicicletas em Pequim.

examples.text: You don't need millions to be happy.

translations.de: Man braucht keine Millionen, um glücklich zu sein.
translations.fr: On n'a pas besoin de millions pour être heureux.
translations.pt: Você não precisa de milhões para ser feliz.

examples.text: The loss amounts to a million dollars.

translations.de: Der Verlust beläuft sich auf eine Millionen Dollar.
translations.fr: La perte s'élève à un million de dollars.
translations.pt: O déficit atinge um milhão de dólares.

examples.text: I've seen it a million times.

translations.de: Das habe ich schon Millionen Mal gesehen.
translations.fr: Je l'ai vu un million de fois.
translations.pt: Eu já vi isso um milhão de vezes.

more.definition: The cardinal number 1 000 000: 10⁶; a thousand thousand (1,000²).; An unspecified very large number.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-ōder. Italian milionebor. Middle French millionbor. Inherited from Middle English milioun, from Middle French milion, from Old French millon, from Italian milione (“million”, from mille (“thousand”, from Latin mille) + -one). Compare -illion.

examples.text: Where is the captain of this ship?

translations.de: Wo ist der Kapitän dieses Schiffes?
translations.fr: Où est le capitaine de ce bateau ?
translations.pt: Onde está o capitão deste navio?

examples.text: Who's the captain of this ship?

translations.de: Wer ist der Kapitän dieses Schiffes?
translations.fr: Qui est le commandant de ce navire ?
translations.pt: Quem é o capitão deste navio?

examples.text: I'm the captain of this ship.

translations.de: Ich bin der Kapitän dieses Schiffes.
translations.fr: Je suis le capitaine de ce bateau.
translations.pt: Eu sou o capitão deste navio.

examples.text: The captain invited them for breakfast.

translations.de: Der Kapitän lud sie zum Frühstück ein.
translations.fr: Le capitaine les a invités pour le petit déjeuner.
translations.pt: O capitão os convidou para o café da manhã.

more.definition: A chief or leader.; The person lawfully in command of a ship or other vessel.; An army officer with a rank between the most senior grade of lieutenant and major.
more.etymology: Late Latin capitāneuslbor. Old French capitainebor. From Middle English capitain, capteyn, from Old French capitaine, from Late Latin capitāneus, from Latin caput (“head”) (English cap). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kap-. Doublet of chieftain, also from Old French.

examples.text: Tom is the captain of the soccer team.

translations.de: Tom ist der Kapitän der Fußballmannschaft.
translations.fr: Tom est le capitaine de l'équipe de foot.
translations.pt: Tom é o capitão do time de futebol.

examples.text: Suddenly, the captain abandoned the ship.

translations.de: Plötzlich verließ der Kapitän das Schiff.
translations.fr: Tout à coup, le capitaine quitta le navire.
translations.pt: De repente, o capitão abandonou o navio.

examples.text: We chose John to be captain.

translations.de: Wir haben John als Mannschaftskapitän gewählt.
translations.fr: Nous avons choisi John pour capitaine.
translations.pt: Elegemos John para ser o capitão.

examples.text: The captain of the ship decided to change course.

translations.de: Der Kapitän des Schiffes entschied sich den Kurs zu ändern.
translations.fr: Le capitaine du navire a décidé de changer de cap.
translations.pt: O comandante do navio decidiu mudar de rumo.

more.definition: To act as captain; To exercise command of a ship, aircraft or sports team.
more.etymology: Late Latin capitāneuslbor. Old French capitainebor. From Middle English capitain, capteyn, from Old French capitaine, from Late Latin capitāneus, from Latin caput (“head”) (English cap). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kap-. Doublet of chieftain, also from Old French.

examples.text: This blackboard is not black, but green.

translations.de: Diese Tafel ist nicht schwarz, sondern grün.
translations.fr: Ce tableau n'est pas noir, mais vert.
translations.pt: Este quadro negro não é negro, mas verde.

examples.text: What colour is the Black Sea?

translations.de: Welche Farbe hat das Schwarze Meer?
translations.fr: Quelle est la couleur de la Mer Noire ?
translations.pt: Qual é a cor do Mar Negro?

examples.text: The girl has black hair and blue eyes.

translations.de: Das Mädchen hat schwarzes Haar und blaue Augen.
translations.fr: La fille a des cheveux noirs et des yeux bleus.
translations.pt: A menina tem cabelos pretos e olhos azuis.

examples.text: I drink green tea, not black.

translations.de: Ich trinke grünen, keinen schwarzen Tee.
translations.fr: Je bois du thé vert, pas du noir.
translations.pt: Eu bebo chá verde, não preto.

more.definition: Absorbing all light and reflecting none; dark and hueless.; Without light.; Belonging to or descended from any of various (African, Aboriginal, etc.) ethnic groups which typically have dark pigmentation of the skin. (See usage notes below.)
more.etymology: From Middle English blak, black, blake, from Old English blæc (“black, dark", also "ink”), from Proto-West Germanic *blak, from Proto-Germanic *blakaz (“burnt”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleg- (“to burn, shine”).

examples.text: The raven is as black as coal.

translations.de: Der Rabe ist kohlschwarz.
translations.fr: Le corbeau est noir comme du charbon.
translations.pt: O corvo é negro como o carvão.

examples.text: Do you have this shirt in black?

translations.de: Haben Sie dieses Hemd auch in schwarz?
translations.fr: Avez-vous cette chemise en noir ?
translations.pt: Você tem essa camisa em preto?

examples.text: We have a black and white dog.

translations.de: Wir haben einen schwarzweißen Hund.
translations.fr: Nous avons un chien noir et blanc.
translations.pt: Nós temos um cachorro preto e branco.

examples.text: I have a black and white dog.

translations.de: Ich habe einen schwarzweißen Hund.
translations.fr: J'ai un chien noir et blanc.
translations.pt: Tenho um cachorro preto e branco.

more.definition: The colour/color perceived in the absence of light, but also when no light is reflected, but rather absorbed.; A black dye or pigment.; A pen, pencil, crayon, etc., made of black pigment.
more.etymology: From Middle English blak, black, blake, from Old English blæc (“black, dark", also "ink”), from Proto-West Germanic *blak, from Proto-Germanic *blakaz (“burnt”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleg- (“to burn, shine”).

examples.text: What's in the black box?

translations.de: Was ist in der Blackbox?
translations.fr: Qu'y a-t-il dans la boîte noire ?
translations.pt: O que há na caixa preta?

examples.text: In general, English taxis are black.

translations.de: Im Allgemeinen sind englische Taxis schwarz.
translations.fr: En général, les taxis anglais sont noirs.
translations.pt: Em geral, os táxis ingleses são pretos.

examples.text: The black cat is eating a white rat.

translations.de: Die schwarze Katze frisst eine weiße Ratte.
translations.fr: Le chat noir mange un rat blanc.
translations.pt: O gato preto está comendo um rato branco.

examples.text: A little black dog is crossing the road.

translations.de: Ein kleiner, schwarzer Hund überquert die Straße.
translations.fr: Un petit chien noir traverse la rue.
translations.pt: Um cachorrinho preto está atravessando a rua.

more.definition: To make black; to blacken.; To apply blacking to (something).; To boycott, usually as part of an industrial dispute.
more.etymology: From Middle English blak, black, blake, from Old English blæc (“black, dark", also "ink”), from Proto-West Germanic *blak, from Proto-Germanic *blakaz (“burnt”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleg- (“to burn, shine”).

examples.text: Please give me a piece of bread.

translations.de: Gib mir bitte ein Stück Brot.
translations.fr: Donne-moi un morceau de pain, je te prie.
translations.pt: Por favor me dê um pedaço de pão.

examples.text: Tom ate three pieces of cake.

translations.de: Tom aß drei Stücke Kuchen.
translations.fr: Tom a mangé trois parts de gâteau.
translations.pt: Tom comeu três pedaços de bolo.

examples.text: Would you like another piece of cake?

translations.de: Möchtest du noch ein Stück Kuchen?
translations.fr: Voulez-vous une autre tranche de gâteau ?
translations.pt: Você gostaria de outro pedaço de bolo?

examples.text: May I have another piece of cake?

translations.de: Kann ich noch ein Stück Kuchen haben?
translations.fr: Puis-je avoir une autre part de gâteau ?
translations.pt: Posso pegar outra fatia de bolo?

more.definition: A part of a larger whole, usually in such a form that it is able to be separated from other parts.; A single item belonging to a class of similar items.; One of the figures used in playing chess, specifically a higher-value figure as distinguished from a pawn; (by extension) those with which draughts, backgammon, and other similar board games are played.
more.etymology: From Middle English pece, peece, peice, from Old French piece, from Late Latin pecia, petia (“broken piece, fragment; parcel of land”), of uncertain origin. Possibly ultimately from Gaulish *pettyā, from Proto-Celtic *kʷezdis (“piece, portion, quota”). Compare Welsh peth (“thing, stuff, junk”), Breton pez (“thing”), Irish cuid (“part, portion”).

examples.text: I want a piece of chocolate cake.

translations.de: Ich möchte ein Stück Schokoladenkuchen.
translations.fr: Je veux un morceau de gâteau au chocolat.
translations.pt: Eu quero um pedaço de bolo de chocolate.

examples.text: Mother divided the cake into eight pieces.

translations.de: Mutter schnitt den Kuchen in 8 Teile.
translations.fr: Mère coupa le gâteau en huit.
translations.pt: A mãe cortou o bolo em oito pedaços.

examples.text: May I have a piece of it?

translations.de: Kann ich ein Stück davon haben?
translations.fr: Puis-je en avoir un morceau ?
translations.pt: Posso pegar um pedaço?

examples.text: She gave him a piece of paper.

translations.de: Sie gab ihm ein Stück Papier.
translations.fr: Elle lui donna un morceau de papier.
translations.pt: Ela lhe deu um pedaço de papel.

more.definition: To assemble (something real or figurative).; To make, enlarge, or repair, by the addition of a piece or pieces; to patch; often with out.; To produce a work of graffiti more complex than a tag.
more.etymology: From Middle English pece, peece, peice, from Old French piece, from Late Latin pecia, petia (“broken piece, fragment; parcel of land”), of uncertain origin. Possibly ultimately from Gaulish *pettyā, from Proto-Celtic *kʷezdis (“piece, portion, quota”). Compare Welsh peth (“thing, stuff, junk”), Breton pez (“thing”), Irish cuid (“part, portion”).

examples.text: Don't scream, or I'll scream louder.

translations.de: Schrei nicht, sonst schreie ich lauter.
translations.fr: Ne hurle pas ou bien je hurlerai plus fort !
translations.pt: Não grite ou eu gritarei mais alto.

examples.text: He screams a lot.

translations.de: Er schreit viel.
translations.fr: Il crie beaucoup.
translations.pt: Ele grita muito.

examples.text: In space, no one can hear you scream.

translations.de: Im Weltall hört dich keiner schreien.
translations.fr: Dans l'espace, personne ne peut t'entendre crier.
translations.pt: No espaço, ninguém pode ouvir o seu grito.

examples.text: A scream broke the silence.

translations.de: Ein Schrei brach die Stille.
translations.fr: Un cri brisa le silence.
translations.pt: Um grito rompeu o silêncio.

more.definition: A loud, emphatic, exclamation of extreme emotion, especially horror, fear, excitement, or anger; it may comprise a word or a sustained, high-pitched vowel sound.; A loud vocalisation of many animals, especially in response to pain or fear.; A form of singing associated with the metal and screamo styles of music. It is a loud, rough, distorted version of the voice; rather than the normal voice of the singer.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English scremen, borrowed from or cognate with Middle Dutch scremen (“to yell; shout”) and Old Norse skræma (“to terrify; scare”); compare West Flemish schreemen, Zealandic schreême (“to shout; yell; cry”), Swedish skrämma (“to spook; frighten”), Danish skræmme (“to scare”), West Frisian skrieme (“to weep”).

examples.text: I don't want you to scream.

translations.de: Ich will nicht, dass du schreist.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas que tu cries.
translations.pt: Eu não quero que você grite.

examples.text: Tom screamed and ran out of the room.

translations.de: Tom schrie und rannte aus dem Zimmer.
translations.fr: Tom cria et courut hors de la pièce.
translations.pt: Tom deu um grito e saiu correndo da sala.

examples.text: I heard someone screaming my name.

translations.de: Ich hörte jemanden meinen Namen schreien.
translations.fr: J'ai entendu quelqu'un crier mon nom.
translations.pt: Eu ouvi alguém gritar o meu nome.

examples.text: Nobody heard Tom's screams.

translations.de: Niemand hörte Toms Schreie.
translations.fr: Personne n'a entendu Tom crier.
translations.pt: Ninguém ouviu os gritos de Tom.

more.definition: To cry out with a shrill voice; to utter a sudden, sharp outcry, or shrill, loud cry, as in fright or extreme pain; to screech, to shriek.; To move quickly; to race.; To be very indicative of; clearly having the characteristics of.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English scremen, borrowed from or cognate with Middle Dutch scremen (“to yell; shout”) and Old Norse skræma (“to terrify; scare”); compare West Flemish schreemen, Zealandic schreême (“to shout; yell; cry”), Swedish skrämma (“to spook; frighten”), Danish skræmme (“to scare”), West Frisian skrieme (“to weep”).

examples.text: You can't force me to marry you.

translations.de: Du kannst mich nicht dazu zwingen dich zu heiraten.
translations.fr: Tu ne peux pas me forcer à me marier avec toi.
translations.pt: Você não pode me forçar a me casar com você.

examples.text: They joined forces against him.

translations.de: Sie haben sich gegen ihn zusammengeschlossen.
translations.fr: Ils se sont ligués contre lui.
translations.pt: Eles uniram forças contra ele.

examples.text: May the force be with you.

translations.de: Möge die Macht mit dir sein!
translations.fr: Que la force soit avec toi.
translations.pt: Que a força esteja com você.

examples.text: Thoughts are forces.

translations.de: Gedanken sind Kräfte.
translations.fr: Les pensées sont des forces.
translations.pt: Pensamentos são forças.

more.definition: Ability to influence; strength or energy of body or mind; active power; vigour; might; capacity of exercising an influence or producing an effect.; The generalized abstraction of this concept.; A particular form or type of force.
more.etymology: From Middle English force, fors, forse, from Old French force, from Late Latin fortia, a noun derived from the neuter plural of Latin fortis (“strong”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰerǵʰ- (“to rise, high, hill”).

examples.text: You can't force us to go.

translations.de: Du kannst uns nicht zwingen zu gehen.
translations.fr: Tu ne peux pas nous forcer à y aller.
translations.pt: Você não pode nos forçar a ir.

examples.text: I was forced to accept his proposal.

translations.de: Ich war gezwungen, seinen Vorschlag anzunehmen.
translations.fr: J'ai été forcé d'accepter sa proposition.
translations.pt: Fui forçado a aceitar a proposta dele.

examples.text: They abandoned the hill to enemy forces.

translations.de: Sie überließen den Hügel der feindlichen Armee.
translations.fr: Ils cédèrent la colline aux forces ennemies.
translations.pt: Cederam a colina às forças inimigas.

examples.text: The armed forces occupied the entire territory.

translations.de: Das Militär besetzte das gesamte Territorium.
translations.fr: Les forces armées occupèrent l’entièreté du territoire.
translations.pt: As forças armadas ocuparam todo o território.

more.definition: To make someone or something do something, often regardless of their will.; To constrain by force; to overcome the limitations or resistance of.; To drive (something) by force, to propel (generally + prepositional phrase or adverb).
more.etymology: From Middle English forcen, from Old French forcier, from Late Latin *fortiāre, from Latin fortia.

examples.text: He is not at all a gentleman.

translations.de: Er ist absolut kein Gentleman.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas du tout un gentleman.
translations.pt: Ele não é mesmo um cavalheiro.

examples.text: The gentleman is a very famous pianist.

translations.de: Der Herr ist ein sehr bekannter Pianist.
translations.fr: Le monsieur est un pianiste très célèbre.
translations.pt: O cavalheiro é um pianista muito famoso.

examples.text: Go ahead, gentlemen.

translations.de: Gehen Sie voraus, meine Herren.
translations.fr: Allez-y, messieurs.
translations.pt: Adiante, cavalheiros.

examples.text: A gentleman would not say such a thing.

examples.text: I have to study for the test.

examples.text: Everyone knows that luck and wealth elicit envy.

examples.text: Some people have all the luck.

examples.text: It was beginner's luck.

translations.de: Das war Anfängerglück.

more.definition: To find something through good fortune; used with into, on, onto or upon.
more.etymology: From Middle English luk, lukke, from Middle Dutch luc, geluc, gelucke (“good luck, fortune”) or Middle Low German lücke, gelücke (“lot, fortune, fate, luck”), of obscure origin; perhaps ultimately related to German Lücke (“gap, opening”) in the sense of "space or opportunity", hence "chance".

examples.text: There is no air on the moon.

translations.de: Diese Klimaanlage hat einen hohen Stromverbrauch.

more.definition: The substance constituting Earth's atmosphere: a gaseous mixture of nitrogen, oxygen, and various trace gases.; The substance of the atmosphere seen as an agency of freshness.; One of the four elements of the ancient Greeks and Romans.
more.etymology: Ancient Greek ᾱ̓ήρ (āḗr)bor. Old French airbor. From Middle English aire, from Old French air, from Latin āēr, from Ancient Greek ἀήρ (aḗr). Displaced native Old English lyft. More at lift, loft.

examples.text: You're building castles in the air.

examples.text: We'll be back on air shortly.

examples.text: Don't you have an air conditioner?

examples.text: We tried to cheer him up.

examples.text: Give me the key to this lock!

more.definition: To fit (a lock) with a key.; To fit (pieces of a mechanical assembly) with a key to maintain the orientation between them.; To mark or indicate with a symbol indicating membership in a class.

more.definition: The amount of time that some being has been alive, or that some thing has been in existence, as measured from its birth or origin until the present or until some other given reference point. (Often measured in number of years; alternatively in months, days, hours, etc.; see also the usage notes); The state of being old; the latter part of life.; Any particular stage of life.
more.etymology: Old French eagebor. examples.text: Be quiet. Don't talk in the theater.

translations.de: Sei still! Im Theater spricht man nicht!
translations.fr: Taisez-vous. Ne parlez pas dans la salle de spectacle.
translations.pt: Fique quieto. Não fale no teatro.

examples.text: You ought to be quiet in a library.

translations.de: In einer Bibliothek hat man sich ruhig zu verhalten.
translations.fr: On devrait se taire dans une bibliothèque.
translations.pt: Você deveria ficar em silêncio em uma biblioteca.

examples.text: Be quiet in the library.

translations.de: Machen Sie keine Geräusche in der Bibliothek.
translations.fr: Ne faites pas de bruit dans la bibliothèque.
translations.pt: Silêncio na biblioteca!

more.definition: The absence of sound; quietness.; The absence of movement; stillness, tranquility.; The absence of disturbance or trouble; peace, security.
more.etymology: From Middle English quiete, from Old French quiet (adjective) and quiete (noun), from Latin quiētus, past participle of quiēscere (“to keep quiet, rest”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kʷyeh₁- (“rest”). Doublet of coy, quit, quite, and quietus. Largely displaced native English still in the sense of "with little or no sound".

examples.text: Why is it so quiet here?

translations.de: Warum ist es hier so ruhig?
translations.fr: Pourquoi est-ce si calme ici ?
translations.pt: Por que está tão quieto aqui?

examples.text: If I were you, I would stay quiet.

translations.de: Ich bliebe an deiner Stelle ruhig.
translations.fr: Si j'étais toi, je resterais tranquille.
translations.pt: Se eu fosse você, ficaria calado.

examples.text: When I speak, you be quiet and listen!

translations.de: Wenn ich rede, bist du still und hörst zu!
translations.fr: Tais-toi et écoute quand je parle !
translations.pt: Quando eu estiver falando, você fica quieto e ouça.

examples.text: The baby was quiet all night.

translations.de: Das Baby war die ganze Nacht still.
translations.fr: Le bébé a été silencieux toute la nuit.
translations.pt: O bebê ficou quieto a noite toda.

more.definition: To cause (someone or something) to become quiet.; To become quiet or calm.
more.etymology: From Middle English quiete, from Old French quiet (adjective) and quiete (noun), from Latin quiētus, past participle of quiēscere (“to keep quiet, rest”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kʷyeh₁- (“rest”). Doublet of coy, quit, quite, and quietus. Largely displaced native English still in the sense of "with little or no sound".

examples.text: I must have made a mistake somewhere.

translations.de: Ich muss irgendwo einen Fehler gemacht haben.
translations.fr: J'ai dû me tromper quelque part.
translations.pt: Eu devo ter cometido um erro em algum lugar.

examples.text: You've got to start somewhere.

translations.de: Irgendwo muss man anfangen.
translations.fr: Il faut bien commencer quelque part.
translations.pt: Tem de começar por algum lugar.

examples.text: Do you want to go somewhere?

translations.de: Willst du irgendwohin?
translations.fr: Tu veux aller quelque part ?
translations.pt: Tu queres ir a algum lugar?

examples.text: Can we go somewhere and talk?

translations.de: Können wir uns irgendwo unterhalten?
translations.fr: Pouvons-nous aller quelque part et discuter ?
translations.pt: Podemos conversar em outro lugar?

more.definition: In an uncertain or unspecified location.; To an uncertain or unspecified location.; At some unspecified point.
more.etymology: From some + where.

examples.text: I've seen you somewhere before.

translations.de: Ich habe dich schon einmal irgendwo gesehen.
translations.fr: Je vous ai déjà vu quelque part.
translations.pt: Eu te vi em algum lugar antes.

examples.text: I thought we were going to go somewhere.

translations.de: Ich dachte wir werden irgendwo hingehen.
translations.fr: Je pensais que nous allions sortir quelque part.
translations.pt: Eu achei que iríamos para algum lugar.

examples.text: I remember having seen her somewhere.

translations.de: Ich erinnere mich, sie irgendwo gesehen zu haben.
translations.fr: Je me souviens l'avoir vue quelque part.
translations.pt: Eu me lembro de tê-la visto em algum lugar.

examples.text: I had my money stolen somewhere.

translations.de: Mir wurde irgendwo mein Geld gestohlen.
translations.fr: On m’a volé mon argent quelque part.
translations.pt: Roubaram meu dinheiro em algum lugar.

more.definition: Unspecified or unknown (unlocated) place or location.
more.etymology: From some + where.

examples.text: Will you explain the rule to me?

translations.de: Wirst du mir die Regel erklären?
translations.fr: M'expliqueras-tu la règle ?
translations.pt: Você vai explicar a regra para mim?

examples.text: Every driver must follow the traffic rules.

translations.de: Jeder Fahrer muss sich an die Verkehrsregeln halten.
translations.fr: Tout conducteur doit observer les règles de la circulation.
translations.pt: Cada motorista deve observar as regras de trânsito.

examples.text: There is an exception to every rule.

translations.de: Zu jeder Regel gibt es eine Ausnahme.
translations.fr: Toutes les règles ont des exceptions.
translations.pt: Há uma exceção para toda regra.

examples.text: We don't have any rules.

translations.de: Wir haben keine Regeln.
translations.fr: Nous n'avons pas de règles.
translations.pt: Não temos regras.

more.definition: A regulation, law, guideline.; A regulating principle.; The act of ruling; administration of law; government; empire; authority; control.
more.etymology: From Middle English reule, rewle, rule, borrowed from Old French riule, reule, from Latin regula (“straight stick, bar, ruler, pattern”), from regō (“to keep straight, direct, govern, rule”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₃réǵeti (“to straighten; right”), from the root *h₃reǵ-; see regent. Doublet of rail, regal, regula, and rigol.

examples.text: Do you know the rules of football?

translations.de: Kennst du die Fußballregeln?
translations.fr: Connais-tu les règles du football ?
translations.pt: Você conhece as regras do futebol?

examples.text: This is an exception to the rule.

translations.de: Das ist eine Ausnahme von der Regel.
translations.fr: C'est une exception à la règle.
translations.pt: Isto é uma exceção à regra.

examples.text: The king ruled the country for years.

translations.de: Der König regierte jahrelang das Land.
translations.fr: Le roi gouverna le pays pendant des années.
translations.pt: O rei governou o país durante anos.

examples.text: We always have to obey the rules.

translations.de: Wir müssen uns immer an die Regeln halten.
translations.fr: Nous devons toujours obéir aux règlements.
translations.pt: Sempre temos que obedecer às regras.

more.definition: To regulate, be in charge of, make decisions for, reign over.; To excel.; To decide judicially.
more.etymology: From Middle English reulen, rulen, borrowed from Old French riuler, from Latin regulāre (“to regulate, rule”), from regula (“a rule”); see regular and regulate.

examples.text: Tom didn't really enjoy studying French.

translations.de: Tom hat es nicht wirklich gefallen, Französisch zu lernen.
translations.fr: Tom n'a pas vraiment apprécié d'étudier le français.
translations.pt: Tom não gostava muito de estudar francês.

examples.text: My children really enjoyed this strawberry ice cream.

translations.de: Meine Kinder haben dieses Erdbeereis genossen.
translations.fr: Mes enfants ont savouré cette glace aux fraises.
translations.pt: Meus filhos adoraram esse sorvete de morango.

examples.text: They seem to be enjoying themselves.

translations.de: Sie scheinen sich zu amüsieren.
translations.fr: Elles semblent s'amuser.
translations.pt: Eles parecem estar se divertindo.

examples.text: She enjoys listening to classical music.

translations.de: Sie hört klassische Musik gern.
translations.fr: Elle aime écouter de la musique classique.
translations.pt: Ela gosta de ouvir música clássica.

more.definition: To receive pleasure or satisfaction from something.; To have the use or benefit of something.; To be satisfied or receive pleasure; to have fun.
more.etymology: From Middle English enjoyen, from Old French enjoier, anjoier, enjoer (“to give joy, receive with joy, rejoice”), equivalent to en- + joy.

examples.text: I am the one who knocks.

translations.de: Ich bin derjenige der klopft.
translations.fr: Je suis celui qui frappe.
translations.pt: Sou eu que estou batendo.

examples.text: May happiness knock on your door.

translations.de: Möge das Glück an Ihre Tür klopfen!
translations.fr: Puisse le bonheur frapper à ta porte.
translations.pt: Que a felicidade bata à sua porta.

examples.text: Please knock on the door before you enter.

translations.de: Bitte klopf an, bevor du herein kommst.
translations.fr: Frappez avant d'entrer, s'il vous plait.
translations.pt: Por favor, chame antes de entrar.

examples.text: Please knock before you come in.

translations.de: Klopfen Sie bitte vor dem Eintreten.
translations.fr: Veuillez frapper avant d'entrer.
translations.pt: Por favor bata a porta antes de entrar.

more.definition: An abrupt rapping sound, as from an impact of a hard object against wood.; A sharp impact.; A criticism.
more.etymology: From Middle English knokken, from Old English cnocian, ġecnocian, ġecnucian, cnucian (“to knock, pound on, beat”), from Proto-West Germanic *knokōn, from Proto-Germanic *knukōną (“to knock”), a suffixed form of *knu-, *knew- (“to pound on, beat”), from Proto-Indo-European *gnew-, *gen- (“to squeeze, pinch, kink, ball up, concentrate”).

examples.text: He always knocks on the door before entering.

translations.de: Er klopft immer an die Tür, bevor er eintritt.
translations.fr: Il frappe toujours à la porte avant d'entrer.
translations.pt: Ele sempre bate na porta antes de entrar.

examples.text: Could you knock a little off the price?

translations.de: Könntest du den Preis ein wenig senken?
translations.fr: Pourriez-vous baisser un peu le prix ?
translations.pt: Você poderia abater um pouco o preço?

examples.text: I knocked, but no one opened the door.

translations.de: Ich klopfte, aber niemand öffnete die Tür.
translations.fr: Je frappai mais personne n'ouvrit la porte.
translations.pt: Bati, mas ninguém abriu a porta.

examples.text: Somebody's knocking at your door.

translations.de: Jemand klopft an deine Tür.
translations.fr: Quelqu'un frappe à votre porte.
translations.pt: Alguém está batendo à sua porta.

more.definition: To rap one's knuckles against something, especially wood.; To criticize verbally; to denigrate; to undervalue.; To kick a ball towards another player; to pass.
more.etymology: From Middle English knokken, from Old English cnocian, ġecnocian, ġecnucian, cnucian (“to knock, pound on, beat”), from Proto-West Germanic *knokōn, from Proto-Germanic *knukōną (“to knock”), a suffixed form of *knu-, *knew- (“to pound on, beat”), from Proto-Indo-European *gnew-, *gen- (“to squeeze, pinch, kink, ball up, concentrate”).

examples.text: Countless stars were twinkling in the sky.

translations.de: Am Himmel funkelten zahlreiche Sterne.
translations.fr: D'innombrables étoiles scintillaient dans le ciel.
translations.pt: Inúmeras estrelas cintilavam no céu.

examples.text: Venus is also known as the Morning Star.

translations.de: Die Venus wird auch als Morgenstern bezeichnet.
translations.fr: Vénus est également connue sous le nom d'Étoile du Matin.
translations.pt: Vênus também é conhecido como estrela-d'alva.

examples.text: There are thousands of stars in the universe.

translations.de: Es gibt Tausende von Sternen im Universum.
translations.fr: Il y a des milliers d'étoiles dans l'univers.
translations.pt: Há milhares de estrelas no universo.

examples.text: The American flag has fifty stars.

translations.de: Die amerikanische Flagge hat fünfzig Sterne.
translations.fr: Le drapeau des USA a cinquante étoiles.
translations.pt: A bandeira americana tem cinquenta estrelas.

more.definition: Any small, natural and bright dot in the sky, most visible in the night or twilight sky. This sense includes the planets, but it is now sometimes used in exclusion of them due to influence from the technical astronomical sense.; A planet thought to influence one's fate; (figuratively) fate or luck.; A very massive ball of plasma with strong enough gravity to have ongoing fusion of hydrogen or heavier elements in its core. In strict technical usage, the Sun is included.
more.etymology: From Middle English sterre, from Old English steorra (“star”), from Proto-West Germanic *sterrō, variant of *sternō, from Proto-Germanic *sternô, *sternǭ (“star”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂stḗr (“star”). Doublet of aster; related to estoile, étoile, stella, and stelo.

examples.text: The stars are shining in the sky.

translations.de: Die Sterne funkeln am Himmel.
translations.fr: Les étoiles brillent dans le ciel.
translations.pt: As estrelas estão brilhando no céu.

examples.text: Do you know the name of this star?

translations.de: Kennen Sie den Namen dieses Sterns?
translations.fr: Connaissez-vous le nom de cette star ?
translations.pt: Você sabe o nome dessa estrela?

examples.text: There are innumerable stars in the universe.

translations.de: Es gibt unzählig viele Sterne im Universum.
translations.fr: Il y a une myriade d'étoiles dans l'univers.
translations.pt: Há incontáveis estrelas no universo.

examples.text: Thousands of stars shone in the heavens.

translations.de: Tausende von Sternen leuchteten am Himmel.
translations.fr: Des milliers d'étoiles brillaient dans les cieux.
translations.pt: Milhares de estrelas brilhavam no céu.

more.definition: To appear as a featured performer or headliner, especially in an entertainment program.; To feature (a performer or a headliner), especially in a movie or an entertainment program.; To mark with a star or asterisk.
more.etymology: From Middle English sterre, from Old English steorra (“star”), from Proto-West Germanic *sterrō, variant of *sternō, from Proto-Germanic *sternô, *sternǭ (“star”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂stḗr (“star”). Doublet of aster; related to estoile, étoile, stella, and stelo.

examples.text: The ball is in your court.

translations.de: Ihr seid an der Reihe.
translations.fr: Le ballon est à toi.
translations.pt: A bola está com você.

examples.text: Tom tossed the ball to Mary.

translations.de: Tom warf Maria den Ball zu.
translations.fr: Tom lança la balle vers Marie.
translations.pt: Tom jogou a bola para Mary.

examples.text: Tom threw the ball to Mary.

translations.de: Tom warf Maria den Ball zu.
translations.fr: Tom jeta la balle à Mary.
translations.pt: Tom jogou a bola para Mary.

examples.text: Hold the ball with both hands.

translations.de: Halt den Ball mit beiden Händen fest.
translations.fr: Tiens le ballon des deux mains.
translations.pt: Segure a bola com as duas mãos.

more.definition: An exclamation to inform players on an adjacent playing area that a loose ball from another game has entered their playing area; typically implies that play should be paused until the ball has been retrieved.; An appeal by the crowd for holding the ball against a tackled player.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *bʰel-der. From Middle English bal, ball, balle, from an unattested Old English *beall, *bealla (“round object, ball”), from Proto-Germanic *balluz, *ballô (“ball”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰol-n- (“ball, bubble”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel- (“to blow, inflate, swell”). Cognate with Old Saxon ball, Dutch bal, Old High German bal, ballo (German Ball (“ball”); Ballen (“bale”)).

examples.text: I don't have a crystal ball.

translations.de: Ich habe keine Kristallkugel.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas de boule de cristal.
translations.pt: Eu não tenho uma bola de cristal.

examples.text: I can juggle three balls.

translations.de: Ich kann mit drei Bällen jonglieren.
translations.fr: Je sais jongler avec trois balles.
translations.pt: Posso fazer malabarismos com três bolas.

examples.text: The cat is playing with the ball.

translations.de: Die Katze spielt mit dem Ball.
translations.fr: Le chat joue avec le ballon.
translations.pt: O gato está brincando com a bola.

examples.text: Now the ball is in your court!

translations.de: Jetzt zeig mal, was du kannst!
translations.fr: Maintenant la balle est dans ton camp !
translations.pt: Agora vamos ver o que você pode fazer!

more.definition: A solid or hollow sphere, or roughly spherical mass.; A quantity of string, thread, etc., wound into a spherical shape.; A food preparation formed into a spherical shape.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *bʰel-der. From Middle English bal, ball, balle, from an unattested Old English *beall, *bealla (“round object, ball”), from Proto-Germanic *balluz, *ballô (“ball”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰol-n- (“ball, bubble”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel- (“to blow, inflate, swell”). Cognate with Old Saxon ball, Dutch bal, Old High German bal, ballo (German Ball (“ball”); Ballen (“bale”)).

examples.text: Is this ball yours or hers?

translations.de: Ist das dein Ball oder ihrer?
translations.fr: Cette balle, est-elle la tienne ou la sienne ?
translations.pt: Esta bola é sua ou dela?

examples.text: We bought some tennis balls.

translations.de: Wir haben ein paar Tennisbälle gekauft.
translations.fr: Nous avons acheté quelques balles de tennis.
translations.pt: Nós compramos algumas bolas de tênis.

examples.text: Throw the ball back to me.

translations.de: Wirf mir den Ball zurück!
translations.fr: Renvoie-moi la balle.
translations.pt: Jogue a bola de volta para mim.

examples.text: The player kicked the ball.

translations.de: Der Spieler hat den Ball gekickt.
translations.fr: Le joueur a frappé le ballon.
translations.pt: O jogador chutou a bola.

more.definition: To form or wind into a ball.; To heat in a furnace and form into balls for rolling.; To have sexual intercourse (with).
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *bʰel-der. From Middle English bal, ball, balle, from an unattested Old English *beall, *bealla (“round object, ball”), from Proto-Germanic *balluz, *ballô (“ball”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰol-n- (“ball, bubble”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel- (“to blow, inflate, swell”). Cognate with Old Saxon ball, Dutch bal, Old High German bal, ballo (German Ball (“ball”); Ballen (“bale”)).

examples.text: I'm going to count to three.

translations.de: Ich werde bis drei zählen.
translations.fr: Je vais compter jusqu'à trois.
translations.pt: Vou contar até três.

examples.text: I knew I could count on you.

translations.de: Ich wusste, auf dich ist Verlass.
translations.fr: Je savais que je pouvais compter sur toi.
translations.pt: Eu sabia que podia contar contigo.

examples.text: You can't count on his help.

translations.de: Du kannst nicht mit seiner Hilfe rechnen.
translations.fr: On ne peut pas compter sur son aide.
translations.pt: Você não pode contar com a ajuda dele.

examples.text: Can you count to one hundred in French?

translations.de: Kannst du auf Französisch bis hundert zählen?
translations.fr: Sais-tu compter jusqu'à cent en français ?
translations.pt: Sabe contar até cem em francês?

more.definition: Countable.; Used to show the amount of like items in a package.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Anglo-Norman counterbor. From Middle English counten, borrowed from Anglo-Norman conter, from Old French conter (“add up; tell a story”), from Latin computō (“to compute”). In this sense, displaced native Old English tellan, whence Modern English tell. Doublet of compute.

examples.text: My son can't count yet.

translations.de: Mein Sohn kann noch nicht zählen.
translations.fr: Mon fils ne sait pas encore compter.
translations.pt: Meu filho ainda não sabe contar.

examples.text: Every minute counts.

translations.de: Jede Minute zählt.
translations.fr: Chaque minute compte.
translations.pt: Cada minuto é importante.

examples.text: Don't worry. You can count on me.

translations.de: Mach dir keine Sorgen. Du kannst dich auf mich verlassen.
translations.fr: Ne crains rien, tu peux te fier à moi.
translations.pt: Não se preocupe. Você pode contar comigo.

examples.text: We have more customers than we can count.

translations.de: Wir haben mehr Kunden, als wir zählen können.
translations.fr: Nous avons plus de clients que nous ne pouvons en compter.
translations.pt: Nós temos mais clientes do que podemos contar.

more.definition: The act of counting or tallying a quantity.; The result of a tally that reveals the number of items in a set; a quantity counted.; A countdown.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Anglo-Norman counterbor. From Middle English counten, borrowed from Anglo-Norman conter, from Old French conter (“add up; tell a story”), from Latin computō (“to compute”). In this sense, displaced native Old English tellan, whence Modern English tell. Doublet of compute.

examples.text: We're counting on you to help.

translations.de: Wir zählen auf deine Hilfe.
translations.fr: Nous comptons sur toi pour aider.
translations.pt: Estamos contando com você para ajudar.

examples.text: It's the thought that counts.

translations.de: Der Gedanke zählt.
translations.fr: C’est l’intention qui compte.
translations.pt: O que importa é a intenção.

examples.text: When angry, count to ten before you speak.

translations.de: Wenn du dich ärgerst, dann zähle bis zehn, ehe du etwas sagst.
translations.fr: Quand tu es en colère, compte jusqu'à dix avant de parler.
translations.pt: Quando estiver com raiva, conte até dez antes de falar.

examples.text: I counted to two hundred.

translations.de: Ich habe bis zweihundert gezählt.
translations.fr: J'ai compté jusqu'à deux-cents.
translations.pt: Contei até duzentos.

more.definition: To recite numbers in sequence.; To determine the number of (objects in a group).; To amount to, to number in total.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Anglo-Norman counterbor. From Middle English counten, borrowed from Anglo-Norman conter, from Old French conter (“add up; tell a story”), from Latin computō (“to compute”). In this sense, displaced native Old English tellan, whence Modern English tell. Doublet of compute.

examples.text: Tom handed Mary a cup of coffee.

translations.de: Tom gab Maria eine Tasse Kaffee.
translations.fr: Tom tendit une tasse de café à Marie.
translations.pt: Tom ofereceu a Mary uma xícara de café.

examples.text: Do you want another cup of coffee?

translations.de: Möchten Sie noch eine Tasse Kaffee?
translations.fr: Veux-tu une autre tasse de café ?
translations.pt: Quer mais uma xícara de café?

examples.text: Please give me a cup of coffee.

translations.de: Bitte geben Sie mir eine Tasse Kaffee.
translations.fr: Donne-moi une tasse de café, je te prie.
translations.pt: Por favor, dá-me uma xícara de café.

examples.text: I put some milk in my coffee.

translations.de: Ich nehme etwas Milch in meinen Kaffee.
translations.fr: Je mis un peu de lait dans mon café.
translations.pt: Eu coloquei leite no meu café.

more.definition: Of a pale brown colour, like that of milk coffee.; Of a table: a small, low table suitable for people in lounge seating to put coffee cups on.
more.etymology: Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa)bor. Ottoman Turkish قهوه (kahve)bor. Italian caffèbor. Dutch koffiebor. Borrowed from Dutch koffie, from Italian caffè, from Ottoman Turkish قهوه (kahve), from Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa). Doublet of café and caffè and cognate with the words for "coffee" in other major European languages, most of which are derived from the Turkish and Italian words.

examples.text: I would like a cup of coffee.

translations.de: Ich möchte gern eine Tasse Kaffee.
translations.fr: Je voudrais une tasse de café.
translations.pt: Gostaria de uma xícara de café.

examples.text: I spilled my coffee on the carpet.

translations.de: Ich habe meinen Kaffee auf dem Teppich verschüttet.
translations.fr: J'ai renversé mon café sur le tapis.
translations.pt: Derramei café no carpete.

examples.text: Don't put sugar in my coffee.

translations.de: Tu keinen Zucker in meinen Kaffee.
translations.fr: Ne mets pas de sucre dans mon café.
translations.pt: Não ponha açúcar no meu café.

examples.text: Do you want a cup of coffee?

translations.de: Möchten Sie eine Tasse Kaffee?
translations.fr: Voulez-vous une tasse de café ?
translations.pt: Queres uma xícara de café?

more.definition: A beverage made by infusing the beans of the coffee plant in hot water.; A serving of this beverage.; The seeds of the plant used to make coffee, called ‘beans’ due to their shape.
more.etymology: Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa)bor. Ottoman Turkish قهوه (kahve)bor. Italian caffèbor. Dutch koffiebor. Borrowed from Dutch koffie, from Italian caffè, from Ottoman Turkish قهوه (kahve), from Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa). Doublet of café and caffè and cognate with the words for "coffee" in other major European languages, most of which are derived from the Turkish and Italian words.

examples.text: I put some cream in my coffee.

translations.de: Ich mache ein wenig Sahne in meinen Kaffee.
translations.fr: Je mis du lait dans mon café.
translations.pt: Eu coloquei um pouco de creme no meu café.

examples.text: Would you like another cup of coffee?

more.definition: To sense a smell or smells.; To detect or perceive; often with out.; Followed by like or of if descriptive: to have a particular smell, whether good or bad.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *smel-der. From Middle English smellen, smillen, smyllen, smullen, from Old English *smyllan, *smiellan (“to smell, emit fumes”), from Proto-West Germanic *smallijan (“to glow, burn, smoulder”), from Proto-Indo-European *smel- (“to burn, smoke, smoulder; tar, pitch”). The noun is from Middle English smel, smil, smul (“smell, odour”).

examples.text: You have only to push the button.

more.definition: A short, directed application of force; an act of pushing.; An act of tensing the muscles of the abdomen in order to expel its contents.; A great effort (to do something).
more.etymology: From Middle English pushen, poshen, posson, borrowed from Middle French pousser (Modern French pousser) from Old French poulser, from Latin pulsare (“to beat, strike”), frequentative of pellere (past participle pulsus). Doublet of pulsate and pulse (verb). Partly displaced native Old English sċūfan, whence Modern English shove.

translations.de: Ich schubste Tom ins Wasser.
translations.fr: J'ai poussé Tom dans l'eau.

examples.text: In case of an emergency, push this button.

examples.text: Tom pushed the shopping cart for his mother.

translations.de: Tom schob seiner Mutter den Einkaufswagen.

translations.pt: Tom empurrou o carrinho de compras para sua mãe.

examples.text: She pushed him out the window.

translations.de: Sie stieß ihn zum Fenster hinaus.
translations.fr: Elle le poussa par la fenêtre.

more.definition: To apply a force to (an object) such that it moves away from the person or thing applying the force.; To continually attempt to persuade (a person) into a particular course of action.; To press or urge forward; to drive.
more.etymology: From Middle English pushen, poshen, posson, borrowed from Middle French pousser (Modern French pousser) from Old French poulser, from Latin pulsare (“to beat, strike”), frequentative of pellere (past participle pulsus). Doublet of pulsate and pulse (verb). Partly displaced native Old English sċūfan, whence Modern English shove.

examples.text: There was absolutely no doubt.

translations.pt: Não havia absolutamente nenhuma dúvida.

more.definition: The part of an object which is (designed to be) held in the hand when used or moved.; An instrument for effecting a purpose (either literally or figuratively); a tool, or an opportunity or pretext.; The gross amount of wagering within a given period of time or for a given event at one of more establishments.

examples.text: Usually, a pot has two handles.

examples.text: I think we can handle this.

more.definition: To touch; to feel or hold with the hand(s).; To manage, use, or wield with the hands.; To manage, control, or direct.
more.etymology: From Middle English handlen, from Old English handlian (“to handle, feel, deal with, discuss”), from Proto-West Germanic *handulōn, from Proto-Germanic *handulōną (“to take, grip, feel”), equivalent to hand + -le.

examples.text: This dog is trained to smell out drugs.

translations.de: Dieser Hund ist darauf abgerichtet, Rauschgift zu erschnüffeln.

translations.de: Sie verkauft Drogen auf Konzerten.

more.definition: A substance used to treat an illness, relieve a symptom, or modify a chemical process in the body for a specific purpose.; A psychoactive substance, especially one which is illegal and addictive, ingested for recreational use, such as cocaine.; Anything, such as a substance, emotion, or action, to which one is addicted.
more.etymology: From Middle English drogge (“medicine”), from Middle French drogue, drocque (“tincture, pharmaceutical product”) (c. 1462), from Middle Dutch or Middle Low German droge, as in droge vate (“dry vats, dry barrels”), mistaking droge for the contents, which were usually dried herbs, plants or wares.

examples.text: Are generics as effective as brand name drugs?

translations.fr: Les génériques sont-ils aussi efficaces que les médicaments de marques ?
translations.pt: Será que os genéricos são tão eficazes quanto os remédios de marca?

more.definition: To administer intoxicating drugs to, generally without the recipient's knowledge or consent.; To add intoxicating drugs to with the intention of drugging someone.; To prescribe or administer drugs or medicines.
more.etymology: From Middle English drogge (“medicine”), from Middle French drogue, drocque (“tincture, pharmaceutical product”) (c. 1462), from Middle Dutch or Middle Low German droge, as in droge vate (“dry vats, dry barrels”), mistaking droge for the contents, which were usually dried herbs, plants or wares.

more.etymology: From Middle English fisch, from Old English fisċ (“fish”), from Proto-West Germanic *fisk, from Proto-Germanic *fiskaz (“fish”), from Proto-Indo-European *piskós (“fish”).

more.etymology: From Old English fiscian, from Proto-West Germanic *fiskōn, from Proto-Germanic *fiskōną.

more.definition: Relating to now, for the time being; current.; Located in the immediate vicinity.; Relating to something a person is referring to in the very context, with a deictic use similar to the demonstrative adjective this.

more.etymology: From Middle English present, from Old French present, from Latin praesent-, praesens, present participle of praeesse (“to be present”), from Latin prae- (“pre-”) + esse (“to be”). Displaced Old English andweard (“present, current”).

translations.pt: Juro que é a última vez.
