more.etymology: From the above verb, or from Middle English sware, from Old English swaru, from Proto-Germanic *swarō.

examples.text: I swear to God.

translations.de: Ich schwöre bei Gott.
translations.fr: Je le jure devant Dieu.
translations.pt: Juro por Deus.

examples.text: He started swearing.

translations.de: Er fing an zu fluchen.
translations.fr: Il s'est mis à jurer.
translations.pt: Ele começou a praguejar.

examples.text: I could have sworn I saw somebody.

translations.de: Ich hätte schwören können, dass ich jemanden gesehen habe.
translations.fr: J'aurais pu jurer avoir vu quelqu'un.
translations.pt: Eu poderia jurar que vi alguém.

examples.text: I swear I won't tell anyone.

translations.de: Ich schwöre, ich werde es niemandem sagen.
translations.fr: Je jure que je ne le dirai à personne.
translations.pt: Eu juro não dizer a ninguém.

more.definition: To take an oath, to promise intensely, solemnly, and/or with legally binding effect.; To take an oath that an assertion is true.; To promise intensely that something is true; to strongly assert.
more.etymology: From Middle English sweren, swerien, from Old English swerian (“to swear, take an oath of office”), from Proto-West Germanic *swarjan, from Proto-Germanic *swarjaną (“to speak, swear”), from Proto-Indo-European *swer- (“to swear”).

examples.text: What is the purpose of your visit?

translations.de: Was ist der Zweck deines Besuches?
translations.fr: Quel est le but de votre visite ?
translations.pt: Qual é o motivo de sua visita?

examples.text: His visits became less frequent as time passed.

translations.de: Seine Besuche wurden allmählich seltener.
translations.fr: Ses visites devenaient de moins en moins fréquentes avec le temps.
translations.pt: Suas visitas tornaram-se menos frequentes conforme o tempo passava.

examples.text: Let's visit my grandpa this weekend.

translations.de: Besuchen wir meinen Großvater am Wochenende!
translations.fr: Rendons visite à mon Papy, ce week-end !
translations.pt: Vamos visitar meu avô nessa semana.

examples.text: I would like to visit New York.

translations.de: Ich würde gern New York besuchen.
translations.fr: Je voudrais visiter New York.
translations.pt: Gostaria de visitar Nova York.

more.definition: A single act of visiting.; A meeting with a doctor at their surgery or the doctor's at one's home.
more.etymology: From Middle English visiten, from Old French visiter, from Latin vīsitō, frequentative of vīsō (“behold, survey”), from videō (“see”). Cognate with Old Saxon wīsōn (“to visit, afflict”), archaic German weisen (“to visit, afflict”). Displaced native Old English sēċan (“to visit”) and sōcn (“a visit”). The noun is from French visite or the verb. Doublet of visite.

examples.text: I'd like to visit Australia someday.

translations.de: Ich möchte irgendwann mal nach Australien.
translations.fr: J'aimerais visiter l'Australie un jour.
translations.pt: Eu gostaria de visitar a Austrália algum dia.

examples.text: We visited Sao Paulo's largest museum.

translations.de: Wir besuchten das größte Museum in São Paulo.
translations.fr: Nous avons visité le plus grand musée de Sao Paulo.
translations.pt: Visitamos o maior museu de São Paulo.

examples.text: Tom visits his parents every weekend.

translations.de: Tom besucht jedes Wochenende seine Eltern.
translations.fr: Tom se rend chez ses parents chaque week-end.
translations.pt: Tom visita seus pais todo final de semana.

examples.text: I can't visit you every day.

translations.de: Ich kann dich nicht jeden Tag besuchen.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas venir te voir chaque jour.
translations.pt: Eu não posso visitá-lo todos os dias.

more.definition: To habitually go to (someone in distress, sickness etc.) to comfort them. (Now generally merged into later senses, below.); To go and meet (a person) as an act of friendliness or sociability.; Of God: to appear to (someone) to comfort, bless, or chastise or punish them. (Now generally merged into later senses, below.)
more.etymology: From Middle English visiten, from Old French visiter, from Latin vīsitō, frequentative of vīsō (“behold, survey”), from videō (“see”). Cognate with Old Saxon wīsōn (“to visit, afflict”), archaic German weisen (“to visit, afflict”). Displaced native Old English sēċan (“to visit”) and sōcn (“a visit”). The noun is from French visite or the verb. Doublet of visite.

examples.text: Something weird's going on here.

translations.de: Hier geht etwas Seltsames vor.
translations.fr: Il se passe un truc bizarre.
translations.pt: Algo estranho está acontecendo aqui.

examples.text: She was acting really weird.

translations.de: Sie benahm sich sehr sonderbar.
translations.fr: Elle se comportait vraiment de façon bizarre.
translations.pt: Ela estava muito estranha.

examples.text: This is a little weird.

translations.de: Das ist ein wenig sonderbar.
translations.fr: C'est un peu bizarre.
translations.pt: Isto é um pouco estranho.

examples.text: There's something weird happening.

translations.de: Es geht etwas Seltsames vor sich.
translations.fr: Il se passe quelque chose d’étrange.
translations.pt: Tem alguma coisa estranha acontecendo.

more.definition: Having an unusually strange character or behaviour.; Deviating from the normal; bizarre.; Relating to weird fiction ("a macabre subgenre of speculative fiction").
more.etymology: From Middle English werde, wierde, wirde, wyrede, wurde, from Old English wyrd (“fate”), from Proto-West Germanic *wurdi, from Proto-Germanic *wurdiz, from Proto-Indo-European *wert- (“to turn, wind”). Cognate with Icelandic urður (“fate”). Related to Old English weorþan (“to become”); more at worth (verb). Doublet of wyrd, a reborrowing of the original sense and spelling.

examples.text: I had a very weird dream.

translations.de: Ich hatte einen sehr seltsamen Traum.
translations.fr: J'ai fait un rêve très bizarre.
translations.pt: Eu tive um sonho muito estranho.

examples.text: I know that this is weird.

translations.de: Ich weiß, dass das seltsam ist.
translations.fr: Je sais que c'est bizarre.
translations.pt: Eu sei que isto é estranho.

examples.text: I always thought that was weird.

translations.de: Ich fand das immer merkwürdig.
translations.fr: J'ai toujours pensé que c'était bizarre.
translations.pt: Sempre pensei que isso fosse estranho.

examples.text: That's weird, isn't it?

translations.de: Schon komisch, nicht?
translations.fr: C'est bizarre, non ?
translations.pt: Isso é esquisito, não é?

more.etymology: From Middle English werde, wierde, wirde, wyrede, wurde, from Old English wyrd (“fate”), from Proto-West Germanic *wurdi, from Proto-Germanic *wurdiz, from Proto-Indo-European *wert- (“to turn, wind”). Cognate with Icelandic urður (“fate”). Related to Old English weorþan (“to become”); more at worth (verb). Doublet of wyrd, a reborrowing of the original sense and spelling.

examples.text: People from Madrid are weird.

translations.de: Leute aus Madrid sind seltsam.
translations.fr: Ils sont fous ces Madrilènes.
translations.pt: As pessoas de Madri são estranhas.

examples.text: This place is weird.

translations.de: Hier geht es komisch zu.
translations.fr: Cet endroit est bizarre.
translations.pt: Este lugar é estranho.

examples.text: Isn't that weird?

translations.de: Ist das nicht seltsam?
translations.fr: Curieux, n'est-ce pas ?
translations.pt: Isso não é estranho?

examples.text: This is so weird.

translations.de: Das ist so seltsam.
translations.fr: C'est tellement bizarre.
translations.pt: Isso é tão estranho.

more.definition: A prediction.; That which comes to pass; a fact.; Weirdness.
more.etymology: From Middle English werde, wierde, wirde, wyrede, wurde, from Old English wyrd (“fate”), from Proto-West Germanic *wurdi, from Proto-Germanic *wurdiz, from Proto-Indo-European *wert- (“to turn, wind”). Cognate with Icelandic urður (“fate”). Related to Old English weorþan (“to become”); more at worth (verb). Doublet of wyrd, a reborrowing of the original sense and spelling.

examples.text: This is really weird.

translations.de: Dies ist wirklich seltsam.
translations.fr: C'est vraiment bizarre.
translations.pt: Isso é estranho mesmo.

examples.text: He's weird.

translations.de: Er ist komisch.
translations.fr: Il est bizarre.
translations.pt: Ele é estranho.

examples.text: Is that weird?

translations.de: Ist das komisch?
translations.fr: Est-ce bizarre ?
translations.pt: Isso é estranho?

examples.text: Japan is weird.

translations.de: Japan ist eigenartig.
translations.fr: Le Japon est bizarre.
translations.pt: O Japão é estranho.

more.definition: To destine; doom; change by witchcraft or sorcery.; To warn solemnly; adjure.
more.etymology: From Middle English werde, wierde, wirde, wyrede, wurde, from Old English wyrd (“fate”), from Proto-West Germanic *wurdi, from Proto-Germanic *wurdiz, from Proto-Indo-European *wert- (“to turn, wind”). Cognate with Icelandic urður (“fate”). Related to Old English weorþan (“to become”); more at worth (verb). Doublet of wyrd, a reborrowing of the original sense and spelling.

examples.text: The dog looked at his master with anxiety.

translations.de: Der Hund schaute seinen Herrn ängstlich an.
translations.fr: Le chien regarda son maître avec anxiété.
translations.pt: O cachorro olhou para o seu mestre com ansiedade.

examples.text: It takes years to master a foreign language.

translations.de: Es dauert Jahre, bis man eine Fremdsprache beherrscht.
translations.fr: Il faut des années afin de maîtriser une langue étrangère.
translations.pt: Leva-se anos para dominar uma língua estrangeira.

examples.text: Money is a good servant but a bad master.

translations.de: Geld ist ein guter Diener, aber ein schlechter Herr.
translations.fr: L'argent est un bon serviteur, mais un mauvais maître.
translations.pt: O dinheiro é um bom servidor, mas um mau senhor.

examples.text: She got her master's degree three years ago.

translations.de: Sie machte den Magister vor drei Jahren.
translations.fr: Elle a eu un diplôme de master il y a trois ans.
translations.pt: Ela conseguiu seu mestrado três anos atrás.

more.definition: Masterful.; Main, principal or predominant.; Highly skilled.
more.etymology: Old French maistrebor. Latin magisterder. From Middle English maister, mayster, meister (noun) and maistren (verb), from Old English mǣster, mæġster, mæġester, mæġister, magister (“master”), from Latin magister (“chief, teacher, leader”), from Old Latin magester, from Proto-Indo-European *méǵh₂s (as in magnus (“great”), also cognate of English much and mickle) + -ester/-ister (compare minister (“servant”)).

examples.text: She got a master's degree three years ago.

translations.de: Sie machte den Magister vor drei Jahren.
translations.fr: Elle a eu un diplôme de master il y a trois ans.
translations.pt: Ela conseguiu seu mestrado três anos atrás.

examples.text: Bu Xiangzhi is one of the most talented Chinese Grand Masters.

translations.de: Bu Xiangzhi ist einer der talentiertesten chinesischen Großmeister.
translations.fr: Bu Xiangzhi est l'un des grands maîtres chinois les plus talentueux.
translations.pt: Bu Xiangzhi é um dos mais talentosos Grandes Mestres chineses.

examples.text: It's not easy to master French at all.

translations.de: Französisch zu meistern ist ganz und gar nicht leicht.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas du tout facile de maîtriser le français.
translations.pt: Não é nada fácil dominar o francês.

examples.text: To master English is difficult.

translations.de: Es ist schwer, Englisch zu meistern.
translations.fr: Maîtriser l'anglais est difficile.
translations.pt: Dominar a língua inglesa é difícil.

more.definition: Someone who has control over something or someone.; The owner of an animal or slave.; The captain of a merchant ship; a master mariner.
more.etymology: Old French maistrebor. Latin magisterder. From Middle English maister, mayster, meister (noun) and maistren (verb), from Old English mǣster, mæġster, mæġester, mæġister, magister (“master”), from Latin magister (“chief, teacher, leader”), from Old Latin magester, from Proto-Indo-European *méǵh₂s (as in magnus (“great”), also cognate of English much and mickle) + -ester/-ister (compare minister (“servant”)).

examples.text: Sooner or later, he will master French.

translations.de: Früher oder später wird er Französisch beherrschen.
translations.fr: Tôt ou tard, il maîtrisera le français.
translations.pt: Mais cedo ou mais tarde, ele vai dominar o francês.

examples.text: Dogs have masters. Cats have staff.

translations.de: Hunde haben Herrchen und Frauchen. Katzen haben Diener.
translations.fr: Les chiens ont des maîtres. Les chats ont des employés.
translations.pt: Os cães têm donos. Os gatos têm empregados.

examples.text: You're the master of your own destiny.

translations.de: Du bist der Herr deines Schicksals.
translations.fr: Tu es le maître de ton propre destin.
translations.pt: Você é o mestre do seu próprio destino.

examples.text: The dog followed its master, wagging its tail.

translations.de: Der Hund folgte seinem Herrchen und wackelte mit dem Schwanz.
translations.fr: Le chien suivit son maître en agitant la queue.
translations.pt: O cachorro seguiu o seu dono balançando sua calda.

more.definition: To be a master.; To become the master of; to subject to one's will, control, or authority; to conquer; to overpower; to subdue.; To learn to a high degree of proficiency.
more.etymology: Old French maistrebor. Latin magisterder. From Middle English maister, mayster, meister (noun) and maistren (verb), from Old English mǣster, mæġster, mæġester, mæġister, magister (“master”), from Latin magister (“chief, teacher, leader”), from Old Latin magester, from Proto-Indo-European *méǵh₂s (as in magnus (“great”), also cognate of English much and mickle) + -ester/-ister (compare minister (“servant”)).

examples.text: The town was destroyed during the war.

translations.de: Die Stadt wurde während des Krieges zerstört.
translations.fr: La ville fut détruite pendant la guerre.
translations.pt: A cidade foi destruída durante a guerra.

examples.text: Termites are destroying the houses.

translations.de: Termiten zerstören die Häuser.
translations.fr: Les termites détruisent les maisons.
translations.pt: Cupins estão destruindo as casas.

examples.text: If you want to be free, destroy your television set.

translations.de: Wenn du frei sein willst, zerstöre deinen Fernseher!
translations.fr: Si tu veux être libre, détruis ton téléviseur !
translations.pt: Se você quer ser livre, destrua sua televisão.

examples.text: The tide destroyed the sand castle.

translations.de: Die Flut zerstörte die Sandburg.
translations.fr: La marée a détruit le château de sable.
translations.pt: A maré destruiu o castelo de areia.

more.definition: To damage beyond use or repair; to damage (something) to the point that it effectively ceases to exist.; To neutralize, undo a property or condition.; To put down or euthanize.
more.etymology: From Middle English destroyen, from Old French destruire, Vulgar Latin *destrugō, from Classical Latin dēstruō, from dē- (“un-, de-”) + struō (“to build”).

examples.text: Our office is around the corner.

translations.de: Unser Büro ist gleich um die Ecke.
translations.fr: Notre bureau est juste au coin de la rue.
translations.pt: Nosso escritório fica perto da esquina.

examples.text: It's true that the earth is round.

translations.de: Es ist wahr, dass die Erde rund ist.
translations.fr: Il est vrai que la Terre est ronde.
translations.pt: É verdade que a Terra é redonda.

examples.text: The Earth rotates round the Sun.

translations.de: Die Erde dreht sich um die Sonne.
translations.fr: La Terre tourne autour du Soleil.
translations.pt: A terra gravita ao redor do sol.

examples.text: She's travelling around the world.

translations.de: Sie reist um die Welt.
translations.fr: Elle voyage autour du monde.
translations.pt: Ela está viajando ao redor do mundo.

more.definition: Circular or cylindrical; having a circular cross-section in one direction.; Spherical; shaped like a ball; having a circular cross-section in more than one direction.; Loosely or approximately circular.
more.etymology: From Middle English round, rounde, from Old Northern French roünt, rund, Old French ront, runt, reont ( > French rond), from both Late Latin retundus and the original Latin rotundus. The noun developed partly from the adjective and partly from the corresponding French noun rond. Doublet of rotund.

examples.text: I'll show you around the city.

translations.de: Ich werde dir die Stadt zeigen.
translations.fr: Je te ferai visiter la ville.
translations.pt: Eu te mostrarei a cidade.

examples.text: Did you buy a round-trip ticket?

translations.de: Hast du eine Rückfahrkarte gekauft?
translations.fr: As-tu acheté un billet aller-retour ?
translations.pt: Você comprou uma passagem de ida e vinda?

examples.text: Is there a post office around here?

translations.de: Gibt es hier in der Nähe eine Post?
translations.fr: Il y a un bureau de poste par ici ?
translations.pt: Há uma agência de correios aqui perto?

examples.text: The world doesn't revolve around you.

translations.de: Die Welt dreht sich auch ohne dich.
translations.fr: Le monde ne tourne pas autour de toi.
translations.pt: O mundo não gira ao redor de ti.

more.definition: A circular or spherical object or part of an object.; A circular or repetitious route.; A general outburst from a group of people at an event.
more.etymology: From Middle English round, rounde, from Old Northern French roünt, rund, Old French ront, runt, reont ( > French rond), from both Late Latin retundus and the original Latin rotundus. The noun developed partly from the adjective and partly from the corresponding French noun rond. Doublet of rotund.

examples.text: There's not a living soul around here.

translations.de: Hier ist keine Menschenseele.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas âme qui vive par ici.
translations.pt: Não há viva alma por aqui.

examples.text: Julian wears round glasses like John Lennon's.

translations.de: Julian trägt eine runde Brille wie John Lennon.
translations.fr: Julien porte des lunettes rondes à la John Lennon.
translations.pt: Julian usa óculos redondos como os de John Lennon.

examples.text: The gossip spread around the school like wildfire.

translations.de: Das Gerücht verbreitete sich an der Schule wie ein Lauffeuer.
translations.fr: Les potins se sont répandus dans l'école comme une traînée de poudre.
translations.pt: A fofoca se espalhou pela escola como um rastilho de pólvora.

examples.text: Things are not going to change around here.

translations.de: Hier wird sich nichts ändern.
translations.fr: Les choses ne vont pas changer, par ici.
translations.pt: As coisas não vão mudar por aqui.

more.definition: To shape something into a curve.; To become shaped into a curve.; To finish; to complete; to fill out; see also round out.
more.etymology: From Middle English round, rounde, from Old Northern French roünt, rund, Old French ront, runt, reont ( > French rond), from both Late Latin retundus and the original Latin rotundus. The noun developed partly from the adjective and partly from the corresponding French noun rond. Doublet of rotund.

examples.text: What do you have in your mouth?

translations.de: Was hast du im Mund?
translations.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu as dans la bouche ?
translations.pt: Que é que tu tens na boca?

examples.text: We eat with our mouths.

translations.de: Wir essen mit dem Mund.
translations.fr: Nous mangeons par la bouche.
translations.pt: Comemos com nossas bocas.

examples.text: He tried to kiss me on the mouth.

translations.de: Er hat versucht, mich auf den Mund zu küssen.
translations.fr: Il a essayé de m'embrasser sur la bouche.
translations.pt: Ele tentou me beijar na boca.

examples.text: You shouldn't speak with your mouth full.

translations.de: Du sollst nicht mit vollem Mund sprechen!
translations.fr: Tu n'es pas censé parler la bouche pleine.
translations.pt: Você não devia falar de boca cheia.

more.definition: The front opening of a creature through which food is ingested.; The end of a river out of which water flows into a sea or other large body of water; or the end of a tributary out of which water flows into a larger river.; An outlet, aperture or orifice.
more.etymology: From Middle English mouth, from Old English mūþ, from Proto-West Germanic *munþ, from Proto-Germanic *munþaz (“mouth”), from Proto-Indo-European *ment- (“to chew; jaw, mouth”).

examples.text: Why is your mouth so big?

translations.de: Wieso ist dein Mund so groß?
translations.fr: Pourquoi ta bouche est-elle si grande ?
translations.pt: Por que a sua boca é tão grande?

examples.text: The lion opened its huge mouth and roared.

translations.de: Der Löwe öffnete sein riesiges Maul und brüllte.
translations.fr: Le lion ouvrit sa gueule énorme et rugit.
translations.pt: O leão abriu sua enorme boca e rugiu.

examples.text: Breathe deeply through your mouth.

translations.de: Tief durch den Mund einatmen!
translations.fr: Respire profondément par la bouche.
translations.pt: Respire fundo pela boca.

examples.text: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth.

translations.de: Einem geschenkten Gaul schaut man nicht ins Maul.
translations.fr: À cheval donné on ne regarde pas la bride.
translations.pt: A cavalo dado não se olham os dentes.

more.definition: To speak; to utter.; To represent (words or sounds) by making the actions of speech, but silently, without producing sound; to frame.; To move the mouth, with or without sound; to form (air or words) with the mouth, with or without sound.
more.etymology: From Middle English mouth, from Old English mūþ, from Proto-West Germanic *munþ, from Proto-Germanic *munþaz (“mouth”), from Proto-Indo-European *ment- (“to chew; jaw, mouth”).

examples.text: I can prove that I am right.

translations.de: Ich kann beweisen, dass ich recht habe.
translations.fr: Je peux prouver que j'ai raison.
translations.pt: Posso provar que tenho razão.

examples.text: This fact proves her innocence.

translations.de: Dieser Fakt beweist ihre Unschuld.
translations.fr: Ce fait prouve son innocence.
translations.pt: Este fato prova sua inocência.

examples.text: Can you prove Tom didn't do it?

translations.de: Kannst du beweisen, daß Tom das nicht getan hat?
translations.fr: Peux-tu prouver que Tom ne l'a pas fait ?
translations.pt: Você pode provar que o Tom não fez isso?

examples.text: How can we prove it?

translations.de: Wie können wir es beweisen?
translations.fr: Comment pouvons-nous le prouver ?
translations.pt: Como podemos provar isso?

more.definition: The process of dough proofing.
more.etymology: From Middle English proven, from Old English prōfian (“to esteem, regard as, evince, try, prove”) and Old French prover (“to prove”), both from Latin probō (“test, try, examine, approve, show to be good or fit, prove”, verb), from probus (“good, worthy, excellent”), from Proto-Indo-European *pro-bʰuH-s (“being in front, prominent”), from *pro-, *per- (“toward”) + *bʰuH- (“to be”).

examples.text: Has that been scientifically proven?

translations.de: Ist das wissenschaftlich erwiesen?
translations.fr: Est-ce que c'est scientifiquement prouvé ?
translations.pt: Isso foi comprovado cientificamente?

examples.text: How can I prove it?

translations.de: Wie kann ich es beweisen?
translations.fr: Comment puis-je le prouver ?
translations.pt: Como posso prová-lo?

examples.text: The exception proves the rule.

translations.de: Ausnahmen bestätigen die Regel.
translations.fr: L'exception confirme la règle.
translations.pt: A exceção confirma a regra.

examples.text: He proved to be an ideal husband.

translations.de: Er stellte sich als idealer Ehemann heraus.
translations.fr: Il s'avéra être un mari idéal.
translations.pt: Ele provou ser um marido ideal.

more.definition: To demonstrate that something is true or viable; to give proof for; to bear out; to testify.; To turn out; to manifest.; To turn out to be.
more.etymology: From Middle English proven, from Old English prōfian (“to esteem, regard as, evince, try, prove”) and Old French prover (“to prove”), both from Latin probō (“test, try, examine, approve, show to be good or fit, prove”, verb), from probus (“good, worthy, excellent”), from Proto-Indo-European *pro-bʰuH-s (“being in front, prominent”), from *pro-, *per- (“toward”) + *bʰuH- (“to be”).

examples.text: Did you think I wouldn't notice?

translations.de: Dachtest du, ich würde das nicht bemerken?
translations.fr: Tu pensais que je ne le remarquerais pas ?
translations.pt: Você pensou que eu não notaria?

examples.text: I didn't notice Tom had gone.

translations.de: Ich hatte nicht bemerkt, dass Tom gegangen war.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas remarqué que Tom était parti.
translations.pt: Não notei que o Tom tinha ido embora.

examples.text: He was too busy to notice it.

translations.de: Er war zu beschäftigt, um es zu bemerken.
translations.fr: Il était trop occupé pour le remarquer.
translations.pt: Ele estava muito ocupado para perceber.

examples.text: She was the first one to notice him.

translations.de: Sie war die Erste, die ihn bemerkt hat.
translations.fr: Elle a été la première à le remarquer.
translations.pt: Ela foi a primeira que o notou.

more.definition: The act of observing; perception.; A written or printed announcement.; A formal notification or warning.
more.etymology: Borrowed from Middle French notice, from the Latin nōtitia. Doublet of notitia.

examples.text: I noticed him sneak into the room.

translations.de: Ich bemerkte, wie er ins Zimmer schlich.
translations.fr: Je l'ai vu se faufiler dans la pièce.
translations.pt: Eu o vi entrar furtivamente no aposento.

examples.text: He will notice sooner or later.

translations.de: Er wird es früher oder später merken.
translations.fr: Il le remarquera tôt ou tard.
translations.pt: Ele vai perceber, cedo ou tarde.

examples.text: I should have noticed it before.

translations.de: Ich hätte das eher bemerken müssen.
translations.fr: J'aurais dû le remarquer avant.
translations.pt: Eu deveria ter notado isso antes.

examples.text: I've never noticed that before.

translations.de: Das habe ich noch nie bemerkt.
translations.fr: Je n'avais jamais remarqué ça avant.
translations.pt: Nunca havia notado isso antes.

more.definition: To become aware of; to observe.; To be noticeable; to show.; To perceive Jewish influence or responsibility.
more.etymology: Borrowed from Middle French notice, from the Latin nōtitia. Doublet of notitia.

examples.text: None of the girls are students.

translations.de: Keins dieser Mädchen ist Studentin.
translations.fr: Aucune de ces filles n'est étudiante.
translations.pt: Nenhuma das garotas é estudante.

examples.text: Do you have a non-smoking section?

translations.de: Haben Sie einen Nichtraucherbereich?
translations.fr: Avez-vous un coin non-fumeur ?
translations.pt: Têm uma área para não fumadores?

examples.text: None of us want that.

translations.de: Keiner von uns will das.
translations.fr: Aucun d'entre nous ne le veut.
translations.pt: Nenhum de nós quer isso.

examples.text: Tom made a lot of suggestions, but none of them were very good.

translations.de: Tom machte eine Menge Vorschläge, aber keiner dieser war sonderlich gut.
translations.fr: Tom a fait beaucoup de suggestions, mais aucune d'elles n'était très bonne.
translations.pt: O Tom fez muitas sugestões, mas nenhuma delas era muito boa.

more.definition: To no extent, in no way.; Not at all, not very.
more.etymology: From Middle English none, noon, non (“not one”), from Old English nān (“not one, not any, none”), from Proto-West Germanic *nain, from Proto-Germanic *nainaz (“none, nought, nothing”), equivalent to ne (“not”) + one.

examples.text: That's none of your business.

translations.de: Das ist nicht deine Sache.
translations.fr: Cela ne vous regarde pas.
translations.pt: Isso não lhe diz respeito.

examples.text: It's none of your business.

translations.de: Das geht dich nichts an.
translations.fr: Ce ne sont pas tes oignons.
translations.pt: Não é da sua conta.

examples.text: He is second to none in physics.

translations.de: In Physik ist er unübertroffen.
translations.fr: Il n'a pas son pareil en physique.
translations.pt: Ele é sem igual em física.

examples.text: He was none other than the king.

translations.de: Er war kein Anderer als der König.
translations.fr: Il n'était rien d'autre que le roi.
translations.pt: Ele era ninguém mais que o rei.

more.definition: Not any; no (usually used only before a vowel or h).
more.etymology: From Middle English none, noon, non (“not one”), from Old English nān (“not one, not any, none”), from Proto-West Germanic *nain, from Proto-Germanic *nainaz (“none, nought, nothing”), equivalent to ne (“not”) + one.

examples.text: None of the old trees survived the fire.

translations.de: Keiner der alten Bäume überstand das Feuer.
translations.fr: Aucun des vieux arbres ne survécut à l'incendie.
translations.pt: Nenhuma das árvores velhas sobreviveu ao incêndio.

examples.text: She wanted a piece of cake, but there was none left.

translations.de: Sie wollte ein Stück Kuchen, aber es gab keinen mehr.
translations.fr: Elle voulait un morceau de gâteau mais il n'y en avait plus.
translations.pt: Ela queria um pedaço de bolo, mas não tinha mais.

examples.text: None of my friends drink coffee.

translations.de: Keiner meiner Freunde trinkt Kaffee.
translations.fr: Aucun de mes amis ne boit de café.
translations.pt: Nenhum dos meus amigos bebe café.

examples.text: None of this is true.

translations.de: Nichts davon ist wahr.
translations.fr: Rien de cela n'est vrai.
translations.pt: Nada disso é verdade.

more.definition: A person without religious affiliation.
more.etymology: From the first sense, since they respond “none” when asked about their religion; also a play on words on nun.

examples.text: I know none of them.

translations.de: Ich kenne keine von ihnen.
translations.fr: Je ne connais aucune d'elles.
translations.pt: Não conheço nenhum deles.

examples.text: What's your favorite non-alcoholic beverage?

translations.de: Was ist dein liebstes nichtalkoholisches Getränk?
translations.fr: Quelle est ta boisson non-alcoolisée préférée ?
translations.pt: Qual é a sua bebida não alcoólica preferida?

examples.text: None of us can speak French.

translations.de: Von uns kann keiner Französisch.
translations.fr: Aucun d'entre nous ne sait parler français.
translations.pt: Nenhum de nós fala francês.

examples.text: None of this makes any sense.

translations.de: Nichts hiervon ergibt irgendeinen Sinn.
translations.fr: Rien de ceci n'a de sens.
translations.pt: Nada disso faz sentido.

more.definition: Not any of a given number or group.; No one, nobody.; No person.
more.etymology: From Middle English none, noon, non (“not one”), from Old English nān (“not one, not any, none”), from Proto-West Germanic *nain, from Proto-Germanic *nainaz (“none, nought, nothing”), equivalent to ne (“not”) + one.

examples.text: I speak Esperanto very badly.

translations.de: Ich spreche sehr schlecht Esperanto.
translations.fr: Je parle très mal l'espéranto.
translations.pt: Falo muito mal o Esperanto.

examples.text: We will miss you badly.

translations.de: Ihr werdet uns schrecklich fehlen.
translations.fr: Tu vas cruellement nous manquer.
translations.pt: Sentiremos muito a sua falta.

examples.text: I'm badly wounded.

translations.de: Ich bin schwer verwundet.
translations.fr: Je suis gravement blessé.
translations.pt: Estou gravemente ferido.

examples.text: I'm bleeding badly.

translations.de: Ich blute stark.
translations.fr: Je saigne gravement.
translations.pt: Eu estou sangrando gravemente.

more.definition: Ill, unwell.
more.etymology: From Middle English badly, baddely, baddeliche, equivalent to bad + -ly.

examples.text: Tom's bag was badly damaged.

translations.de: Toms Tasche war schwer beschädigt.
translations.fr: Le sac de Tom était très endommagé.
translations.pt: A bolsa do Tom foi seriamente danificada.

examples.text: I must have expressed myself badly.

translations.de: Ich muss mich schlecht ausgedrückt haben.
translations.fr: J'ai dû mal m'exprimer.
translations.pt: Eu devo ter me expressado mal.

examples.text: I am badly in need of your help.

translations.de: Ich brauche dringend Ihre Hilfe.
translations.fr: J'ai vraiment besoin de ton aide.
translations.pt: Eu preciso muito da sua ajuda.

examples.text: They really sing very badly!

translations.de: Sie singen wirklich sehr schlecht!
translations.fr: Ils chantent vraiment très mal !
translations.pt: Eles realmente cantam muito mal!

more.definition: In a bad manner.; Very much; to a great degree.
more.etymology: From Middle English badly, baddely, baddeliche, equivalent to bad + -ly.

examples.text: The school is farther than the station.

translations.de: Die Schule ist weiter weg als der Bahnhof.
translations.fr: L'école est plus loin que la gare.
translations.pt: A escola fica mais longe do que a estação.

examples.text: Can you give me directions to the station?

translations.de: Können Sie mir sagen, wie ich zum Bahnhof komme?
translations.fr: Pouvez-vous me donner des indications pour aller à la gare ?
translations.pt: O senhor pode me dar instruções para a estação?

examples.text: The train station is not far from here.

translations.de: Der Bahnhof ist nicht weit von hier.
translations.fr: La gare n'est pas loin d'ici.
translations.pt: A estação ferroviária não fica longe daqui.

examples.text: The station was empty because it was Sunday.

translations.de: Auf dem Bahnhof war nichts los, weil Sonntag war.
translations.fr: La gare était vide parce que c'était dimanche.
translations.pt: A estação estava vazia porque era domingo.

more.definition: A regular stopping place for ground transportation.; A ground transportation depot.; A place where one stands or stays or is assigned to stand or stay.
more.etymology: From Middle English stacioun, borrowed from Anglo-Norman estation, from Latin statiōnem, accusative of statiō (“standing, post, job, position”), whence also Italian stazione. Doublet of stagione. Cognate with Ancient Greek ἵστημι (hístēmi), στάσις (stásis), Old English standan (whence English stand).

examples.text: I bumped into him at the station.

translations.de: Ich stieß zufällig am Bahnhof auf ihn.
translations.fr: Je l'ai croisé à la gare.
translations.pt: Eu trombei com ele na estação.

examples.text: Is there a bank near the station?

translations.de: Gibt es in der Nähe des Bahnhofs eine Bank?
translations.fr: Y a-t-il une banque proche de la gare ?
translations.pt: Tem um banco perto da estação?

examples.text: I'll accompany you to the station.

translations.de: Ich begleite dich bis zum Bahnhof.
translations.fr: Je vais t'accompagner jusqu'à la gare.
translations.pt: Eu o acompanharei até a estação.

examples.text: We got to the station at six.

translations.de: Wir kamen um sechs Uhr am Bahnhof an.
translations.fr: Nous sommes arrivés à la gare à 6 heures.
translations.pt: Chegamos na estação às seis.

more.definition: To put in place to perform a task.; To put in place to perform military duty.; To play in the manner of a calling station.
more.etymology: From Middle English stacioun, borrowed from Anglo-Norman estation, from Latin statiōnem, accusative of statiō (“standing, post, job, position”), whence also Italian stazione. Doublet of stagione. Cognate with Ancient Greek ἵστημι (hístēmi), στάσις (stásis), Old English standan (whence English stand).

examples.text: I don't want to say goodbye to you.

translations.de: Ich möchte mich nicht von dir verabschieden.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas te dire adieu.
translations.pt: Eu não quero dizer-te adeus.

examples.text: She left without saying goodbye.

translations.de: Sie ging, ohne sich zu verabschieden.
translations.fr: Elle s'en alla sans dire au revoir.
translations.pt: Ela foi embora sem se despedir.

examples.text: Go and say goodbye to him before he leaves.

translations.de: Geh ihm „Auf Wiedersehen“ sagen, bevor er weg ist.
translations.fr: Va lui dire au revoir avant qu'il ne s'en aille.
translations.pt: Vá dizer adeus para ele antes que ele vá embora.

examples.text: I have to say goodbye.

translations.de: Ich muss auf Wiedersehen sagen.
translations.fr: Il me faut dire au revoir.
translations.pt: Eu tenho que me despedir.

more.definition: Farewell; a formula used to another person or persons when the speaker, writer, or person addressed is departing.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *wíterosder. Old English wiþerclip. Proto-Indo-European *uswísder. English goodinflu. From earlier goodby, Godby, Godby'e, Godbwye, God b'w'y, God bwy yee, God buy you, God be wi' you, each a progressively shorter contraction of God be with ye or God be with you. Note the change of God to good by confusion with good morning, good night, etc. Modernly analysed as good + bye.

examples.text: Do you want to say goodbye?

translations.de: Willst du auf Wiedersehen sagen?
translations.fr: Voulez-vous dire au revoir ?
translations.pt: Você quer dizer adeus?

examples.text: I'd like to say goodbye.

translations.de: Ich möchte mich verabschieden.
translations.fr: J'aimerais prendre congé.
translations.pt: Eu gostaria de dizer adeus.

examples.text: Don't leave without saying goodbye.

translations.de: Gehe nicht, ohne dich zu verabschieden.
translations.fr: Ne partez pas sans dire au revoir.
translations.pt: Não vá embora sem dizer adeus.

examples.text: Go say goodbye to Tom.

translations.de: Verabschiede dich von Tom!
translations.fr: Va dire au revoir à Tom.
translations.pt: Vá se despedir de Tom.

more.definition: An utterance of goodbye, the wishing of farewell to someone.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *wíterosder. Old English wiþerclip. Proto-Indo-European *uswísder. English goodinflu. From earlier goodby, Godby, Godby'e, Godbwye, God b'w'y, God bwy yee, God buy you, God be wi' you, each a progressively shorter contraction of God be with ye or God be with you. Note the change of God to good by confusion with good morning, good night, etc. Modernly analysed as good + bye.

examples.text: I just dropped in to say goodbye.

translations.de: Ich bin nur gekommen, um »Tschüß« zu sagen.
translations.fr: Je suis venue simplement pour dire adieu.
translations.pt: Eu só parei para falar tchau.

examples.text: We've said our goodbyes.

translations.de: Wir haben uns verabschiedet.
translations.fr: Nous dîmes nos adieux.
translations.pt: Nós nos despedimos.

examples.text: It's time to say goodbye.

translations.de: Es ist Zeit, uns zu verabschieden.
translations.fr: Il est venu le temps de faire nos adieux.
translations.pt: Chegou a hora de dizer adeus.

examples.text: He didn't even say goodbye.

translations.de: Er verabschiedete sich nicht einmal.
translations.fr: Il n'a même pas dit au revoir.
translations.pt: Ele nem sequer se despediu.

more.definition: To say goodbye; to wish somebody farewell on parting.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *wíterosder. Old English wiþerclip. Proto-Indo-European *uswísder. English goodinflu. From earlier goodby, Godby, Godby'e, Godbwye, God b'w'y, God bwy yee, God buy you, God be wi' you, each a progressively shorter contraction of God be with ye or God be with you. Note the change of God to good by confusion with good morning, good night, etc. Modernly analysed as good + bye.

examples.text: I want to buy some dark glasses.

translations.de: Ich will eine Sonnenbrille kaufen.
translations.fr: Je veux acheter des lunettes noires.
translations.pt: Quero comprar óculos escuros.

examples.text: It's getting darker and darker.

translations.de: Es wird immer dunkler.
translations.fr: Il fait de plus en plus sombre.
translations.pt: Está escurecendo cada vez mais.

examples.text: It was a dark and stormy night.

translations.de: Es war eine dunkle und stürmische Nacht.
translations.fr: C'était une nuit sombre et tempétueuse.
translations.pt: Foi uma noite sombria e tempestuosa.

examples.text: She is very afraid of the dark.

translations.de: Sie hat große Angst vor der Dunkelheit.
translations.fr: Elle a très peur du noir.
translations.pt: Ela tem muito medo do escuro.

more.definition: Having an absolute or (more often) relative lack of light.; Extinguished.; Deprived of sight; blind.
more.etymology: From Middle English derk, from Old English deorc, from Proto-West Germanic *derk (“dark”), of uncertain origin, but possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dʰerg- (“dim, dull”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰer- (“dull, dirty”).

examples.text: A dog can see in the dark.

translations.de: Ein Hund kann im Dunkeln sehen.
translations.fr: Un chien peut voir dans l'obscurité.
translations.pt: Os cachorros enxergam no escuro.

examples.text: All cats are grey in the dark.

translations.de: Nachts sind alle Katzen grau.
translations.fr: La nuit tous les chats sont gris.
translations.pt: Todos os gatos são cinza no escuro.

examples.text: Why is the smoke dark grey?

translations.de: Warum ist der Rauch dunkelgrau?
translations.fr: Pourquoi la fumée est-elle gris foncé ?
translations.pt: Por que a fumaça é cinza escuro?

examples.text: It's much too dark to play tennis.

translations.de: Es ist viel zu dunkel zum Tennisspielen.
translations.fr: Il fait bien trop sombre pour jouer au tennis.
translations.pt: Está escuro demais para jogar tênis.

more.definition: A complete or (more often) partial absence of light.; Ignorance.; Nightfall.
more.etymology: From Middle English derk, derke, dirke, dyrke, from the adjective (see above), or possibly from an unrecorded Old English *dierce, *diercu (“dark, darkness”).

examples.text: The sky got dark, and it started raining.

translations.de: Der Himmel verdunkelte sich, und es fing an zu regnen.
translations.fr: Le ciel s'est assombri et il s'est mis à pleuvoir.
translations.pt: O céu ficou escuro e começou a chover.

examples.text: I have to go. It's getting dark.

translations.de: Ich muß los. Es wird schon dunkel.
translations.fr: Je dois y aller. Il se met à faire noir.
translations.pt: Tenho que ir. Está ficando escuro.

examples.text: It's very dark in here.

translations.de: Es ist sehr dunkel hier drin.
translations.fr: Il fait très sombre ici.
translations.pt: Está muito escuro aqui.

examples.text: The room was dark and cold.

translations.de: Das Zimmer war dunkel und kalt.
translations.fr: La pièce était sombre et froide.
translations.pt: O quarto era escuro e frio.

more.definition: To grow or become dark, darken.; To remain in the dark, lurk, lie hidden or concealed.; To make dark, darken; to obscure.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English derken, from Old English deorcian, from Proto-West Germanic *derkōn, from *derk (“dirty, dark”) + *-ōn.

examples.text: I want to go to the park.

translations.de: Ich möchte in den Park gehen.
translations.fr: Je veux aller au parc.
translations.pt: Eu quero ir ao parque.

examples.text: There are many parks in our town.

translations.de: Es gibt viele Parks in unserer Stadt.
translations.fr: Il y a beaucoup de parcs dans notre ville.
translations.pt: Há muitos parques em nossa cidade.

examples.text: What're you doing in this park?

translations.de: Was machst du in diesem Park?
translations.fr: Que faites-vous dans ce parc ?
translations.pt: O que você está fazendo neste parque?

examples.text: I'm going to park the car.

translations.de: Ich werde das Auto parken.
translations.fr: Je vais garer la voiture.
translations.pt: Eu vou estacionar o carro.

more.definition: A tract of ground kept in its natural state, about or adjacent to a residence, such as for the preservation of game, for walking, riding, or the like.; A piece of ground in or near a city or town, enclosed and kept for ornament and recreation.; An enclosed parcel of land stocked with animals for hunting, which one may have by prescription or royal grant.
more.etymology: Old French parcbor. From Middle English park, from Old French parc (“livestock pen”), from Medieval Latin parcus, parricus, from Frankish *parrik (“enclosure, pen, fence”).

examples.text: I used to live near a park.

translations.de: Ich wohnte einmal neben einem Park.
translations.fr: J'habitais près d'un parc.
translations.pt: Eu morava perto de um parque.

examples.text: Ask him where he parked his car.

translations.de: Frag ihn, wo er sein Auto geparkt hat.
translations.fr: Demande-lui où il a garé sa voiture.
translations.pt: Pergunte-lhe onde estacionou seu carro.

examples.text: Tom went to the park with Mary.

translations.de: Tom ist mit Mary in den Park gegangen.
translations.fr: Tom est allé au parc avec Marie.
translations.pt: O Tom foi para o parque com a Mary.

examples.text: You can't park your car here.

translations.de: Hier können Sie Ihr Auto nicht parken.
translations.fr: Vous ne pouvez garer votre véhicule ici.
translations.pt: Você não pode estacionar seu carro aqui.

more.definition: To bring (something such as a vehicle) to a halt or store in a specified place.; To defer (a matter) until a later date.; To bring together in a park, or compact body.
more.etymology: Old French parcbor. From Middle English park, from Old French parc (“livestock pen”), from Medieval Latin parcus, parricus, from Frankish *parrik (“enclosure, pen, fence”).

examples.text: He killed the old lady just for kicks.

translations.de: Er hat die alte Dame einfach so zum Spaß getötet.
translations.fr: Il a tué la vieille dame juste pour le plaisir.
translations.pt: Ele matou a velha senhora por curtição.

examples.text: I’m going to kick his butt.

translations.de: Dem werde ich in den Hintern treten.
translations.fr: Je vais lui botter les fesses.

examples.text: That's like a kick in the nuts.

translations.de: Das ist wie ein Tritt in die Eier.
translations.fr: C'est comme un coup de pied dans les parties.

examples.text: She gave him a good kick.

translations.de: Sie gab ihm einen ordentlichen Tritt.
translations.fr: Elle lui a donné un bon coup de pied.

more.definition: A hit or strike with the leg, foot or knee.; The action of swinging a foot or leg.; A kicking motion used in a swim stroke.
more.etymology: From Middle English kyken (“to strike out with the foot”), from Old Norse kikna (“to sink at the knees”) and keikja (“to bend backwards”) (compare Old Norse keikr (“bent backwards, the belly jutting forward”)), from Proto-Germanic *kaikaz (“bent backwards”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Germanic *kī-, *kij- (“to split, dodge, swerve sidewards”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵeyH- (“to sprout, shoot”).

examples.text: My father kicked me out of the house.

translations.de: Mein Vater warf mich aus dem Haus.
translations.fr: Mon père m'a mis à la porte.
translations.pt: Meu pai me expulsou da casa.

examples.text: Tom is kicking the ball.

translations.de: Tom tritt den Ball.
translations.fr: Tom donne un coup de pied dans le ballon.
translations.pt: O Tom chuta a bola.

examples.text: He killed the old lady just for kicks.

translations.de: Er hat die alte Dame einfach so zum Spaß getötet.
translations.fr: Il a tué la vieille dame juste pour le plaisir.
translations.pt: Ele matou a velha senhora por curtição.

examples.text: Who kicked this ball?

translations.de: Wer hat diesen Ball getreten?
translations.fr: Qui a tapé ce ballon ?
translations.pt: Quem chutou esta bola?

more.definition: To strike or hit with the foot or other extremity of the leg.; To make a sharp jerking movement of the leg, as to strike something.; To direct to a particular place by a blow with the foot or leg.
more.etymology: From Middle English kyken (“to strike out with the foot”), from Old Norse kikna (“to sink at the knees”) and keikja (“to bend backwards”) (compare Old Norse keikr (“bent backwards, the belly jutting forward”)), from Proto-Germanic *kaikaz (“bent backwards”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Germanic *kī-, *kij- (“to split, dodge, swerve sidewards”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵeyH- (“to sprout, shoot”).

examples.text: Skunks fear neither dogs, nor men.

translations.de: Stinktiere fürchten weder Hunde noch Menschen.
translations.fr: Les mouffettes n'ont pas peur des chiens ou des humains.
translations.pt: Os gambás não têm medo de cachorros, nem de homens.

examples.text: Fear not because there is nothing to fear.

translations.de: Fürchte nichts, denn es gibt nichts zu fürchten.
translations.fr: Ne crains rien car il n'y a rien à craindre.
translations.pt: Não tema a nada, porque não há nada a temer.

examples.text: The girl was trembling with fear.

translations.de: Das Mädchen zitterte vor Angst.
translations.fr: La fille tremblait de peur.
translations.pt: A menina estava tremendo de medo.

examples.text: Fools rush in where angels fear to tread.

translations.de: Narren stürzen sich auf etwas, wovor Engel zurückschrecken.
translations.fr: Les fous se précipitent là où les anges craignent de mettre les pieds.
translations.pt: Os tolos se apressam a entrar onde os anjos têm receio de pisar.

more.etymology: From Middle English fere, feore, from Old English fēre (“able to go, fit for service”), from Proto-Germanic *fēriz (“passable”), from Proto-Indo-European *per- (“to put across, ferry”). Cognate with Scots fere, feir (“well, active, sound”), Middle High German gevüere (“able, capable, fit, serviceable”), Swedish för (“capable, able, stout”), Icelandic fær (“able”). Related to fare.

examples.text: I fear we are too late.

translations.de: Ich fürchte, wir kommen zu spät.
translations.fr: Je crains que nous n'arrivions trop tard.
translations.pt: Acho que chegamos tarde demais.

examples.text: Why I should fear death?

translations.de: Warum sollte ich den Tod fürchten?
translations.fr: Pourquoi devrais-je craindre la mort ?
translations.pt: Por que eu deveria temer a morte?

examples.text: What's your biggest fear?

translations.de: Wovor hast du am meisten Angst?
translations.fr: Quelle est ta plus grosse crainte ?
translations.pt: Qual é o seu maior medo?

examples.text: Tom doesn't fear death.

translations.de: Tom fürchtet sich nicht vorm Tod.
translations.fr: Tom n'a pas peur de mourir.
translations.pt: O Tom não teme a morte.

more.definition: A strong, unpleasant emotion or feeling caused by actual or perceived danger or threat.; A phobia, a sense of fear induced by something or someone in particular.; Something one is afraid of; the object of one’s fear.
more.etymology: From Middle English feer, fere, fer (“fear”), from Old English fǣr, ġefǣr (“calamity, sudden danger, peril, sudden attack, terrible sight”), from Proto-Germanic *fērō, *fērą (“danger”), from Proto-Indo-European *per- (“to go through, carry forth, try”).

examples.text: Hope is more powerful than fear.

translations.de: Hoffnung ist mächtiger als Angst.
translations.fr: L'espoir est plus puissant que la peur.
translations.pt: A esperança é mais poderosa que o medo.

examples.text: Many fears are born of fatigue and loneliness.

translations.de: Viele Befürchtungen sind die Folge von Erschöpfung und Einsamkeit.
translations.fr: De nombreuses craintes naissent de l'épuisement et de la solitude.
translations.pt: Muitos medos nascem da fadiga e da solidão.

examples.text: Tom preferred to be loved rather than to be feared.

translations.de: Tom wollte lieber geliebt als gefürchtet werden.
translations.fr: Tom préférait être aimé plutôt qu'être craint.
translations.pt: Tom preferia ser amado a ser temido.

examples.text: I fear we're too late.

translations.de: Ich fürchte, wir kommen zu spät.
translations.fr: Je crains que nous n'arrivions trop tard.
translations.pt: Acho que chegamos tarde demais.

more.definition: To be afraid of (something or someone); to consider or expect (something or someone) with alarm.; To feel fear.; To worry about, to feel concern for, to be afraid for [with for].
more.etymology: From Middle English feer, fere, fer (“fear”), from Old English fǣr, ġefǣr (“calamity, sudden danger, peril, sudden attack, terrible sight”), from Proto-Germanic *fērō, *fērą (“danger”), from Proto-Indo-European *per- (“to go through, carry forth, try”).

examples.text: What time will Tom arrive in Boston?

translations.de: Wann kommt Tom in Boston an?
translations.fr: À quelle heure Tom arrivera-t-il à Boston ?
translations.pt: A que horas Tom chegará a Boston?

examples.text: Thanks to you, I arrived on time.

translations.de: Dank dir kam ich pünktlich an.
translations.fr: Grâce à toi, je suis arrivé à l'heure.
translations.pt: Graças a vocês, cheguei no horário.

examples.text: He was the last person to arrive.

translations.de: Er war die letzte Person, die ankam.
translations.fr: Il fut le dernier à arriver.
translations.pt: Ele foi a última pessoa a chegar.

examples.text: We'll arrive there within an hour.

translations.de: Binnen einer Stunde sind wir da.
translations.fr: Nous y arriverons en moins d'une heure.
translations.pt: Nós chegaremos lá daqui a uma hora.

more.definition: To reach; to get to a certain place.; To obtain a level of success or fame; to succeed.; To come; said of time.
more.etymology: From Middle English arriven, ariven, from Old French ariver, from Early Medieval Latin adrīpāre (“to land, come ashore”), derived from Latin rīpa (“shore, river-bank”). Displaced native oncome, tocome. For the semantic evolution, compare Old English ġelandian, ġelendan, lendan (“to arrive at land; land”) > Middle English alenden, landen (“to arrive; arrive at shore; land”).

examples.text: The wind blew all day.

translations.de: Der Wind wehte den ganzen Tag.
translations.fr: Le vent souffla tout le jour.
translations.pt: Ventou o dia todo.

examples.text: March winds and April showers bring forth May flowers.

translations.de: Winde im März und im April dann Regen bescheren im Mai einen Blumensegen.
translations.fr: Les vents de mars et les pluies d'avril laissent place aux fleurs de mai.
translations.pt: Os ventos de março e as chuvas de abril trazem depois as flores de maio.

examples.text: The wind is blowing hard.

translations.de: Es weht ein starker Wind.
translations.fr: Le vent souffle fortement.
translations.pt: Está ventando forte.

examples.text: The wind fanned the flames.

translations.de: Der Wind fachte die Flammen an.
translations.fr: Le vent a attisé les flammes.
translations.pt: O vento ateou o fogo.

more.definition: Real or perceived movement of atmospheric air usually caused by convection or differences in air pressure.; Air artificially put in motion by any force or action.; The ability to breathe easily.
more.etymology: From Middle English wynd, wind, from Old English wind (“wind”), from Proto-West Germanic *wind, from Proto-Germanic *windaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wéh₁n̥tos (“wind”), from earlier *h₂wéh₁n̥ts (“wind”), derived from the present participle of *h₂weh₁- (“to blow”).

examples.text: What is the direction of the wind?

translations.de: Wie ist die Windrichtung?
translations.fr: Quelle est la direction du vent ?
translations.pt: Qual é a direção do vento?

examples.text: The roof was torn off by strong winds.

translations.de: Das Dach wurde von starken Winden weggerissen.
translations.fr: Le toit fut arraché à cause des vents forts.
translations.pt: O telhado foi arrancado devido aos fortes ventos.

examples.text: Someday I'll run like the wind.

translations.de: Irgendwann werde ich wie der Wind rennen.
translations.fr: Un jour je courrai comme le vent.
translations.pt: Algum dia eu vou correr como o vento.

examples.text: Her long blond hair blew in the wind.

translations.de: Ihre langen blonden Haare wehten im Wind.
translations.fr: Ses longs cheveux blonds volaient au vent.
translations.pt: O vento agitava seus longos cabelos loiros.

more.definition: To blow air through a wind instrument or horn to make a sound.; To cause (someone) to become breathless, as by a blow to the abdomen, or by physical exertion, running, etc.; To cause a baby to bring up wind by patting its back after being fed.
more.etymology: From Middle English wynd, wind, from Old English wind (“wind”), from Proto-West Germanic *wind, from Proto-Germanic *windaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wéh₁n̥tos (“wind”), from earlier *h₂wéh₁n̥ts (“wind”), derived from the present participle of *h₂weh₁- (“to blow”).

examples.text: He's an excellent brain surgeon.

translations.de: Er ist ein großartiger Hirnchirurg.
translations.fr: C'est un excellent chirurgien du cerveau.
translations.pt: Ele é um excelente neurocirurgião.

examples.text: All human beings have brains.

translations.de: Alle Menschen haben ein Gehirn.
translations.fr: Tous les êtres humains ont un cerveau.
translations.pt: Todos os seres humanos têm cérebro.

examples.text: The brain needs a continuous supply of blood.

translations.de: Das Gehirn braucht kontinuierliche Blutzufuhr.
translations.fr: Le cerveau a besoin d'un afflux continu de sang.
translations.pt: O cérebro precisa de um suprimento contínuo de sangue.

examples.text: It's a brain-teaser.

translations.de: Das ist eine Knobelaufgabe.
translations.fr: C'est un casse-tête.
translations.pt: Isto é um quebra-cabeças.

more.definition: The control center of the central nervous system of an animal located in the skull, consisting of the cerebrum, cerebellum, and brainstem, which is responsible for perception, cognition, attention, memory, emotion, and action.; A part of the brain, especially associated with particular mental functions, abilities, etc.; Mind.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English brayn, from Old English bræġn, from Proto-West Germanic *bragn, from Proto-Germanic *bragną, from Proto-Indo-European *mrógʰ-n̥ ~ *mrégʰ-n̥-s, from *mregʰ- + *-n̥.

examples.text: The brain is just a complicated machine.

translations.de: Das Gehirn ist nur eine komplizierte Maschine.
translations.fr: Le cerveau n'est qu'une machine compliquée.
translations.pt: O cérebro é somente uma máquina complicada.

examples.text: Hard studies make strong brains.

translations.de: Schwierige Studien stärken den Intellekt.
translations.fr: Les études difficiles renforcent l'intellect.
translations.pt: Estudos difíceis fazem cérebros fortes.

examples.text: The brain has a complex structure.

translations.de: Das Gehirn hat eine komplexe Struktur.
translations.fr: Le cerveau a une structure complexe.
translations.pt: O cérebro tem uma estrutura complexa.

examples.text: Make your brain work before talking!

translations.de: Erst Gehirn einschalten, dann denken!
translations.fr: Fais marcher ton cerveau, avant de parler !
translations.pt: Faça seu cérebro trabalhar antes de falar!

more.definition: To dash out the brains of; to kill by smashing the skull.; To strike (someone) on the head.; To destroy; to put an end to.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English brayn, from Old English bræġn, from Proto-West Germanic *bragn, from Proto-Germanic *bragną, from Proto-Indo-European *mrógʰ-n̥ ~ *mrégʰ-n̥-s, from *mregʰ- + *-n̥.

examples.text: The shop stays open all day.

translations.de: Der Laden ist den ganzen Tag offen.
translations.fr: Le magasin reste ouvert toute la journée.
translations.pt: A loja fica aberta o dia todo.

examples.text: I live next door to the toy shop.

translations.de: Ich wohne in der Nähe des Spielzeugladens.
translations.fr: J'habite juste à côté du magasin de jouets.
translations.pt: Moro ao lado da loja de brinquedos.

examples.text: Is there a photo shop in the hotel?

translations.de: Gibt es in dem Hotel ein Fotogeschäft?
translations.fr: Y a-t-il un photographe dans l'hôtel ?
translations.pt: Há uma loja de fotografia no hotel?

examples.text: There's a book shop across from my house.

translations.de: Bei mir gibt es auf der anderen Straßenseite eine Buchhandlung.
translations.fr: Il y a une librairie en face de chez moi.
translations.pt: Há uma livraria em frente à minha casa.

more.etymology: From Middle English shoppe, schoppe, from Old English sċoppa (“shed; booth; stall; shop”), from Proto-Germanic *skupp-, *skup- (“barn, shed”), from Proto-Indo-European *skub-, *skup- (“to bend, bow, curve, vault”). Cognate with Dutch schop (“shed”), German Schuppen (“shed”), German Schober (“barn”), French échoppe (“booth, shop”) (< Germanic). The verb is denominal.

examples.text: Is there a shop at this zoo?

translations.de: Gibt es ein Geschäft in diesem Zoo?
translations.fr: Il y a un magasin dans ce zoo ?
translations.pt: Tem uma loja neste zoológico?

examples.text: It being Sunday, the shops were not open.

translations.de: Da Sonntag war, waren die Geschäfte nicht geöffnet.
translations.fr: Comme on était dimanche, les magasins n'étaient pas ouverts.
translations.pt: Sendo domingo, as lojas não estavam abertas.

examples.text: This used to be a butcher's shop.

translations.de: Das hier war einmal ein Fleischerladen.
translations.fr: C'était une boucherie avant.
translations.pt: Isto aqui era um açougue.

examples.text: I work in a flower shop.

translations.de: Ich arbeite in einem Blumenladen.
translations.fr: Je travaille chez un fleuriste.
translations.pt: Eu trabalho numa floricultura.

more.definition: An establishment that sells goods or services to the public; originally only a physical location, but now a virtual establishment as well.; A place where things are manufactured or crafted; a workshop.; A large garage where vehicle mechanics work.
more.etymology: From Middle English shoppe, schoppe, from Old English sċoppa (“shed; booth; stall; shop”), from Proto-Germanic *skupp-, *skup- (“barn, shed”), from Proto-Indo-European *skub-, *skup- (“to bend, bow, curve, vault”). Cognate with Dutch schop (“shed”), German Schuppen (“shed”), German Schober (“barn”), French échoppe (“booth, shop”) (< Germanic). The verb is denominal.

examples.text: This used to be a butcher shop.

translations.de: Das hier war einmal ein Fleischerladen.
translations.fr: C'était une boucherie avant.
translations.pt: Isto aqui era um açougue.

examples.text: Can you do some shopping for me?

translations.de: Könntest du für mich einkaufen gehen?
translations.fr: Pouvez-vous me faire les courses ?
translations.pt: Você pode fazer umas compras para mim?

examples.text: There are many expensive shops along the avenue.

translations.de: Entlang der Allee gibt es viele teure Geschäfte.
translations.fr: Il y a de nombreux magasins chers le long de l'avenue.
translations.pt: Há muitas lojas caras ao longo da avenida.

examples.text: Mom remained in the car while Dad shopped.

translations.de: Mama blieb im Auto, während Papa einkaufen ging.
translations.fr: Maman est restée dans la voiture pendant que papa faisait les courses.
translations.pt: A mamãe ficou no carro enquanto o papai fazia as compras.

more.definition: To visit stores or shops to browse or explore merchandise, especially with the intention of buying such merchandise.; To browse or purchase products from (a catalog, an internet website, etc.), mostly from home.; To report the criminal activities or whereabouts of someone to an authority.
more.etymology: From Middle English shoppe, schoppe, from Old English sċoppa (“shed; booth; stall; shop”), from Proto-Germanic *skupp-, *skup- (“barn, shed”), from Proto-Indo-European *skub-, *skup- (“to bend, bow, curve, vault”). Cognate with Dutch schop (“shed”), German Schuppen (“shed”), German Schober (“barn”), French échoppe (“booth, shop”) (< Germanic). The verb is denominal.

examples.text: What did he draw on the blackboard?

translations.de: Was hat er auf die Tafel gezeichnet?
translations.fr: Qu'a-t-il dessiné au tableau ?
translations.pt: O que ele desenhou no quadro?

examples.text: Let's draw a stone.

translations.de: Zeichnen wir einen Stein.
translations.fr: Dessinons une pierre.
translations.pt: Vamos desenhar uma pedra.

examples.text: Did you draw this yourself?

translations.de: Hast du das selbst gezeichnet?
translations.fr: C’est toi qui as dessiné ça ?
translations.pt: Você mesmo desenhou isto?

examples.text: I like to draw pictures.

translations.de: Ich zeichne gern.
translations.fr: J'aime dessiner.
translations.pt: Eu gosto de desenhar.

more.definition: Pull back your bowstring in preparation to shoot.
more.etymology: The verb is derived from Middle English dragen, draghen, draue, drauen, drauhen, drawe, drawen, draȝe, draȝen, draȝhenn (“to drag, pull; to draw (out); to attract; to entice, lure; to lead; to make a drawing; to move, travel; etc.”), from Old English dragan (“to drag, draw”), from Proto-West Germanic *dragan (“to carry, haul”), from Proto-Germanic *draganą (“to carry, draw, pull”); further etymology uncertain, often …

examples.text: It's hard to draw a circle without a compass.

translations.de: Es ist schwierig, ohne einen Zirkel einen Kreis zu zeichnen.
translations.fr: Il est difficile de tracer un cercle sans compas.
translations.pt: É difícil desenhar um círculo sem um compasso.

examples.text: Tom draws well.

translations.de: Tom zeichnet gut.
translations.fr: Tom dessine bien.
translations.pt: Tom desenha bem.

examples.text: Draw a line on the paper.

translations.de: Zeichne einen Strich auf das Papier.
translations.fr: Tracez une ligne sur le papier.
translations.pt: Desenhe uma linha no papel.

examples.text: I can't draw, but my sister is a great artist.

translations.de: Ich kann nicht zeichnen, aber meine Schwester ist eine große Künstlerin.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas dessiner, mais ma sœur est une grande artiste.
translations.pt: Eu não sei desenhar, mas minha irmã é uma grande artista.

more.definition: That which draws: that which attracts e.g. a crowd.; The act of drawing a gun from a holster, etc.; The procedure by which the result of a lottery is determined.
more.etymology: The verb is derived from Middle English dragen, draghen, draue, drauen, drauhen, drawe, drawen, draȝe, draȝen, draȝhenn (“to drag, pull; to draw (out); to attract; to entice, lure; to lead; to make a drawing; to move, travel; etc.”), from Old English dragan (“to drag, draw”), from Proto-West Germanic *dragan (“to carry, haul”), from Proto-Germanic *draganą (“to carry, draw, pull”); further etymology uncertain, often …

examples.text: What conclusions can be drawn from this?

translations.de: Welche Schlussfolgerungen lassen sich hieraus ziehen?
translations.fr: Quelles conclusions peut-on en tirer ?
translations.pt: Que conclusões podem ser tiradas disso?

examples.text: Could you draw a map for me?

translations.de: Könntest du mir eine Karte zeichnen?
translations.fr: Pourrais-tu me tracer une carte ?
translations.pt: Poderias desenhar um mapa para mim?

examples.text: A person who draws poorly is not an artist.

translations.de: Wer schlecht zeichnet, ist kein Künstler.
translations.fr: Celui qui dessine mal n’est pas un artiste.
translations.pt: Quem desenha mal não é artista.

examples.text: Our math teacher drew a circle on the blackboard.

translations.de: Unser Mathematiklehrer zeichnete einen Kreis auf die Tafel.
translations.fr: Notre professeur de mathématiques traça un cercle au tableau.
translations.pt: Nosso professor de matemática desenhou um círculo na lousa.

more.definition: To pull (someone or something) in a particular direction or manner.; To move (a body part) in a particular direction.; Often followed by tight: to pull (something, such as a belt or string) so that it tightens or wraps around something more closely.
more.etymology: The verb is derived from Middle English dragen, draghen, draue, drauen, drauhen, drawe, drawen, draȝe, draȝen, draȝhenn (“to drag, pull; to draw (out); to attract; to entice, lure; to lead; to make a drawing; to move, travel; etc.”), from Old English dragan (“to drag, draw”), from Proto-West Germanic *dragan (“to carry, haul”), from Proto-Germanic *draganą (“to carry, draw, pull”); further etymology uncertain, often …

examples.text: My mother is busy in the kitchen.

translations.de: Meine Mutter hat in der Küche zu tun.
translations.fr: Ma mère est occupée à la cuisine.
translations.pt: Minha mãe está ocupada na cozinha.

examples.text: She is as busy as a bee.

translations.de: Sie ist fleißig wie eine Biene.
translations.fr: Elle est très occupée.
translations.pt: Ela está muito ocupada.

examples.text: I'm too busy to help him.

translations.de: Ich bin zu beschäftigt, um ihm zu helfen.
translations.fr: Je suis trop occupé pour l'aider.
translations.pt: Estou muito ocupado para ajudá-lo.

examples.text: I know that she has been busy.

translations.de: Ich weiß, dass sie viel zu tun hatte.
translations.fr: Je sais qu'elle a été occupée.
translations.pt: Eu sei que ela tem estado ocupada.

more.definition: Crowded with business or activities; having a great deal going on.; Engaged with or preoccupied by an activity or person.; Having much work to do; having much to get done.
more.etymology: From Middle English bisy, busie, from Old English bisiġ (“busy, occupied, diligent”), from Proto-West Germanic *bisīg (“diligent; zealous; busy”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian biesich (“active, diligent, hard-working, industrious”), Dutch bezig (“busy”), Low German besig (“busy”).

examples.text: I'm not as busy as Tom.

translations.de: Ich bin nicht so beschäftigt wie Tom.
translations.fr: Je ne suis pas aussi occupé que Tom.
translations.pt: Não estou tão ocupado quanto o Tom.

examples.text: Tom said that he had been busy.

translations.de: Tom sagte, er sei beschäftigt gewesen.
translations.fr: Tom a dit qu'il était occupé.
translations.pt: Tom disse que tinha coisas para fazer.

examples.text: Tom told Mary that he was busy.

translations.de: Tom sagte Maria, dass er beschäftigt sei.
translations.fr: Tom a dit à Mary qu'il était occupé.
translations.pt: Tom disse a Maria que estava ocupado.

examples.text: Can't you see I'm busy?

translations.de: Siehst du nicht, dass ich beschäftigt bin?
translations.fr: Ne vois-tu pas que je suis occupé ?
translations.pt: Não está vendo que estou ocupado?

more.definition: A police officer.
more.etymology: From Middle English bisy, busie, from Old English bisiġ (“busy, occupied, diligent”), from Proto-West Germanic *bisīg (“diligent; zealous; busy”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian biesich (“active, diligent, hard-working, industrious”), Dutch bezig (“busy”), Low German besig (“busy”).

examples.text: I'm now busy writing a book.

translations.de: Ich bin gerade damit beschäftigt, ein Buch zu schreiben.
translations.fr: Je suis occupé en ce moment à écrire un livre.
translations.pt: Agora estou ocupado escrevendo um livro.

examples.text: I know that you're very busy, too.

translations.de: Ich weiß, dass du auch sehr beschäftigt bist.
translations.fr: Je sais que tu es très occupée, toi aussi.
translations.pt: Eu sei que você também está muito ocupado.

examples.text: I'm not busy at all.

translations.de: Ich bin gar nicht beschäftigt.
translations.fr: Je ne suis pas occupé du tout.
translations.pt: Não estou tão ocupado assim.

examples.text: You don't seem very busy.

translations.de: Du scheinst nicht sehr beschäftigt zu sein.
translations.fr: Tu n'as pas l'air très occupée.
translations.pt: Você não parece muito ocupado.

more.definition: To make somebody busy or active; to occupy.
more.etymology: From Middle English bisien, from Old English bisgian (“to occupy, employ, trouble, afflict”), from Proto-West Germanic *bisīgōn. Cognate with Old Frisian bisgia (“to use”).

examples.text: I'm too tired to do study.

translations.de: Ich bin zu müde zum Lernen.
translations.fr: Je suis trop fatigué pour étudier.
translations.pt: Estou cansado demais para estudar.

examples.text: I study at the University of Hyogo.

translations.de: Ich studiere an der Universität Hyōgo.
translations.fr: J'étudie à l'université de Hyogo.
translations.pt: Eu estudo na universidade de Hyogo.

examples.text: She went to Germany to study medicine.

translations.de: Sie ist nach Deutschland gegangen, um Medizin zu studieren.
translations.fr: Elle est allée en Allemagne pour étudier la médecine.
translations.pt: Ela foi para a Alemanha para estudar medicina.

examples.text: I study French in addition to English.

translations.de: Neben Englisch lerne ich Französisch.
translations.fr: J'étudie le français en plus de l'anglais.
translations.pt: Eu estudo francês além do inglês.

more.definition: Mental effort to acquire knowledge or learning.; The act of studying or examining; examination.; Any particular branch of learning that is studied; any object of attentive consideration.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English studie, from Old French estudie (Modern French étude), borrowed from Latin studium (“zeal, dedication, study”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tewd- (“to push, to hit”). Doublet of etude and studio.

examples.text: I'd like to study in Boston.

translations.de: Ich würde gerne in Boston studieren.
translations.fr: J'aimerais étudier à Boston.
translations.pt: Eu gostaria de estudar em Boston.

examples.text: I'm studying French and web design.

translations.de: Ich lerne Französisch und Webdesign.
translations.fr: Je suis en train d'étudier le français et le web design.
translations.pt: Estou estudando francês e web design.

examples.text: She studies, but doesn't learn.

translations.de: Sie studiert, lernt aber nicht.
translations.fr: Elle étudie, mais n'apprend pas.
translations.pt: Ela estuda, mas não aprende.

examples.text: I don't want to study French.

translations.de: Ich will kein Französisch studieren.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas étudier le français.
translations.pt: Eu não quero estudar francês.

more.definition: To review materials already learned in order to make sure one does not forget them, usually in preparation for an examination.; To take a course or courses on a subject.; To acquire knowledge on a subject with the intention of applying it in practice.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English studien, from Old French estudier (Modern French étudier), from estudie (noun), borrowed from Latin studium. Displaced Old English cneordlæcan.

examples.text: That's a crime against humanity!

translations.de: Das ist ein Verbrechen gegen die Menschheit!
translations.fr: C'est un crime contre l'humanité !
translations.pt: Isso é um crime contra a humanidade!

examples.text: He must pay for his crimes.

translations.de: Er muss für seine Verbrechen bezahlen.
translations.fr: Il doit payer pour ses crimes.
translations.pt: Ele deve pagar por seus crimes.

examples.text: It was a crime of passion.

translations.de: Es war ein Verbrechen aus Eifersucht.
translations.fr: C'était un crime passionnel.
translations.pt: Foi um crime passional.

examples.text: Torture is a crime against humanity.

translations.de: Folter ist ein Verbrechen gegen die Menschheit.
translations.fr: La torture est un crime contre l'humanité.
translations.pt: A tortura é um crime contra a humanidade.

more.definition: A specific act committed in violation of the law, especially criminal law.; Any great sin or wickedness; iniquity.; Criminal acts collectively.
more.etymology: From Middle English cryme, crime, from Old French crime, crimne, from Latin crīmen. Displaced native Old English firen.

examples.text: Genocide is a crime against humanity.

translations.de: Völkermord ist ein Verbrechen gegen die Menschheit.
translations.fr: Le génocide est un crime contre l'humanité.
translations.pt: Genocídio é um crime contra a humanidade.
