more.definition: Something that is accepted.
more.etymology: First attested about 1380. From Middle English accepten, borrowed from Old French accepter, or directly from Latin acceptō, acceptāre (“receive”), frequentative of accipiō, formed from ad- + capiō (“to take”). Displaced native Old English onfōn.

examples.text: They have accepted the current situation.

translations.de: Sie haben die aktuelle Situation akzeptiert.
translations.fr: Ils ont accepté la situation actuelle.
translations.pt: Aceitaram a situação atual.

examples.text: Why didn't Mary accept Tom's gift?

translations.de: Warum hat Maria Toms Geschenk nicht angenommen?
translations.fr: Pourquoi Mary n'a-t-elle pas accepté le cadeau de Tom ?
translations.pt: Por que Mary não aceitou o presente de Tom?

examples.text: This restaurant only accepts cash.

translations.de: Dieses Restaurant akzeptiert nur Bargeld.
translations.fr: Ce restaurant n'accepte que du liquide.
translations.pt: Este restaurante só aceita dinheiro.

examples.text: I'd like to thank you for accepting my invitation.

translations.de: Ich möchte dir dafür danken, dass du meine Einladung angenommen hast.
translations.fr: Je vous remercie d'avoir accepté mon invitation.
translations.pt: Eu gostaria de agradecer-lhe por aceitar o meu convite.

more.definition: To receive, especially with a consent, with favour, or with approval.; To admit to a place or a group.; To regard as proper, usual, true, or to believe in.
more.etymology: First attested about 1380. From Middle English accepten, borrowed from Old French accepter, or directly from Latin acceptō, acceptāre (“receive”), frequentative of accipiō, formed from ad- + capiō (“to take”). Displaced native Old English onfōn.

examples.text: The restaurant is across from the hotel.

translations.de: Das Restaurant befindet sich gegenüber dem Hotel.
translations.fr: Le restaurant est en face de l'hôtel.
translations.pt: O restaurante fica em frente ao hotel.

examples.text: Are there hotels on the island?

translations.de: Gibt es Hotels auf der Insel?
translations.fr: Y a-t-il des hôtels sur l'île ?
translations.pt: Há hotéis na ilha?

examples.text: How do I get to the hotel?

translations.de: Wie komme ich zum Hotel?
translations.fr: Comment est-ce que je vais à l'hôtel ?
translations.pt: Como eu vou para o hotel?

examples.text: They were prohibited from leaving the hotel.

translations.de: Es war ihnen untersagt, das Hotel zu verlassen.
translations.fr: On leur refusa de quitter l'hôtel.
translations.pt: Eles foram proibidos de deixar o hotel.

more.definition: A large town house or mansion; a grand private residence, especially in France.; An establishment that provides accommodation and other services for paying guests; normally larger than a guesthouse, and often one of a chain.; A public house or pub.
more.etymology: French hôtelbor. Borrowed from French hôtel, from Middle French hostel, from Old French ostel, from Late Latin hospitālis (“hospice, shelter, guesthouse”), from Latin hospitālis (“hospitable”). Doublet of hostel and hospital.

examples.text: Whose book is that on the table?

translations.de: Wessen Buch liegt auf dem Tisch?
translations.fr: À qui est le livre sur la table ?
translations.pt: De quem é o livro em cima da mesa?

examples.text: The cat is sitting on the table.

translations.de: Die Katze sitzt auf dem Tisch.
translations.fr: Le chat est assis sur le bureau.
translations.pt: O gato está em cima da mesa.

examples.text: There is a biscuit underneath the table.

translations.de: Unter dem Tisch liegt ein Keks.
translations.fr: Un biscuit se trouve sous la table.
translations.pt: Tem biscoito debaixo da mesa.

examples.text: Tom put thirty dollars on the table.

translations.de: Tom legte dreißig Dollar auf den Tisch.
translations.fr: Tom mit trente dollars sur la table.
translations.pt: Tom pôs trinta dólares sobre a mesa.

more.definition: An item of furniture with a flat top surface raised above the ground, usually on one or more legs.; A flat tray which can be used as a table.; A supply of food or entertainment.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English table, tabel, tabil, tabul, from Old English tabele, tabul, tablu, tabule, tabula (“board”); also as tæfl, tæfel, an early Germanic borrowing of Latin tabula (“tablet, board, plank, chart”). The sense of “piece of furniture” is from Old French table, of same Latin origin; Old English used bēod or bord instead for this meaning: see board. Doublet of tabula and tavla.

examples.text: The flowers will brighten up the table.

translations.de: Mit den Blumen wird der Tisch freundlicher aussehen.
translations.fr: Les fleurs vont enjoliver la table.
translations.pt: As flores vão dar mais vida à mesa.

examples.text: There are two plates on the table.

translations.de: Auf dem Tisch stehen zwei Teller.
translations.fr: Il y a deux assiettes sur la table.
translations.pt: Há dois pratos em cima da mesa.

examples.text: There's a cat on the table.

translations.de: Auf dem Tisch ist eine Katze.
translations.fr: Il y a un chat sur la table.
translations.pt: Tem um gato na mesa.

examples.text: The cat is sleeping on the table.

translations.de: Die Katze schläft auf dem Tisch.
translations.fr: Le chat dort sur la table.
translations.pt: O gato está dormindo em cima da mesa.

more.definition: To tabulate; to put into a table or grid.; To put on the table of a commission or legislative assembly; to propose for formal discussion or consideration, to put on the agenda.; To remove from the agenda, to postpone dealing with; to shelve (to indefinitely postpone consideration or discussion of something).
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English table, tabel, tabil, tabul, from Old English tabele, tabul, tablu, tabule, tabula (“board”); also as tæfl, tæfel, an early Germanic borrowing of Latin tabula (“tablet, board, plank, chart”). The sense of “piece of furniture” is from Old French table, of same Latin origin; Old English used bēod or bord instead for this meaning: see board. Doublet of tabula and tavla.

examples.text: I need to search for my pen.

translations.de: Ich muss meinen Stift suchen.
translations.fr: Je dois rechercher mon stylo.
translations.pt: Preciso procurar minha caneta.

examples.text: He went traveling in search of adventure.

translations.de: Er ging auf Reisen, da er abenteuerlustig war.
translations.fr: Il partit voyager à la recherche d'aventures.
translations.pt: Ele foi viajar em busca de aventura.

examples.text: Who searches, finds.

translations.de: Wer sucht, der findet.
translations.fr: Qui cherche, trouve.
translations.pt: Quem procura encontra.

examples.text: Two librarians search for two books.

translations.de: Zwei Bibliothekare suchen nach zwei Büchern.
translations.fr: Deux bibliothécaires recherchent deux livres.
translations.pt: Dois bibliotecários procuram dois livros.

more.definition: An attempt to find something.; The act of searching in general.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker-der. Ancient Greek κίρκος (kírkos)bor. Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Anglo-Norman sercherbor. Inherited from Middle English serchen, borrowed from Anglo-Norman sercher, Old French cerchier, from Late Latin circō, ,circāre (“to circle; go around; search for”), from circus. Unrelated to German suchen, which is cognate with English seek.

examples.text: The police searched Tom's car.

translations.de: Die Polizei durchsuchte Toms Auto.
translations.fr: La police a fouillé le véhicule de Tom.
translations.pt: A polícia revistou o carro de Tom.

examples.text: Which search engine do you use?

translations.de: Welche Suchmaschine benutzt du?
translations.fr: Quel moteur de recherche utilisez-vous ?
translations.pt: Qual mecanismo de busca você usa?

examples.text: I am searching for my brother.

translations.de: Ich suche meinen Bruder.
translations.fr: Je cherche mon frère.
translations.pt: Eu estou procurando meu irmão.

examples.text: I am in search of the lost language.

translations.de: Ich bin auf der Suche nach der verlorengegangen Sprache.
translations.fr: Je suis à la recherche de la langue perdue.
translations.pt: Estou na busca do idioma perdido.

more.definition: To look in (a place) for something.; To look thoroughly.; To put a phrase into a search engine, especially one besides Google.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker-der. Ancient Greek κίρκος (kírkos)bor. Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Anglo-Norman sercherbor. Inherited from Middle English serchen, borrowed from Anglo-Norman sercher, Old French cerchier, from Late Latin circō, ,circāre (“to circle; go around; search for”), from circus. Unrelated to German suchen, which is cognate with English seek.

examples.text: In the winter, days are shorter.

translations.de: Im Winter sind die Tage kürzer.
translations.fr: En hiver, les journées sont plus courtes.
translations.pt: No inverno os dias são mais curtos.

examples.text: He's always short of money.

translations.de: Er ist immer knapp bei Kasse.
translations.fr: Il est toujours à court d'argent.
translations.pt: Ele está sempre apertado.

examples.text: Take the shortest route to Paris.

translations.de: Nimm den kürzesten Weg nach Paris!
translations.fr: Prenez le chemin le plus court pour aller à Paris.
translations.pt: Pegue a rota mais curta para Paris.

examples.text: People say that life is short.

translations.de: Die Leute sagen, das Leben sei kurz.
translations.fr: Les gens disent que la vie est courte.
translations.pt: As pessoas dizem que a vida é curta.

more.definition: Having a small distance from one end or edge to another, either horizontally or vertically.; Of a person, living being, or object, having a comparatively small height.; Having little duration.
more.etymology: From Middle English schort, short, from Old English sċeort, sċort (“short”), from Proto-West Germanic *skurt, from Proto-Germanic *skurtaz (“short”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker-. Doublet of shirt, skirt, and curt.

examples.text: I will stay here for a short period.

translations.de: Ich werde hier für eine kurze Zeit bleiben.
translations.fr: Je ne resterai pas longtemps ici.
translations.pt: Ficarei aqui por um breve período de tempo.

examples.text: I have been busy writing a short story.

translations.de: Ich war damit beschäftigt, eine Kurzgeschichte zu schreiben.
translations.fr: J'ai été très occupé par l'écriture d'une petite histoire.
translations.pt: Eu tenho andado ocupado escrevendo uma pequena estória.

examples.text: I'm short of cash at the moment.

translations.de: Ich bin im Moment knapp bei Kasse.
translations.fr: En ce moment, je manque de liquidités.
translations.pt: Não tenho dinheiro suficiente neste momento.

examples.text: Mozart's life was very short.

translations.de: Mozarts Leben war sehr kurz.
translations.fr: La vie de Mozart fut très courte.
translations.pt: A vida de Mozart foi muito curta.

more.definition: Abruptly, curtly, briefly.; Unawares.; Without achieving a goal or requirement.
more.etymology: From Middle English schort, short, from Old English sċeort, sċort (“short”), from Proto-West Germanic *skurt, from Proto-Germanic *skurtaz (“short”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker-. Doublet of shirt, skirt, and curt.

examples.text: Rabbits have long ears and short tails.

translations.de: Kaninchen haben lange Ohren und kurze Schwänze.
translations.fr: Les lapins ont de longues oreilles et une petite queue.
translations.pt: Os coelhos têm orelhas compridas e rabo curto.

examples.text: Tom is wearing leather shorts.

translations.de: Tom trägt kurze Lederhosen.
translations.fr: Tom porte une culotte de cuir.
translations.pt: Tom está usando calças de couro.

examples.text: We had a short vacation in February.

translations.de: Einen kurzen Urlaub im Februar hatten wir.
translations.fr: Nous avons eu de courtes vacances en février.
translations.pt: Em fevereiro tivemos umas férias curtas.

examples.text: This coat is too short on me.

translations.de: Dieser Mantel ist mir zu klein.
translations.fr: Ce manteau est trop court pour moi.
translations.pt: Este casaco está muito curto em mim.

more.definition: A short circuit.; A short film.; A short-form vertical video.
more.etymology: From Middle English schort, short, from Old English sċeort, sċort (“short”), from Proto-West Germanic *skurt, from Proto-Germanic *skurtaz (“short”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker-. Doublet of shirt, skirt, and curt.

examples.text: Our country is running short of energy resources.

translations.de: Unserem Land gehen die Energieressourcen aus.
translations.fr: Les ressources énergétiques de notre pays s'épuisent.
translations.pt: Os recursos energéticos de nosso país estão se esgotando.

examples.text: Let's take a short cut.

translations.de: Nehmen wir eine Abkürzung!
translations.fr: Prenons un raccourci !
translations.pt: Vamos pegar um atalho.

examples.text: They only allowed carryons on the short-haul flight.

translations.de: Auf dem Kurzstreckenflug war nur Handgepäck erlaubt.
translations.fr: Ils n'autorisaient que les bagages à main sur le vol court-courrier.
translations.pt: Só permitiam bagagem de mão no voo de curta distância.

examples.text: My short-term memory is getting shorter and shorter.

translations.de: Mein Kurzzeitgedächtnis wird immer kürzer.
translations.fr: Ma mémoire immédiate est de plus en plus courte.
translations.pt: Minha memória de curto prazo está se tornando mais e mais curta.

more.definition: Deficient in.; Having a negative position in.
more.etymology: From Middle English schort, short, from Old English sċeort, sċort (“short”), from Proto-West Germanic *skurt, from Proto-Germanic *skurtaz (“short”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker-. Doublet of shirt, skirt, and curt.

examples.text: Life is short, you have to enjoy it!

translations.de: Das Leben ist kurz, man muss es genießen!
translations.fr: La vie est courte, il faut en profiter !
translations.pt: A vida é curta, é preciso aproveitá-la!

examples.text: You aren't as short as I am.

translations.de: Du bist nicht so klein wie ich.
translations.fr: Tu n'es pas aussi petit que moi.
translations.pt: Você não é tão baixo como eu.

examples.text: He suggested that we take a short rest.

translations.de: Er schlug vor, eine kurze Pause zu machen.
translations.fr: Il a suggéré que nous prenions un petit repos.
translations.pt: Ele sugeriu que descansássemos um pouco.

examples.text: He continued his work after a short break.

translations.de: Er arbeitete nach einer kurzen Pause weiter.
translations.fr: Il continua son travail après une courte pause.
translations.pt: Ele continuou com seu trabalho depois de um breve descanso.

more.definition: To cause a short circuit in (something).; To short circuit.; To provide with an amount smaller than that agreed or labeled; to shortchange.
more.etymology: From Middle English schort, short, from Old English sċeort, sċort (“short”), from Proto-West Germanic *skurt, from Proto-Germanic *skurtaz (“short”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker-. Doublet of shirt, skirt, and curt.

examples.text: She walked twenty miles a day.

translations.de: Sie ging zwanzig Meilen am Tag.
translations.fr: Elle a parcouru vingt milles à pied par jour.
translations.pt: Ela caminhava vinte milhas por dia.

examples.text: The bridge is one mile above.

translations.de: Die Brücke ist eine Meile flussaufwärts.
translations.fr: Le pont est à un mille en amont.
translations.pt: A ponte fica uma milha a montante.

examples.text: That town is two miles away.

translations.de: Jene Stadt ist zwei Meilen entfernt.
translations.fr: Cette ville est distante de 2 miles.
translations.pt: Aquela cidade fica a duas milhas de distância.

examples.text: The station is two miles away.

translations.de: Der Bahnhof ist zwei Meilen entfernt.
translations.fr: La gare est à deux miles d'ici.
translations.pt: A estação fica a duas milhas daqui.

more.definition: The international mile: a unit of length precisely equal to 1.609344 kilometers established by treaty among Anglophone nations in 1959, divided into 5,280 feet or 1,760 yards.; Any of several customary units of length derived from the 1593 English statute mile of 8 furlongs, equivalent to 5,280 feet or 1,760 yards of various precise values.; Any of many customary units of length derived from the Roman mile (mille passus) of 8 stades or 5,000 Roman feet.
more.etymology: From Middle English myle, mile, from Old English mīl, from Proto-West Germanic *mīliju, a borrowing of Latin mīlia, mīllia, plural of mīle, mīlle (“mile”) (literally ‘thousand’ but used as a short form of mīlle passūs (“a thousand paces”)).

examples.text: You've painted the walls, haven't you?

translations.de: Du hast die Wände gestrichen, oder?
translations.fr: Vous avez peint les murs, n'est-ce pas ?
translations.pt: Você pintou as paredes, não pintou?

examples.text: The walls support the ceiling.

translations.de: Die Wände tragen die Decke.
translations.fr: Les murs soutiennent le plafond.
translations.pt: As paredes sustentam o teto.

examples.text: The elevator has green walls.

translations.de: Der Aufzug hat grüne Wände.
translations.fr: L'ascenseur a des parois vertes.
translations.pt: O elevador tem paredes verdes.

examples.text: We painted the walls white.

translations.de: Wir haben die Wände weiß gestrichen.
translations.fr: Nous avons peint les murs en blanc.
translations.pt: Pintamos as paredes de branco.

more.definition: A rampart of earth, stones etc. built up for defensive purposes.; A structure built for defense surrounding a city, castle etc.; Each of the substantial structures acting either as the exterior of or divisions within a structure.
more.etymology: From Middle English wal, from Old English weall (“wall, dike, earthwork, rampart, dam, rocky shore, cliff”), from Proto-West Germanic *wall (“wall, rampart, entrenchment”), from Latin vallum (“wall, rampart, entrenchment, palisade”), from Proto-Indo-European *welH- (“to turn, wind, roll”).

examples.text: The catapult hurled the boulder over the castle walls.

translations.de: Das Katapult schleuderte den Felsen über die Schlossmauern.
translations.fr: La catapulte propulsa le boulet par-dessus les murs du château.
translations.pt: A catapulta lançou o pedregulho por cima das muralhas do castelo.

examples.text: If walls could talk, what stories would they tell us?

translations.de: Wenn Wände reden könnten, welche Geschichten würden sie uns erzählen?
translations.fr: Si les murs pouvaient parler, quelles histoires nous conteraient-ils ?
translations.pt: Se as paredes falassem, que histórias nos contariam?

examples.text: The walls have ears.

translations.de: Die Wände haben Ohren.
translations.fr: Les murs ont des oreilles.
translations.pt: As paredes têm ouvidos.

examples.text: We're going to paint the wall.

translations.de: Wir werden die Wand streichen.
translations.fr: Nous allons peindre le mur.
translations.pt: Nós vamos pintar a parede.

more.definition: To enclose with, or as if with, a wall or walls.; To use a wallhack.; To wallbang.
more.etymology: From Middle English wal, from Old English weall (“wall, dike, earthwork, rampart, dam, rocky shore, cliff”), from Proto-West Germanic *wall (“wall, rampart, entrenchment”), from Latin vallum (“wall, rampart, entrenchment, palisade”), from Proto-Indo-European *welH- (“to turn, wind, roll”).

examples.text: Our teacher is a real idiot.

translations.de: Unser Lehrer ist ein echter Trottel.
translations.fr: Notre professeur est un parfait idiot.
translations.pt: O nosso professor é um perfeito idiota.

examples.text: You think I'm an idiot?

translations.de: Hältst du mich für einen Dummkopf?
translations.fr: Vous me prenez pour un idiot ?
translations.pt: Você acha que eu sou idiota?

examples.text: Tom is a useful idiot.

translations.de: Tom ist ein nützlicher Idiot.
translations.fr: Tom est un idiot utile.
translations.pt: O Tom é um idiota útil.

examples.text: Tom called me an idiot.

translations.de: Tom hat mich einen Idioten genannt.
translations.fr: Tom m’a traité d’idiot.
translations.pt: Tom me chamou de idiota.

more.etymology: Latin idiotalbor. Old French idiotebor. From Middle English idiote, ydiote, from Old French idiote (later idiot), from Latin idiota, from Ancient Greek ἰδιώτης (idiṓtēs, “a private citizen, one who has no professional knowledge, layman”), from ἴδιος (ídios, “one's own, pertaining to oneself, private”). Doublet of idiota. By surface analysis, idi- + -ot.

examples.text: What a bunch of idiots!

translations.de: Was für eine Menge Idioten!
translations.fr: Quelle bande d'idiots !
translations.pt: Que bando de idiotas!

examples.text: I consider Tom an idiot.

translations.de: Ich halte Tom für einen Idioten.
translations.fr: Je considère Tom comme un idiot.
translations.pt: Eu considero Tom um idiota.

examples.text: I felt like an idiot.

translations.de: Ich kam mir wie ein Idiot vor.
translations.fr: Je me sentis idiote.
translations.pt: Eu me senti um idiota.

examples.text: I'm such an idiot.

translations.de: Ich bin so eine Idiotin!
translations.fr: Je suis un tel idiot.
translations.pt: Sou burro pra caramba.

more.definition: A person of low general intelligence.; A person who makes stupid decisions; a fool.
more.etymology: Latin idiotalbor. Old French idiotebor. From Middle English idiote, ydiote, from Old French idiote (later idiot), from Latin idiota, from Ancient Greek ἰδιώτης (idiṓtēs, “a private citizen, one who has no professional knowledge, layman”), from ἴδιος (ídios, “one's own, pertaining to oneself, private”). Doublet of idiota. By surface analysis, idi- + -ot.

examples.text: I saw the boy jump over the fence and run away.

translations.de: Ich sah, wie der Junge über den Zaun sprang und weglief.
translations.fr: J’ai vu le garçon sauter par-dessus la clôture puis s’enfuir.
translations.pt: Eu vi o rapaz saltar sobre a cerca e fugir.

examples.text: Don't jump!

translations.de: Spring nicht!
translations.fr: Ne saute pas !
translations.pt: Não pule!

examples.text: I can jump.

translations.de: Ich kann springen.
translations.fr: Je peux sauter.
translations.pt: Eu posso pular.

examples.text: Did Tom jump, or was he pushed?

translations.de: Ist Tom gesprungen oder wurde er gestoßen?
translations.fr: Tom a-t-il sauté ou a-t-il été poussé ?
translations.pt: Tom pulou ou foi empurrado?

more.etymology: From Middle English jumpen (“to walk quickly, run, jump”), probably of Middle Low German or North Germanic origin, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *gumpōną ~ *gumbōną (“to hop, skip, bounce”), an iterative verb. The OED suggests an imitative origin. Related to jumble. In the sense “to propel oneself” it displaced leap partially and spring largely.

examples.text: I'm going to jump.

translations.de: Ich werde springen.
translations.fr: Je vais sauter.
translations.pt: Eu vou saltar.

examples.text: Go jump in the lake.

translations.de: Geh und spring in den See.
translations.fr: Va te noyer !
translations.pt: Vá pular no lago.

examples.text: It's dangerous to jump off a moving train.

translations.de: Es ist gefährlich, aus einem fahrenden Zug zu springen.
translations.fr: Il est dangereux de sauter d'un train en marche.
translations.pt: É perigoso pular de um trem em movimento.

examples.text: Don't jump to conclusions.

translations.de: Ziehe keine voreiligen Schlüsse.
translations.fr: Ne tire pas de conclusions hâtives.
translations.pt: Não tire conclusões precipitadas.

more.etymology: From Middle English jumpen (“to walk quickly, run, jump”), probably of Middle Low German or North Germanic origin, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *gumpōną ~ *gumbōną (“to hop, skip, bounce”), an iterative verb. The OED suggests an imitative origin. Related to jumble. In the sense “to propel oneself” it displaced leap partially and spring largely.

examples.text: I saw the man jump.

translations.de: Ich sah den Mann springen.
translations.fr: J'ai vu l'homme sauter.
translations.pt: Vi o homem pular.

examples.text: How high can you jump?

translations.de: Wie hoch kannst du springen?
translations.fr: À quelle hauteur peux-tu sauter ?
translations.pt: Quão alto você consegue pular?

examples.text: She can jump high.

translations.de: Sie kann hoch springen.
translations.fr: Elle peut sauter haut.
translations.pt: Ela sabe pular alto.

examples.text: The girl was afraid to jump down from the roof.

translations.de: Das Mädchen hatte Angst, vom Dach herunter zu springen.
translations.fr: La jeune fille avait peur de sauter du toit.
translations.pt: A menina teve medo de saltar do telhado.

more.definition: The act of jumping; a leap; a spring; a bound.; An effort; an attempt; a venture.; A dislocation in a stratum; a fault.
more.etymology: From Middle English jumpen (“to walk quickly, run, jump”), probably of Middle Low German or North Germanic origin, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *gumpōną ~ *gumbōną (“to hop, skip, bounce”), an iterative verb. The OED suggests an imitative origin. Related to jumble. In the sense “to propel oneself” it displaced leap partially and spring largely.

examples.text: The cat jumped onto the table.

translations.de: Die Katze sprang auf den Tisch.
translations.fr: Le chat a sauté sur la table.
translations.pt: O gato pulou em cima da mesa.

examples.text: I won't let you jump.

translations.de: Ich werde Sie nicht springen lassen.
translations.fr: Je ne te laisserai pas sauter.
translations.pt: Eu não vou deixar você pular.

examples.text: He committed suicide by jumping off a bridge.

translations.de: Er beging Selbstmord durch Sprung von einer Brücke.

more.definition: To propel oneself rapidly upward, downward and/or in any horizontal direction such that momentum causes the body to become airborne.; To cause oneself to leave an elevated location and fall downward.; To pass by means of a spring or leap; to overleap.
more.etymology: From Middle English jumpen (“to walk quickly, run, jump”), probably of Middle Low German or North Germanic origin, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *gumpōną ~ *gumbōną (“to hop, skip, bounce”), an iterative verb. The OED suggests an imitative origin. Related to jumble. In the sense “to propel oneself” it displaced leap partially and spring largely.

examples.text: I like Tom's blue pineapple.

examples.text: This came like a bolt from the blue.

more.definition: To make or become blue; to turn blue.; To treat the surface of steel so that it is passivated chemically and becomes more resistant to rust.; To brighten by treating with blue (laundry aid).
more.etymology: From Middle English blew, blewe, from Anglo-Norman blew, from Middle French bleu, from Old French blöe, bleve, blef (“blue”), from Frankish *blāu (“blue”) (perhaps through a Late Latin blāvus, blāvius (“blue”) attested from Isidore of Seville), from Proto-Germanic *blēwaz (“blue, dark blue”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰlēw- (“yellow, blond, grey”).

examples.text: I'd like to talk to the head of security.

translations.de: Ich würde gerne den Sicherheitschef sprechen.
translations.fr: J'aimerais m'entretenir avec le responsable de la sécurité.

translations.de: Die Sicherheitsleute ließen uns nicht hinein.

examples.text: A firewall guarantees your security on the internet.

more.definition: The condition of not being threatened, especially physically, psychologically, emotionally, or financially.; Something that secures.; An organization or department responsible for providing security by enforcing laws, rules, and regulations as well as maintaining order.
more.etymology: From secure + -ity, from Middle English securite, from Middle French securité (modern sécurité), from Latin sēcūritās, from Latin sēcūrus (“safe, secure”), from sē- (“without”) + cūra (“care”); see cure. examples.text: The leaves on the trees have turned red.

examples.text: He has no trouble climbing trees.

more.definition: A perennial woody plant taller and larger than a shrub with a wooden trunk and, at some distance from the ground, having leaves and branches.; Any other plant (such as a large shrub or herb) that is reminiscent of the above in form and size.; An object made from a tree trunk and having multiple hooks or storage platforms.

examples.text: There are maple trees in this forest.

examples.text: Are there many trees in the park?

more.definition: To chase (an animal or person) up a tree.; To place in a tree.; To place upon a shoe tree; to fit with a shoe tree; to stretch upon a shoe tree.
more.etymology: From Middle English trau, tre, tree, treo, treou, trew, trewe, troe, trouȝh, trouȝgh, trow, trowe, from Old English trēo, trēow, trēu, trīo, trīow, trȳw (“tree; wood; forest; beam, cudgel, log; cross”), from Proto-West Germanic *treu, from Proto-Germanic *trewą (“tree”), from pre-Germanic *dréwom, thematic e-grade derivative of Proto-Indo-European *dóru (“tree”). examples.text: I thought you knew this area.

more.definition: A measure of the extent of a surface; it is measured in square units.; A particular geographic region.; Any particular extent of surface, especially an empty or unused extent.

examples.text: My flat is on the third floor.

translations.de: Meine Wohnung ist im dritten Stock.

more.definition: The interior bottom or surface of a house or building; the supporting surface of a room.; The bottom surface of a natural structure, entity, or space (e.g. cave, forest, ocean, desert, etc.); the ground (surface of the Earth).; A structure formed of beams, girders, etc, with proper covering, which divides a building horizontally into storeys/stories.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English floor, floour, flor, flore, flour, flur, vlor, from Old English flōr (“floor, pavement; deck; gangplank”), from Proto-West Germanic *flōr, from Proto-Germanic *flōraz (“ground; floor”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂ros (“floor”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat”).

examples.text: How many floors does this building have?

more.definition: To cover or furnish with a floor.; To strike down or lay level with the floor; to knock down.; To push (a pedal) down to the floor, especially to accelerate.

From Middle English servise, from Old English serfis, from Old French servise (French service), from the verb servir, from Latin servitium (compare Portuguese serviço, Italian servizio, Norman sèrvice, Spanish servicio), from servus (“servant; serf; slave”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ser-wo-s (“guardian”), possibly from *ser- (“watch over, protect”).

examples.text: Tom told me to treat others with respect.

translations.pt: Ele sempre me trata como criança.

examples.text: Don't treat me like a child.

translations.pt: Não me trate como a uma criança.

translations.de: Nur dass du’s weißt: ich habe dich nicht beleidigt!

examples.text: In case of an emergency, get in touch with my agent.

examples.text: I learned French instead of German.

translations.fr: J'ai appris le français au lieu de l'allemand.

translations.de: Spielen wir, statt fernzusehen, doch Karten!
translations.fr: Jouons aux cartes plutôt que d'écouter la télévision.
translations.pt: Joguemos cartas em vez de ver televisão.

translations.fr: Nous avons planté des arachides plutôt que du coton.

examples.text: We swim to the boat.

translations.de: Wir schwimmen zum Boot.
translations.fr: Nous nageons jusqu'au bateau.
translations.pt: Nadamos até o barco.

more.definition: To travel by boat.; To transport in a boat.; To place in a boat.
more.etymology: From Middle English bot, boot, boet, boyt (“boat”), from Old English bāt (“boat”), from Proto-West Germanic *bait, from Proto-Germanic *baitaz, *baitą (“boat, small ship”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeyd- (“to break, split”) (whence also fissure via Latin). Cognate with Old Norse beit (“boat”), Middle Dutch beitel (“little boat”).

examples.text: Black smoke came out of the chimney.

examples.text: My father neither drinks nor smokes.

translations.de: Mein Vater trinkt weder, noch raucht er.
translations.fr: Mon père ne fume pas et ne boit pas non plus.
translations.pt: Meu pai nem bebe nem fuma.

examples.text: Do you mind if I smoke a cigarette?

translations.de: Stört es dich, wenn ich eine rauche?
translations.fr: Ça te dérange si je fume une cigarette ?
translations.pt: Importa-se que eu fume um cigarro?

examples.text: John doesn't smoke any more.

translations.de: Johannes raucht nicht mehr.
translations.fr: Jean ne fume plus.
translations.pt: John não fuma mais.

more.definition: The visible vapor/vapour, gases, and fine particles given off by burning or smoldering material.; A cigarette.; Anything to smoke (e.g. cigarettes, marijuana, etc.)
more.etymology: From Middle English smoke, from Old English smoca (“smoke”), probably a derivative of the verb (see below). Related to Dutch smook (“smoke”), Middle Low German smôk (“smoke”), German Schmauch (“smoke (from a gun barrel)”).

examples.text: I didn't know that Tom smoked.

translations.de: Ich wusste nicht, dass Tom raucht.
translations.fr: Je ne savais pas que Tom fumait.

examples.text: Tom told me that Mary quit smoking.

translations.de: Tom erzählte mir, dass Mary mit dem Rauchen aufgehört hätte.
translations.fr: Thomas m'a raconté que Marie avait arrêté de fumer.

examples.text: You may not smoke in the elevator.

translations.de: Im Aufzug ist Rauchen nicht gestattet.
translations.fr: Tu ne peux pas fumer dans l'ascenseur.
translations.pt: Não podes fumar no elevador.

examples.text: Tom smokes three packs of cigarettes a day.

translations.de: Tom raucht drei Schachteln Zigaretten am Tag.
translations.fr: Tom fume trois paquets de cigarettes par jour.
translations.pt: Tom fuma três maços de cigarro por dia.

more.definition: To inhale and exhale the smoke from a burning cigarette or cigar, burning material in a pipe, etc.; To inhale and exhale tobacco smoke.; To give off smoke.
more.etymology: From Middle English smoken, from Old English smocian (“to smoke, to emit smoke”), from Proto-West Germanic *smokōn, from Proto-Germanic *smukōną (“to smoke”), ablaut derivative of Proto-Germanic *smaukaną (“to smoke”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)mewg- (“to smoke”).

examples.text: I wasn't able to escape.

translations.de: Ein Entkommen war mir nicht möglich.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas pu m'échapper.
translations.pt: Eu não consegui escapar.

examples.text: No man escapes death.

translations.de: Niemand entrinnt dem Tod.
translations.fr: Aucun homme n'échappe à la mort.

examples.text: We didn't help Tom escape.

translations.de: Wir haben Tom nicht bei der Flucht geholfen.
translations.fr: Nous n'avons pas aidé Tom à s'échapper.
translations.pt: Não ajudamos o Tom a escapar.

examples.text: Fortunately, they were able to escape.

translations.de: Zum Glück konnten sie entkommen.
translations.fr: Heureusement, ils ont pu s'échapper.
translations.pt: Felizmente, eles conseguiram escapar.

more.definition: The act of leaving a dangerous or unpleasant situation.; Leakage or outflow, as of steam or a liquid, or an electric current through defective insulation.; Something that has escaped; an escapee.
more.etymology: From Middle English escapen, from Anglo-Norman and Old Northern French escaper ( = Old French eschaper, modern French échapper), from Vulgar Latin *excappāre (“to escape a garment, get out of one's clothing”, literally “to free oneself from one's cape”), from Latin ex- (“out”) + Late Latin cappa (“cape, cloak”). Cognate with escapade. Also doublet of scape.

examples.text: She abetted him in escaping from prison.

translations.de: Sie war ihm bei seinem Gefängnisausbruch behilflich.
translations.fr: Elle l'a aidé à s'échapper de la prison.
translations.pt: Ela o incitou a fugir da prisão.

examples.text: A tiger has escaped from the zoo.

translations.de: Ein Tiger ist aus dem Zoo ausgebrochen.
translations.fr: Un tigre s'est échappé du zoo.
translations.pt: Um tigre escapou do zoológico.

examples.text: How did you manage to escape?

translations.de: Wie ist dir die Flucht gelungen?
translations.fr: Comment as-tu réussi à t'échapper ?
translations.pt: Como vocês conseguiram fugir?

examples.text: Nobody escapes their destiny.

translations.de: Niemand entkommt seinem Schicksal.
translations.fr: Nul n'échappe à son destin.
translations.pt: Ninguém foge do seu destino.

more.definition: To get free; to free oneself.; To break out of confinement.; To avoid (any unpleasant person or thing); to elude, get away from.
more.etymology: From Middle English escapen, from Anglo-Norman and Old Northern French escaper ( = Old French eschaper, modern French échapper), from Vulgar Latin *excappāre (“to escape a garment, get out of one's clothing”, literally “to free oneself from one's cape”), from Latin ex- (“out”) + Late Latin cappa (“cape, cloak”). Cognate with escapade. Also doublet of scape.

examples.text: Wild boars grunt in the meadow.
The dog emitted grunts.
The animals began to howl and bark and grunt.
Wild boar grunt if you get close to them.

more.definition: A short snorting sound, often to show disapproval, or used as a reply when one is reluctant to speak.; The snorting cry of a pig.; Any fish of the perciform family Haemulidae.
more.etymology: From Middle English grunten, from Old English grunnettan (“to grunt”), from Proto-West Germanic *grunnattjan, from Proto-Germanic *grunnatjaną (“to grunt”), frequentative of Proto-Germanic *grunnōną (“to grunt”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰrun- (“to shout”). Cognate with German grunzen (“to grunt”), Danish grynte (“to grunt”). The noun senses are all instances of zero derivation from the verb.

examples.text: The boar is grunting.

translations.de: Das Wildschwein grunzt.

examples.text: He grunted his thanks.

examples.text: Marzipan pigs do not grunt.

translations.de: Marzipanschweine grunzen nicht.

examples.text: The pig grunts.

translations.de: Das Schwein grunzt.

more.definition: To make a grunt or grunts.; To break wind; to fart.
more.etymology: From Middle English grunten, from Old English grunnettan (“to grunt”), from Proto-West Germanic *grunnattjan, from Proto-Germanic *grunnatjaną (“to grunt”), frequentative of Proto-Germanic *grunnōną (“to grunt”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰrun- (“to shout”). Cognate with German grunzen (“to grunt”), Danish grynte (“to grunt”). The noun senses are all instances of zero derivation from the verb.

examples.text: There are seven continents on the earth.

translations.de: Es gibt sieben Kontinente auf der Erde.
translations.fr: Il y a sept continents sur Terre.

examples.text: Who were the Seven Sages of ancient Greece?

translations.de: Wer waren die sieben Weisen des antiken Griechenlands?

translations.de: Die sieben Musen unterstützten die Künstler.

examples.text: The train is made up of seven cars.

translations.de: Der Zug besteht aus sieben Wagen.

more.definition: A numerical value equal to 7; the number following six and preceding eight.; Describing a group or set with seven elements.
more.etymology: PIE word *septḿ̥ From Middle English seven, from Old English seofon (“seven”), from Proto-West Germanic *sebun (“seven”), from Proto-Germanic *sebun (“seven”), from Proto-Indo-European *septḿ̥ (“seven”).

examples.text: Don't waste your time and money.

translations.de: Verschwende nicht deine Zeit und dein Geld.
translations.fr: Ne gaspille pas ton temps ni ton argent.
translations.pt: Não desperdice seu tempo e seu dinheiro.

examples.text: Helping others is never a waste of time.

translations.de: Anderen zu helfen ist nie eine Zeitverschwendung.

examples.text: Don't waste too much time.

translations.fr: Ne perds pas trop de temps.

examples.text: I think you're wasting your time.

translations.pt: Tentarei não incomodar ninguém.

examples.text: It doesn't bother me.

translations.de: Es stört mich nicht.
translations.fr: Ça ne me dérange pas.

translations.fr: Mon frère m'embête !

examples.text: Don't bother me.

translations.pt: Tom colou na prova de história.

examples.text: What's the purpose of your trip?

translations.de: Was ist der Zweck ihrer Reise?
translations.fr: Quel est l'objet de ton voyage ?
translations.pt: Qual é o propósito da sua viagem?

examples.text: He loves taking trips.

translations.de: Er geht gern auf Reisen.
translations.fr: Il adore voyager.
translations.pt: Ele adora viajar.

examples.text: We must cancel our trip to Japan.

translations.de: Wir müssen unsere Reise nach Japan absagen.
translations.fr: Nous devons annuler notre voyage pour le Japon.
translations.pt: Temos que cancelar a nossa viagem ao Japão.

examples.text: I was on a trip to India.

translations.de: Ich war auf einer Reise nach Indien.
translations.fr: J'étais en voyage en Inde.
translations.pt: Eu estava de viagem pela Índia.

more.definition: A journey; an excursion or jaunt.; A short outing for a specified purpose.; A period of time in which one experiences drug-induced reverie or hallucinations.
more.etymology: From Middle English trippen (“tread or step lightly and nimbly, skip, dance”), perhaps from Old French triper (“to hop or dance around, strike with the feet”), from a Frankish source; or alternatively from Middle Dutch trippen (“to skip, trip, hop, stamp, trample”) (> Modern Dutch trippelen (“to toddle, patter, trip”)).

examples.text: We have to cancel our trip to Japan.

translations.de: Wir müssen unsere Reise nach Japan stornieren.
translations.fr: Nous devons annuler notre voyage pour le Japon.
translations.pt: Temos que cancelar a nossa viagem ao Japão.

examples.text: The old man tripped over his own feet.

translations.de: Der alte Mann stolperte über seine eigenen Füße.
translations.fr: Le vieil homme a trébuché.
translations.pt: O velhinho tropeçou no seu próprio pé.

examples.text: Why did Tom cancel his trip?

translations.de: Warum hat Tom seine Reise abgebrochen?
translations.fr: Pourquoi Tom a-t-il annulé son voyage ?
translations.pt: Por que Tom cancelou sua viagem?

examples.text: We are planning a trip to New York.

translations.de: Wir planen eine Reise nach New York.
translations.fr: Nous planifions un voyage pour New York.
translations.pt: Estamos planejando uma viagem para Nova Iorque.

more.definition: To fall over or stumble over an object as a result of striking it with one's foot; To cause (a person or animal) to fall or stumble by knocking their feet from under them.; To be guilty of a misstep or mistake; to commit an offence against morality, propriety, etc
more.etymology: From Middle English trippen (“tread or step lightly and nimbly, skip, dance”), perhaps from Old French triper (“to hop or dance around, strike with the feet”), from a Frankish source; or alternatively from Middle Dutch trippen (“to skip, trip, hop, stamp, trample”) (> Modern Dutch trippelen (“to toddle, patter, trip”)).

examples.text: I don't have to cook it.

translations.de: Ich muss es nicht kochen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas besoin de le faire cuire.
translations.pt: Não preciso cozinhá-lo.

examples.text: She cooks for him every day.

translations.de: Sie kocht für ihn jeden Tag.
translations.fr: Elle cuisine pour lui quotidiennement.
translations.pt: Ela cozinha para ele todos os dias.

examples.text: He wants to learn how to cook.

translations.de: Er möchte gern das Kochen lernen.
translations.fr: Il veut apprendre à faire la cuisine.
translations.pt: Ele quer aprender a cozinhar.

examples.text: The cook is sitting in the kitchen.

translations.de: Der Koch sitzt in der Küche.
translations.fr: Le cuisinier est assis dans la cuisine.
translations.pt: O cozinheiro está sentado na cozinha.

more.definition: A person who prepares food.; The head cook of a manor house.; The degree or quality of cookedness of food.
more.etymology: Vulgar Latin *cocusbor. From Middle English cook, from Old English cōc (“a cook”), from Latin cocus, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *pekʷ- (“to cook, become ripe”). Cognate with Cimbrian khoch (“cook”), Dutch kok (“cook”), German Koch (“cook”), Luxembourgish Kach (“cook”), Danish kok (“cook”), Icelandic kokkur (“cook”), Norwegian Bokmål and Norwegian Nynorsk kokk (“cook”), Swedish kock (“cook”).

examples.text: They say she's good at cooking.

translations.de: Es heißt, sie könne gut kochen.
translations.fr: On dit qu'elle est bonne cuisinière.
translations.pt: Eles dizem que ela é uma boa cozinheira.

examples.text: I don't have time to cook.

translations.de: Ich habe keine Zeit zum Kochen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas le temps de cuisiner.
translations.pt: Não tenho tempo de cozinhar.

examples.text: I really liked what you cooked for me.

translations.de: Es hat wirklich gut geschmeckt, was du für mich gekocht hast.
translations.fr: J'ai beaucoup aimé ce que vous avez cuisiné pour moi.
translations.pt: Gostei muito do que você cozinhou para mim.

examples.text: I don't know how to cook.

translations.de: Ich kann nicht kochen.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas cuisiner.
translations.pt: Eu não sei cozinhar.

more.definition: To prepare food for eating, typically by heating it, combining it with other ingredients, seasoning it, preparing it for serving, etc.; To apply heat to food in the course of preparing it, particularly in a way that transforms it rather than simply making it warmer.; To undergo cooking.
more.etymology: Vulgar Latin *cocusbor. From Middle English coken, from the noun cook. In the slang sense of "proceed with some plan", coined by American rapper from California Lil B in 2010 and popularized in viral tweets and TikToks in mid-2022.

examples.text: You may choose any book you like.

translations.de: Du darfst jedes Buch wählen, das du magst.
translations.fr: Tu peux choisir n'importe quel livre que tu aimes.
translations.pt: Você pode escolher o livro que quiser.

examples.text: You can't choose your parents.

translations.de: Man kann sich seine Eltern nicht aussuchen.
translations.fr: On ne choisit pas ses parents.
translations.pt: Você não pode escolher seus pais.

examples.text: Most people choose the default option.

translations.de: Die meisten wählen die Standardeinstellung.
translations.fr: La plupart des gens choisissent l'option par défaut.
translations.pt: A maioria das pessoas escolhe a opção padrão.

examples.text: Of two evils, choose the lesser.

translations.de: Von zwei Übeln wähle das kleinere.
translations.fr: Entre deux maux, choisis le moindre.
translations.pt: De dois males escolha o menor.

more.definition: The binomial coefficient of the previous and following number.
more.etymology: From Middle English chesen, from Old English ċēosan (“to choose, seek out, select, elect, decide, test, accept, settle for, approve”), from Proto-West Germanic *keusan, from Proto-Germanic *keusaną (“to test; to choose”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵéwseti (“to choose, taste”), from *ǵews- (“to taste, try”).

examples.text: You may choose whichever book you like.

translations.de: Sie können sich ein beliebiges Buch aussuchen.
translations.fr: Tu peux choisir n'importe quel livre que tu aimes.
translations.pt: Você pode escolher o livro que quiser.

examples.text: We can't choose who our parents are.

translations.de: Man kann sich seine Eltern nicht aussuchen.
translations.fr: On ne choisit pas ses parents.
translations.pt: Não podemos escolher os nossos pais.

examples.text: You should choose a strong password!

translations.de: Sie sollten ein starkes Passwort wählen!
translations.fr: Vous devez choisir un mot de passe plus robuste !
translations.pt: Você deve escolher uma senha forte!

examples.text: I had to choose between A and B.

translations.de: Ich musste zwischen A und B wählen.
translations.fr: Je devais choisir entre A et B.
translations.pt: Eu tive de escolher entre A e B.

more.etymology: From Middle English chose, chos, chooce, a Northern dialectal form of Middle English chois (“choice”). Cognate with Scots chose, choose, chuse (“choosing, choice, selection”). Doublet of choice, see which for more.

examples.text: I don't want to be chosen.

translations.de: Ich möchte nicht ausgewählt werden.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas être choisi.
translations.pt: Eu não quero ser escolhido.

examples.text: You may choose what you like.

translations.de: Du kannst dir aussuchen, was du willst.
translations.fr: Tu peux choisir ce que tu veux.
translations.pt: Você pode escolher o que quiser.

examples.text: Not choosing is choosing already.

translations.de: Nicht wählen ist schon ein Wahl.
translations.fr: Ne pas choisir, c'est encore choisir.
translations.pt: Não escolher já é fazer uma escolha.

examples.text: We've chosen a hotel near the museums.

translations.de: Wir haben ein Hotel nahe den Museen gewählt.
translations.fr: Nous avons choisi un hôtel près des musées.
translations.pt: Escolhemos um hotel perto dos museus.

more.definition: To pick; to make the choice of; to select.; To elect.; To decide to act in a certain way.
more.etymology: From Middle English chesen, from Old English ċēosan (“to choose, seek out, select, elect, decide, test, accept, settle for, approve”), from Proto-West Germanic *keusan, from Proto-Germanic *keusaną (“to test; to choose”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵéwseti (“to choose, taste”), from *ǵews- (“to taste, try”).

examples.text: I have to change tires.

translations.de: Ich muss die Reifen wechseln.
translations.fr: Je dois changer de pneus.
translations.pt: Tenho de mudar os pneus.

translations.de: Im Reifen steckte ein Nagel.

examples.text: Tom tires easily.

translations.de: Tom wird schnell müde.
translations.fr: Tom se fatigue facilement.
translations.pt: Tom se cansa facilmente.

examples.text: We found a nail stuck in the tire.

translations.de: Im Reifen steckte ein Nagel.
translations.fr: Nous avons trouvé un clou enfoncé dans le pneu.
translations.pt: Encontramos um prego preso no pneu.

more.definition: US and Canada spelling of tyre: The rubber covering on a wheel.; US spelling of tyre: The metal rim of a wheel, especially that of a railroad locomotive.; A child's apron covering the upper part of the body, and tied with tape or cord; a pinafore. Also tier.
more.etymology: Probably from Middle English tir(e) (“equipment, furnshings, ornament”). See the details at tyre.

examples.text: Replace the old tires with new ones.

translations.de: Tauschen Sie den alten Satz Reifen durch einen neuen aus.
translations.fr: Échangez l'ancien train de pneus contre un neuf.
translations.pt: Troque os pneus velhos por pneus novos.

examples.text: The policemen shot at the car's tires.

translations.de: Die Polizisten schossen auf die Reifen des Wagens.
translations.fr: Les policiers ont tiré sur les pneus de la voiture.
translations.pt: Os policiais atiraram nos pneus do carro.

examples.text: The policemen fired at the car's tires.

translations.de: Die Polizisten schossen auf die Reifen des Wagens.
translations.fr: Les policiers ont tiré sur les pneus de la voiture.
translations.pt: Os policiais atiraram nos pneus do carro.

examples.text: I'll slash your tires!

translations.de: Ich zerstech’ dir die Reifen!
translations.fr: Je te lacérerai les pneus !
translations.pt: Corto-te os pneus!

more.definition: To become sleepy or weary.; To make sleepy or weary.; To become bored or impatient (with).
more.etymology: From Middle English tiren, tirien, teorien, from Old English tȳrian, tēorian (“to fail, cease, become weary, be tired, exhausted; tire, weary, exhaust”), of uncertain origin. Possibly from Proto-West Germanic *teuʀōn (“to cease”), which is possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dews- (“to fail, be behind, lag”). Compare Ancient Greek δεύομαι (deúomai, “to lack”), Sanskrit दोष (dóṣa, “crime, fault, vice, deficiency”).

examples.text: The iPhone is an extraordinary cell phone.

translations.de: Das iPhone ist ein außergewöhnliches Handy.
translations.fr: L'iPhone est un téléphone portable extraordinaire.
translations.pt: O iPhone é um telefone celular extraordinário.

examples.text: Can you give me your cell number?

translations.de: Kannst du mir deine Handy-Nummer geben?
translations.fr: Peux-tu me donner ton numéro de portable ?
translations.pt: Você me passa o seu número de telefone?

examples.text: Simply put, a human being is an aggregate of many cells.

translations.de: Einfach ausgedrückt, ein Mensch ist eine Ansammlung von Zellen.
translations.fr: Pour simplifier, un être humain est un agrégat de nombreuses cellules.
translations.pt: Em termos simples, um ser humano é um agregado de muitas células.

examples.text: I hope my cell phone is found soon.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, mein Handy wird bald gefunden.
translations.fr: J'espère que mon téléphone portable sera bientôt retrouvé.
translations.pt: Espero que meu celular seja logo encontrado.

more.definition: A single-room dwelling for a hermit.; A small monastery or nunnery dependent on a larger religious establishment.; A small room in a monastery or nunnery accommodating one person.
more.etymology: From Middle English celle, selle, from Old English cell (attested in inflected forms), from Latin cella (“chamber, small room, compartment”), later reinforced by Old French cel, sele, Old French cele. Ultimately from Proto-Italic *kelnā, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱelneh₂, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱel- (“to cover”). Doublet of cella and hall. Displaced native Old English cleofa whence English cleve.

examples.text: The amoeba is a single-celled organism.

translations.de: Die Amöbe ist ein einzelliger Organismus.
translations.fr: L'amibe est un organisme unicellulaire.
translations.pt: A ameba é um organismo unicelular.

examples.text: It's a single-cell organism.

translations.de: Das ist ein einzelliger Organismus.
translations.fr: C'est un organisme unicellulaire.
translations.pt: É um organismo unicelular.

examples.text: This cell phone is really expensive.

translations.de: Dieses Handy ist richtig teuer.
translations.fr: Ce téléphone portable est vraiment cher.
translations.pt: Este celular é realmente caro.

examples.text: The cell has a system for processing stored information.

translations.de: Die Zelle verfügt über ein System zum Verarbeiten der gespeicherten Informationen.
translations.fr: La cellule dispose d'un système pour traiter les informations stockées.
translations.pt: A célula dispõe de um sistema para processar informações armazenadas.

more.definition: To place or enclose in a cell.
more.etymology: From Middle English celle, selle, from Old English cell (attested in inflected forms), from Latin cella (“chamber, small room, compartment”), later reinforced by Old French cel, sele, Old French cele. Ultimately from Proto-Italic *kelnā, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱelneh₂, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱel- (“to cover”). Doublet of cella and hall. Displaced native Old English cleofa whence English cleve.

examples.text: They can't track us anymore.

translations.de: Sie können uns nicht mehr verfolgen.
translations.fr: Ils ne peuvent plus nous suivre.
translations.pt: Eles não podem mais nos rastrear.

examples.text: I was on the wrong track.

translations.de: Ich war auf dem Holzweg.
translations.fr: J'avais fait fausse route.
translations.pt: Eu estava no caminho errado.

examples.text: I lost track of the time.

translations.de: Ich habe völlig die Zeit vergessen.
translations.fr: Je perdis la notion du temps.
translations.pt: Eu perdi a noção do tempo.

examples.text: You're on the right track.

translations.de: Du bist auf dem richtigen Weg.
translations.fr: Tu es sur la bonne pente.
translations.pt: Você está no caminho certo.

more.definition: A mark left by something that has passed along.; A mark or impression left by the foot, either of man or animal.; The entire lower surface of the foot; said of birds, etc.
more.etymology: From Middle English trak, tracke, from Old French trac (“track of horses, trail, trace”), of uncertain origin.

examples.text: I lost track of time.

translations.de: Ich habe völlig die Zeit vergessen.
translations.fr: J'ai perdu le fil du temps.
translations.pt: Perdi a noção do tempo.

examples.text: You are way off track.

translations.de: Du bist vom Weg abgekommen.
translations.fr: Tu es hors-piste.
translations.pt: Você está fora da pista.

examples.text: This is my favorite track on the entire disc.

translations.de: Das ist mein Lieblingslied auf der ganzen CD.
translations.fr: De tout le disque, c'est ma piste préférée.
translations.pt: Esta é a minha faixa favorita no disco inteiro.

examples.text: The train was derailed by a piece of iron on the track.

translations.de: Durch ein Stück Eisen, das auf den Gleisen lag, ist der Zug entgleist.
translations.fr: Le train a déraillé à cause d'un morceau de fer qui était sur les rails.
translations.pt: O trem descarrilou por causa de um pedaço de ferro sobre os trilhos.

more.definition: To observe the (measured) state of a person or object over time.; To monitor the movement of a person or object.; To match the movement or change of a person or object.
more.etymology: From Middle English trak, tracke, from Old French trac (“track of horses, trail, trace”), of uncertain origin.

examples.text: I asked Tom to open the window.

translations.de: Ich bat Tom das Fenster zu öffnen.
translations.fr: J'ai demandé à Tom d'ouvrir la fenêtre.
translations.pt: Pedi a Tom para abrir a janela.

examples.text: I'd like to leave the windows open.

translations.de: Ich möchte die Fenster offenlassen.
translations.fr: J'aimerais laisser les fenêtres ouvertes.
translations.pt: Eu gostaria de deixar as janelas abertas.

examples.text: A bee flew out of the window.

translations.de: Eine Biene flog aus dem Fenster.
translations.fr: Une abeille vola par la fenêtre.
translations.pt: A abelha saiu pela janela.

examples.text: The cat wants the window opened.

translations.de: Die Katze möchte, dass das Fenster geöffnet wird.
translations.fr: Le chat veut que la fenêtre soit ouverte.
translations.pt: O gato quer que alguém lhe abra a janela.

more.definition: An opening, usually covered by one or more panes of clear glass, to allow light and air from outside to enter a building or vehicle.; An opening, usually covered by glass, in a shop which allows people to view the shop and its products from outside; a shop window.; The shutter, casement, sash with its fittings, or other framework, which closes a window opening.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₃ekʷ-der. Old Norse vindaugabor. From Middle English wyndowe, wyndown, from Old Norse vindauga (“window”, literally “wind-eye; wind-hole”), equivalent to wind + eye. Cognate with Scots windae and windock, Faroese vindeyga, Norwegian Bokmål vindu, Norwegian Nynorsk vindauge, Danish vindue, archaic Swedish vindöga, Elfdalian windog.

examples.text: I saw my reflection in the window.

translations.de: Ich sah mein Spiegelbild in dem Fenster.
translations.fr: J'ai vu mon reflet dans la vitre.
translations.pt: Eu vi o meu reflexo na janela.

examples.text: Does the wall have any windows?

translations.de: Hat die Wand Fenster?
translations.fr: Le mur a-t-il des fenêtres ?
translations.pt: A parede tem alguma janela?

examples.text: It is this window that he broke.

translations.de: Das ist das Fenster, das er eingeschlagen hat.
translations.fr: C'est cette fenêtre qu'il a cassée.
translations.pt: Esta é a janela que ele quebrou.

examples.text: Someone must've left the window open.

translations.de: Jemand muss das Fenster offen gelassen haben.
translations.fr: Quelqu'un doit avoir laissé la fenêtre ouverte.
translations.pt: Alguém deve ter deixado a janela aberta.

more.definition: To furnish with windows.; To place at or in a window.; To apply a window function to (a signal).
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₃ekʷ-der. Old Norse vindaugabor. From Middle English wyndowe, wyndown, from Old Norse vindauga (“window”, literally “wind-eye; wind-hole”), equivalent to wind + eye. Cognate with Scots windae and windock, Faroese vindeyga, Norwegian Bokmål vindu, Norwegian Nynorsk vindauge, Danish vindue, archaic Swedish vindöga, Elfdalian windog.

examples.text: Have you already paid the bill?

translations.de: Hast du die Rechnung bereits bezahlt?
translations.fr: As-tu déjà payé la facture?
translations.pt: Vocês já pagaram a conta?

translations.de: Tom weigerte sich, seine Rechnungen zu bezahlen.

examples.text: I've got bills to pay.

examples.text: Tom left without paying the bill.

translations.de: Tom ging, ohne die Rechnung zu bezahlen.
translations.fr: Tom est parti sans payer l'addition.
translations.pt: Tom foi embora sem pagar a conta.

more.definition: A written list or inventory. (Now obsolete except in specific senses or set phrases; bill of lading, bill of goods, etc.); A document, originally sealed; a formal statement or official memorandum. (Now obsolete except with certain qualifying words; bill of health, bill of sale etc.); A draft of a law, presented to a legislature for enactment; a proposed or projected law.
more.etymology: From Middle English bille, from Anglo-Norman bille, from Old French bulle, from Medieval Latin bulla (“seal, sealed document”). Doublet of bull (“papal bull; bubble”) and bulla.

examples.text: Do you have any one dollar bills?

translations.de: Haben sie Ein-Dollar-Scheine?
translations.fr: Est-ce que tu aurais un billet d'un dollar ?
translations.pt: Você teria uma nota de um dólar?

examples.text: If anyone can do it, Bill can.

translations.de: Wenn es jemand kann, dann Bill.
translations.fr: S'il y en a un qui peut le faire, c'est Bill.
translations.pt: Se qualquer um pode fazê-lo, Bill pode.

examples.text: You shouldn't have paid the bill.

translations.de: Du hättest die Rechnung nicht zahlen sollen.

examples.text: I'll bring you the bill immediately.

translations.fr: Je vous apporte l’addition tout de suite.
translations.pt: Trarei a conta imediatamente.

more.definition: To advertise by a bill or public notice.; To charge; to send a bill to.; to stroke bill against bill, with reference to doves; to caress in fondness
more.etymology: From Middle English bille, from Anglo-Norman bille, from Old French bulle, from Medieval Latin bulla (“seal, sealed document”). Doublet of bull (“papal bull; bubble”) and bulla.

examples.text: Well, Cupid is a terrible sniper.

translations.de: Nun, als Scharfschütze ist Amor eine Katastrophe.
translations.fr: Eh bien, Cupidon est un très mauvais tireur d'élite.
translations.pt: Bom, Cupido é um péssimo atirador.

examples.text: There was a terrible accident on the freeway.

translations.de: Auf der Autobahn gab es einen schrecklichen Unfall.
translations.fr: Il y a eu un terrible accident sur l'autoroute.
translations.pt: Houve um acidente horrível na rodovia.

examples.text: The meat was giving off a terrible smell.

translations.de: Das Fleisch roch schrecklich.
translations.fr: La viande dégageait une odeur épouvantable.
translations.pt: A carne estava exalando um cheiro terrível.

translations.fr: J'ai attrapé un rhume carabiné.

more.definition: Causing terror, alarm or fear; dreadful; Formidable, powerful.; Intense; extreme in degree or extent.

Compare terror, deter. By surface analysis, terror + -ible. Displaced Old English atol and sliþe, while also largely overtaking grimm.

examples.text: I had a terrible dream last night.

translations.de: Ich hatte letzte Nacht einen schrecklichen Traum.
translations.fr: Cette nuit, j'ai fait un rêve horrible.
translations.pt: Eu tive um sonho horrível esta noite.

examples.text: I'd make a terrible spy.

translations.de: Ich wäre ein furchtbarer Spion.
translations.fr: Je ferais un épouvantable espion.
translations.pt: Eu seria um péssimo espião.

examples.text: I've got a terrible headache.

translations.de: Ich habe schreckliche Kopfschmerzen.
translations.fr: J'ai un terrible mal de tête.
translations.pt: Estou com uma terrível dor de cabeça.

examples.text: This movie is so terrible it's hilarious.

translations.de: Dieser Film ist so schlecht, dass es schon wieder lustig ist.
translations.fr: Ce film est tellement nul que c'en est risible.
translations.pt: Esse filme é tão ruim que é engraçado.

more.etymology: Latin terribilislbor. Old French terriblebor. Inherited from Middle English terrible, from Old French terrible, from Latin terribilis (“frightful”), from terreō (“to frighten, terrify, alarm; to deter by terror, scare (away)”). Compare terror, deter. By surface analysis, terror + -ible. Displaced Old English atol and sliþe, while also largely overtaking grimm.

examples.text: He is having difficulty breathing.

translations.de: Das Atmen fällt ihm schwer.
translations.fr: Il a du mal à respirer.
translations.pt: Ele está tendo dificuldade ao respirar.

translations.fr: Une seule erreur, et vous avez échoué.

examples.text: Are you married or single?

translations.de: Bist du verheiratet oder Single?

translations.de: Sie ist jung und ledig.
translations.fr: Elle est jeune et célibataire.

examples.text: Is she single or married?

translations.de: Ist sie ledig oder verheiratet?
translations.fr: Est-elle célibataire ou mariée ?

examples.text: Is he married or single?

translations.de: Ist er verheiratet oder ledig?
translations.fr: Est-il marié ou célibataire ?
translations.pt: Ele é casado ou solteiro?

examples.text: I can't afford to waste a single yen.

translations.de: Ich kann es mir nicht leisten, nur einen einzigen Yen zu verschwenden.
translations.fr: Je ne peux me permettre de gaspiller le moindre yen.
translations.pt: Eu não posso gastar nem um iene.

examples.text: There isn't a single cloud in the sky.

translations.de: Nicht eine einzige Wolke ist am Himmel.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas un seul nuage dans le ciel.
translations.pt: Não há uma nuvem sequer no céu.

more.definition: To get a hit that advances the batter exactly one base.; To thin out.; To take the irregular gait called singlefoot.
more.etymology: From Middle English single, sengle, from Old French sengle, saingle, sangle, from Latin singulus, a diminutive derived from Proto-Indo-European *sem- (“one”). Akin to Latin simplex (“simple”). See simple, and compare singular.

examples.text: A bee is not a bird.

translations.de: Eine Biene ist kein Vogel.
translations.fr: Une abeille n'est pas un oiseau.
translations.pt: A abelha não é um pássaro.

examples.text: The bird is trying to get the insect.

translations.de: Der Vogel versucht, das Insekt zu fangen.
translations.fr: L'oiseau tente de capturer l'insecte.
translations.pt: O pássaro tenta capturar o inseto.

examples.text: A penguin is a bird that cannot fly.

translations.de: Ein Pinguin ist ein Vogel, der nicht fliegen kann.
translations.fr: Le pingouin est un oiseau qui ne peut pas voler.
translations.pt: O pinguim é uma ave que não pode voar.

examples.text: What kind of bird is this?

translations.de: Was für ein Vogel ist das?
translations.fr: Quel est cet oiseau ?
translations.pt: Que tipo de pássaro é este?

more.definition: Able to be passed with very little work; having the nature of a bird course.
more.etymology: From Middle English bird, brid, from Old English bridd (“chick, fledgling, chicken”), of uncertain origin (see Old English bridd for more). Originally from a term used of birds that could not fly (chicks, fledglings, chickens) as opposed to the general Old English term for flying birds, fugol (modern fowl). Gradually replaced fowl as the most common term starting in the 14th century.

examples.text: The eagle is a bird of prey.

translations.de: Der Adler ist ein Raubvogel.
translations.fr: L'aigle est un rapace.
translations.pt: A águia é uma ave de rapina.

examples.text: I killed two birds with one stone.

translations.de: Ich schlug zwei Fliegen mit einer Klappe.
translations.fr: J'ai fait d'une pierre deux coups.
translations.pt: Eu matei dois passarinhos com uma pedra.

examples.text: What is the name of that bird?

translations.de: Welchen Namen hat dieser Vogel?
translations.fr: Comment s'appelle cet oiseau ?
translations.pt: Qual é o nome deste pássaro?

examples.text: I threw a stone at the bird.

translations.de: Ich warf einen Stein nach dem Vogel.
translations.fr: Je jetai une pierre en direction de l'oiseau.
translations.pt: Atirei uma pedra ao pássaro.

more.definition: An animal of the clade (traditionally class) Aves in the phylum Chordata, characterized by being warm-blooded, having feathers and wings usually capable of flight, having a beaked mouth, and laying eggs.; A girl or woman, especially one considered sexually attractive.; A girlfriend.
more.etymology: From Middle English bird, brid, from Old English bridd (“chick, fledgling, chicken”), of uncertain origin (see Old English bridd for more). examples.text: There are many birds in this park.

translations.de: In diesem Park sind viele Vögel.
translations.fr: Il y a beaucoup d'oiseaux dans ce parc.
translations.pt: Há muitos pássaros neste parque.

examples.text: I see a bird on the roof.

translations.de: Ich sehe einen Vogel auf dem Dach.
translations.fr: Je vois un oiseau sur le toit.
translations.pt: Estou vendo um pássaro no telhado.

examples.text: The boy observed the birds all day.

translations.de: Der Junge beobachtete die Vögel den ganzen Tag lang.
translations.fr: Le petit garçon observa les oiseaux toute la journée.
translations.pt: O menino ficou o dia todo observando os pássaros.

examples.text: A gigantic bird came flying toward him.

translations.de: Ein riesiger Vogel kam auf ihn zu geflogen.
translations.fr: Un oiseau géant vola vers lui.
translations.pt: Um pássaro gigantesco veio voando na sua direção.

more.definition: To observe or identify wild birds in their natural environment.; To catch or shoot birds; to hunt birds.; To seek for game or plunder; to thieve.
more.etymology: From Middle English bird, brid, from Old English bridd (“chick, fledgling, chicken”), of uncertain origin (see Old English bridd for more). Originally from a term used of birds that could not fly (chicks, fledglings, chickens) as opposed to the general Old English term for flying birds, fugol (modern fowl). Gradually replaced fowl as the most common term starting in the 14th century.

examples.text: How can I serve you?

translations.de: Womit kann ich Ihnen dienen?
translations.fr: Que puis-je pour votre service ?

examples.text: In Spain they serve lunch at about two o'clock.

translations.de: In Spanien servieren sie das Mittagessen ungefähr um zwei Uhr.
translations.fr: En Espagne, on sert le dîner vers deux heures.
translations.pt: Na Espanha, serve-se o almoço lá pelas duas.

examples.text: I'll be very happy if I can serve you.

translations.de: Ich würde mich sehr freuen, wenn ich dir behilflich sein kann.
translations.fr: Je serai très heureux de pouvoir te servir.
translations.pt: Ficarei muito feliz se puder servi-lo.

examples.text: It's better to chill white wine before you serve it.

translations.de: Es ist besser, den Weißwein vor dem Servieren zu kühlen.
translations.fr: Il vaut mieux refroidir le vin blanc avant que vous serviez.
translations.pt: É melhor esfriar o vinho branco antes de servir.

more.definition: An act of putting the ball or shuttlecock in play in various games.; A portion of food or drink, a serving.; An impressive presentation (especially of a person's appearance).
more.etymology: Old French servirbor. From Middle English serven, from Old French servir, from Latin serviō (“be a slave; serve”), from Latin servus (“slave; servant”), which perhaps derives from Etruscan (compare Etruscan proper names 𐌔𐌄𐌓𐌅𐌉 (servi), 𐌔𐌄𐌓𐌅𐌄 (serve)), or from Proto-Indo-European *ser- (“watch over, protect”).

examples.text: Does this restaurant serve vegan dishes?

translations.de: Serviert dieses Restaurant vegane Gerichte?
translations.fr: Ce restaurant sert-il des plats végétaliens ?
translations.pt: Este restaurante serve pratos veganos?

examples.text: Supper is served at nine-thirty.

translations.de: Das Abendessen wird neun Uhr dreißig serviert.
translations.fr: Le dîner est servi à neuf heures et demie.
translations.pt: O jantar será servido às nove e meia.

examples.text: It serves you right.

translations.de: Das hast du verdient!
translations.fr: Bien fait pour vous.
translations.pt: Isso é bem feito para você.

examples.text: What time will dinner be served?

translations.de: Wann wird das Abendessen serviert?
translations.fr: À quelle heure le diner sera-t-il servi ?
translations.pt: Que hora será servido o jantar?

more.definition: To be a formal servant for (a god or deity); to worship in an official capacity.; To be a servant for; to work for, to be employed by.; To wait upon (someone) at table; to set food and drink in front of, to help (someone) to food, meals etc.
more.etymology: Old French servirbor. From Middle English serven, from Old French servir, from Latin serviō (“be a slave; serve”), from Latin servus (“slave; servant”), which perhaps derives from Etruscan (compare Etruscan proper names 𐌔𐌄𐌓𐌅𐌉 (servi), 𐌔𐌄𐌓𐌅𐌄 (serve)), or from Proto-Indo-European *ser- (“watch over, protect”).

examples.text: A large machine is moving in the sky.

translations.de: Viele Leute benutzen Geldautomaten, um Geld abzuheben.
translations.fr: Beaucoup de gens utilisent des distributeurs de billets pour retirer de l'argent.
translations.pt: Muitas pessoas utilizam caixas eletrônicos para retirar dinheiro.

examples.text: Someday I'll buy a cotton candy machine.

translations.de: Eines Tages werde ich eine Zuckerwattemaschine kaufen.

translations.pt: Um dia eu vou comprar uma máquina de fazer algodão doce.

examples.text: We bought a new washing machine.

translations.de: Wir haben eine neue Waschmaschine gekauft.

examples.text: I am repairing the washing machine.

translations.de: Ich repariere die Waschmaschine.

translations.pt: Estou consertando a máquina de lavar.

examples.text: The factory uses many complicated machines.

translations.de: In der Fabrik werden viele komplizierte Maschinen eingesetzt.
translations.fr: L'usine utilise de nombreuses machines compliquées.
translations.pt: A fábrica usa muitas máquinas complicadas.

examples.text: The washing machine has broken down.

translations.de: Die Waschmaschine ist kaputtgegangen.

translations.pt: A máquina de lavar roupa quebrou.

examples.text: Is there a washing machine in the house?

translations.de: Gibt es im Hause eine Waschmaschine?

translations.pt: Tem alguma máquina de lavar na casa?

more.definition: To make by machinery.; To shape or finish by machinery; (usually, more specifically) to shape subtractively by metal-cutting with machine-controlled toolpaths.

Displaced native Old English searu.

examples.text: I don't want to go anywhere.

translations.fr: Personne ne m'attend nulle part.
translations.pt: Ninguém está me esperando em nenhum lugar.

examples.text: We're not going anywhere today.

translations.pt: Não vamos a lugar nenhum hoje.

examples.text: Have you seen my glasses anywhere?

translations.fr: As-tu vu mes lunettes quelque part ?

examples.text: You can put it anywhere.

translations.fr: Tu peux le mettre n'importe où.

examples.text: These minerals are not found anywhere else in the world.

examples.text: I never go anywhere.

translations.fr: Je ne vais jamais nulle part.

examples.text: Are you going anywhere?

translations.de: Man kann überall hingehen.
translations.fr: Tu peux aller n'importe où.

examples.text: It's more dangerous than I thought.

translations.de: Es ist gefährlicher, als ich dachte.
translations.fr: C'est plus dangereux que je ne le pensais.
translations.pt: É mais perigoso do que eu pensava.

examples.text: It's dangerous to climb this mountain.

translations.de: Es ist gefährlich, diesen Berg zu besteigen.
translations.fr: Gravir cette montagne est dangereux.
translations.pt: É perigoso escalar esta montanha.

examples.text: This river is dangerous to swim in.

translations.de: Es ist gefährlich, in diesem Fluss zu schwimmen.
translations.fr: Nager dans cette rivière est dangereux.
translations.pt: É perigoso nadar neste rio.

examples.text: These activities are interesting but dangerous.

translations.de: Diese Aktivitäten sind interessant, aber gefährlich.
translations.fr: Ces activités sont intéressantes, mais elles sont dangereuses.
translations.pt: Essas atividades são interessantes, mas são perigosas.

more.definition: Full of danger.; Causing danger; ready to do harm or injury.

examples.text: Children often cry just to attract attention.

translations.de: Kinder weinen oft nur, um Aufmerksamkeit zu bekommen.
translations.fr: Les enfants pleurent souvent juste pour attirer l'attention.
translations.pt: As crianças geralmente choram apenas para chamar atenção.

examples.text: You must pay attention to his advice.

translations.de: Du musst seinem Rat Beachtung schenken.
translations.fr: Tu dois prêter attention à ses conseils.
translations.pt: Você deve levar o conselho dele a sério.

examples.text: I should've paid a little more attention.

translations.fr: J'aurais dû faire un peu plus attention.
translations.pt: Eu deveria ter prestado um pouco mais de atenção.

examples.text: He paid no attention to her.

more.definition: Mental focus.; An action or remark expressing concern for or interest in someone or something, especially romantic interest.; A state of alertness in the standing position.

examples.text: She gets good marks in English.

translations.pt: Ela tira boas notas em inglês.

translations.fr: À vos marques, prêts, partez !

more.definition: That which is left; relic; remainder.; That which is left of a human being after the life is gone; relics; a dead body.; Posthumous works or productions, especially literary works.
more.etymology: From Middle English remainen, from Old French remain-, stressed stem of remanoir, from Latin remaneō, maneō, from Proto-Indo-European *men- (“to stay”). More at beleave and belive.

examples.text: Not knowing what to say, I remained silent.

more.definition: To stay after others or other parts have been removed or otherwise disappeared.; To be left after a number or quantity has been subtracted or cut off; to be left as not included or comprised.; To continue unchanged in place, form, or condition, or undiminished in quantity; to abide; to stay; to endure; to last.
more.etymology: From Middle English remainen, from Old French remain-, stressed stem of remanoir, from Latin remaneō, maneō, from Proto-Indo-European *men- (“to stay”). Displaced native Middle English beliven, bliven (“to remain”) (from Old English belīfan (“to remain, stay”)) due to confluence with related Middle English beleven (“to leave behind”), with which it merged. more.definition: A facial expression comprised by flexing the muscles of both ends of one's mouth, often showing the front teeth, without vocalisation, and in humans is a common involuntary or voluntary expression of happiness, pleasure, amusement, goodwill, or anxiety.; Favour; propitious regard.
