examples.text: I have a dog and a cat.

translations.de: Ich habe einen Hund und eine Katze.
translations.fr: J'ai un chien et un chat.
translations.pt: Eu tenho um cachorro e um gato.

examples.text: The cat was basking in the sun.

translations.de: Die Katze aalte sich in der Sonne.
translations.fr: Le chat se prélassait au soleil.
translations.pt: O gato estava se aquecendo ao sol.

examples.text: The cat is sleeping on the chair.

translations.de: Die Katze schläft auf dem Stuhl.
translations.fr: Le chat dort sur la chaise.
translations.pt: O gato está dormindo na cadeira.

examples.text: My canary was killed by a cat.

translations.de: Mein Kanarienvogel wurde von einer Katze getötet.
translations.fr: Mon canari a été tué par un chat.
translations.pt: Meu canário foi morto por um gato.

more.definition: Catastrophic; terrible, disastrous.
more.etymology: Abbreviations.

examples.text: The cat is sitting on the desk.

translations.de: Die Katze sitzt auf dem Schreibtisch.
translations.fr: Le chat est assis sur le bureau.
translations.pt: O gato está sentado na mesa.

examples.text: I don't like cats very much.

translations.de: Ich mag Katzen nicht so besonders.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas beaucoup les chats.
translations.pt: Eu não gosto muito de gatos.

examples.text: I saw a cat on the roof.

translations.de: Ich habe eine Katze auf dem Dach gesehen.
translations.fr: J'ai aperçu un chat sur le toit.
translations.pt: Eu vi um gato no telhado.

examples.text: I'd like to have a cat.

translations.de: Ich hätte gern eine Katze.
translations.fr: Je voudrais avoir un chat.
translations.pt: Eu queria ter um gato.

more.definition: A mammal of the family Felidae.; A carnivorous, four-legged, generally furry domesticated species (Felis catus) of feline animal, commonly kept as a house pet.; The flesh of this animal eaten as food.
more.etymology: From Middle English cat, catte, from Old English catt (“male cat”), catte (“female cat”), from Proto-West Germanic *kattu, from Proto-Germanic *kattuz, generally thought to be from Late Latin cattus (“domestic cat”) (c. 350, Palladius), from Latin catta (c. 75 A.D., Martial), possibly from an Afroasiatic language. Doublet of gato.

examples.text: The cat is sleeping on the sofa.

translations.de: Die Katze schläft auf dem Sofa.
translations.fr: Le chat dort sur le canapé.
translations.pt: O gato está dormindo no sofá.

examples.text: I have a dog and two cats.

translations.de: Ich habe einen Hund und zwei Katzen.
translations.fr: J'ai un chien et deux chats.
translations.pt: Eu tenho um cachorro e dois gatos.

examples.text: We have a cat and a dog.

translations.de: Wir haben eine Katze und einen Hund.
translations.fr: Nous avons un chat et un chien.
translations.pt: Temos um gato e um cachorro.

examples.text: We keep three dogs and a cat.

translations.de: Wir haben drei Hunde und eine Katze.
translations.fr: Nous gardons trois chiens et un chat.
translations.pt: Nós temos três cachorros e um gato.

more.definition: To hoist (an anchor) by its ring so that it hangs at the cathead.; To flog with a cat-o'-nine-tails.; To go wandering at night.
more.etymology: From Middle English cat, catte, from Old English catt (“male cat”), catte (“female cat”), from Proto-West Germanic *kattu, from Proto-Germanic *kattuz, generally thought to be from Late Latin cattus (“domestic cat”) (c. 350, Palladius), from Latin catta (c. 75 A.D., Martial), possibly from an Afroasiatic language. Doublet of gato.

examples.text: Jugurtha and Rome were bitter enemies.

translations.de: Jugurtha und Rom waren erbitterte Feinde.
translations.fr: Jugurtha et Rome étaient des ennemis jurés.
translations.pt: Jugurta e Roma eram inimigos ferrenhos.

examples.text: The friend of my enemy is my enemy.

translations.de: Der Freund meines Feindes ist mein Feind.
translations.fr: L'ami de mon ennemi est mon ennemi.
translations.pt: O amigo do meu inimigo é meu inimigo.

examples.text: I'm my own worst enemy.

translations.de: Ich bin mir selbst der ärgste Feind.
translations.fr: Je suis mon pire ennemi.
translations.pt: Eu sou o meu próprio pior inimigo.

examples.text: Tom has a lot of enemies.

translations.de: Tom hat viele Feinde.
translations.fr: Tom a beaucoup d'ennemis.
translations.pt: Tom tem muitos inimigos.

more.definition: Someone who is hostile to, feels hatred towards, opposes the interests of, or intends injury to someone else.; A hostile force or nation; a fighting member of such a force or nation.; Something harmful or threatening to another
more.etymology: From Middle English enemy, enemye, enmy, borrowed from Old French enemi, anemi (Modern French ennemi), from Latin inimīcus, from in- (“not”) + amīcus (“friend”). Displaced Middle English fend (“enemy”), from Old English fēond (“enemy”), which survived into Modern English as fiend, but with a different meaning. Doublet of inimic.

examples.text: Who are the enemies of the youth?

translations.de: Wer sind die Feinde der Jugend?
translations.fr: Qui sont les ennemis de la jeunesse ?
translations.pt: Quem são os inimigos da juventude?

examples.text: Don't make an enemy of him.

translations.de: Mach ihn dir nicht zum Feind.
translations.fr: Ne t'en fais pas un ennemi.
translations.pt: Não faça dele um inimigo.

examples.text: Today's friends are tomorrow's enemies.

translations.de: Was heute Freund, ist morgen Feind.
translations.fr: L'ami d'aujourd'hui est l'ennemi de demain.
translations.pt: Os amigos de hoje são os inimigos de amanhã.

examples.text: The city was bombed by enemy planes.

translations.de: Die Stadt wurde von Feindflugzeugen bombardiert.
translations.fr: La ville a subi le bombardement d’avions ennemis.
translations.pt: A cidade foi bombardeada por aviões inimigos.

more.definition: To make an enemy of.
more.etymology: From Middle English enemy, enemye, enmy, borrowed from Old French enemi, anemi (Modern French ennemi), from Latin inimīcus, from in- (“not”) + amīcus (“friend”). Displaced Middle English fend (“enemy”), from Old English fēond (“enemy”), which survived into Modern English as fiend, but with a different meaning. Doublet of inimic.

examples.text: What's your favorite memory from childhood?

translations.de: Welches ist Ihre liebste Kindheitserinnerung?
translations.fr: Quel est ton meilleur souvenir d'enfance ?
translations.pt: Qual é a lembrança favorita de sua infância?

examples.text: Creditors have better memories than debtors.

translations.de: Gläubiger haben ein besseres Gedächtnis als Schuldner.
translations.fr: Les créanciers ont meilleure mémoire que les débiteurs.
translations.pt: Os credores têm melhor memória que os devedores.

examples.text: He is suffering from loss of memory.

translations.de: Er leidet an Gedächtnisverlust.
translations.fr: Il souffre d'amnésie.
translations.pt: Ele está sofrendo de perda de memória.

examples.text: I wish I had a better memory.

translations.de: Ich wünschte, ich hätte ein besseres Gedächtnis.
translations.fr: J'aurais aimé avoir meilleure mémoire.
translations.pt: Queria ter uma memória melhor.

more.definition: The ability of the brain to record information or impressions with the facility of recalling them later, usually at will.; A record of a thing or an event stored and available for later use by an organism.; The part of a computer that stores variable executable code or data (RAM) or unalterable executable code or default data (ROM).
more.etymology: From Anglo-Norman memorie, Old French memoire etc., from Latin memoria (“the faculty of remembering, remembrance, memory, a historical account”), from memor (“mindful, remembering”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)mer- (to remember), related to Ancient Greek μνήμη (mnḗmē, “memory”) μέρμερος (mérmeros, “anxious”), μέριμνα (mérimna, “care, thought”), Old English ġemimor (“mindful, remembering”). More at mimmer.

examples.text: His behavior is my primary concern.

translations.de: Sein Verhalten ist meine größte Sorge.
translations.fr: Son comportement est ma préoccupation première.
translations.pt: Seu comportamento é minha preocupação primária.

examples.text: The question doesn't concern me.

translations.de: Die Frage betrifft mich nicht.
translations.fr: Cette question ne me concerne pas.
translations.pt: Essa questão não me concerne.

examples.text: It doesn't concern you.

translations.de: Das geht dich nichts an.
translations.fr: Ça ne te concerne pas.
translations.pt: Isso não te interessa.

examples.text: Don't concern yourself.

translations.de: Mach dir keine Sorgen.
translations.fr: Ne vous inquiétez pas.
translations.pt: Não se preocupe.

more.definition: That which affects one’s welfare or happiness. A matter of interest to someone.; The placement of interest or worry on a subject.; A worry; a sense that something may be wrong; an identification of a possible problem.
more.etymology: Borrowed from Middle French concerner, from Medieval Latin concernō, concernere (“I distinguish, have respect to”), from Latin concernō (“to mix, sift, or mingle together, as in a sieve”), combined form of con- + cernō (“distinguish”).

examples.text: Are you concerned about water consumption?

translations.de: Sind Sie besorgt über den Wasserverbrauch?
translations.fr: La consommation d'eau vous préoccupe-t-elle ?
translations.pt: Você se preocupa com o consumo de água?

examples.text: It's no concern of mine.

translations.de: Das ist nicht meine Angelegenheit.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas mon affaire.
translations.pt: Não é da minha conta.

examples.text: Climate change concerns us all.

translations.de: Der Klimawandel geht uns alle an.
translations.fr: Le changement climatique nous concerne tous.
translations.pt: As alterações climáticas dizem respeito a todos nós.

examples.text: Your problems don't concern me.

translations.de: Deine Probleme kümmern mich nicht.
translations.fr: Tes problèmes ne me concernent pas.
translations.pt: Seus problemas não me interessam.

more.definition: To relate or belong to; to have reference to or connection with; to affect the interest of; to be of importance to.; To engage by feeling or sentiment; to interest.; To make somebody worried.
more.etymology: Borrowed from Middle French concerner, from Medieval Latin concernō, concernere (“I distinguish, have respect to”), from Latin concernō (“to mix, sift, or mingle together, as in a sieve”), combined form of con- + cernō (“distinguish”).

examples.text: He likes to travel. I do, too.

translations.de: Er reist gerne. Ich auch.
translations.fr: Il aime voyager. Moi aussi.
translations.pt: Ele gosta de viajar. Também eu.

examples.text: Jean travels less than Alice.

translations.de: Johanna verreist seltener als Elke.
translations.fr: Jean voyage moins qu'Alice.
translations.pt: Jean viaja menos que Alice.

examples.text: I want to travel to the moon.

translations.de: Ich will zum Mond reisen.
translations.fr: Je veux voyager sur la Lune.
translations.pt: Quero viajar para a Lua.

examples.text: I'd like to travel alone.

translations.de: Ich würde gerne alleine reisen.
translations.fr: J'aimerais voyager seul.
translations.pt: Gostaria de viajar sozinha.

more.definition: The act of traveling; passage from place to place.; A series of journeys.; An account of one's travels.
more.etymology: From Middle English travail, travell, from Old French travail, travaille, travaillie, traval, travalle, traveaul, traveil, traveille, travel. Doublet of travail.

examples.text: He doesn't like traveling by plane.

translations.de: Er reist nicht gerne mit dem Flugzeug.
translations.fr: Il n'aime pas voyager en avion.
translations.pt: Ele não gosta de viajar de avião.

examples.text: Have you ever traveled in a plane?

translations.de: Bist du schon einmal mit dem Flugzeug verreist?
translations.fr: Avez-vous déjà voyagé en avion ?
translations.pt: Vocês já viajaram de avião?

examples.text: I like to travel and meet new people.

translations.de: Ich reise gern und lerne neue Leute kennen.
translations.fr: J'aime voyager et rencontrer de nouvelles personnes.
translations.pt: Eu gosto de viajar e conhecer gente nova.

examples.text: She was afraid of travelling alone.

translations.de: Sie hatte Angst, allein zu verreisen.
translations.fr: Elle avait peur de voyager seule.
translations.pt: Ela tinha medo de viajar sozinha.

more.definition: To be on a journey, often for pleasure or business and with luggage; to go from one place to another.; To pass from one place to another; to move or transmit.; To move illegally by walking or running without dribbling the ball.
more.etymology: PIE word *tréyes From Middle English travelen (“to make a laborious journey, travel”) from Middle Scots travailen (“to toil, work, travel”), alteration of Middle English travaillen (“to toil, work”), from Old French travailler (“to trouble, suffer, be worn out”). See the doublets travail and travois. Compare typologically routine << Latin rupta via.

examples.text: I'm going to be a teacher.

translations.de: Ich werde Lehrerin sein.
translations.fr: Je vais être enseignante.
translations.pt: Eu vou ser professor.

examples.text: I erased the blackboard for the teacher.

translations.de: Ich wischte für den Lehrer die Tafel.
translations.fr: J'ai effacé le tableau pour la maîtresse.
translations.pt: Eu apaguei o quadro para o professor.

examples.text: Mr. Hirayama is a very good teacher.

translations.de: Herr Hirayama ist ein sehr guter Lehrer.
translations.fr: Monsieur Hirayama est un très bon professeur.
translations.pt: O Senhor Hirayama é um professor muito bom.

examples.text: The new teacher is in the classroom.

translations.de: Die neue Lehrerin ist in der Klasse.
translations.fr: Le nouveau professeur est dans la classe.
translations.pt: O novo professor está na sala de aula.

more.definition: A person who teaches, especially one employed in a school; preceptor.; The index finger; the forefinger.; An indication; a lesson.
more.etymology: From Middle English techere, equivalent to teach + -er. More at teach.

examples.text: I want to speak to a lawyer.

translations.de: Ich will mit einem Anwalt sprechen.
translations.fr: Je veux parler à un avocat.
translations.pt: Eu quero falar com um advogado.

examples.text: What's your lawyer's name?

translations.de: Wie ist der Name deines Anwalts?
translations.fr: Comment s'appelle ton avocat ?
translations.pt: Qual é o nome do seu advogado?

examples.text: I need a lawyer who can speak French.

translations.de: Ich brauche einen Anwalt, der Französisch spricht.
translations.fr: J'ai besoin d'un avocat qui parle français.
translations.pt: Eu preciso de um advogado que saiba falar francês.

examples.text: I just had a talk with your lawyer.

translations.de: Ich hatte gerade ein Gespräch mit deinem Anwalt.
translations.fr: Je viens d'avoir une conversation avec ton avocat.
translations.pt: Acabei de ter uma conversa com seu advogado.

more.definition: A professional person with a graduate law degree that qualifies for legal work (such as Juris Doctor); A professional person qualified (as by a law degree or bar exam) and authorized to practice law as an attorney-at-law, solicitor, advocate, barrister or equivalent, i.e. represent parties in lawsuits or trials and give legal advice.; A legal layman who argues points of law.
more.etymology: From Middle English lawiere, lawier, lawer, equivalent to law + -yer.

examples.text: I want to speak to my lawyer.

translations.de: Ich will meinen Anwalt sprechen.
translations.fr: Je veux parler à mon avocat.
translations.pt: Quero falar com meu advogado.

examples.text: I can't afford a lawyer.

translations.de: Ich kann mir keinen Anwalt leisten.
translations.fr: Je ne peux me permettre un avocat.
translations.pt: Não tenho condições de contratar um advogado.

examples.text: I don't need a lawyer.

translations.de: Ich brauche keinen Anwalt.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas besoin d'avocat.
translations.pt: Eu não preciso de um advogado.

examples.text: Tom wants to be a lawyer.

translations.de: Tom will Jurist werden.
translations.fr: Tom veut être avocat.
translations.pt: Tom quer ser advogado.

more.definition: To practice law.; To perform, or attempt to perform, the work of a lawyer.; To make legalistic arguments.
more.etymology: From Middle English lawiere, lawier, lawer, equivalent to law + -yer.

examples.text: Please understand my position.

translations.de: Bitte verstehe meine Position.
translations.fr: Veuillez comprendre ma position.
translations.pt: Por favor, entenda minha posição.

examples.text: In your position, I'd probably have done the same thing.

translations.de: An deiner Stelle hätte ich sicherlich auch so gehandelt.
translations.fr: À ta place, j'aurais probablement fait la même chose.
translations.pt: Em teu lugar, provavelmente teria feito a mesma coisa.

examples.text: Tom applied for the position, but he didn't get it.

translations.de: Tom hat sich für die Stelle beworben, aber er hat sie nicht bekommen.
translations.fr: Tom a postulé pour le poste, mais il ne l'a pas obtenu.
translations.pt: O Tomás candidatou-se ao lugar, mas não o conseguiu.

examples.text: Which do I prefer? Sex or chess? It depends on the position.

translations.de: Welches bevorzuge ich? Sex oder Schach? Das hängt von der Position ab.
translations.fr: Lequel est-ce que je préfère ? Le sexe ou les échecs ? Cela dépend de la position.
translations.pt: Qual eu prefiro? Sexo ou xadrez? Depende da posição.

more.definition: A place or location.; A post of employment; a job.; A status or rank.
more.etymology: From Middle English posicioun, from Old French posicion, from Latin positiō (“a putting, position”), from positus (“placed, situated”), past participle of pōnō (“to place”); see ponent. Compare apposition, composition, deposition; see pose.

examples.text: All the players were in position.

translations.de: Alle Spieler waren in Position.
translations.fr: Tous les joueurs étaient en position.
translations.pt: Todos os jogadores estavam em posição.

examples.text: Are you content with your position in the company?

translations.de: Sind Sie mit Ihrer Position im Unternehmen zufrieden?
translations.fr: Êtes-vous satisfait de votre situation dans la société ?
translations.pt: Você está satisfeito com sua posição na empresa?

examples.text: Put yourself in my position.

translations.de: Versetze dich in meine Lage.
translations.fr: Mets-toi à ma place.
translations.pt: Coloque-se em meu lugar.

examples.text: Is everything in position?

translations.de: Ist alles an seinem Platz?
translations.fr: Est-ce que tout est en place ?
translations.pt: Está tudo em posição?

more.definition: To put into place.
more.etymology: From Middle English posicioun, from Old French posicion, from Latin positiō (“a putting, position”), from positus (“placed, situated”), past participle of pōnō (“to place”); see ponent. Compare apposition, composition, deposition; see pose.

examples.text: Have your brothers won the match?

translations.de: Haben Ihre Brüder das Match gewonnen?
translations.fr: Vos frères ont-ils gagné le match ?
translations.pt: Teus irmãos ganharam a partida?

examples.text: That dress matches her red hair.

translations.de: Das Kleid passt gut zu ihren roten Haaren.
translations.fr: Cette robe va bien avec ses cheveux roux.
translations.pt: Esse vestido combina com o seu cabelo ruivo.

examples.text: Does your carpet match your drapes?

translations.de: Passt Ihr Teppich zu Ihren Vorhängen?
translations.fr: Votre tapis est-il assorti à vos rideaux ?
translations.pt: O tapete da senhora combina com suas cortinas?

examples.text: The tennis match was postponed due to rain.

translations.de: Das Tennisspiel wurde aufgrund des Regens verschoben.
translations.fr: Le match de tennis a été reporté en raison de la pluie.

translations.fr: Y a-t-il de la place pour une personne de plus ?
translations.pt: Tem espaço para mais uma pessoa?

examples.text: There is no air in space.

translations.de: Im Weltraum gibt es keine Luft.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas d'air dans l'espace.
translations.pt: Não há ar no Espaço.

more.definition: The distance between objects.; A physical extent across two or three dimensions (sometimes for or to do something).; A physical extent in all directions, seen as an attribute of the universe (now usually considered as a part of space-time), or a mathematical model of this.
more.etymology: Latin spatiumlbor. Anglo-Norman spacebor. From Middle English space, from Anglo-Norman space, variant of espace, espas, et al.; and spaze, variant of espace, from Latin spatium, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)peh₂- (“to stretch, to pull”). Partially displaced native Old English rum, whence Modern English room.

examples.text: Is there space for one more person?

translations.de: Ist noch Platz für eine weitere Person?
translations.fr: Y a-t-il de la place pour une personne de plus ?
translations.pt: Tem espaço para mais uma pessoa?

examples.text: The eternal silence of these infinite spaces terrifies me.

translations.de: Das ewige Schweigen dieser unendlichen Räume schreckt mich.
translations.fr: Le silence éternel de ces espaces infinis m'effraie.
translations.pt: O eterno silêncio desses espaços infinitos me amedronta.

examples.text: This document takes up a lot of space.

translations.de: Dieses Dokument nimmt viel Platz ein.
translations.fr: Ce document prend beaucoup de place.
translations.pt: Este documento ocupa muito espaço.

examples.text: The bed took up a lot of space.

translations.de: Das Bett hat viel Platz weggenommen.
translations.fr: Le lit prenait beaucoup de place.
translations.pt: A cama tomou muito espaço.

more.definition: To set some distance apart.; To insert or utilise spaces in a written text.; To space out (become distracted, lose focus).
more.etymology: Latin spatiumlbor. Anglo-Norman spacebor. From Middle English space, from Anglo-Norman space, variant of espace, espas, et al.; and spaze, variant of espace, from Latin spatium, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)peh₂- (“to stretch, to pull”). Partially displaced native Old English rum, whence Modern English room.

examples.text: War is peace. Freedom is slavery. Ignorance is strength.

translations.de: Krieg ist Friede. Freiheit ist Sklaverei. Unwissenheit ist Kraft.
translations.fr: La guerre c'est la paix, la liberté c'est l'esclavage, l'ignorance c'est la force.
translations.pt: Guerra é paz. Liberdade é escravidão. Ignorância é força.

examples.text: The whole nation wants peace.

translations.de: Das ganze Land will Frieden.
translations.fr: Toute la nation veut la paix.
translations.pt: Toda a nação quer paz.

examples.text: We are longing for peace.

translations.de: Wir sehnen uns nach Frieden.
translations.fr: Nous désirons ardemment la paix.
translations.pt: Ansiamos pela paz.

examples.text: An olive branch symbolizes peace.

translations.de: Ein Ölzweig symbolisiert den Frieden.
translations.fr: Une branche d'olivier symbolise la paix.
translations.pt: Um ramo de oliveira simboliza a paz.

more.definition: Peace out; goodbye.
more.etymology: Anglo-Norman peisbor. From Middle English pees, pes, pais, borrowed from Anglo-Norman peis and Old French pais (“peace”), from Latin pāx (“peace”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂ḱ- (“to fasten, stick, place”), related to Latin pacīscor (“agree, stipulate”), Latin pangō (“fasten, fix”); see pact. Doublet of pax. Displaced native Old English sibb, frēols, and broadly ousted friþ (modern frith).

examples.text: They only wanted a just peace.

translations.de: Sie wollten nur einen gerechten Frieden.
translations.fr: Ils voulaient seulement une paix juste.
translations.pt: Queriam tão somente uma paz justa.

examples.text: Nothing is as important as peace.

translations.de: Nichts ist so wichtig wie Friede.
translations.fr: Rien n'est aussi important que la paix.
translations.pt: Nada é tão importante como a paz.

examples.text: They exchange peace for war.

translations.de: Sie tauschen Frieden gegen Krieg.
translations.fr: Ils changent la paix pour la guerre.
translations.pt: Eles trocam a paz pela guerra.

examples.text: Reconciliation among religions is the foundation of world peace.

translations.de: Versöhnung zwischen den Religionen ist die Grundlage für den Weltfrieden.
translations.fr: Le rapprochement entre religions est le fondement de la paix mondiale.
translations.pt: A reconciliação entre as religiões é fundamental para a paz mundial.

more.definition: A state of tranquility, quiet, and harmony. For instance, a state free from civil disturbance.; A feeling of tranquility, free from oppressive and unpleasant thoughts and emotions.; Death.
more.etymology: Anglo-Norman peisbor. From Middle English pees, pes, pais, borrowed from Anglo-Norman peis and Old French pais (“peace”), from Latin pāx (“peace”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂ḱ- (“to fasten, stick, place”), related to Latin pacīscor (“agree, stipulate”), Latin pangō (“fasten, fix”); see pact. Doublet of pax. Displaced native Old English sibb, frēols, and broadly ousted friþ (modern frith).

examples.text: The war is over. Man can live in peace again.

translations.de: Der Krieg ist vorbei. Der Mensch kann wieder in Frieden leben.
translations.fr: La guerre est finie. L'homme peut à nouveau vivre en paix.
translations.pt: A guerra acabou. O homem pode viver em paz novamente.

examples.text: We come in peace.

translations.de: Wir kommen in Frieden.
translations.fr: Nous venons en paix.
translations.pt: Estamos vindo em paz.

examples.text: I come in peace.

translations.de: Ich komme in Frieden.
translations.fr: Je viens en paix.
translations.pt: Venho em paz.

examples.text: Everybody wants permanent peace.

translations.de: Jeder möchte dauerhaften Frieden.
translations.fr: Tout le monde veut une paix durable.
translations.pt: Todos querem a paz permanente.

more.definition: To make peace; to put at peace; to be at peace.; To peace out.
more.etymology: Anglo-Norman peisbor. From Middle English pees, pes, pais, borrowed from Anglo-Norman peis and Old French pais (“peace”), from Latin pāx (“peace”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂ḱ- (“to fasten, stick, place”), related to Latin pacīscor (“agree, stipulate”), Latin pangō (“fasten, fix”); see pact. Doublet of pax. Displaced native Old English sibb, frēols, and broadly ousted friþ (modern frith).

examples.text: I have a pebble in my shoe.

translations.de: Ich habe einen Stein im Schuh.
translations.fr: J'ai un caillou dans ma chaussure.
translations.pt: Há uma pedra em meu sapato.

examples.text: I need a new pair of shoes.

translations.de: Ich brauche neue Schuhe.
translations.fr: J'ai besoin d'une nouvelle paire de chaussures.
translations.pt: Preciso de um novo par de sapatos.

examples.text: Can you mend these shoes for me?

translations.de: Können Sie mir diese Schuhe reparieren?
translations.fr: Pouvez-vous me réparer ces chaussures ?
translations.pt: Você pode me arrumar esses sapatos?

examples.text: He bought a new pair of shoes.

translations.de: Er kaufte ein neues Paar Schuhe.
translations.fr: Il a acheté une nouvelle paire de chaussures.
translations.pt: Ele comprou um par de sapatos novos.

more.definition: A protective covering for the foot, with a bottom part composed of thick leather or plastic sole and often a thicker heel, and a softer upper part made of leather or synthetic material. Shoes generally do not extend above the ankle, as opposed to boots, which do.; A piece of metal designed to be attached to a horse's foot as a means of protection; a horseshoe.; A device for holding multiple decks of playing cards, allowing more games to be played by reducing the time between shuffles.
more.etymology: From Middle English scho, sho, from Old English sċōh (“shoe”), from Proto-West Germanic *skōh, from Proto-Germanic *skōhaz (“shoe”), of unclear etymology; possibly a derivation from *skehaną (“to move quickly”), from Proto-Indo-European *skek- (“to move quickly, jump”).

examples.text: I must buy a pair of shoes.

translations.de: Ich muss mir ein paar Schuhe kaufen.
translations.fr: Je dois acheter une paire de chaussures.
translations.pt: Preciso comprar um par de sapatos.

examples.text: My sister washes her shoes every Sunday.

translations.de: Meine Schwester wäscht ihre Schuhe jeden Sonntag.
translations.fr: Ma sœur lave ses chaussures tous les dimanches.
translations.pt: Minha irmã lava os sapatos dela todos os domingos.

examples.text: These shoes were designed in France.

translations.de: Diese Schuhe wurden in Frankreich entworfen.
translations.fr: Ces chaussures ont été conçues en France.
translations.pt: Esses sapatos foram projetados na França.

examples.text: Take off your shoes before entering.

translations.de: Schuhe aus, bevor Sie hineingehen!
translations.fr: Enlevez vos chaussures avant d'entrer.
translations.pt: Tire os sapatos antes de entrar.

more.definition: To put shoes on one's own feet.; To put shoes on someone or something else's feet, especially to put horseshoes on a horse.; To cover an object with a protective layer of material.
more.etymology: From Middle English scho, sho, from Old English sċōh (“shoe”), from Proto-West Germanic *skōh, from Proto-Germanic *skōhaz (“shoe”), of unclear etymology; possibly a derivation from *skehaną (“to move quickly”), from Proto-Indo-European *skek- (“to move quickly, jump”).

examples.text: She fell in love with a certain prince.

translations.de: Sie hat sich in einen bestimmten Prinzen verliebt.
translations.fr: Elle est tombée amoureuse d'un certain prince.
translations.pt: Ela se apaixonou por um certo príncipe.

examples.text: I'm almost certain Tom will do that.

translations.de: Ich bin mir fast sicher, dass Tom das tun wird.
translations.fr: Je suis presque sûr que Tom le fera.
translations.pt: Estou quase certo de que Tom fará isso.

examples.text: Nothing is more certain than death.

translations.de: Nichts ist sicherer als der Tod.
translations.fr: Rien n'est plus certain que la mort.
translations.pt: Nada é mais certo que a morte.

examples.text: I met her on a certain winter day.

translations.de: Ich traf sie eines Wintertages.
translations.fr: Je la rencontrai un certain jour d'hiver.
translations.pt: Eu a conheci num certo dia de inverno.

more.definition: Sure in one's mind, positive; absolutely confident in the truth of something.; Not to be doubted or denied; established as a fact.; Sure to happen, inevitable; assured.
more.etymology: From Middle English certeyn, certein, certain, borrowed from Old French certain, from a Vulgar Latin unattested form *certānus, extended form of Latin certus (“fixed, resolved, certain”), of the same origin as cretus, past participle of cernere (“to separate, perceive, decide”).

examples.text: I was certain that you'd come.

translations.de: Ich war überzeugt, dass du kommen würdest.
translations.fr: J'étais certain que tu viendrais.
translations.pt: Tinha certeza de que viria.

examples.text: I'm certain that he'll come.

translations.de: Ich bin sicher, dass er kommt.
translations.fr: Je suis certain qu'il viendra.
translations.pt: Estou certo de que ele virá.

examples.text: You are right to a certain extent.

translations.de: In gewissem Maße hast du recht.
translations.fr: Vous avez raison dans une certaine mesure.
translations.pt: Você está certo até certo ponto.

examples.text: My mother is certain to say no.

translations.de: Meine Mutter sagt ganz bestimmt nein.
translations.fr: Ma mère dira certainement non.
translations.pt: Minha mãe certamente dirá que não.

more.definition: Having been determined but not specified.
more.etymology: From Middle English certeyn, certein, certain, borrowed from Old French certain, from a Vulgar Latin unattested form *certānus, extended form of Latin certus (“fixed, resolved, certain”), of the same origin as cretus, past participle of cernere (“to separate, perceive, decide”).

examples.text: It is certain that he will come here.

translations.de: Es ist sicher, dass er hierher kommt.
translations.fr: Il est certain qu'il viendra ici.
translations.pt: É certo que ele virá aqui.

examples.text: I met a certain Mr Smith.

translations.de: Ich habe einen gewissen Mr. Smith getroffen.
translations.fr: J'ai rencontré un certain M. Smith.
translations.pt: Conheci um tal de Sr. Smith.

examples.text: I agree with you to a certain extent.

translations.de: In einigen Punkten stimme ich dir zu.
translations.fr: Je suis d'accord avec toi d'une certaine manière.
translations.pt: Concordo com você até certo ponto.

examples.text: I don't know for certain.

translations.de: Ich bin mir nicht sicher.
translations.fr: Je n'en suis pas certain.
translations.pt: Eu não tenho certeza.

more.definition: Unnamed or undescribed members (of).
more.etymology: From Middle English certeyn, certein, certain, borrowed from Old French certain, from a Vulgar Latin unattested form *certānus, extended form of Latin certus (“fixed, resolved, certain”), of the same origin as cretus, past participle of cernere (“to separate, perceive, decide”).

examples.text: I'm afraid this key doesn't fit.

translations.de: Ich fürchte, dass der Schlüssel nicht passt.
translations.fr: J'ai bien peur que cette clé ne marche pas.
translations.pt: Temo que esta chave não entre.

examples.text: The boy's as fit as a fiddle!

translations.de: Der Junge ist fit wie ein Turnschuh!
translations.fr: Le garçon est en pleine forme !
translations.pt: O garoto está em boa forma!

examples.text: Do you think it'll fit?

translations.de: Denkst du, dass es passen wird?
translations.fr: Penses-tu que ce sera la bonne taille ?
translations.pt: Você acha que isso vai caber?

examples.text: These books are not fit for young readers.

translations.de: Diese Bücher sind nichts für junge Leser.
translations.fr: Ces livres ne conviennent pas à de jeunes lecteurs.
translations.pt: Estes livros não são apropriados para leitores jovens.

more.definition: Suitable; proper; Adapted to a purpose or environment.; In good shape; physically well.
more.etymology: Possibly from Middle English fit (“an adversary of equal power”), of uncertain further origin. The original sense appears to have been "to marshal or deploy troops", which shifted to "to suit (troops to a certain location" > "suitable", and may be further related to Icelandic fitja (“to web, knit, cast on”).

examples.text: The dress fits you very well.

translations.de: Das Kleid steht dir sehr gut.
translations.fr: La robe te va très bien.
translations.pt: O vestido te cai muito bem.

examples.text: That dress fits her perfectly.

translations.de: Dieses Kleid paßt ihr perfekt.
translations.fr: Cette robe lui va parfaitement.
translations.pt: Esse vestido fica perfeito nela.

examples.text: That nickname fits him perfectly.

translations.de: Sein Spitzname passt perfekt zu ihm.
translations.fr: Ce pseudo lui convient parfaitement.
translations.pt: Esse pseudônimo lhe cai perfeito.

examples.text: The suit fits well.

translations.de: Der Anzug sitzt gut.
translations.fr: Le costume me va bien.
translations.pt: O terno assenta bem.

more.definition: The degree to which something fits.; Conformity of elements one to another.; The part of an object upon which anything fits tightly.
more.etymology: Possibly from Middle English fit (“an adversary of equal power”), of uncertain further origin. The original sense appears to have been "to marshal or deploy troops", which shifted to "to suit (troops to a certain location" > "suitable", and may be further related to Icelandic fitja (“to web, knit, cast on”).

examples.text: This coat fits you.

translations.de: Dieser Mantel steht dir.
translations.fr: Ce manteau est à ta taille.
translations.pt: Este abrigo te serve.

examples.text: This stopper does not fit the bottle.

translations.de: Dieser Verschluss passt nicht auf die Flasche.
translations.fr: Ce bouchon n'est pas adapté à la bouteille.
translations.pt: Esta tampa não cabe na garrafa.

examples.text: This fits perfectly.

translations.de: Das passt perfekt.
translations.fr: Ça correspond parfaitement.
translations.pt: Isto cabe perfeitamente.

examples.text: Try on this new suit to see if it fits well.

translations.de: Probiere diesen neuen Anzug an, damit wir sehen, ob er gut passt.
translations.fr: Essaie ce nouveau costume pour voir s'il te va bien.
translations.pt: Experimente este terno novo para ver se ele assenta bem em você.

more.definition: To be suitable for.; To have sufficient space available at some location to be able to be there.; To conform to in size and shape.
more.etymology: Possibly from Middle English fit (“an adversary of equal power”), of uncertain further origin. The original sense appears to have been "to marshal or deploy troops", which shifted to "to suit (troops to a certain location" > "suitable", and may be further related to Icelandic fitja (“to web, knit, cast on”).

examples.text: Did you see the ruins?

translations.de: Haben Sie die Ruinen gesehen?
translations.fr: Avez-vous vu les ruines ?
translations.pt: Vocês viram as ruínas?

examples.text: If you invite them, they will ruin the party.

translations.de: Wenn Sie sie einladen, werden sie die Party ruinieren.
translations.fr: Si vous les invitez, ils gâcheront la fête.
translations.pt: Se você os convidar, eles vão estragar a festa.

examples.text: Don't let this ruin your friendship.

translations.de: Lasst eure Freundschaft daran nicht zerbrechen.
translations.fr: Ne laisse pas ceci ruiner votre amitié.
translations.pt: Não deixe que isso estrague sua amizade.

examples.text: The old castle is a ruin.

translations.de: Die alte Burg ist eine Ruine.
translations.fr: Le vieux château est en ruine.
translations.pt: O velho castelo é uma ruína.

more.definition: The remains of a destroyed or dilapidated construction, such as a house or castle.; The state of being a ruin, destroyed or decayed.; Something that leads to serious trouble or destruction.
more.etymology: From Middle English ruyne, ruine, from Old French ruine, from Latin ruīna (“overthrow, ruin”), from ruō (“to fall down, tumble, sink in ruin, rush”).

examples.text: The old castle is a ruin.

translations.de: Die alte Burg ist eine Ruine.
translations.fr: Le vieux château est en ruine.
translations.pt: O velho castelo é uma ruína.

examples.text: Everything is ruined because of you.

translations.de: Deinetwegen ist jetzt alles hin.
translations.fr: Tout est fichu à cause de toi.
translations.pt: Está tudo arruinado, graças a você.

examples.text: The tower stood amid the ruins.

translations.de: Der Turm stand inmitten der Ruinen.
translations.fr: La tour se dressait au milieu des ruines.
translations.pt: A torre ficou entre as ruínas.

examples.text: I think exams are ruining education.

translations.de: Ich denke, dass Prüfungen die Erziehung ruinieren.
translations.fr: Je pense que les examens ruinent l'éducation.
translations.pt: Eu acho que as provas estão arruinando com a educação.

more.definition: To cause the fiscal ruin of; to bankrupt or drive out of business.; To destroy or render something no longer usable or operable.; To destroy (e.g. a city) so as to leave ruins.
more.etymology: From Middle English ruyne, ruine, from Old French ruine, from Latin ruīna (“overthrow, ruin”), from ruō (“to fall down, tumble, sink in ruin, rush”).

examples.text: Heat is a form of energy.

translations.de: Wärme ist eine Energieform.
translations.fr: La chaleur est une forme d'énergie.
translations.pt: O calor é uma forma de energia.

examples.text: Some consider language as a form of knowledge.

translations.de: Manche betrachten Sprache als eine Art Wissen.
translations.fr: Certains considèrent la langue comme une forme de savoir.
translations.pt: Alguns consideram que linguagem é uma forma de conhecimento.

examples.text: Tom filled out the application form.

translations.de: Tom füllte das Antragsformular aus.
translations.fr: Tom remplit le formulaire d'inscription.
translations.pt: Tom preencheu o formulário de inscrição.

examples.text: Fill out this form, please.

translations.de: Bitte füllen Sie dieses Formular aus.
translations.fr: Veuillez remplir ce formulaire.
translations.pt: Preencha este formulário, por favor.

more.definition: The shape or visible structure of a thing or person.; A thing that gives shape to other things as in a mold.; Regularity, beauty, or elegance.
more.etymology: From Middle English forme (“shape, figure, manner, bench, frame, seat, condition, agreement, etc.”), borrowed from Old French forme, from Latin fōrma (“shape, figure, image, outline, plan, mold, frame, case, etc., manner, sort, kind, etc.”). In sense "division grouping school students" (now dated), derived from public school nomenclature later adopted by state schools.

examples.text: He formed the clay into a bowl.

translations.de: Er formte den Ton zu einer Kugel.
translations.fr: Il a façonné un bol avec l'argile.
translations.pt: Com a argila ele estava moldando uma bacia.

examples.text: Attack is the best form of defense.

translations.de: Angriff ist die beste Verteidigung.
translations.fr: La meilleure défense, c'est l'attaque.
translations.pt: A melhor defesa é o ataque.

examples.text: Swimming is a form of exercise.

translations.de: Schwimmen ist eine Form der körperlichen Übung.
translations.fr: Nager est une sorte d'exercice.
translations.pt: Nadar é uma forma de exercício.

examples.text: A snail's shell is spiral in form.

translations.de: Das Haus einer Schnecke hat die Form einer Spirale.
translations.fr: La coquille d'un escargot a la forme d'une spirale.
translations.pt: A concha de um caracol tem a forma de uma espiral.

more.definition: To assume (a certain shape or visible structure).; To give (a shape or visible structure) to a thing or person.; To take shape.
more.etymology: From Middle English forme (“shape, figure, manner, bench, frame, seat, condition, agreement, etc.”), borrowed from Old French forme, from Latin fōrma (“shape, figure, image, outline, plan, mold, frame, case, etc., manner, sort, kind, etc.”). In sense "division grouping school students" (now dated), derived from public school nomenclature later adopted by state schools.

examples.text: It is going to rain this afternoon.

translations.de: Heute Nachmittag wird es regnen.
translations.fr: Il va pleuvoir cet après-midi.
translations.pt: Vai chover hoje à tarde.

examples.text: Usually, I don't take an afternoon nap.

translations.de: Normalerweise mache ich kein Mittagsschläfchen.
translations.fr: D'habitude, je ne fais pas de sieste l'après-midi.
translations.pt: Normalmente, eu não faço a sesta.

examples.text: Let's spend the afternoon together.

translations.de: Verbringen wir den Nachmittag zusammen!
translations.fr: Passons l’après-midi ensemble !
translations.pt: Vamos passar a tarde juntos.

examples.text: What are you doing this afternoon?

translations.de: Was wirst du heute Nachmittag machen?
translations.fr: Que faites-vous cet après-midi ?
translations.pt: O que vocês vão fazer essa tarde?

more.etymology: From Middle English afternone, after-non, equivalent to after- + noon.

examples.text: She intends to play tennis tomorrow afternoon.

translations.de: Sie hat morgen Nachmittag vor, Tennis zu spielen.
translations.fr: Elle prévoit de jouer au tennis demain après-midi.
translations.pt: Ela pretende jogar tênis amanhã à tarde.

examples.text: What do you do in the afternoon?

translations.de: Was machst du am Nachmittag?
translations.fr: Que faites-vous l'après-midi ?
translations.pt: O que você faz à tarde?

examples.text: He came at three in the afternoon.

translations.de: Er ist um drei Uhr nachmittags gekommen.
translations.fr: Il est venu à trois heures de l'après-midi.
translations.pt: Ele veio às três da tarde.

examples.text: I have nothing to do this afternoon.

translations.de: Ich habe heute Nachmittag nichts zu tun.
translations.fr: Je n'ai rien à faire cet après-midi.
translations.pt: Não tenho nada que fazer esta tarde.

more.definition: The part of the day from noon or lunchtime until sunset, evening, or suppertime or 6pm.; The later part of anything, often with implications of decline.; A party or social event held in the afternoon.
more.etymology: From Middle English afternone, after-non, equivalent to after- + noon.

examples.text: Neither gold nor greatness make us happy.

translations.de: Gold nicht, auch nicht Größe verhilft uns hin zum Glück.
translations.fr: Ni l'or ni la grandeur ne nous rendent heureux.
translations.pt: Nem o ouro nem a grandeza nos fazem felizes.

examples.text: Iron is much more useful than gold.

translations.de: Eisen ist viel nützlicher als Gold.
translations.fr: Le fer est beaucoup plus utile que l'or.
translations.pt: O fero é muito mais útil do que o ouro.

examples.text: Did you say money or gold?

translations.de: Hast du „Geld“ oder „Gold“ gesagt?
translations.fr: Avez-vous dit l'argent ou l'or ?
translations.pt: Dinheiro ou ouro?

examples.text: All that glisters is not gold.

translations.de: Nicht alles, was glitzert, ist Gold.
translations.fr: Tout ce qui brille n'est pas or.
translations.pt: Nem tudo que brilha é ouro.

more.definition: Made of gold.; Having the colour of gold.; Premium, superior.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰĺ̥h₃-to-mder. From Middle English gold, from Old English gold (“gold”), from Proto-West Germanic *golþ, from Proto-Germanic *gulþą (“gold”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰl̥h₃tóm (“gold”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰelh₃- (“green, yellow”). Related to yellow; see there for more.

examples.text: The cup is made of gold.

translations.de: Der Kelch besteht aus Gold.
translations.fr: Le calice est fait d'or.

examples.text: I beg your pardon?

examples.text: I'm begging you.

examples.text: I beg your pardon?

more.definition: To request the help of someone, often in the form of money.; To plead with someone for help, a favor, etc.; to entreat.; To unwillingly provoke a negative, often violent, reaction.

examples.text: I am used to driving a truck.

translations.de: Ich bin es gewohnt, einen Lastwagen zu fahren.
translations.fr: Je suis habitué à conduire un camion.
translations.pt: Estou acostumado a dirigir caminhões.

examples.text: This road is too narrow for trucks to pass.

translations.de: Diese Straße ist für den LKW-Verkehr zu schmal.
translations.fr: Cette route est trop étroite pour le passage des camions.
translations.pt: Essa estrada é muito estreita para caminhões passarem.

examples.text: Look out! There's a truck coming!

translations.de: Pass auf! Da kommt ein Lkw!
translations.fr: Attention ! Voici un camion qui arrive !
translations.pt: Olhe! Tem um caminhão vindo!

examples.text: He's in the other truck.

translations.de: Er ist in dem anderen Lkw.
translations.fr: Il est dans l'autre camion.
translations.pt: Ele está no outro caminhão.

more.definition: A small wheel or roller, specifically the wheel of a gun carriage.; The ball on top of a flagpole.; On a wooden mast, a circular disc (or sometimes a rectangle) of wood near or at the top of the mast, usually with holes or sheaves to reeve signal halyards; also a temporary or emergency place for a lookout. "Main" refers to the mainmast, whereas a truck on another mast may be called (on the mizzenmast, for example) "mizzen-truck".
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *drem-influ. Ancient Greek τροχῐλείᾱ (trokhĭleíā)der. Medieval Latin trochleader. Anglo-Norman troclebor. Perhaps a shortening of truckle, related to Latin trochus (“iron hoop, wheel”) from Ancient Greek τροχός (trokhós).

examples.text: I almost got run over by a truck.

translations.de: Fast hätte mich ein Lastwagen überfahren.

examples.text: You assemble trucks.

translations.de: Du baust Lastwagen zusammen.

examples.text: The car crashed into the truck.

translations.de: Das Auto stieß mit dem LKW zusammen.
translations.fr: La voiture a heurté le camion.

examples.text: I was nearly run over by a truck.

translations.de: Ich bin fast von einem LKW überfahren worden.
translations.fr: J'ai failli être écrasé par un camion.
translations.pt: Quase fui atropelado por um caminhão.

more.definition: To drive a truck.; To convey by truck.; To travel, to proceed.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *drem-influ. Ancient Greek τροχῐλείᾱ (trokhĭleíā)der. Medieval Latin trochleader. Anglo-Norman troclebor. Perhaps a shortening of truckle, related to Latin trochus (“iron hoop, wheel”) from Ancient Greek τροχός (trokhós).

examples.text: He won the third prize.

translations.de: Er hat den dritten Preis gewonnen.
translations.fr: Il a remporté le troisième prix.

examples.text: Early Western haiku often rhymed the first and third lines.

translations.de: Im frühen westlichen Haiku reimten sich oft die erste und die dritte Zeile.
translations.fr: Les premiers haïkus occidentaux faisaient souvent rimer la première et la troisième ligne.
translations.pt: Os primeiros haicais ocidentais geralmente rimavam o primeiro e o terceiro versos.

examples.text: A third of the world's rainforests are found in Brazil.

translations.de: Ein Drittel der Urwälder der Welt befinden sich in Brasilien.
translations.fr: Un tiers des forêts tropicales humides du monde se trouve au Brésil.
translations.pt: Um terço das florestas tropicais do mundo encontra-se no Brasil.

examples.text: Those words are in the second and third tiers of frequency.

translations.de: Diese Wörter befinden sich in der zweiten und dritten Stufe der Häufigkeit.
translations.fr: Ces mots se situent dans les deuxième et troisième niveaux de fréquence.

more.definition: The ordinal form of the cardinal number three; Coming after the second.

examples.text: I took the lift to the third floor.

translations.fr: C'est le trois octobre.

examples.text: It's October the third.

translations.de: Es ist der dritte Oktober.

examples.text: Where will you give your vote?

translations.fr: Je n'ai voté pour personne.

translations.de: Einige Wähler warteten Stunden darauf zu wählen.

translations.de: Tom sagt, er werde nicht wählen.
translations.fr: Tom dit qu'il ne votera pas.
translations.pt: O Tom diz que não vai votar.

more.definition: A formalized choice on legally relevant measures such as employment or appointment to office or a proceeding about a legal dispute.; An act or instance of participating in such a choice, e.g., by submitting a ballot.; Any judgment of intellect leading not only to a formal opinion but also to a particular choice in a legally relevant measure, a point of view as published.

translations.de: Tom und Maria stimmten für Johannes.

translations.pt: Tom e Maria votaram em João.

examples.text: If voting changed anything, they'd make it illegal.

examples.text: There's a bomb on board!

examples.text: Is this computer connected to the Internet?

translations.pt: Este computador está conectado à internet?

examples.text: I don't know much about computers.

translations.de: Ich möchte einen neuen Computer kaufen.

examples.text: I have to get a new computer.

translations.fr: Tom passe trop de temps sur l'ordinateur.

examples.text: To be honest, I don't know.

more.definition: Scrupulous with regard to telling the truth; not given to swindling, lying, or fraud; upright.; True, especially as far as is known by the person making the statement; fair; unbiased.; In good faith; without malice.

examples.text: To be honest, I don't know anything.

translations.de: Ehrlich gesagt, weiß ich nichts.
translations.fr: Pour être honnête, je ne sais rien.
translations.pt: Para ser honesto, não sei de nada.

translations.pt: Eu sempre tento ser honesto.

translations.fr: Je veux que tu sois honnête avec moi.

more.definition: Honestly; really.
more.etymology: From Middle English honest, honeste (“honourable, appropriate, excellent”), from Old French honeste, from Latin honestus, from honor. translations.fr: Es-tu sincère ou me mens-tu ?

translations.fr: Il est pauvre mais honnête.

examples.text: My apartment is on the fourth floor.

more.definition: A complete domicile occupying only part of a building, especially one for rent; a flat.; A room within a house.; A conceptual space used for separation in the threading architecture. Objects in one apartment cannot directly access those in another, but must use a proxy.

examples.text: How often do you brush your teeth?

translations.fr: Court-il au succès ou à l'échec ?
translations.pt: Ele terá sucesso ou fracassará?

translations.de: Diesmal kannst du nicht durchfallen.
translations.fr: Tu ne peux pas échouer cette fois-ci.

examples.text: It's cheaper to take the bus.

more.definition: A motor vehicle for transporting large numbers of people along roads.; A coach, a bus used for long travels.; An electrical conductor or interface serving as a common connection for two or more circuits or components.
collocations: catch the bus — to get on it in time
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₃ep-der. Latin omnibuslbor. French omnibusbor. English omnibusclip. Clipping of omnibus. Superseded earlier 'bus, where the apostrophe indicated a clipping. The shift in spelling likely reflects the fact that modern speakers no longer perceive this term as a clipping. The electrical sense is derived from figurative application of the automotive sense.

examples.text: Let's pretend this never happened.

translations.de: Tun wir so, als wäre das nie passiert!
translations.fr: Faisons comme si ça n'était jamais arrivé.
translations.pt: Vamos fingir que isto nunca aconteceu.

translations.de: Lass uns so tun, als wären wir Aliens.
translations.fr: Faisons semblant d'être des extraterrestres.
translations.pt: Vamos fingir que somos alienígenas.

examples.text: I'm going to pretend that didn't happen.

translations.de: Ich werde so tun, als wäre das nicht passiert.
translations.fr: Je vais faire comme si ça n'était pas arrivé.
translations.pt: Vou fazer de conta que isso não aconteceu.

examples.text: I tried to pretend that I didn't care.

translations.de: Ich versuchte, so zu tun, als wäre es mir egal.
translations.fr: J'ai essayé de faire semblant de m'en moquer.

more.etymology: Latin praetendōlbor. Anglo-Norman pretendreder. From Anglo-Norman pretendre, Middle French pretendre (French prétendre (“to claim, demand”)), from Latin praetendere (“to put forward, hold out, pretend”), from prae- (“pre-”) + tendō (“stretch”); see tend.

examples.text: We can't pretend that this didn't happen.

translations.de: Wir können nicht so tun, als wäre das nicht passiert.
translations.fr: Nous ne pouvons pas prétendre que ça n'est pas arrivé.
translations.pt: Não podemos fingir que isto não aconteceu.

translations.de: Kinder ahmen in ihren Spielen gern Erwachsene nach.

translations.de: Tu nicht so, als wüsstest du nicht, wovon ich rede!
translations.fr: Ne faites pas semblant d'ignorer de quoi je parle !
translations.pt: Não finja que você não sabe do que eu estou falando.

examples.text: I don't pretend to understand women.

translations.fr: Je ne prétends pas comprendre les femmes.

translations.fr: L'été est la plus chaude saison de l'année.

translations.de: Es wird von Tag zu Tag wärmer.
translations.fr: Il fait plus chaud de jour en jour.
translations.pt: Está ficando mais quente dia após dia.

more.definition: Of a somewhat high temperature, often but not always connoting that the high temperature is pleasant rather than uncomfortable.; Friendly and with affection.; Having a color in the part of the visible electromagnetic spectrum between red and yellow-green.
more.etymology: From Middle English warm, werm, from Old English wearm, from Proto-West Germanic *warm, from Proto-Germanic *warmaz, from one of: * Proto-Indo-European *wór-mo-s, from *wer- (“to burn”), which is related to Hittite 𒉿𒊏𒀀𒉌 (warāni, “to burn”), Armenian վառել (vaṙel, “to burn, heat, warm”), Old Church Slavonic варити (variti, “to cook, boil”).

examples.text: My hand is in warm water.

translations.de: Meine Hand ist in warmem Wasser.
translations.fr: Ma main est dans de l'eau chaude.

translations.fr: L'eau est assez chaude pour y nager.

translations.fr: Aujourd'hui, il fait beau et chaud.
translations.pt: Hoje está um dia agradável e cálido.

translations.de: Diese Blumen wachsen in warmen Ländern.

more.etymology: From Middle English engyn, from Anglo-Norman engine, Old French engin (“skill, cleverness, war machine”), from Latin ingenium (“innate or natural quality, nature, genius, a genius, an invention, (in Late Latin) a war-engine, battering-ram”), related to ingignō (“to instil by birth, implant, produce in”). examples.text: They found Tom in the crowd.

more.definition: A group of people congregated or collected into a close body without order.; Several things collected or closely pressed together; also, some things adjacent to each other.; The so-called lower orders of people; the populace; the vulgar.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *grewt-der. From Middle English crouden, from Old English crūdan, from Proto-West Germanic *krūdan, from Proto-Germanic *krūdaną, *kreudaną, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *grewt- (“to push; press”). Cognate with German Low German kroden (“to push, shove”), Dutch kruien (“to push, shove”).

examples.text: The train was very crowded.

more.definition: To press forward; to advance by pushing.; To press together or collect in numbers.; To press or drive together, especially into a small space; to cram.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *grewt-der. From Middle English crouden, from Old English crūdan, from Proto-West Germanic *krūdan, from Proto-Germanic *krūdaną, *kreudaną, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *grewt- (“to push; press”). Cognate with German Low German kroden (“to push, shove”), Dutch kruien (“to push, shove”).

examples.text: There's really a ghost in my house.

more.definition: In the form be ghost: not present or involved; absent, gone.
more.etymology: The noun is derived from Middle English gost, from Old English gāst, gǣst (“breath, spirit, soul, ghost”) (compare modern English Holy Ghost), from Proto-West Germanic *gaist, from Proto-Germanic *gaistaz, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéysdos, from *ǵʰéysd- (“anger, agitation”). The h in the spelling appears in the Prologue to William Caxton’s Royal Book, printed in 1484, in a reference to the “Holy Ghoost”.

examples.text: Tell us a ghost story.

translations.de: Erzähle uns mal eine Gespenstergeschichte!

examples.text: I'm not afraid of ghosts.

translations.fr: Je n'ai pas peur des fantômes.
translations.pt: Não tenho medo de fantasmas.

examples.text: I don't believe in ghosts.

translations.de: Ich glaube nicht an Geister.
translations.fr: Je ne crois pas aux fantômes.

more.definition: A disembodied soul; a soul or spirit of a deceased person; a spirit appearing after death.; Any faint shadowy semblance; an unsubstantial image.; A false image, such as in a photographic print or negative, on a television screen, radar display, or telescope, caused by poor or double reception or reflection (from a lens or screen).
more.etymology: The noun is derived from Middle English gost, from Old English gāst, gǣst (“breath, spirit, soul, ghost”) (compare modern English Holy Ghost), from Proto-West Germanic *gaist, from Proto-Germanic *gaistaz, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéysdos, from *ǵʰéysd- (“anger, agitation”). The h in the spelling appears in the Prologue to William Caxton’s Royal Book, printed in 1484, in a reference to the “Holy Ghoost”.

more.etymology: The noun is derived from Middle English gost, from Old English gāst, gǣst (“breath, spirit, soul, ghost”) (compare modern English Holy Ghost), from Proto-West Germanic *gaist, from Proto-Germanic *gaistaz, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéysdos, from *ǵʰéysd- (“anger, agitation”). more.definition: The soul of a person or other creature.; A supernatural being, often but not exclusively without physical form; ghost, fairy, angel.; Enthusiasm.
more.etymology: Latin spīrituslbor. Old French espiritbor. From Middle English spirit, from Old French espirit (“spirit”), from Latin spīritus (“breath; spirit”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)peys- (“to blow, breathe”). Compare inspire, respire, transpire, all ultimately from Latin spīrō (“to breathe, blow, respire”). In this sense, displaced native Middle English gast (from Old English gāst), whence modern English ghost.

more.definition: To carry off, especially in haste, secrecy, or mystery.; Sometimes followed by up: to animate with vigour; to excite; to encourage; to inspirit.
more.etymology: Latin spīrituslbor. Old French espiritbor. more.etymology: From French exister, from Latin existō, exsistō (“I am, I exist, appear, arise”), from ex (“out”) + sistere (“to set, place”) (related to stare (“to stand, to be stood”)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *stísteh₂ti, from the root *steh₂- (“stand”); see stand. more.definition: To determine (something which was exposed to doubt or question); to resolve conclusively; to set or fix (a time, an order of succession, etc).; To conclude, to cause (a dispute) to finish.; In particular, to terminate (a lawsuit), usually out of court, by agreement of all parties.

more.definition: A large and often winding stream which drains a land mass, carrying water down from higher areas to a lower point, oftentimes ending in another body of water, such as an ocean or in an inland sea.; Any large flow of a liquid in a single body.; The last card dealt in a hand.

Displaced native Middle English sax (“knife”), from Old English seax; and Middle English coutel, qwetyll (“knife”) from Old French coutel.

examples.text: Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius.

translations.de: Wasser gefriert bei 0 Grad Celsius.
translations.fr: L'eau gèle à zéro degré Celsius.
translations.pt: A água congela a zero grau centígrado.

examples.text: It may freeze next week.

translations.de: Nächste Woche gibt es vielleicht Frost.
translations.fr: Il se peut qu'il gèle la semaine prochaine.
translations.pt: Pode ser que vá gear na semana que vem.

examples.text: Water becomes solid when it freezes.

translations.de: Wasser wird fest, wenn es gefriert.
translations.fr: L'eau devient solide quand elle gèle.
translations.pt: A água se torna sólida quando congela.

examples.text: You're going to freeze to death.

translations.de: Du wirst noch erfrieren!
translations.fr: Vous allez mourir de froid.
translations.pt: Vocês vão morrer de frio.

more.definition: A period of intensely cold weather.; A halt of a regular operation.; The state when either a single computer program, or the whole system ceases to respond to inputs.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *prews-der. English freezedeverb. Deverbal from freeze (verb), see which for further etymology.

examples.text: Water freezes at zero Celsius, right?

translations.de: Wasser gefriert doch bei null Grad Celsius, oder?
translations.fr: L'eau gèle à zéro degré Celsius, n'est-ce pas ?
translations.pt: A água congela em zero graus Celsius, certo?

examples.text: Please freeze the fish and meat.

translations.de: Bitte frieren Sie den Fisch und das Fleisch ein.
translations.fr: Surgelez le poisson et la viande, s'il vous plaît.
translations.pt: Por favor, congele o peixe e a carne.

examples.text: We were nearly frozen to death.

translations.de: Wir waren fast totgefroren.
translations.fr: Nous étions presque morts gelés.
translations.pt: Quase morremos congelados.

examples.text: The milk froze and became solid.

translations.de: Die Milch gefror und wurde fest.
translations.fr: Le lait se gela et devint solide.
translations.pt: O leite congelou e ficou sólido.

more.definition: Especially of a liquid, to become solid due to low temperature.; To lower something's temperature to the point that it freezes or becomes hard.; To drop to a temperature below zero degrees celsius, where water turns to ice.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *prews-der. From Middle English fresen, from Old English frēosan (“to freeze”), from Proto-West Germanic *freusan, from Proto-Germanic *freusaną (“to freeze”), from Proto-Indo-European *prews- (“to freeze; frost”).

examples.text: I learned a lot this weekend.

translations.de: Ich habe dieses Wochenende viel gelernt.
translations.fr: J'ai beaucoup appris ce week-end.
translations.pt: Eu aprendi muito neste fim de semana.

examples.text: We spent the weekend with friends.

translations.de: Wir haben das Wochenende mit Freunden verbracht.
translations.fr: Nous avons passé le weekend avec des amis.
translations.pt: Nós passamos o fim de semana com amigos.

examples.text: She spent the weekend by herself.

translations.de: Sie hat das Wochenende allein verbracht.
translations.fr: Elle a passé le week-end seule.
translations.pt: Ela passou o fim de semana sozinha.

examples.text: I spent the weekend reading a long novel.

translations.de: Ich verbrachte das Wochenende damit, einen langen Roman zu lesen.
translations.fr: J'ai passé le week-end à lire un long roman.
translations.pt: Passei o final de semana lendo um longo romance.

more.definition: Of, relating to or for the weekend.; Occurring at the weekend.
more.etymology: From week + end. Originally a Northern England regionalism (see 1903 quotation), in more general use from late 19th century. Compare Saterland Frisian Wiekeneende (“weekend”), West Frisian wykein (“weekend”), Dutch weekeinde (“weekend”), German Low German Wekenenn (“weekend”), German Wochenende (“weekend”).

examples.text: I don't like working on weekends.

translations.de: Ich arbeite nicht gerne am Wochenende.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas travailler le week-end.
translations.pt: Não gosto de trabalhar aos fins de semana.

examples.text: What're your plans for the weekend?

translations.de: Was haben Sie am Wochenende vor?
translations.fr: Quels sont tes plans pour le week-end ?
translations.pt: Quais são os seus planos para o fim de semana?

examples.text: I had a lot of fun last weekend.

translations.de: Ich hatte letztes Wochenende viel Spaß.
translations.fr: Je me suis beaucoup amusé, le week-end dernier.
translations.pt: Eu me diverti muito no último final de semana.

examples.text: Do you have any plans for the weekend?

translations.de: Hast du schon etwas für das Wochenende vor?
translations.fr: As-tu le moindre projet pour le week-end ?
translations.pt: Você tem algum plano para o fim de semana?

more.definition: The break in the working week, usually two days including the traditional holy or sabbath day. Thus in Western countries, Saturday and Sunday.
more.etymology: From week + end. Originally a Northern England regionalism (see 1903 quotation), in more general use from late 19th century. Compare Saterland Frisian Wiekeneende (“weekend”), West Frisian wykein (“weekend”), Dutch weekeinde (“weekend”), German Low German Wekenenn (“weekend”), German Wochenende (“weekend”).

examples.text: My brother goes fishing every weekend.

translations.de: Mein Bruder geht an jedem Wochenende angeln.
translations.fr: Mon frère va à la pêche tous les week-ends.
translations.pt: Meu irmão vai pescar todos os fins de semana.

examples.text: I love three-day weekends.

translations.de: Ich liebe dreitägige Wochenenden.
translations.fr: J'adore les week-ends de trois jours.
translations.pt: Adoro fins de semana prolongados.

examples.text: I'm going to take it easy this weekend.

translations.de: Ich werde es dieses Wochenende leicht angehen lassen.
translations.fr: Je vais me la couler douce ce week-end.
translations.pt: Eu vou pegar leve neste fim de semana.

examples.text: Are you enjoying your weekend?

translations.de: Genießen Sie das Wochenende?
translations.fr: Prends-tu plaisir à ton week-end ?
translations.pt: Você está aproveitando seu fim de semana?

more.definition: To spend the weekend.
more.etymology: From week + end. Originally a Northern England regionalism (see 1903 quotation), in more general use from late 19th century. Compare Saterland Frisian Wiekeneende (“weekend”), West Frisian wykein (“weekend”), Dutch weekeinde (“weekend”), German Low German Wekenenn (“weekend”), German Wochenende (“weekend”).

examples.text: Does this price include meals?

translations.de: Sind in diesem Preis Mahlzeiten inbegriffen?
translations.fr: Ce prix comprend-il les repas ?
translations.pt: Este preço inclui as refeições?

examples.text: The entrée includes a beverage.

translations.de: Im Eintritt ist ein Getränk inbegriffen.
translations.fr: L'entrée comprend une boisson.
translations.pt: A entrada inclui uma bebida.

examples.text: Don't forget to include me in the count.

translations.de: Vergessen Sie nicht, mich mitzuzählen.
translations.fr: N'oublie pas de m'inclure dans le nombre.
translations.pt: Não se esqueça de me incluir na contagem.

examples.text: Why doesn't the list of languages include Maltese?

translations.de: Warum ist Maltesisch nicht in der Sprachliste drin?
translations.fr: Pourquoi la liste des langues ne comprend-elle pas le maltais ?
translations.pt: Por que a lista de idiomas não inclui maltês?

more.definition: A piece of source code or other content that is dynamically retrieved for inclusion in another item.
more.etymology: From Middle English includen, borrowed from Latin inclūdere (“to shut in, enclose, insert”), from in- (“in”) + claudere (“to shut”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂w- (“key, hook, nail”). Doublet of enclose. Displaced native Old English belūcan (“to include,” also “to shut in”).

examples.text: Batteries are not included.

translations.de: Batterien sind nicht enthalten.
translations.fr: Les piles ne sont pas incluses.
translations.pt: As baterias não estão incluídas.

examples.text: This amount includes tax.

translations.de: Dieser Betrag beinhaltet die Steuer.
translations.fr: Cette somme inclut les taxes.
translations.pt: Essa quantia inclui imposto.

examples.text: Does that include everything?

translations.de: Ist da alles mit inbegriffen?
translations.fr: Est-ce que c'est tout compris ?
translations.pt: Isso inclui tudo?

examples.text: She has had multiple plastic surgeries, including breast augmentations and a nose job.

translations.fr: Elle a eu recours à de multiples interventions de chirurgie esthétique, notamment des augmentations mammaires et une opération du nez.
translations.pt: Ela já fez várias cirurgias plásticas, inclusive aumento dos seios e uma reforma do nariz.

more.definition: To bring into a group, class, set, or total as a (new) part or member.; To consider as part of something; to comprehend.; To use a directive that allows the use of source code from another file.
more.etymology: From Middle English includen, borrowed from Latin inclūdere (“to shut in, enclose, insert”), from in- (“in”) + claudere (“to shut”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂w- (“key, hook, nail”). Doublet of enclose. Displaced native Old English belūcan (“to include,” also “to shut in”).

examples.text: Did you think about our offer?

translations.de: Hast du über unser Angebot nachgedacht?
translations.fr: As-tu réfléchi à notre offre ?
translations.pt: Você pensou sobre a nossa oferta?

examples.text: I can't offer you anything in return.

translations.de: Ich kann dir nichts im Gegenzug bieten.
translations.fr: Je ne peux rien vous offrir en retour.

examples.text: May I offer you a drink?

translations.de: Darf ich Ihnen etwas zu trinken anbieten?
translations.fr: Je vous offre à boire ?
translations.pt: Posso oferecer-lhes algo a beber?

more.definition: A proposal that has been made.; Something put forth, bid, proffered or tendered.; An invitation to enter into a binding contract communicated to another party which contains terms sufficiently definite to create an enforceable contract if the other party accepts the invitation.
more.etymology: From Middle English offer, from Old English offrian (“offer or make a sacrifice”) rather than from Old French offre (“offer”), from offrir (“to offer”), from Latin offerō (“to present, bring before”). Compare North Frisian offer (“sacrifice, donation, fee”), Dutch offer (“offering, sacrifice”), German Opfer (“victim, sacrifice”), Danish offer (“victim, sacrifice”), Icelandic offr (“offering”). See verb below.

examples.text: I offered to lend money to her.

translations.de: Ich erbot mich, ihr Geld zu leihen.
translations.fr: Je lui ai offert de lui prêter de l'argent.
translations.pt: Ofereci-me para emprestar dinheiro a ela.

examples.text: Why did you turn down his offer?

translations.de: Warum hast du sein Angebot abgelehnt?
translations.fr: Pourquoi as-tu refusé sa proposition  ?
translations.pt: Por que você recusou a oferta dele?

examples.text: Gonzales offers a bike to all his employees in Europe.

translations.de: Gonzales schenkt allen seinen Angestellten in Europa ein Fahrrad.
translations.fr: Gonzales offre un vélo à tous ses employés en Europe.
translations.pt: Gonzales dá uma bicicleta a todos seus funcionários na Europa.

examples.text: They didn't offer me anything to drink.

translations.de: Sie haben mir nichts zu trinken angeboten.
translations.fr: Elles ne m'ont rien offert à boire.
translations.pt: Não me ofereceram nada de beber.

more.definition: To propose or express one's willingness (to do something).; To present in words; to proffer; to make a proposal of; to suggest.; To place at someone’s disposal; to present (something) to be either accepted or turned down.
more.etymology: From Middle English offren, offrien. In the religious senses inherited from Old English offrian (“to offer, sacrifice, bring an oblation”); otherwise from Old French ofrir. Both ultimately from Latin offerō (“to present, bestow, bring before”, literally “to bring to”), from Latin ob + ferō (“bring, carry”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰer- (“to carry, bear”), later reinforced by Old French offrir (“to offer”).

examples.text: He earns twice as much as me.

examples.text: Yes! I won twice in a row!

translations.de: Ja! Ich habe zweimal hintereinander gewonnen!
translations.fr: Ouais ! J’ai gagné deux fois de suite !
translations.pt: Isso! Ganhei duas vezes seguidas!

more.definition: Two times.; Doubled in quantity, intensity, or degree.
more.etymology: From earlier twise, from Middle English twies, twiȝes, from Old English twīġes (“twice”), from twīwa, twīġa ("twice"; whence Middle English twie (“twice”)) + -es (adverbial genitive ending). examples.text: The mirror has fallen because it is heavy.

translations.de: Der Spiegel ist heruntergefallen, weil er schwer ist.
translations.fr: Le miroir est tombé parce qu'il est lourd.

more.definition: Thermal energy.; Heating system; a system that raises the temperature of a room or building.; The output of a heating system.
more.etymology: From Middle English hete, from Old English hǣtu, from Proto-West Germanic *haitī, from Proto-Germanic *haitį̄ (“heat”), from Proto-Indo-European *keHy- (“heat; hot”). Cognate with Scots hete (“heat”), Saterland Frisian Hatte (“heat”), Old High German heizī (“heat”). Related also to Dutch hitte (“heat”), German Hitze (“heat”), Swedish hetta (“heat”), Faroese and Icelandic hiti (“heat”). Related to hot.

examples.text: It's necessary for you to go.

translations.fr: Il est nécessaire que tu partes.
translations.pt: É necessário que você vá.

more.etymology: From Middle English necessarye, from Old French necessaire, from Latin necessārius (“unavoidable, inevitable, required”), variant of necesse (“unavoidable, inevitable”), probably from ne or non cessum, from the perfect passive participle of cēdō (“yield; avoid, withdraw”); see cede.

translations.fr: Elle est réservée par la nature.
translations.pt: Ela é reservada por natureza.

translations.fr: On ne peut changer la nature.

more.definition: The way things are, the totality of all things in the physical universe and their order, especially the physical world in contrast to spiritual realms and flora and fauna as distinct from human conventions, art, and technology.; The essential or innate characteristics of a person or thing which will always tend to manifest, especially in contrast to specific contexts, reason, religious duty, upbringing, and personal pretense or effort.; The distinguishing characteristic of a person or thing, understood as its general class, sort, type, etc.

examples.text: This transparent liquid contains a kind of poison.

examples.text: Certain poisons, properly used, are useful.

translations.fr: Certains poisons, correctement utilisés, sont utiles.
translations.pt: Alguns venenos, usados corretamente, são úteis.

examples.text: If your child drinks poison, rush him to the hospital.

translations.de: Wenn Ihr Kind Gift trinkt, bringen Sie es schnellstens ins Krankenhaus.

examples.text: It's poison.

examples.text: Carbon monoxide poisoning can cause hallucinations.

examples.text: Suspicion is the poison of friendship.

translations.de: Man hat unsere Hunde vergiftet.
translations.fr: On a empoisonné nos chiens.

more.definition: To use poison to kill or paralyse (somebody).; To pollute; to cause to become poisonous.; To cause to become much worse.
more.etymology: From Middle English poysoun, poyson, pusoun, from Old French poison, poisun, from Latin pōtiōnem (“drink, a draught, a poisonous draught, a potion”), from pōtō (“to drink”). examples.text: His failure taught me a good lesson.

translations.de: Sein Scheitern war mir eine Lehre.
translations.fr: Son échec m'a enseigné une bonne leçon.
translations.pt: Seu fracasso me ensinou uma boa lição.

examples.text: Maria takes piano lessons once a week.

translations.de: Maria nimmt einmal pro Woche Klavierunterricht.
translations.fr: Maria prend des cours de piano une fois par semaine.
translations.pt: Maria tem aulas de piano uma vez por semana.

examples.text: He was asleep during the lesson.

translations.de: Er schlief im Unterricht.

examples.text: So much for today's lesson.

examples.text: Let's start with Lesson Ten.

more.definition: To give a lesson to; to teach.
more.etymology: From Middle English lessoun, from Old French leçon, from Latin lēctiō, lēctiōnem (“a reading”), from legō (“to read; to gather”). Doublet of lection.

examples.text: Coffee is Brazil's main product.

translations.de: Kaffee ist Brasiliens Haupterzeugnis.

more.etymology: Mid 16th century, from French carrière (“road; racecourse”), from Italian carriera, from Old Occitan carreira, from Late Latin carrāria based on Latin carrus (“wheeled vehicle”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱr̥sós, from *ḱers- (“to run”); alternatively, from Middle French carriere, from Old Occitan.

translations.de: Deine Familie sollte dir wichtiger sein als deine Karriere.
translations.fr: Votre famille devrait passer avant votre carrière.
translations.pt: Sua família deve vir antes da sua carreira.

examples.text: Stars can be seen clearly in this area.

translations.fr: Ils sont clairement contre nous.

more.definition: That which limits the extent of anything; limit, extremity, bound, boundary, terminus.; Any of the binding conditions or promises in a contract or agreement.; Specifically, the conditions in a legal contract that specify the price and also how and when payment must be made.
more.etymology: Old French termebor. From Middle English terme, borrowed from Old French terme, from Latin terminus (“a bound, boundary, limit, end; in Medieval Latin, also a time, period, word, covenant, etc.”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *térmn̥ (“stump, end, boundary”). Doublet of terminus and termon. Old English had termen, from the same source.
