more.definition: The act of speaking in a quiet voice, especially without vibration of the vocal cords; the sound thus produced.; A rumor.; A faint trace or hint (of something).
more.etymology: From Middle English whisperen, from Old English hwisprian (“to mutter, murmur, whisper”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwisprōn, from Proto-Germanic *hwisprōną (“to hiss, whistle, whisper”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱweys-, *ḱwey- (“to hiss, whistle, whisper”). Cognate with Dutch wisperen (“to whisper”), German wispern (“to mumble, whisper”).

more.definition: To speak softly or under one's breath, so as to be heard only by one near at hand; to utter words without sonant breath; to talk without that vibration of the vocal cords which gives sonorous, or vocal, sound.; To say (something) softly or under one's breath, so as to be heard only by one near at hand; to utter (something) without sonant breath, without that vibration of the vocal cords which gives sonorous, or vocal, sound.; To mention privately and confidentially, or in a whisper.
more.etymology: From Middle English whisperen, from Old English hwisprian (“to mutter, murmur, whisper”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwisprōn, from Proto-Germanic *hwisprōną (“to hiss, whistle, whisper”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱweys-, *ḱwey- (“to hiss, whistle, whisper”). Cognate with Dutch wisperen (“to whisper”), German wispern (“to mumble, whisper”).

Cognate with Middle High German waben (“to wave”), German wabern (“to waft”), Icelandic váfa (“to fluctuate, waver, doubt”). See also waver.

examples.text: Can you give me an example?

translations.de: Kannst du mir ein Beispiel geben?
translations.fr: Tu peux me donner un exemple ?
translations.pt: Você poderia me dar um exemplo?

examples.text: Please give us some examples.

translations.de: Gib uns bitte einige Beispiele.
translations.fr: Donnez-nous des exemples s'il vous plait.
translations.pt: Por favor, nos dê alguns exemplos.

examples.text: For example, do you like English?

translations.de: Zum Beispiel, magst du Englisch?
translations.fr: Par exemple, est-ce que tu aimes l’anglais ?
translations.pt: Por exemplo, você gosta de inglês?

examples.text: Let me give you an example.

more.definition: Something that is representative of all such things in a group.; Something that serves to illustrate or explain a rule.; Something that serves as a pattern of behaviour to be imitated (a good example) or not to be imitated (a bad example).
more.etymology: From Middle English example, exaumple, from Old French example, essaumple, from Latin exemplum (“sample, pattern, specimen, copy for imitation, etc.”, literally “what is taken out”); see exempt. Doublet of exemplum and sample. Displaced native Middle English forebisne, from Old English forebȳsn; and Middle English bisne, from Old English bȳsn (modern English bizen).

examples.text: I'll give you an example.

examples.text: The examples in this dictionary are easy to understand.

translations.pt: Os exemplos neste dicionário são fáceis de entender.

examples.text: Can you give me another example?

translations.fr: Peux-tu me fournir un autre exemple ?
translations.pt: Você pode me dar outro exemplo?

examples.text: You should follow Tom's example.

translations.de: Nimm dir ein Beispiel an Tom!
translations.fr: Tu devrais suivre l'exemple de Tom.
translations.pt: Você deveria seguir o exemplo de Tom.

more.definition: To be illustrated or exemplified (by).
more.etymology: From Middle English example, exaumple, from Old French example, essaumple, from Latin exemplum (“sample, pattern, specimen, copy for imitation, etc.”, literally “what is taken out”); see exempt. Doublet of exemplum and sample. Displaced native Middle English forebisne, from Old English forebȳsn; and Middle English bisne, from Old English bȳsn (modern English bizen).

examples.text: Don't rush me.

examples.text: Don't rush.

examples.text: I've got to rush.

translations.de: Ich muss mich beeilen.
translations.fr: Je dois me dépêcher.
translations.pt: Tenho que me apressar.

examples.text: Are you in a rush?

translations.de: Sind Sie in Eile?
translations.fr: Êtes-vous pressé ?
translations.pt: Você está com pressa?

more.definition: A sudden forward motion.; A surge.; General haste.

examples.text: Tom was rushed to the hospital.

examples.text: It was done in a rush.

more.definition: To hurry; to perform a task with great haste, often not properly or without thinking carefully.; To flow or move forward rapidly or noisily.; To dribble rapidly.
more.etymology: Perhaps from Middle English ruschen, russchen (“to rush, startle, make a loud rushing noise”), from Old English hrysċan (“to jolt, startle”), from Proto-West Germanic *hurskijan, from Proto-Germanic *hurskijaną (“to startle, drive”), from *hurskaz (“fast, rapid, quick”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱers- (“to run, hurry”).

examples.text: According to the radio, it'll rain tomorrow.

translations.de: Laut Radio wird es morgen regnen.
translations.fr: Selon la radio, il va pleuvoir demain.
translations.pt: De acordo com o rádio, vai chover amanhã.

examples.text: According to Tom, Jane got married last month.

translations.de: Laut Tom hat Jane letzten Monat geheiratet.
translations.fr: D'après Tom, Jane s'est mariée le mois dernier.
translations.pt: Segundo Tom, Jane se casou o mês passado.

examples.text: We arranged the books according to size.

translations.de: Wir haben die Bücher nach Größe geordnet.
translations.fr: Nous avons classé les livres par taille.
translations.pt: Nós arrumamos os livros de acordo com o tamanho.

examples.text: All men are equal according to the law.

translations.de: Alle Menschen sind vor dem Gesetz gleich.
translations.fr: Tous les hommes sont égaux selon la loi.
translations.pt: Todos os homens são iguais perante a lei.

more.definition: Agreeing; in agreement or harmony; harmonious.
more.etymology: From accord + -ing.

examples.text: All men are equal according to the law.

translations.de: Alle Menschen sind vor dem Gesetz gleich.
translations.fr: Tous les hommes sont égaux selon la loi.
translations.pt: Todos os homens são iguais perante a lei.

examples.text: Everything went according to plan.

translations.de: Alles lief nach Plan.
translations.fr: Tout s'est déroulé selon le plan.
translations.pt: Tudo correu de acordo com o plano.

examples.text: The salary is fixed according to age and experience.

translations.de: Das Gehalt richtet sich nach dem Alter und der Berufserfahrung.
translations.fr: Le salaire est fixé en fonction de l'âge et de l'expérience.
translations.pt: O salário é fixo de acordo com a idade e a experiência.

examples.text: The meaning of words can change according to their context.

translations.de: Die Bedeutung eines Wortes kann sich durch den Zusammenhang ändern.
translations.fr: Le sens des mots peut changer en fonction de leur contexte.

more.etymology: From accord + -ing.

examples.text: I have hardly any money with me.

translations.de: Ich habe kaum Geld dabei.
translations.fr: Je n'ai presque pas d'argent sur moi.
translations.pt: Dificilmente tenho dinheiro comigo.

examples.text: I hardly ever go to museums.

translations.de: Ich gehe selten ins Museum.
translations.fr: Je ne vais quasiment jamais dans des musées.
translations.pt: Eu raramente vou a museus.

examples.text: I could hardly believe my eyes.

translations.de: Ich traute meinen Augen kaum.
translations.fr: Je pouvais à peine croire mes yeux.
translations.pt: Eu mal podia acreditar no que estava vendo.

examples.text: She's hardly ever home.

translations.de: Sie ist fast nie zu Hause.
translations.fr: Elle n'est pratiquement jamais chez elle.
translations.pt: Ela quase nunca está em casa.

more.definition: Barely, only just, almost not.; Certainly not; not at all.
more.etymology: From Middle English hardely, hardliche, from Old English heardlīċe (“boldly; hardily; without ease; in a way that causes pain; not easily; only by degrees”), equivalent to hard + -ly. Compare Dutch hardelijk, German härtlich.

examples.text: I have hardly any English books.

translations.de: Ich habe kaum englische Bücher.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pratiquement pas de livres anglais.
translations.pt: Eu não tenho praticamente nenhum livro de Inglês.

examples.text: I hardly ever get sick.

translations.de: Ich bin kaum einmal krank.
translations.fr: Je ne tombe presque jamais malade.
translations.pt: Eu raramente fico doente.

examples.text: I hardly see you anymore.

translations.de: Ich sehe dich kaum noch.
translations.fr: Je ne te vois quasiment plus.
translations.pt: Quase não te vejo mais.

examples.text: I hardly slept last night.

translations.de: Ich habe letzte Nacht kaum geschlafen.
translations.fr: J'ai à peine dormi, la nuit passée.
translations.pt: Eu mal dormi a noite passada.

more.definition: Not really.
more.etymology: From Middle English hardely, hardliche, from Old English heardlīċe (“boldly; hardily; without ease; in a way that causes pain; not easily; only by degrees”), equivalent to hard + -ly. Compare Dutch hardelijk, German härtlich.

examples.text: There is a windmill on the hill.

translations.de: Auf dem Hügel steht eine Windmühle.
translations.fr: Il y a un moulin à vent sur la colline.
translations.pt: Há um moinho de vento na colina.

examples.text: Our country doesn't have any mountains, only hills.

translations.de: Unser Land besitzt keine Berge, es hat lediglich Hügel.
translations.fr: Notre pays n'a pas de montagnes, il n'a que des collines.
translations.pt: Em nosso país não se encontram montanhas, mas só morros.

examples.text: They began to climb the hill.

translations.de: Sie begannen, den Hügel zu ersteigen.
translations.fr: Ils commencèrent à grimper sur la colline.
translations.pt: Eles começaram a escalar a colina.

examples.text: The building on the hill is our school.

translations.de: Das Gebäude auf dem Hügel ist unsere Schule.
translations.fr: Le bâtiment sur la colline est notre école.
translations.pt: O prédio na colina é a nossa escola.

more.definition: An elevated landmass smaller than a mountain.; A sloping part of a landscape, especially one with a road, trail, etc.; A heap of earth surrounding a plant.
more.etymology: From Middle English hil (“hill”), from Old English hyll (“hill”), from Proto-West Germanic *hulli (“hill”), from Proto-Germanic *hulliz (“hill”), from Proto-Indo-European *kl̥Hnís (“top, hill, rock”) (compare also Proto-Germanic *halluz (“stone, rock”)).

examples.text: There is a house on the hill.

translations.de: Auf dem Hügel steht ein Haus.
translations.fr: Il y a une maison sur la colline.
translations.pt: Existe uma casa na Colina.

examples.text: There are a lot of hills in this region.

translations.de: In dieser Region gibt es viele Hügel.
translations.fr: Il y a beaucoup de collines dans cette région.
translations.pt: Há muitas colinas nesta região.

examples.text: He went down the hill.

translations.de: Er ging den Hügel hinunter.
translations.fr: Il descendit de la colline.
translations.pt: Ele desceu o morro.

examples.text: The hill is always green.

translations.de: Der Hügel ist immer grün.
translations.fr: La colline est toujours verte.
translations.pt: A colina está sempre verde.

more.definition: To form into a heap or mound.; To heap or draw earth around plants.
more.etymology: From Middle English hil (“hill”), from Old English hyll (“hill”), from Proto-West Germanic *hulli (“hill”), from Proto-Germanic *hulliz (“hill”), from Proto-Indo-European *kl̥Hnís (“top, hill, rock”) (compare also Proto-Germanic *halluz (“stone, rock”)).

examples.text: I cannot possibly help you.

translations.de: Ich kann dir unmöglich helfen.
translations.fr: Il m'est impossible de t'aider.

examples.text: I think either of these could possibly be a valid translation into Japanese.

examples.text: Could you possibly translate this for me?

translations.fr: Ce qu'il a dit est dans le domaine du possible.

more.definition: Perhaps; indicates that the proposition may be true (is not certainly false) regardless of any facts or circumstances known to, stated by or implied by the speaker.; In the realm of possibility; indicates that the action may successfully be performed (is not impossible) regardless of any facts or circumstances known to, stated by or implied by the speaker that might limit the performance.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der. Proto-Germanic *līkąder. From possible + -ly.

examples.text: I grant there is no strength in old age.

translations.de: Ich gebe zu, dass es im Alter keine Stärke gibt.
translations.fr: Je reconnais qu'il n'y a pas de force dans la vieillesse.
translations.pt: Admito que não há força na velhice.

examples.text: He has no more strength.

translations.de: Er hat keine Kraft mehr.
translations.fr: Il n'a plus de force.
translations.pt: Ele não tem mais força.

examples.text: My muscular strength has weakened from lack of exercise.

translations.de: Meine Muskelkraft ist geschwächt, aus Mangel an Bewegung.
translations.fr: Ma force musculaire a diminué faute d'entrainement.
translations.pt: A minha força muscular enfraqueceu por falta de exercício físico.

examples.text: I don't have the strength to keep trying.

translations.de: Ich habe nicht die Kraft, es weiter zu versuchen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas la force de continuer à essayer.
translations.pt: Eu não tenho forças para continuar tentando.

more.definition: The quality or degree of being strong.; The intensity of a force or power; potency.; The strongest part of something; that on which confidence or reliance is based.
more.etymology: From Middle English strengthe, from Old English strengþu (“strength”), from Proto-West Germanic *strangiþu (“strongness; strength”), equivalent to strong + -th (abstract nominal suffix). examples.text: The ability to show weakness is a strength.

translations.de: Schwäche zeigen zu können ist eine Stärke.
translations.fr: La capacité à montrer ses faiblesses est une force.
translations.pt: A capacidade de mostrar fraqueza é uma força.

examples.text: Everyone has strengths and weaknesses.

translations.fr: Tout le monde a ses forces et ses faiblesses.
translations.pt: Todos têm forças e fraquezas.

examples.text: Tom needs to regain his strength.

translations.de: Tom muss wieder zu Kräften kommen.
translations.fr: Tom doit reprendre des forces.
translations.pt: Tom precisa recuperar as forças.

examples.text: Don't underestimate your own strength.

translations.de: Unterschätze nicht deine eigene Kraft.
translations.fr: Ne sous-estimez pas votre propre force !
translations.pt: Não subestimeis vossas próprias forças.

more.etymology: From Middle English strengthe, from Old English strengþu (“strength”), from Proto-West Germanic *strangiþu (“strongness; strength”), equivalent to strong + -th (abstract nominal suffix). examples.text: He saved himself somehow.

translations.de: Irgendwie rettete er sich.
translations.fr: Il s'en est sorti, d'une manière ou d'une autre.

examples.text: Somehow, Tom knew.

translations.de: Irgendwie wusste Tom Bescheid.
translations.fr: Pourtant, Tom savait.
translations.pt: De algum modo, Tom sabia.

examples.text: I'll find the money somehow.

translations.fr: Je trouverai l'argent d'une manière ou d'une autre.
translations.pt: Vou dar um jeito de arranjar o dinheiro.

examples.text: Tom somehow managed to swim across the river.

translations.de: Irgendwie schaffte Tom es, über den Fluss zu schwimmen.
translations.pt: De alguma maneira, Tom conseguiu atravessar o rio.

more.definition: In one way or another; in a way not yet known or explained; by some means
more.etymology: From some + how.

examples.text: What's your opinion on that?

translations.de: Was meinen Sie dazu?
translations.fr: Quel est votre avis sur la question ?
translations.pt: Qual é a tua opinião sobre isso?

examples.text: No one wants to listen to my opinions.

translations.de: Niemand will meine Meinungen hören.
translations.fr: Personne ne veut entendre mon avis.
translations.pt: Ninguém quer ouvir as minhas opiniões.

examples.text: Your opinion is important to me.

translations.de: Deine Meinung ist mir wichtig.
translations.fr: Ton avis compte pour moi.
translations.pt: A sua opinião é importante para mim.

examples.text: No one asked for your opinion.

translations.de: Niemand hat dich um deine Meinung gefragt.
translations.fr: Personne ne t'a demandé ton avis.
translations.pt: Ninguém pediu vossa opinião.

more.definition: A belief, judgment or perspective that a person has formed, either through objective or subjective reasoning, about a topic, issue, person or thing.; The judgment or sentiment which the mind forms of persons or things; estimation.; The formal decision, or expression of views, of a judge, an umpire, a doctor, or other party officially called upon to consider and decide upon a matter or point submitted.

examples.text: I would like to hear your opinion.

translations.de: Ich würde gern Ihre Meinung hören.
translations.fr: J'aimerais entendre votre opinion.
translations.pt: Gostaria de ouvir a sua opinião.

examples.text: Don't confuse opinions with facts.

translations.de: Verwechseln Sie nicht Meinungen mit Fakten.
translations.fr: Ne confondez pas les opinions avec les faits.
translations.pt: Não confundam opiniões com fatos.

examples.text: I ask you for your opinion.

translations.de: Ich bitte Sie um Ihre Meinung.
translations.fr: Je vous demande votre avis.
translations.pt: Peço-vos a vossa opinião.

examples.text: Your opinion is somewhat old-fashioned.

translations.de: Deine Ansicht ist ein wenig altmodisch.
translations.fr: Ton opinion est un peu démodée.
translations.pt: A sua opinião está um pouco fora de moda.

more.etymology: From English opine + -ion, from Middle English opinion, opinioun, from Anglo-Norman and Middle French opinion, from Latin opīniō, from opīnor (“to opine”). Displaced native Old English wēna.

examples.text: What season do you like the best?

translations.de: Welche Jahreszeit magst du am liebsten?

translations.pt: De qual estação do ano você gosta mais?

examples.text: We have four seasons in Japan.

translations.de: In Japan gibt es vier Jahreszeiten.
translations.fr: Il y a quatre saisons au Japon.
translations.pt: Temos quatro estações no Japão.

examples.text: Spring is the season of love.

translations.de: Der Frühling ist die Jahreszeit der Liebe.
translations.fr: Le printemps est la saison de l'amour.
translations.pt: A primavera é a estação do amor.

examples.text: What is the best season for whale watching?

translations.de: Wann ist die beste Zeit für Walbeobachtungen?
translations.fr: Quelle est la meilleure saison pour observer les baleines ?
translations.pt: Qual é a melhor época para observação de baleias?

more.definition: Each of the divisions of a year based on the prevailing weather: spring, summer, autumn (fall) and winter; or the rainy (monsoon) and dry season, depending on the climate.; A period of the year when something particular happens.; A period of the year in which a place is most busy or frequented for business, amusement, etc.

examples.text: Which season do you like the best?

translations.de: Welche Jahreszeit magst du am liebsten?
translations.fr: Quelle est votre saison préférée ?
translations.pt: De qual estação do ano você gosta mais?

examples.text: There are only two seasons in the tropics.

translations.de: In den Tropen gibt es nur zwei Jahreszeiten.
translations.fr: Dans les tropiques il n'y a que deux saisons.
translations.pt: Há apenas duas estações nos trópicos.

examples.text: I seasoned the fish with salt and pepper.

translations.de: Ich würzte den Fisch mit Salz und Pfeffer.

translations.pt: Eu temperei o peixe com sal e pimenta.

examples.text: Hotels are cheaper in the off season.

more.definition: To habituate, accustom, or inure (someone or something) to a particular use, purpose, or circumstance.; To prepare by drying or hardening, or removal of natural juices.; To become mature; to grow fit for use; to become adapted to a climate.
more.etymology: From Middle English sesoun, seson (“time of the year”), from Old French seson, saison (“time of sowing, seeding”), from Latin satiō (“act of sowing, planting”) from satum, past participle of serō (“to sow, plant”) from Proto-Indo-European *seh₁- (“to sow, plant”). examples.text: Female driver, constant danger.

translations.de: Sitzt eine Frau am Steuer, wird die Fahrt oft ungeheuer.

translations.pt: Mulher no volante, perigo constante.

translations.de: Der Lehrer hat weibliche Schüler.
translations.fr: Le professeur a des étudiantes.

translations.de: Tom hat viele Freundinnen.
translations.fr: Tom a beaucoup d'amies.
translations.pt: Tom tem muitas amigas.

more.definition: Belonging to the sex which typically produces eggs (ova), or to the gender which is typically associated with it.; Characteristic of this sex/gender. (Compare feminine, womanly.); Tending to lead to or regulate the development of sexual characteristics typical of this sex.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁(y)-der. Old French femelebor. From Middle English female, an alteration of Middle English femele, from Old French femele, femelle (“female”), from Medieval Latin fēmella (“a female”), from Latin fēmella (“a girl, a young female, a young woman”), diminutive of fēmina (“a woman”).

examples.text: The male teacher has female students.

translations.de: Der Lehrer hat weibliche Schüler.
translations.fr: Le professeur a des étudiantes.
translations.pt: O professor tem alunas.

examples.text: Tom has a lot female friends.

translations.de: Tom hat viele Freundinnen.
translations.fr: Tom a beaucoup d'amies.
translations.pt: Tom tem muitas amigas.

examples.text: Is that dog male or female?

translations.de: Ist dieser Hund männlich oder weiblich?
translations.fr: Ce chien est-il un mâle ou une femelle?
translations.pt: Esse cachorro é macho ou fêmea?

examples.text: Males are always more beautiful than females.

translations.de: Männchen sind immer schöner als Weibchen.
translations.fr: Les mâles sont toujours plus beaux que les femelles.
translations.pt: Os machos são sempre mais bonitos que as fêmeas.

more.definition: An animal of the sex that produces eggs.; A human of feminine gender; a girl or woman.; A plant which produces only that kind of reproductive organ capable of developing into fruit after impregnation or fertilization; a pistillate plant.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁(y)-der. Old French femelebor. From Middle English female, an alteration of Middle English femele, from Old French femele, femelle (“female”), from Medieval Latin fēmella (“a female”), from Latin fēmella (“a girl, a young female, a young woman”), diminutive of fēmina (“a woman”).

examples.text: Don't interfere in others' affairs.

translations.de: Misch dich nicht in anderer Leute Angelegenheiten ein.
translations.fr: Ne vous mêlez pas des affaires des autres.
translations.pt: Não se intrometa nas coisas dos outros.

examples.text: I don't want to be involved in this affair.

translations.de: Ich möchte nicht in diese Affäre hineingezogen werden.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas être impliqué dans cette affaire.
translations.pt: Não quero ser envolvido nesse negócio.

examples.text: You shouldn't interfere in other people's affairs.

translations.de: Du sollst dich nicht in Angelegenheiten anderer einmischen.
translations.fr: Vous ne devriez pas vous mêler des affaires des autres.
translations.pt: Você não se deve intrometer nos assuntos alheios.

examples.text: That is an internal affair of this country.

translations.de: Das ist eine innere Angelegenheit dieses Landes.
translations.fr: C'est une affaire intérieure à ce pays.
translations.pt: Isso é um assunto interno deste país.

more.definition: Something which is done or is to be done; business of any kind, commercial, professional, or public.; Any proceeding or action which it is wished to refer to or characterize vaguely.; An action or engagement not of sufficient magnitude to be called a battle.
more.etymology: Old French afaireder. From Middle English afere, affere, from Old French afaire, from a- + faire (“to do”), from Latin ad- + facere (“to do”). See fact, and compare ado.

examples.text: He's a powerful sorcerer.

translations.de: Er ist ein mächtiger Zauberer.
translations.fr: C'est un puissant sorcier.
translations.pt: Ele é um bruxo poderoso.

examples.text: She's a powerful witch.

translations.de: Sie ist eine mächtige Hexe.
translations.fr: C'est une puissante sorcière.
translations.pt: Ela é uma bruxa poderosa.

examples.text: Tom is powerful.

translations.de: Tom ist mächtig.
translations.fr: Tom est puissant.
translations.pt: O Tom é poderoso.

examples.text: We're powerful.

translations.de: Wir sind stark.
translations.fr: Nous sommes puissants.
translations.pt: Nós somos poderosos.

more.definition: Having, or capable of exerting, power or influence.; Leading to many or important deductions.; Large; capacious; said of veins of ore.
more.etymology: From Middle English pouerful, powarfull. By surface analysis, power + -ful.

examples.text: They made more powerful arms.

translations.de: Sie bauten stärkere Waffen.
translations.fr: Ils construisirent des armes plus puissantes.
translations.pt: Eles fizeram mais armas poderosas.

examples.text: He is powerful.

translations.de: Er ist mächtig.
translations.fr: Il est puissant.
translations.pt: Ele é poderoso.

examples.text: Hope is more powerful than fear.

translations.de: Hoffnung ist mächtiger als Angst.
translations.fr: L'espoir est plus puissant que la peur.
translations.pt: A esperança é mais poderosa que o medo.

examples.text: Moral leadership is more powerful than any weapon.

translations.de: Die moralische Führungskraft ist stärker als jede Waffe.
translations.fr: L'autorité morale est plus puissante que n'importe quelle arme.
translations.pt: Liderança moral é mais poderosa do que qualquer arma.

more.etymology: From Middle English pouerful, powarfull. By surface analysis, power + -ful.

examples.text: She doesn't eat meat, does she?

translations.de: Sie isst kein Fleisch, stimmt’s?
translations.fr: Elle ne mange pas de viande, n'est-ce pas ?
translations.pt: Ela não come carne, né?

examples.text: Is eating less meat a good idea?

translations.de: Ist es gut, weniger Fleisch zu essen?
translations.fr: Est-ce que manger moins de viande est une bonne idée ?
translations.pt: Comer menos carne é uma boa ideia?

examples.text: The dog didn't eat the meat.

translations.de: Der Hund fraß das Fleisch nicht.
translations.fr: Le chien n'a pas mangé la viande.
translations.pt: O cachorro não comeu a carne.

examples.text: I don't eat meat myself.

translations.de: Ich selbst esse kein Fleisch.
translations.fr: Je ne mange pas de viande moi-même.
translations.pt: Eu mesmo não como carne.

more.definition: The flesh (muscle tissue) of a killed animal used as food.; A food designed to replicate its taste and texture (such as plant-based meat).; A type of meat, by anatomic position and provenance.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *meh₂d-der. Inherited from Middle English mete (“food”), from Old English mete (“food”), from Proto-West Germanic *mati (“food”), from Proto-Germanic *matiz (“food”), from Proto-Indo-European *meh₂d- (“to be wet; grease, fat”).

examples.text: Someone left their umbrella in the hall.

translations.de: Jemand hat seinen Regenschirm im Saal stehen lassen.
translations.fr: Quelqu'un a laissé son parapluie dans le couloir.
translations.pt: Alguém deixou seu guarda-chuva no salão.

examples.text: The speaker swaggered into the lecture hall.

translations.de: Der Redner betrat pompös den Konferenzraum.
translations.fr: Le conférencier se pavanait dans la salle de conférence.
translations.pt: O palestrante entrou pomposamente na sala da conferência.

examples.text: The city hall isn't far from here.

translations.de: Das Rathaus ist nicht weit entfernt von hier.
translations.fr: La mairie n'est pas loin d'ici.
translations.pt: A prefeitura não fica longe daqui.

examples.text: He entered the hall of fame.

translations.de: Er betrat die Ruhmeshalle.
translations.fr: Il entra au Panthéon.
translations.pt: Ele entrou para o hall da fama.

more.definition: A corridor; a hallway.; A large meeting room.; A manor house (originally because a magistrate's court was held in the hall of his mansion).
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English halle (“hall”), from Old English heall (“hall, dwelling, house, palace, temple, law-court”), from Proto-West Germanic *hallu (“hall”), from Proto-Germanic *hallō (“hall”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱel- (“to hide, conceal”).

examples.text: Would you like a cup of milk?

translations.de: Möchtest du eine Tasse Milch?
translations.fr: Voudrais-tu une tasse de lait ?
translations.pt: Você gostaria de um copo de leite?

examples.text: I've drunk three cups of coffee already.

translations.de: Ich habe schon drei Tassen Kaffee getrunken.
translations.fr: J'ai déjà bu trois tasses de café.
translations.pt: Já bebi três xícaras de café.

examples.text: France have won the World Cup.

translations.de: Frankreich hat bei der Weltmeisterschaft gesiegt.
translations.fr: La France a gagné la Coupe du Monde.
translations.pt: A França venceu a Copa do Mundo.

examples.text: They drank a cup of coffee.

translations.de: Sie tranken eine Tasse Kaffee.
translations.fr: Ils ont bu une tasse de café.
translations.pt: Eles tomaram uma xícara de café.

more.definition: A concave vessel for drinking, usually made of opaque material (as opposed to a glass) and with a handle.; The contents of said vessel.; A US unit of liquid measure equal to 8 fluid ounces (¹⁄₁₆ of a US gallon; 236.5882365 mL) or 240 mL.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *kewp-der. Proto-Indo-European *gew-der. Inherited from Middle English cuppe, coppe, from the merger of Old English cuppe (“cup”) and Old English copp (“cup, vessel”). Old English cuppe is a borrowing from Late Latin cuppa, itself of obscure origin, but probably from earlier Latin cūpa (“tub, cask”), from Proto-Indo-European *kewp- (“a hollow”).

examples.text: Would you like a cup of coffee?

translations.de: Möchtest du eine Tasse Kaffee?
translations.fr: Voudrais-tu une tasse de café ?
translations.pt: Gostaria de uma xícara de café?

examples.text: You've drunk three cups of coffee.

translations.de: Du hast drei Tassen Kaffee getrunken.
translations.fr: Tu as bu trois tasses de café.

examples.text: Please give me a cup of milk.

translations.de: Gib mir bitte eine Tasse Milch.
translations.fr: S'il te plaît, donne-moi une tasse de lait.
translations.pt: Por favor, dá-me um copo de leite.

examples.text: What about a cup of coffee?

translations.de: Wie wäre es mit einer Tasse Kaffee?
translations.fr: Et si on prenait une tasse de café ?
translations.pt: Que tal uma xícara de café?

more.definition: To form into the shape of a cup, particularly of the hands.; To hold something in cupped hands.; To pour (a liquid, drink, etc.) into a cup.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *kewp-der. Proto-Indo-European *gew-der. Inherited from Middle English cuppe, coppe, from the merger of Old English cuppe (“cup”) and Old English copp (“cup, vessel”). Old English cuppe is a borrowing from Late Latin cuppa, itself of obscure origin, but probably from earlier Latin cūpa (“tub, cask”), from Proto-Indo-European *kewp- (“a hollow”).

examples.text: The rumour has already spread.

translations.de: Das Gerücht hat schon die Runde gemacht.
translations.fr: La rumeur s'est déjà répandue.
translations.pt: O rumor já se espalhou.

examples.text: The bird spread its wings.

translations.de: Der Vogel spreizte die Flügel.
translations.fr: L'oiseau déploya ses ailes.
translations.pt: O pássaro estendeu suas asas.

examples.text: A fire can spread faster than you can run.

translations.de: Ein Feuer kann sich schneller ausbreiten, als man rennen kann.
translations.fr: Un feu peut se propager plus rapidement qu'on ne peut courir.
translations.pt: Um incêndio pode se espalhar mais rápido do que você pode correr.

examples.text: She spread the gossip all over the town.

translations.de: Sie verteilte den Tratsch in der gesamten Stadt.
translations.fr: Elle a répandu la rumeur dans toute la ville.
translations.pt: Ela espalhou a fofoca por toda a cidade.

more.definition: The act of spreading.; Something that has been spread.; A layout, pattern or design of cards arranged for a reading.
more.etymology: From Middle English spreden, from Old English sprǣdan (“to spread, expand”), from Proto-Germanic *spraidijaną (“to spread”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)per- (“to strew, sow, sprinkle”).

examples.text: She spread a beautiful cloth on a table.

translations.de: Sie breitete eine wunderschöne Decke auf dem Tisch aus.
translations.fr: Elle étala une belle nappe sur une table.
translations.pt: Ela estendeu uma toalha muito bonita sobre a mesa.

examples.text: He spread butter on the bread.

translations.de: Er schmierte Butter aufs Brot.
translations.fr: Il étala du beurre sur le pain.
translations.pt: Ele passou manteiga no pão.

examples.text: The news spread all over Japan.

translations.de: Die Nachricht verbreitete sich über ganz Japan.
translations.fr: Les nouvelles se répandirent à travers tout le Japon.
translations.pt: A notícia se espalhou por todo o Japão.

examples.text: How does this disease spread?

translations.de: Wie breitet sich diese Krankheit aus?
translations.fr: Comment se répand la maladie ?
translations.pt: Como esta doença se espalha?

more.definition: To stretch out, open out (a material etc.) so that it more fully covers a given area of space.; To extend (individual rays, limbs etc.); to stretch out in varying or opposing directions. simple past and past participle of spread; To disperse, to scatter or distribute over a given area.
more.etymology: From Middle English spreden, from Old English sprǣdan (“to spread, expand”), from Proto-Germanic *spraidijaną (“to spread”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)per- (“to strew, sow, sprinkle”).

examples.text: The United States is abundant in natural resources.

translations.de: Die Vereinigten Staaten sind reich an natürlichen Ressourcen.
translations.fr: Les États-Unis sont riches en ressources naturelles.
translations.pt: Os Estados Unidos são abundantes em recursos naturais.

examples.text: Japan is poor in natural resources.

translations.de: Japan ist arm an natürlichen Ressourcen.
translations.fr: Le Japon est pauvre en ressources naturelles.
translations.pt: O Japão é pobre em recursos naturais.

examples.text: A rainbow is a natural phenomenon.

translations.de: Ein Regenbogen ist ein Naturphänomen.
translations.fr: Un arc-en-ciel est un phénomène naturel.
translations.pt: O arco-íris é um fenômeno natural.

examples.text: China is rich in natural resources.

translations.de: China ist reich an Bodenschätzen.
translations.fr: La Chine est riche en ressources naturelles.
translations.pt: A China é rica em recursos naturais.

more.definition: Existing in the nature of a person or thing; innate, not acquired or learned.; Normally associated with a particular person or thing; inherently related to the nature of a thing or creature.; As expected; reasonable, normal; naturally arising from the given circumstances.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English natural, borrowed from Old French natural, naturel, from Latin nātūrālis, from nātus, the perfect participle of nāscor (“be born”, verb). Displaced native Old English ġecynde. By surface analysis, natur(e) + -al.

examples.text: Earthquakes and floods are natural disasters.

translations.de: Erdbeben und Hochwasser sind Naturkatastrophen.
translations.fr: Les tremblements de terre et les inondations sont des catastrophes naturelles.
translations.pt: Terremotos e enchentes são desastres naturais.

examples.text: Water is a natural resource of vital importance.

translations.de: Wasser ist eine natürliche Ressource von größter Wichtigkeit.
translations.fr: L'eau est une ressource naturelle de la plus haute importance.
translations.pt: A água é um recurso natural de importância vital.

examples.text: Australia is rich in natural resources.

translations.de: Australien ist reich an natürlichen Ressourcen.
translations.fr: L'Australie est riche en ressources naturelles.
translations.pt: A Austrália é rica em recursos naturais.

examples.text: The Moon is the only natural satellite of Earth.

translations.de: Der Mond ist der einzige natürliche Satellit der Erde.
translations.fr: La Lune est le seul satellite naturel de la Terre.
translations.pt: A Lua é o único satélite natural da Terra.

more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English natural, borrowed from Old French natural, naturel, from Latin nātūrālis, from nātus, the perfect participle of nāscor (“be born”, verb). Displaced native Old English ġecynde. By surface analysis, natur(e) + -al.

examples.text: I like to drink natural mineral water.

translations.de: Ich trinke gerne natürliches Mineralwasser.
translations.fr: J'aime boire de l'eau minérale naturelle.
translations.pt: Adoro tomar água mineral natural.

examples.text: The Moon is a so-called natural satellite.

translations.de: Der Mond ist ein sogenannter Trabant.
translations.fr: La Lune est un satellite dit naturel.
translations.pt: A Lua é um assim chamado satélite natural.

examples.text: The Black Forest gateau is a natural aphrodisiac.

translations.de: Schwarzwälder Kirschtorte ist ein natürliches Aphrodisiakum.
translations.fr: La forêt-noire est un aphrodisiaque naturel.
translations.pt: O bolo Floresta Negra é um afrodisíaco natural.

examples.text: The earth's moon is a natural satellite.

translations.de: Der Mond der Erde ist ein natürlicher Satellit.
translations.fr: La lune de la Terre est un satellite naturel.
translations.pt: A Lua da Terra é um satélite natural.

more.definition: A note that is not or is no longer to be modified by an accidental.; The symbol ♮ used to indicate such a natural note.; One with an innate talent at or for something.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English natural, borrowed from Old French natural, naturel, from Latin nātūrālis, from nātus, the perfect participle of nāscor (“be born”, verb). Displaced native Old English ġecynde. By surface analysis, natur(e) + -al.

examples.text: A red light is often used as a danger signal.

translations.de: Ein rotes Licht wird oft als Warnsignal verwendet.
translations.fr: Une lumière rouge est souvent utilisée comme un signal de danger.
translations.pt: Uma luz vermelha é frequentemente usada como um sinal de perigo.

examples.text: My mobile hasn't got a signal.

translations.de: Mein Handy hat kein Netz.
translations.fr: Mon portable n'a pas de réseau.

examples.text: Did you hear the alarm signal?

translations.de: Hast du das Alarmsignal gehört?
translations.fr: Avez-vous entendu le signal d'alarme ?

examples.text: A smile sends a friendship signal.

translations.fr: Un sourire envoie un signal d'amitié.
translations.pt: Um sorriso envia um sinal de amizade.

more.etymology: From Old French segnal, seignal or Medieval Latin signāle; noun use of the neuter of Late Latin signālis, from Latin signum; verb use from 1805, as a shortened from signalize (1650s). Doublet of signum and sign.

translations.de: Er gab uns das Signal anzufangen.

examples.text: Don't change lanes without signaling.

translations.de: Nicht die Spur wechseln, ohne zu blinken!
translations.fr: Ne change pas de voie sans mettre ton clignotant.

translations.de: Der Polizist bedeutete ihm anzuhalten.
translations.fr: Le policier lui intima de s'arrêter.

examples.text: I maxed out my credit card.

translations.de: Ich habe mein Kreditkartenlimit ausgeschöpft.
translations.fr: J'ai épuisé ma carte de crédit.

examples.text: Do you have a credit card?

translations.de: Haben Sie eine Kreditkarte?
translations.fr: Avez-vous une carte de crédit ?
translations.pt: Você tem cartão de crédito?

examples.text: Which credit cards can I use?

translations.de: Welche Kreditkarten kann ich nutzen?
translations.fr: Quelles cartes de crédit puis-je utiliser ?

examples.text: I lost my credit card.

translations.pt: Eu perdi o meu cartão de crédito.

examples.text: I would like to pay with a credit card.

more.definition: To believe; to put credence in.; To add to an account.; To acknowledge the contribution of.

examples.text: Tom denied that he was the thief.

translations.de: Tom bestritt, der Dieb zu sein.
translations.fr: Tom a nié qu'il était le voleur.
translations.pt: Tom negou que ele era o ladrão.

examples.text: Watch out for thieves around here.

translations.de: Pass auf die Diebe hier in der Gegend auf.
translations.fr: Fais gaffe aux voleurs dans le coin.
translations.pt: Tenha cuidado com ladrões por esses arredores.

examples.text: Once a thief, always a thief.

translations.de: Einmal ein Dieb, immer ein Dieb.
translations.fr: Qui a bu boira.
translations.pt: Uma vez ladrão, sempre ladrão.

translations.de: Der Dieb will die Schuhe nicht kaufen.
translations.fr: Le voleur ne veut pas acheter les chaussures.
translations.pt: O ladrão não quer comprar os sapatos.

Cognate with Saterland Frisian Tjoof (“thief”), West Frisian tsjeaf (“thief”), Dutch dief (“thief”), Low German Deef, Deev (“thief”), German Dieb (“thief”), Danish tyv (“thief”), Swedish tjuv (“thief”), Icelandic þjófur (“thief”).

examples.text: Rob, go watch TV.

translations.de: Rob, geh' fernsehen.
translations.fr: Rob, va regarder la télé.
translations.pt: Rob, vai assistir à TV.

examples.text: We intend to rob a bank.

translations.fr: On a l'intention de braquer une banque.
translations.pt: Nós pretendemos assaltar um banco.

examples.text: This law will rob us of our basic rights.

translations.de: Dieses Gesetz wird uns unsere Grundrechte rauben.
translations.fr: Cette loi nous privera de nos droits fondamentaux.

examples.text: Rob told me the good news!

translations.de: Rob erzählte mir von den guten Neuigkeiten!
translations.pt: Rob me contou a boa notícia!

more.definition: A syrup made of evaporating fruit juice over a fire, usually mixed with sugar or honey, and especially used for medicinal purposes.

examples.text: He was robbed of all his money.

more.definition: A slightly curved but almost flat dish from which food is served or eaten.; Such dishes collectively.; The contents of such a dish.
more.etymology: From Middle English plate, from Old French plate, from Medieval Latin plata, from Vulgar Latin *plat(t)us, from Ancient Greek πλατύς (platús, “broad, flat, wide”). Compare Spanish plato. (foot): Cockney rhyming slang, from "plates of meat" for "feet".

examples.text: These plates are hand painted.

translations.de: Diese Teller sind handbemalt.
translations.fr: Ces assiettes sont peintes à la main.
translations.pt: Estes pratos são pintados à mão.

examples.text: Who broke the plate?

translations.de: Wer hat den Teller zerbrochen?
translations.fr: Qui a cassé l'assiette ?
translations.pt: Quem quebrou o prato?

examples.text: There are no clean plates.

translations.de: Es gibt keine sauberen Teller.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas d'assiettes propres.
translations.pt: Não há pratos limpos.

examples.text: They brought the plates and put them on the table.

translations.de: Sie brachten die Teller und stellten sie auf den Tisch.
translations.fr: Ils apportèrent les assiettes et les posèrent sur la table.
translations.pt: Trouxeram os pratos e puseram-nos em cima da mesa.

more.definition: To cover the surface material of an object with a thin coat of another material, usually a metal.; To place the various elements of a meal on the diner's plate prior to serving.; To score a run.
more.etymology: From Middle English platen, from Old English platian and Old French plater, both ultimately from Latin plata (see above).

examples.text: Can you whistle?

translations.de: Kannst du pfeifen?
translations.fr: Savez-vous siffler ?
translations.pt: Você sabe assobiar?

examples.text: I cannot whistle.

translations.de: Ich kann nicht pfeifen.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas siffler.
translations.pt: Não sei assobiar.

examples.text: Do you know how to whistle?

translations.de: Können Sie pfeifen?
translations.fr: Savez-vous siffler ?
translations.pt: Você sabe assobiar?

examples.text: I can't whistle.

translations.de: Ich kann nicht pfeifen.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas siffler.
translations.pt: Não sei assobiar.

more.definition: A device designed to be placed in the mouth and blown, or driven by steam or some other mechanism, to make a whistling sound.; An act of whistling.; A shrill, high-pitched sound made by whistling.
more.etymology: From Middle English whistel, whistil, whistle, from Old English hwistle, from the verb (see below).

examples.text: Do you know how to whistle?

translations.de: Können Sie pfeifen?
translations.fr: Savez-vous siffler ?
translations.pt: Você sabe assobiar?

examples.text: My sister was whistling merrily.

translations.de: Meine Schwester pfiff munter vor sich hin.
translations.fr: Ma sœur sifflait joyeusement.
translations.pt: Minha irmã estava assobiando alegremente.

examples.text: I can't whistle.

translations.de: Ich kann nicht pfeifen.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas siffler.
translations.pt: Não sei assobiar.

examples.text: He can't whistle.

translations.de: Er kann nicht pfeifen.
translations.fr: Il ne sait pas siffler.
translations.pt: Ele não sabe assobiar.

more.definition: To make a shrill, high-pitched sound by forcing air through the mouth. To produce a whistling sound, restrictions to the flow of air are created using the teeth, tongue and lips.; To make a similar sound by forcing air through a musical instrument or a pipe etc.; To move in such a way as to create a whistling sound.
more.etymology: From Middle English whistlen, from Old English hwistlan, hwistlian (“to whistle”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwistlōn, from Proto-Germanic *hwistlōną (“to make a hissing sound”). Cognate with Swedish vissla (“to whistle”), Icelandic hvísla (“to whisper”), Russian свистеть (svistetʹ, “to whistle”).

examples.text: Ziri signed the contract.

translations.de: Ziri unterschrieb den Vertrag.
translations.fr: Ziri a signé le contrat.
translations.pt: Ziri assinou o contrato.

examples.text: We have a contract.

translations.de: Wir haben einen Vertrag.
translations.fr: Nous avons un contrat.
translations.pt: Nós temos um contrato.

examples.text: Tom signed the contract.

translations.de: Tom unterschrieb den Vertrag.
translations.fr: Tom signa le contrat.
translations.pt: Tom assinou o contrato.

examples.text: Look over the contract well, before you sign it.

translations.de: Sieh dir den Vertrag gut an, ehe du ihn unterschreibst.
translations.fr: Regardez bien le contrat avant de le signer.
translations.pt: Olhe bem o contrato antes de assiná-lo.

more.etymology: From Middle English, from Old French contract, from Latin contractus (noun), from contrahere (“to bring together, to bring about, to conclude a bargain”) [from con- (“with, together”) + trahere (“to draw, to pull”)] + -tus (suffix forming nouns from verbs).

examples.text: This contract is null and void.

translations.de: Dieser Vertrag ist null und nichtig.
translations.fr: Ce contrat est nul et non avenu.
translations.pt: Este contrato é inválido e sem efeito.

examples.text: I've already signed the contract.

translations.de: Ich habe den Vertrag bereits unterschrieben.
translations.fr: J'ai déjà signé le contrat.
translations.pt: Eu já assinei o contrato.

examples.text: Have you already signed the contract?

translations.de: Hast du den Vertrag schon unterzeichnet?
translations.fr: Avez-vous déjà signé le contrat ?
translations.pt: Vocês já assinaram o contrato?

examples.text: Tom refused to sign the contract.

translations.de: Tom weigerte sich, den Vertrag zu unterzeichnen.
translations.fr: Tom a refusé de signer le contrat.
translations.pt: Tom se recusou a assinar o contrato.

more.definition: An agreement between two or more parties, to perform a specific job or work order, often temporary or of fixed duration and usually governed by a written agreement.; A period of work agreed to under a temporary contract.; An agreement which the law will enforce in some way. A legally binding contract must contain at least one promise, i.e., a commitment or offer, by an offeror to and accepted by an offeree to do something in the future. A contract is thus executory rather than executed.
more.etymology: From Middle English, from Old French contract, from Latin contractus (noun), from contrahere (“to bring together, to bring about, to conclude a bargain”) [from con- (“with, together”) + trahere (“to draw, to pull”)] + -tus (suffix forming nouns from verbs).

examples.text: Tom translated the contract into French.

translations.de: Tom übersetzte den Vertrag ins Französische.
translations.fr: Tom a traduit le contrat en français.
translations.pt: Tom traduziu o contrato em francês.

examples.text: We need to have a contract.

translations.de: Wir brauchen einen Vertrag.
translations.fr: Nous avons besoin d'un contrat.
translations.pt: Precisamos de um contrato.

examples.text: It is very important to sign this contract today.

translations.de: Es ist sehr wichtig, diesen Vertrag heute zu unterzeichnen.
translations.fr: Il est très important de signer ce contrat aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: É muito importante assinar este contrato hoje.

examples.text: Did you sign the contract?

translations.de: Hast du den Vertrag unterschrieben?
translations.fr: Avez-vous signé le contrat ?
translations.pt: Vocês assinaram o contrato?

more.definition: To draw together or nearer; to shorten, narrow, or lessen.; To shorten by omitting a letter or letters or by reducing two or more vowels or syllables to one.; To make an agreement or contract; to covenant.
more.etymology: From Middle English, from Middle French contracter, from Latin contractum, past participle of contrahere (“to bring together, to bring about, to conclude a bargain”), from con- (“with, together”) + trahere (“to draw, to pull”). The verb developed after the noun, and originally meant only "draw together"; the sense "make a contract with" developed later.

examples.text: The original is unfaithful to the translation.

translations.de: Das Original hält sich nicht an die Übersetzung.
translations.fr: L'original est infidèle à la traduction.
translations.pt: O original é infiel à tradução.

examples.text: The translation is true to the original.

translations.de: Die Übersetzung ist originalgetreu.
translations.fr: La traduction est fidèle à l'original.
translations.pt: A tradução é fiel ao original.

examples.text: Bill has a lot of original ideas.

translations.de: Bill hat viele originelle Ideen.
translations.fr: Bill a beaucoup d'idées originales.
translations.pt: Bill tem muitas ideias originais.

examples.text: These translations are close to the original text.

translations.de: Diese Übersetzungen sind nah am Originaltext.
translations.fr: Ces traductions sont proches du texte original.
translations.pt: Estas traduções estão próximas do texto original.

more.definition: Relating to the origin or beginning; preceding all others.; First in a series of copies or versions.; Newly created.
more.etymology: From Middle English original, from Old French original, from Late Latin orīginālis (“primitive, original”), from Latin orīgō (“beginning, source, origin”), equivalent to origin + -al; see origin.

examples.text: I think that these paintings are very original.

translations.de: Ich denke, dass diese Bilder sehr originell sind.
translations.fr: Je trouve que ces tableaux sont très originaux.
translations.pt: Acho que esses quadros são muito originais.

examples.text: These are the originals.

translations.de: Hier sind die Originale.
translations.fr: En voici les originaux.
translations.pt: Estes são os originais.

examples.text: I like the original better than the remix.

translations.de: Ich mag das Original mehr als den Remix.
translations.fr: Je préfère l'original au remixage.
translations.pt: Eu gosto mais da original do que o remix.

examples.text: Translations are nothing more than interpretations of the original.

translations.de: Übersetzungen sind nichts anderes als Interpretationen des Originals.
translations.fr: Les traductions ne sont rien de plus que des interprétations de l'original.
translations.pt: As traduções nada mais são que interpretações do original.

more.definition: An object or other creation (e.g. narrative work) from which all later copies and variations are derived.; A person with a unique and interesting personality or creative talent.; A newly designed garment released by a fashion designer as part of a collection.
more.etymology: From Middle English original, from Old French original, from Late Latin orīginālis (“primitive, original”), from Latin orīgō (“beginning, source, origin”), equivalent to origin + -al; see origin.

examples.text: Don't mix up comets and asteroids.

translations.de: Verwechsle nicht Kometen mit Asteroiden.
translations.fr: Ne confondez pas les comètes et les astéroïdes.
translations.pt: Não confunda cometas com asteroides.

examples.text: I don't like to mix business with pleasure.

translations.de: Ich mag es nicht, Geschäft mit Vergnügen zu verbinden.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas mélanger le travail avec le plaisir.
translations.pt: Não gosto de misturar negócios com diversão.

examples.text: Kiwis taste like a mix between a banana and a strawberry.

translations.de: Kiwis schmecken wie eine Mischung aus Banane und Erdbeere.
translations.fr: Les kiwis ont le goût d'un mélange entre une banane et une fraise.
translations.pt: O sabor do kiwi é uma mistura de banana e morango.

examples.text: Oil and water don't mix.

translations.de: Öl und Wasser mischen sich nicht.
translations.fr: L'huile et l'eau ne sont pas miscibles.
translations.pt: O óleo não se mistura com água.

more.definition: The result of mixing two or more substances; a mixture.; The result of combining items normally kept separate.; A preparation, usually in the form of a powder, into which other ingredients can be mixed to prepare a specified foodstuff.
more.etymology: A merger of a nominal use of the verb and a borrowing from Anglo-Norman mixte, from Latin mixtus, past participle of misceō (“mix”). Nowadays regarded automatically as the nominal form of the verb.

examples.text: Don't mix up comets and asteroids.

translations.de: Verwechsle nicht Kometen mit Asteroiden.
translations.fr: Ne confondez pas les comètes et les astéroïdes.
translations.pt: Não confunda cometas com asteroides.

examples.text: She mixed him up with someone else.

translations.de: Sie verwechselte ihn mit jemand anderem.
translations.fr: Elle le prit pour quelqu'un d'autre.
translations.pt: Ela confundiu ele com outra pessoa.

examples.text: You cannot mix oil and water.

translations.de: Man kann Öl und Wasser nicht vermischen.
translations.fr: Tu ne peux pas mélanger de l'huile avec de l'eau.
translations.pt: Não dá para misturar óleo e água.

examples.text: I don't like to mix business with pleasure.

translations.de: Ich mag es nicht, Geschäft mit Vergnügen zu verbinden.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas mélanger le travail avec le plaisir.
translations.pt: Não gosto de misturar negócios com diversão.

more.definition: To stir together.; To combine (items from two or more sources normally kept separate).; To form by mingling; to produce by the stirring together of ingredients; to concoct from different parts.
more.etymology: From Middle English mixen (attested in past tense as mixed, myxyd), from Old English *mixian, miscian, from Proto-West Germanic *miskijan, from Proto-West Germanic *miskijan (“to mix”), from Proto-Indo-European *miḱ-sḱé-ti, from *meyǵ-, *meyḱ- (“to mix”).

examples.text: I am getting weaker and weaker!

translations.de: Ich werde immer schwächer.
translations.fr: Je deviens de plus en plus faible.
translations.pt: Eu estou ficando cada vez mais fraco!

examples.text: I feel a little weak today.

translations.de: Ich fühle mich heute ein bisschen schwach.
translations.fr: Je me sens un peu faible aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Estou me sentindo um pouco mole hoje.

examples.text: A chain is no stronger than its weakest link.

translations.de: Eine Kette ist nur so stark wie ihr schwächstes Glied.
translations.fr: Une chaîne n'est aussi forte que son maillon le plus faible.
translations.pt: Uma corrente não é mais forte do que seu elo mais fraco.

examples.text: Women are physically weaker than men.

translations.de: Frauen sind physisch schwächer als Männer.
translations.fr: Les femmes sont physiquement plus faibles que les hommes.
translations.pt: As mulheres são fisicamente mais fracas do que os homens.

more.definition: Lacking in force (usually strength) or ability.; Unable to sustain a great weight, pressure, or strain.; Limp, soft.
more.etymology: From Middle English waik, wayk, wayke, weik, weyk, borrowed from Old Norse veikr (“weak”), from Proto-Germanic *waikwaz (“weak, yielded, pliant, bendsome”), from *wīkwaną (“to cease, fold, yield; to retreat”), from Proto-Indo-European *weyg- (“to bend, turn, wind”), from *weh₁y- (“to plait, twist, weave, wind; to cover, enclose, wrap”).

examples.text: What do you think the audience wants?

translations.de: Was, denkst du, wünscht sich das Publikum?
translations.fr: Que penses-tu que le public veuille ?
translations.pt: O que você acha que o público quer?

examples.text: The audience didn't like it.

translations.de: Dem Publikum hat es nicht gefallen.
translations.fr: Le public ne l'a pas aimé.
translations.pt: O público não gostou.

examples.text: The audience consisted mainly of students.

translations.de: Das Publikum bestand hauptsächlich aus Studenten.
translations.fr: Le public était essentiellement composé d'étudiants.
translations.pt: O público consistia principalmente de estudantes.

examples.text: The audience acclaimed the actors for their performance.

translations.de: Das Publikum feierte die Schauspieler für ihre Darbietung.
translations.fr: Le public a acclamé les acteurs pour leur représentation.
translations.pt: O público aplaudiu os atores pela performance.

more.definition: A group of people within hearing; specifically, a large gathering of people listening to or watching a performance, speech, etc.; A widespread or nationwide viewing or listening public, as of a TV or radio network or program.; A formal meeting with a state or religious dignitary.
more.etymology: From Middle English audience, from Middle French audience, from Old French audience, from Latin audientia, from present participle audiēns (“hearing”), from verb audiō (“to hear”). Doublet of audiencia.

examples.text: At this hour, there is incredible traffic.

translations.de: Um diese Zeit ist ein unglaublicher Verkehr.
translations.fr: À cette heure il y a un trafic incroyable.
translations.pt: Nessa hora há um tráfego incrível.

examples.text: What they did was incredible.

translations.de: Was sie getan haben, war unglaublich.
translations.fr: Ce qu'ils ont fait était incroyable.
translations.pt: O que eles fizeram foi incrível.

examples.text: The concert was incredible.

translations.de: Das Konzert war traumhaft.
translations.fr: Le concert était comme un rêve.
translations.pt: O concerto foi incrível.

examples.text: This technology is an incredible thing!

translations.de: Diese Technologie ist eine unglaubliche Sache!
translations.fr: Cette technologie est une chose incroyable !
translations.pt: Essa tecnologia é uma coisa incrível!

more.definition: Too implausible to be credible; beyond belief.; Amazing; astonishing; awe-inspiring.; Marvellous; profoundly affecting; wonderful; excellent.
more.etymology: From Middle English incredible, from Latin incrēdibilis (“that cannot be believed”), from in- (“not”) + crēdibilis (“worthy of belief”), from crēdō (“believe”), equivalent to in- + credible.

examples.text: Do you have your own flat?

translations.de: Hast du eine eigene Wohnung?
translations.fr: Tu as ton propre appartement ?
translations.pt: Tu tens teu próprio apartamento?

examples.text: My boyfriend never leaves the flat without cigarettes.

translations.de: Mein Freund verlässt die Wohnung nie ohne Zigaretten.
translations.fr: Mon petit ami ne quitte jamais l'appartement sans cigarettes.
translations.pt: Meu namorado nunca sai do apartamento sem cigarros.

examples.text: It was believed that the earth was flat.

translations.de: Man glaubte, dass die Erde eine Scheibe wäre.
translations.fr: On croyait que la Terre était plate.
translations.pt: Acreditava-se que a Terra era plana.

examples.text: My bicycle has a flat tire.

translations.de: Mein Fahrrad hat einen Platten.
translations.fr: Mon vélo a un pneu à plat.
translations.pt: Minha bicicleta está com um pneu furado.

more.definition: Having no variations in height.; In a horizontal line or plane; not sloping.; Smooth; having no protrusions, indentations or other surface irregularities, or relatively so.
more.etymology: Old Norse flatrbor. From Middle English flat, a borrowing from Old Norse flatr (compare Norwegian and Swedish flat, Danish flad), from Proto-Germanic *flataz, from Proto-Indo-European *pleth₂- (“flat”); akin to Saterland Frisian flot (“smooth”), German Flöz (“a geological layer”), Ancient Greek πλατύς (platús), Latvian plats, Sanskrit प्रथस् (prathas, “extension”). Doublet of plat and pleyt.

examples.text: You have a flat tyre.

translations.de: Du hast einen Platten.
translations.fr: Tu as un pneu crevé.
translations.pt: Você tem um pneu vazio.

examples.text: Would you like a furnished or an unfurnished flat?

translations.de: Wünschen Sie eine möblierte oder eine nicht möblierte Wohnung?
translations.fr: Souhaitez-vous un appartement meublé ou non meublé ?
translations.pt: Tu gostarias de um apartamento mobilado ou por mobilar?

examples.text: Some people still believe that the world is flat.

translations.de: Manche Menschen glauben noch immer, dass die Erde eine Scheibe sei.
translations.fr: Certaines personnes croient encore que le monde est plat.
translations.pt: Algumas pessoas ainda acreditam que o mundo é plano.

examples.text: People used to think that the earth was flat.

translations.de: Früher glaubten die Menschen, dass die Erde flach sei.
translations.fr: Autrefois, les gens pensaient que la Terre était plate.
translations.pt: As pessoas costumavam pensar que a Terra era plana.

more.definition: So as to be flat.; Completely, firmly, or unequivocally.; Exactly; precisely.
more.etymology: Old Norse flatrbor. From Middle English flat, a borrowing from Old Norse flatr (compare Norwegian and Swedish flat, Danish flad), from Proto-Germanic *flataz, from Proto-Indo-European *pleth₂- (“flat”); akin to Saterland Frisian flot (“smooth”), German Flöz (“a geological layer”), Ancient Greek πλατύς (platús), Latvian plats, Sanskrit प्रथस् (prathas, “extension”). Doublet of plat and pleyt.

examples.text: I don't like this flat, because the bedrooms are too dark.

translations.de: Ich mag diese Wohnung nicht, weil die Schlafzimmer zu dunkel sind.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas cet appartement parce que les chambres à coucher sont trop sombres.
translations.pt: Não gosto deste apartamento, porque os quartos são muito escuros.

examples.text: I had to push my bicycle because I had a flat tire.

translations.de: Ich musste mein Fahrrad schieben, weil ich einen Platten hatte.
translations.fr: J'ai dû pousser mon vélo, car j'avais un pneu à plat.
translations.pt: Tive que empurrar minha bicicleta porque tinha um pneu furado.

examples.text: My flat has a large living room.

translations.de: Meine Wohnung hat ein großes Wohnzimmer.
translations.fr: Mon appartement a une grande salle de séjour.
translations.pt: Meu apartamento tem uma sala de estar grande.

examples.text: They're happy with their new flat.

translations.de: Sie sind mit ihrer neuen Wohnung zufrieden.
translations.fr: Ils sont contents de leur nouvel appartement.
translations.pt: Eles estão felizes com o seu novo apartamento.

more.definition: An area of level ground (sometimes covered with shallow or tidal water).; Level ground in general.; Level horse-racing ground, as contrasted with courses incorporating jumps, or the racing done on such ground.
more.etymology: Old Norse flatrbor. From Middle English flat, a borrowing from Old Norse flatr (compare Norwegian and Swedish flat, Danish flad), from Proto-Germanic *flataz, from Proto-Indo-European *pleth₂- (“flat”); akin to Saterland Frisian flot (“smooth”), German Flöz (“a geological layer”), Ancient Greek πλατύς (platús), Latvian plats, Sanskrit प्रथस् (prathas, “extension”). Doublet of plat and pleyt.

examples.text: He lives in a flat.

translations.de: Er hat eine Wohnung.
translations.fr: Il vit dans un appartement.
translations.pt: Ele mora em apartamento.

examples.text: I got a flat tire.

translations.de: Ich habe einen Platten.
translations.fr: J'ai crevé un pneu.
translations.pt: Estou com um pneu furado.

examples.text: The earth is flat.

translations.de: Die Erde ist eine Scheibe.
translations.fr: La Terre est plate.
translations.pt: A Terra é plana.

examples.text: The joke fell flat.

translations.de: Der Witz war ein Rohrkrepierer.
translations.fr: La blague est tombée à plat.
translations.pt: Ninguém achou graça na piada.

more.definition: To make a flat call; to call without raising.; To become flat or flattened; to sink or fall to an even surface.; To fall from the pitch.
more.etymology: Old Norse flatrbor. From Middle English flat, a borrowing from Old Norse flatr (compare Norwegian and Swedish flat, Danish flad), from Proto-Germanic *flataz, from Proto-Indo-European *pleth₂- (“flat”); akin to Saterland Frisian flot (“smooth”), German Flöz (“a geological layer”), Ancient Greek πλατύς (platús), Latvian plats, Sanskrit प्रथस् (prathas, “extension”). Doublet of plat and pleyt.

examples.text: These flowers bloom in the spring.

translations.de: Diese Blumen blühen im Frühjahr.
translations.fr: Ces fleurs fleurissent au printemps.
translations.pt: Estas flores desabrocham na primavera.

examples.text: Eagles congregate here in the spring.

translations.de: Im Frühling gibt es hier einen Andrang von Adlern.
translations.fr: Les aigles se réunissent ici au printemps.
translations.pt: As águias se reúnem aqui na primavera.

examples.text: Next spring I want to go to Hawaii.

translations.de: Im nächsten Frühling will ich nach Hawaii.
translations.fr: Le printemps suivant, je veux aller à Hawaï.
translations.pt: Na próxima primavera quero ir pro Hawaii.

examples.text: No autumn fruit without spring blossom.

translations.de: Keine Früchte im Herbst ohne Blüten im Frühling.
translations.fr: Point de fruit d'automne sans bourgeon de printemps.
translations.pt: O outono não pode dar frutos se a primavera não produzir flores.

examples.text: Do you like spring or autumn?

translations.de: Magst du lieber den Frühling oder den Herbst?
translations.fr: Aimes-tu le printemps ou l'automne ?
translations.pt: Você gosta da primavera ou do outono?

examples.text: I like spring better than fall.

translations.de: Den Frühling mag ich mehr als den Herbst.
translations.fr: Je préfère le printemps à l'automne.
translations.pt: Gosto mais da primavera do que do outono.

examples.text: My father is retiring next spring.

translations.de: Mein Vater geht im nächsten Frühjahr in den Ruhestand.
translations.fr: Mon père part à la retraite au printemps prochain.
translations.pt: Meu pai se aposenta na próxima primavera.

examples.text: The town is famous for its hot spring.

translations.de: Die Stadt ist berühmt für ihre heißen Quellen.
translations.fr: Cette ville est connue pour sa source chaude.

more.definition: To give (permission or wish).; To give (bestow upon or confer, particularly in answer to prayer or request).; To agree with (someone) on (something); to accept (something) for the sake of argument; to admit to (someone) that (something) is true.

examples.text: Bill was late for school as usual.

more.definition: The action of trying at something.; An assault or attack, especially an assassination attempt.; A substantial but unsuccessful effort (to commit a crime).

The noun is from the 1530s, the sense "an assault on somebody's life, assassination attempt" (French attentat) is from 1580. By surface analysis, at- + tempt.

examples.text: His eyes were shining with joy.

translations.fr: Après le repas, je demandai l'addition.
translations.pt: Depois da refeição eu pedi a conta.

examples.text: Garlic enhances the flavor of meals.

translations.de: Knoblauch verbessert den Geschmack einer Speise.
translations.fr: L'ail renforce la saveur des plats.
translations.pt: O alho realça o sabor das comidas.

examples.text: Take this medicine after each meal.

translations.de: Nehmen Sie das Medikament nach jeder Mahlzeit.
translations.fr: Prends ce médicament après chaque repas.
translations.pt: Tome esse remédio depois de cada refeição.

examples.text: These things constitute a balanced meal.

translations.de: Diese Sachen bilden eine ausgewogene Mahlzeit.
translations.fr: Ces choses constituent un repas équilibré.
translations.pt: Estas coisas constituem uma refeição balanceada.

more.definition: To defile or taint.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *melh₂-der. From Middle English mele, from Old English melu (“meal, flour”), from Proto-West Germanic *melu, from Proto-Germanic *melwą (“meal, flour”), from Proto-Indo-European *melh₂- (“to grind, mill”).

examples.text: His sacrifice will not be in vain.

translations.de: Sein Opfer wird nicht vergebens sein.
translations.fr: Son sacrifice ne restera pas vain.
translations.pt: O sacrifício dele não será em vão.

examples.text: A good sacrifice is a sacrifice that is not.

translations.de: Ein gutes Opfer ist ein Opfer, das es nicht ist.
translations.fr: Un bon sacrifice est un sacrifice qui n'en est pas un.
translations.pt: Um bom sacrifício é um sacrifício que não o é.

examples.text: How can I sacrifice myself for something I don't believe in?

translations.de: Wie kann ich mich für etwas opfern, woran ich nicht glaube?
translations.fr: Comment puis-je me sacrifier pour quelque-chose en lequel je ne crois pas ?
translations.pt: Como eu posso me sacrificar por algo que eu não acredito?

examples.text: The priest can sacrifice on the altar.

translations.de: Der Priester kann auf dem Altar opfern.
translations.fr: Le prêtre peut sacrifier sur l'autel.
translations.pt: O sacerdote pode sacrificar no altar.

more.definition: Originally, the killing (and often burning) of a human being or an animal as an offering to a deity; later, also the offering of an object to a deity.; A human being or an animal, or a physical object or immaterial thing (see etymology 1 sense 1.3), offered to a deity.; The offering of devotion, penitence, prayer, thanksgiving, etc., to a deity.
more.etymology: Latin sacerder. Latin -iusnom. Latin sacrificiumlbor. Old French sacrifisebor. From Middle English sacrifice (“act of offering a life or object to a deity; the life or object so offered”), from Anglo-Norman sacrefiz, and Old French sacrifice, sacrifise (modern French sacrifice), from Latin sacrificium (“something offered to a deity, sacrifice”), from sacrum (“sacrifice, sacrificial rite”) + faciō (“to do, to make”) …

examples.text: The soldier sacrificed himself to save his friend's life.

translations.de: Der Soldat opferte sich, um seinem Freunde das Leben zu retten.
translations.fr: Le soldat s'est sacrifié pour sauver la vie de son ami.
translations.pt: O soldado se sacrificou para salvar a vida do amigo dele.

examples.text: A true sacrifice is a false sacrifice.

translations.de: Ein echtes Opfer ist ein falsches Opfer.
translations.fr: Un vrai sacrifice est un faux sacrifice.
translations.pt: Um verdadeiro sacrifício é um falso sacrifício.

examples.text: His sacrifice will not be in vain.

translations.fr: Son sacrifice ne restera pas vain.

examples.text: A good sacrifice is a sacrifice that is not.

translations.de: Ein gutes Opfer ist ein Opfer, das es nicht ist.
translations.fr: Un bon sacrifice est un sacrifice qui n'en est pas un.
translations.pt: Um bom sacrifício é um sacrifício que não o é.

more.definition: To offer (a human being or an animal, or an object) to a deity.; To destroy or kill (a human being or an animal); specifically (sciences), to kill (an animal) for a scientific experiment or test.; To destroy or surrender (something) for the sake of something else regarded as more urgent or valuable.
more.etymology: From Middle English sacrificen (“to offer a sacrifice to a deity”), from sacrifice (see etymology 1) + -en (suffix forming infinitives of verbs).

examples.text: Tom told me that he was lonely.

translations.de: Tom hat mir erzählt, dass er einsam sei.
translations.fr: Tom m'a dit qu'il se sentait seul.
translations.pt: Tom me disse que ele estava solitário.

examples.text: I feel very lonely these days.

translations.de: Dieser Tage fühle ich mich sehr einsam.
translations.fr: Je me sens très seul ces jours-ci.
translations.pt: Venho me sentindo muito solitário nesses dias.

examples.text: She lived a lonely life.

translations.de: Sie führte ein einsames Leben.
translations.fr: Elle a vécu une vie solitaire.
translations.pt: Ela vivia uma vida solitária.

examples.text: I feel so lonely.

translations.de: Ich fühle mich so einsam.
translations.fr: Je me sens si seul.
translations.pt: Sinto-me tão só.

more.definition: Unhappy due to feeling isolated from contact with other people.; Unfrequented by people; desolate.; Without companions; solitary.
more.etymology: From lone + -ly, or from an apheretic shortening of alonely. See lone.

examples.text: Fat people are harder to kidnap.

translations.de: Dicke sind schwerer zu entführen.

examples.text: The boogeyman kidnaps naughty children.

translations.fr: Le croque-mitaine enlève les vilains enfants.

examples.text: Tom was the one who tried to kidnap Mary.

translations.de: Es war Tom, der versucht hat, Mary zu entführen.

examples.text: Tom didn't kidnap Mary.

translations.pt: Tom não sequestrou Mary.

more.definition: The crime, or an instance, of kidnapping.
more.etymology: From kid + nap (“to nab; to grab”). Originally Thieves' cant, referring to the practice of stealing children and shipping them to colonies or plantations as laborers. First attested c. 1680.

examples.text: The mayor's daughter has been kidnapped.

translations.de: Die Tochter des Bürgermeisters wurde entführt.
translations.fr: La fille du maire a été enlevée.
translations.pt: A filha do prefeito foi sequestrada.

examples.text: Tom's daughter has been kidnapped.

translations.de: Toms Tochter wurde entführt.
translations.fr: La fille de Tom a été kidnappée.
translations.pt: A filha de Tom foi sequestrada.

examples.text: The king's son was kidnapped.

translations.de: Der Sohn des Königs wurde entführt.
translations.fr: Le Prince a été enlevé.
translations.pt: O filho do rei foi sequestrado.

examples.text: I find it hard to believe that Tom was involved in the kidnapping.

translations.de: Es fällt mir schwer zu glauben, dass Tom an der Entführung beteiligt war.
translations.fr: J'ai du mal à croire que Tom soit impliqué dans l'enlèvement.
translations.pt: Eu acho difícil acreditar que Tom esteve envolvido no sequestro.

more.definition: To seize or detain (a person) unlawfully and transport or conceal them, sometimes for ransom.
more.etymology: From kid + nap (“to nab; to grab”). Originally Thieves' cant, referring to the practice of stealing children and shipping them to colonies or plantations as laborers. First attested c. 1680.

translations.de: Ich würde gerne meine vorhergehende Erklärung widerrufen.

examples.text: Not every untrue statement is a lie.

translations.de: Nicht jede unwahre Aussage ist eine Lüge.
translations.fr: Toute affirmation fausse n'est pas un mensonge.
