examples.text: He kissed her passionately on the lips.

translations.de: Er küsste sie leidenschaftlich auf den Mund.
translations.fr: Il l'embrassa passionnément sur la bouche.
translations.pt: Ele a beijou apaixonadamente nos lábios.

examples.text: Don't worry. My lips are sealed.

translations.de: Keine Sorge! Meine Lippen sind versiegelt.
translations.fr: Ne t'en fais pas, je suis muet comme une tombe.
translations.pt: Não se preocupe, eu serei um túmulo.

examples.text: You've got something on your lip.

translations.de: Du hast etwas auf deiner Lippe.
translations.fr: Tu as quelque chose sur la lèvre.
translations.pt: Você tem algo no seu lábio.

examples.text: The words escaped my lips.

translations.de: Die Worte sind mir rausgerutscht.
translations.fr: Les mots m'ont échappé des lèvres.
translations.pt: As palavras escaparam de meus lábios.

more.definition: Either of the two fleshy protrusions around the opening of the mouth.; A part of the body that resembles a lip, such as the edge of a wound or the labia.; The projecting rim of an open container or a bell, etc.; a short open spout.
more.etymology: From Middle English lippe, from Old English lippa, lippe (“lip”), from Proto-West Germanic *lippjō (“lip”), from Proto-Germanic *lepô, from Proto-Indo-European *leb- (“to hang loosely, droop, sag”).

examples.text: Your lips are like roses.

translations.de: Deine Lippen sind wie Rosen.
translations.fr: Tes lèvres sont comme des roses.
translations.pt: Seus lábios são como rosas.

examples.text: You have beautiful lips.

translations.de: Sie haben schöne Lippen.
translations.fr: Vous avez de très belles lèvres.
translations.pt: Você tem lábios bonitos.

examples.text: His lips touched hers.

translations.de: Seine Lippen berührten die ihrigen.
translations.fr: Ses lèvres ont touché les siennes.
translations.pt: Seus lábios tocaram os dela.

examples.text: She licked her lips.

translations.de: Sie leckte sich die Lippen.
translations.fr: Elle se lécha les lèvres.
translations.pt: Ela lambeu os lábios.

more.definition: To touch or grasp with the lips; to kiss; to lap the lips against (something).; To touch lightly.; To wash against a surface, lap.
more.etymology: From Middle English lippe, from Old English lippa, lippe (“lip”), from Proto-West Germanic *lippjō (“lip”), from Proto-Germanic *lepô, from Proto-Indo-European *leb- (“to hang loosely, droop, sag”).

examples.text: I'm your king and you're my queen.

translations.de: Ich bin dein König und du bist meine Königin.
translations.fr: Je suis ton roi et tu es ma reine.
translations.pt: Eu sou seu rei e você é minha rainha.

examples.text: In chess, the bishop is closer to the queen.

translations.de: Im Schach ist der Läufer näher bei der Dame.
translations.fr: Aux échecs, le fou est plus proche de la dame.
translations.pt: No xadrez, o bispo fica bem próximo da dama.

examples.text: When was Queen Victoria born?

translations.de: Wann wurde Königin Victoria geboren?
translations.fr: Quand la Reine Victoria est-elle née ?
translations.pt: Quando é que a Rainha Victória nasceu?

examples.text: In each beehive there can only be one queen.

translations.de: In jedem Bienenstock kann es nur eine Bienenkönigin geben.
translations.fr: Il ne peut y avoir qu'une seule reine par ruche.
translations.pt: Em cada colmeia só pode haver uma única rainha.

more.definition: The wife, consort, or widow of a king.; A female monarch.; The Virgin Mary (especially in formulations such as Queen of Heaven, Queen of Glory).
more.etymology: From Middle English quene, queen, cwen, from Old English cwēn (“queen”), from Proto-West Germanic *kwāni, from Proto-Germanic *kwēniz (“wife, woman”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷénh₂s (“woman”).

examples.text: The queen is in her castle.

translations.de: Die Königin ist in ihrem Schloss.
translations.fr: La reine est dans son château.
translations.pt: A rainha está em seu castelo.

examples.text: I captured Tom's queen with my knight.

translations.de: Ich habe Toms Dame mit meinem Springer geschlagen.
translations.fr: J'ai capturé la dame de Tom avec mon cavalier.
translations.pt: Capturei a dama de Tom com meu cavalo.

examples.text: Tom treated Mary like a queen.

translations.de: Tom behandelte Maria wie eine Königin.
translations.fr: Tom a traité Mary comme une reine.
translations.pt: Tom tratava Maria como uma rainha.

examples.text: The king and queen are coming.

translations.de: Der König und die Königin kommen.
translations.fr: Le roi et la reine arrivent.
translations.pt: O rei e a rainha estão vindo.

more.definition: To make a queen or (figuratively) to give the status of a queen.; To promote a pawn to a queen.; To be the queen bee of a colony.
more.etymology: From Middle English quene, queen, cwen, from Old English cwēn (“queen”), from Proto-West Germanic *kwāni, from Proto-Germanic *kwēniz (“wife, woman”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷénh₂s (“woman”).

examples.text: He believes that there is a spy among us.

translations.de: Er glaubt, es gibt einen Spion unter uns.
translations.fr: Il pense qu'il y a un espion parmi nous.
translations.pt: Ele acha que há um espião entre nós.

examples.text: Tom is a spy.

translations.de: Tom ist ein Spion.
translations.fr: Tom est un espion.
translations.pt: O Tom é espião.

examples.text: She is suspected of being a spy.

translations.de: Sie wird verdächtigt, eine Spionin zu sein.
translations.fr: On la suspecte d'être une espionne.
translations.pt: Ela é suspeita de ser uma espiã.

examples.text: She's here to spy on us.

translations.de: Sie ist hier, um uns auszuspionieren.
translations.fr: Elle est ici pour nous espionner.
translations.pt: Ela está aqui para nos espionar.

more.definition: A person who secretly watches and examines the actions of other individuals or organizations and gathers information on them (usually to gain an advantage).; A defensive player assigned to cover an offensive backfield player man-to-man when they are expected to engage in a running play, but the offensive player does not run with the ball immediately.
more.etymology: From Middle English spien, aphetic variant of earlier espien (“to espy”), from Old French espier (“to spy”), from Frankish *spehōn (“to spy”), from Proto-Germanic *spehōną (“to see, look”), from Proto-Indo-European *speḱ- (“to look”). Akin to German spähen (“to spy”), Dutch spieden (“to spy”).

examples.text: She's here to spy on us.

translations.de: Sie ist hier, um uns auszuspionieren.
translations.fr: Elle est ici pour nous espionner.
translations.pt: Ela está aqui para nos espionar.

examples.text: He's here to spy on us.

translations.de: Er ist hier, um uns zu bespitzeln.
translations.fr: Il est ici pour nous espionner.
translations.pt: Ele está aqui para nos espionar.

examples.text: You aren't a spy, are you?

translations.de: Du bist kein Spion, oder?
translations.fr: Tu n'es pas un espion, si ?
translations.pt: Você não é um espião, não é?

examples.text: They're spies.

translations.de: Das sind Spione.
translations.fr: Ce sont des espions.
translations.pt: Elas são espiãs.

more.definition: To act as a spy.; To spot; to catch sight of; to espy.; To search narrowly; to scrutinize.
more.etymology: From Middle English spien, aphetic variant of earlier espien (“to espy”), from Old French espier (“to spy”), from Frankish *spehōn (“to spy”), from Proto-Germanic *spehōną (“to see, look”), from Proto-Indo-European *speḱ- (“to look”). Akin to German spähen (“to spy”), Dutch spieden (“to spy”).

examples.text: Have you read any interesting books lately?

translations.de: Haben Sie in der letzten Zeit interessante Bücher gelesen?
translations.fr: Avez-vous lu des livres intéressants dernièrement ?
translations.pt: Leu algum livro interessante recentemente?

examples.text: I've been very busy lately.

translations.de: In letzter Zeit bin ich sehr beschäftigt.
translations.fr: J'ai été très occupé ces derniers temps.
translations.pt: Tenho estado muito ocupado ultimamente.

examples.text: Have you seen any movies lately?

translations.de: Hast du in letzter Zeit irgendwelche Filme gesehen?
translations.fr: Avez-vous vu des films récemment ?
translations.pt: Tens visto algum filme ultimamente?

examples.text: By the way, have you seen him lately?

translations.de: Ach ja, hast du ihn in letzter Zeit mal gesehen?
translations.fr: À ce propos, l'as-tu vu dernièrement ?
translations.pt: A propósito, o tens visto ultimamente?

more.definition: Recently; not long ago; of late; not long since.; In a late manner; after-the-fact.; Formerly.
more.etymology: From Middle English lately, latly, equivalent to late + -ly. Compare Old English lætlīċe (“slowly, tardily”), Middle Low German lātlîk (“careless, slack, sloppy”).

examples.text: The workers took pride in their work.

translations.de: Die Arbeiter waren stolz auf ihre Arbeit.
translations.fr: Les ouvriers étaient fiers de leur travail.
translations.pt: Os trabalhadores se orgulhavam de seu trabalho.

examples.text: Tom is a hard worker.

translations.de: Tom ist sehr fleißig.
translations.fr: Tom est très travailleur.
translations.pt: Tom é um trabalhador dedicado.

examples.text: The workers are wiring the new house.

translations.de: Die Arbeiter verdrahten das neue Haus.
translations.fr: Les ouvriers mettent en place le réseau électrique de la nouvelle maison.
translations.pt: Os trabalhadores estão fazendo a fiação da casa nova.

examples.text: Millions of workers lost their jobs.

translations.de: Millionen von Arbeitern verloren ihre Stellen.
translations.fr: Des millions de travailleurs perdirent leurs emplois.
translations.pt: Milhões de trabalhadores perderam seus empregos.

more.definition: One who works: a person who performs labor for a living; traditionally, especially, manual labor.; A nonreproductive social insect, such as ant, bee, termite, or wasp.; A thread performing one instance of a particular task within a program.
more.etymology: Latin -āriusnom. Latin -āriusbor. Inherited from Middle English worchere, werkere, equivalent to work + -er. Displaced the older term wright, from Old English wyrhta.

examples.text: There is a limit to everything.

translations.de: Alles hat seine Grenzen.
translations.fr: Il y a une limite à toutes choses.
translations.pt: Há limite para tudo.

examples.text: Don't exceed the speed limit.

translations.de: Überschreite nicht die Höchstgeschwindigkeit!
translations.fr: Ne dépasse pas la limite de vitesse.
translations.pt: Não ultrapasse o limite de velocidade.

examples.text: There's no speed limit.

translations.de: Es gibt keine Geschwindigkeitsbegrenzung.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas de limite de vitesse.
translations.pt: Não há limite de velocidade.

examples.text: Don't go over the speed limit.

translations.de: Nicht die Höchstgeschwindigkeit überschreiten!
translations.fr: Ne dépasse pas la limite de vitesse.

more.definition: Being a fixed limit game.
more.etymology: From Middle English limit, from Old French limit, from oblique stem of Latin līmes, līmit- (“a cross-path or balk between fields, hence a boundary, boundary line or wall, any path or road, border, limit”). Displaced native Old English ġemǣre. Doublet of limes.

examples.text: Our love has no limits.

translations.de: Unsere Liebe hat keine Grenzen.
translations.fr: Notre amour n'a pas de limites.
translations.pt: Nosso amor não tem limites.

examples.text: Human cruelty has no limits.

translations.de: Die Grausamkeit des Menschen ist grenzenlos.
translations.fr: La cruauté humaine est sans limites.
translations.pt: A crueldade humana não tem limites.

examples.text: There are no limits.

translations.de: Es gibt keine Grenzen.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas de limite.
translations.pt: Não há limites.

examples.text: Everything has its limits.

translations.de: Alles hat eine Grenze.
translations.fr: Toute chose a ses limites.
translations.pt: Há limite para tudo.

more.definition: A restriction; a bound beyond which one may not go or proceed.; A value to which a sequence converges. Equivalently, the common value of the upper limit and the lower limit of a sequence: if the upper and lower limits are different, then the sequence has no limit (i.e., does not converge).; Any of several abstractions of this concept of limit.
more.etymology: From Middle English limit, from Old French limit, from oblique stem of Latin līmes, līmit- (“a cross-path or balk between fields, hence a boundary, boundary line or wall, any path or road, border, limit”). Displaced native Old English ġemǣre. Doublet of limes.

examples.text: I want to test my limits.

translations.de: Ich will meine Grenzen austesten.
translations.fr: Je veux tester mes limites.
translations.pt: Quero testar meus limites.

examples.text: There is a limit to everything.

translations.de: Alles hat seine Grenzen.
translations.fr: Il y a une limite à toutes choses.
translations.pt: Há limite para tudo.

examples.text: Our inventory is very limited.

translations.de: Wir haben nur sehr begrenzte Lagerbestände.
translations.fr: Nous avons un stock très limité.
translations.pt: Nosso estoque é muito limitado.

examples.text: She wanted to test her limits.

translations.de: Sie wollte ihre Grenzen austesten.
translations.fr: Elle voulait tester ses limites.
translations.pt: Ela queria testar os seus limites.

more.definition: To restrict; to circumscribe; not to allow to go beyond a certain bound, to set boundaries.; To have a limit in a particular set.
more.etymology: From Middle English limiten, from Old French limiter, from Latin līmitō (“to bound, limit, fix, determine”), from līmes; see noun.

examples.text: Tom wants to become a priest.

translations.de: Tom will Priester werden.
translations.fr: Tom veut devenir prêtre.
translations.pt: Tom quer ser padre.

examples.text: Before, the priests used to say mass in Latin.

translations.de: Früher haben die Priester die Messe auf Latein gehalten.
translations.fr: Avant, les prêtres disaient la messe en latin.
translations.pt: Antes, os sacerdotes celebravam a missa em Latim.

examples.text: My brother has become a priest.

translations.de: Mein Bruder wurde Priester.
translations.fr: Mon frère est devenu prêtre.
translations.pt: Meu irmão virou padre.

examples.text: Tom is a priest.

translations.de: Tom ist Priester.
translations.fr: Tom est un prêtre.
translations.pt: Tom é um padre.

translations.fr: Vous allez avoir du mal.
translations.pt: Você vai passar um sufoco.

examples.text: I have a rough idea where it is.

translations.de: Ich habe eine ungefähre Ahnung, wo es ist.
translations.fr: J'ai une vague idée où ça se situe.
translations.pt: Tenho uma ligeira ideia de onde está.

examples.text: The sea is rough.

translations.de: Die See ist rau.
translations.fr: La mer est agitée.
translations.pt: O mar está agitado.

examples.text: Tom's face feels rough because he needs to shave.

translations.de: Toms Gesicht fühlt sich rau an, weil er sich rasieren muss.
translations.fr: Le visage de Tom est rugueux car il a besoin de se raser.
translations.pt: O rosto de Tom está áspero porque ele precisa se barbear.

more.definition: To create in an approximate form.; To break the rules by being excessively violent.; To commit the offense of roughing, i.e. to punch another player.
more.etymology: From Middle English rough, roughe, roȝe, row, rou, ru, ruȝ, ruh, from Old English rūg, rūh, from Proto-Germanic *rūhaz. Cognate with Scots ruch, rouch (“rough”), Saterland Frisian ruuch, rouch (“rough”), West Frisian rûch (“rough”), Low German ruuch (“rough”), Dutch ruig (“rough”), German rau(h) (“rough”), Danish ru (“uneven on the surface, "rough", "rugged"”).

examples.text: What is the location of the country?

translations.de: Wo befindet sich das Land?
translations.fr: Quelle est la localisation du pays ?
translations.pt: Qual é a localização do país?

examples.text: This store is in a prime location.

translations.de: Dieses Geschäft hat eine erstklassige Lage.
translations.fr: Ce magasin est bien situé.

examples.text: This room's location is great.

translations.fr: C'est une pièce très bien exposée.
translations.pt: A localização deste quarto é ótima.

examples.text: This location has the best view in the city.

translations.de: Diese Lage hat die schönste Aussicht in der Stadt.
translations.fr: Cette position a la meilleure vue de la ville.

more.definition: A particular point or place in physical space.; An act of locating.; An apartheid-era urban area populated by non-white people; a township.
more.etymology: Borrowed from Latin locatio, locationis (“a placing”), from locare (“to place, put, set, let”), from locus (“a place”). Equivalent to locate + -ion.

examples.text: In older people, wounds take a long time to heal.

translations.de: Bei älteren Menschen brauchen Verletzungen länger um zu heilen.
translations.fr: Chez les personnes âgées, les plaies mettent longtemps à cicatriser.
translations.pt: Nas maiores, as feridas saram após muito tempo.

examples.text: Time heals all wounds.

translations.de: Die Zeit heilt alle Wunden.
translations.fr: Le temps guérit tout.
translations.pt: O tempo cura todas as feridas.

examples.text: This looks like a gunshot wound.

translations.de: Das hier sieht wie eine Schussverletzung aus.
translations.fr: On dirait une blessure par balle.
translations.pt: Isto parece um ferimento a bala.

examples.text: The wound is not yet healed.

translations.de: Die Wunde ist noch nicht verheilt.
translations.fr: La blessure n'est pas encore guérie.
translations.pt: A ferida ainda não foi curada.

more.definition: An injury, such as a cut, stab, or tear, to a (usually external) part of the body.; An injury to a person by which the skin is divided or its continuity broken.; A hurt to a person's feelings, reputation, prospects, etc.
more.etymology: Noun from Middle English wund, from Old English wund, from Proto-West Germanic *wundu, from Proto-Germanic *wundō (“wound”), from Proto-Indo-European *wen- (“to strive, toil, win”).

examples.text: Alexander was wounded by an arrow.

translations.de: Alexander wurde durch einen Pfeil verwundet.
translations.fr: Alexandre a été blessé par une flèche.
translations.pt: Alexandre foi ferido por uma flecha.

examples.text: He was wounded in the war.

translations.de: Er wurde im Krieg verwundet.
translations.fr: Il a été blessé à la guerre.
translations.pt: Ele foi ferido na guerra.

examples.text: He was mortally wounded.

translations.de: Er wurde tödlich verwundet.
translations.fr: Il a été mortellement blessé.
translations.pt: Ele foi fatalmente ferido.

examples.text: Tom was wounded.

translations.de: Tom wurde verletzt.
translations.fr: Tom était blessé.
translations.pt: Tom foi ferido.

more.definition: To hurt or injure (someone) by cutting, piercing, or tearing the skin.; To hurt (a person's feelings).
more.etymology: Noun from Middle English wund, from Old English wund, from Proto-West Germanic *wundu, from Proto-Germanic *wundō (“wound”), from Proto-Indo-European *wen- (“to strive, toil, win”).

examples.text: I heard they found an alien artifact on the moon.

translations.de: Ich habe gehört, man hätte ein außerirdisches Artefakt auf dem Mond gefunden.
translations.fr: J'ai entendu dire qu'ils avaient trouvé un objet extraterrestre sur la lune.
translations.pt: Ouvi dizer que haviam encontrado um objeto extraterrestre na Lua.

examples.text: This gold Rolex is an expensive watch alien to my lifestyle.

translations.de: Diese goldene Rolex ist eine teure Armbanduhr, die nicht zu meinem Lebensstil passt.
translations.fr: Cette Rolex en or est une montre très coûteuse qui n'a rien à voir avec mon style de vie.
translations.pt: Um relógio Rolex de ouro como esse não corresponde ao meu estilo de vida.

examples.text: Their ideas seem totally alien to us.

translations.de: Ihre Ideen erscheinen uns vollkommen fremdartig.
translations.fr: Leurs idées nous paraissent complètement étrangères.

examples.text: Such actions are alien to our beliefs.

translations.de: Solche Taten sind unseren Überzeugungen fremd.
translations.fr: De telles actions sont contraires à nos croyances.

more.definition: Not belonging to the same country, land, or government, or to the citizens or subjects thereof; foreign.; Very unfamiliar, strange, or removed.; Pertaining to extraterrestrial life; typical of an extraterrestrial creature.
more.etymology: From Middle English alien, a borrowing from Old French alien, aliene, from Latin aliēnus (“belonging to someone else”, later “exotic, foreign”), from Latin alius (“other”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂élyos. Related to English else.

examples.text: I was abducted by aliens.

translations.de: Ich wurde von Außerirdischen entführt.
translations.fr: J'ai été kidnappé par des extra-terrestres.
translations.pt: Fui abduzido por alienígenas.

examples.text: This gold Rolex is an expensive watch alien to my lifestyle.

translations.pt: Um relógio Rolex de ouro como esse não corresponde ao meu estilo de vida.

examples.text: Tom believes that the government wants to hide the truth about aliens.

translations.de: Tom glaubt, dass die Regierung versucht, die Wahrheit über Außerirdische geheimzuhalten.
translations.fr: Tom croit que le gouvernement cache la vérité au sujet des extraterrestres.
translations.pt: Tom acredita que o governo quer esconder a verdade sobre os alienígenas.

examples.text: These aliens want to enslave humanity.

translations.de: Diese Außerirdischen wollen die Menschheit versklaven.
translations.fr: Ces extraterrestres veulent asservir l'humanité.
translations.pt: Estes alienígenas querem escravizar a humanidade.

more.definition: A person, animal, plant, or other thing which is from outside the family, group, organization, or territory under consideration.; A citizen or national of another sovereign state.; A mischievous or suspicious foreigner.
more.etymology: From Middle English alien, a borrowing from Old French alien, aliene, from Latin aliēnus (“belonging to someone else”, later “exotic, foreign”), from Latin alius (“other”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂élyos. Related to English else.

examples.text: I dreamed I had been abducted by aliens.

translations.de: Ich träumte, ich wäre von Außerirdischen entführt worden.
translations.fr: J'ai rêvé que j'avais été enlevé par des extraterrestres.

examples.text: He thinks that aliens exist.

translations.de: Er glaubt, dass es Außerirdische gibt.
translations.fr: Il pense que les extraterrestres existent.
translations.pt: Ele acha que existem alienígenas.

more.definition: To estrange; to alienate.; To transfer the ownership of something.
more.etymology: From Middle English alien, a borrowing from Old French alien, aliene, from Latin aliēnus (“belonging to someone else”, later “exotic, foreign”), from Latin alius (“other”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂élyos. Related to English else.

examples.text: We should cancel the hike.

translations.de: Wir sollten die Wanderung streichen.
translations.fr: Nous devrions annuler la randonnée.
translations.pt: Devemos cancelar a caminhada.

examples.text: There is nothing to cancel.

translations.de: Da gibt es nichts zu stornieren.
translations.fr: Il n'y a rien à annuler.
translations.pt: Não há nada para cancelar.

examples.text: Should I cancel the call?

translations.de: Sollte ich den Anruf abbrechen?
translations.fr: Dois-je annuler l'appel ?
translations.pt: Devo cancelar a chamada?

examples.text: I'll cancel.

translations.de: Ich werde absagen.
translations.fr: J'annulerai.
translations.pt: Cancelarei.

more.definition: A cancellation.; A control message posted to Usenet that serves to cancel a previously posted message.; The suppression on striking out of matter in type, or of a printed page or pages.
more.etymology: From Middle English cancellen, from Anglo-Norman canceler (“to cross out with lines”) (modern French chanceler (“to stagger, sway”)), from Old French canceler, from Latin cancellō (“to make resemble a lattice”), from cancellus (“a railing or lattice”), diminutive of cancer (“a lattice”).

examples.text: We need to cancel the meeting.

translations.de: Wir müssen das Treffen absagen.
translations.fr: Nous devons annuler le rendez-vous.
translations.pt: Nós precisamos cancelar o encontro.

examples.text: He cancelled the meeting at the last minute.

translations.de: Er hat die Sitzung im letzten Augenblick abgesagt.
translations.fr: Il a annulé la réunion à la dernière minute.
translations.pt: Ele cancelou a reunião no último minuto.

examples.text: Today's meeting has been canceled.

translations.de: Das heutige Treffen wurde abgesagt.
translations.fr: La réunion d'aujourd'hui a été annulée.
translations.pt: A reunião de hoje foi cancelada.

examples.text: If it rains tomorrow, the excursion will be canceled.

translations.de: Wenn es morgen regnet, wird der Ausflug abgesagt werden.
translations.fr: S'il pleut demain, l'excursion sera annulée.
translations.pt: Se chover amanhã, a excursão será cancelada.

more.definition: To cross out something with lines etc.; To invalidate or annul something.; To mark something (such as a used postage stamp) so that it cannot be reused.
more.etymology: From Middle English cancellen, from Anglo-Norman canceler (“to cross out with lines”) (modern French chanceler (“to stagger, sway”)), from Old French canceler, from Latin cancellō (“to make resemble a lattice”), from cancellus (“a railing or lattice”), diminutive of cancer (“a lattice”).

examples.text: What is the exchange rate?

translations.de: Wie ist der Wechselkurs?
translations.fr: Quel est le taux de change ?
translations.pt: Qual é a taxa de câmbio?

examples.text: Brazil has one of the highest crime rates in the world.

translations.de: Brasilien hat eine der höchsten Kriminalitätsraten der Welt.
translations.fr: Le Brésil a l'un des taux de criminalité les plus élevés au monde.
translations.pt: O Brasil tem uma das maiores taxas de criminalidade do mundo.

examples.text: He is sure to pass the exam if he studies at this rate.

translations.de: Er wird sicher die Prüfung bestehen, wenn er in diesem Tempo lernt.
translations.fr: Il est certain de réussir l'examen s'il étudie à ce rythme.
translations.pt: Ele certamente vai passar no exame se estudar com essa regularidade.

more.etymology: From Middle English rate, from Old French rate, from Medieval Latin rata, from Latin prō ratā parte (“according to a fixed part”), from ratus (“fixed”), from rērī (“think, deem, judge, estimate", originally "reckon, calculate”).

examples.text: At any rate, I did my duty.

translations.de: Auf jeden Fall habe ich meine Pflicht getan.
translations.fr: Quoi qu'il en soit, j'ai fait mon devoir.
translations.pt: De qualquer jeito eu fiz o meu dever.

more.definition: To assign or be assigned a particular rank or level.; To evaluate or estimate the value of.; To consider or regard.
more.etymology: From Middle English rate, from Old French rate, from Medieval Latin rata, from Latin prō ratā parte (“according to a fixed part”), from ratus (“fixed”), from rērī (“think, deem, judge, estimate", originally "reckon, calculate”).

examples.text: Life is a fatal sexually transmitted disease.

translations.de: Das Leben ist eine tödliche, sexuell übertragbare Krankheit.
translations.fr: La vie est une maladie mortelle sexuellement transmissible.
translations.pt: A vida é uma doença fatal sexualmente transmissível.

examples.text: Medicine is the study of diseases.

translations.de: Medizin ist die Lehre von Krankheiten.
translations.fr: La médecine est l'étude des maladies.
translations.pt: A medicina é o estudo das doenças.

examples.text: My baby has a hereditary disease.

translations.de: Mein Baby hat eine Erbkrankheit.
translations.fr: Mon bébé souffre d'une maladie héréditaire.
translations.pt: Meu bebê tem uma doença hereditária.

examples.text: Racism is the most dangerous disease of our time.

translations.de: Rassismus ist die gefährlichste Krankheit unserer Zeit.
translations.fr: Le racisme est la maladie la plus dangereuse de notre époque.
translations.pt: O racismo é a doença mais perigosa do nosso tempo.

more.definition: An abnormal condition of a human, animal or plant that causes discomfort or dysfunction; distinct from injury insofar as the latter is usually instantaneously acquired.; Any abnormal or harmful condition, as of society, people's attitudes, way of living etc.; A lack of ease; uneasiness; trouble; vexation; disquiet.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *trísinflu. Proto-Indo-European *(H)yéh₁kt ~ *(H)ih₁kéntder. Proto-Indo-European *-éh₁tiinflu. Anglo-Norman desesebor. From Middle English disese, from Anglo-Norman desese, disaise, from Old French desaise, from des- + aise.

examples.text: It's a disease that can't be prevented.

translations.de: Es ist eine Erkrankung, der man nicht vorbeugen kann.
translations.fr: On ne peut pas prévenir cette maladie.
translations.pt: É uma doença da qual não há como se prevenir.

examples.text: Vaccinations help prevent childhood diseases.

translations.de: Impfungen tragen zur Verhütung von Kinderkrankheiten bei.
translations.fr: Les vaccinations aident à protéger contre les maladies infantiles.
translations.pt: A vacinação ajuda a prevenir as doenças infantis.

examples.text: Louis Pasteur discovered that germs cause most infectious diseases.

translations.de: Louis Pasteur hat entdeckt, dass die meisten ansteckenden Krankheiten von Keimen verursacht werden.
translations.fr: Louis Pasteur découvrit que les bactéries causent la plupart des maladies infectieuses.
translations.pt: Louis Pasteur descobriu que as bactérias causam a maioria das doenças infecciosas.

examples.text: Mumps is an infectious disease.

translations.de: Mumps ist eine ansteckende Krankheit.
translations.fr: Les oreillons sont une maladie infectieuse.
translations.pt: A caxumba é uma doença infecciosa.

more.definition: To infect with a disease.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *trísinflu. Proto-Indo-European *(H)yéh₁kt ~ *(H)ih₁kéntder. Proto-Indo-European *-éh₁tiinflu. Anglo-Norman desesebor. From Middle English disese, from Anglo-Norman desese, disaise, from Old French desaise, from des- + aise.

examples.text: This cheese is made from sheep's milk.

translations.de: Dieser Käse wird aus Schafsmilch hergestellt.
translations.fr: Ce fromage est fait avec du lait de brebis.

more.definition: Said while being photographed, to give the impression of smiling.
more.etymology: Perhaps an alteration of cheers.

examples.text: I don't like goat cheese.

translations.de: Ich mag keinen Ziegenkäse.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas le fromage de chèvre.
translations.pt: Não gosto de queijo de cabra.

examples.text: This cheese is made from goat's milk.

translations.de: Dieser Käse wird aus Ziegenmilch gemacht.
translations.fr: Ce fromage est préparé à base de lait de chèvre.
translations.pt: Este queijo é feito de leite de cabra.

examples.text: Everybody knows the moon is made of cheese.

translations.de: Jeder weiß, dass der Mond aus Käse ist.
translations.fr: Tout le monde sait que la lune est faite de fromage.
translations.pt: Todo mundo sabe que a Lua é feita de queijo.

examples.text: I bought some cheese and milk.

translations.de: Ich habe Käse und ein bisschen Milch gekauft.
translations.fr: J'ai acheté du fromage et du lait.
translations.pt: Comprei um pouco de queijo e de leite.

Cognate with Saterland Frisian Síes (“cheese”), West Frisian tsiis (“cheese”), Dutch kaas (“cheese”), German Low German Kees (“cheese”), German Käse (“cheese”).

examples.text: That cheese is made from sheep's milk.

examples.text: Several mice are eating cheese.

translations.de: Mehrere Mäuse fressen Käse.

translations.pt: Vários ratos estão comendo queijo.

examples.text: I can't eat cheese.

translations.de: Ich kann Käse nicht essen.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas manger de fromage.
translations.pt: Eu não posso comer queijo.

examples.text: I don't like cheese.

translations.de: Ich mag keinen Käse.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas le fromage.
translations.pt: Eu não gosto de queijo.

more.definition: To prepare curds for making cheese.; To make holes in a pattern of circuitry to decrease pattern density.; To smile excessively, as for a camera.
more.etymology: Latin cāseusbor. From Middle English chese, from Anglian Old English ċēse, from Proto-West Germanic *kāsī, borrowed from Latin cāseus. Doublet of queso. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Síes (“cheese”), West Frisian tsiis (“cheese”), Dutch kaas (“cheese”), German Low German Kees (“cheese”), German Käse (“cheese”).

examples.text: My father insisted that we should go.

translations.de: Mein Vater bestand darauf, dass wir gehen sollten.
translations.fr: Mon père a insisté pour que nous partions.
translations.pt: Meu pai insistiu que deveríamos ir.

examples.text: I'll do it, if you insist.

translations.de: Ich mach es, wenn du darauf bestehst.
translations.fr: Je le ferai, si tu insistes.
translations.pt: Eu faço, já que você insiste.

examples.text: She insisted on her innocence.

translations.de: Sie beharrte auf ihrer Unschuld.
translations.fr: Elle insistait sur son innocence.
translations.pt: Ela insistiu na sua inocência.

examples.text: Life is really simple, but we insist on making it complicated.

translations.de: Das Leben ist eigentlich einfach, aber wir können es nicht lassen, es kompliziert zu machen.
translations.fr: La vie est vraiment simple, mais nous nous acharnons à la rendre compliquée.
translations.pt: A vida é realmente simples, mas insistimos em torná-la complicada.

more.definition: To hold up a claim emphatically.; To demand continually that something happen or be done; to reiterate a demand despite requests to abandon it.
more.etymology: Partly from Middle French insister, from Latin īnsistere; and partly from a back-formation from insistence. Compare typologically from the same PIE root Bulgarian настоявам (nastojavam), Russian наста́ивать (nastáivatʹ).

examples.text: Bring out your knights before developing the bishops.

translations.de: Bringen Sie Ihre Springer heraus, bevor Sie die Läufer entwickeln.
translations.fr: Sortez vos cavaliers avant de développer les fous.
translations.pt: Traga seus cavalos para o jogo antes de desenvolver os bispos.

examples.text: Spain is a developed country.

translations.de: Spanien ist ein Industriestaat.
translations.fr: L'Espagne est un pays développé.
translations.pt: A Espanha é um país desenvolvido.

examples.text: Reading develops the mind.

translations.de: Lesen schult den Verstand.
translations.fr: La lecture éduque l'esprit.
translations.pt: Ler desenvolve a mente.

examples.text: I'm developing an Android application.

translations.de: Ich entwickle eine Android-App.
translations.fr: Je suis en train de développer une application Android.
translations.pt: Estou desenvolvendo uma aplicação Android.

more.definition: To change with a specific direction, progress.; To progress through a sequence of stages.; To advance; to further; to promote the growth of.
more.etymology: Borrowed from French développer, from Middle French desveloper, from Old French desveloper, from des- + voloper, veloper, vloper (“to wrap, wrap up”) (compare Italian sviluppare, Old Italian alternative form goluppare (“to wrap”)) from Vulgar Latin *vloppō, *wloppō (“to wrap”) ultimately from Proto-Germanic *wrappaną, *wlappaną (“to wrap, roll up, turn, wind”), from Proto-Indo-European *werb- (“to turn, bend”) …

examples.text: I don't like working the graveyard shift.

translations.de: Die Geisterstundenschicht gefällt mir nicht.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas travailler de nuit.

examples.text: Can you drive a stick shift?

translations.de: Kannst du ein Auto mit Schaltgetriebe fahren?
translations.fr: Sais-tu conduire une voiture à boîte manuelle ?

examples.text: My shift's almost over.

translations.de: Meine Schicht ist fast vorbei.
translations.fr: Mon service est presque terminé.

examples.text: He works the night shift.

translations.de: Er hat Nachtschicht.
translations.fr: Il travaille en équipe de nuit.

more.definition: A movement to do something, a beginning.; An act of shifting; a slight movement or change.; A type of women's undergarment of dress length worn under dresses or skirts, a slip or chemise.
more.etymology: The verb is from Middle English schiften, from Old English sċiftan (“to divide, separate into shares; appoint, ordain; arrange, organise”), from Proto-West Germanic *skiftijan, from Proto-Germanic *skiftijaną, *skiptijaną, from earlier *skipatjaną (“to organise, put in order”), from Proto-Indo-European *skeyb- (“to separate, divide, part”), from Proto-Indo-European *skey- (“to cut, divide, separate, part”).

examples.text: You'd better get a shift on.

translations.de: Du solltest dich besser beeilen.
translations.fr: Tu ferais mieux de te dépêcher.

examples.text: The wind is shifting.

translations.de: Der Wind dreht sich.
translations.fr: Le vent tourne.

Doublet of cashel, castell, castellum, and château.

examples.text: It must have cost a fortune.

more.definition: Destiny, especially favorable.; A prediction or set of predictions about a person's future provided by a fortune teller.; A small slip of paper with wise or vaguely prophetic words printed on it, baked into a fortune cookie.
more.etymology: From Middle English fortune, from Old French fortune, from Latin fortuna (“fate, luck”). The plural form fortunae meant “possessions”, which also gave fortune the meaning of “riches”.

examples.text: It must have cost a fortune.

translations.de: Das muss ein Vermögen gekostet haben.

examples.text: He left a large fortune to his son.

translations.de: Er hinterließ seinem Sohn ein beträchtliches Vermögen.

examples.text: May fortune smile on you.

translations.fr: Puisse la fortune te sourire !

more.definition: To provide (someone) with a fortune.; To tell the fortune of (someone); to presage.

examples.text: Luck plays an important role in our life.

examples.text: Cycling plays an important role in Munich.

translations.de: Der Radverkehr spielt in München eine wichtige Rolle.

examples.text: What's your role in this affair?

translations.fr: Quel est ton rôle dans cette affaire ?

more.definition: A character or part played by a performer or actor.; The expected behaviour of an individual in a society.; The function or position of something.

examples.text: Draw me a large circle.

translations.de: Zeichne mir einen großen Kreis.
translations.fr: Dessine-moi un grand cercle.
translations.pt: Desenhe-me um grande círculo.

examples.text: Quit going around in circles and get to the point.

translations.de: Hör auf, um den heißen Brei herumzureden, und komm zur Sache.
translations.fr: Arrête de tourner autour du pot et viens-en au fait.
translations.pt: Pare de dar voltas e vá direto ao ponto.

examples.text: A circle is always round.

translations.de: Ein Kreis ist immer rund.
translations.fr: Un cercle est toujours rond.
translations.pt: Um círculo sempre é redondo.

examples.text: Please circle the right answer.

translations.de: Bitte die richtige Antwort umkreisen.
translations.fr: Entourez la bonne réponse, s'il vous plaît.
translations.pt: Por favor circule a resposta certa.

more.definition: A two-dimensional geometric figure, a line, consisting of the set of all those points in a plane that are equally distant from a given point (center).; A two-dimensional geometric figure, a disk, consisting of the set of all those points of a plane at a distance less than or equal to a fixed distance (radius) from a given point.; The orbit of an astronomical body.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker-der. Ancient Greek κίρκος (kírkos)bor. Old French cerclebor. From Middle English circle, cercle, from Old French cercle and Latin circulus, diminutive of Latin circus (“circle, circus”), from Ancient Greek κίρκος (kírkos, “circle, ring”), related to Old English hring (“ring”). Compare also Old English ċircul (“circle, zodiac”), which came from the same Latin source.

examples.text: The students sat in a circle.

translations.de: Die Schüler saßen im Kreis.
translations.fr: Les élèves se sont assis en cercle.
translations.pt: Os estudantes se sentaram em círculo.

examples.text: The moon circles the earth.

translations.de: Der Mond kreist um die Erde.
translations.fr: La Lune tourne autour de la Terre.
translations.pt: A Lua circunda a Terra.

examples.text: A helicopter circled over us.

translations.de: Ein Hubschrauber kreiste über uns.
translations.fr: Un hélicoptère décrivait des cercles au-dessus de nous.

examples.text: The answer leads us to a vicious circle.

translations.fr: La réponse nous mène à un cercle vicieux.

more.definition: To travel around along a curved path; to orbit.; To surround; to encompass within a circle.; To place in a circle; to make a circle.

Compare also Old English ċircul (“circle, zodiac”), which came from the same Latin source.

examples.text: God is the name of the great mystery.

translations.fr: Dieu est le nom du grand mystère.
translations.pt: Deus é o nome do grande mistério.

more.definition: Something secret or unexplainable; an unknown.; Someone or something with an obscure or puzzling nature.; An account, story, book, film, or play, often with the theme of crime or murder, with a surprise ending that explains all the strange events that have occurred.
more.etymology: From Middle English mysterie, from Anglo-Norman misterie (Old French mistere), from Latin mysterium, from Ancient Greek μυστήριον (mustḗrion, “a mystery, a secret, a secret rite”), from μύστης (mústēs, “initiated one”), from μυέω (muéō, “to initiate”), from μύω (múō, “to shut”). more.definition: Made of the metal iron.; Strong (as of will), inflexible.
more.etymology: Proto-Celtic *īsarnombor. From Middle English iren, from Old English īsern, īsærn, īren, īsen, from Proto-West Germanic *īsarn, from Proto-Germanic *īsarną (“iron”), from Proto-Celtic *īsarnom (“iron”), possibly a derivation from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ésh₂r̥ (“blood”).

examples.text: I have to iron my shirt.

translations.de: Ich muss mein Hemd bügeln.
translations.fr: Je dois repasser ma chemise.

examples.text: Gold is more precious than iron.

translations.de: Gold ist wertvoller als Eisen.
translations.fr: L'or est plus précieux que le fer.
translations.pt: O ouro é mais precioso do que o ferro.

examples.text: Can you iron this T-shirt for me, please?

examples.text: Gold is heavier than iron.

translations.fr: L'or est plus lourd que le fer.
translations.pt: Ouro pesa mais do que ferro.

more.definition: A common, inexpensive metal, silvery grey when untarnished, that rusts, is attracted by magnets, and is used in making steel: a chemical element having atomic number 26 and symbol Fe.; Any material, not a steel, predominantly made of elemental iron.; A tool or appliance made of metal, which is heated and then used to transfer heat to something else; most often a thick piece of metal fitted with a handle and having a flat, roughly triangular bottom, which is heated and used to press wrinkles from clothing, and now usually containing an electrical heating apparatus.
more.etymology: Proto-Celtic *īsarnombor. From Middle English iren, from Old English īsern, īsærn, īren, īsen, from Proto-West Germanic *īsarn, from Proto-Germanic *īsarną (“iron”), from Proto-Celtic *īsarnom (“iron”), possibly a derivation from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ésh₂r̥ (“blood”).

examples.text: Beans have a lot of iron.

examples.text: This shirt needs to be ironed.

translations.de: Dieses Hemd muss gebügelt werden.
translations.fr: Cette chemise a besoin d'être repassée.

examples.text: Their job is to iron clothes.

translations.de: Ihre Arbeit ist es, Kleider zu bügeln.
translations.fr: Leur travail consiste à repasser des vêtements.
translations.pt: O trabalho deles é passar roupas.

examples.text: This bridge is made of iron.

translations.de: Diese Brücke ist aus Eisen.
translations.fr: Ce pont est en fer.
translations.pt: Esta ponte é de ferro.

more.definition: To pass an iron over (clothing or some other item made of cloth) in order to remove creases.; To engage in such pressing of clothing.; To furnish, clad, or arm with iron.
more.etymology: Proto-Celtic *īsarnombor. From Middle English iren, from Old English īsern, īsærn, īren, īsen, from Proto-West Germanic *īsarn, from Proto-Germanic *īsarną (“iron”), from Proto-Celtic *īsarnom (“iron”), possibly a derivation from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ésh₂r̥ (“blood”).

examples.text: He doesn't live in my neighborhood.

examples.text: Do you live in this neighborhood?

more.definition: The residential area near one's home.; The inhabitants of a residential area.; A formal or informal division of a municipality or region.
more.etymology: From an alteration of earlier neighborred (“neighborhood”), from Middle English neȝeburredde, neheborreden, equivalent to neighbor + -red; the term being interpreted as neighbor + -hood. For change in suffix (-red to -hood), compare brotherhood. Cognates Cognate with Scots nichbourheid (“neighbourhood”). Compare also Dutch naburigheid (“neighbourhood”).

examples.text: I'll be back on Monday.

more.etymology: From Middle English Monday, Monenday, from Old English mōnandæġ (“day of the moon”), from Proto-West Germanic *mānini dag, a calque (interpretātiō germānica) of Latin diēs Lūnae, equivalent to Moon + day. See also Japanese 月曜日 (“Moon's day”).

examples.text: The first day of the week is Monday.

more.etymology: From Middle English Monday, Monenday, from Old English mōnandæġ (“day of the moon”), from Proto-West Germanic *mānini dag, a calque (interpretātiō germānica) of Latin diēs Lūnae, equivalent to Moon + day. See also Japanese 月曜日 (“Moon's day”).

examples.text: They replaced the defective TV with a new one.

translations.pt: Eles substituíram a televisão defeituosa por uma nova.

examples.text: We must pay the tax.

translations.fr: Nous devons payer l'impôt.

examples.text: The price includes tax.

examples.text: What is tax?

translations.de: Was ist eine Steuer?
translations.fr: Qu'est-ce qu'une taxe ?

more.definition: Money or goods collected by a government (or an entity to whom the government has delegated this power, e.g. in tax farming) to fund itself and its services, for example by levying a charge on income, purchases (sales), property or harvest, other than that money which is collected by the government in exchange for specific goods (e.g. the purchase of surplus vehicles).; A charge (of money, food, labor, etc) collected by a person, organization, etc; something required (exacted) from someone who is (really or notionally) under the control of the taxer, such as a contribution or service.; A burdensome demand
more.etymology: From Middle English taxe, from Middle French taxe, from Medieval Latin taxa, from Latin taxō (“to appraise, value, estimate; (medieval) to tax”). Doublet of task. Displaced native Old English gafol, which was also the word for “tribute” and “rent”.

examples.text: I don't like paying taxes.

examples.text: Is this product tax-exempt?

more.definition: To impose and collect a tax from (a person or company).; To impose and collect a tax on (something).; To make excessive demands on.
more.etymology: From Middle English taxen, from Anglo-Norman taxer (“to impose a tax”), from Latin taxāre (“to handle, to censure, to appraise, to compute”).

translations.fr: On gagne en sagesse avec l'âge.
translations.pt: Adquirimos sabedoria com a idade.

examples.text: No pain, no gain!

translations.de: Ohne Fleiß kein Preis.
translations.fr: On n'a rien sans peine.
translations.pt: Sem dor, sem ganho!

examples.text: I don't want to gain weight.

translations.de: Ich will nicht zunehmen.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas prendre de poids.
translations.pt: Eu não quero ganhar peso.

examples.text: You gain one point for every opponent piece you capture.

translations.de: Für jeden gefangenen Gegnerstein erhältst du einen Punkt.
translations.fr: Un point est gagné pour chaque pierre de l'adversaire qui est capturée.
translations.pt: Ganha-se um ponto por cada peça do oponente que se captura.

more.etymology: From dialectal English gen, gin, short for again, agen (“against”); also Middle English gain, gayn, gein, ȝæn (“against”), from Old English gēan, geġn (“against”). More at against.

examples.text: Ill-gotten gains never benefit anyone.

translations.de: Gestohlenes Gut gedeiht selten gut.
translations.fr: Bien mal acquis ne profite jamais.
translations.pt: Adquirido ilegalmente não é proveitoso.

examples.text: I've gained three kilograms.

translations.de: Ich habe drei Kilo zugenommen.
translations.fr: J'ai pris trois kilos.
translations.pt: Engordei três quilos.

examples.text: They're gaining on us.

translations.de: Sie holen uns ein.
translations.fr: Ils nous rattrapent.
translations.pt: Eles estão ganhando da gente.

examples.text: You've gained weight.

translations.de: Du hast zugenommen.
translations.fr: Tu as pris du poids.
translations.pt: Você ganhou peso.

more.definition: To acquire possession of.; To have or receive advantage or profit; to acquire gain; to grow rich; to advance in interest, health, or happiness; to make progress.; To increase.
more.etymology: From Middle English gayn, gain, gein (“profit, advantage”), from Old Norse gagn (“benefit, advantage, use”), from Proto-Germanic *gagną, *gaganą (“gain, profit", literally "return”), from Proto-Germanic *gagana (“back, against, in return”), a reduplication of Proto-Germanic *ga- (“with, together”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱóm (“next to, at, with, along”).

examples.text: The falcon has perfect vision.

translations.de: Der Falke hat eine perfekte Sicht.
translations.fr: Le faucon a une vision parfaite.
translations.pt: O falcão tem uma visão perfeita.

examples.text: There are no real visions.

translations.de: Es gibt keine echten Visionen.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas de visions réelles.
translations.pt: Não há visões reais.

examples.text: Mary had a vision.

translations.de: Maria hatte eine Vision.
translations.fr: Mary eut une vision.
translations.pt: Mary teve uma visão.

examples.text: There is a lack of long-term vision for Europe.

translations.de: Es fehlt eine langfristige Vision für Europa.
translations.fr: Il manque une vision à long terme pour l'Europe.
translations.pt: Falta uma visão de longo-prazo para a Europa.

more.definition: The sense or ability of sight.; Something seen; an object perceived visually.; Something imaginary one thinks one sees.
more.etymology: Latin vīsiōlbor. Anglo-Norman visiounbor. From Middle English visioun, from Anglo-Norman visioun, from Old French vision, from Latin vīsiō (“vision, seeing”), noun of action from the perfect passive participle visus (“that which is seen”), from the verb videō (“to see”) + action noun suffix -iō.

more.definition: To imagine something as if it were to be true.; To present as in a vision.; To provide with a vision.
more.etymology: Latin vīsiōlbor. Anglo-Norman visiounbor. From Middle English visioun, from Anglo-Norman visioun, from Old French vision, from Latin vīsiō (“vision, seeing”), noun of action from the perfect passive participle visus (“that which is seen”), from the verb videō (“to see”) + action noun suffix -iō.

examples.text: Without your help, I would have drowned.

translations.de: Ohne deine Hilfe wäre ich ertrunken.
translations.fr: Si tu ne m'avais pas aidé, je me serais noyé.
translations.pt: Sem tua ajuda, teria me afogado.

examples.text: He saved a dog from drowning.

translations.de: Er rettete einen Hund vor dem Ertrinken.
translations.fr: Il a sauvé un chien de la noyade.
translations.pt: Ele salvou um cachorro de se afogar.

examples.text: You won't drown if you learn how to swim.

translations.de: Wenn du schwimmen lernst, ertrinkst du nicht.
translations.fr: Tu ne te noieras pas si tu apprends à nager.
translations.pt: Você não vai se afogar se aprender a nadar.

examples.text: A girl drowned in the pond yesterday.

translations.de: Ein Mädchen ist gestern im Teich ertrunken.
translations.fr: Une fille s'est noyée dans la mare hier.
translations.pt: Uma garota se afogou no lago ontem.

more.definition: To die from suffocation while immersed in water or other fluid.; To kill by suffocating in water or another liquid.; To be flooded: to be inundated with or submerged in (literally) water or (figuratively) other things; to be overwhelmed.
more.etymology: From Middle English drownen, drounen, drunen (“to drown”), of obscure and uncertain origin. The OED suggests an unattested Old English form *drūnian. Harper 2001 points to Old English druncnian, ġedruncnian (> Middle English drunknen, dronknen (“to drown”)), "probably influenced" by Old Norse drukkna (cf. Icelandic drukkna, Danish drukne (“to drown”)). Funk & Wagnall's has 'of uncertain origin'.

examples.text: What was the cause of the explosion?

translations.de: Was war der Grund für die Explosion?
translations.fr: Quelle était la cause de l'explosion ?
translations.pt: Qual foi a causa da explosão?

examples.text: Tom was killed in the explosion.

translations.de: Tom kam bei der Explosion ums Leben.
translations.fr: Tom a été tué dans l'explosion.
translations.pt: Tom foi morto na explosão.

examples.text: The explosion came about by accident.

translations.de: Es kam aus Versehen zur Explosion.
translations.fr: L'explosion s'est produite par accident.
translations.pt: A explosão foi produzida por acidente.

examples.text: The workman died from the explosion.

translations.de: Der Arbeiter starb infolge der Explosion.
translations.fr: L'ouvrier est décédé des suites de l'explosion.
translations.pt: O operário morreu por causa da explosão.

more.definition: A violent release of energy (sometimes mechanical, nuclear, or chemical); an act or instance of exploding.; The sound of an explosion.; A sudden, uncontrolled or rapid increase, expansion, or bursting out.
more.etymology: Latin explosiōnemder. French explosionbor. From French explosion, from Latin explōsio, from explōdo (“to drive out by clapping”), from ex- and plōdo (“to clap or strike”). For more information see explode.

examples.text: Who is the wisest person you know?

translations.de: Wer ist die klügste Person, die du kennst?
translations.fr: Quelle est la personne la plus savante que tu connais ?
translations.pt: Qual é a pessoa mais sábia que você conhece?

examples.text: She is older and wiser now.

translations.de: Sie ist jetzt älter und weiser.
translations.fr: Elle est plus âgée et plus sage, maintenant.
translations.pt: Agora ela é mais idosa e mais sábia.

examples.text: He was wise enough to take her advice.

translations.de: Er war so klug, ihren Rat anzunehmen.
translations.fr: Il fut assez malin pour accepter son conseil.
translations.pt: Ele era sábio o suficiente para seguir teu conselho.

examples.text: Apollo adjudged Socrates the wisest man.

translations.de: Apollo hielt Sokrates für den weisesten Mann.
translations.fr: Apollon a déclaré Socrate l'homme le plus sage.
translations.pt: Apolo considerou Sócrates o mais sábio dos homens.

more.definition: Showing good judgement or the benefit of experience.; Disrespectful.; Aware, informed (to something).
more.etymology: From Middle English wys, wyse, from Old English wīs (“wise”), from Proto-Germanic *wīsaz (“knowledgeable, wise”), from Proto-Indo-European *wéydos (“seeing; knowledge”), from *weyd- (“to see”).

examples.text: A word is enough to a wise man.

translations.de: Dem klugen Kopf genügt ein Wort.
translations.fr: Un mot est assez pour un homme sage.
translations.pt: Para bom entendedor, meia palavra basta.

examples.text: It was a wise decision.

translations.de: Es war ein weiser Entschluss.
translations.fr: Ce fut une sage décision.
translations.pt: Foi uma decisão sábia.

examples.text: The old man looked wise.

translations.de: Der alte Mann sah weise aus.
translations.fr: Le vieil homme avait l'air avisé.
translations.pt: O idoso parecia sábio.

examples.text: You made a wise choice.

translations.de: Du hast weise gewählt.
translations.fr: Tu as fait un choix judicieux.
translations.pt: Fizeste uma escolha sábia.

more.etymology: From Middle English wise, from Old English wīse, from Proto-Germanic *wīsō. Cognate with Dutch wijze, German Weise, Norwegian vis, Swedish visa, vis, Italian guisa, Spanish guisa. Compare -wise. Doublet of guise.

examples.text: He's very wise.

translations.de: Er ist sehr weise.
translations.fr: Il est très sage.
translations.pt: Ele é muito sábio.

examples.text: She is very wise.

translations.de: Sie ist sehr weise.
translations.fr: Elle est très sage.
translations.pt: Ela é muito sábia.

examples.text: A wise businessman knows how to clamp down on costs.

translations.de: Ein weiser Geschäftsmann weiß, wie man Kosten niedrig hält.
translations.fr: Un homme d'affaires avisé sait comment restreindre les coûts.
translations.pt: Um empresário inteligente sabe como reduzir os custos.

examples.text: It is true she is young, but she is wise.

translations.de: Es ist wahr, dass sie jung ist, aber sie ist weise.
translations.fr: Il est vrai qu'elle est jeune, mais elle est sage.
translations.pt: É verdade que ela é jovem, mas ela é sábia.

more.definition: To become wise.; Usually with "up", to inform or learn.
more.etymology: From Middle English wys, wyse, from Old English wīs (“wise”), from Proto-Germanic *wīsaz (“knowledgeable, wise”), from Proto-Indo-European *wéydos (“seeing; knowledge”), from *weyd- (“to see”).

examples.text: I did not have sexual relations with that woman.

translations.de: Ich hatte keine sexuelle Beziehung mit dieser Frau.
translations.fr: Je n'eus pas de relations sexuelles avec cette femme.
translations.pt: Eu não tive relações sexuais com essa mulher.

examples.text: Sexual harassment has now become a social issue.

translations.de: Sexuelle Belästigung ist nun zu einem gesellschaftlichen Thema geworden.
translations.fr: Le harcèlement sexuel est maintenant devenu un problème de société.
translations.pt: Assédio sexual tornou-se uma questão social.

examples.text: There's nothing sexual about it.

translations.fr: Il n'y a rien de sexuel là-dedans.
translations.pt: Não tem nada de sexual nisso.

examples.text: Men tend to exaggerate their number of sexual partners.

translations.de: Männer neigen bei der Zahl ihrer Beischlafpartner zur Übertreibung.
translations.fr: Les hommes ont tendance à gonfler le nombre de leurs partenaires sexuels.

more.definition: Arising from the fact of being male or female; pertaining to sex or gender, or to the social relations between the sexes.; Capable of sexual reproduction; sexed, sexuate.; Pertaining to sexual intercourse or other intimate physical contact.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *sek-der. Proto-Indo-European *séks-u-sder. Latin sexuālisbor. Borrowed from Latin sexuālis. By surface analysis, sex + -ual.

examples.text: When life is too stressful, sexual function decreases.

translations.de: Wenn das Leben zu stressig ist, schwächt das die sexuelle Funktion.
translations.fr: Lorsque la vie est trop stressante, la fonction sexuelle décroît.

examples.text: Men sometimes overestimate their sexual prowess.

translations.de: Männer überschätzen mitunter ihre sexuellen Fähigkeiten.
translations.fr: Les hommes surestiment parfois leurs prouesses sexuelles.

more.definition: A species which reproduces by sexual rather than asexual reproduction, or a member of such a species.; A person who experiences sexual attraction, a person who has interest in or desire for sex (especially as contrasted with an asexual).
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *sek-der. Proto-Indo-European *séks-u-sder. Latin sexuālisbor. Borrowed from Latin sexuālis. By surface analysis, sex + -ual.

examples.text: Is the cursor on the screen?

translations.de: Ist der Cursor auf dem Bildschirm?
translations.fr: Le pointeur est-il à l'écran ?
translations.pt: O cursor está na tela?

examples.text: Children must not spend too much time in front of screens.

translations.de: Kinder dürfen nicht zu viel Zeit vor Bildschirmen verbringen.
translations.fr: Les enfants ne doivent pas passer trop de temps devant les écrans.
translations.pt: As crianças não devem passar muito tempo na frente das telas.

examples.text: Turn the screen off and on again.

translations.de: Mach den Bildschirm aus und wieder an.
translations.fr: Éteins l'écran et rallume-le.

examples.text: A screen divided the room into two.

translations.de: Ein Wandschirm teilte das Zimmer in zwei Hälften.
translations.fr: Un écran séparait la pièce en deux.

more.definition: A physical divider intended to block an area from view, or provide shelter from something dangerous.; A dwarf wall or partition carried up to a certain height for separation and protection, as in a church, to separate the aisle from the choir, etc.; A stand of trees or other plants that can block wind.
more.etymology: From Middle English scren, screne (“windscreen, firescreen”), from Anglo-Norman escren (“firescreen, the tester of a bed”), Old French escren, escrein, escran (modern French écran (“screen”)), from Middle Dutch scherm, from Old Dutch skirm, from Proto-West Germanic *skirmi, from Proto-Germanic *skirmiz (“fur, shelter, covering, screen”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to cut, divide”).

examples.text: When does the screening start?

translations.de: Wann fängt die Filmvorführung an?
translations.fr: Quand commence la projection ?

examples.text: Tom's eyes were glued to the screen.

translations.fr: Les yeux de Tom étaient collés à l'écran.
translations.pt: Os olhos de Tom estavam vidrados na tela.

more.definition: To filter by passing through a screen.; To filter.; To shelter or conceal.
more.etymology: From Middle English scren, screne (“windscreen, firescreen”), from Anglo-Norman escren (“firescreen, the tester of a bed”), Old French escren, escrein, escran (modern French écran (“screen”)), from Middle Dutch scherm, from Old Dutch skirm, from Proto-West Germanic *skirmi, from Proto-Germanic *skirmiz (“fur, shelter, covering, screen”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to cut, divide”).

examples.text: I'll go wherever you go.

translations.de: Ich werde gehen, wohin du gehst.
translations.fr: J'irai où que tu ailles.
translations.pt: Eu irei aonde quer que vás.

examples.text: Put it wherever there is room.

translations.de: Stell es irgendwohin, wo Platz ist.
translations.fr: Mets-la là où il y a de la place.
translations.pt: Coloque onde houver espaço.

examples.text: You may sit wherever you like.

translations.de: Du kannst dich hinsetzen, wo du magst.
translations.fr: Tu peux t'asseoir où tu veux.
translations.pt: Você pode sentar-se onde quiser.

examples.text: Leave it wherever you want.

translations.de: Lassen Sie es, wo immer Sie wollen.
translations.fr: Laissez-le où vous voulez.
translations.pt: Deixe-o onde quiser.

more.definition: Where ever; an emphatic form of where.; In, at or to any place that one likes or chooses.; The place (no matter where) in, at or to which.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-osinflu. Proto-West Germanic *aiwder. From where + -ever.

examples.text: Sit wherever you like.

translations.de: Setz dich hin, wo du willst.
translations.fr: Assieds-toi où tu veux !
translations.pt: Sente-se onde desejar.

examples.text: Wherever you go, I will follow you.

translations.de: Wohin du auch gehst, ich werde dir folgen.
translations.fr: Je te suivrai peu importe où tu vas.
translations.pt: Onde quer que você vá, eu o seguirei.

examples.text: His dog follows him wherever he goes.

translations.de: Sein Hund folgt ihm, wo auch immer er hingeht.
translations.fr: Son chien le suit où qu'il aille.
translations.pt: O cachorro dele o segue aonde ele for.

examples.text: I'll follow you wherever you go.

translations.de: Ich werde dir folgen, wohin du auch gehen wirst.
translations.fr: Où que tu ailles, je te suivrai.
translations.pt: Onde quer que você vá, eu o seguirei.

more.definition: Regardless of the place in, at or to which.; In, at or to any place (that); anywhere.; In, at or to all places or situations (that); everywhere.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-osinflu. Proto-West Germanic *aiwder. From where + -ever.

examples.text: The experiment confirmed his theory.

translations.de: Das Experiment bestätigte seine Theorie.
translations.fr: L'expérience a confirmé sa théorie.
translations.pt: O experimento confirmou sua teoria.

examples.text: It's an experiment.

translations.de: Es ist ein Experiment.
translations.fr: C'est une expérience.
translations.pt: É um experimento.

examples.text: The experiment was successful.

translations.de: Das Experiment war ein Erfolg.
translations.fr: L'expérience fut une réussite.
translations.pt: O experimento foi bem sucedido.

examples.text: The experiment failed.

translations.de: Das Experiment scheiterte.
translations.fr: L'expérience a échoué.
translations.pt: O experimento falhou.

more.definition: A test under controlled conditions made to either demonstrate a known truth, examine the validity of a hypothesis, or determine the efficacy or likelihood of something previously untried.
more.etymology: From Middle English experiment, from Old French esperiment (French expérience), from Latin experimentum (“experience, attempt, experiment”), from experior (“to experience, to attempt”), itself from ex + *perior, in turn from Proto-Indo-European *per-.

examples.text: Let's do a scientific experiment.

translations.de: Machen wir ein wissenschaftliches Experiment.
translations.fr: Faisons une expérience scientifique.
translations.pt: Façamos uma experiência científica.

examples.text: Without experiments and mathematics, we would never have understood what we understand.

translations.de: Ohne Experimente und Mathematik hätten wir nie verstanden, was wir verstehen.
translations.fr: Sans les expériences et les mathématiques, nous n'aurions jamais compris ce que nous comprenons.
translations.pt: Sem experimentos e sem matemática, jamais teríamos compreendido o que compreendemos.

examples.text: The result of the experiment was a blue substance.

translations.de: Bei dem Experiment kam eine blaue Substanz heraus.
translations.fr: Le résultat de l'expérience était une substance bleue.
translations.pt: O resultado da experiência foi uma substância azul.

examples.text: The experiment has to begin.

translations.de: Das Experiment muss losgehen.
translations.fr: L'expérience doit commencer.
translations.pt: O experimento tem de começar.

more.definition: To conduct an experiment.; To try something to observe the results.
more.etymology: From Middle English experiment, from Old French esperiment (French expérience), from Latin experimentum (“experience, attempt, experiment”), from experior (“to experience, to attempt”), itself from ex + *perior, in turn from Proto-Indo-European *per-.

examples.text: This is an important victory.

translations.de: Dies ist ein wichtiger Sieg.
translations.fr: C'est une victoire importante.
translations.pt: Esta é uma vitória importante.

examples.text: This is a great victory.

translations.de: Das ist ein großer Sieg.
translations.fr: C'est une grande victoire.
translations.pt: Esta é uma grande vitória.

examples.text: It's an easy victory.

translations.de: Es ist ein leichter Sieg.
translations.fr: C'est une victoire facile.
translations.pt: É uma vitória fácil.

examples.text: The victory is ours.

translations.de: Der Sieg ist unser.
translations.fr: La victoire est à nous.
translations.pt: A vitória é nossa.

more.definition: Used to encourage someone to achieve success, or to celebrate a success or triumph.
more.etymology: The noun is derived from Middle English victory, victori, victorie (“supremacy, victory; a defeat or vanquishing, conquest; superior military force; might, power, strength; triumphal celebration or procession; monument commemorating a defeat; superior position, dominance; mastery; moral victory, vindication; success, triumph; redemption, salvation; resurrection of Jesus; means of achieving spiritual victory; reward …

examples.text: It's an easy victory.

translations.de: Es ist ein leichter Sieg.

examples.text: The victory is ours.

translations.de: Der Sieg ist unser.
translations.fr: La victoire est à nous.
translations.pt: A vitória é nossa.

examples.text: Victory is unlikely but not impossible.

translations.de: Der Sieg ist unwahrscheinlich, aber nicht unmöglich.
translations.fr: La victoire est improbable mais pas impossible.
translations.pt: A vitória é improvável, mas não impossível.

examples.text: Victory is on our side.

translations.de: Der Sieg ist unser.
translations.fr: La victoire est de notre côté.
translations.pt: A vitória está do nosso lado.

more.definition: The condition or state of having won a battle or competition, or having succeeded in an effort; (countable) an instance of this.; Alternative letter-case form of Victory (“(uncountable) the Roman goddess of victory, the counterpart of the Greek goddess Nike; also (countable), an artistic depiction of her, chiefly as a winged woman”).
more.etymology: The noun is derived from Middle English victory, victori, victorie (“supremacy, victory; a defeat or vanquishing, conquest; superior military force; might, power, strength; triumphal celebration or procession; monument commemorating a defeat; superior position, dominance; mastery; moral victory, vindication; success, triumph; redemption, salvation; resurrection of Jesus; means of achieving spiritual victory; reward …

examples.text: Victory is on our side.

translations.de: Der Sieg ist unser.
translations.fr: La victoire est de notre côté.
translations.pt: A vitória está do nosso lado.

examples.text: Congratulations on the victory!

translations.de: Glückwunsch zum Sieg!
translations.fr: Félicitations pour la victoire !
translations.pt: Parabéns pela vitória!

examples.text: This is an important victory.

translations.de: Dies ist ein wichtiger Sieg.
translations.fr: C'est une victoire importante.
translations.pt: Esta é uma vitória importante.

examples.text: This is a great victory.

translations.de: Das ist ein großer Sieg.
translations.fr: C'est une grande victoire.
translations.pt: Esta é uma grande vitória.

more.etymology: From Middle English victorien (“to overcome, vanquish”), from Old French victorier, or from Medieval Latin victōriāre, from Latin victōria (noun); see further at etymology 1. Cognates * Italian vittoriare

examples.text: The comrades know our opinions.

translations.de: Die Genossen kennen unsere Meinung.
translations.fr: Les camarades connaissent nos opinions.
translations.pt: Os camaradas conhecem nossas opiniões.

examples.text: Our comrade is reading a novel.

translations.de: Unser Kamerad liest einen Roman.
translations.fr: Notre camarade lit un roman.

examples.text: Run, comrade, the old world is behind you!

translations.fr: Cours, camarade, le vieux monde est derrière toi !
translations.pt: Corra, camarada, o velho mundo está atrás de você!

examples.text: Comrade Tom fell in love with comrade Mary.

translations.de: Genosse Tom hat sich in Genossin Maria verliebt.

more.definition: A mate, companion, or associate.; A companion in battle; fellow soldier.; A fellow socialist, communist or other similarly politically aligned person.

examples.text: A living dog is better than a dead lion.

translations.de: Lieber ein lebendiger Hund als ein toter Löwe.
translations.fr: Chien en vie vaut mieux que lion mort.
translations.pt: Mais vale cão vivo que leão morto.

more.definition: Of the light brown color that resembles the fur of a lion.
more.etymology: From Middle English lyoun, lion, leon, borrowed from Old French lion, from Latin leō, (accusative: leōnem), from Ancient Greek λέων (léōn), of unclear origin. Doublet of Leo, leu, lev, and Lyon. Displaced Old English lēo, from the same Latin source.

examples.text: Joe and I saw a lion yesterday.

translations.de: Joe und ich haben gestern einen Löwen gesehen.
translations.fr: Joe et moi avons vu un lion hier.
translations.pt: O Joe e eu vimos um leão ontem.

examples.text: Many years ago, there were lions in Greece.

translations.de: Vor vielen Jahren gab es Löwen in Griechenland.
translations.fr: Il y a de nombreuses années, il y avait des lions en Grèce.
translations.pt: Muitos anos atrás, havia leões na Grécia.

examples.text: After having opened his cage the lion escaped.

translations.de: Nachdem er seinen Käfig geöffnet hatte, entkam der Löwe.
translations.fr: Après avoir ouvert sa cage, le lion s'est échappé.
translations.pt: Depois de abrir a jaula, o leão escapou.

examples.text: Tom opened the lion's cage.

translations.de: Tom öffnete den Löwenkäfig.
translations.fr: Thomas ouvrit la cage du lion.
translations.pt: Tom abriu a jaula do leão.

more.definition: A big cat, Panthera leo, native to Africa, India and formerly much of Europe.; A male lion, as opposed to a lioness, which is characterized by having a flowing shaggy mane and taking little part in hunting, which can be done cooperatively.; Any of various extant and extinct big cats, especially the mountain lion.
more.etymology: From Middle English lyoun, lion, leon, borrowed from Old French lion, from Latin leō, (accusative: leōnem), from Ancient Greek λέων (léōn), of unclear origin. Doublet of Leo, leu, lev, and Lyon. Displaced Old English lēo, from the same Latin source.

examples.text: Medical science has made a dramatic advance.

examples.text: Why do you have to be so dramatic?

more.definition: Of or relating to the drama.; Striking in appearance or effect.; Having a powerful, expressive singing voice.

examples.text: It's rare to meet nice people like you.

examples.text: True friendships are even rarer than diamonds.

translations.de: Wahre Freundschaften sind seltener noch als Diamanten.

more.definition: Very uncommon; scarce.; Small in number (but not unusual); infrequent; sparse.; Thin; of low density.

examples.text: This product was made in China.

translations.de: Dieses Produkt wurde in China gefertigt.

examples.text: This product is made in Italy.

examples.text: They were mostly women.

Those doors certainly didn't smash themselves open.

examples.text: We used emergency measures to revive the cardiac arrest patient.

translations.de: Wir griffen zu Notmaßnahmen, um den Patienten mit Herzstillstand wiederzubeleben.

examples.text: Have you measured it?

more.definition: To ascertain the quantity of a unit of material via calculated comparison with respect to a standard.; To be of (a certain size), to have (a certain measurement).; To estimate the unit size of something.

translations.pt: Bicicletas são ferramentas para sustentabilidade urbana.

examples.text: A language is much more than just a communication tool.

examples.text: Humans aren't the only animals that use tools.

more.definition: Any physical device meant to ease or do a task.; Any piece of equipment used in a profession, such as a craftsman's.; Anything that aids someone to perform an operation; an instrument; a means.
more.etymology: From Middle English tool, tol, from Old English tōl (“tool, implement, instrument”, literally “that with which one prepares something”), perhaps borrowed from Old Norse tól, but at any rate ultimately from Proto-Germanic *tōlą (“that which is used in preparation, tool”), from Proto-Indo-European *dewh₂- (“to tie to, secure”), equivalent to taw (“to prepare”) + -le (agent suffix).

examples.text: Interlingua is a modern tool for international communication.

more.definition: A current (constantly changing) trend, favored for frivolous rather than practical, logical, or intellectual reasons.; Popular trends, especially in clothing; the industry that designs clothing and sometimes other related items.; A style or manner in which something is done.

Inherited from Middle English facioun, from Anglo-Norman fechoun (compare Jersey Norman faichon), variant of Old French faceon, fazon, façon (“fashion, form, make, outward appearance”), from Latin factiō (“a making”), from faciō (“do, make”); see fact. Doublet of faction.

examples.text: Mary is always up to date with the latest fashions.

examples.text: What's in fashion in Paris?

more.definition: To make, build or construct, especially in a crude or improvised way.
more.etymology: Old French façonbor. Inherited from Middle English facioun, from Anglo-Norman fechoun (compare Jersey Norman faichon), variant of Old French faceon, fazon, façon (“fashion, form, make, outward appearance”), from Latin factiō (“a making”), from faciō (“do, make”); see fact. Doublet of faction.

examples.text: He was satisfied with his new car.

more.etymology: Variant of Middle English bakke, of North Germanic origin (akin to Danish aftenbakke and Swedish nattbacka, both now dialectal). Displaced native Old English dreċċan, gremman.

translations.fr: L'éclair précède le tonnerre.
translations.pt: O relâmpago precede o trovão.

more.definition: The loud rumbling, cracking, or crashing sound caused by expansion of rapidly heated air around a lightning bolt.; A deep, rumbling noise resembling thunder.; An alarming or startling threat or denunciation.
more.etymology: From Middle English thunder, thonder, thundre, thonre, thunnere, þunre, from Old English þunor (“thunder”), from Proto-West Germanic *þunr, from Proto-Germanic *þunraz, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ten-, *(s)tenh₂- (“to thunder”). Compare astound, astonish, stun. Germanic cognates include West Frisian tonger, Dutch donder, German Donner, Old Norse Þórr (English Thor), Danish torden, Norwegian Nynorsk tore.

more.definition: To produce thunder; to sound, rattle, or roar, as a discharge of atmospheric electricity.; To make a noise like thunder.; To (make something) move very fast (with loud noise).
more.etymology: From Middle English thundren, from Old English þunrian (“to thunder”), from Proto-West Germanic *þunrōn, from Proto-Germanic *þunrōną (“to thunder”).

examples.text: My robot's name is Multi.

more.definition: Of water: containing salt, saline.; Treated with salt as a preservative; cured with salt, salted.; Of land, fields etc.: flooded by the sea.
more.etymology: PIE word *sḗh₂l From Middle English salt, from Old English sealt, from Proto-West Germanic *salt, from Proto-Germanic *saltą, from Proto-Indo-European *sḗh₂l (“salt”). Doublet of sal, salary, and salsa, all ultimately from Latin sāl (“salt”), which it superseded as the general term for "salt". Cognate with Dutch zout, German Salz, Danish, Faroese, Icelandic, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Swedish salt.

more.definition: A common substance, chemically consisting mainly of sodium chloride (NaCl), used extensively as a food ingredient, seasoning, condiment, and preservative.; One of the compounds formed from the reaction of an acid with a base, where a positive ion replaces a hydrogen of the acid.; A sailor (also old salt).

more.definition: To fly apart with sudden violent force; to blow up, to burst, to detonate, to go off.; To destroy with an explosion.; To make a violent or emotional outburst; to suddenly give expression to powerful and often negative or unpleasant emotion, especially anger.
