translations.fr: Elle me dit qu'elle voulait un chien de compagnie.
translations.pt: Ela me disse que queria ter um cachorro de estimação.

more.definition: An animal kept as a companion or otherwise for pleasure, rather than for some practical benefit or use.; Something kept as a companion, including inanimate objects.; One who is excessively loyal to a superior and receives preferential treatment.
more.etymology: Originally northern dialectal, from Scots pet (“an animal that has been tamed and is kept as a pet; a darling or favourite; a petted or spoiled child”), probably from Scottish Gaelic peata (“pet, tamed animal, spoiled child”), from Middle Irish petta, peta (“pet, lap-dog”), of uncertain origin, possibly from a pre-Indo-European substrate. Compare also peat (“pet, darling, woman”), which is likely not related.

examples.text: The girl has a rabbit as a pet.

translations.de: Das Mädchen hat ein Kaninchen als Haustier.
translations.fr: La jeune fille a un lapin comme animal de compagnie.
translations.pt: A garota tem um coelho como animal de estimação.

examples.text: Tom is not fond of pets.

translations.de: Tom mag keine Haustiere.
translations.fr: Tom n'aime pas les animaux de compagnie.
translations.pt: Tom não gosta de animais de estimação.

examples.text: The black cat purred, as if he was being petted.

translations.de: Die schwarze Katze hat geschnurrt, als ob man sie streicheln würde.
translations.fr: Le chat noir a ronronné, comme s'il était caressé.
translations.pt: O gato preto ronronou como se estivesse sendo acariciado.

examples.text: This is my neighbor's pet.

translations.de: Das ist das Haustier meines Nachbarn.
translations.fr: C'est l'animal de compagnie de mon voisin.
translations.pt: Este é o animal de estimação do meu vizinho.

more.definition: To stroke or fondle (an animal).; To stroke or fondle (another person) amorously.; To be petulant or upset; to have a problem with.
more.etymology: Originally northern dialectal, from Scots pet (“an animal that has been tamed and is kept as a pet; a darling or favourite; a petted or spoiled child”), probably from Scottish Gaelic peata (“pet, tamed animal, spoiled child”), from Middle Irish petta, peta (“pet, lap-dog”), of uncertain origin, possibly from a pre-Indo-European substrate. Compare also peat (“pet, darling, woman”), which is likely not related.

examples.text: The exit is on the left.

translations.de: Der Ausgang ist links.
translations.fr: La sortie est à gauche.
translations.pt: A saída está à esquerda.

examples.text: Excuse me, where's the exit?

translations.de: Entschuldigung, wo ist der Ausgang?
translations.fr: Excusez-moi, où est la sortie ?
translations.pt: Desculpe-me, onde fica a saída?

examples.text: Did you find the exit?

translations.de: Hast du den Ausgang gefunden?
translations.fr: Tu as trouvé la sortie ?
translations.pt: Você encontrou a saída?

examples.text: Is there another exit?

translations.de: Gibt es noch einen Ausgang?
translations.fr: Y a-t-il une autre issue ?
translations.pt: Tem outra saída?

more.definition: An act of going out or going away, or leaving; a departure.; The action of an actor leaving a scene or the stage.; An opening or passage through which one can go from inside a place (such as a building, a room, or a vehicle) to the outside; an egress.
more.etymology: Latin exitusder. From Middle English exit, from Latin exitus (“departure, going out; way by which one may go out, egress; (figuratively) conclusion, termination; (figuratively) death; income, revenue”), from exeō (“to depart, exit; to avoid, evade; (figuratively) to escape; of time: to expire, run out”) + -tus (suffix forming action nouns from verbs).

examples.text: Where's the exit?

translations.de: Wo ist der Ausgang?
translations.fr: Où est la sortie ?
translations.pt: Onde fica a saída?

examples.text: We missed the exit.

translations.de: Wir haben die Abfahrt verpasst.
translations.fr: Nous avons loupé la sortie.
translations.pt: Perdemos a saída.

examples.text: Where is the exit?

translations.de: Wo ist der Ausgang?
translations.fr: Où est la sortie ?
translations.pt: Onde está a saída?

examples.text: Take the emergency exit!

translations.de: Nehmen Sie den Notausgang!
translations.fr: Prenez la sortie de secours !
translations.pt: Vá pela saída de emergência!

more.definition: To go out or go away from a place or situation; to depart, to leave.; To leave a scene or depart from a stage.; To depart from life; to die.
more.etymology: Latin exitusder. From Middle English exit, from Latin exitus (“departure, going out; way by which one may go out, egress; (figuratively) conclusion, termination; (figuratively) death; income, revenue”), from exeō (“to depart, exit; to avoid, evade; (figuratively) to escape; of time: to expire, run out”) + -tus (suffix forming action nouns from verbs).

examples.text: I did my best to prevent this.

translations.de: Ich habe mein Möglichstes getan, um das zu verhindern.
translations.fr: J'ai fait de mon mieux pour éviter ceci.
translations.pt: Fiz o que pude para evitar isso.

examples.text: Sickness prevented him from going out.

translations.de: Wegen Krankheit konnte er nicht ausgehen.
translations.fr: Il n'a pas pu sortir à cause de la maladie.
translations.pt: Uma enfermidade o prevenia de sair.

examples.text: How can I prevent this from happening?

translations.de: Wie kann ich verhindern, dass das geschieht?
translations.fr: Comment puis-je en prévenir l'occurrence ?
translations.pt: Como eu posso evitar que isto aconteça?

examples.text: Your navel-gazing prevents you from seeing what's really important.

translations.de: Euer Nabelschauertum hindert euch daran, zu sehen, was wirklich wichtig ist.
translations.fr: Votre nombrilisme vous empêche de voir ce qui est vraiment important.
translations.pt: A tua fixação com o próprio umbigo impede-te de ver o que é realmente importante.

more.definition: To stop (an outcome); to keep from (doing something).
more.etymology: From Middle English preventen (“anticipate”), from Latin praeventus, perfect passive participle of praeveniō (“to anticipate”), from prae (“before”) + veniō (“to come”).

examples.text: I have no intention of staying.

translations.de: Ich habe nicht die Absicht zu bleiben.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas l'intention de rester.
translations.pt: Não tenho intenção de ficar.

examples.text: What are your intentions?

translations.de: Was sind deine Absichten?
translations.fr: Quelles sont vos intentions ?
translations.pt: Quais são as suas intenções?

examples.text: That wasn't my intention.

translations.de: Das war nicht meine Absicht.
translations.fr: Ce n'était pas mon intention.
translations.pt: Não era essa a minha intenção.

examples.text: Hell is paved with good intentions.

translations.de: Die Hölle ist mit guten Vorsätzen gepflastert.
translations.fr: L'enfer est pavé de bonnes intentions.
translations.pt: O inferno está cheio de boas intenções.

more.definition: A course of action that a person intends to follow.; A goal or purpose.; A process of the healing of a wound.
more.etymology: Latin intentiōlbor. Old French entencionder. Middle French ententionbor. From Middle English entencioun, intention, from Old French entencion, from Latin intentiō, intentiōnem. Compare intent. Equivalent to intent + -ion.

examples.text: I have no intention of telling you the result.

translations.de: Ich habe nicht die Absicht, Ihnen das Ergebnis mitzuteilen.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas l'intention de vous faire part du résultat.
translations.pt: Não tenho intenção de te dizer o resultado.

examples.text: We judge ourselves by our intentions and others by their actions.

translations.de: Wir beurteilen uns selbst nach unseren Absichten, andere aber nach ihren Taten.
translations.fr: Nous nous jugeons de par nos intentions tandis que nous jugeons les autres de par leurs actions.
translations.pt: Nós nos julgamos por nossas intenções e os outros por suas ações.

more.definition: To intend.
more.etymology: Latin intentiōlbor. Old French entencionder. Middle French ententionbor. From Middle English entencioun, intention, from Old French entencion, from Latin intentiō, intentiōnem. Compare intent. Equivalent to intent + -ion.

examples.text: The brain is a neural network that updates itself with each learned task.

translations.de: Das Gehirn ist ein neuronales Netz, das sich bei jeder erlernten Aufgabe selbst aktualisiert.
translations.fr: Le cerveau est un réseau de neurones qui se met à jour à chaque tâche apprise.
translations.pt: O cérebro é uma rede neural que se atualiza a cada tarefa aprendida.

examples.text: This railway station is an important hub in the local transport network.

translations.de: Dieser Bahnhof ist ein wichtiger Knotenpunkt im Nahverkehrsnetz.

examples.text: A network of railroads spreads all over Japan.

translations.fr: Un réseau de chemin de fer s'étend sur tout le Japon.
translations.pt: Uma rede de trilhos de trem está espalhada sobre todo o Japão.

more.definition: Any interconnected group or system.; A set of people with sociocultural connections to one another; especially, such a set consisting of occupational or business connections.; A group of affiliated television stations that broadcast common programs from a parent company.
more.etymology: From net + work; the nonliteral sense and its subsenses are extended from the literal sense; they are now the dominant senses. Cognate with German Netzwerk.

translations.fr: Gloire à l'Ukraine !
translations.pt: Glória à Ucrânia!

translations.de: Seine mutigen Taten brachten ihm Ruhm.
translations.fr: Ses actes de bravoures lui apportèrent la gloire.

examples.text: He announced the next singer.

translations.de: Er kündigte den nächsten Sänger an.
translations.fr: Il annonça le chanteur suivant.
translations.pt: Ele anunciou o próximo cantor.

examples.text: He officially announced himself as a candidate.

translations.fr: Il a officiellement annoncé sa candidature.
translations.pt: Ele anunciou oficialmente sua candidatura.

more.definition: To give public notice of, especially for the first time; to make known.; To pronounce; to declare by judicial sentence.; To act as announcer for (an event, usually sports).
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Latin annūntiōder. Old French anoncierder. From Old French anoncier, from Latin annūntiāre, from ad + nūntiō (“report, relate”), from nūntius (“messenger, bearer of news”). See nuncio. Doublet of annunciate. See also an-.

translations.de: Der Wissenschaftler suchte in dem Tal nach Dinosaurierknochen.
translations.fr: Le scientifique cherchait dans la vallée pour des os de dinosaures.
translations.pt: O cientista pesquisou pelos ossos dos dinossauros no vale.

more.definition: An elongated depression cast between hills or mountains, often with a river flowing through it.; An area which drains itself into a river.; Any structure resembling one, e.g. the interior angle formed by the intersection of two sloping roof planes.
more.etymology: From Middle English valeye, valey, from Anglo-Norman valey, Old French valee (compare French vallée), from Latin vallēs/vallis. Doublet of vlei and vly. Displaced native dene, from dene and partially displaced native dale, from dæl.

examples.text: Without music, the world is a valley of tears.

translations.de: Ohne Musik ist die Welt ein Jammertal.
translations.fr: Sans musique, le monde est une vallée de larmes.

examples.text: How beautiful the valleys are in spring!

examples.text: The scientist searched for the bones of the dinosaurs in the valley.

examples.text: Communism will never be reached in my lifetime.

translations.de: Der Kommunismus wird nie erreicht werden, solange ich lebe.
translations.fr: Le communisme ne sera jamais atteint de mon vivant.
translations.pt: O comunismo nunca será atingido enquanto eu viver.

examples.text: Schubert was little known in his lifetime.

more.definition: The duration of the life of someone or something.; A long period of time.

examples.text: The elephant is liked by little children.

translations.de: Der Elefant wird von kleinen Kindern gemocht.
translations.fr: Cet éléphant est aimé des jeunes enfants.
translations.pt: As criancinhas gostam do elefante.

examples.text: The misfortune of the ants makes the elephants laugh.

translations.de: Das Unglück der Ameisen macht die Elefanten lachen.
translations.fr: Le malheur des fourmis fait le rire des éléphants.
translations.pt: Os elefantes acham graça do infortúnio das formigas.

examples.text: What is the elephant's age?

translations.de: Wie alt ist der Elefant?
translations.fr: Quel est l'âge de l'éléphant ?
translations.pt: Qual é a idade do elefante?

examples.text: Have you ever seen an elephant?

more.definition: A large mammal of the family Elephantidae in the order Proboscidea, having a trunk, and native to Africa and Asia.; Anything huge and ponderous.; Synonym of elephant paper.
more.etymology: From Middle English elefant, elefaunt, from Old French elefant, elefan, olifant, re-latinized in Middle French as elephant, from Latin elephantus, from Ancient Greek ἐλέφᾱς (eléphās) (gen. ἐλέφαντος (eléphantos)). Believed to be derived from an Afroasiatic form such as Proto-Berber *eḷu (“elephant”) (compare Tamahaq êlu, Tamasheq alu) or Egyptian ꜣbw (“elephant; ivory”). More at ivory.

examples.text: I don't have anything to declare.

examples.text: The city council elected Marcus deputy mayor.

more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English counseil (“meeting, conference, commune”), from Old French conseil (“advice, deliberation, thought”), from Latin cōnsilium (“plan, intention, design, purpose”), from cōnsulō (“consult, seek counsel from, take counsel from, deliberate, reflect”), from Proto-Indo-European *selh₁- (“take, grab”).

examples.text: The function of most genes remains a mystery.

translations.fr: Le rôle de la plupart des gènes demeure un mystère.

translations.fr: Certaines maladies sont causées par un gène défectueux.

examples.text: Genes consist of a specific sequence of DNA.

translations.fr: Les gènes consistent en une séquence particulière d'ADN.

examples.text: If you could choose the genes for your children, would you?

translations.fr: Si vous pouviez choisir les gènes de votre enfant, le feriez-vous ?

more.definition: A theoretical unit of heredity of living organisms which may take several values and (in principle) predetermines a precise trait of an organism's form (phenotype), such as hair color.; A segment of DNA or RNA from a cell's or an organism's genome, that may take several forms and thus parameterizes a phenomenon, such as (often) the structure of a protein.
more.etymology: From German Gen, from Ancient Greek γενεά (geneá, “generation, descent”), from the aorist infinitive of γίγνομαι (gígnomai, “to come into being”). Coined by Danish botanist Wilhelm Ludwig Johannsen in 1909, in a German-language publication, from the last syllable of pangene.

examples.text: The Japanese art of flower arrangement is called ikebana.

examples.text: He pressed his pants.

examples.text: You shouldn't have signed a confession.

more.definition: A person, usually undead, animated by unnatural forces (such as magic), with no soul or will of his or her own, typically being slow, obedient, and harmless unless directed to be harmful.; A dead person, reanimated through some fictional agency as a fungus, virus, or the like, that has an insatiable desire to eat living humans, typically depicted as aggressive, fast moving, and infectious.; An apathetic or slow-witted person.
more.etymology: First attested in the 18th century. Partially through Louisiana Creole zombi (“zombie; ghost”), Haitian Creole zonbi (“zombie”), and French zombi (“zombie”). Compare Kongo nzambi (“god”), zumbi (“fetish”), and Kimbundu nzumbi (“ghost”) (see Portuguese zumbi, Sranan Tongo dyumbi), and Caribbean folklore's jumbie (“a spirit or demon”).

more.definition: Mental acceptance of a claim as true.; Faith or trust in the reality of something; often based upon one's own reasoning, trust in a claim, desire of actuality, and/or evidence considered.; Something believed.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *lewbʰ-der. From Middle English bileve, from Old English lēafa, from Proto-West Germanic *laubu from Proto-Germanic *laubō. Compare German Glaube (“faith, belief”). The replacement of final /v/ with /f/ is due to the analogy of noun-verb pairs with /f/ in the noun but /v/ in the verb, creating a pair belief : believe on the model of e.g. grief : grieve or proof : prove.

examples.text: I have lived here for thirty years.

translations.de: Ich habe dreißig Jahre lang hier gelebt.
translations.fr: J'ai vécu ici pendant trente ans.
translations.pt: Eu vivi aqui durante trinta anos.

examples.text: How do you say XXX in your language?

translations.de: Wie sagt man XXX in deiner Sprache?
translations.fr: Comment dites-vous XXX dans votre langue ?
translations.pt: Como se diz XXX na sua língua?

examples.text: He is in his early thirties.

translations.de: Er ist Anfang Dreißig.
translations.fr: Il est au début de la trentaine.
translations.pt: Ele tem uns trinta e poucos anos.

examples.text: February does not have thirty days.

translations.de: Der Februar hat keine dreißig Tage.
translations.fr: Février n'a pas trente jours.
translations.pt: Fevereiro não tem trinta dias.

more.definition: A rack of thirty beers.; A commercial lasting 30 seconds.
more.etymology: From Middle English thirty, metathetic alternant of thritty, from Old English þrītiġ, þrittiġ (“thirty”), from Proto-Germanic *þrīz tigiwiz (“thirty”, literally “three tens”), equivalent to three + -ty. Cognate with Scots therty, tretty (“thirty”), West Frisian tritich (“thirty”), Dutch dertig (“thirty”), German dreißig (“thirty”).

examples.text: Did you say thirteen or thirty?

translations.de: Hast du „dreizehn“ oder „dreißig“ gesagt?
translations.fr: Vous avez dit treize ou trente ?
translations.pt: Disseste treze ou trinta?

examples.text: Tom immigrated to Australia when he was thirty.

translations.de: Tom ist mit dreißig nach Australien eingewandert.
translations.fr: Tom a immigré en Australie lorsqu'il avait trente ans.
translations.pt: Tom imigrou para a Austrália aos trinta anos.

examples.text: You said that thirty minutes ago.

translations.de: Das hast du schon vor einer halben Stunde gesagt.
translations.fr: Tu as dit ça il y a une demi-heure.
translations.pt: Você disse isso trinta minutos atrás.

examples.text: I woke up thirty minutes ago.

translations.de: Ich bin vor einer halben Stunde aufgewacht.
translations.fr: Je me suis réveillé il y a trente minutes.
translations.pt: Eu acordei há trinta minutos.

more.definition: The cardinal number occurring after twenty-nine and before thirty-one, represented in Arabic numerals as 30.
more.etymology: From Middle English thirty, metathetic alternant of thritty, from Old English þrītiġ, þrittiġ (“thirty”), from Proto-Germanic *þrīz tigiwiz (“thirty”, literally “three tens”), equivalent to three + -ty. Cognate with Scots therty, tretty (“thirty”), West Frisian tritich (“thirty”), Dutch dertig (“thirty”), German dreißig (“thirty”).

examples.text: And thus the lion fell in love with the ewe.

translations.de: Und so verliebte sich der Löwe in das Schaf.
translations.fr: Et ainsi le lion tomba-t-il amoureux de la brebis.
translations.pt: E deste modo o leão se apaixonou pela ovelha.

examples.text: Thus spoke Zarathustra.

translations.de: Also sprach Zarathustra.
translations.fr: Ainsi parlait Zoroastre.
translations.pt: Assim falava Zaratustra.

examples.text: Quantum physics thus reveals a basic oneness of the universe.

translations.de: Auf diese Weise deckt die Quantenphysik eine grundlegende Einheitlichkeit des Weltalls auf.
translations.fr: La physique quantique révèle ainsi une unité fondamentale de l'univers.
translations.pt: A física quântica revela, assim, uma unidade básica do universo.

examples.text: Does anyone have any questions thus far?

translations.de: Hat bisher jemand Fragen?
translations.fr: Jusqu'ici, est-ce que quelqu'un a des questions ?

more.definition: In this way or manner.; As a result.
more.etymology: From Middle English thus, þus, from Old English þus (“thus, in this way, as follows, in this manner, to this extent”), from Proto-West Germanic *þus (“so, thus”), perhaps originally from a variant of the instrumental form of this, related to Old English þȳs (“by this, with this”), Old Saxon thius (“by this, with this”).

examples.text: Are you trying to blackmail me?

translations.fr: Vous essayez de me faire chanter ?
translations.pt: Estão tentando me chantagear?

examples.text: Tom is vulnerable to blackmail.

translations.de: Tom ist erpreßbar.
translations.fr: Tom est sujet au chantage.

examples.text: This is blackmail.

translations.de: Das ist Erpressung!
translations.fr: C'est du chantage.

examples.text: That's blackmail.

translations.fr: C'est du chantage.
translations.pt: Isso é chantagem.

more.definition: The extortion of money or favors by threats of public accusation, critique, or exposure.; Compromising material that can be used to extort someone.; A type of roleplay where the submissive shares information that may be exploited by the dominant.
more.etymology: From black + mail (“a piece of money”). Compare Middle English blak rente (“a type of blackmail levied by Irish chieftains”). The word is variously derived from the tribute paid by English and Scottish border dwellers to border reivers in return for immunity from raids and other harassment.

examples.text: She is being blackmailed by him.

translations.de: Sie wird von ihm erpresst.
translations.fr: Il exerce sur elle du chantage.
translations.pt: Ela está sendo chantageada por ele.

examples.text: Somebody is blackmailing me.

translations.de: Es erpresst mich einer.
translations.fr: Quelqu'un me fait chanter.
translations.pt: Alguém está me chantageando.

examples.text: She was blackmailed by him.

translations.de: Sie wurde von ihm erpresst.
translations.fr: Il la faisait chanter.
translations.pt: Ela foi chantageada por ele.

examples.text: I'm being blackmailed.

translations.de: Ich werde erpresst.
translations.fr: On me fait chanter.
translations.pt: Estou sendo chantageado.

more.definition: To extort money or favors from (a person) by exciting fears of injury other than bodily harm, such as injury to reputation, distress of mind, false accusation, etc.; To speak ill of someone; to defame someone.
more.etymology: From black + mail (“a piece of money”). Compare Middle English blak rente (“a type of blackmail levied by Irish chieftains”). The word is variously derived from the tribute paid by English and Scottish border dwellers to border reivers in return for immunity from raids and other harassment.

examples.text: You absolutely must not lick the floor.

translations.de: Du darfst auf keinen Fall über den Boden lecken.
translations.fr: Vous ne devez surtout pas lécher le sol.

examples.text: He arse-licks his boss.

translations.de: Er schleimt sich bei seinem Chef ein.
translations.fr: Il lèche le cul de son patron.

examples.text: Cats often lick each other.

translations.de: Katzen belecken sich häufig gegenseitig.
translations.pt: Os gatos costumam lamber uns aos outros.

examples.text: Men lick their lips when they look at her.

translations.fr: Les hommes se lèchent les babines quand ils la regardent.
translations.pt: Os homens lambem os beiços quando olham para ela.

more.definition: The act of licking; a stroke of the tongue.; The amount of some substance obtainable with a single lick.; A quick and careless application of anything, as if by a stroke of the tongue.
more.etymology: From Middle English likken, from Old English liccian, from Proto-West Germanic *likkōn, from Proto-Germanic *likkōną (“to lick”), from Proto-Indo-European *leyǵʰ- (“to lick”). Sense evolution towards violence unclear; not paralleled in any other Germanic language.

examples.text: Kissing a person who smokes is like licking an ashtray.

translations.de: Jemanden, der raucht, zu küssen ist so, wie an einem Aschenbecher zu lecken.
translations.fr: Embrasser une personne qui fume, c'est comme lécher un cendrier.
translations.pt: Beijar uma pessoa que fuma é como lamber um cinzeiro.

examples.text: He licked his lips.

translations.de: Er leckte sich die Lippen.
translations.fr: Il se lécha les lèvres.
translations.pt: Ele lambeu os lábios.

examples.text: Mary is licking an ice cream cone.

translations.de: Maria schleckt an einer Eiswaffel.
translations.fr: Marie lèche un cornet de crème glacée.
translations.pt: Mary está lambendo uma casquinha de sorvete.

examples.text: The spoon the dog licked is made of plastic.

translations.de: Der Löffel, den der Hund abgeleckt hat, ist aus Plastik.
translations.fr: La cuillère que le chien a léché est à plastique.
translations.pt: A colher que o cachorro lambeu é de plástico.

more.definition: To stroke with the tongue.; To lap; to take in with the tongue.; To perform cunnilingus.
more.etymology: From Middle English likken, from Old English liccian, from Proto-West Germanic *likkōn, from Proto-Germanic *likkōną (“to lick”), from Proto-Indo-European *leyǵʰ- (“to lick”). Sense evolution towards violence unclear; not paralleled in any other Germanic language.

examples.text: The penis entered the vagina.

translations.de: Der Penis drang in die Vagina ein.
translations.fr: Le pénis a pénétré le vagin.
translations.pt: O pênis entrou na vagina.

examples.text: I have a big penis.

translations.de: Ich habe einen großen Penis.
translations.fr: J’ai un gros pénis.

examples.text: Tom has a large penis.

translations.fr: Tom a une grosse bite.
translations.pt: O Tom tem um pênis grande.

examples.text: The penis is one of the male reproductive organs.

translations.de: Der Penis ist eines der männlichen Geschlechtsorgane.
translations.pt: O pênis é um dos órgãos reprodutores masculinos.

more.definition: The male erectile reproductive organ used for sexual intercourse that in the human male and other placental mammals is also used for urination; the tubular portion of the external male genitalia (excluding the scrotum).; A similar erectile sexual organ present in the cloacas of male amniotes.
more.etymology: Latin pēnislbor. Learned borrowing from Latin pēnis, from Proto-Italic *peznis, from Proto-Indo-European *pes-ni-s, from *pes- (“penis”). First attested in the late 17th century. Displaced native English pintle, tarse, pillicock.

examples.text: Wow! What a big box!

translations.de: Meine Güte! Was für eine große Kiste!
translations.fr: Ouf ! Quelle grosse boîte !
translations.pt: Nossa! Que caixa grande!

examples.text: He wooed them with promises of higher wages.

translations.de: Er lockte sie mit besserem Lohn.
translations.fr: Il les a attirés avec des promesses de salaires plus élevés.

examples.text: Wow, it's pretty cold today.

translations.de: Brr, ist das arschkalt heute.
translations.fr: Brrr, il fait plutôt froid aujourd'hui.
translations.pt: Poxa, está muito frio hoje.

examples.text: Oh wow, you are fast.

translations.de: Potzblitz, bist du schnell!
translations.fr: Mon Dieu, tu es rapide.
translations.pt: Caramba, você é rápido.

more.definition: To endeavor to gain someone's affection or support.; Often of a man, to try to persuade (someone) to be in an amorous relationship with.; To court solicitously; to invite with importunity; to solicit in love.
more.etymology: From Middle English wowen, woȝen, from Old English wōgian (“to woo, court, marry”), of uncertain origin. Cognate with Scots wow (“to woo”). Perhaps related to Old English wōg, wōh (“bending, crookedness”), in the specific sense of "bend or incline (some)one toward oneself".

examples.text: I need people I can rely on.

translations.de: Ich brauche Leute, auf die ich mich verlassen kann.
translations.fr: J'ai besoin de personnes sur lesquelles je peux compter.
translations.pt: Preciso de gente com quem possa contar.

examples.text: I relied on Tom.

translations.de: Ich verließ mich auf Tom.
translations.fr: Je me suis reposé sur Tom.
translations.pt: Eu confiei no Tomás.

examples.text: You can always rely on me.

translations.de: Du kannst dich stets auf mich verlassen.
translations.fr: Tu peux toujours compter sur moi.
translations.pt: Você sempre pode confiar em mim.

examples.text: He's a man you can rely on.

translations.de: Er ist ein Mann, auf den du rechnen kannst.
translations.fr: C'est un homme sur qui tu peux compter.
translations.pt: Ele é um homem com quem você pode contar.

more.definition: To trust; to have confidence in.; To depend; to be dependent upon.; To be intellectually contingent from; to stem from.
more.etymology: From Middle English relien, from Old French relier (“fasten, attach, rally, oblige”), from Latin religo (“fasten, bind fast”), from re- + ligo.

examples.text: May I open the curtain?

translations.de: Kann ich den Vorhang aufmachen?
translations.fr: Puis-je tirer le rideau ?
translations.pt: Posso abrir a cortina?

examples.text: Tom opened the curtains.

translations.de: Tom zog die Vorhänge auf.
translations.fr: Tom a ouvert les rideaux.
translations.pt: Tom abriu as cortinas.

examples.text: The curtain caught on fire.

translations.de: Der Vorhang hatte Feuer gefangen.
translations.fr: Le rideau prit feu.
translations.pt: A cortina pegou fogo.

examples.text: These new curtains don't go well with the rugs.

translations.de: Diese neuen Gardinen passen nicht gut zu den Teppichen.
translations.fr: Ces nouveaux rideaux ne sont pas bien assortis aux tapis.
translations.pt: Estas cortinas novas não combinam com os tapetes.

more.definition: A piece of cloth covering a window, bed, etc. to offer privacy and keep out light.; A similar piece of cloth that separates the audience and the stage in a theater.; The beginning of a show; the moment the curtain rises.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English curtine, from Old French cortine, from Late Latin cōrtīna (“curtain”), a calque from Ancient Greek.

examples.text: I forgot to close the curtains.

translations.de: Ich habe vergessen, die Vorhänge zuzuziehen.
translations.fr: J'ai oublié de fermer les rideaux.
translations.pt: Esqueci-me de fechar as cortinas.

examples.text: Let's hide behind the curtain.

translations.de: Verstecken wir uns hinter dem Vorhang!
translations.fr: Cachons-nous derrière le rideau.
translations.pt: Escondamo-nos atrás da cortina.

examples.text: We were changing the curtains.

translations.de: Wir waren dabei, die Vorhänge zu wechseln.
translations.fr: Nous étions en train de changer les rideaux.
translations.pt: Estávamos mudando as cortinas.

examples.text: Can I open the curtain?

translations.de: Kann ich den Vorhang aufmachen?
translations.fr: Est-ce que je peux ouvrir le rideau ?
translations.pt: Posso abrir a cortina?

more.definition: To cover (a window) with a curtain; to hang curtains.; To hide, cover or separate as if by a curtain.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English curtine, from Old French cortine, from Late Latin cōrtīna (“curtain”), a calque from Ancient Greek.

examples.text: The beach was lined with palm trees.

translations.de: Den Strand säumten Palmen.
translations.fr: La plage était bordée de palmiers.

examples.text: Her palms were sweaty.

translations.de: Sie hatte schwitzige Hände.
translations.pt: As palmas dela estavam suadas.

examples.text: Show the palm of your hand!

translations.fr: Montre ta paume de main !
translations.pt: Mostre a palma da sua mão!

examples.text: I'm interested in palm reading.

translations.de: Ich interessiere mich fürs Handlesen.
translations.fr: Je m'intéresse à la lecture des lignes de la main.

more.definition: Any of various evergreen trees from the family Palmae or Arecaceae, which are mainly found in the tropics.; A branch or leaf of the palm, anciently borne or worn as a symbol of victory or rejoicing.; Triumph; victory.
more.etymology: From Middle English palme, from Old English palm, palma (“palm-tree, palm-branch”), from Latin palma (“palm-tree, palm-branch, palm of the hand”), from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥h₂meh₂, *pl̥h₂emeh₂ (“palm of the hand”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat”). Cognate with Dutch palm, German Palme, Danish palme, Icelandic pálmur (“palm”).

examples.text: We are climbing the palm tree.

translations.de: Wir klettern auf die Palme.
translations.pt: Estamos subindo na palmeira.

examples.text: I am interested in palm reading.

translations.de: Ich interessiere mich fürs Handlesen.
translations.fr: Je m'intéresse à la lecture des lignes de la main.

examples.text: I usually use hearts of palm in my recipes.

translations.fr: J'utilise en général des cœurs de palmier dans mes recettes.
translations.pt: Eu costumo usar palmito em minhas receitas.

examples.text: Tom is planting a palm tree in his backyard.

translations.de: Tom pflanzt in seinem Hinterhof eine Palme.
translations.fr: Tom plante un palmier dans son arrière-cour.

more.definition: To hold or conceal something in the palm of the hand, e.g., for an act of sleight of hand or to steal something.; To hold something without bending the fingers significantly.; To move something with the palm of the hand.
more.etymology: From Middle English palme, paume, from Old French palme, paulme, paume (“palm of the hand, ball, tennis”), from Latin palma (“palm of the hand, hand-breadth”), from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥h₂(e)meh₂ (“palm of the hand”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat”). Doublet of palmo, palma, and pam.

examples.text: Those missiles are one hundred percent effective.

translations.de: Diese Raketen sind hundertprozentig wirksam.
translations.pt: Esses mísseis são cem por cento eficazes.

examples.text: We have guided missiles and misguided men.

translations.de: Wir haben ferngesteuerte Geschosse und irregeleitete Menschen.
translations.fr: Nous avons des missiles guidés et des hommes égarés.

examples.text: Everyone in Hawaii received an emergency alert that a ballistic missile was inbound.

translations.de: An alle auf Hawaii erging die Warnung, dass eine ballistische Rakete auf dem Weg sei.
translations.pt: Todas as pessoas no Havai receberam um alerta de emergência de que um míssil balístico se aproximava.

examples.text: The Cuban Missile Crisis brought the world to the brink of nuclear war.

translations.de: Die kubanische Raketenkrise brachte die Welt an den Rand eines atomaren Krieges.
translations.fr: La crise des missiles de Cuba a placé le monde au bord de la guerre nucléaire.

more.definition: Any object used as a weapon by being thrown or fired through the air, such as stone, arrow or bullet.; A self-propelled projectile whose trajectory can be adjusted after it is launched.
more.etymology: From Latin missile (“thrown weapon, projectile”), neuter of missilis (“throwable, capable of being thrown”), from mittere (“to send”). From 1611. Compare Middle French missile (“projectile”), from 1636.

examples.text: What's the minimum wage in Australia?

translations.de: Was ist in Australien der Mindestlohn?

translations.pt: Quanto é o salário mínimo na Austrália?

examples.text: In most countries, teachers do not receive high wages.

translations.de: In den meisten Ländern beziehen Lehrer kein hohes Gehalt.
translations.fr: Dans la plupart des pays, les enseignants ne perçoivent pas de salaires élevés.

translations.pt: O salário do pecado é a morte.

more.definition: An amount of money paid to a worker for a specified quantity of work, usually calculated on an hourly basis and expressed in an amount of money per hour.
more.etymology: From Middle English wage, from Anglo-Norman wage, from Old Northern French wage, a northern variant of Old French gauge, guage (whence modern French gage), Medieval Latin wadium, from Frankish *waddī (cognate with Old English wedd), from Proto-Germanic *wadją (“pledge”), from Proto-Indo-European *wedʰ- (“to pledge, redeem a pledge”). Akin to Old Norse veðja (“to pledge”), Gothic 𐍅𐌰𐌳𐌹 (wadi), Dutch wedde.

translations.de: Was ist in Australien der Mindestlohn?
translations.fr: Quel est le salaire minimum en Australie ?

examples.text: In most countries, teachers do not receive high wages.

translations.fr: Dans la plupart des pays, les enseignants ne perçoivent pas de salaires élevés.
translations.pt: Na maioria dos países, os professores não recebem altos salários.

translations.de: Denn der Tod ist der Sünde Sold.
translations.fr: Le salaire du péché, c'est la mort.
translations.pt: O salário do pecado é a morte.

more.definition: To conduct or carry out (a war or other contest).; To adventure, or lay out, for hire or reward; to hire out.
more.etymology: From Middle English wagen (“to pledge”), from Anglo-Norman, Old Northern French wagier, a northern variant of Old French guagier (whence modern French gager), itself either from guage or from a derivative of Frankish *waddī, possibly through a Vulgar Latin intermediate *wadiō from *wadium (see the noun above). See Medieval Latin wadiō and wadium for more.

examples.text: Africa is the cradle of humanity.

translations.de: Afrika ist die Wiege der Menschheit.
translations.fr: L'Afrique est le berceau de l'humanité.
translations.pt: A África é o berço da humanidade.

examples.text: War is a crime against humanity.

translations.de: Krieg ist ein Verbrechen gegen die Menschheit.
translations.fr: La guerre est un crime contre l'humanité.
translations.pt: A guerra é um crime contra a humanidade.

examples.text: Literature teaches us about humanity.

translations.de: Die Literatur bringt uns Dinge über die Menschheit bei.
translations.fr: La littérature nous enseigne sur l'humanité.
translations.pt: A literatura nos ensina sobre a humanidade.

examples.text: You're the last hope for humanity.

translations.de: Ihr seid der Menschheit letzte Hoffnung.
translations.fr: Tu es le dernier espoir de l'humanité.
translations.pt: Você é a última esperança da humanidade.

more.definition: Humankind; human beings as a group.; The human condition or nature.; The quality of being benevolent; humane traits of character; humane qualities or aspects.
more.etymology: Inherited from Middle English humanyte, humanite, humanitye, from Old French humanité, from Latin hūmānitās. By surface analysis, human or humane + -ity. Partly displaced mankind, from Old English mancynn (literally “human race”).

examples.text: Ding is playing on the computer.

translations.fr: Ding joue sur ordinateur.
translations.pt: Ding está jogando no computador.

examples.text: What a ding-a-ling!

translations.fr: Quel folingue !

examples.text: Have you ever played ding-dong ditch?
Ding, ding! It's the right answer!

more.definition: Very minor damage caused by being struck; a small dent or chip.; A rejection.; The high-pitched resonant sound of a bell.
more.etymology: From Middle English dingen, dyngen (strong verb), from Old English *dingan (“to ding”), from Proto-West Germanic *dingwan, from Proto-Germanic *dingwaną (“to beat”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰen- (“to beat, push”).

examples.text: Ding is playing on the computer.

translations.fr: Ding joue sur ordinateur.
translations.pt: Ding está jogando no computador.

examples.text: The bell dinged, and the doors opened.
Tobias was playing ding-dong ditch.
Jonas never went ding-dong ditching after that.

more.definition: To hit or strike.; To dash; to throw violently.; To inflict minor damage upon, especially by hitting or striking.
more.etymology: From Middle English dingen, dyngen (strong verb), from Old English *dingan (“to ding”), from Proto-West Germanic *dingwan, from Proto-Germanic *dingwaną (“to beat”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰen- (“to beat, push”).

examples.text: Please say the alphabet in reverse.

translations.de: Bitte, sage das Alphabet rückwärts auf.
translations.fr: Dis l'alphabet à l'envers, je te prie !
translations.pt: Por favor, diga o alfabeto ao contrário.

examples.text: He did the reverse of what I asked.

translations.de: Er hat das Gegenteil von dem getan, worum ich ihn gebeten hatte.
translations.fr: Il a fait l'inverse de ce que j'ai demandé.
translations.pt: Ele fez o contrário do que eu pedi.

examples.text: Put the car in reverse.

translations.de: Parke rückwärts ein.
translations.fr: Mets la voiture en marche arrière.

examples.text: It's time to reverse the trend.

translations.fr: Il est temps d'inverser la tendance.
translations.pt: É hora de reverter a tendência.

more.definition: Opposite, contrary; going in the opposite direction.; Pertaining to engines, vehicle movement etc. moving in a direction opposite to the usual direction.; To be in the non-default position; to be set for the lesser-used route.

more.definition: A person living on adjacent or nearby land; a person situated adjacently or nearby; anything (of the same type of thing as the subject) in an adjacent or nearby position.; One who is near in sympathy or confidence.; A fellow human being.

more.definition: A flying insect of the order Lepidoptera, distinguished from moths by their diurnal activity and generally brighter colouring.; The imago (final form) of such an insect, consisting usually of a long body with large flat wings, as opposed to earlier instars such as caterpillar or pupa.; A use of surgical tape, cut into thin strips and placed across an open wound to hold it closed.

more.definition: To cut (food) almost entirely in half and spread the halves apart, in a shape suggesting the wings of a butterfly.; To cut strips of surgical tape or plasters into thin strips, and place across (a gaping wound) to close it.; To cause events after the point of divergence to not happen as they did in real history, and people conceived after the point of divergence to not exist in recognizable form, due to the random variations introduced by the butterfly effect.
more.etymology: Ancient Greek βούτῡρον (boútūron)bor. Latin būtȳrumbor. Proto-Germanic *fleuganądeverb. From Middle English buterflie, butturflye, boterflye, from Old English buterflēoge, equivalent to butter + fly. Cognate with Dutch botervlieg, German Butterfliege (“butterfly”).

more.definition: In full primary radar: a method of detecting a distant object and determining its position, velocity, or other characteristics by analysing radio waves (usually microwaves) which are sent towards the object and which reflect off its surfaces; also, the field of study of this method.; In full secondary radar: a method of detecting a distant object and determining its position, velocity, or other characteristics by analysing signals transmitted by the object in response to radio waves sent towards the object.; Often preceded by a descriptive word: a system using one of the above detection methods, differentiated by configuration or platform, frequency, power, and other technical attributes.
more.etymology: Latin radiusder. Proto-Indo-European *kʷelh₁-der. Ancient Greek τῆλε (têle)lbor. French télégraphebor. Old French -ieder. English radiotelegraphyclip. Latin dētēctiōbor. Proto-Indo-European *(H)rek-der. Proto-Indo-European *h₃reǵ-der. Proto-Germanic *rinkanąder. Latin -ereinflu. Old French rengierbor. The noun is derived from RADAR by anacronymic evolution.

more.definition: An incident or event that disgraces or damages the reputation of the persons or organization involved.; Damage to one's reputation.; Widespread moral outrage, indignation, as over an offence to decency.
more.etymology: From Middle French scandale (“indignation caused by misconduct or defamatory speech”), from Ecclesiastical Latin scandalum (“that on which one trips, cause of offense”, literally “stumbling block”), from Ancient Greek σκάνδαλον (skándalon, “a trap laid for an enemy, a cause of moral stumbling”), from Proto-Indo-European *skand- (“to jump”). Cognate with Latin scandō (“to climb”).

more.definition: Resentful desire of something possessed by another or others (but not limited to material possessions).; An object of envious notice or feeling.; A red-skinned variety of eating apple.

Cognate to Proto-Slavic *zavistь (“envy”). Displaced native Old English æfest and nīþ.

more.definition: To feel displeasure or hatred towards (someone) for their good fortune or possessions.; To resentfully or discontentedly desire (something someone else has that one lacks).

Cognate to Proto-Slavic *zavistь (“envy”). Displaced native Old English æfest and nīþ.

From Middle English ay, ai, from Old Norse ei, from Proto-Germanic *aiwaz (“eternity, age”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eyu- (“vitality”); cognate with Old English ā, Ancient Greek ἀεί (aeí, “always”), and Latin aevum (“an age”).

translations.pt: Nossa casa foi atingida por um raio. Felizmente temos para-raios.

examples.text: Spare the rod and spoil the child.

translations.de: Wer mit der Rute spart, verzieht das Kind.
translations.fr: Qui aime bien, châtie bien.

more.definition: To reinforce concrete with metal rods.; To furnish with rods, especially lightning rods.; To penetrate sexually.
more.etymology: From Middle English rodde, from Old English *rodd or *rodde (attested in dative plural roddum (“rod, pole”)), of uncertain origin, but probably from Proto-Germanic *rudd- (“stick, club”), from Proto-Indo-European *rewdʰ- (“to clear land”). Compare Old Norse rudda (“club”). For the root, compare English rid. Presumably unrelated to Proto-Germanic *rōdō (“rod, pole”).

examples.text: The participation of Muslims in politics is of fundamental importance to society.

translations.de: Die Beteiligung der Muslime in der Politik ist von grundlegender Bedeutung für die Gesellschaft.
translations.fr: La participation des musulmans à la politique est d'une importance fondamentale pour la société.
translations.pt: A participação dos muçulmanos na política é de fundamental importância na sociedade.

examples.text: This is a matter of supreme importance.

translations.de: Das ist eine Sache von höchster Bedeutung.
translations.fr: C'est là une question d'une importance cruciale.
translations.pt: Esta é uma questão de suma importância.

examples.text: They know the importance of protecting the earth.

translations.de: Sie wissen, wie wichtig es ist, die Erde zu beschützen.
translations.fr: Ils connaissent l'importance de protéger la terre.
translations.pt: Eles sabem a importância de proteger a terra.

examples.text: Social media is growing in importance.

translations.de: Die Bedeutung sozialer Medien wächst.
translations.fr: L'importance des médias sociaux augmente.
translations.pt: A mídia social está crescendo em importância.

more.definition: The quality or condition of being important or worthy of note.; significance or prominence.; personal status or standing.
more.etymology: From Middle English importaunce, from Middle French importance, from Medieval Latin importantia. By surface analysis, import (“to be important”) + -ance.

examples.text: He accidentally hit his thumb with the hammer.

translations.de: Er schlug sich versehentlich mit dem Hammer auf den Daumen.
translations.fr: Il s'est accidentellement frappé le pouce avec son marteau.

examples.text: He accidentally got on the wrong train.

translations.de: Er hat versehentlich den falschen Zug genommen.
translations.fr: Il a pris le mauvais train par erreur.

examples.text: Tom accidentally shot himself in the foot.

translations.de: Tom hat sich aus Versehen in den Fuß geschossen.
translations.fr: Tom s'est accidentellement tiré dans le pied.

translations.fr: J'ai renversé ton thé sans faire exprès, désolé.

more.definition: In an accidental manner; by chance, unexpectedly.; Unintentionally.; Used with the verb omitted but implied, the verb itself having the meaning 'omit', 'delete' or similar.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der. Proto-Germanic *līkąder. From accidental + -ly.

examples.text: She doesn't need sympathy, but support.

translations.de: Sie braucht kein Mitleid, sondern Unterstützung.
translations.fr: Elle n'a pas besoin de compassion, mais de soutien.
translations.pt: Ela não precisa de compaixão, mas sim de apoio.

examples.text: Please accept my sympathies.

translations.fr: Veuillez accepter mes condoléances.
translations.pt: Por favor, aceite minhas condolências.

examples.text: Empathy is not the same as sympathy.

translations.de: Empathie ist nicht das Gleiche wie Sympathie.
translations.fr: L'empathie n'est pas la même chose que la compassion.

examples.text: I don't need your sympathy.

translations.de: Ihr Mitleid brauche ich nicht.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas besoin de ta pitié.

more.definition: A feeling of pity or sorrow for the suffering or distress of another.; The formal expression of pity or sorrow for someone else's misfortune.; The ability to share the feelings of another.
more.etymology: Borrowed from Middle French sympathie, from Late Latin sympathīa (“feeling in common”), from Ancient Greek σῠμπᾰ́θειᾰ (sŭmpắtheiă, “fellow feeling”), from σῠμπᾰθής (sŭmpăthḗs, “affected by like feelings; exerting mutual influence, interacting”) + -ῐᾰ (-ĭă, “-y”, nominal suffix). Equivalent to sym- (“acting or considered together”) + -pathy (“feeling”).

examples.text: He remained a bachelor all his life.

translations.fr: Il est resté célibataire toute sa vie.

examples.text: That man is definitely a bachelor.

translations.fr: Cet homme est sans nul doute célibataire.

examples.text: If he were a bachelor, I would marry him.

translations.de: Wenn er noch Junggeselle wäre, würde ich ihn heiraten.

examples.text: Tom is a confirmed bachelor.

more.definition: A person, especially a man, who is socially regarded as able to marry but has not yet.; A bachelor apartment.; A male animal without a mate during breeding season.

more.definition: A former wife (from a previous marriage after a divorce).
more.etymology: Latin ex-der. Middle French ex-bor. From ex- + wife.

examples.text: This is democracy, I think.

translations.de: Das ist Demokratie, denke ich.
translations.fr: C’est la démocratie, je crois.
translations.pt: Isto é democracia, eu acho.

examples.text: Germany is a parliamentary democracy.

translations.fr: L'Allemagne est une démocratie parlementaire.
translations.pt: A Alemanha é uma democracia parlamentária.

examples.text: Democracy is the dictatorship of the majority.

examples.text: He stands for democracy.

more.definition: Rule by the people, especially as a form of government, such as; A form of government where the people elect representatives who propose and approve laws and administer the government on their behalf (representative democracy).; A form of government where the people vote directly on laws and government decisions (direct democracy).
more.etymology: From Middle French democratie (French démocratie), from Medieval Latin dēmocratia, from Ancient Greek δημοκρᾰτῐ́ᾱ (dēmokrătĭ́ā). By surface analysis, demo- (“people”) + -cracy (“rule”).

examples.text: She presented him with the trophy.

translations.de: Er hielt die Trophäe in die Höhe.

more.definition: An object, usually in the form of a statuette, cup, or shield, awarded for success in a competition or to mark a special achievement.; An object taken as a prize by a hunter, or a conqueror or belligerent, especially one that is displayed.; Any emblem of success; a status symbol.
more.etymology: From Middle French trophée, from Latin trophaeum (“a sign of victory, a monument”), tropaeum, from Ancient Greek τρόπαιον (trópaion, “monument of an enemy's defeat”), from neuter of τροπαῖος (tropaîos, “of defeat”), from τροπή (tropḗ, “a rout, a turning of an enemy”). Doublet of tropæum.

examples.text: She presented him with the trophy.

translations.de: Sie hat ihm die Trophäe überreicht.

more.definition: To set, fix or determine (a time or place for something such as a meeting, or the meeting itself) by authority or agreement.; To name (someone to a post or role).; To furnish or equip (a place) completely; to provide with all the equipment or furnishings necessary; to fit out.

translations.pt: Paciência é essencial para um professor.

examples.text: We need few words to express what is essential.

translations.de: Wir brauchen wenige Worte, um auszudrücken, was wesentlich ist.
translations.fr: Il nous faut peu de mots pour exprimer l’essentiel.
translations.pt: Precisamos de poucas palavras para exprimir o que é importante.

more.definition: Necessary.; Very important; of high importance.; Necessary for survival but not synthesized by the organism, thus needing to be ingested.
more.etymology: From Late Latin essentiālis, from Latin essentia (“being, essence”).

examples.text: Patience is essential for a teacher.

translations.de: Geduld ist für einen Lehrer unerlässlich.
translations.fr: La patience est essentielle pour un professeur.
translations.pt: Paciência é essencial para um professor.

examples.text: Water is essential to life.

translations.de: Wasser ist für das Leben unverzichtbar.
translations.fr: L'eau est essentielle à la vie.
translations.pt: A água é essencial à vida.

examples.text: The camera was essential for me.

translations.de: Die Kamera war mir unentbehrlich.
translations.fr: L'appareil photo était pour moi essentiel.
translations.pt: A câmara foi essencial para mim.

examples.text: The two most essential parts of speech are verbs and nouns.

translations.de: Die beiden wichtigsten Wortarten sind Verben und Substantive.
translations.fr: Les deux parties les plus essentielles du discours sont les verbes et les noms.
translations.pt: As duas partes mais essenciais do discurso são verbos e substantivos.

more.definition: A necessary ingredient.; A fundamental ingredient.
more.etymology: From Late Latin essentiālis, from Latin essentia (“being, essence”).

examples.text: This disease is caused by a rare genetic mutation.

translations.de: Diese Krankheit wird von einer seltenen genetischen Mutation hervorgerufen.
translations.fr: Cette maladie est causée par une mutation génétique rare.

examples.text: There seems to be some genetic problem with this animal.

translations.de: Es scheint da ein genetisches Problem mit diesem Tier zu geben.
translations.fr: On dirait que cet animal a un problème génétique.

examples.text: The chromosomes in our cells contain the whole of our genetic material.

translations.fr: Les chromosomes de nos cellules contiennent l'ensemble de notre matériel génétique.
translations.pt: Os cromossomos nas nossas células contêm todo nosso material genético.

examples.text: Should we use genetic engineering on people?

translations.pt: Devemos usar engenharia genética em seres humanos?

more.definition: Relating to genetics or genes.; Caused by genes.; Of or relating to origin (genesis).
more.etymology: Coined from genesis, similarly to antithesis, antithetic. Reflects Ancient Greek γενετικός (genetikós), from γένεσις (génesis) + -κός (-kós). Ultimately from Ancient Greek γίγνομαι (gígnomai, “I come into being”). By surface analysis, gene + -tic or gen(esis) + -etic.

examples.text: Why are you speaking so loudly?

translations.de: Warum sprechen Sie so laut?
translations.fr: Pourquoi parlez-vous si fort ?
translations.pt: Por que está falando tão alto?

examples.text: Tom was talking very loudly.

translations.de: Tom sprach sehr laut.
translations.fr: Tom parlait très fort.
translations.pt: Tom estava falando muito alto.

examples.text: I spoke loudly so that everyone could hear me.

translations.de: Ich sprach laut, so dass mich jeder hören konnte.
translations.fr: Je parlai fort, de manière à ce que chacun puisse m'entendre.
translations.pt: Eu falei alto para que todo mundo pudesse me ouvir.

examples.text: She spoke loudly.

translations.de: Sie redete laut.
translations.fr: Elle parlait fort.
translations.pt: Ela falou em voz alta.

more.definition: In a loud manner; at a high volume.; In a loud manner; gaudily, showily.
more.etymology: From Middle English loudly, equivalent to loud + -ly.

examples.text: Chemistry is a marvelous science.

translations.fr: La chimie est une science merveilleuse.

examples.text: This forum is marvellous.

translations.de: Dieses Forum ist wunderbar.
translations.fr: Ce forum est merveilleux.
translations.pt: Este fórum é maravilhoso.

examples.text: It's marvellous.

translations.de: Es ist wunderbar.
translations.fr: C'est merveilleux.

examples.text: What marvelous weather.

translations.de: Was für ein prächtiges Wetter.
translations.fr: Quel merveilleux temps !
translations.pt: Que tempo maravilhoso.

more.definition: Exciting wonder or surprise; astonishing; wonderful.
more.etymology: First attested from 1300 as Middle English merveilous, from Old French merveillus, from merveille (“a wonder”), equivalent to marvel + -ous.

examples.text: It's time to polish up my English for a trip.

translations.de: Es ist Zeit, mein Englisch für eine Reise aufzupolieren.

translations.pt: É hora de aperfeiçoar meu inglês para uma viagem.

examples.text: If you enjoyed studying Russian, you will certainly enjoy Polish too.

translations.pt: Se gostaste de estudar o Russo, certamente vais gostar também do Polonês.

examples.text: She speaks Hebrew with her mother and Polish with her father.

examples.text: You should polish your shoes before you go to the party.

translations.fr: Tu devrais cirer tes chaussures avant d'aller à la soirée.
translations.pt: Você deveria polir seus sapatos antes de ir para a festa.

more.definition: Of, from or native to Poland, or relating to the Polish language.
more.etymology: From Pole + -ish. Doublet of Poylish.

examples.text: He wanted to polish his shoes.

translations.de: Er wollte seine Schuhe putzen.
translations.fr: Il voulait cirer ses chaussures.
translations.pt: Ele quis engraxar seus sapatos.

examples.text: I don't understand Polish.

translations.fr: Je ne comprends pas le polonais.
translations.pt: Eu não entendo polonês.

examples.text: I am a Polish journalist.

translations.fr: Je suis un journaliste polonais.

examples.text: Do you speak Polish?

translations.de: Sprichst du Polnisch?
translations.fr: Tu parles polonais ?
translations.pt: Você fala polonês?

more.definition: The language spoken in Poland.; A breed of chickens with a large crest of feathers.
more.etymology: From Pole + -ish. Doublet of Poylish.

more.definition: Physically attractive (of a person).
more.etymology: From good + looking. Compare Dutch goeduitziend (“good-looking”), German gutaussehend (“good-looking”).

examples.text: We sell sensors for motorized awnings.

examples.text: The sensors aren't detecting anything unusual.

translations.de: Die Sensoren erfassen nichts Außergewöhnliches.

examples.text: Has this phone got a fingerprint sensor?

translations.de: Hat dieses Telefon eine Fingerabdruckerkennung?

more.definition: A device or organ that detects certain external stimuli and responds in a distinctive manner.

examples.text: Perry has acquired the habit of thinking aloud.

translations.de: Perry hat sich angewöhnt, laut zu denken.
translations.fr: Perry a pris l'habitude de penser à voix haute.
translations.pt: Perry adquiriu o hábito de pensar alto.

examples.text: That which is easily acquired is easily lost.

translations.fr: Ce qui est facilement gagné est facilement perdu.
translations.pt: O que facilmente se ganha, facilmente se perde.

examples.text: One can acquire this book only in a store.

translations.de: Dieses Buch gibt es nur in einem Laden.
translations.pt: Este livro só está disponível nas lojas.

examples.text: She acquired a knowledge of French.

translations.fr: Elle a acquis des connaissances en français.
translations.pt: Ela aprendeu francês.

more.definition: To get.; To gain, usually by one's own exertions; to get as one's own.; To become affected by an illness.
more.etymology: From Middle English acqueren, from Old French aquerre, from Latin acquirō; ad- + quaerō (“to seek for”). See quest.

examples.text: Did I pronounce your name correctly?

translations.fr: Ai-je bien prononcé votre nom ?

examples.text: How do you pronounce her name?

translations.de: Wie spricht man ihren Namen aus?
translations.fr: Comment prononce-t-on son nom ?
translations.pt: Como se pronuncia o nome dela?

examples.text: Is there anyone who can pronounce this word?

translations.de: Kann jemand dieses Wort aussprechen?
translations.fr: Y a-t-il quelqu'un qui puisse prononcer ce mot ?
translations.pt: Tem alguém que possa pronunciar esta palavra?

examples.text: We learned how to pronounce Japanese.

translations.de: Wir lernten die japanische Aussprache.
translations.fr: Nous avons appris à prononcer le japonais.
translations.pt: Aprendemos a pronunciar o japonês.

more.definition: Eggcorn of pronouns.

examples.text: Am I pronouncing this word correctly?

translations.de: Spreche ich dieses Wort richtig aus?
translations.fr: Est-ce que je prononce ce mot correctement ?
translations.pt: Estou pronunciando essa palavra corretamente?

examples.text: I can't pronounce this word.

translations.de: Die meisten Konsonanten werden wie im Englischen ausgesprochen.
translations.fr: La plupart des consonnes se prononcent comme en anglais.
translations.pt: A maioria das consoantes são pronunciadas como em Inglês.

more.definition: To declare formally, officially or ceremoniously.; To declare authoritatively, or as a formal expert opinion.; To pronounce dead.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Latin prōnūntiōlbor. Old French prononcierbor. Recorded since c.1330 as Middle English pronouncen (“to utter, declare officially”), from Old French prononcier, from Latin prōnūntiō, itself from prō- (“forth, out, in public”) + nūntiō (“to announce”) from nūntius (“messenger”).

examples.text: He put the book on the shelf.

translations.de: Er stellte das Buch ins Regal.
translations.fr: Il mit le livre sur l'étagère.
translations.pt: Ele colocou o livro na prateleira.

examples.text: There are a lot of shelves in this library.

translations.fr: Il y a beaucoup d'étagères dans cette bibliothèque.
translations.pt: Há muitas estantes nesta biblioteca.

translations.de: Ich nahm ein Buch aus dem Regal.

more.definition: A flat, rigid structure, fixed at right angles to a wall or forming a part of a cabinet, desk, etc., and used to display, store, or support objects.; The capacity of such an object; A projecting ledge that resembles such an object.

From Middle English schelfe, probably from Old English sċylfe, sċilfe (“shelf, ledge, deck of a ship”), from Proto-West Germanic *skilfijā, from Proto-Germanic *skelfō (“shelf, ledge, cliff”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kelH- (“to cut”), distantly related to sculpt, carve and shell.

examples.text: Without loss of generality, we can say that the sequence converges to zero.

translations.fr: Personne ne pouvait se rappeler de la succession des évènements.

translations.pt: Uma sequência miserável de derrotas nos desanimou.

examples.text: Laziness is the mother of invention.

translations.de: Die Faulheit ist die Mutter der Erfindung.
translations.fr: La paresse est la mère de l'invention.
translations.pt: A preguiça é a mãe da invenção.

examples.text: Necessity is the mother of invention.

translations.de: Notwendigkeit ist die Mutter aller Erfindungen.

examples.text: Radio is a great invention.

translations.de: Das Radio ist eine großartige Erfindung.

examples.text: Language is one of the most important inventions of mankind.

translations.de: Die Sprache ist eine der wichtigsten Erfindungen der Menschheit.

examples.text: I'll take that into consideration.

translations.fr: J'y réfléchirai.

translations.fr: Pourquoi es-tu si maladroit ?
translations.pt: Por que você é tão desajeitado?

examples.text: The clumsy man envied her extraordinary talent.

translations.de: Der unbeholfene Mann beneidete sie um ihre außergewöhnliche Begabung.
translations.pt: O homem desajeitado invejava o talento extraordinário dela.

examples.text: I'm clumsy.

translations.de: Ich habe zwei linke Hände.
translations.pt: Sou desastrado.

examples.text: Seals are clumsy and awkward on land, but very graceful in the water.

translations.de: Seehunde sind schwerfällig und unbeholfen auf dem Land, aber sehr anmutig im Wasser.
translations.fr: Les phoques sont malhabiles et maladroits sur terre, mais très gracieux dans l'eau.
translations.pt: As focas são desajeitadas e estranhas em terra, mas muito graciosas na água.

more.definition: A clumsy person.
more.etymology: Possibly from an alteration of clumsed (“benumbed”) or from clumse (“a stupid fellow; lout”) + -y. More at clumse.

examples.text: They will obliterate the opposition.

translations.de: Sie werden die Opposition ausschalten.
translations.pt: Eles irão destruir a oposição.

examples.text: Markku ran up against strong opposition with his proposal.

translations.de: Markku stieß mit seinem Vorschlag auf starken Widerstand.
translations.pt: Markku encontrou forte oposição à sua proposta.

examples.text: The opposition was divided.

translations.fr: L'opposition était divisée.
translations.pt: A oposição estava dividida.

examples.text: Opposition to the embargo was growing.

translations.de: Der Widerstand gegen das Embargo wurde stärker.
translations.fr: L'opposition à l'embargo allait croissante.

more.definition: The action of opposing or of being in conflict.; An opposite or contrasting position.; The apparent relative position of two celestial bodies when one is at an angle of 180 degrees from the other as seen from the Earth.
more.etymology: From Middle English opposicioun, from Old French oposicion (whence French opposition), from Late Latin oppositiō, translating Ancient Greek ἀντίθεσις (antíthesis), from the past participle stem of classical Latin oppōnō (“to set against”). Equivalent to oppose + -ition.

examples.text: I can't find the equation.

translations.de: Ich kann die Gleichung nicht finden.
translations.fr: Je n'arrive pas à trouver l'équation.
translations.pt: Não consigo encontrar a equação.

examples.text: I don't know how to prove this math equation.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, wie ich diese mathematische Gleichung lösen soll.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas comment démontrer cette équation mathématique.
translations.pt: Não sei como provar esta equação matemática.

examples.text: In general, little is known about nonlinear second order differential equations.

translations.de: Im Allgemeinen weiß man wenig über nicht lineare Differentialgleichungen zweiter Ordnung.
translations.fr: En général, on en sait peu sur les équations différentielles non linéaires du second ordre.
translations.pt: Em geral se sabe pouco acerca de equações diferenciais não-lineares de segunda ordem.

examples.text: The child cannot solve the third degree equation.

translations.fr: L'enfant ne peut pas résoudre l'équation du troisième degré.
translations.pt: A criança não consegue resolver a equação do terceiro grau.

more.definition: The act or process of equating two or more things, or the state of those things being equal (that is, identical).; An assertion that two expressions are equal, expressed by writing the two expressions separated by an equal sign; in mathematical problems, equations describe various essential aspects of the problem, each of which contributes to the resolution of the problem in part.; A small correction to observed values to remove the effects of systematic errors in an observation.
more.etymology: From Old French, from Latin aequātiō (“an equalizing”). Morphologically equate + -ion

examples.text: Children, as well as adults, crave love and attention.

translations.de: Kinder und auch Erwachsene sehnen sich nach Liebe und Zuwendung.
translations.fr: Les enfants, tout comme les adultes, ont un grand besoin d'amour et d'attention.
translations.pt: As crianças adoram afeição e atenção bem como os adultos.

examples.text: Tom craves attention.

translations.de: Tom giert nach Aufmerksamkeit.
translations.fr: Tom a soif d'attention.

more.definition: A formal application to a court to make a particular order.

examples.text: Astronomy is the science of heavenly bodies.

translations.de: Astronomie ist die Wissenschaft von den Himmelskörpern.
translations.fr: L'astronomie est la science des corps célestes.
translations.pt: A astronomia é a ciência dos corpos celestes.

examples.text: A heavenly comfort, I don't know how, takes hold of me.

translations.de: Mich ergreift, ich weiß nicht wie, himmlisches Behagen.
translations.fr: Un réconfort céleste, je ne sais comment, s'empare de moi.
translations.pt: Não sei como, um bem-estar celestial se apodera de mim.

examples.text: There are countless heavenly bodies in space.

translations.de: Im Universum gibt es unzählbar viele Himmelskörper.
translations.fr: Il y a un nombre incalculable de corps célestes dans l'espace.

examples.text: Chasubles are the costume of the fools at the heavenly court.

translations.de: Messgewänder sind das Kostüm der Narren am Himmlischen Hof.

more.definition: Of or pertaining to Heaven, the eternal celestial abode of God or the gods.; Synonym of celestial: of or pertaining to the heavens, the sky regarded as the realm of the sun, moon, planets, and stars.; Strongly or sublimely good, beautiful, or pleasurable.

examples.text: Do you think he resembles his father?

translations.de: Findest du, dass er seinem Vater ähnelt?
translations.fr: Crois-tu qu'il ressemble à son père ?
translations.pt: Você acha que ele se parece com o pai?

examples.text: These two brothers resemble each other.

translations.de: Die beiden Brüder ähneln sich.
translations.fr: Ces deux frères se ressemblent.
translations.pt: Estes dois irmãos lembram um ao outro.

examples.text: The girl resembled her mother.

translations.de: Das Mädchen ähnelte seiner Mutter.
translations.fr: La fille ressemblait à sa mère.
translations.pt: A garota era parecida à mãe.

examples.text: Her face resembles her mother's.

translations.de: Ihr Gesicht ähnelt dem ihrer Mutter.
translations.fr: Son visage ressemble celui de sa mère.
translations.pt: Seu rosto parece ao da mãe.

more.definition: To be like or similar to (something); to represent as similar.
more.etymology: From Middle English resemblen, from Anglo-Norman resembler, ressembler, from re- + sembler (“to seem”). By surface analysis, re- + semble.

examples.text: I can't understand the psychology of adolescents.

translations.de: Ich verstehe nichts von der Psychologie Heranwachsender.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas comprendre la psychologie des adolescents.
translations.pt: Não consigo entender a psicologia dos adolescentes.

examples.text: I study psychology.

translations.de: Ich studiere Psychologie.
translations.fr: J'étudie la psychologie.
translations.pt: Estudo psicologia.

examples.text: I majored in psychology.

translations.de: Mein Hauptfach war Psychologie.
translations.fr: Je me suis spécialisé en psychologie.
translations.pt: Eu me formei em psicologia.

examples.text: The book contains tidbits of information about psychology.

translations.fr: Le livre contient des bribes d'informations sur la psychologie.
translations.pt: O livro contém informações detalhadas sobre psicologia.

more.definition: The study of the human mind.; The study of human or animal behavior.; The study of the soul.
more.etymology: From French psychologie, from Renaissance Latin psychologia, from Ancient Greek ψυχή (psukhḗ, “soul”) + -λογία (-logía, “study of”), equivalent to psycho- + -logy. The Latin term is believed by some to have been coined in a lost treatise by Croatian humanist Marko Marulić (1450–1524), but this is disputed by other scholars.

examples.text: The work is hereby done.

translations.de: Die Arbeit ist hiermit erledigt.
translations.fr: Le travail est effectué par la présente.

examples.text: I hereby declare the opening of the Olympic Games.

translations.fr: Je déclare les Jeux Olympiques ouverts.
translations.pt: Declaro a abertura dos Jogos Olímpicos.

examples.text: Prohibition is hereby officially prohibited.

translations.de: Verbieten ist hiermit offiziell verboten.
translations.fr: La prohibition est dorénavant officiellement prohibée.

examples.text: I hereby tender my resignation.

translations.fr: Par la présente, je remets ma démission.

more.definition: By this means, action or process.
more.etymology: From here + by.

examples.text: I'm waiting for the ferry.

translations.de: Ich warte auf die Fähre.
translations.fr: J'attends le ferry.
translations.pt: Eu estou esperando pela balsa.

examples.text: Tom offered to ferry us across the river in his boat.

translations.fr: Tom proposa de nous faire traverser la rivière dans son bateau.
translations.pt: Tom se ofereceu para transportar-nos através do rio em seu barco.

examples.text: The travelers took a ferry across the river.

translations.de: Die Reisenden überquerten den Fluss mit einer Fähre.
translations.pt: Os viajantes atravessaram o rio numa barca.

examples.text: When's the last ferry?

translations.de: Wann geht die letzte Fähre?
translations.pt: Quando sai a última balsa?

more.definition: A boat or ship used to transport people, smaller vehicles and goods from one port to another, usually on a regular schedule.; A place where passengers are transported across water in such a ship.; The service constituted by this watercraft's operation; the business (company) that operates such a service.
more.etymology: The verb is from Middle English ferien (“to carry, convey”), from Old English ferian, from Proto-West Germanic *farjan, from Proto-Germanic *farjaną, which see for cognates. This verb is the causative of Proto-Germanic *faraną (“to go, travel”), whence English fare; ultimately from the Proto-Indo-European root *per-.

examples.text: Economics is the study of economic mechanisms.

translations.de: Ökonomie ist das Studium wirtschaftlicher Mechanismen.
translations.fr: L'économie c'est l'étude des mécanismes économiques.

examples.text: Bureaucracy is a giant mechanism operated by pygmies.

translations.de: Die Bürokratie ist ein gewaltiger Mechanismus, der von Pygmäen betrieben wird.
translations.pt: A burocracia é um mecanismo gigantesco operado por pigmeus.

examples.text: Fever is one of the body's defence mechanisms.

translations.de: Fieber gehört zu den Abwehrmechanismen des Körpers.
translations.fr: La fièvre est un des mécanismes de défense de l'organisme.

examples.text: The mechanism of this machine is complicated.

translations.de: Der Mechanismus dieser Maschine ist kompliziert.
translations.fr: Le mécanisme de cette machine est compliqué.

more.definition: Any mechanical means for the conversion or control of motion, or the transmission or control of power.; Any combination of cams, gears, links, belts, chains and logical mechanical elements.; A group of entities, such as objects, that interact together.
more.etymology: Ancient Greek μηχᾰνή (mēkhănḗ)der. New Latin mechanismuslbor. Learned borrowing from New Latin mechanismus.

examples.text: I don't dispute the facts.

translations.de: Ich streite die Fakten nicht ab.
translations.fr: Je ne conteste pas les faits.

examples.text: Old disputes are easily revived.

translations.de: Alter Zank wird leicht erneut.
translations.fr: Les vieilles disputes se ravivent facilement.

examples.text: We succeeded in settling the dispute.

translations.de: Es gelang uns, den Streit zu schlichten.
translations.fr: Nous avons réussi à régler le différend.

examples.text: The dispute was settled peacefully.

translations.de: Der Streit wurde friedlich gelöst.
translations.pt: A disputa foi resolvida pacificamente.

more.definition: An argument or disagreement; a failure to agree.; A disagreement between parties in a contract, lawsuit, treaty, or other legal matter.; Verbal controversy or disagreement; altercation; debate.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *trísinflu. Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Old French desputerbor. From Middle English disputen, from Old French desputer (French disputer), from Latin disputāre (“to dispute, discuss, examine, compute, estimate”), from dis- (“apart”) + putāre (“to reckon, consider, think, originally make clean, clear up”), related to purus (“pure”). Compare compute, count, impute, repute, amputate, etc.

examples.text: The dispute turned quickly into a war.

translations.de: Der Streit verwandelte sich schnell in einen Krieg.
translations.fr: La dispute se transforma vite en guerre.

examples.text: International disputes must be settled peacefully.

translations.de: Internationale Konflikte müssen friedlich gelöst werden.
translations.fr: Les conflits internationaux doivent être résolu pacifiquement.

examples.text: I'm not disputing that.

translations.de: Das bestreite ich nicht.
translations.fr: Je ne conteste pas cela.

examples.text: I disputed with him about world peace for an hour.

translations.de: Ich stritt mich mit ihm eine Stunde lang über den Weltfrieden.
translations.pt: Discuti com ele sobre paz mundial por um hora.

more.definition: To contend in argument; to argue against something maintained, upheld, or claimed, by another.; To make a subject of disputation; to argue pro and con; to discuss.; To oppose by argument or assertion; to controvert; to express dissent or opposition to; to call into question; to deny the truth or validity of.
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *trísinflu. Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Old French desputerbor. From Middle English disputen, from Old French desputer (French disputer), from Latin disputāre (“to dispute, discuss, examine, compute, estimate”), from dis- (“apart”) + putāre (“to reckon, consider, think, originally make clean, clear up”), related to purus (“pure”). Compare compute, count, impute, repute, amputate, etc.

examples.text: My car is a gas-hog.

translations.fr: Les autorités ont libéré d'une porcherie quinze cochons négligés.

translations.fr: John aime monopoliser toute l'attention.

more.definition: Any animal belonging to the Suidae family of mammals, especially the pig, the warthog, and the boar.; An adult swine, at or above a certain body weight.; A greedy person or thing; one who refuses to share; a gluttonous one.
more.etymology: From Middle English hog, from Old English hogg, hocg (“hog”), possibly from Old Norse hǫggva (“to strike, chop, cut”), from Proto-Germanic *hawwaną (“to hew, forge”), from Proto-Indo-European *kewh₂- (“to beat, hew, forge”). Cognate with Old High German houwan, Old Saxon hauwan, Old English hēawan (English hew). Hog originally meant a castrated male pig, hence a sense of “the cut one”.

more.definition: A case of translucent or transparent material made to protect a flame, or light, used to illuminate its surroundings.; Especially, a metal casing with lens used to illuminate a stage (e.g. spotlight, floodlight).; An open structure of light material set upon a roof, to give light and air to the interior.

more.definition: To search or attempt to find something in the dark, or, as a blind person, by feeling; to move about hesitatingly, as in darkness or obscurity; to feel one's way, as with the hands, when one can not see.; To touch (another person) closely and (especially) sexually.; To intentionally and inappropriately touch or rub against another person, in such a manner as to make the contact appear accidental, for the purpose of one's sexual gratification.

examples.text: For circumstantial evidence, that's plenty.

more.definition: Pertaining to or dependent on circumstances, especially as opposed to essentials; incidental, not essential.; Involving evidence that relies on inference to connect it to a conclusion of fact, thus, suggesting guilt but not directly proving it.; Abounding with minor circumstances; in great detail; particular.

more.definition: An elemental (spirit or corporeal creature associated with a classical element) associated with earth.; One of a race of imaginary human-like beings, usually depicted as short and typically bearded males, who inhabit the inner parts of the earth and act as guardians of mines, mineral treasure, etc.; in modern fantasy literature and games, when distinguished from dwarves, gnomes are usually smaller than dwarves and more focused on engineering than mining.; A person of a small stature or misshapen features, or of a strange appearance.
more.etymology: From French gnome (“gnome”), from New Latin gnomus, used by Paracelsus as a synonym for pygmaeus (“pygmy”).
